总结

It's eight years after the war and Hermione Granger has taken a break from her career at the Ministry of Magic to compile an oral history of the conflict. She's interviewed just about everyone she can get her hands on but she wants to be thorough. And that means getting in contact with a very unwilling Lucius Malfoy.
战后八年，赫敏·格兰杰 （Hermione Granger） 从魔法部的职业生涯中抽身出来，编纂了一场冲突的口述历史。她几乎采访了所有她能接触到的人，但她想做到彻底。而这意味着要与一个非常不情愿的卢修斯·马尔福取得联系。

- - - - -

"For your information, I'm not shopping it around yet because I still don’t have access to all of the sources I need.”
“供您参考，我还没有货比三家，因为我仍然无法获得我需要的所有资源。”

“You’ve got to be joking. You must have interviewed every living person that was even tangentially connected to the war.”
“你得在开玩笑。你一定采访过每一个活着的人，哪怕是与战争有直接联系的人。

“Not everyone,” Hermione said, turning in her seat to reach up for the mug of tea she’d left on the kitchen counter.
“不是所有人，”赫敏说，在座位上转过身来，伸手去拿她留在厨房柜台上的茶杯。

“Who’s left? The trolley lady from the Hogwarts Express?”
“谁还剩下？霍格沃茨特快列车的手推车女郎？

“Your father.”
“你的爸爸。”

Malfoy opened his mouth and then closed it again with a click of his teeth, shaking his head. “You don’t want to do that, Granger.”
马尔福张开嘴，然后又咬牙切齿地闭上了，摇了摇头。“你不想那样做，格兰杰。”

第一章April 12th 2006
四月 12th 2006

“Well, Malfoy, I think that’s us finally done,” Hermione Granger said, tapping her voice recorder with her wand and wearing a tired but triumphant smile.
“嗯，马尔福，我想我们终于完成了，”赫敏·格兰杰说，用魔杖敲打着她的录音机，露出疲惫但得意洋洋的笑容。

“Not before time.”
“不早于时间。”

Lifting her Quick Quotes Quill from its matching parchment mid-word, Hermione raised her eyebrow at Draco Malfoy who merely smiled thinly in response. He sat across from her at her tiny kitchen table, his back to the rain-spattered window, with a faintly steaming mug of tea clutched in his pale, long-fingered hands. It was the mug he always used during their appointments—the biggest one she owned. 
赫敏从匹配的羊皮纸上拿起她的快速语录羽毛笔，向德拉科·马尔福扬起眉毛，而德拉科·马尔福只是淡淡地笑了笑作为回应。他坐在她对面的厨房小桌子旁，背对着被雨水溅起的窗户，苍白的长手指手里攥着一杯淡淡冒着热气的茶。那是他在他们约会时总是用的杯子——她拥有的最大的杯子。

Sometimes it occurred to Hermione how strange it was that Draco Malfoy of all people was a regular visitor in her flat and that he was there often enough to have developed an attachment to one of her mugs. But so much of her life had changed over the past two years and, really, he had become one of the more pleasant additions.
有时候赫敏会想，德拉科·马尔福是她公寓的常客，而且他经常在那里，以至于对她的一个杯子产生了依恋，这是多么奇怪。但在过去的两年里，她的生活发生了很大变化，真的，他已经成为了更令人愉快的人之一。

“You’re talking like you haven’t absolutely relished talking to me about yourself for nine straight weeks,” she said, her mouth pursed sceptically. 
“你说得好像你连续九周都不喜欢和我谈论你自己，”她说，怀疑地撅起嘴巴。

“ That I enjoyed,” he said, raising a corrective finger, then lowering it to point directly at her. “And I’m certain you did, too. What I did not enjoy was sitting at this increasingly alarming table.” 
“我喜欢，”他说，举起一根纠正的手指，然后放下它直接指向她。“而且我敢肯定你也这样做了。我不喜欢的是坐在这张越来越令人担忧的桌子上。

Hermione flushed and followed Malfoy’s gaze down. The formica surface of her small, rectangular kitchen table had not been visible for a long time. It was littered with books, folders, broken quills and endless piles of parchment scrawled with notes of varying legibility. The sense of disorganisation wasn't helped, she was sure, by the fact that they were crammed into the only corner of her boxy kitchen that wasn't occupied by a counter. There was only room for three chairs around the table and with her and Draco in two of them, the third was occupied by an increasingly precarious pile of books.
赫敏涨红了脸，顺着马尔福的目光往下看。她那张长方形的小厨房桌子的富美家表面已经很久没有出现过了。它散落着书籍、文件夹、破损的羽毛笔和无尽的羊皮纸，上面潦草地写着各种易读的笔记。她确信，这种杂乱无章的感觉并没有得到帮助，因为他们被塞在她四四方方的厨房里唯一一个没有柜台的角落里。桌子周围只有三把椅子的空间，她和德拉科坐在其中两把椅子上，第三把椅子被一堆越来越不稳定的书占据。

“It’s surely a cry for help. Have you ever tidied it?”
“这肯定是求救的呼声。你整理过它吗？

Hermione shuffled her Quick Quotes notes from that day into their own pile and marked them with a green sticker. Getting to her feet, she assessed the table with a frown, trying to determine the route through the mess that would cause the least amount of disturbance.
赫敏把她那天的快速报价笔记整理成一堆，然后用绿色的贴纸标记它们。她站起来，皱着眉头打量着桌子，试图确定穿过这片混乱的路线，才能造成最少的干扰。

“It’s an organised mess,” she murmured, tutting as she peered around different piles without touching them to find where she’d last placed Malfoy’s folder. “I know where everything is. Eventually.”
“真是一团糟，”她喃喃自语着，一边啧啧称奇地环顾着不同的书堆，却没有碰到它们，以找到她上次把马尔福的文件夹放在哪里。“我知道所有东西都在哪里。最终。

“You need an actual work space, Granger. This flat is barely large enough to live in, never mind to live in and to work in.”
“你需要一个真正的工作空间，格兰杰。这套公寓勉强够住，更不用说住和工作了。

“Well, we don’t all have manors to swan around in, Malfoy,” Hermione said scathingly. With a small whoop she found the folder she was looking for and slid his notes into it. Finally looking up, she found him watching her with faint exasperation. “This is all the space I have and I’ve managed for almost two years. It’s fine .”
“嗯，我们可不是都有庄园可以四处逛逛的，马尔福，”赫敏严厉地说。她呐喊一声，找到了她要找的文件夹，把他的笔记滑进去。最后，她抬起头来，发现他带着淡淡的恼怒看着她。“这就是我拥有的全部空间，我已经管理了将近两年。没关系。

“Seems it.” His tone was dry as he lifted his mug up for a drink, only to find that a sheet of parchment was stuck to its bottom. “I’d just like to be sure that I’m contributing to an academic work of value rather than an absolute bloody shambles.”
“好像。”当他举起杯子喝水时，他的语气很干涩，却发现一张羊皮纸粘在了它的底部。“我只是想确保我正在为一项有价值的学术工作做出贡献，而不是绝对的血腥混乱。”

He gingerly peeled the parchment away from his mug with a pointed look and Hermione reached out to snatch it from him. “You are contributing to a work of value. Oral history is a rapidly developing and valuable field of research and documentation.”
他小心翼翼地把羊皮纸从杯子上剥下来，目光尖锐地看着赫敏，赫敏伸手从他手里抢过来。“你正在为一项有价值的工作做出贡献。口述历史是一个快速发展且有价值的研究和记录领域。

“I’ll take your word for it.” Malfoy took another sip of his tea. “I also won’t miss that stupid little thing.” He nodded disdainfully at Hermione’s voice recorder and she made an offended noise, snatching it up from the table. 
“我会相信你的话。”马尔福又喝了一口茶。“我也不会错过那个愚蠢的小东西。”他轻蔑地对赫敏的录音机点了点头，她发出了冒犯的声音，从桌子上抢了过来。

It was a Weasley’s Wizard Wheezes product and Hermione’s favourite invention of George’s by far. Shaped like a tiny gramophone, it was charmed to record sound and spit it back out. It was much like a magical tape recorder, which made sense because George had made it after Hermione had introduced him to the concept of mix tapes. Fascinated, he’d been adamant that Angelina would have to have the magical equivalent for Valentine’s Day even if he had to make it himself. So he had. And Hermione had purchased one for each of her interviewees. 
这是韦斯莱的巫师喘息产品，也是赫敏迄今为止最喜欢的乔治发明。它的形状像一台小留声机，它被吸引来录制声音并将其吐出。它很像一个神奇的录音机，这是有道理的，因为乔治是在赫敏向他介绍混音带的概念后制作的。他着迷了，一直坚持认为安吉丽娜必须拥有相当于情人节的魔法，即使他必须自己制作。所以他做到了。赫敏已经为她的每个受访者买了一本。

“Excuse me, I think it’s clever and adorable. And extremely useful.”
“对不起，我觉得它很聪明，很可爱。而且非常有用。

“Why do I feel like that’s exactly the kind of thing you’d like someone to say about you,” Malfoy said, his lip curled. Hermione flushed and placed the Wheezebox back on the table.
“为什么我觉得那正是你希望别人对你说的那种话，”马尔福说，他的嘴唇弯了起来。赫敏脸红了，把喘息盒放回桌子上。

“I suppose now that you’ve got everything you need from me, I’m never going to hear from you again.” He placed a mocking hand over his heart. “You do know how to make a man feel cheap, Granger.”
“我想现在你已经从我这里得到了你需要的一切，我再也不会收到你的消息了。”他用一只嘲弄的手捂住了自己的心。“你确实知道如何让男人觉得自己很贱，格兰杰。”

“Oh, no, I’m afraid you’ve definitely not seen the last of me. I’ll be back in touch as I put your sections together. I might need to clarify some things with you. I imagine you’ll want to cast your eye over some proofs, too. I’m more than happy for you to have an input—a small input—until publication.”
“哦，不，恐怕你肯定没有看到我的最后一面。我会在整理您的部分时与您联系。我可能需要和你澄清一些事情。我想你也会想把目光投向一些证明。我非常高兴你能在出版之前有意见——一个小小的意见。

“And do you have a publisher yet?”
“那你有出版商吗？”

“No,” Hermione said, dropping into her seat with a frown at Draco. “But that’s only because I’ve not been shopping a proposal around.”
“不，”赫敏说，皱着眉头看着德拉科坐进座位。“但那只是因为我没有四处寻找提案。”

“Granger, just let me help you. The family name is far from what it was but I might be able to sway a few people. I could mention that you’re working on something and I’m sure they’ll snap it up. War hero bookworm writes war book.” He raised his hands in the air as though imagining the words on a poster. “Guaranteed interest. We’ll leave off the history part. Boring." Ignoring her huff of indignation, he added, "Not decided on the oral aspect. It could be good if we want to reach an audience that reads words but doesn't take in full sentences. Maybe ask Weasley about that."

“哦，看在老天爷的份上，”赫敏咕哝道。“供您参考，我还没有货比三家，因为我仍然无法获得我需要的所有资源。”

“你得在开玩笑。你一定采访过每一个活着的人，哪怕是与战争有直接联系的人。

“不是所有人，”赫敏说，在座位上转过身来，伸手去拿她留在厨房柜台上的那杯茶。

“谁还剩下？霍格沃茨特快列车的手推车女郎？

“Your father.”
“你的爸爸。”

Malfoy opened his mouth and then closed it again with a click of his teeth, shaking his head. “You don’t want to do that, Granger.”
马尔福张开嘴，然后又咬牙切齿地闭上了，摇了摇头。“你不想那样做，格兰杰。”

“Of course I do. The whole point of what I’m doing is to gather a variety of perspectives on the war and there are so few people from…”
“我当然知道。我所做的全部意义在于收集关于战争的各种观点，而来自......”

“我这边。”

“That’s not what I was going to say.”
“我不是想说的。”

“Well, you can say it. You were probably thinking it.”
“嗯，你可以这么说。你可能在想。

She always stepped around it where she could, though there were times when he made that difficult for her. “There are so few people who fought with Voldemort who are in any position to speak to me about their experiences.”
赫敏叹了口气，现在已经非常熟悉马尔福倾向于抓住每一个机会邀请人们对他感到厌恶或鄙视他在战争期间的行为的方式。她总是尽可能地绕过它，尽管有时他会让她感到困难。“很少有人和伏地魔一起战斗过，他们能和我谈论他们的经历。”

“你有我，这还不够吗？我告诉了你在战争期间经历的一切。你可能把我每天穿的裤子的颜色记在那个文件夹的某个地方。

“You have told me everything and it’s been fantastic ,” Hermione said. “But your father was there for two wars and he managed to survive both of them. He’d be an invaluable source.”
“你什么都告诉我了，这真是太棒了，”赫敏说。“但你父亲在那里参加了两场战争，他设法在两场战争中幸存下来。他将是一个非常宝贵的来源。

Draco drummed his fingers against the edge of his mug, his fingernails making a series of small tings as they bounced off the porcelain. “Look, I won’t stop you from asking him but the answer will be no.”
德拉科用手指敲打着杯子的边缘，他的指甲在瓷器上弹开时发出一连串的小叮叮当当。“听着，我不会阻止你问他，但答案是否定的。”

Shifting in her seat, Hermione looked down into her tea. “I have and it was. Multiple times.”
赫敏在座位上挪动了一下，低头看着她的茶。“我有，而且曾经是。好几次。

“ Granger .” Malfoy sounded exasperated and she looked up to see that, indeed, he was. “How have you been asking him? He’s been locked in the manor for eight years .”
“格兰杰。”马尔福听起来很生气，她抬起头来，发现他确实是。“你最近怎么问他？他已经被锁在庄园里八年了。

“I’ve been sending owls.” Hermione ran a finger around the rim of her cup, her gaze sliding over Draco’s shoulder to look out the window at the wet April weather. “For a few weeks now. He hasn’t answered a single one.”
“我一直在送猫头鹰。”赫敏用一根手指在她的杯边滑过，她的目光从德拉科的肩膀上滑过，看着窗外潮湿的四月天气。“现在已经有几周了。他一个都没回答。

Draco made a sound that was somewhere between a laugh and a moan of anguish. “So that’s why he’s been so irritable recently. Stop sending owls, Granger. One day one of them won’t come back and you’ll have that on your conscience.”
德拉科发出的声音介于笑声和痛苦的呻吟之间。“所以这就是他最近如此烦躁的原因。别再派猫头鹰了，格兰杰。总有一天，他们中的一个不会回来，你会良心无愧的。

“I thought maybe if you asked him—” Hermione began but Draco immediately shook his head and held up a hand. 
“我想，如果你问他——”赫敏开始说话，但德拉科立刻摇了摇头，举起了一只手。

“He’ll still say no.” At Hermione’s look of scepticism, Draco slid his mug to the side and leaned towards her, his elbow balanced on a book. “Granger, I live in the manor with him and he barely talks to me . I see him maybe once every four or five days and if I’m lucky I’ll get a full conversation out of him. Between the house arrest and the Magic Dampener, he’s not really been the most...agreeable company.”
“他还是会说不。”看着赫敏怀疑的眼神，德拉科把杯子滑到一边，靠向她，他的胳膊肘在一本书上保持平衡。“格兰杰，我和他住在庄园里，他几乎不和我说话。我可能每四五天见他一次，如果幸运的话，我会和他进行一次完整的交谈。在软禁和魔法阻尼器之间，他并不是真正最......令人愉快的伙伴。

Crossing her arms, Hermione leaned back in her seat. “Doesn’t he see that he’s pretty lucky to have avoided Azkaban? I mean—”
赫敏交叉双臂，向后靠在座位上。“他难道没有看到他很幸运地避开了阿兹卡班吗？我是说——”

“Yes,” Draco tilted his head and gave her a penetrating look. “I’m sure marching into his home and taking that approach is guaranteed to break through his barriers and unlock the loquacious man that still lies beneath.”
“是的，”德拉科歪着头，狠狠地看了她一眼。“我敢肯定，走进他的家并采取这种方法肯定会突破他的障碍，解开仍然隐藏在下面的懒散男人。”

Hermione flushed and shifted, not entirely sure why she felt a twinge of guilt. “Surely there must be something that would convince him.”
赫敏脸红了，动了动，不完全确定她为什么会感到一阵内疚。“肯定有什么东西能说服他。”

“I can hardly see what you can offer him. He’s short on freedom and magic but he’s still got plenty of money. And, no offence, but while I think company would be good for him I’m not sure he’d relish yours.”
“我几乎看不出你能给他什么。他缺乏自由和魔法，但他仍然有很多钱。而且，没有冒犯，但虽然我认为有人陪伴对他有好处，但我不确定他会不会喜欢你的。

They fell into silence, the only sounds being a steady drip coming from Hermione’s kitchen tap and the gentle patter of the rain against the window. Taking a drink, Hermione assessed Draco over the rim of her mug. He was skim-reading the top sheet of a pile of parchment that sat by his elbow. The red sticker told her it was a section of her interviews with McGonagall. She’d gathered so many perspectives from the war. Harry, Ron and the rest of the surviving Weasleys, of course, as well as many of the surviving members of the Order. Even Aberforth had consented to speak with her. 
他们陷入了沉默，唯一的声音是赫敏厨房水龙头不断滴落的声音和雨水轻轻拍打窗户的声音。赫敏喝了一口，隔着杯子的边缘打量着德拉科。他正在略读放在他手肘边的一堆羊皮纸的顶页。红色贴纸告诉她，这是她对麦格采访的一部分。她从战争中收集了很多观点。当然，哈利、罗恩和其他幸存的韦斯莱一家，以及许多幸存的骑士团成员。就连阿不福思也同意和她谈谈。

Draco had been a particularly big win. It had taken weeks of pestering just to get him to agree to meet her. But she was determined that she wouldn’t just record the voices of the Order; she wanted to connect narratives from across the battlefields for a more complete picture. Draco had, after much back and forth, come to appreciate what she was trying to do and believed that she wasn’t trying to trap him into some humiliating exposé. 
德拉科是一场特别大的胜利。他花了好几个星期的纠缠才让他同意见她。但她决心不只是记录教团的声音;她想将来自各个战场的叙述联系起来，以获得更完整的画面。经过多次来回，德拉科已经明白了她想要做的事情，并相信她并不是想让他陷入某种羞辱性的揭露中。

With so many former Death Eaters dead or locked in the depths of Azkaban, in some senses she needed Lucius Malfoy. He had been in Voldemort’s inner circle; he would surely know things that his son didn’t and have a perspective that no one else she had interviewed could have. 
有这么多前食死徒死去或被关在阿兹卡班的深处，从某种意义上说，她需要卢修斯·马尔福。他一直在伏地魔的核心圈子里;他肯定会知道他儿子不知道的事情，并且拥有她采访过的其他人无法拥有的观点。

“What if I could get the Magic Dampener removed? Or a reduction in his sentence?”
“如果我能把魔法阻尼器拿走呢？还是减刑？

Draco’s head snapped up, whatever had been occupying his attention on the parchment forgotten. “You think you could do that?”
德拉科猛地抬起头，把他注意力放在羊皮纸上的任何东西都忘了。“你觉得你能做到吗？”

“Maybe,” Hermione said, her face screwing up as she considered the conversations she would need to have. “I don’t think I could get his house arrest waived entirely but shaving a few years off doesn’t seem impossible.”
“也许吧，”赫敏说，她的脸在考虑她需要进行的对话时变得糟糕。“我不认为我能完全免除他的软禁，但减少几年的软禁似乎并非不可能。”

“Well, anything less than the twenty years he got would be an improvement,” Draco muttered. 
“嗯，任何少于他得到的二十年都会是一种进步，”德拉科咕哝道。

Hermione pressed her lips together, electing not to comment. After the war, Draco and Narcissa had walked free thanks to Narcissa’s actions and Harry’s testimony on their behalf. Lucius Malfoy, on the other hand, had fared less well. He had borne the brunt of the public’s anger at the Malfoy family and received a twenty year house arrest. To add insult to injury, he was fitted with a Magic Dampener which rendered him unable to use his magic. Hermione hadn’t been especially sorry and nor had anyone else.
赫敏紧紧抿着嘴唇，选择不发表评论。战后，德拉科和纳西莎多亏了纳西莎的行动和哈利为他们作证，才得以自由自在。另一方面，卢修斯·马尔福的情况就不那么好了。他首当其冲地承受了公众对马尔福家族的愤怒，并被软禁了二十年。雪上加霜的是，他被装上了魔法阻尼器，这使他无法使用他的魔法。赫敏没有特别抱歉，其他人也没有。

“You’ve already suggested you think my father deserved what he got, so why would you do this?”
“你已经说过了，你认为我父亲应得的，那你为什么要这样做呢？”

Setting her hands flat on the parchment in front of her, Hermione stretched her fingers wide to indicate that she was effectively laying her cards on the table. “Because I’m desperate. And it’s the only thing I think might even slightly persuade him.”
赫敏双手平放在面前的羊皮纸上，张大了手指，表示她实际上是把她的卡片放在桌子上。“因为我很绝望。这是我认为唯一可能稍微说服他的事情。

Nodding slowly, Draco leaned back to give her a sweeping look. “I think you’re probably right.” Sighing, Draco shrugged his shoulders and shook his head in a way that told Hermione she had him. “Alright, Granger, you win. I’ll put it to him.”
德拉科缓缓地点了点头，向后靠了靠，扫视了她一眼。“我想你可能是对的。”德拉科叹了口气，耸了耸肩，摇了摇头，仿佛在告诉赫敏她已经拥有了他。“好吧，格兰杰，你赢了。我会告诉他的。

“Thank you!” Hermione grinned widely and bounced in her seat. “Oh, you won’t regret this, Malfoy. I’ll get in touch with Kingsley to start a conversation.”
“谢谢你！”赫敏咧嘴一笑，在座位上蹦蹦跳跳。“哦，你不会后悔的，马尔福。我会联系 Kingsley 开始对话。

Running a hand through his short blonde hair, Draco stopped its progress at the back of his neck and rubbed a spot of tension he found there. “Merlin knows something needs to change. Just the other day Astoria was telling me she doesn’t want our child growing up in a house where they could reasonably mistake their grandfather for a ghost. Is that not the most depressing thing you’ve ever heard?”
德拉科用一只手抚摸着他的金发，在他的脖子后面停下了脚步，揉了揉他在那里发现的一丝紧张。“梅林知道有些事情需要改变。就在前几天，Astoria 告诉我，她不希望我们的孩子在一个他们可以合理地将祖父误认为鬼魂的房子里长大。这难道不是你听过的最令人沮丧的事情吗？

“Then tell him what I’m proposing and, if he’s amenable, I’ll see what I can do. How is Astoria, by the way?”
“然后告诉他我有什么建议，如果他愿意的话，我看看我能做什么。对了，阿斯托利亚怎么样了？

Draco’s face immediately brightened at the prospect of being able to discuss his wife but Hermione didn’t miss the tiredness around his eyes. “She’s doing well. Late pregnancy certainly agrees with her more than the early days, though she still has the odd day where her strength disappears entirely.” 
德拉科的脸上立刻因为能够讨论他的妻子而变得明亮起来，但赫敏并没有错过他眼中的疲惫。“她做得很好。怀孕晚期肯定比怀孕早期更符合她的观点，尽管她仍然有一天她的力量完全消失。

It was hard not to stretch a sympathetic hand out to Draco, so she did. He didn’t take it but he never did; Hermione just liked to let him know that it was there. In the relatively short time they had been developing a friendly relationship, Hermione had noticed that Draco Malfoy didn’t like to touch. He didn’t mind if she reached out and touched him but to meet in the middle, to extend his hand to meet hers, seemed to be too great an act of exposure for him. Learning what she had about his experiences in the war and the long periods of lonely isolation he had gone through, Hermione couldn’t say she was offended. Understandably, he had built walls. As Hermione saw it, she was there to help him communicate through them, maybe remove a brick or two at a time, rather than to knock them down. 
很难不向Draco伸出同情的手，所以她就伸出了手。他没有接受，但他从未接受;赫敏只是喜欢让他知道它就在那里。在他们建立友好关系的相对较短的时间里，赫敏注意到德拉科·马尔福不喜欢触摸。他并不介意她伸手触摸他，但在中间相遇，伸出手来碰她的手，对他来说似乎是一种太大的暴露行为。了解了他在战争中的经历和他所经历的长期孤独孤立，赫敏不能说她被冒犯了。可以理解的是，他筑起了围墙。在赫敏看来，她在那里帮助他通过他们进行交流，也许一次移走一两块砖头，而不是把他们推倒。

Draco had revealed his anxieties to Hermione about Astoria’s delicate constitution and how it might be worsened by pregnancy on their third meeting. In the end, they had spent their allotted time that week not having a recorded interview but simply chatting as friends might. It was then that Hermione had realised how few friends Draco Malfoy actually had and it had tugged at her sympathy in a way she could never have expected. He wasn’t the same boy she had known at Hogwarts and, though she wouldn’t tell him, she had decided she would be there for him as much as he would allow her to. That was her way of rebuilding and moving forward.
德拉科在他们第三次见面时向赫敏透露了他对阿斯托利亚脆弱的体质以及怀孕可能会如何恶化的焦虑。最后，他们在那一周分配的时间里没有进行录音采访，而只是像朋友一样聊天。就在那时，赫敏意识到德拉科·马尔福的朋友实际上是多么的少，这以一种她从未预料到的方式拉扯着她的同情心。他不是她在霍格沃茨认识的那个男孩，虽然她不肯告诉他，但她已经决定，只要他允许她，她就会尽可能多地陪在他身边。这就是她重建和前进的方式。

“It’s not long until you’ll have a child to occupy your every living moment. In fact,” Hermione raised her eyes to the ceiling as she counted up the months, “yes, Astoria must be due a little bit after Ginny Potter. She and Harry are having their second soon.”
“用不了多久，你就会有一个孩子来占据你生命中的每一刻。事实上，“赫敏抬起眼睛看向天花板，数着月份，”是的，阿斯托利亚肯定比金妮·波特晚了一点。她和哈利很快就会有他们的第二个孩子。

“Of course Potter’s already on number two,” Draco scoffed, shifting his position in his seat to cross his legs. “That’ll be the Weasley urge to propagate converging with his innate need to one-up me.”
“当然，波特已经排在第二位了，”德拉科嘲笑道，把座位上的位置挪了个弯，交叉着双腿。“那将是韦斯莱想要传播的冲动，与他与生俱来的需要汇聚在一起，以超越我。”

Hermione laughed, drawing a narrow-eyed glare from Draco. “Malfoy, do you really think Harry impregnated Ginny just so he could say he has one more child than you?” 
赫敏笑了起来，引来了德拉科眯起眼睛的目光。“马尔福，你真的认为哈利让金妮怀孕只是为了说他比你多一个孩子吗？”

“I said it was innate ; he might not even realise he’s doing it. Wouldn’t put it past him, though.”
“我说这是天生的;他甚至可能没有意识到自己在这样做。不过，他不会把球放过他。

“Your children will be attending Hogwarts together,” Hermione pointed out. “An olive branch extended now could be a good chance to stop history repeating itself.”
“你的孩子会一起去霍格沃茨的，”赫敏指出。“现在伸出橄榄枝可能是阻止历史重演的好机会。”

“Thank you for the advice, oh wise woman of history.” Malfoy gave her a mocking deferential wave before tipping his head back to drain the last of his tea. “Anyway, I’d best be off. I promised Astoria I’d bring her some cauldron cakes from Diagon Alley on the way back to the manor and it’s getting close to tea time.”
“谢谢你的建议，哦，历史上的智慧女性。”马尔福嘲讽地恭敬地向她挥了挥手，然后把头往后仰，把最后一口茶都喝光了。“不管怎样，我最好还是走吧。我答应过阿斯托利亚，我会在回庄园的路上从对角巷给她带一些大锅蛋糕，现在已经快到下午茶时间了。

“Oh!” Hermione slid from her seat, careful not to disturb any of her papers, and hurried to the kitchen, Malfoy watching her warily. Opening a tin on the counter, Hermione bustled around the tiny kitchen with her back to him, eventually returning to the table with a foil-wrapped square which she placed before him.
“哦！”赫敏从座位上滑下来，小心翼翼地不打扰她的任何文件，然后匆匆忙忙地走向厨房，马尔福警惕地看着她。赫敏打开柜台上的一个罐子，背对着他，在小厨房里忙碌着，最后拿着一个用铝箔包裹的方块回到桌子旁，放在他面前。

“What,” Malfoy said, raising the soft package to his eyes and inspecting it with faint disgust, “is this?”
“什么，”马尔福说，把软包裹举到眼睛前，带着淡淡的厌恶检查它，“这是吗？

“It’s lemon cake. I made it myself.”
“这是柠檬蛋糕。我自己做到了。

“ You cook? In here ?” He gestured to the table. “Isn’t that some kind of fire hazard?”
“你做饭？在这儿？他指了指桌子。“这不是某种火灾隐患吗？”

“I bake,” Hermione corrected, then hesitated before adding, “I bake this one thing. Ginny’s craved it through both of her pregnancies, so I’ve gotten into the habit of having a few slices ready to go at all times. Astoria might like it.”
“我烤，”赫敏纠正道，然后犹豫了一下，才补充道，“我烤这一样东西。Ginny 在她的两次怀孕中都渴望它，所以我养成了随时准备好几片的习惯。阿斯托利亚可能会喜欢它。

Draco looked doubtful and brought the package closer to his face to sniff it delicately. Hermione rolled her eyes and placed her hands on her hips. “Just throw it out if she doesn’t.”
德拉科一脸疑惑，把包裹凑近他的脸，小心翼翼地闻了闻。赫敏翻了个白眼，把手放在她的臀部上。“如果她不这样做，就把它扔掉。”

He shook his head but, to Hermione’s satisfaction, he also slipped the foil-wrapped cake into the pocket of his robes that were hanging over the back of his chair. 
他摇了摇头，但令赫敏满意的是，他还把铝箔纸包裹的蛋糕塞进了挂在椅背上的长袍口袋里。

“Don’t forget to ask your father,” she reminded him as he started moving to get to his feet.
“别忘了问你爸爸，”她提醒他，他开始站起来。

Draco grumbled something that sounded like “I bloody won’t”, his tall frame moving awkwardly in the cramped space to lift his robes. He managed to slide his right arm in successfully before hitting the elbow of his left against the wall beside him with a muttered curse.
德拉科咕哝着一句，听起来像是“我的不会”，他高大的身躯在狭窄的空间里笨拙地移动着，掀起了他的长袍。他成功地将右臂滑入，然后用左手的肘部撞在旁边的墙上，喃喃自语地咒骂着。

“Maybe you could convince your mother next?” Hermione asked hopefully as she lifted their empty mugs from the table and carried them to the sink.
“也许你接下来能说服妈？”赫敏满怀希望地问道，她从桌子上拿起他们的空杯子，把它们带到水槽里。

Draco choked out a laugh as he carefully adjusted his robes into a more comfortable position on his shoulders. “Check your ambition, Granger. You’re more likely to get him than you are to get her.” 
德拉科哽咽着笑了起来，他小心翼翼地把长袍调整到肩膀上更舒服的位置。“检查你的雄心壮志，格兰杰。你得到他的可能性比你得到她的可能性更大。

Placing his hand on the back of his chair to push it under the table, Draco stopped to watch Hermione rinse the mugs. Feeling the weight of his gaze, she turned, shaking droplets of water from her hands. “What?”
德拉科把手放在椅背上，把它推到桌子下面，然后停下来看着赫敏冲洗杯子。感觉到他目光的重量，她转过身来，抖掉了手上的水滴。“什么？”

“You really want to interview him, don’t you?” 
“你真的很想采访他，不是吗？”

“I wouldn’t be asking you to do this if I didn’t.”
“如果我不这样做，我就不会要求你这样做。”

“You know that you’d need to come to the manor.”
“你知道你得来庄园。”

Hesitating, her face scrunched at the thought, Hermione shifted her weight from one foot to the other. “Like I said: I’m desperate.”
赫敏犹豫了一下，她的脸因为这个想法而皱起了眉头，她把重心从一只脚转移到了另一只脚上。“就像我说的：我很绝望。”

“ And ,” Draco continued, “if he does actually agree to this, he won’t be nice to you, Granger. I love my father a great deal but I don’t think I could tell you in all honesty that the war has made him a better person.”
“而且，”德拉科继续说，“如果他真的同意了，他就不会对你好了，格兰杰。我非常爱我的父亲，但我认为我无法诚实地告诉你，战争使他成为一个更好的人。

Crossing her arms, Hermione raised an eyebrow. “Do you really think I’m expecting your father to be nice to me? I don’t want to braid his hair, Malfoy, I want to ask him some questions. More importantly, I want him to be honest with me when he answers them. I’m fully aware that asking for honesty from your father is likely to preclude any kind of niceness .”
赫敏交叉双臂，扬起了一道眉毛。“你真的以为我期待你爸爸对我好吗？”我不想给他编辫子，马尔福，我想问他一些问题。更重要的是，我希望他在回答问题时对我诚实。我完全知道，要求你父亲诚实很可能会排除任何形式的善意。

“Fine, fine,” Draco said, raising his hands in surrender. “It was just a friendly warning. I’ll keep up my end of the bargain and you see what you can do about yours.” Malfoy moved to leave the kitchen, pausing in the doorway with his hand on the frame. “See you next week?” he asked, without turning to look at her.
“好吧，好吧，”德拉科说，举起双手投降。“这只是一个友好的警告。我会继续履行我的协议，你看看你能做些什么。马尔福离开了厨房，在门口停了下来，手放在门框上。“下周见？” 他问道，没有转头看她。

Officially, their interviews were over; Hermione had learned all she could from Draco for her oral history. Rather than remind him of that, she smiled at his back. “Sounds great.” Draco departed without another word, leaving Hermione with a fond smile on her face.
正式地，他们的采访结束了;赫敏从德拉科那里学到了她能学到的一切口述历史。她没有提醒他，而是对着他的背影微笑。“听起来不错。”德拉科一言不发地离开了，留下赫敏脸上露出了深情的笑容。

With Malfoy gone, Hermione let time get away from her. Pulling her mixing bowl and some ingredients from her kitchen cupboard, she began the methodical process of baking a fresh lemon cake; she had given him her last slice. It was her mother’s recipe—one of only two recipes Hermione had learned from her, much to her regret—and it was so familiar that she didn’t need any kind of instructions. 
马尔福走后，赫敏让时间从她身边流走。她从厨房橱柜里拿出她的搅拌碗和一些配料，开始有条不紊地烘烤新鲜的柠檬蛋糕;她已经把最后一片给了他。这是她妈妈的食谱——赫敏从她那里学到的仅有的两种食谱之一，这让她很遗憾——而且它是如此熟悉，以至于她不需要任何形式的指导。

Hermione loved interviewing her sources but the activity required her to be utterly switched on and her sessions could last hours if she and her interviewee struggled to find a natural cut-off point. So, while baking required exactitude, making the lemon cake was a soothing and almost passive activity for her. She found, particularly in the aftermath of her interviews, that it was the perfect way to move her brain down a gear and recharge.
赫敏喜欢采访她的消息来源，但这项活动需要她完全开机，如果她和她的受访者努力找到一个自然的分界点，她的会议可能会持续几个小时。因此，虽然烘焙需要精确，但制作柠檬蛋糕对她来说是一项舒缓且几乎是被动的活动。她发现，尤其是在采访之后，这是让她的大脑降档并充电的完美方式。

After sliding the cake into her oven, jiggling the damaged door to the left as she closed it, Hermione glanced at the clock and turned her attention to her work station. Malfoy was right, not that she’d ever admit it to him: she did need more space. But it was hard to come by. She had considered asking McGonagall to let her use the Hogwarts library but the idea of being around loud students looking for any excuse to be distracted from their studies didn’t appeal in the least. Being on long-term leave from the Ministry meant that she didn’t have an office there anymore, either. Overall, in her poky one bedroom flat, it was the best she could do. 
把蛋糕滑进烤箱，关上门时把坏掉的门向左晃动，赫敏看了一眼时钟，把注意力转向了她的工作站。马尔福是对的，并不是说她永远不会向他承认：她确实需要更多的空间。但这很难获得。她曾考虑过让麦格让她使用霍格沃茨图书馆，但和吵闹的学生在一起，找任何借口分散学习注意力的想法一点也不吸引人。从魔法部长期休假意味着她在那里也不再有办公室了。总的来说，在她破旧的一居室公寓里，这是她能做的最好的事情。

Opening Malfoy’s folder, she collected a few loose sheets of parchment from around it and read them over before sliding them inside. They were just notes she’d taken on the Malfoy family history in preparation for her interviews with Draco. Unfortunately, it was a mind-numbingly long history—as they would undoubtedly be proud to point out—and the sheer amount of material available meant that Draco’s folder bulged larger than most. That wasn’t to mention the books she’d found in which the Malfoy name was repeatedly mentioned in connection with magical politics, wars and laws. Individual biographical details were harder to come by without properly digging but the family name was weaved through wizarding history.
打开马尔福的文件夹，她从周围收集了几张松散的羊皮纸，仔细阅读了一遍，然后把它们滑进去。它们只是她为了准备采访德拉科而记下的关于马尔福家族历史的笔记。不幸的是，这是一段令人麻木的漫长历史——正如他们无疑会自豪地指出的那样——而且可用的材料数量之多意味着 Draco 的文件夹比大多数文件夹都大。更不用说她找到的那些书中，马尔福的名字被反复提及与魔法政治、战争和法律有关。如果不适当挖掘，个人传记细节就很难获得，但这个家族的名字已经编织在巫师历史中。

In the end, she hadn’t really needed any of the information and hadn’t delved much deeper than their family tree. But, if she was going to end up interviewing Lucius, she wanted to keep all of the resources she’d gathered to hand. Hermione had a feeling that being prepared would be key to conversations with that particular Malfoy.
最后，她并没有真正需要任何信息，也没有深入研究他们的家谱。但是，如果她最终要采访 Lucius，她想把她收集到的所有资源都留在手头。赫敏有一种感觉，做好准备将是与那个特定的马尔福交谈的关键。

Closing the folder gently, Hermione considered the offer she’d asked Draco to pass onto his father. Her desperation had perhaps made her overly optimistic about what she could reasonably expect to ask of Kingsley. But she had to try.
轻轻地合上文件夹，赫敏考虑了她让德拉科转达给他父亲的提议。她的绝望或许使她对自己可以合理地期望对金斯莱的要求过于乐观。但她必须尝试。

The sharp beep of the oven extracted Hermione from her reverie and she returned to withdraw the cake so that she could leave it to cool on the counter. Pulling her apron over her head, Hermione threw it over the back of a chair and hurried to her bedroom to change for her weekly dinner at the Potters. 
烤箱尖锐的哔哔声将赫敏从遐想中拉了出来，她回去把蛋糕拿出来，这样她就可以把它放在柜台上冷却了。赫敏把围裙套在头上，把它扔在椅背上，然后匆匆忙忙地回到自己的卧室换衣服，为她每周在波特家的晚餐换衣服。

After the birth of James, they’d agreed as a group that a more structured social life was probably necessary if they had any hope of seeing one another with a degree of regularity. Hermione, adoring structure, had probably been the most enthusiastic about the idea. Ron had grumbled about the loss of impromptu trips to the pub with Harry, though a sharp whack from his sister had closed his mouth quickly enough. 
詹姆斯出生后，他们作为一个群体一致认为，如果他们有任何希望以一定程度的规律性见到彼此，那么更有条理的社交生活可能是必要的。赫敏，喜欢结构，可能是对这个主意最热衷的人。罗恩抱怨说自己失去了和哈利一起去酒吧的即兴旅行，尽管他姐姐的一记猛烈的打击让他很快就闭上了嘴。

Flicking through her wardrobe, Hermione sighed at the abundance of denim and polyester. Her time away from the Ministry on half-pay meant that her journey towards building a more mature wardrobe had slipped back somewhat and she found she was dressing more like her teenage self with every passing day. Settling on her jeans and a worn Breton stripe jumper, she swiftly changed and attempted to make her long, messy curls more presentable.
赫敏翻阅着她的衣橱，叹息着那里丰富的牛仔布和涤纶布。她以半薪离开魔法部的时间意味着她建立更成熟衣橱的旅程已经倒退了一些，她发现自己每天都穿得更像十几岁的自己。穿上牛仔裤和破旧的布列塔尼条纹套头衫，她迅速改变并试图让她那凌乱的长卷发更像样。

Another glance at the clock as she ran back into the kitchen told Hermione that she was only twenty minutes late. She grabbed her wand from the counter and pointed it at the cake, which immediately started depositing itself into a tin while she retrieved a cold bottle of white wine from the fridge. 
当她跑回厨房时，又看了一眼时钟，赫敏发现她只迟到了二十分钟。她从柜台上拿出魔杖对准蛋糕，蛋糕立即开始放入罐子里，同时她从冰箱里拿出一瓶冰凉的白葡萄酒。

After a final cursory inspection of her kitchen and double checking that the oven was off, Hermione bustled towards her living room fireplace, cake and wine bundled in her arms.
在最后粗略地检查了她的厨房并仔细检查了烤箱是否关闭后，赫敏匆匆忙忙地走向她客厅的壁炉，怀里掏着蛋糕和葡萄酒。

See the end of the chapter for more notes
更多注释见本章末尾A happy, wailing James Potter was the first thing that Hermione encountered when she stepped into the Potters’ living room. Just short of two years old, he was at the point where he could walk for extended periods but he still had moments where his head threw off his balance, sending him careening forwards with dangerous speed. He was just about to go headlong into Hermione’s legs when Harry swept him off his feet and up into the air, earning himself a delighted scream. 
当赫敏踏入波特家的客厅时，她首先看到的是快乐、哀嚎的詹姆·波特。刚满两岁，他已经到了可以长时间行走的地步，但他仍然有头部失去平衡的时刻，使他以危险的速度向前冲刺。他正要一头扎进赫敏的腿上，哈利把他从脚上扫到空中，让自己高兴地尖叫起来。

Grinning as he arranged his wriggling son in his arms, Harry eyed the cake and wine in Hermione’s. “Lemon cake and wine? Oh, you are most welcome, Hermione Granger, bringer of peace and joy.”
哈利咧嘴一笑，把他扭动的儿子搂在怀里，盯着赫敏家的蛋糕和酒。“柠檬蛋糕和葡萄酒？哦，不客气，赫敏·格兰杰，和平与欢乐的带来者。

“Hello, mister,” Hermione said fondly, leaning towards James to give him a kiss. He hid his face in Harry’s neck, abashed, and Hermione laughed. 
“你好，先生，”赫敏深情地说，俯身向詹姆斯亲吻。他把脸藏在哈利的脖子上，羞愧地笑了起来。

“Sorry,” Harry grinned, clearly not sorry at all. “He’s been really attached to me this past week. Ginny’s absolutely furious about it. Keeps threatening that she’ll raise the next one to be on her team. Whatever that means.”
“对不起，”哈利咧嘴一笑，显然一点也不抱歉。“在过去的一周里，他真的很依恋我。金妮对此非常生气。不断威胁说她会培养下一个加入她团队的人。不管这意味着什么。

Turning, Harry began walking out of the room, speaking over his shoulder to her. “Ron and Ginny are in the kitchen.” Hermione trailed after Harry and, to her amusement, spied James peeking at her over his father’s shoulder. She stuck her tongue out and he ducked down again, a messy tuft of black hair and two pudgy hands the only evidence that he was there at all. 
哈利转过身来，开始走出房间，转过头对她说。“罗恩和金妮在厨房里。”赫敏跟在哈利身后，令她好笑的是，她发现詹姆斯从他父亲的肩膀上偷看她。她伸出舌头，他又弯下身子，一簇凌乱的黑发和两只胖乎乎的手是他在那里的唯一证据。

“Hermione’s here!” Harry called, pushing the door to the kitchen open. 
“赫敏来了！”哈利喊道，推开了厨房的门。

Warm greetings from Ron and Ginny met Hermione as she followed Harry into the kitchen. Before she could even register where their voices had come from, they descended on her, Ginny plucking the cake from her arms while Ron grabbed the wine.
罗恩和金妮热情地问候了赫敏，赫敏跟着哈利走进了厨房。她甚至还没反应清他们的声音是从哪里传来的，他们就向她扑来，金妮从她怀里摘下蛋糕，而罗恩则抓起酒。

“You are a gem ,” Ginny said, cradling the cake over her large belly like a practice baby. “I’ve been thinking about this all day.”
“你是一颗宝石，”金妮说，像个练习婴儿一样把蛋糕抱在她的大肚子上。“我整天都在想这个问题。”

“And I’ve been thinking about this all day,” said Ron with a fond look at the wine as he pulled glasses from a cupboard on the opposite side of the kitchen. 
“我一整天都在想这个问题，”罗恩说，一边深情地看着酒，一边从厨房对面的橱柜里拿出玻璃杯。

The Potter’s kitchen was much larger than Hermione’s but that was the benefit of having a three-bedroom house in Godric’s Hollow over a one-bedroom flat in north London. Although they had spent the first years of their marriage in Grimmauld Place, when Ginny had gotten pregnant with James she’d managed to convince Harry to leave the house he’d inherited from Sirius. 
波特家的厨房比赫敏的要大得多，但那是在戈德里克山谷有一栋三居室的房子，而不是在伦敦北部的一套一居室公寓。虽然他们结婚的最初几年都在格里莫广场度过，但当金妮怀上詹姆斯时，她设法说服哈利离开他从小天狼星那里继承的房子。

Hermione hadn’t been there for the discussion but Harry had told her that Ginny had cited the “creepy vibe” of Grimmauld Place, as well as the less-than-stellar relationships of its former family, as evidence that it was an unsuitable place to raise children. Hermione couldn’t say she disagreed with Ginny but it was, she thought, a testament to how much Harry loved his wife that he’d been willing to leave the place for her. The incompatibility of Walburga Black's portrait and sleeping children probably helped him make the decision too.
赫敏没有去那里讨论，但哈利告诉她，金妮引用了格里莫广场的“令人毛骨悚然的氛围”，以及它以前家庭不那么光彩的关系，作为证明它不适合抚养孩子的地方。赫敏不能说她不同意金妮的观点，但她想，这证明了哈利有多么爱他的妻子，他愿意为她离开这个地方。沃尔布加·布莱克 （Walburga Black） 的肖像和熟睡的孩子之间的不相容可能也帮助他做出了决定。

From Hermione’s perspective, their home in Godric’s Hollow was much more suitable. Warm and welcoming, it was as much home to her as her own flat. Perhaps more so. With a pleased sigh, Hermione sank into one of the chairs at the large table in the centre of the room. Her fingers rubbed over the well-scrubbed wood, appreciating the lack of parchment littering its surface. She wondered if it was odd that she enjoyed coming to the home of her toddler-rearing friends for its comparatively soothing neatness. 
从赫敏的角度来看，他们在戈德里克山谷的家要合适得多。这里温暖而好客，对她来说就像她自己的公寓一样。也许更重要。赫敏高兴地叹了口气，坐进了房间中央大桌子旁的一把椅子上。她的手指在擦洗过的木头上摩擦，欣赏着表面没有散落的羊皮纸。她想知道她喜欢来到她蹒跚学步的朋友们的家里，因为它相对舒缓的整洁，这是否很奇怪。

“Sorry I’m late,” she said. “I had my last meeting with Malfoy today so I ended up starting on the cake a little later than I intended.”
“对不起，我来晚了，”她说。“我今天和马尔福有最后一次会面，所以我最终开始工作的时间比我预期的要晚一点。”

A noise of disgust from just over Hermione’s shoulder signalled Ron’s presence. He set a glass of white wine in front of her before sliding into the seat to her right with his own glass. “I still can’t believe you let the ferret in your flat.”
赫敏的肩膀上传来一阵厌恶的声音，表明罗恩的存在。他把一杯白葡萄酒放在她面前，然后拿着自己的杯子滑到她右边的座位上。“我还是不敢相信你让雪貂进了你的公寓。”

“Well, where would you rather we go, Ron?” Hermione asked, picking up her wine and rolling her eyes. “Someplace public where everyone can stare at us?”
“嗯，罗恩，你希望我们去哪儿？”赫敏问道，拿起她的酒，翻了个白眼。“一个每个人都可以盯着我们看的公共场所？”

“I think having as many witnesses as possible can’t hurt,” said Ron darkly. 
“我觉得有尽可能多的证人不会有什么坏处，”罗恩阴沉地说。

“Malfoy wouldn’t dare hurt Hermione, Ron,” Ginny said from across the room, where she was lifting the lemon cake from Hermione’s tin to deposit it in one of her own.
“马尔福不敢伤害赫敏，罗恩，”金妮在房间的另一头说，她正从赫敏的罐子里拿出柠檬蛋糕，把它放进她自己的罐子里。

“Not with the eye the Auror office still has on his family,” Harry added as he struggled to settle a wriggling James into his high chair at the far end of the table.
“不是用傲罗办公室还在关注他的家人，”哈利补充道，他努力让扭动着的詹姆斯坐到桌子远端的高脚椅上。

Hermione shook her head, swallowing a large gulp of wine. It had taken a while for her friends to come to terms with her desire to interview Malfoy. She’d spent numerous weeks repeatedly explaining the purpose of their meetings and what they’d mean for her oral history. Eventually they'd accepted it. Unfortunately, they still couldn’t quite grasp the idea that she actually didn’t mind Malfoy on a personal level. 
赫敏摇摇头，吞下了一大口酒。她的朋友们花了一段时间才接受她想采访马尔福的愿望。她花了好几个星期反复解释他们见面的目的，以及他们对她的口述历史意味着什么。最终他们接受了它。不幸的是，他们仍然无法完全理解她实际上在个人层面上并不介意马尔福的想法。

The only person who seemed remotely understanding was, surprisingly, Harry, who mostly avoided outrightly criticising Draco. Hermione supposed it had something to do with the fact that he had spoken up for Malfoy and his mother at their trials following the war and liked Hermione’s assurances that he had done the right thing. But Harry didn’t often speak up when Hermione attempted to defend Draco to Ron and Ginny. She imagined he thought it wasn’t an argument worth having; Weasley and Malfoy enmity went further back than their own school days, after all.  
令人惊讶的是，唯一一个似乎完全理解的人是哈利，他基本上避免直接批评德拉科。赫敏认为这与他在战后的审判中为马尔福和他母亲发声有关，并且喜欢赫敏保证他做了正确的事情。但是当赫敏试图向罗恩和金妮为德拉科辩护时，哈利并不经常发声。她想象他认为这不是一个值得争论的争论;毕竟，韦斯莱和马尔福的敌意可以追溯到他们自己的学生时代。

“I’ve already told you, Malfoy is fine . I like spending time with him.”
“我已经跟你说过了，马尔福没事。我喜欢和他在一起。

“Mental,” muttered Ron with a shake of his head. “Absolutely mental.”
“精神上的，”罗恩摇摇头咕哝道。“绝对是精神上的。”

“Spending literal weeks of your life with someone, exploring their memories and emotions, is a highly intimate experience, Ron,” Hermione snapped. “It’s perfectly natural for some kind of empathy and mutuality to develop. You might want to try something similar sometime.”
“和某人一起度过生命中的几周，探索他们的记忆和情感，是一种非常亲密的经历，罗恩，”赫敏厉声说。“发展出某种同理心和互惠互利是很自然的。你可能想在某个时候尝试类似的东西。

Ron choked into his glass and hurriedly brushed droplets of wine from his t-shirt as Harry and Ginny snickered at him. 
罗恩呛到他的杯子里，匆匆忙忙地从他的T恤上拂去酒滴，而哈利和金妮则对他嘲笑。

“Please, Hermione,” he said, raising a palm in a plea of mercy as he coughed. “Don’t mention Malfoy and intimacy in the same sentence again. I have a highly fertile imagination.”
“求求你了，赫敏，”他说，一边咳嗽一边举起一只手掌恳求怜悯。“不要再在同一句话里提到马尔福和亲密关系了。我有非常丰富的想象力。

“Moving on ,” said Ginny, lowering into the seat across from Ron with a huff and a quelling look at Hermione, who had just opened her mouth with a very nasty look in her eye. “I’ve ordered Chinese food so I hope you weren’t hoping for a home-cooked meal tonight.”
“继续，”金妮说，气喘吁吁地坐到罗恩对面的座位上，平静地看了赫敏一眼，赫敏刚刚张开嘴，眼神里露出非常难狠的神情。“我已经点了中餐，所以我希望你今晚不要指望吃家常菜。”

Once Hermione and Ron had backed down and assured Ginny that Chinese was exactly what they wanted, the evening followed its usual routine of drinking, talking and, once the food eventually arrived, eating. 
当赫敏和罗恩让步并向金妮保证中文正是他们想要的时，这个夜晚就按照往常的惯例喝酒、聊天，一旦食物最终上来，就吃东西。

As Harry, Ron and Hermione opened a second bottle of wine and the chatter began to get too loud, James attempted to draw the room’s attention back to himself by flinging his food at Harry and screaming excitedly. It was only after Harry was hit with a sixth boiled broccoli floret, much to Ron and Ginny’s delight, that he got to his feet with a tired sigh to take his son to bed. 
当哈利、罗恩和赫敏打开第二瓶酒时，喋喋不休的声音开始变得太大声，詹姆斯试图把房间里的注意力拉回到自己身上，把食物扔向哈利，兴奋地尖叫起来。直到哈利被第六个煮熟的西兰花小花击中后，罗恩和金妮才疲惫地叹了口气，站起来，把儿子抱到床上。

“You know, Hermione,” said Ginny in a tone that Hermione found suspiciously casual given the predatory intent with which she speared a piece of chicken on her fork. “Harry told me that Terry Boot was asking about you today in the Ministry lunchroom.”
“你知道的，赫敏，”金妮说，语气让赫敏觉得很随意，因为她在叉子上刺了一块鸡肉。“哈利告诉我，特里·布特今天在魔法部的午餐室里问你。”

From the corner of her eye, Hermione saw Ron’s head bob up to look at Ginny, a long noodle dangling from his lips. 
赫敏用眼角的余光看到罗恩歪着头看着金妮，一条长长的面条从他的嘴唇上垂下来。

“The Ravenclaw?” Hermione asked with a frown. Reaching for a napkin, she passed it to Ron for his chin without even glancing at him.
“拉文克劳？”赫敏皱着眉头问道。她伸手拿起餐巾纸，递给罗恩放在他的下巴上，甚至没有看他一眼。

“That’s the one.” Ginny cast a faintly disgusted look at her brother. “Works in the Ministry’s archives, although you'll obviously already be aware of that. He asked Harry how your project is coming along and how much longer you might be on sabbatical.”
“就是那个。”金妮向她的哥哥投去淡淡的厌恶眼神。“在魔法部的档案中工作，尽管你显然已经知道了。他问 Harry 你的项目进展如何，你可能会休假多长时间。

Hermione took a sip of wine, her eyes narrowed as she tried to see where Ginny was trying to take the conversation. “That’s...nice, I suppose?”
赫敏啜了一口酒，眯起眼睛，试图看清金妮试图把话题引向哪里。“那是......不错吧？

“It is, isn’t it?” said Ginny cheerfully. “I think you should ask him out.”
“是的，不是吗？”“我觉得你应该约他出去。”

“Ginny, no!” 
“金妮，不！”

Eyebrows raised, chin drawn down into her neck, Ginny looked back and forth between Ron and Hermione, both of whom had shouted her name at the same time. Glancing at one another, they then immediately focused on their plates as though their meals had suddenly become incredibly interesting.
金妮扬起眉毛，下巴贴在脖子上，在罗恩和赫敏之间来回打量，他们俩都同时喊着她的名字。他们互相看了一眼，然后立即专注于自己的盘子，仿佛他们的饭菜突然变得非常有趣。

“I’ll get to you in a minute,” Ginny said to Hermione, before turning to her brother with a stern look. “First, you .”
“我一会儿就来找你，”金妮对赫敏说，然后转身用严厉的眼神看向她的哥哥。“首先，你。”

Ron audibly gulped as Ginny raised a finger to point at him from across the table. “It’s none of your business who Hermione asks out, Ron Weasley. You two aren’t going out; you tried and it was a disaster. In fact, I don’t know if Hannah—your current girlfriend , remember?—would be all that pleased to hear that you’re having a jealous little fit over the idea of Hermione developing an interest in someone else.”
罗恩大口大口地喝了一口水，金妮从桌子对面举起一根手指指向他。“赫敏约谁不关你的事，罗恩·韦斯莱。你们俩不出去;你试过了，结果是一场灾难。事实上，我不知道汉娜——你现在的女朋友，还记得吗——听到你对赫敏对别人产生兴趣的想法感到嫉妒。

“It’s nothing to do with jealousy ,” Ron muttered, his ears and neck rapidly reddening. “It’s just...it’s Terry Boot, innit? Bit of a drip. Think Hermione could do with someone that’s got a bit... more to them.”
“这和嫉妒没关系，”罗恩咕哝着，他的耳朵和脖子很快就红了起来。“只是......是 Terry Boot，innit？有点滴。想想赫敏可以和一个有点...... 对他们来说更多。

Hermione couldn’t help the fond smile that Ron’s words brought to her face and she gently elbowed him in the side. He shifted away, embarrassed. 
赫敏忍不住露出罗恩的话给她带来的深情微笑，她轻轻地用手肘碰了碰他的侧面。他尴尬地移开了。

They had tried a relationship immediately after the war but it just hadn’t worked out for them. A combination of extreme busyness in the rebuilding efforts, Ron’s staunch certainty about his plans for the future and Hermione’s dissatisfaction with her present had led to their relationship falling apart after four years. It had been extremely difficult but, since then, Ron had started seeing Hannah Abbot and, as far as Hermione could tell, he was very happy with her. 
他们在战后立即尝试过一段关系，但对他们来说就是没有成功。重建工作的极度忙碌，罗恩对未来计划的坚定把握，以及赫敏对她现在的不满，导致他们的关系在四年后分崩离析。这非常困难，但从那以后，罗恩开始见到汉娜·艾伯特，据赫敏所知，他对她非常满意。

At first, it had been odd for Hermione to see Ron with someone else but she’d come to notice that Ron and Hannah were never impatient or aggravated with one another the way she and Ron had often been. In the immediate aftermath of their breakup, Hermione had been keen to lay the blame for all of their arguments solely at Ron’s feet, citing his short fuse and general argumentativeness. But seeing how calm and patient he was with Hannah had made Hermione realise that the fault couldn’t possibly lie with just one of them; it had simply been the way they were together as a couple. They weren’t compatible.
起初，赫敏看到罗恩和别人在一起很奇怪，但她逐渐注意到，罗恩和汉娜从来没有像她和罗恩经常那样不耐烦或生气。在他们分手后，赫敏一直热衷于将他们所有的争论都归咎于罗恩，理由是他短暂的导火索和普遍的争论。但看到他对汉娜的冷静和耐心，赫敏意识到，错不可能只在于他们中的一个;这只是他们作为一对夫妇在一起的方式。他们不兼容。

“I appreciate your concern, Ginny. Really, I do. But I don't want to ask Terry Boot out. I don’t want to ask anyone out.”
“我很感激你的关心，金妮。真的，我愿意。但我不想请 Terry Boot 出去。我不想约任何人出去。

“He won’t reject you, Hermione,” Ginny assured her with a sympathetic look. “Your hair is much better now.”
“他不会拒绝你的，赫敏，”金妮用同情的眼神向她保证。“你的头发现在好多了。”

Ron snorted into his wine as Hermione flushed a deep pink. “It’s not about rejection , Ginny. Or my hair. I just don’t have time for dating right now. I took my sabbatical from the Ministry to compile this oral history and I need to focus my efforts on finishing it. I’m coming up on two years away and Kingsley strongly hinted that was as much time as he would be willing to give me.”
罗恩哼了一声，赫敏脸红了一阵深粉色。“这不是关于拒绝的，金妮。或者我的头发。我现在没有时间约会。我从魔法部休假来编纂这段口述历史，我需要集中精力完成它。我还有两年的时间，金斯利强烈暗示这是他愿意给我的时间。

“But you told us you’ve finished your interviews with Malfoy,” Ginny pointed out hurriedly, hoping to trip Hermione up. “So, surely that frees you up a bit. You need to have some fun , Hermione. A couple of dates can’t hurt. Besides, Terry Boot is cute ! And you know that must be true because it rhymes.”
“但你告诉我们你已经完成了对马尔福的采访，”金妮急忙指出，希望能绊倒赫敏。“所以，这肯定会让你自由一点。你得找点乐子，赫敏。几次约会也无妨。此外，Terry Boot 很可爱！你知道这一定是真的，因为它押韵。

Hermione shook her head, managing to laugh at Ginny’s persistence. “No . Anyway, I might be starting a new set of interviews soon, so I have to prioritise those. I can’t be sure how much of my time they’ll take up.”
赫敏摇了摇头，勉强嘲笑了金妮的坚持。“不。无论如何，我可能很快就会开始一系列新的面试，所以我必须优先考虑这些。我不确定他们会占用我多少时间。

“More interviews?” asked Ginny, waving her fork in a fit of disbelief that sent rice flying across the table. “Who the hell else could possibly be left?”
“还有更多采访吗？”金妮问道，她难以置信地挥舞着叉子，让米饭在桌子上飞了起来。“还能留下谁？”

“Peeves?” Ron suggested. “Oh, or maybe that bloke that sells those weird little amulets outside the Three Broomsticks, you know the—”
“皮鬼？”罗恩提议道。“哦，或者是那个在三把扫帚外面卖那些奇怪的小护身符的家伙，你知道的——”

“It’s Lucius Malfoy.”
“是卢修斯·马尔福。”

The uproar was instantaneous. Ginny dropped her fork onto her plate with a clatter while Ron sloshed wine all over the table, each loudly and hastily talking over the other. There was something truly alarming, Hermione thought, about having two wide-eyed Weasleys leaning into your face, their words running together so as to be practically incomprehensible. She could only hear snippets of what they were saying but phrases like “got to be joking”, “evil bastard” and “absolutely mental ” broke through.
一片哗然瞬间就引起了。金妮咔嚓一声把叉子扔在盘子上，而罗恩则把酒洒满了桌子，两人都大声匆忙地互相交谈。赫敏想，有两个睁大眼睛的韦斯莱靠在你的脸上，他们的话语连在一起，几乎让人难以理解，这真是令人震惊。她只能听到他们所说的片段，但像 “一定是在开玩笑”、“邪恶的混蛋 ”和 “绝对精神 ”这样的短语突破了。

“What are you lot shouting about?” came Harry’s irate voice from the kitchen doorway. “I just got James to sleep so if you wake him then I will cry and that is so much worse.”
“你们这群人在喊什么？”哈利愤怒的声音从厨房门口传来。“我刚刚让詹姆斯睡着了，所以如果你叫醒他，我就会哭，情况更糟。”

Ron and Ginny turned to him, both speaking at once while Hermione looked on with her mouth slightly open. Harry held up his right hand to stop them, his left pushing up his glasses so that he could pinch the bridge of his nose. “One at a time. Please.”
罗恩和金妮转向他，两人同时说话，而赫敏微微张着嘴在一旁看着。哈利举起右手阻止他们，左手推起眼镜，这样他就可以捏住自己的鼻梁。“一次一个。 拜托了。

“Hermione is going to interview Lucius Malfoy for her oral history thingy,” Ginny finally managed to say, her cheeks pink. “Tell her how stupid and terrible that is as an idea.”
“赫敏要去采访卢修斯·马尔福，因为她是口述历史的事情，”金妮终于开口了，她的脸颊通红。“告诉她，这个主意是多么愚蠢和可怕。”

“I’m not definitely doing it,” Hermione interjected quickly. “I’m just trying to make it happen.”
“我肯定不会这么做，”赫敏迅速地打断道。“我只是想让它发生。”

“Wait, this is a thing you’re trying to force ?” asked Ron. “He doesn’t even want to do it? Hermione, are you okay ?”
“等等，这是你想强迫的事情？”“他甚至不想这样做？赫敏，你还好吗？

“I’m fine,” Hermione said through gritted teeth.
“我没事，”赫敏咬牙切齿地说。

“Honestly, Hermione, Malfoy junior was bad enough,” Ginny said, her hands cradling her stomach as though protecting her unborn child from Hermione's bad decisions, “but Malfoy senior ? I don’t remember any of those books about the Goblin Wars we read at school offering the perspective of the goblins. I mean, I don't actually really remember what those books said full stop. But the point still stands: no one wanted to hear what they had to say, so why do you want to hear what he has to say?”
“老实说，赫敏，小马尔福已经够坏了，”金妮说，她的手捂着肚子，仿佛在保护她未出生的孩子免受赫敏的错误决定，“但是老马尔福呢？我不记得我们在学校读过的那些关于哥布林战争的书中，有没有提供哥布林视角的书。我的意思是，我实际上并不记得那些书是怎么说的。但关键仍然是：没有人想听他们要说的话，那么你为什么想听他要说什么呢？

“Maybe those books should have offered that perspective,” Hermione said with a sigh. “Besides, I’ve already told you, I’m not doing this to establish a narrative. I’m doing it to record personal, contrasting perspectives side-by-side. It’ll help us create a fuller record of events. We don’t know all that much about the Death Eaters, you know, not really. His perspective would be pretty unique.”
“也许那些书应该提供那种视角，”赫敏叹了口气说。“此外，我已经告诉过你了，我这样做不是为了建立叙事。我这样做是为了并排记录个人的、对比鲜明的观点。它将帮助我们创建更完整的事件记录。我们对食死徒了解不多，你知道的，不是真的。他的观点会非常独特。

“Uniquely twisted,” muttered Ron, reaching for the bottle of wine.
“特别扭曲，”罗恩咕哝着，伸手去拿那瓶酒。

Ginny pointed at Ron. “Exactly! Why would you want his perspective? We already know how utterly evil he is; why do you need to hear it from his own slimy mouth?”
金妮指着罗恩。“正是！你为什么想要他的观点？我们已经知道他有多么邪恶;你为什么需要从他自己黏糊糊的嘴里听到呢？

“She wants his perspective because she’s Hermione. And I'm pretty sure we went over all this with the other Malfoy.” Harry spoke from the doorway with a knowing look at Hermione who mouthed her gratitude, hoping the the others wouldn't see her face. “After that, surely you both know she’s going to go ahead and do exactly what she wants regardless of how loudly you both shout at her, so give over.”
“她想要他的观点，因为她是赫敏。而且我很确定我们和另一个马尔福一起讨论过这一切。哈利从门口说，用会心的眼神看着赫敏，赫敏说着感激之情，希望其他人不要看到她的脸。“在那之后，你们肯定都知道她会继续做她想做的事，不管你们俩对她大喊大叫，所以让步吧。”

“Well, I just think that some perspectives aren’t worth having,” said Ginny. “And if he has any sense he’ll keep his foul mouth shut .” Seeing Harry looking at her with his eyebrows raised, Ginny held up her hands. “I’m done, I’m done.”
“嗯，我只是觉得有些观点不值得拥有，”金妮说。“如果他有任何理智，他就会闭上他的污言秽语。”看到哈利扬起眉毛看着她，金妮举起了手。“我完了，我完了。”

Keen for the evening to return to warm and friendly fun, Hermione elected not to tell Harry, Ron and Ginny what she was offering Malfoy to tempt him into speaking with her. There was, she felt, no point in having a bigger argument over something that might not even happen. Accepting Ron’s offer of another glass of wine, Hermione tried to ignore the unsettled feeling that was stirring low in her stomach. 
赫敏渴望让这个夜晚回到温暖友好的乐趣中，她选择不告诉哈利、罗恩和金妮她给马尔福什么东西，以诱惑他和她说话。她觉得，对于甚至可能不会发生的事情进行更大的争论是没有意义的。赫敏接受了罗恩再喝一杯酒的提议，试图忽略她胃里低处翻腾的不安情绪。

四月 15th 2006

When Draco Malfoy couldn’t find his father in his private study, the library, or the kennels, he knew he would be successful in the greenhouse. 
当德拉科·马尔福在他的私人书房、图书馆或狗窝里找不到他的父亲时，他知道自己会在温室里取得成功。

Lucius Malfoy’s world had shrunk rather dramatically when the Ministry had put him under house arrest eight years previously. He hadn’t said a word about it but Draco hadn’t failed noticed that, rather than expand to fill the sprawling manor, rather than chafe at its confines, Lucius had taken it upon himself to reduce his world even further to only a handful of rooms. Whether that was deliberate or not, Draco wasn’t sure but it never failed to make him feel slightly uncomfortable. It wasn’t the kind of reaction he’d expected from his father. It did, at least, make him easier to track down. 
卢修斯·马尔福的世界在八年前魔法部将他软禁时，已经急剧缩小了。他一句话也没说，但德拉科并没有注意到，卢修斯并没有扩大规模来填满这个庞大的庄园，也没有对它的界限感到恼火，而是主动将他的世界进一步缩小到只有几个房间。这是否是故意的，德拉科不确定，但这总是让他感到有点不舒服。这不是他所期望的父亲会做出的那种反应。至少，这确实使他更容易被追踪。

Sure enough, when Draco opened the door to the greenhouse, stepping out of the April drizzle and into its humid heat, he heard the rustles and sighs that signalled his father’s presence. 
果然，当德拉科打开温室的门，走出四月的细雨，走进潮湿的高温中时，他听到了沙沙作响和叹息声，这表明他父亲的存在。

It had taken Draco a few days to work up the courage to pass along Granger’s request. Astoria had been very taken with the idea, agreeing with his instinct that it might be good for his father to talk to someone, anyone, who wasn’t them. But when Draco had tried to talk tactics about how to broach the matter with Lucius, Astoria had become impatient.
德拉科花了几天时间才鼓起勇气把格兰杰的请求转达了。阿斯托利亚对这个主意非常感兴趣，他同意他的直觉，即他的父亲与不是他们的人交谈可能是件好事。但当德拉科试图讨论如何与卢修斯讨论这件事的策略时，阿斯托利亚已经变得不耐烦了。

“He’s your father,” she’d said as though that somehow solved his problem and didn't make it more difficult. “Just talk to him.” 
“他是你的爸爸，”她说，仿佛这以某种方式解决了他的问题，并没有让事情变得更困难。“跟他谈谈就好。”

As though it was that easy. The Greengrasses had always been a curiously communicative family. For Pure-bloods, anyway. Most of the time, Draco appreciated the positive influence that Astoria’s relatively pleasant upbringing brought to their own relationship; thanks to her insistence, they talked to one another, shared things. Against his expectations, the openness made him happier and, as far as he was concerned, better. But when she tried to encourage him to take the same approach with his father, he wondered how much she actually paid attention to, or understood, the family she had married into.
好像就这么简单。格林格拉斯一家一直是一个善于交流的家庭。无论如何，对于纯血统来说。大多数时候，德拉科很欣赏阿斯托利亚相对愉快的成长经历给他们自己的关系带来的积极影响;多亏了她的坚持，他们彼此交谈，分享东西。出乎他意料的是，这种开放让他更快乐，对他来说，这让他变得更好。但是，当她试图鼓励他对他的父亲采取同样的方法时，他想知道她实际上有多关注或理解她嫁入的这个家庭。

Ducking under damp hanging leaves and stepping around green tentacles that wriggled threateningly when he veered too close, Draco eventually found his father hunched over a workstation in the centre of the greenhouse. On hearing his son’s footsteps approaching, Lucius looked up from the notes he was taking.
Draco 躲在潮湿的垂叶下，绕过绿色的触手，当他转向太近时，这些触手会威胁性地蠕动，最终发现他的父亲正弯着腰坐在温室中央的一个工作站上。听到儿子的脚步声靠近，卢修斯从他正在记下的笔记中抬起头来。

“Draco,” he said in greeting, straightening up and setting his quill down. The stiffness of his tone was only ever matched by the stiffness of his posture these days.
“德拉科，”他打招呼说，直起身来放下他的羽毛笔。如今，他语气的僵硬与他的姿势僵硬相得益彰。

“Father,” Draco nodded and, hands in his pockets, approached the workstation to peer down at his father’s neat notes.
“爸爸，”德拉科点点头，双手插在口袋里，走近工作台，低头看了看他爸爸那整齐的笔记。

“The asphodel is coming along well,” Lucius said, pointing to a series of measurements he had recorded with accompanying scaled diagrams.
“水仙子进展顺利，”卢修斯说，指着他记录的一系列测量结果和随附的比例图。

After a quick glance at Lucius for permission, Draco slid the parchment towards himself so that he could read it better. He found he couldn’t entirely take it in—his mind was mostly occupied with how the hell he was going to ask his father to talk to Granger. 
德拉科快速看了一眼卢修斯，请求允许后，将羊皮纸滑向自己，以便他能更好地阅读。他发现自己无法完全理解——他的脑子里大部分时间都放在了他到底要如何让他的父亲和格兰杰谈谈。

Lucius hadn’t been best pleased when Draco had revealed his intention to take part in Granger’s project. The arguments had been numerous, long and, to Astoria’s exasperation, eventually rather loud. But, in the end, Lucius Malfoy had been forced to realise that it was no longer in his power to stop his son doing what he wanted. It hadn’t— still didn’t—sit well.  
卢修斯对德拉科透露他打算参与格兰杰的项目感到不高兴。争论很多次，很长，而且，令阿斯托利亚恼火的是，最终相当响亮。但是，到头来，卢修斯·马尔福被迫意识到，他已经没有能力阻止他的儿子为所欲为了。它没有——仍然没有——坐好。

“You’re right,” Draco murmured, sliding the parchment back across the workbench. “It won’t be long before I can collect it for my potions.”
“你说得对，”德拉科喃喃自语，一边把羊皮纸滑回工作台上。“用不了多久，我就可以收集它来制作我的魔药了。”

Lucius nodded and stepped back to remove the protective apron he wore while working in the greenhouse. Draco couldn’t help but shake his head when his father’s smart white shirt and suit trousers were revealed. He couldn’t count how many times he’d tried to tell Lucius that he might find casual clothes more comfortable for his work in the greenhouse but, without fail, his father would look down at what he was wearing and snap that it was casual. Probably because it didn’t involve a cravat. There was, Draco supposed, some comfort to be found in his father’s insistence in retaining his dress habits. He could take them as a sign that he didn’t have to worry that much.
卢修斯点点头，向后退一步，取下了他在温室工作时穿的防护围裙。当他爸爸的时髦白衬衫和西装裤被揭露时，德拉科忍不住摇了摇头。他数不清有多少次他试图告诉卢修斯，他可能会觉得休闲装更适合他在温室里工作，但毫无疑问，他的父亲会低头看他穿的衣服，说这是休闲装。可能是因为它不涉及领结。德拉科想，从他父亲坚持保持他的着装习惯中可以找到一些安慰。他可以把这些看作是他不必那么担心的标志。

“I will let you know when it’s ready,” Lucius said, neatly folding his apron and slotting it into a shelf under the workbench.
“等它准备好了，我会告诉你的，”卢修斯说，整齐地折叠他的围裙，把它塞进工作台下的架子里。

“Thank you, father. Are you sure I can’t help—”
“谢谢你，爸爸。你确定我帮不上忙吗——”

“Draco,” Lucius interrupted, his tone terse, “as I have told you multiple times: I do not require your assistance. I may not be able to use my magic anymore but I can still do this .” 
“德拉科，”卢修斯打断了他，语气简洁，“我已经告诉过你好几次了：我不需要你的帮助。我可能无法再使用我的魔法了，但我仍然可以做到这一点。

Draco swallowed his urge to ask his father if he’d ever considered that working in the greenhouse might be something they could do together as equals, without any implication that one of them was any more or less skilled than the other. But he knew he would be wasting his breath. The Magic Dampener had wounded his father’s pride and, as yet, Draco had not found a way to heal it that did not involve simply staying out of his way for prolonged periods.
德拉科忍住了自己的冲动，问他爸爸，他有没有想过在温室里工作可能是他们可以平等地一起做的事情，而没有任何暗示他们中的一个比另一个更熟练或更不熟练。但他知道他会浪费呼吸。魔法阻尼器已经伤害了他父亲的自尊心，到目前为止，德拉科还没有找到一种不涉及长时间不挡他的路的方法来治愈它。

Wearing a frown, Lucius began unrolling his shirt sleeves from their position at his elbows, picking up his cufflinks from where he’d left them on the table. “Why are you here, Draco?”
卢修斯皱着眉头，开始从肘部的位置解开衬衫袖子，从他放在桌子上的地方捡起他的袖扣。“你为什么在这里，德拉科？”

It was hard not to sigh. Couldn’t he just be coming to see his father? Was that really so hard for him to consider?
很难不叹息。他就不能来看他的爸爸吗？这对他来说真的很难考虑吗？

“I finished my meetings with Granger.”
“我结束了与格兰杰的会议。”

“Why,” Lucius drawled, inserting his second cufflink and pulling his sleeve straight with what Draco perceived to be an unnecessary sharpness, “do you think that would be of any interest to me?”
“为什么，”卢修斯抽出手，插上他的第二个袖扣，用德拉科认为不必要的尖锐方式拉直了他的袖子，“你觉得这会引起我的兴趣吗？

“Well, you were so concerned over my decision to take part in them, I thought you might be pleased to know that they’re over and that they actually went very well.”
“嗯，你对我参加比赛的决定如此担心，我想你可能会很高兴知道他们已经结束了，而且他们实际上进行得非常顺利。”

Lucius tsked and stepped around Draco, heading in the direction of the exit with surprising speed. “I would have been pleased had they not taken place at all. As it is, I care as little about how those meetings went as you cared about my opinion on them.”
卢修斯啧了一声，绕过德拉科，以惊人的速度朝着出口的方向走去。“如果它们根本没有发生，我会很高兴。事实上，我并不关心那些会议的进展情况，就像你关心我对它们的看法一样。

Whacking a hanging leaf out of his face and ducking under another, Draco followed his father. They were getting off to a bad start. “Are you really just not going to tell me that she’s been sending you owls for weeks?”
Draco从脸上捶下一片挂叶，躲在另一片树叶下，跟着他的父亲走。他们的开局很糟糕。“你真的不打算告诉我她已经给你送了好几个星期的猫头鹰了吗？”

“Why would I?”
“我为什么呢？”

“Well, you might find that talking about it is a better approach than marching around the manor wearing a scowl as you have been.”
“嗯，你可能会发现谈论这件事比像以前那样皱着眉头在庄园里走来走去要好。”

They exited the mugginess of the greenhouse and Draco appreciatively gulped down the cool, fresh spring air. Lucius stopped abruptly and turned to face Draco with his arms crossed.
他们走出了闷热的温室，德拉科感激地大口大口地呼吸着凉爽、清新的春天空气。卢修斯突然停下脚步，转身面对双臂交叉的德拉科。

“She will give up.”
“她会放弃的。”

Draco barked out a laugh. “You don’t know Hermione Granger.”
德拉科大笑起来。“你不了解赫敏·格兰杰。”

“And I do not want to,” Lucius snapped. “I’m not like you and Astoria; I am not willing to lower myself.”
“我不想，”卢修斯厉声说。“我不像你和阿斯托利亚;我不愿意降低自己。

“I have not lowered myself.” 
“我没有降低自己。”

“We will agree to disagree. As ever, these days.”
“我们会同意不同意。这些天一如既往。

Lucius spun on his heel and began to make his way through the grounds and back towards the manor. With an aggravated tut , Draco followed him, increasing his pace to a light jog to catch up and keep up.
卢修斯转身，开始穿过地面，回到庄园。德拉科恼怒地啧啧了一声，跟在他后面，加快了他的步伐，以轻快的慢跑来追上并跟上。

“She asked me to talk to you,” Draco said, just about managing to stop himself from reaching out to grab his father’s elbow. That would take them from bad to worse. “About taking part in her project.”
“她让我和你谈谈，”德拉科说，几乎要设法阻止自己伸手抓住他父亲的胳膊肘。这将使他们变得更糟。“关于参加她的项目。”

“My son: the Mudblood’s messenger. How wonderful. You can’t imagine my pride.”
“我的儿子：泥巴种的信使。多么美妙。你无法想象我的骄傲。

“Don’t call her that,” Draco said, coming up alongside Lucius. The light spring rain had started again and Draco impatiently brushed a damp lock of hair away from his forehead, glaring at the side of his father’s resolute and stony face.
“别这么叫她，”德拉科说，走到卢修斯身边。小春雨又开始了，德拉科不耐烦地拂去额头上的一缕湿漉漉的头发，瞪着他父亲坚毅而坚硬的脸庞。

“It’s what she is.”
“这就是她。”

“It’s not—she’s not—she’s not what that word means.”
“不是——她不是——她不是那个词的意思。”

Lucius did nothing more than scoff, his eyes fixed on the looming manor. It was clear he seemed to think that if he could just get inside, he’d be able to shake Draco off and end their conversation. Draco had no intention of letting him do that.
卢修斯只做了些嘲笑，他的眼睛盯着若隐若现的庄园。很明显，他似乎在想，如果他能进去，他就能把德拉科甩开，结束他们的谈话。德拉科无意让他那样做。

“She wants to interview you like she interviewed me,” Draco pressed.
“她想像采访我一样采访你，”德拉科追问道。

“I don’t care what she wants.”
“我不在乎她想要什么。”

“Fine then,” Draco snapped, his patience utterly frayed. “ I want her to interview you.”
“那就好，”德拉科厉声说，他的耐心完全被磨碎了。“我想让她采访你。”

They reached the entrance to the manor and Lucius stopped, forcing Draco to almost trip over his own feet to avoid crashing into the back of him. Lucius turned to look at his son and though he didn’t say ‘I don’t care what you want’, Draco had a feeling it was on the tip of his tongue. He found he was actually grateful that his father had managed to find it in himself to swallow the words. 
他们来到了庄园的入口，卢修斯停了下来，迫使德拉科差点被自己的脚绊倒，以免撞到他的后背。卢修斯转头看向他的儿子，虽然他没有说“我不在乎你想要什么”，但德拉科有一种感觉，这在他的舌尖上。他发现他其实很感激他的父亲设法在自己身上找到了吞下这些话的能力。

“What harm can it do to speak to her?” Draco asked, imploring.
“跟她说话有什么害处？”德拉科恳求地问。

“A great deal of harm, Draco. Are you really so naive?” Lucius asked, his eyes narrowing. “Our name is tarnished enough as it is. I will not allow some spiteful little Mudblood to take my words and twist them into whatever shape suits her for her book of post-war glorification.”
“伤害很大，德拉科。你真的这么天真吗？卢修斯眯起眼睛问道。“我们的名字已经被玷污得够厉害了。我不会允许一些恶毒的小泥巴种把我的话歪曲成任何适合她战后荣耀之书的形状。

“Granger wouldn’t do that. I’ve already told you that’s not what she’s trying to do. She’s not like the Prophet hacks that were snooping around, she’s…honourable.” The word sounded ridiculously old-fashioned to Draco’s ears but, really, that’s exactly what Granger was.
“格兰杰不会那样做。我已经告诉过你，那不是她想做的事情。她不像那些四处窥探的先知黑客，她是......尊敬的。这个词在德拉科的耳朵里听起来很老套，但实际上，这正是格兰杰的本质。

A mocking smile, closer to a sneer, crawled its way onto Lucius’ face. “Does dear Astoria know you defend the Granger girl so passionately ?”
一个嘲讽的笑容，更接近于冷笑，爬上了卢修斯的脸。“亲爱的阿斯托利亚知道你如此热情地保护格兰杰女孩吗？”

“Don’t try to change the subject by twisting my association with Granger into something it isn’t,” Draco said, his hands curling into fists. “She wants to record your words exactly. She’s not got an agenda.”
“不要试图通过扭曲我和格兰杰的联系来改变话题，”德拉科说，他的手蜷缩成拳头。“她想把你的话准确地记录下来。她没有议程。

Eyes rolling, as though he could hardly bear to hear what he was hearing, Lucius drawled, “ Everyone has an agenda, Draco.”
卢修斯翻了个白眼，仿佛几乎不忍心听到他所听到的，他抽了抽，“每个人都有议程，德拉科。

“No. She’s thorough, she’s...honest. She’s Granger . This is just the kind of thing she does.” 
“不。她很彻底，她......诚实。她是格兰杰。她就是这样做的。

There was a pause in which Lucius considered his son with a mildly nauseated expression. “I am not interested and I am not willing to discuss this further.”
停顿了一下，卢修斯用略带恶心的表情看着他的儿子。“我不感兴趣，也不愿意进一步讨论这个问题。”

As Lucius turned to enter the manor, Draco reached out, stopping just short of touching Lucius’ back. “If you help her, she’ll help you.”
当卢修斯转身进入庄园时，德拉科伸出手来，在碰到卢修斯的背之前停了下来。“如果你帮助她，她也会帮助你。”

Lucius dropped his hand from the door. His raised shoulders spoke to his reluctance as he fractionally turned his head to the side to look at his son out of the corner of his eye. “How could she possibly help me ?”
卢修斯把手从门上放了下来。他抬起的肩膀说出了他的不情愿，他微微地把头转向一边，用眼角的余光看着他的儿子。“她怎么可能帮我？”

“She said she’d talk to Shacklebolt about reducing your sentence. Maybe even getting your wand back. Don’t you want that?”
“她说她会和 Shacklebolt 谈谈减刑的事情。甚至可能拿回你的魔杖。你不想要那个吗？

Lucius huffed out a disbelieving little laugh and dropped his head so that he was gazing down at his perfectly polished leather shoes. “And you honestly think that she could manage that?”
卢修斯难以置信地笑了起来，低下头，低头凝视着他那双擦得完美的皮鞋。“你真的觉得她能办到吗？”

“She’s a war hero who fought alongside the Minister for Magic himself. If I were you, I wouldn’t make any assumptions about what Hermione Granger can and cannot manage. She’s in a better position than either of us to plead your case.”
“她是一位与魔法部长本人并肩作战的战争英雄。如果我是你，我不会对赫敏·格兰杰能做什么和不能做什么做出任何假设。她比我们中的任何一个人都更适合为你辩护。

There was a pause in which Draco stared at the back of his father's head. It was about as useful as looking at his face given the uncompromising impassivity that had taken residence there.
德拉科盯着他父亲的后脑勺停顿了一下。这和看着他的脸一样有用，因为那里已经占据了不妥协的冷漠。

“Write to her,” Draco said with a sigh and a shake of his head. “Just...see what she has to say.”
“写信给她，”德拉科叹了口气，摇了摇头说。“只是......看看她怎么说。

With a cursory look over his shoulder that took in his son’s increasingly lank hair and the imploring tilt to his eyebrows, Lucius entered the manor without another word. Draco waited several minutes before following him. 
卢修斯粗略地回头看了一眼，注意到儿子越来越稀疏的头发和恳求的眉毛，一言不发地走进了庄园。德拉科等了几分钟才跟着他。

His father was bitter, lonely and frustrated, he reminded himself in an attempt to soothe his temper. He lashed out because he had too much pride to do anything else. Granger would have her work cut out if she ever got close enough to start it.
他的父亲痛苦、孤独和沮丧，他提醒自己，试图平息自己的脾气。他猛烈抨击是因为他太骄傲了，不敢做任何其他事情。如果格兰杰离得足够近，可以开始这项工作，她的工作就会被淘汰。

Hermione dropped her parchment onto the sofa cushion beside her and rubbed her eyes. Glancing down at her watch, she saw it was getting close to midnight. That meant she’d been working on editing Kingsley’s interviews for four hours. No wonder there was a pain forming in the back of her head. And the front. And the sides. 
赫敏把羊皮纸丢在旁边的沙发垫上，揉了揉眼睛。她低头看了一眼手表，发现已经接近午夜了。这意味着她已经花了四个小时来编辑金斯利的采访。难怪她的后脑勺会感到疼痛。还有前面。还有侧面。

Exhaling, she rolled her shoulders and dropped her neck back to rest it against the sofa, staring at the speckled white plaster of her ceiling. The idea of getting up and going through her pre-bed routine felt like too much. It was far more tempting to just move her parchment to the coffee table and curl up on her side. As she debated with herself over just how much more comfortable her bed really was, Hermione heard a soft tapping at her living room window. Rolling her head to the side, she saw the glowing orange eyes of an owl peering through the glass. 
她呼出一口气，转动肩膀，把脖子向后垂，靠在沙发上，盯着天花板上斑驳的白色石膏。起床并完成她的睡前例行公事的想法感觉太过分了。把她的羊皮纸移到咖啡桌上，蜷缩在一边要诱人得多。当她和自己争论她的床到底舒服了多少时，赫敏听到客厅的窗户轻轻敲打。她把头转向一边，看到一只猫头鹰闪闪发光的橙色眼睛透过玻璃窥视着。

Blinking away the blurred vision caused by her prolonged intense focus, Hermione rose to her feet and approached the window, opening the latch to slide it up. Cool night air blew into the room, raising goosebumps on her arms as the owl hopped over the threshold and spread its large wings to soar onto her coffee table.
赫敏眨了眨眼，驱散了她长时间集中注意力造成的模糊视线，站起身来，走近窗户，打开门闩，将窗户滑上去。凉爽的夜风吹进房间，当猫头鹰跳过门槛，张开大翅膀翱翔到她的咖啡桌上时，她的手臂起了鸡皮疙瘩。

It was an eagle owl that she didn’t recognise, with a plumage that was unusually pale for the species. It was far too well-cared and well-behaved to be a post office owl. Standing on the center of her table, giving her an imperious look, it held out a leg bearing a scroll of parchment. Approaching slowly, Hermione gently untied the parchment and, with one more questioning glance up at the owl, split the wax seal to unfurl it.
这是一只她不认识的雕鸮，它的羽毛对这个物种来说异常苍白。它太被照顾了，也太乖巧了，不可能是一只邮局的猫头鹰。它站在桌子的中央，专横地看着她，伸出一条腿，上面放着一卷羊皮纸。赫敏慢慢地走近，轻轻地解开羊皮纸，又疑惑地抬头看了猫头鹰一眼，劈开蜡封，展开了它。

“Miss Granger,
“格兰杰小姐，

I do not appreciate you press ganging my son into the army of owls you have recruited to harass me these past weeks. I am not interested in your project or its aims, whatever they may be. If you are trying to appeal to my better nature, you are not going about it the right way. Desist.
我不感激你强迫我的儿子加入你在过去几周招募来骚扰我的猫头鹰大军。我对你的项目或它的目标不感兴趣，无论它们是什么。如果你试图迎合我更好的本性，那你就没有以正确的方式去做。停止。

Lucius A. Malfoy”
卢修斯·马尔福”

Hermione’s grip on the parchment tightened as she scanned its contents. Better nature ? Who was he kidding? Lowering it, she fixed her attention on the glaring owl.
赫敏在扫描羊皮纸上的内容时握得更紧了。 更好的自然 ？他在开谁玩笑？放下它，她把注意力集中在那只瞪着眼睛的猫头鹰身上。

“ Wait ,” she said to it, dropping the parchment to spring across the hall into the kitchen, her socks sliding on the tiled floor. Snatching a leaf of parchment, her quill and some ink from the table, she returned to the living room, relieved to see that the owl had listened. 
“等等，”她对它说，扔下羊皮纸，穿过走廊跳进厨房，她的袜子在瓷砖地板上滑动。她从桌子上抓起一张羊皮纸、羽毛笔和一些墨水，回到客厅，看到猫头鹰听了，她松了一口气。

“I’ll be two seconds,” she promised, holding up two fingers. The owl clicked its beak haughtily and reluctantly hopped to the side to give her room as she lowered herself to her knees in front of the coffee table to scrawl a hasty reply. 
“我等两秒钟，”她承诺道，举起两根手指。猫头鹰傲慢地咔嚓咔嚓地咔嚓咔嚓地喙，不情愿地跳到一边让给她空间，同时她跪在咖啡桌前，匆匆地回答。

“Mr Malfoy,
“马尔福先生，

If you weren’t interested in what I have to say, we both know you would have simply continued to ignore me. And I’m fairly sure your owl would have ignored my request to stay.”
如果你对我要说的话不感兴趣，我们都知道你只会继续无视我。而且我相当确定你的猫头鹰会无视我留下来的请求。

Out of her corner of her eyes, Hermione could see the owl was looking down at her parchment, and wondered if it could read what she was writing. 
赫敏用眼角的余光看到猫头鹰正低头看着她的羊皮纸，想知道它是否能读懂她在写什么。

“I can only assume that Draco told you what I’m willing to offer you in exchange for your cooperation and that you wish to have it in writing by my own hand. I would like to interview you and I am willing to advocate to the Minister on your behalf for some kind of respite in your sentence. I would prefer to discuss this in person and ask you to please consider a meeting. You do not need to give me your final answer now.
“我只能假设德拉科告诉你，我愿意给你什么来换取你的合作，而且你希望我亲手把它写成。我想采访你，我愿意代表你向部长寻求某种缓刑。我更愿意亲自讨论这个问题，并请您考虑召开一次会议。你现在不需要给我最后的答案。

Regards,
问候

Hermione J. Granger.”
赫敏·格兰杰。

On seeing her pleading face, the owl held out its leg in a way that made Hermione think that if it could have rolled its eyes in disdain, it would have. It was, however, extremely still and patient as her shaking hands fumbled with the parchment. 
看到她恳求的脸，猫头鹰伸出腿，让赫敏觉得，如果它能轻蔑地翻白眼，它就会这样做。然而，当她颤抖的手摸索着羊皮纸时，它却是极其静止和耐心的。

Once the owl had departed, Hermione exhaled slowly and sank from her knees onto her backside on the floor, leaning her back against the base of the sofa. Lucius Malfoy was surely interested, surely . He wouldn’t have written otherwise. Resting her forearms on her knees, Hermione turned her gaze to the still-open window. There was no point in her going to bed now; she had to wait for a reply. He would reply.
猫头鹰一走，赫敏慢慢地呼出一口气，从膝盖上沉到地板上的背上，背靠在沙发的底座上。卢修斯·马尔福肯定很感兴趣，肯定。他不会写其他东西。赫敏将前臂放在膝盖上，将目光转向仍然敞开的窗户。她现在上床睡觉已经没有意义了;她不得不等待回复。他会回答。

Hermione wasn’t sure how long passed but when the owl swooped back through her open window, she sat up straight and clambered onto her feet. With a baleful look, the owl held out its leg. Unfurling the parchment, Hermione hungrily read the brief reply.
赫敏不确定过了多久，但当猫头鹰从她敞开的窗户猛扑回来时，她坐直了身子，爬了起来。猫头鹰一脸恶毒地伸出了腿。展开羊皮纸，赫敏如饥似渴地阅读着简短的回复。

“ April 27th. 2pm. The Manor.” 
“4 月 27 日。下午 2 点，庄园。

Eyebrow raised, she peered at the owl. “Well, I’m not really sure how I’m supposed to reply to that,” she said, holding the parchment up for it to read, “are you?”
她扬起眉毛，凝视着猫头鹰。“嗯，我不太确定我该怎么回答，”她说，一边举起羊皮纸让它读起来，“你是吗？

With a hoot, the owl spread its wings and took off out the window. Still holding the parchment, Hermione slid the window closed behind it and then bent her head to re-read what Malfoy had written. Rude , she thought, her lips pursed. Not that that was surprising. She could tell the full stops—an impressive amount of them relative to the number of words he had written—appeared to have been almost stabbed into the parchment. It was remarkable his quill hadn’t pierced through. But she had his interest and if she got what she wanted, he could be as rude as he liked.
猫头鹰吼了一声，张开了翅膀，飞出了窗外。赫敏仍然拿着羊皮纸，把窗户关上，然后低下头重新读了一遍马尔福写的东西。 粗鲁，她想，抿起嘴唇。这并不奇怪。她能看出那些句号——相对于他写的字数来说，这个句号的数量相当可观——似乎几乎被刺进了羊皮纸。值得注意的是，他的羽毛笔没有刺穿。但她有他的兴趣，如果她得到了她想要的，他可以随心所欲地粗鲁。
