April 27th 
4 月 27 日

Hermione was nervous. Nervous enough that the entire morning before her meeting with Lucius Malfoy was a write-off. Every time she tried to focus on writing or reading, her mind wandered to Malfoy Manor. It would be the first time she’d been there since…well, since the last time. The time when her friends had been locked in the dungeon and she had been pulled by her hair onto the drawing room floor to be tortured by Bellatrix Lestrange. The faint scar on Hermione’s forearm itched at the memory. 
赫敏很紧张。她紧张到她与卢修斯·马尔福会面前的整个上午都被注销了。每次她试图专注于写作或阅读时，她的思绪都会飘向马尔福庄园。这将是她从那以后第一次来这里......嗯，自从上次以来。她的朋友们被锁在地牢里，她被拽着头发拉到客厅的地板上，被贝拉特里克斯·莱斯特兰奇折磨。赫敏前臂上淡淡的伤疤在回忆中发痒。

Whenever Hermione thought she was at risk of becoming overwhelmed by the memory of that night, she liked to close her eyes and recount the key gains they’d made out of it—the location of the cup, the help of Griphook, the loyalty of the Elder Wand. It didn’t make the memories go away, it didn’t make what had happened to her any better, but re-framing it made it easier for her to breathe. In the waking hours, at least. Getting a rational grip on nightmares was a little more difficult. 
每当赫敏觉得自己有可能被那天晚上的记忆所淹没时，她就会闭上眼睛，讲述他们从中得到的关键收获——杯子的位置，拉环的帮助，老魔杖的忠诚。这并没有让记忆消失，也没有让发生在她身上的事情变得更好，但重新构建它让她更容易呼吸。至少在醒着的时候。理性地控制噩梦有点困难。

Hermione wondered if Lucius Malfoy had chosen 2pm with an ulterior motive—it was a time that was preceded by just enough waking hours to allow her to sink into dread. Depositing her barely-eaten lunch on the kitchen counter, she glanced up at the clock for what might have been the sixth or seventh time that hour. Almost time.
赫敏想知道卢修斯·马尔福选择下午2点是不是别有用心——在那之前，她醒着的时间刚好足以让她陷入恐惧。她把几乎没吃完的午餐放在厨房的柜台上，抬头看了一眼时钟，这可能是那个小时的第六次或第七次了。差不多时间了。

As much to distract herself as anything, Hermione walked through to her living room and hauled her bulky, worn leather satchel onto the coffee table, opening it to inspect its contents. She had her Quick Quotes Quill, spare parchment, a fresh Wheezebox, a Muggle notebook and pen, and three books in case she found herself somewhere with time to read. She wasn’t expecting to interview Lucius Malfoy on their first meeting but it never hurt to be prepared. 
为了分散自己的注意力，赫敏走进她的客厅，把她笨重、破旧的皮包拖到咖啡桌上，打开它检查里面的东西。她有她的快速报价羽毛笔、备用羊皮纸、一个新的喘息盒、一个麻瓜笔记本和钢笔，还有三本书，以防她有时间阅读。她没想到会在他们的第一次见面时采访卢修斯·马尔福，但做好准备从来没有坏处。

What she didn’t have was any kind of offer from Kingsley. Given Lucius Malfoy had only offered her a week between contact and meeting, it was nigh on impossible that she’d manage to get a meeting with the Minister for Magic at such short notice. Perhaps the elder Malfoy knew that would be the case, or hoped it would. Hermione had, however, been able to secure a meeting for the day after so, depending on how things went, she knew she had that to dangle in front of him.
她没有得到的是金斯利的任何形式的提议。鉴于卢修斯·马尔福只给她提供了一周的接触和会面时间，她几乎不可能在这么短的时间内与魔法部长会面。也许老马尔福知道会是这样，或者希望会这样。然而，赫敏已经能够安排第二天的会议，所以，根据事情的进展，她知道她有这个机会在他面前悬着。

When the time approached a quarter to, Hermione took a fortifying deep breath and left her flat, apparating from outside her front door to the gate outside Malfoy Manor as Draco had instructed. 
当时间接近四分之一时，赫敏深吸了一口气，离开了她的公寓，按照德拉科的指示，从她的前门外幻影来到马尔福庄园外的大门。

The morning after receiving his father’s letter, she had written to thank him. His reply had expressed little but surprise. Clearly, she thought, he hadn’t expected he would be successful but he had given her more comprehensive instructions on how to get to the manor. 
收到他父亲的信后的第二天早上，她写信感谢他。他的回答除了惊讶之外，几乎没有什么表情。显然，她想，他没想到自己会成功，但他已经给了她更全面的指示，告诉她如何到达庄园。

The wrought iron gates were an unfriendly early impression but, as Draco had promised, when Hermione informed them of her name and the purpose of her visit, they swung open. Without any ominous creaking, incredibly. 
这些锻铁门给人的早期印象很不友好，但正如德拉科所承诺的那样，当赫敏告诉他们她的名字和她来此的目的时，它们就打开了。令人难以置信的是，没有任何不祥的吱吱声。

The gravel drive stretched out in front of her and Hermione was grateful that the April cloud and rain had broken to reveal a spotlessly blue sky and beaming sun. Sliding her light jacket from her shoulders, she slung it over her satchel and began her walk. 
碎石路在她面前延伸，赫敏很庆幸四月的乌云和雨水已经打破，露出一尘不染的蓝天和灿烂的阳光。她从肩膀上脱下轻便的夹克，把它挂在书包上，开始走路。

The grass on either side of her was absurdly green and she would have been amazed if magic wasn’t somehow involved in its care. The same went for the exquisitely shaped hedges that lined the drive. As she moved further from the front gate, Hermione found, looking left and right, that the walls that surrounded the grounds disappeared from view. She could have fooled herself into thinking she was in an open park, were it not for the enormous manor looming ahead of her. 
她两边的草都是荒谬的绿色，如果不是魔法以某种方式参与照顾它，她会感到惊讶。车道两旁形状精美的树篱也是如此。当她从前门走得更远时，赫敏发现，左右看了看，包围着院子的墙壁已经从视线中消失了。她本可以自欺欺人地以为自己在一个开放的公园里，如果不是眼前是一座巨大的庄园。

A rustle from a hedge ahead made Hermione stop short, her breath held and her hand clutching the strap of her bag. With a shrill trill, a large bird came strutting out in front of her. It was, she realised with a perplexed blink, a peacock. It was snow white, almost glowing, and Hermione gaped as it passed her by without a single glance in her direction.
前方树篱传来的沙沙声让赫敏停了下来，她屏住了呼吸，手紧紧抓住了包的带子。随着一声尖锐的颤音，一只大鸟昂首阔步地出现在她面前。她困惑地眨了眨眼，意识到那是一只孔雀。它是雪白的，几乎发光，赫敏目瞪口呆地看着它从她身边经过，没有看她一眼。

It wasn’t until the peacock had disappeared completely from her view that Hermione continued her walk, her head shaking in wonder. It somehow made so much sense to her that Draco Malfoy had been raised in a house where playing in the front garden could lead to an unfortunate encounter with a territorial and aggressive species of bird. No wonder he was so insistent about which mug he used.
直到孔雀完全从她的视线中消失后，赫敏才继续走着，她的头惊奇地摇了摇。不知何故，德拉科·马尔福是在一所房子里长大的，在前花园玩耍可能会导致不幸地遇到一种有领地意识和攻击性的鸟类。难怪他对自己用的杯子如此执着。

Turning a corner, Hermione was finally greeted with a view of the whole front of the manor, rather than just a portion of it. It was an undeniably beautiful home. Obviously old but without the worn, weathered look that affected most old Muggle buildings. If she had to make a guess, she would have said it was in the French style, with a dark roof and pale stone walls that were lined with tall, rectangular windows.
转过一个拐角，赫敏终于看到了庄园的整个正面，而不仅仅是它的一部分。不可否认，这是一个美丽的家。显然很旧，但没有影响大多数古老麻瓜建筑的破旧、风化的外观。如果非要她猜的话，她会说这是法式风格，深色的屋顶和苍白的石墙，两旁是高大的矩形窗户。

By the time she got to the front door, the heat of the sun had caused a faint band of perspiration to form around Hermione’s hairline and on the back of her neck. Fanning her hair out to ease her discomfort, she contemplated the two enormous wooden front doors and the round door knockers at their centres. Stepping forward, squinting at the worn iron, Hermione noted that they depicted an ouroboros. 
当她走到前门时，太阳的热量已经使赫敏的发际线和脖子后面形成了一条淡淡的汗带。她把头发扇开以缓解她的不适，凝视着两扇巨大的木制前门和位于它们中央的圆形门环。赫敏向前走，眯着眼睛看着破旧的熨斗，注意到它们描绘的是衔尾蛇。

Flexing her hand a few times, she finally reached up and gripped the cold iron. Lifting it, she banged it against the door once, twice, and then allowed it to rest. It didn’t take long before the door on the right swung open and Hermione came face to face with Draco Malfoy. 
她弯曲了几次手，终于伸手抓住了冰冷的熨斗。她抬起它，在门上敲了一会儿、两下，然后让它静下来。没过多久，右边的门就打开了，赫敏与德拉科·马尔福面对面。

“Oh,” she said, her head pulling back. “I didn’t expect you.”
“哦，”她说，把头往后拉。“我没想到你。”

Oddly, the sight of him comforted her. He had, she guessed, simply become familiar to her over the weeks they had spent together; a friendly face. It made sense that his presence went some small way to offsetting the unpleasantness of returning to the manor.  
奇怪的是，看到他让她感到安慰。她猜想，他只是在他们一起度过的几周里对她变得熟悉了;一张友好的面孔。他的出现在某种程度上抵消了返回庄园的不愉快，这是有道理的。

“You know this is my house, right?” he asked wryly.
“你知道这是我的房子，对吧？”

“Well, yes, but I didn’t think you’d do things like answer doors. Bit menial for you.”
“嗯，是的，但我没想到你会做像应答门这样的事情。对你来说有点卑微。

Draco rolled his eyes and stepped back from the door, sweeping his arm out to invite her in. “Fucking hell, Granger, at least step over the threshold before casting aspersions.”
德拉科翻了个白眼，从门口往后退了一步，伸出手臂邀请她进来。“他妈的，格兰杰，至少在辱骂之前跨过门槛。”

“Nice peacocks, by the way,” she said, walking into the entrance hall, more focused on trying to take in all of her surroundings than on Draco’s disgruntled face. 
“顺便说一句，漂亮的孔雀，”她说，走进门厅，比起Draco那张不满的脸，她更专注于试图把周围的所有东西都看进去。

“I fucking hate them,” he muttered, closing the door behind her.
“我他妈的讨厌他们，”他咕哝着，关上了她身后的门。

The entrance hall of Malfoy Manor was grand. That was, Hermione thought, the only word for it really. A pale stone floor spread out beneath her feet until it reached an imperial staircase flanked by beautifully ornate stone bannisters. Hermione’s footsteps echoed in the cavernous space and she turned on the spot, her gaze lifting to the high, vaulted ceiling.
马尔福庄园的门厅很宏伟。赫敏想，这是唯一能形容它的词。苍白的石头地板在她的脚下展开，直到它到达一个帝王楼梯，两侧是美丽华丽的石栏杆。赫敏的脚步声在洞穴中回荡，她原地转过身来，目光抬头看向高高的拱形天花板。

“You know,” Draco said in a sly voice, his hands in his pockets as he watched her, “If I didn’t know better, I’d venture to say that you might be impressed.”
“你知道的，”德拉科用狡猾的声音说，双手插在口袋里看着她，“如果我不知道的话，我敢说你可能会留下深刻的印象。

Hermione stopped, dragging her eyes away from the enormous crystal chandelier that hung down in the centre of the room to scoff at Draco. “You’ve been in my flat, yes? I can’t remember the last time I had this much space while still being inside .”
赫敏停了下来，把目光从挂在房间中央的巨大水晶吊灯上移开，嘲笑德拉科。“你一直在我的公寓里，对吧？我不记得上一次我还在里面的时候有这么多空间是什么时候了。

“It gets annoying,” he said, moving towards the staircase and gesturing for her to follow. “This hall feels twice as big when you're desperate for a piss and running across it to get to the bathroom. Come on. You’re meeting my father in his study.”
“这很烦人，”他说，走向楼梯，示意她跟上。“当你急切地想小便并跑过它去洗手间时，这个大厅感觉要大一倍。加油。你在我爸爸的书房里见他。

As they walked upstairs, Hermione still looking around with interest but keeping her hands firmly to herself, Draco said, “I thought I might sit in, if that’s alright.”
当他们走上楼时，赫敏仍然饶有兴趣地环顾四周，但双手紧紧地捂着自己，德拉科说，“我想我可以坐进去，如果没问题的话。

Giving him a narrow-eyed look, Hermione followed him up the next set of stairs. “You phrased that like it was a choice but I feel like that was you telling me that you’re going to be sitting in.”
赫敏眯起眼睛看了他一眼，跟着他上了下一组楼梯。“你说这就像是一种选择，但我觉得那是你告诉我你会坐下来。”

“You always were quick, Granger.”
“你总是很快的，格兰杰。”

“Who are you doing that for? Me or your father?”
“你这样做是为了谁？我还是你爸爸？

Draco led her down a long corridor on the second landing, looking like he was truly considering his answer. “It’s best for everyone involved, I think. Including me.”
德拉科领着她走过第二个楼梯口的一条长长的走廊，看起来他真的在考虑他的答案。“我认为这对所有相关人员都是最好的。包括我。

They walked side-by-side and, feeling eyes on their progress, Hermione turned her attention to the many portraits that lined the walls. They were silent, watchful and Hermione could see in the expressions of most of them a mixture of curiosity and pre-emptive disdain. That was the Malfoy way, wasn’t it? Scorn first, ask questions later. 
他们并肩走着，赫敏感觉到有人注视着他们的进步，她把注意力转向了墙上的许多肖像。他们沉默，警惕，赫敏能从他们大多数人的表情中看出好奇和先发制人的轻蔑混合在一起。这就是马尔福的方式，不是吗？先轻蔑，后提问。

Hermione was so distracted by a scene of three waifish blonde women being served by a house elf in a white barrister's wig that she didn’t see that Draco had stopped. With a surprised oomph , her head bounced off his back and she stumbled backwards. 
赫敏被三个怀特金发女人被一个戴着白色大律师假发的家养小精灵服务的场景分散了注意力，以至于她没有看到德拉科已经停下来了。带着惊讶的哄抬，她的头从他的背上弹了起来，她踉踉跄跄地向后退去。

Draco turned quickly to give her an impatient look as she smoothed her fringe self-consciously. 
德拉科迅速转过身来，不耐烦地看了她一眼，同时她不自觉地抚平了她的刘海。

“Sorry; wasn’t looking,” she mumbled, dropping her gaze to adjust her bag on her shoulder.
“对不起;没看，“她喃喃自语，垂下目光调整了一下肩上的包。

“Granger,” he said, a pleading quality to his voice that caught Hermione’s interest, “before we go in there just...please remember that my father is an unhappy, angry man who’s been locked up for eight years with a view to being locked up for twelve more.”
“格兰杰，”他说，他的声音里带着恳求的特质引起了赫敏的兴趣，“在我们进去之前......请记住，我父亲是一个不快乐、愤怒的人，他被关了八年，结果又想再被关十二年。

Hermione surveyed the high ceilings and peered down the long stretch of plushly-carpeted corridor to the tall window at its end. Bright daylight spilled inside, making the space pleasantly warm despite its stone walls. 
赫敏打量着高高的天花板，沿着铺着毛绒地毯的长长的走廊往下看，望向走廊尽头的高大窗户。明亮的日光洒进室内，尽管有石墙，但空间却显得宜人温暖。

“Yes,” she said flatly, “this is a veritable prison. I’m sure it’s been a struggle. Spending his weekdays in the west wing and his weekends in the east must get repetitive. Has he considered changing the routine?”
“是的，”她断然地说，“这是一座名副其实的监狱。我敢肯定这是一场斗争。他在西翼度过工作日，在东翼度过周末，这一定是重复的。他有没有考虑过改变这个习惯？

Draco’s head dropped so that his chin was almost on his chest and he squeezed the bridge of his nose. “Granger, I swear to—” He broke off and glared at her, raising a finger in warning. “If you’ve just come here to rile him up then don’t bother going in there. Conversing with him is bad enough these days so please do not make it worse.”
德拉科低着头，下巴几乎贴在胸前，他捏了捏自己的鼻梁。“格兰杰，我发誓——”他打断了她，瞪着她，举起一根手指警告。“如果你只是来这里激怒他，那就别费心进去了。这些天和他交谈已经够糟糕了，所以请不要让事情变得更糟。

Shuffling her feet, Hermione dropped her chin into her neck, feeling an irritating twinge of guilt. “I won’t.” Returning her eyes to his, she saw he was looking at her intently, his arms folded across his chest. “I won’t . 
赫敏拖着脚，把下巴贴进她的脖子里，感到一阵恼人的内疚感。“我不会。”她把目光回到他的身上，看到他正专注地看着她，双臂交叉在胸前。“我不会。

“You better not. Allowing you two to mix is going against all of my instincts as a potion-maker, so don’t make me regret it.” He started walking again, raising a directive hand. “It’s just up here.”
“你最好不要。让你们俩混在一起违背了我作为魔药制作者的所有直觉，所以不要让我后悔。他又开始走路，举起一只指示性的手。“就在这里。”

“Are you still making those potions for St. Mungo’s?” Hermione asked, her attention now firmly fixed on Draco rather than his home. 
“你还在为圣芒戈制作那些魔药吗？”赫敏问道，她的注意力现在牢牢地盯着德拉科，而不是他的家。

“Yes.” He gave her a sidelong smile. “Now that they’ve decided I’m not out to poison innocent civilians and that my dreamless sleep potions are, in fact, flawless, they’ve started requesting more from me. I’ve been working on some blood thinning draughts this week. I don’t think my father is overly enamoured with the idea of his son becoming a freelance potioneer but...he supports it in his own way. And it brings me some degree of peace to know what I’m doing might be helping.”
“是的。”他向她微微一笑。“既然他们已经决定我不是来毒害无辜的平民，而且我的无梦睡眠药水实际上是完美无瑕的，他们开始向我索取更多。这周我一直在研究一些血液稀释剂。我不认为我父亲过分迷恋他的儿子成为一名自由职业者的想法，但是......他以自己的方式支持它。这让我在一定程度上感到平静，因为我知道我正在做的事情可能会有所帮助。

Hermione was about to tell him how pleased she was for him when he stopped again, this time outside a large wooden door with a brightly polished brass handle. Reaching out, he set his hand on it and gave her one last look over his shoulder. 
赫敏正要告诉他她对他有多高兴，这时他又停了下来，这一次是在一扇大木门外面，门上有一个光亮的黄铜把手。他伸出手，把手放在上面，最后回头看了她一眼。

“Remember what I said.”
“记住我说过的话。”

Before she could so much as think of a sarcastic retort, Draco pushed the door to his father’s study open and stepped inside. Hermione followed him over the threshold, her feet moving from the plush carpet of the corridor back to a hard stone floor. 
还没来得及想出一句讽刺的反驳，德拉科推开了他父亲书房的门，走了进去。赫敏跟着他越过门槛，她的脚从走廊的毛绒地毯上移回坚硬的石头地板上。

Looking to her right, Hermione took in a wall of bookcases and, as her eyes travelled left, a gently crackling fireplace with a comfortable-looking deep green leather sofa in front of it. There were glass cabinets dotted around the room, some containing books, others small sculptures or trinkets that she was itching to take a closer look at. All the furniture was a dark mahogany and the walls were panelled to match. It made the room feel smaller than it was but, curiously, not necessarily cosy. Turning her head, her eyes travelled over an ornate persian rug spread over the floor and up the length of a large, shiny desk before they finally landed on the figure of Lucius Malfoy. 
赫敏向右看，看到了一整面墙的书架，当她的目光向左移动时，一个轻轻噼啪作响的壁炉，前面有一张看起来很舒服的深绿色真皮沙发。房间里点缀着玻璃柜，有些里面装着书，有些是她渴望仔细看一眼的小雕塑或小饰品。所有的家具都是深色桃花心木，墙壁也镶板与之相配。它让房间感觉比实际小，但奇怪的是，它不一定舒适。她转过头，目光扫过铺在地板上的华丽波斯地毯，沿着一张闪亮的大桌子的长度向上移动，最后落在了卢修斯·马尔福的身影上。

He was standing behind his desk at the rightmost of two large windows, surveying the view over the grounds to the rear of the manor. From behind he looked much the same as the last time she had seen him at his trial; tall and straight-backed with platinum hair and exquisitely tailored black robes. 
他站在书桌后面两扇大窗户的最右边，打量着庄园后方的庭院景色。从后面看，他和她上次在审判他时看到他时差不多;高大挺拔的背部，铂金色的头发和剪裁精美的黑色长袍。

His face was more drawn than she remembered. But overall, he was not all that different; still cold and intimidating with the vaguest hint of a sneer playing about his lips. 
“喝水了，”卢修斯说，终于转过身来面对他们，他的注意力牢牢地盯着他的儿子，而不是赫敏。当她打量着他时，她首先想到的是他看起来很疲惫。他的脸比她记得的还要紧张。但总的来说，他并没有那么不同;他的嘴唇上还带着一丝隐约的冷笑和威慑。

As she moved into a new position in the centre of the room, Lucius Malfoy drew his seat out from behind his desk and lowered himself into it. Hermione hovered uncertainly as Draco closed the door, her eyes still darting around to take in some of the finer details of the room. 
赫敏被德拉科强迫将目光从年长的马尔福身上移开，德拉科用拍打着的双手，将她带出门口，进一步进入房间。当她移动到房间中央的新位置时，卢修斯·马尔福从书桌后面拉出他的座位，把自己放进去。当德拉科关上门时，赫敏不确定地盘旋着，她的眼睛仍然四处扫视，以观察房间的一些更精细的细节。

There was such a pervasive air of wealth that Hermione couldn’t help but feel very aware of how faded the denim of her jeans had become. A slight chill in the region of her lower abdomen reminded her of the fact that her t-shirt was just slightly too short in the body after she had shrunk it in the wash. Looking down, she tugged at it, trying to disguise the movement as adjusting the weight of the satchel slung over her shoulder. 
财富的气息无处不在，赫敏不禁非常清楚她的牛仔裤已经变得多么褪色了。她小腹区域略带寒意，这让她想起了这样一个事实，她的 T 恤在洗涤中缩水后，身体略微太短了。她低头拉扯着它，试图将这个动作伪装成在调整挂在她肩上的背包的重量。

Once he could see he had her attention, he let his eyes trail down her body at a leisurely pace, a shadow of a smirk passing over his face. Hermione grit her teeth, determined that she could dampen the heat rising in her cheeks through sheer force of will. 
她抬起头，发现卢修斯·马尔福舒适地坐在他的办公桌后面，只是看着她。察觉到他目光中的轻蔑，她直起身来，抬起下巴。一旦他看到他引起了她的注意，他就让他的眼睛悠闲地沿着她的身体滑下，一丝得意的笑容在他的脸上掠过。赫敏咬紧牙关，决心要靠纯粹的意志力来抑制脸颊上升的热度。

It took Draco clearing his throat to regain her attention. Glancing his way, she saw him looking apprehensively between them. “You can sit down, Granger.” He gestured to a single seat in front of his father’s desk. 
德拉科清了清嗓子才重新引起了她的注意。她瞥了他一眼，看到他忧心忡忡地看着他们。“你可以坐下，格兰杰。”他指了指他父亲办公桌前的一个座位。

Then, worrying that appeared too defensive, she uncrossed them and placed them in her lap, her fingers fidgeting between her thighs.

The sun’s rays didn’t seem to be strong enough, or brave enough, to shine directly into the office. 
她注意到，德拉科没有座位，但他似乎并不关心。相反，他走到父亲的书桌后面，靠在左边窗户的窗台上，交叉着双臂。赫敏越过肩膀，清晰地瞥见了庄园翠绿的地面和湛蓝、阳光明媚的天空。太阳的光线似乎不够强烈，也不够勇敢，无法直接照进办公室。

赫敏抬头看了一眼德拉科，然后看了看卢修斯。近距离看，她能更清楚地看到疲惫。他一直都是苍白的，但他的眼睛下面有一点蓝灰色，让她想起了墨水的污迹。

“Draco insisted on the location,” Lucius drawled. “I favoured the drawing room.”
“德拉科坚持要这个位置，”卢修斯抽搐着。“我喜欢客厅。”

赫敏身体僵硬，越过卢修斯的肩膀，德拉科闭上了眼睛，把头靠在窗户上，发出微弱的砰砰声。赫敏咽下了喉咙里的一团东西，直视着卢修斯·马尔福冰冷、灰色的眼睛，发现它们正在梳理她的脸，寻找反应。

He’s an unhappy, angry man. He’s an unhappy, angry man , a voice that sounded oddly like Draco’s repeated in her head. He’s a fucking arsehole, is what he is , snapped a voice that sounded much more like her own. 
他是一个不快乐、愤怒的人。他是一个不快乐、愤怒的男人，这个声音听起来很奇怪，就像德拉科在她脑海中重复的声音一样。 他妈是个混蛋，他就是这个屁眼，吼道一声，听起来更像她自己的声音。

Possibly, you’ve encountered something similar before but it’s essentially a method of recording a historical period through interviews with people directly involved in the events.”

I think it might be interesting to dig into...into the personal to broaden our understanding of wider events. And I think it’s important to draw from as wide a range of sources as possible.”

赫敏张开又闭上了嘴，她的脸在想卢修斯·马尔福怎么会滥用这样的协议。“嗯，我不确定这完全是......”看到他毫不妥协的下巴，赫敏稍微软化了一点。“如果发生这种情况，我愿意参与讨论。但我认为你不会不高兴。

On seeing a doubtful expression pass over his face, Hermione sat forward. “I’m not looking to harm you or your reputation Mr Malfoy. How you are presented will be entirely down to how you present yourself . It’s in your control.”
赫敏看到脸上掠过疑惑的表情，坐了起来。“我不想伤害你或你的名声，马尔福先生。你如何被展示将完全取决于你如何展示自己。这在你的控制之下。

Lucius unclasped his hands and leaned back in his seat, one elbow balanced on the arm. Running the side of his forefinger below his lower lip, he watched Hermione carefully. Remembering how Harry had always said Dumbledore made him feel like he was being x-rayed, she rather felt that she was experiencing the same thing.
卢修斯松开双手，向后靠在座位上，一只手肘平衡在手臂上。他用食指滑到下唇下面，仔细地看着赫敏。想起哈利总是说邓布利多让他觉得自己像在接受X光检查，她宁愿觉得自己也在经历同样的事情。

“I am willing to provisionally agree to what you’ve offered,” Lucius said eventually, lowering his hand from his face. “This is entirely dependent on the results of your meeting with the Minister. You may return at the same time next week if, and only if, you have secured something from him for me.”
“我愿意暂时同意你的提议，”卢修斯最终说，把手从他的脸上放下来。“这完全取决于你与部长的会议结果。你可以下周的同一时间回来，当且仅当你为我从他那里得到了一些东西。

Hermione couldn’t help the wide grin that spread over her face and she immediately looked from Lucius to Draco, who had raised his head in surprise. Meeting her eyes, he shrugged.
赫敏忍不住脸上绽放出灿烂的笑容，她立即把目光从卢修斯身上移开，看向德拉科，德拉科惊讶地抬起了头。对上她的眼睛，他耸了耸肩。

“Thank you, Mr Malfoy. I mean it, you really won’t be unhappy.” Hermione rose from her seat, and hauled her satchel onto her shoulder, bouncing on the balls of her feet. “You might even enjoy it.”
“谢谢你，马尔福先生。我是认真的，你真的不会不高兴的。赫敏从座位上站起来，把她的书包拽到肩上，在她的脚掌上弹跳。“你甚至可能会喜欢它。”

With an expression that made Hermione mightily glad he could no longer perform magic, Lucius Malfoy rose from his own chair to look down his nose at her. “I cannot even begin to express to you how much I doubt that, Miss Granger. Please leave.”
卢修斯·马尔福的表情让赫敏非常高兴他不能再施展魔法了，他从自己的椅子上站起来，低头看着她。“我什至无法向你表达我有多么怀疑这一点，格兰杰小姐。请离开。

Not willing to allow him to sour her victory, Hermione turned lightly on her heel and made for the door, Draco following her. 
赫敏不愿意让他破坏她的胜利，她轻轻地转过身来，向门口走去，德拉科跟在她后面。

“Remember what I said,” Lucius said to her back as Draco opened the door for them. “Do not bother coming back if your meeting with the Minister for Magic bears no fruit.”
“记住我说过的话，”卢修斯在德拉科为他们开门时对她的背影说。“如果你和魔法部长的会面没有结果，就别费心回来了。”

Hermione felt far lighter as she strolled down the corridors of Malfoy Manor towards the exit. Draco walked by her side but she could sense that he was more subdued.
赫敏沿着马尔福庄园的走廊向出口走去，感觉轻松多了。德拉科走在她身边，但她能感觉到他更加低调了。

“Granger, do you really think Shacklebolt will be willing to give you a hand with this?”
“格兰杰，你真的觉得沙克尔会愿意帮你一把吗？”

“I can only try,” Hermione said. “I’m hoping to frame it that Kingsley would be rewarding your father for post-war cooperation and contribution to a worthy record, rather than that he would be incentivising him to take part in the first place, if that makes sense.”
“我只能试试，”赫敏说。“我希望将金斯利描述为金斯利会奖励你父亲在战后的合作和对有价值的记录的贡献，而不是他首先会激励他参加，如果这是有道理的。”

Draco looked perturbed. “I think father might be expecting the latter. He wants assurances.”
德拉科看起来很不安。“我想爸爸可能期待的是后者。他想要保证。

Hermione pulled her lower lip between her teeth and chewed thoughtfully. “I’m going to try my best.”
赫敏把下唇拉到牙齿之间，若有所思地咀嚼着。“我会尽力而为。”

When they reached the door, Draco opened the door for Hermione and stepped back to allow her to exit into the sun. “Er, Granger,” he said as she stepped onto the front step, “before you go: do you have any more of that lemon cake?”
当他们走到门口时，德拉科为赫敏开了门，然后退后一步，让她走出去，让她走出去，沐浴在阳光下。“呃，格兰杰，”当她走上前面的台阶时，他说，“在你走之前，你还有那个柠檬蛋糕吗？

“Ah, so it went down well, did it?” Hermione asked with a knowing smile.
“啊，所以进展顺利，是吗？”赫敏带着会心的微笑问道。

“You have no idea.” Hermione was amused to see that Draco looked mildly distressed. “I’m afraid of what you’ve started. Cauldron Cakes are no longer good enough.”
“你不知道。”赫敏看到德拉科看起来有点痛苦，感到很有趣。“我害怕你开始的事情。Cauldron Cakes 已经不够好了。

“I’ll bring some with me next week,” she said soothingly. “I promise.”
“我下周会带一些，”她安慰地说。“我保证。”

April 28th
4月28日

Hermione tried to ignore the curious glances she received from Ministry workers as she rode the lift to her meeting with Kingsley. 
赫敏试图无视她在乘坐电梯去见金斯莱时从魔法部工作人员那里收到的好奇目光。

"Level Five, Department of International Magical Co-operation, incorporating the International Magical Trading Standards Body, the International Magical Office of Law and the International Confederation of Wizards, British Seats." 
“第五层，国际魔法合作部，包括国际魔法贸易标准机构、国际魔法法律办公室和国际巫师联合会，英国席位。”

Hermione squeezed herself into the back of the lift as it hurtled along, folding her body into the corner. After leaving the Ministry on sabbatical, she did her best to avoid it. Whenever Harry asked her to meet for lunch, she would insist that he meet her outside of the building. It just wasn’t worth the curious questions from her former—technically, still, she supposed—co-workers. 
赫敏挤进电梯的后部，电梯飞驰着，把身体缩进了角落里。在休假离开魔法部后，她尽力避免它。每当哈利约她见面吃午饭时，她都会坚持让他在大楼外见她。她只是不值得从她的前同事那里提出好奇的问题——从技术上讲，她猜还是这样。

None of them seemed quite able to grasp why Hermione Granger, one of the most promising and fastest risers the Ministry had seen in nearly a decade, would suddenly duck out after five years of service to spend all of her time interviewing people about something that had already happened. 
他们似乎都不太明白为什么赫敏·格兰杰，魔法部近十年来见过的最有前途、最迅速崛起的人之一，会在服务五年后突然躲出来，把所有的时间都花在采访人们已经发生的事情上。

When she would explain, always wearing an overly bright smile, that it was only a sabbatical and that she’d be back eventually, they’d offer her pitying smiles that she interpreted as saying, ‘but it’s not just a sabbatical, is it, dear? All got a bit much for you, didn’t it?’ She hated it. One day she knew she was going to crack and tell someone the truth. 
当她总是带着过于灿烂的笑容解释说，这只是一次休假，她最终会回来时，他们会向她露出可怜的微笑，她把这些笑容解释为，“但这不仅仅是一次休假，是吗，亲爱的？对你来说，一切都有点多了，不是吗？她讨厌它。有一天，她知道她会崩溃并告诉别人真相。

“Well, yes, as a matter of fact going straight from Hogwarts, through the war and then into the Ministry made me feel like I was hurtling along a never-ending mineshaft without a single second to take a breath. Sometimes I would wake in the night, drenched in cold sweat, and I’d be too afraid to look at my hands, convinced that I’d find my skin had sagged and aged because I’d just let my life pass me by in a red-taped blur of bureaucracy and boredom. Working in a world I barely understood anymore with people who didn’t want to improve things if it minorly inconvenienced or didn’t explicitly benefit them was eating me up from the inside out." 
“嗯，是的，事实上，直接从霍格沃茨出发，经历战争，然后进入魔法部，让我觉得自己就像在一个永无止境的矿井上飞驰，没有一秒钟的喘息时间。有时我会在夜里醒来，浑身冒冷汗，我不敢看自己的手，确信我会发现我的皮肤已经下垂和衰老，因为我只是让我的生活在官僚主义和无聊的红色胶带模糊中从我身边过去。在一个我几乎不再理解的世界里工作，与那些不想改善事情的人一起工作，如果它只是轻微的不便或没有明确地使他们受益，这让我从内到外都被吞噬了。

Hermione gave a self-satisfied little snort at the thought of such an outburst and saw the man beside her take two nervous steps towards the opposite side of the lift. It was possible her face was showing the generally malevolent spirit of her thoughts.
赫敏一想到这样的爆发，就得意地哼了一声，看到她身边的男人紧张地向电梯的另一边走了两步。她的脸上可能流露出她思想中普遍的恶毒。

"Level Two, Department of Magical Law Enforcement, including the Improper Use of Magic Office, Auror Headquarters, and Wizengamot Administration Services." 
“第二层，魔法执法部，包括不当使用魔法办公室、傲罗总部和威森加摩管理服务。”

When the lift stopped, the anxious little man cleared out of the lift and Hermione realised with no small amount of relief that she was alone. No one else entered the lift, except for a small purple paper aeroplane stamped with the Ministry seal. It buzzed irritatingly around Hermione’s head as the lift jolted to life again. 
当电梯停下来时，那个焦急的小个子男人从电梯里走了出来，赫敏松了一口气，意识到她一个人。没有其他人进入电梯，除了一架盖有魔法部印章的紫色小纸飞机。它在赫敏的头上发出恼人的嗡嗡声，电梯再次颠簸起来。

"Level One, Minister for Magic and support staff, incorporating the Office of the Minister for Magic, the Office of the Advisor to the Minister for Magic, the Office of the Senior Undersecretary to the Minister for Magic, the Office of the Junior Assistant to the Minister for Magic.” 
“一级，魔法部长和支持人员，包括魔法部长办公室、魔法部长顾问办公室、魔法部长高级副秘书办公室、魔法部长初级助理办公室。”

Squaring her shoulders, Hermione stepped into the quiet corridors surrounding the Minister for Magic’s office. Shortly before her departure from the Ministry, she had gotten used to treading the path to Kingsley’s office. They had always gotten on well and, as Hermione moved up in the Department for the Regulation of Magical Creatures, she had found Kingsley calling on her an increasing amount. Sometimes it was for her opinion, sometimes it was to ask her to do something he wouldn’t entrust to anyone else, and sometimes it was just for a cup of tea. As the grind of the Ministry had become more and more wearing on her, Hermione had found his summons to be small bright spots in otherwise grey weeks. 
赫敏挺直肩膀，走进了魔法部长办公室周围安静的走廊。在她离开魔法部前不久，她已经习惯了踏上通往金斯莱办公室的小路。他们一直相处得很好，随着赫敏在魔法生物监管部的升职，她发现金斯莱越来越多地打电话给她。有时是为了她的意见，有时是让她做一些他不会托付给别人的事情，有时只是为了喝杯茶。随着魔法部的辛苦对她来说越来越疲惫，赫敏发现他的召唤在原本灰暗的几周里只是小亮点。

A curly-haired young man sat at a desk outside the Minister’s office and he looked up as he heard Hermione approach. How he managed that given the degree to which the thick carpets on Level One absorbed sound, she wasn’t sure. 
一个卷发的年轻人坐在部长办公室外的桌子旁，他抬起头来，听到赫敏走近。考虑到一楼厚厚的地毯吸收声音的程度，他是怎么做到的，她不确定。

“Miss Granger,” the young man greeted her with a smile. “Go right in, the Minister is expecting you.”
“格兰杰小姐，”年轻人微笑着向她打招呼。“快进去，部长在等你。”

With a grateful nod, Hermione strode towards Kingsely’s door, giving her customary little knock of warning before pushing it open. Kingsley was seated behind his desk and Hermione was pleased to see that, rather than the usual piles of parchment in front of him, he had made room for a small tea tray. 
赫敏感激地点了点头，大步走向金斯利的门，在推开门之前，她习惯性地轻轻敲了敲门。金斯莱坐在他的书桌后面，赫敏很高兴地看到，他面前没有通常的羊皮纸堆，而是为一个小茶盘腾出了空间。

“Hermione,” he stood, his deep, warm voice almost an embrace. “Please, come in.”
“赫敏，”他站起来，他低沉、温暖的声音几乎是一个拥抱。“请进来。”

Approaching the desk, Hermione reached across to shake Kingsley’s hand and lowered herself into a chair in front of him. He waited until she was fully seated before following suit and then reached out to begin preparing her tea.
走近桌子，赫敏伸手与金斯莱握手，然后坐在他面前的椅子上。他等到她完全坐下后才效仿，然后伸手开始为她准备茶。

“I can’t believe you still remember how I like my tea,” Hermione said, her eyebrows raised.
“我不敢相信你还记得我有多喜欢我的茶，”赫敏说，她的眉毛扬起。

“I’ve found learning someone’s tea preference is one of those small things that makes a striking impression in a meeting,” Kingsley said, glancing up at her with a sly smile as he stirred a teaspoon of honey into her mug before adding a small splash of milk. “It gives the impression of humbleness.”
“我发现了解某人的茶偏好是在会议中给人留下深刻印象的小事之一，”金斯利说，他狡猾地笑着抬头看了她一眼，同时将一茶匙蜂蜜搅拌到她的杯子里，然后加入一小滴牛奶。“它给人的印象是谦逊。”

“God, you’re good,” she muttered with a shake of her head.
“上帝，你很好，”她摇着头咕哝道。

“I have to be,” Kingsley said, passing her tea across the table and waving away her thanks. “Remembering your tea preference was, admittedly, quite a feat; it’s been several months since I last saw you, Hermione.”
“我必须这样，”金斯利说，一边把茶递过桌子，挥手道谢。“诚然，记住你对茶的偏好是一件了不起的事情;我上次见到你已经好几个月了，赫敏。

Hermione didn’t miss the admonishment in his tone and cringed into her cup. “I’m sorry, Kingsley. I’ve just been busy with my interviews and writing. It’s not because I don’t want to see you. You’re busier than me, anyway. It’s not like you have time to sit with former employees to talk about nothing.”
赫敏没有错过他语气中的告诫，畏缩地坐在她的杯子里。“对不起，金斯利。我只是忙于我的采访和写作。不是因为我不想见你。反正你比我还忙。你没有时间与前雇员坐在一起无所事事。

Kingsley lifted his own tea—five sugars—to his lips and took a long drink, watching her over the rim. “I don’t consider you a former employee, Hermione,” he corrected as he set his cup down. “You’re on sabbatical, remember? How long has that been now?”
金斯莱把自己的茶——五颗糖——举到嘴边，喝了一大口，一边看着她。“我不认为你是前雇员，赫敏，”他放下杯子纠正道。“你正在休假，记得吗？现在已经有多久了？

“Just short of two years,” Hermione said, painfully aware that he’d agreed to place her on half-pay for two years, after which they’d discuss her options.
“就短两年，”赫敏说，痛苦地意识到他已经同意让她半薪两年，之后他们会讨论她的选择。

“And how are you faring?”
“那你怎么样了？”

“I’m well,” Hermione said slowly, her finger toying with the handle of her cup. “My oral history is coming along. I’ve completed the majority of my interviews and I’m making good progress in working them into chapters.”
“我没事，”赫敏缓缓地说，她的手指玩弄着她的杯柄。“我的口述历史正在发展。我已经完成了大部分采访，并且在将它们分成章节方面取得了良好的进展。

“Ah,” Kingsley said, flashing her a disappointed smile. “I confess, I was rather hoping you were coming here to tell me you wish to return to your post.”
“啊，”金斯利说，向她露出一个失望的笑容。“我承认，我倒是希望你来这里告诉我，你想回到你的岗位上来。”

An anxious twist in Hermione’s stomach made her shift in her seat and drop her gaze. “Not yet, Kingsley. I’m sorry. I have one last source that I’m keenly pursuing.”
赫敏的肚子焦急地扭动着，让她在座位上动了动，垂下了目光。“还没，金斯利。对不起。我还有最后一个来源，我正在努力寻找。

“Just one?” Kingsley asked, nodding his head as though pleased by the news. “You make it sound as though they are fleeing you.”
“就一个？”金斯利问道，点点头，似乎对这个消息感到高兴。“你让它听起来好像他们正在逃离你。”

“Well, they’re not the most eager of participants,” Hermione said with a smile that was closer to a grimace. “It’s Lucius Malfoy, you see.”
“嗯，他们不是最热心的参与者，”赫敏说，笑容更接近于做鬼脸。“你看，是卢修斯·马尔福。”

Kingsley’s head ceased nodding and he leaned back slowly in his chair to assess Hermione. Raising his hand to his ear, he began fiddling with his earring in the way that he always did when he was thinking. 
金斯莱的头不再点头，他慢慢地靠在椅子上，打量着赫敏。他把手举到耳边，开始摆弄他的耳环，就像他思考时一样。

“An unexpected choice.”
“一个出乎意料的选择。”

“I interviewed his son, Draco,” Hermione explained, subtly sliding her hands from the desk to wipe the clamminess that was developing on them on her jeans. “It seemed like a natural next step.”
“我采访了他的儿子，德拉科，”赫敏解释道，巧妙地将手从桌子上滑开，擦去牛仔裤上形成的湿漉漉的。“这似乎是自然而然的下一步。”

“But he’s resistant?”
“但他有抵抗力吗？”

“Yes,” Hermione said with a sigh. “That’s actually…Kingsley, I was actually hoping you might be able to help me with that.”
“是的，”赫敏叹了口气说。“那实际上是......金斯利，我其实希望你能帮我解决这个问题。

“I see,” Kingsley said slowly, his finger running around the shell of his ear. “And how could I help?”
“我明白了，”金斯利缓缓地说，他的手指在他的耳壳上滑过。“那我能帮什么忙呢？”

“Well,” Hermione reached up to grip her cup with both hands, turning it between them. “I know he’ll do it if I can offer him something that might tempt him.” Kingsley’s eyebrows were slowly rising up his forehead. “A little reward for being good and contributing to a collaborative post-war project, you know.”
“嗯，”赫敏伸手用双手握住她的杯子，在他们之间转动。“我知道如果我能给他一些可能诱惑他的东西，他会这样做的。”金斯莱的眉毛缓缓地扬起了他的额头。“你知道的，对表现优秀并为战后合作项目做出贡献的一点奖励。”

“I’m afraid I don’t see how that requires me, Hermione.”
“恐怕我看不出这需要我什么，赫敏。”

He was going to draw it out of her, Hermione thought with a sharp but completely internal tut . Kingsley was one of the most intelligent men she knew; there was no way he hadn’t figured out what she was hinting at.
他要从她身上抽出来，赫敏尖锐但完全在内心的啧啧称奇。金斯利是她认识的最聪明的人之一;他不可能不知道她在暗示什么。

“I was thinking you might help me secure something worth offering.” Hermione knew her tone was so determinedly casual it came all the way back around to sounding suspect but she had started and didn’t see the point in stopping. “I’m just throwing some ideas off the top of my head here: what if we returned his wand to him? Or maybe even reduced his total sentence?”
“我在想你可能会帮我找到一些值得奉献的东西。”赫敏知道她的语气是如此的随意，以至于听起来又回到了可疑的程度，但她已经开始了，她看不出停下来有什么意义。“我只是在这里抛出一些想法：如果我们把他的魔杖还给他呢？或者甚至可能减轻他的总刑期？

Seeing that Kingsley’s raised eyebrows were not coming down and were actually, if at all possible, climbing higher, Hermione quickly added, “I’m not saying by a huge amount but maybe just... a couple...of years?” Hermione trailed off when she realised that Kingsley was not being swept along by her ideas.
看到金斯莱扬起的眉毛并没有落下，而且实际上，如果可能的话，她爬得更高了，赫敏赶紧补充道，“我不是说很多，但也许只是......一对......几年？当赫敏意识到金斯莱并没有被她的想法所左右时，她停下了脚步。

“As I said, Hermione,” Kingsley rubbed his forehead, looking perturbed, “I was rather hoping you were coming here to tell me you wanted to return to the Ministry. I would like to see you back here, making a difference.”
“就像我说的，赫敏，”金斯莱揉了揉他的额头，看起来有些不安，“我真希望你来这里告诉我你想回到魔法部。我希望看到你回到这里，有所作为。

Hermione heard the subtle slight in his words and lifted her tea to take a tight-lipped sip in an effort to compose herself. There was no point in snapping at Kingsley; what he said didn’t come from a bad place and she would only feel terrible in the aftermath.
赫敏听出了他话语中微妙的轻蔑，端起茶来抿了一口，努力让自己冷静下来。对金斯利大发雷霆是没有意义的;他说的话并不是来自一个坏地方，她只会在事后感到可怕。

“I will come back, Kingsley,” she finally said, lowering the cup to the desk, “but this project has been good for me and it’s important that I see it through. Your own interview is going to be a significant part of the book—you were my biggest inside-the-Ministry source—aren’t you keen to see it in print one day?”
“我会回来的，金斯利，”她终于说，把杯子放到桌子上，“但这个项目对我来说很好，我必须把它完成。你自己的采访将成为这本书的重要组成部分——你是我最大的内阁消息来源——你不是很想有一天看到它出版吗？

“I am pleased to have been able to contribute in my own small way, Hermione.” Kingsley offered her an appeasingly gratified smile. “And I’m also pleased that you feel that some time away has been positive for you. But I would have thought you’d get more benefit out of taking part in some more hands-on and practical work.” 
“我很高兴能够以自己的方式做出贡献，赫敏。”金斯莱向她露出一个令人满意的微笑。“我也很高兴你觉得离开一段时间对你来说是积极的。但我本以为你会从参加一些更多的实践和实践工作中获得更多好处。

Determined not to respond with ill-advised haste, Hermione pinched the tip of her tongue between her teeth, focusing on the pain of it as Kingsley went on. “I’m afraid I struggle to understand why you’re so determined to linger in the war. At the Ministry, we’re rebuilding and moving forward. I always got the impression you shared those goals.”
赫敏决定不以不明智的匆忙来回应，她用牙齿捏住了舌尖，随着金斯莱继续说下去，她专注于它的痛苦。“恐怕我很难理解你为什么这么决心在战争中徘徊。在教育部，我们正在重建和前进。我一直觉得你有相同的目标。

Despite having almost bitten through the pointed tip of her tongue, Hermione’s tone was still sharp when she responded. “Just because everyone else is happy to sweep the war under the carpet for the sake of moving on doesn’t mean I am, Kingsley. I tried that for years. It didn’t work. So I’m trying something different.”
尽管几乎咬穿了她的尖舌尖，但赫敏回应时的语气仍然很尖锐。“仅仅因为其他人都乐于为了继续前进而将战争扫地出门，并不意味着我是，金斯利。我尝试了好几年。它没有奏效。所以我正在尝试一些不同的东西。

“But moving on takes time, Hermione. And patience. There is nothing to be gained from walking forward while your gaze remains fixed behind you.”
“但继续前进需要时间，赫敏。还有耐心。当你的目光一直固定在身后时，向前走是没有任何好处的。

“I don't think that's entirely true,” Hermione said quietly. “There are lessons we can learn from what happened and I think we can benefit from dissecting the minds of the people who were involved in the events as much as the events themselves.”
“我不认为这完全正确，”赫敏轻声说。“我们可以从发生的事情中吸取教训，我认为我们可以从剖析参与事件的人的思想以及事件本身中受益。”

“I hardly think dissecting the mind of Lucius Malfoy will teach us how to create a just society which aims to do the right things.” 
“我不认为剖析卢修斯·马尔福的思想会教会我们如何创造一个公正的社会，旨在做正确的事情。”

“No, but I wouldn’t mind knowing more about the hows and whys of his choices. I found interviewing Draco to be more enlightening than I expected. Besides the usefulness, Kingsley, sometimes it’s nice just to have knowledge for its own sake.”
“不，但我不介意更多地了解他的选择是怎么做的，以及为什么。我发现采访 Draco 比我预期的更有启发性。除了有用之外，金斯利，有时仅仅为了知识本身而拥有知识也很好。

Kingsley gave her a sceptical look and stirred a sixth spoonful of sugar into his tea. Hermione couldn’t tell if that was a good sign or a bad one; he had never done it in front of her before. 
金斯利怀疑地看了她一眼，然后把第六勺糖倒进了他的茶里。赫敏分不清这是个好兆头还是坏兆头;他以前从来没有在她面前做过。

“Kingsley,” Hermione sighed, leaning back in her chair while keeping her hands planted on the desk, “I was invited into the wizarding world at the age of eleven and within six years, there were people prepared to kill me for accepting that invitation.” She lowered her hands down into her lap and rubbed at the faint scar hidden behind her thin, long-sleeved top. “I just can’t—sometimes I wonder if I ever really knew the wizarding world. I need to understand—and if I can’t then I need to know —what makes people...”
“金斯利，”赫敏叹了口气，向后靠在椅子上，双手放在桌子上，“我在十一岁的时候就被邀请进入魔法世界，不到六年，就有人准备因为接受了那个邀请而杀了我。她把手放到膝盖上，揉搓着藏在她薄薄的长袖上衣后面的淡淡的伤疤。“我就是不能——有时候我会想我是否真的了解过魔法世界。我需要理解——如果我不能理解，那么我就需要知道——是什么让人们......”

Trailing off, unsure of how to express exactly what she wanted, Hermione looked up and found that Kingsley’s expression had collapsed into a weary frown. 
赫敏慢慢地走开，不知道该如何表达她想要的东西，她抬起头，发现金斯莱的表情已经皱成了疲惫的眉头。

“Hermione, I fear you’re going to be disappointed by the answers you receive. You cannot change the past and one man’s story will not provide you with a blueprint for creating a better future.”
“赫敏，我担心你会对你收到的答案感到失望。你无法改变过去，一个人的故事不会为你提供创造更美好未来的蓝图。

“Maybe not,” Hermione raised her shoulder in a shrug. “But while I don’t ever want to forget what we fought for, Kingsley, I also don’t want to run the risk of forgetting what we were fighting against.”
“也许不是，”赫敏耸耸肩。“但是，虽然我永远不想忘记我们为之奋斗的东西，金斯利，但我也不想冒着忘记我们曾经为之奋斗的东西的风险。”

Kingsley exhaled through his nose and shook his head. Taking a drink, he lowered his cup and leaned back in his chair to observe her, his hands clasped in his lap. 
金斯利用鼻子呼出一口气，摇了摇头。喝了一口，他放下杯子，靠在椅子上看着她，双手紧握在膝盖上。

“Look,” he said, “if I’m being perfectly honest, I’m not sure how much I can do for you here. After the events of his trial, many considered Lucius Malfoy’s sentence to be fair, or even lenient. He only avoided Azkaban by the grace of Harry’s testimony.”
“听着，”他说，“如果我说实话，我不确定我能在这里为你做多少事情。在他的审判事件之后，许多人认为卢修斯·马尔福的判决是公平的，甚至是宽大的。他只是靠着哈利的证词才避开了阿兹卡班。

“I know that. I also know that almost a decade has passed and that, as Minister for Magic, you have the power to...acknowledge acts which might hint at a desire to atone.”
“我知道。我也知道已经过去了将近十年，作为魔法部长，您有能力......承认可能暗示赎罪欲望的行为。

Kingsley raised an eyebrow which distinctly asked Hermione who she was kidding. “He has yet to show any such desire. To anyone.”
金斯莱挑了挑眉毛，显然是在问赫敏她在开什么玩笑。“他还没有表现出任何这样的愿望。对任何人。

“Helping me would certainly be a step in the right direction, don’t you think? Working with a Muggle-born.”
“帮助我肯定是朝着正确方向迈出的一步，你不觉得吗？和一个麻瓜出身的人一起工作。

“I’d find it hard to believe in the sincerity of his actions when you clearly intend to dangle his reward in front of him as his primary incentive, Hermione.”
“我很难相信他的行为是真诚的，因为你明明打算把他的奖励作为他的主要激励，赫敏。”

An exasperated but fond smile was tugging at Kingsley’s lips and Hermione couldn’t help but grin guiltily at him. “Kingsley, I know you want me to return to the Ministry but I’m not going to abandon what I’m working on.”
金斯莱的嘴唇上扯着一个恼怒但又可爱的笑容，赫敏忍不住对他咧嘴一笑。“金斯莱，我知道你想让我回到魔法部，但我不会放弃我正在做的事情。”

“What if I tell you that rather than lessen his sentence for helping you, I’ll use anything he might additionally confess to have him locked up for longer?”
“如果我告诉你，与其因为帮助你而减轻他的刑期，不如用他可能额外供认的任何东西来把他关得更久呢？”

“ Would you do that?”
“你会那样做吗？”

Kingsley tapped the edge of his cup with his forefinger, looking down into the ripples it caused on the surface of his tea. “No,” he said finally and reluctantly. “No, I wouldn’t. He’s been tried and convicted for his actions in both wars and more trials would not especially fit the spirit of moving on that I’m trying to cultivate.”
金斯利用食指敲了敲杯子的边缘，低头看着它在茶叶表面引起的涟漪。“不，”他终于不情愿地说。“不，我不会。他因在两场战争中的行为而受到审判和定罪，更多的审判并不特别符合我正在努力培养的继续前进的精神。

Hermione nodded—that was exactly what she’d thought. Refusal to move on was, after all, what he hated about what she was doing.
赫敏点点头——她正是这么想的。毕竟，拒绝继续前进是他讨厌她所做的事情的原因。

“Then what if I withdraw your half pay?” he asked, glancing up at her from under his furrowed brow.
“那如果我把你的一半工资拿出来呢？”他问道，从他皱起的眉头下抬头瞥了她一眼。

The idea of that made Hermione’s smile falter and her heart hammer. She wasn’t struggling but without that stipend, she would be. Of course, she couldn’t tell him that. “Then I’ll have to find a way to manage. I’m not giving up.”
这个想法让赫敏的笑容变得迟钝，她的心也受到了打击。她没有挣扎，但如果没有这笔津贴，她就会挣扎。当然，她不能告诉他。“那我就得想办法管理了。我不会放弃。

Kingsley scoffed and pointed a finger at her. “This is why I want you back, you know. Passion, commitment, drive . We need those qualities here. You’re wasting them on getting things for Lucius Malfoy.”
金斯利嘲笑着用手指指着她。“这就是我希望你回来的原因，你知道的。激情、承诺、动力。我们在这里需要这些品质。你把他们浪费在给卢修斯·马尔福买东西上了。

“I’m not doing this for Lucius Malfoy, Kingsley,” Hermione said, mortified by the mere suggestion. “I’m doing it for myself .”
“我不是为了卢修斯·马尔福做这件事，金斯莱，”赫敏说，仅仅因为这个建议就感到羞愧。“我这样做是为了我自己。”

“And once this project is complete, will you return to the Ministry then?”
“那么，一旦这个项目完成，你会回到魔法部吗？”

Guilt tugged Hermione’s stomach like a fish hook. If she was completely honest with herself, she didn’t particularly relish the idea of returning to the Ministry. Maybe, she reasoned with herself, when she felt she’d done something for herself—done some writing alongside her reading—she’d warm to the idea. 
内疚像鱼钩一样拉扯着赫敏的肚子。如果她对自己完全诚实，她并不是特别喜欢重返魔法部的想法。也许，她心里想着，当她觉得自己为自己做了些什么——在阅读的同时写了一些东西——她会喜欢这个想法。

“I certainly don’t have any other plans.” 
“我当然没有任何其他计划。”

Kingsley drummed his fingers rapidly on the surface of his desk, looking at Hermione through narrowed eyes. 
金斯利用手指在桌子上快速敲打，眯起眼睛看着赫敏。

“Alright, Hermione. I will see what I can do.” He held up a cautioning finger when Hermione half-rose from her seat in delight. “By that I mean I will put my finger to the wind and see what kind of reaction I can reasonably expect if I suggest showing Lucius Malfoy any kind of mercy. But I can make no promises yet.”
“好吧，赫敏。我会看看我能做些什么。当赫敏高兴地从座位上半站起来时，他举起了一根警告的手指。“我的意思是，如果我建议对卢修斯·马尔福表现出任何形式的怜悯，我会合理地期待什么样的反应。但我还不能做出任何承诺。

“Thank you, Kingsley. I can work with that. I can work with hope.” Hermione said, though a small part of her mind doubted that was actually true. Would hope really be enough for a man like Lucius Malfoy?
“谢谢你，金斯利。我可以处理它。我可以带着希望工作。赫敏说，尽管她心中有一小部分怀疑这是否真的是真的。希望对卢修斯·马尔福这样的男人来说真的足够了吗？

Chapter 6
第 6 章Chapter Summary
本章小结

Hermione returns to Malfoy Manor with her vague offerings from her meeting with Kingsley. Will Kingsley's promise of trying his best to get Malfoy something be enough?
赫敏带着她与金斯莱会面时含糊不清的提议回到马尔福庄园。金斯利承诺尽他最大的努力让马尔福得到一些东西就足够了吗？

注释见本章末尾May 4th
5月4日

When Hermione arrived at Malfoy Manor for the second meeting—a week after the first, as agreed—she was greeted at the front door by a harried looking Draco. He was distractedly trying to button his robes with one hand as he pulled the door open, glancing up at her only to make sure of who he was looking at. 
当赫敏到达马尔福庄园参加第二次会议时——按照约定，在第一次会议的一周后——在前门迎接她的是一个看起来焦急的德拉科。他一边拉开门，一边分心地试图用一只手扣上长袍的扣子，抬头看了她一眼，只是为了确定他正在看谁。

“Granger, punctual as always,” he said, letting go of the door handle to use both hands to fix his collar. “Come in, come in.”
“格兰杰，一如既往的准时，”他说，松开门把手，用双手固定他的衣领。“进来，进来。”

“You seem—”
“你看起来——”

“Late?” he asked. “That’s because I am. Astoria’s check-up at St. Mungo’s has been moved forward by an hour so I’m going to meet her.”
“迟到？”“那是因为我是。阿斯托利亚在圣芒戈医院的检查已经提前了一个小时，所以我要去见她。

His movements became even more irate as his collar wouldn’t lay flat. Before he could do himself an injury, Hermione stepped forward and placed her fingers on the back of his hand. “Malfoy,” she said, taking out her wand. “It will be fine. She will be fine.” Hermione tapped at his collar and it corrected itself with a tight jerking motion that made Draco grimace. “ You will be fine.”
他的动作变得更加愤怒，因为他的衣领不能平放。在他能够伤害自己之前，赫敏走上前，将手指放在他的手背上。“马尔福，”她说，一边掏出她的魔杖。“会没事的。她会没事的。赫敏轻敲了他的衣领，它用一个紧绷的抽搐动作纠正了自己，这让德拉科做了个鬼脸。“你会没事的。”

His shoulders seemed to drop several inches as he exhaled and dragged a hand through his hair. “I know, it’s just—” he cut himself short and shook his head. “Look, I need to get to the Floo but...my father.”
他的肩膀似乎下垂了几英寸，他呼出一口气，一只手拽着他的头发。“我知道，只是——”他打断了自己，摇了摇头。“听着，我需要去飞路，但是......我的父亲。

“We don’t need a supervisor.”
“我们不需要主管。”

“Are you absolutely sure about that?” he asked with a doubtful narrowing of his eyes. “I got a real sense that if I hadn’t been standing in front of them, one of you might have left the building through his study windows last time.”
“你绝对确定吗？” 他疑惑地眯起眼睛问道。“我真的感觉到，如果我没有站在他们面前，你们中的一个人上次可能会从他的书房窗户离开大楼。”

“We’ll be fine .”
“我们会没事的。”

Hermione wasn’t actually sure how firmly she believed that but Draco looked so utterly harassed that she wanted nothing more than for him to get to Astoria to settle his mind. Clearly unconvinced but willing to lie to himself for the sake of an easier life, Draco nodded. 
赫敏其实并不确定她有多坚信这一点，但德拉科看起来是如此彻底的骚扰，以至于她只想让他去阿斯托利亚安抚一下。显然不相信，但为了更轻松的生活，他愿意对自己撒谎，他点了点头。

“Alright. You remember the way to his study, yes? Just up the stairs and…” he trailed off, his hands vaguely directing left and right as he backed away towards a door to the left of them.
“好吧。你还记得去他书房的路，对吧？就在楼梯上......”他慢慢地走开，双手模糊地左右指着，同时他退到他们左边的一扇门里。

“I remember,” she said firmly, pointing to the door and assuming it led to some kind of Floo. “Now go.”
“我记得，”她坚定地说，指着门，假设它导致了某种飞路。“现在走。”

“I’m sure I’ll be back by the time you’re done,” he called over his shoulder before disappearing through the door. “I’ll try to catch you before you go!”
“我确定你做完的时候我会回来的，”他回头喊道，然后消失在门外。“我会在你走之前抓住你！”

The door closed with an echoing clunk and Hermione was left standing in the cavernous entrance hall, her hand clutching the strap of her bag. She had lied; she could not remember the way to Lucius Malfoy’s study. Hogwarts was bigger than Malfoy Manor and she’d managed to learn her way around there, she reasoned to herself. After several years, admittedly, but still. 
门关上了，发出一声回荡的叮当声，留下赫敏站在洞穴般的入口大厅里，她的手紧紧抓住包的带子。她撒了谎;她记不清去卢修斯·马尔福书房的路了。霍格沃茨比马尔福庄园大，她设法在那里学会了自己的方法，她心里想。几年后，诚然，但仍然如此。

With a sigh, Hermione closed the front door and began to make her way up the central staircase knowing that, at least, was the correct start. When the stairs split, she turned right. They had definitely turned right. Reaching the top of the stairs she looked around, gnawing at her lower lip. A vase standing on a pedestal to her left struck her as familiar, so she started down that corridor, the sound of her trainers muffled by the thick carpets. 
赫敏叹了口气，关上了前门，开始沿着中央楼梯走去，她知道，至少，这是正确的开始。当楼梯劈开时，她向右转。他们肯定是向右转的。到达楼梯顶端时，她环顾四周，啃咬着自己的下唇。她左边基座上的一个花瓶让她觉得很熟悉，于是她开始沿着那条走廊走，她的运动鞋的声音被厚厚的地毯掩盖了。

Trying to use her memory of the paintings she’d observed on her first visit, Hermione felt fairly confident that she was moving in the right direction. All she had to do was avoid the cold and curious glares of the paintings’ inhabitants. It was only when she reached a long corridor that she felt sure was the right one—the large window at its end was the tell—that she stopped entirely. There were doors all the way along on either side and she couldn’t for the life of her remember which one was the study. Who had hallways this long in their home? It was ludicrous.
赫敏试图利用她第一次来访时看到的画作的记忆，觉得自己正朝着正确的方向前进。她所要做的就是避开画中居民的冰冷和好奇的目光。直到她走到一条长长的走廊时，她才觉得自己是正确的——走廊尽头的大窗户就是问题所在——她才完全停了下来。两边都有门，她一辈子都记不清哪一扇是书房。谁家里有这么长时间的走廊？这太荒谬了。

Shifting from foot to foot, Hermione considered her options. She could always just try each one and hope that wouldn’t result in walking in on Lucius Malfoy using the toilet or something. Hermione shuddered. She would knock on each one and then try it. 
赫敏从一只脚换到另一只脚，考虑了她的选择。她总是可以尝试每一个，希望这不会导致路修斯·马尔福使用马桶或其他什么东西。赫敏浑身颤抖。她会敲敲每一个，然后尝试一下。

“You there,” said a commanding female voice.
“你在那儿，”一个威严的女声说。

Hermione started, turning left and right on the spot. Eventually, her eyes landed on a painting of a young woman who was giving her an appraising look. The woman was dressed in opulent blue robes, the edges highlighted by glimmering, intricately painted gold stitching. Her deep brown hair fell loose and flowed down to her waist, which had a jewel-encrusted golden belt draped around it. It didn’t matter that the jewels had been painted, Hermione thought they looked ludicrously expensive.

这幅画像仔细地审视着她，显然是想权衡她有多无聊和她有多不愿意帮忙。“很好，”她终于叹了口气，指了指她的框架侧面。“跟我来。”这个女人把她的长袍前襟抬离地面一英寸，开始走向附近的肖像，对居民的抗议完全无动于衷。

赫敏确信卢修斯·马尔福正在考虑他想做的所有事情。她的肚子不舒服地翻动着，提醒着她刚刚激怒了一个危险的男人。如果他决定伤害她的满足感值得失去他所剩无几的自由呢？尤其是因为他并不像她希望的那样执着于把它拿回来。

Her parents were older than that but they had always seemed younger than he did. Probably because they enjoyed life and did nice things. Even if they were now doing them without her or any memory of her.
那个高领子可不舒服，赫敏沉思着，手肘靠在椅子的扶手上，用拳头捂着下巴。他真的让她想起了个老德拉科。至少在表面上是这样。是鼻子。可能还有下巴。虽然她认为他并不老，但确切地说。他得，什么，四十多岁了？也许接近 50 人。她的父母比那年长，但他们似乎总是比他年轻。可能是因为他们享受生活并做了好事。即使他们现在在没有她或她的任何记忆的情况下做这些事情。

He still looked tired but his face wasn’t obviously aged in any way. In fact, when his lips weren’t arranged in a sneer they looked almost—Hermione tilted her head—normal? Hermione was watching him so closely that she didn’t miss the way he shifted in his chair. A sly smile curled at her lips. Perhaps her inspection was finally getting to him. 
他看起来仍然很疲惫，但他的脸上并没有明显的衰老。事实上，当他的嘴唇没有冷笑时，它们看起来几乎——赫敏歪了歪头——正常吗？赫敏一直如此密切地看着他，以至于她没有错过他在椅子上移动的方式。她的嘴角弯起一抹狡猾的笑容。也许她的检查终于找到了他。

With a delicate but deliberately audible sigh, Hermione lowered her hands to her lap and pushed herself to her feet, looking around the office with the air of a woman who didn’t know what to be up to. The kind of woman, she guessed, that would put Lucius Malfoy on edge. Her trainers padded against the stone floor as she wandered the room, the sound becoming more muted when she crossed over the Persian rug. 
赫敏轻轻地叹了口气，把手放到膝盖上，站起身来，以一个不知道该做什么的女人的气势环顾着办公室。她猜想，是什么样的女人会让卢修斯·马尔福紧张不安。她在房间里走来走去，运动鞋垫在石头地板上，当她越过波斯地毯时，声音变得更加柔和。

Hands behind her back, Hermione explored slowly, pausing every few steps to look at a statue or a painting. She noticed there were no portraits in this room. Obviously, he liked his privacy. A finely carved end table was topped with elegant glass bottles and Hermione leaned down to look at them. Alcohol. Probably very expensive and not especially tasty.
赫敏双手背在背后，慢慢地探索着，每走几步就会停下来看一尊雕像或一幅画。她注意到这个房间里没有肖像。显然，他喜欢自己的隐私。一个精雕细琢的茶几上放着优雅的玻璃瓶，赫敏俯下身子看着它们。酒精。可能非常昂贵，而且不是特别好吃。

Stopping by one of his glass cabinets, she kept her hands behind her back and leaned in to inspect the small golden spyglass that was inside on the uppermost shelf. It was covered in delicate etchings and, leaning close enough that her breath fogged the glass, Hermione realised they were constellations. Beautiful .
在他的一个玻璃柜前停下脚步，她双手背在身后，俯身检查最上面架子上里面的金色小望远镜。上面布满了精致的蚀刻画，赫敏靠得足够近，以至于她的呼吸都把玻璃弄得雾蒙蒙的，这让赫敏意识到它们是星座。 美丽。

Feeling eyes on her, Hermione quickly glanced towards the desk but Malfoy appeared to be completely focused on his book. After watching him for a few more seconds, she turned her back on him entirely and wound her way over to the bookcase on the opposite side of his office. It went from the floor to the ceiling and ran along the length of the wall. Many of the books looked extremely old, the lettering on their leather spines worn and hard to read. Briefly forgetting where she was, Hermione drew even closer to the shelves and bent at the waist to look at some of the books lower down. 
赫敏感觉到有人在看着她，迅速地向桌子看了一眼，但马尔福似乎完全专注于他的书。又看了他几秒钟后，她完全背对着他，蜿蜒地走到他办公室对面的书架上。它从地板一直延伸到天花板，沿着墙壁的长度延伸。许多书看起来非常古老，皮革书脊上的字母磨损且难以阅读。赫敏暂时忘记了自己在哪里，她更靠近书架，弯下腰看下面的一些书。

She was reaching out to touch one of them when she heard the unmistakable sound of Lucius Malfoy softly clearing his throat. Snatching her hand back, Hermione straightened up and looked over her shoulder. He wasn’t looking at her, his head still bent over his book. With narrowed eyes, Hermione turned back around and reached for a book on a higher shelf and, once again, just before her fingertips could land on the spine, she heard him clear his throat, more firmly this time. 
她正伸手去摸其中一个人，这时她听到了卢修斯·马尔福轻声清嗓子的声音。赫敏把手抓回来，直起身来，回头看了看。他没有看着她，他的头仍然低着头看他的书。赫敏眯起眼睛，转过身来，伸手去拿高架上的一本书，再一次，就在她的指尖落在书脊上之前，她听到他清了清嗓子，这次更用力了。

Hermione spun around, arms crossed, and glared at him from across the room. He appeared not to notice and kept his focus resolutely on his book. It was sorely tempting to try reaching for a third time but something stopped her. A vague sense of self-preservation, possibly. 
赫敏转过身来，双臂交叉，从房间的另一头瞪着他。他似乎没有注意到，并坚定地将注意力集中在他的书上。她很想尝试第三次伸手，但有什么东西阻止了她。可能是一种模糊的自我保护意识。

Instead, she crossed the room again but made sure to run a casual finger all the way along the top of the leather sofa as she passed it, her eyes fixed on Malfoy. It was gratifying to see him raise a finger up to his temple and rub a small circle there.
相反，她再次穿过房间，但确保在经过真皮沙发时，她的手指随意地沿着皮沙发的顶部一直滑过，她的眼睛盯着马尔福。看到他把一根手指举到太阳穴上，在那里画了一个小圆圈，真是令人欣慰。

“We’re almost at an hour, Mr Malfoy,” Hermione said on reaching his desk. “Are you really going to give up what might be your last opportunity to gain something of your old life back?”
“我们差不多一个小时了，马尔福先生，”赫敏走到他的办公桌前说。“你真的要放弃可能是你最后的机会来找回你以前的生活吗？”

Ever so slowly, he looked up from his book and met her eyes. For a brief second, she thought he might speak but he merely blinked in an uncompromising way that reminded her of Crookshanks on those nights when he’d insisted on sitting across her half-finished essays. Infuriating .
他慢慢地从书中抬起头来，与她的眼睛相遇。有那么一瞬间，她以为他可能会说话，但他只是毫不妥协地眨了眨眼，这让她想起了克鲁克香克斯在那些坚持要坐在她半成品论文面前的夜晚。 令人愤怒。

“Fine,” Hermione snapped, grabbing the Wheezebox and quill to shove them in her bag. “Fine. You can just sit here forever, silent and alone in your study with your books that no one else can touch and never use your magic again. That’s fine by me.”
“好吧，”赫敏厉声说，抓起喘息盒和羽毛笔把它们塞进了她的包里。“好吧。你可以永远坐在这里，安静地、独自一人在你的书房里，拿着你的书，别人不能碰，再也不用你的魔法了。这对我来说很好。

His eyes narrowed as Hermione turned on her heel and marched to the door. On reaching it, she abruptly halted, hand on the handle, and looked down at her bag. Closing his book, Malfoy frowned as he watched her relinquish the handle to rummage inside her bag. Withdrawing some kind of silver package, she marched it over to his desk and tossed it so that it landed with a thump on the wooden surface. As it rolled towards him, Lucius uncrossed his legs and pushed his chair back slightly.
当赫敏转过身来，走向门口时，他眯起了眼睛。当她走到门口时，她突然停了下来，手放在把手上，低头看了看她的包。合上书，马尔福皱起眉头，看着她放下把手，在包里翻找。她掏出某种银包裹，把它带到他的桌子前，把它扔了出去，让它砰地一声落在木头上。当它向他滚来时，卢修斯松开了他的双腿，将他的椅子稍微向后推。

“It’s cake ,” she said in an angry tone that jarred with her words. “I brought it for Astoria so just give it to Draco when you see him. It won’t benefit you in any way but they’ll appreciate it.”
“这是蛋糕，”她用一种与她的话语相悖的愤怒语气说。“我把它带给阿斯托利亚的，所以当你看到德拉科时就把它交给他吧。它不会以任何方式对你有好处，但他们会感激的。

With that, she hauled the door open and slammed it shut behind her hard enough to make the bottles on his end table rattle. Lucius was relaxing back into his chair, eyeing the slab of wrapped cake in front of him with an expression of mild disgust, when he heard a muffled yelp of frustrated rage from down the hall. He stared at the door and then, curling his right hand into a fist and pressing the knuckle of his forefinger to his lips, he allowed himself a single, quiet snort of amusement before picking up his quill to resume his writing.  
说完，她把门拉开，砰的一声关上了，砰的一声关上了，以至于他茶几上的瓶子都发出了嘎嘎作响的声音。卢修斯正放松地坐回椅子上，用略带厌恶的表情盯着面前的一块包裹好的蛋糕，这时他听到大厅里传来一声沮丧的愤怒的低沉叫喊。他盯着门口，然后，右手捏成拳头，食指指节贴在嘴唇上，他让自己安静地哼了一声，然后拿起羽毛笔继续他的写作。

Chapter 7
第 7 章Chapter Summary
本章小结

Draco attempts to talk Lucius around and Hermione and Ginny discuss the difficulties of dealing with a man like Lucius Malfoy.
德拉科试图说服卢修斯，赫敏和金妮讨论与卢修斯·马尔福这样的男人打交道的困难。

Chapter Notes
章节注释

Honestly, thank you so much for the positive reactions to the last chapter! I was all aflutter. The portrait will be back a few times. I love her, as I love everyone that's been kind enough to read this.
老实说，非常感谢您对上一章的积极反应！我浑身发抖。肖像会回来几次。我爱她，就像我爱所有好心阅读这篇文章的人一样。

Hermione allowed herself a restrained scream of frustration into her hands when she was halfway down the corridor. He was a nightmare . A man his age using the silent treatment of all things. 
赫敏在走廊走到一半时，让自己克制地发出沮丧的尖叫。他简直是一场噩梦。一个他这个年纪的人，对万物无声处理。

“I did tell you!” called the portrait who had led her to Malfoy’s study. 
“我确实告诉过你了！”

“I tried ,” Hermione snapped as she passed, not wishing to stop to talk any longer than she had to. God forbid he overhear her lingering.
“我试过了，”赫敏在经过时厉声说，她不想停下来再多说一会儿。上帝保佑他偷听她徘徊不去。

Allowing her storming pace to slow slightly as she wound her way back through the manor, Hermione tried to ignore the annoying roiling in her stomach. Alright, so she had promised him something that she couldn’t give him right away. Really, she was aware that she shouldn’t have. But couldn’t he see that he might get what he wanted if he just helped her a little first? He was going to need to help her either way if he did want anything. Besides, he was the one who had been a Death Eater; he should be proving himself.
赫敏在蜿蜒穿过庄园时，让她暴风雨的步伐稍微放慢了一点，她试图无视她胃里恼人的翻腾。好吧，所以她答应了他一些她不能马上给他的东西。真的，她知道她不应该这样做。但是他难道看不到，如果他先帮助她一点，他可能会得到他想要的东西吗？如果他真的想要什么，他无论如何都需要帮助她。此外，他就是那个曾经是食死徒的人; 他应该证明自己。

The further she got from the study, the more a tide of embarrassment eroded Hermione’s anger and her internal self-justifications started to fade. She could barely believe that she had let him and his petulance get the best of her. Had she slammed the door? God . It was just that she’d spent so long on researching the stupid oral history and she wanted it to be right . To be thorough. 
她越是远离书房，一股尴尬的浪潮就越是侵蚀了赫敏的愤怒，她内心的自我辩解也开始消退。她几乎不敢相信，她竟然让他和他的任性占了上风。她关上了门吗？ 神。只是她花了这么长时间研究那些愚蠢的口述历史，她希望它是正确的。要彻底。

By the time she reached the entrance hall, Hermione wanted nothing more than to go home and eat a slab of the lemon cake she had made. As she descended the stairs, eyes fixed on the front door and freedom, Draco appeared in the entrance hall, looking in much better spirits than when he had left. 
当她到达门厅时，赫敏只想回家吃一块她做的柠檬蛋糕。当她走下楼梯时，眼睛盯着前门和自由，德拉科出现在门厅里，看起来比他离开时精神好多了。

“You made it through the hour!” he called up to her, clapping his hands and then stopping mid-step. “He’s not dead up there, is he?”
“你熬过了一个小时！”他向她喊道，拍了拍手，然后在半步中停了下来。“他没有死在那儿，对吧？”

“No,” Hermione grumbled, coming down the last of the stairs to meet him in the hall. “He sounds like he could be, though.”
“不，”赫敏抱怨着，从楼梯的最后一层走下来，在大厅里迎接他。“不过，他听起来可能是。”

Draco frowned. “What happened?”
德拉科皱起眉头。“发生了什么事？”

“I couldn’t get Kingsley to guarantee anything,” Hermione said, impatiently sweeping some hair from her forehead. “And you were right: your father wants assurances.”
“我没法让金斯莱保证什么，”赫敏说，不耐烦地扫了扫额头上的一些头发。“你是对的：你爸爸想要保证。”

“Well, what did Shacklebolt say?” Draco asked, his frown deepening as he folded his arms.
“嗯，沙克尔说了什么？”德拉科问道，他交叠着双臂，眉头皱得更深了。

“He said he’d see what he can do.”
“他说他会看看他能做什么。”

“But he didn’t say no?”
“但他没有说不？”

“Well, no, but he didn’t say yes either. So your father is out. We sat in silence for an hour because I was stupid enough to think that I could out-stubborn a man who is capable of clinging to patently ludicrous prejudices for multiple decades.”
“嗯，没有，但他也没有说是。所以你爸爸出去了。我们沉默地坐了一个小时，因为我愚蠢到认为我可以打败一个能够坚持几十年明显荒谬的偏见的人。

Draco pressed his lips together to form a thin line. “I’ll speak to him.”
德拉科把嘴唇紧紧地抿在一起，形成一条细线。“我会和他谈谈。”

“Malfoy I’m really not sure it’s even worth—”
“马尔福，我真的不确定这是否值得——”

“ I’ll speak to him,” he said more firmly. “Wait for my owl.”
“我会和他谈谈，”他更坚定地说。“等我的猫头鹰。”

Reluctant to fan the small spark of hope that Draco’s determined expression lit in her belly, Hermione nodded and changed the subject. “The appointment went okay?”
赫敏不愿意煽动德拉科坚定的表情在她肚子里点燃的希望之火，她点了点头，改变了话题。“预约还好吗？”

“Swimmingly,” Draco smiled. “Mother and baby are doing well. They’re still not entirely sure how Astoria’s blood curse will impact her after the birth but they’re satisfied at the moment.”
“游泳，”德拉科微笑着。“妈妈和宝宝都很好。他们仍然不完全确定阿斯托利亚的血诅咒在她出生后会有什么影响，但他们现在很满意。

“That’s wonderful news. I don’t like to say ‘I told you so’—”
“这是个好消息。我不喜欢说'我早就告诉过你了'——”

“Oh, you absolutely do Granger.”
“哦，你绝对喜欢格兰杰。”

“But I did tell you so,” Hermione finished with a soft smile. “I left some more lemon cake with your father.”
“但我确实告诉你了，”赫敏温柔地笑着说完。“我又给你爸爸留了一些柠檬蛋糕。”

Raising a single eyebrow, Draco turned his head sceptically. “He took the cake from you?”
Draco挑了挑眉毛，怀疑地转过头来。“他从你那里拿走了蛋糕？”

“He didn’t have a choice,” Hermione muttered darkly. “Anyway, I’ll be off. Don’t worry too much about your dad, Malfoy. If he’s really not interested in speaking to me, there’s no point in forcing the matter. That’s not really what this work is supposed to be about.”
“他别无选择，”赫敏阴沉地咕哝着。“不管怎样，我要走了。别太担心你爸爸，马尔福。如果他真的不想和我说话，那么强迫这件事就没有意义了。这并不是这件作品的真正意义所在。

With a wave over her shoulder, Hermione exited the manor looking far more dispirited than when she had entered it.
赫敏在肩膀上挥了挥手，走出了庄园，看起来比她进来时要沮丧得多。

“I hope you’re pleased with yourself.”
“我希望你对自己满意。”

Lucius Malfoy looked up from his parchment to see his son standing in the doorway to his office, hand on the doorknob and a very grim expression on his face. He was obviously talking about the Granger girl and Lucius allowed a corner of his lips to twitch upwards in vindictive amusement.
卢修斯·马尔福从羊皮纸上抬起头来，看到他的儿子站在办公室的门口，手扶着门把手，脸上露出非常严峻的表情。他显然在谈论格兰杰女孩，卢修斯让他的嘴角在报复性的逗乐中向上抽搐。

“I confess, I am.” 
“我承认，我是。”

“You actually are aren’t you?” Draco asked, disbelieving, as he stepped into the room and closed the door behind him. “You’re genuinely pleased that you pushed a twenty-six year old witch to the end of her tether.”
“你真的是，不是吗？”德拉科不敢置信地问道，他走进房间，关上了身后的门。“你真的很高兴你把一个二十六岁的女巫推到了她枷锁的尽头。”

Lucius rolled his eyes and set his quill down on his desk. Clearly he wasn’t going to be allowed to get much more done. “I have so few diversions these days, Draco. Indulge me.”
卢修斯翻了个白眼，把羽毛笔放在桌子上。显然，他不会被允许完成更多工作。“这些天我很少有消遣的地方，德拉科。放纵我吧。

Draco scoffed, making his way across the room towards the table of expensive whiskeys. Lucius eyed his son’s back as he lifted a bottle, read the label, and pulled out the cork with a pop . 
德拉科嗤之以鼻，穿过房间走向那桌昂贵的威士忌。卢修斯看着儿子的背影，他举起一个瓶子，读了看标签，啪的一声拔出了软木塞。

“You’re lucky she didn’t hex you,” Draco said, glancing over his shoulder. “Or punch you,” he added as a quiet afterthought. At that Lucius raised his eyebrows, though the idea that physical violence was something Mudbloods might often resort to didn’t especially surprise him. They would be comfortable rolling in the earth. 
“你很幸运，她没有对你下咒，”德拉科说，回头瞥了一眼他的肩膀。“或者打你一拳，”他事后悄悄地补充道。听到这话，卢修斯扬起了眉毛，尽管泥巴种可能经常采取身体暴力的想法并没有让他特别惊讶。他们会很舒服地在地上打滚。

Turning on his heel, Draco approached with two glasses of whiskey in hand, sliding one across the desk towards Lucius who accepted it without comment. Lifting the glass and estimating a generous three-finger measure, Lucius downed it all in one without a change in his expression. As he sat the glass down with a satisfied sigh, he saw his son looking at him with a small frown.
德拉科转过身来，手里拿着两杯威士忌走过来，其中一杯滑过桌子，走向卢修斯，卢修斯一言不发地接过了它。卢修斯举起酒杯，估算了一下慷慨的三指量量，一口气喝下了酒，表情没有变化。当他满意地叹息着坐下杯子时，他看到他的儿子皱着眉头看着他。

“What?” Lucius said, his tone on the edge of being snappish.
“什么？”卢修斯说，他的语气几乎显得生硬。

“Are you really not going to cooperate with her?” Draco asked, sinking into the chair that Granger had vacated.
“你真的不打算和她合作吗？”德拉科问道，一头扎进了格兰杰腾出的椅子上。

“She made promises she couldn’t keep and I didn’t make any promises at all. Don’t act as though I’m the one in the wrong.”
“她做出了她无法兑现的承诺，我根本没有做出任何承诺。别装作我是错的那个人。

“Shacklebolt didn’t turn her request down, though,” Draco said, lifting his forefinger from his glass to point it at his father. “If you behave yourself and help her with this, he might be swayed to do something for you.”
“不过，沙克尔没有拒绝她的请求，”德拉科说，从杯子里拿起食指，指向他的父亲。“如果你表现得好并帮助她，他可能会动摇为你做点什么。”

“I find it hard to be tempted by ‘maybe’s and ‘might be’s, Draco,” Lucius said, waving a dismissive hand. “I would rather retain the little dignity I have left than bare my soul to an undeserving Mudblood just for the mere chance of the taste of a crumb of freedom.”
“我发现很难被'也许'和'可能'所诱惑，德拉科，”卢修斯说，不屑一顾地挥了挥手。“我宁愿保留我所剩无几的尊严，也不愿把我的灵魂暴露给一个不配的泥巴种，只为了尝尝一粒自由的机会。”

Draco was quiet as he took a long drink. Lowering his glass and cradling it against his stomach, he tilted his head to give his father a piercing look. “Don’t you want to be able to visit mother?”
德拉科喝了一大口酒，很安静。他放下酒杯，把杯子贴在肚子上，歪着头狠狠地瞪了父亲一眼。“你不想去看望妈妈吗？”

卢修斯的鼻孔张开了，他瞬间咬紧了牙关。“没有什么能阻止她来这里，”他说，声音冰冷。“从来没有。”

“也没有什么能诱惑她，”德拉科厉声说，让他的父亲迅速眨了眨眼。这差不多是他几乎要退缩的程度。德拉科的语气变成了指责。“你要放弃了。”

“I am not.”
“我不是。”

“Yes, you are. You’d rather cloister yourself in this study for the next half century or so than try anything that might improve your circumstances. Do you know how depressing that is to witness? From you of all people?”
“是的，你是。你宁愿在接下来的半个世纪左右的时间里把自己封闭在这项研究中，也不愿尝试任何可能改善你情况的事情。你知道目睹那件事有多令人沮丧吗？从你们所有人中出来的吗？

“I do not live to please you, Draco,” Lucius said, his voice quiet but simmering with anger.
“我活着不是为了取悦你，德拉科，”卢修斯说，他的声音很平静，但充满了愤怒。

“Obviously not,” Draco said, his patience worn thin, “but the least you could do is live to please yourself .”
“显然不是，”德拉科说，他的耐心逐渐消磨殆尽，“但你至少能做的就是活着取悦自己。

“I am fine.”
“我很好。”

“You’re miserable .” 
“你真可怜。”

“And you are my son ,” Lucius growled. “You have no right to speak to me in such a manner.”
“而你是我的儿子，”卢修斯咆哮道。“你没有权利用这种方式跟我说话。”

With a sigh, Draco sat whiskey on the table with more force than he intended. “I care about you, father.”
德拉科叹了口气，用比他想象的更大的力气把威士忌放在桌子上。“我很关心你，爸爸。”

Lucius had nothing to say to that but he shifted in his seat and broke eye contact with his son, a sign of his mild to extreme discomfort. The love had always been there between the Malfoys; it was just rarely verbally expressed. As was proper. Astoria had ruined that with all her well-intentioned declarations and conversations. Lucius could still remember the first time she’d attempted to instigate a ‘heart-to-heart’, as she’d called it. The look on her face when he’d told her he didn’t have one was a memory he cherished. The resultant telling off he got from Draco he cherished less.
卢修斯对此无话可说，但他在座位上挪动了一下，中断了与儿子的眼神交流，这是他轻微到极度不适的迹象。马尔福夫妇之间的爱一直存在;只是很少用口头表达。这是正确的。阿斯托利亚用她所有善意的声明和对话毁掉了这一点。卢修斯仍然记得她第一次试图煽动她所说的“心连心”是什么时候。当他告诉她他没有口罩时，她脸上的表情是他珍惜的回忆。他从德拉科那里得到的告别让他不那么珍惜了。
