“你就不能试试和格兰杰合作吗？”德拉科恳求道。“如果你这样做了，你可能会找回一些以前的生活。如果它开始看起来你不会，你可以......退出。撤回您的同意。

“As though she’d allow that to happen once she had me in her claws.”
“就好像一旦她把我抓在爪子里，她就会允许这种情况发生。”

“She’d have to,” Draco said, lifting his glass to take another gulp of whiskey and wincing as it burned on its way down. “She’s all ethical and stuff. Hates the idea of wronging anyone. Ranted about it for ages before she interviewed me.”
“她得这么做，”德拉科说，举起酒杯又喝了一口威士忌，当威士忌在喝下去的时候，他皱起了眉头。“她很有道德。讨厌冤枉任何人的想法。在她采访我之前，我为此咆哮了很长时间。

“Does she do that often?”
“她经常这样做吗？”

Draco didn’t miss the tired apprehension in his father’s voice and couldn’t stop the small smile that came to his lips; Granger probably came close to a living nightmare for Lucius Malfoy.
德拉科没有错过他父亲声音中疲惫的忧虑，也挡不住他嘴角的一丝微笑;格兰杰可能差点成为卢修斯·马尔福的活生生的噩梦。

“Do what?”
“做什么？”

“ Rant ,” Lucius said impatiently.
“咆哮，”卢修斯不耐烦地说。

“She can do,” Draco shrugged. “If you push the wrong buttons. The stick she’s got up her arse is kind of different to the one you’ve got up yours, so it might take you some time to figure out what those are.”
“她能做到，”德拉科耸耸肩。“如果你按错了按钮。她插在屁股上的棍子和你插在屁股上的棍子有点不同，所以你可能需要一些时间来弄清楚那些是什么。

“Draco.” Lucius’ voice was low with warning and utterly devoid of amusement but Draco was pleased and slightly giddy; they were having the most frank conversation they’d had in months, maybe even years. He’d missed it. He’d have to send Granger flowers.
“德拉科。”卢修斯的声音低沉而警告，完全没有乐趣，但德拉科很高兴，略带头晕;他们正在进行几个月，甚至几年来最坦率的对话。他错过了。他得给格兰杰送花。

“I’ll write to her and invite her back,” Draco pushed. “You don’t have to.” 
“我会写信给她，邀请她回来，”德拉科推搡道。“你不必这样做。”

Lucius didn’t say anything. Instead he opened a drawer in his desk and retrieved a foil wrapped package from within. Depositing it on the wooden surface with a sneer of distaste, he pushed it towards his son with the tip of his finger. 
卢修斯什么也没说。相反，他打开了书桌上的一个抽屉，从里面拿出了一个用铝箔包裹的包裹。他不满地一笑，将它放在木头上，用指尖把它推向儿子。

“She left this. For you.” 
“她离开了这个。为了你。

Reaching across the table, Draco grabbed the cake with a pleased smile and lifted it into his lap. “Do you want to try some?” he asked, pointing down at it. “It’s very good.”
Draco伸手越过桌子，带着满意的笑容抓住蛋糕，把它举到他的腿上。“你想尝尝吗？” 他指着它问道。“这非常好。”

Lucius gave him a look that suggested he’d rather choke and Draco sighed, shaking his head. “I’ll write to her. We’ll give this one more try.”
卢修斯看了他一眼，似乎他宁愿窒息，德拉科叹了口气，摇了摇头。“我会写信给她。我们会再试一次。

To his relief, though Lucius didn’t consent, he also didn’t protest. Draco suspected it was because he was already formulating a plan to ruin the next meeting but that was Granger’s problem, not his.
令他松了一口气的是，虽然卢修斯不同意，但他也没有抗议。德拉科怀疑这是因为他已经在制定一个破坏下一次会议的计划，但那是格兰杰的问题，不是他的问题。

When Hermione arrived home and closed her front door behind her with a tired sigh, she vaguely wondered whether she had any of that red wine left in the cupboard and if it would pair well with a huge slab of lemon cake. It seemed like a stretch but she had the kind of pain forming in her head that could only be cured by questionable food choices.
当赫敏回到家，疲惫地叹了口气关上前门时，她隐约想知道她橱柜里有没有留下那杯红酒，它是否能与一大块柠檬蛋糕搭配。这似乎有点牵强，但她的脑海中形成了那种痛苦，只有通过有问题的食物选择才能治愈。

Stepping into the kitchen, Hermione came to an abrupt halt when she saw that the cake she had made was no longer on the counter where she had left it. Frowning, Hermione half-turned in the doorway when she heard the clink of cutlery meeting porcelain from the living room. 
走进厨房，赫敏看到她做的蛋糕已经不在她放下的柜台上，戛然而止。赫敏皱着眉头，在门口半转身，这时她听到了客厅里餐具与瓷器相遇的叮当声。

Ginny Potter was reclined on her sofa, a plate piled with cake balanced on her growing belly while she delicately picked at it with a fork. On the coffee table, Hermione spied the rest of the cake in the tin in which she’d placed it that morning. 
金妮·波特斜靠在沙发上，一个堆满蛋糕的盘子在她不断增长的肚子上保持平衡，而她则用叉子小心翼翼地挑选着它。在咖啡桌上，赫敏在她那天早上放蛋糕的罐子里偷偷摸摸地吃了蛋糕。

“My mouse problem has gotten a lot more human, it seems,” Hermione said drily.  
“看来，我的老鼠问题变得更像人了，”赫敏冷淡地说。

Ginny jumped and swore at the unexpected sound of Hermione’s voice, catching her plate before it could slide onto the floor. 
金妮听到赫敏出乎意料的声音，跳了起来，咒骂着，在她的盘子滑到地板上之前接住了她的盘子。

“I’m sorry,” she said with a grimace. “I ate all the cake you brought last week and I sensed that you had more.”
“对不起，”她做了个鬼脸说。“我吃掉了你上周带来的所有蛋糕，我感觉到你吃得更多。”

“ How ?”
“怎么？”

“I honestly don’t know, I just felt it. A sixth sense.” Ginny shrugged and ate another forkful of cake. “In my stomach. And then I decided to hang around because my mum is looking after James and it’s so quiet in your flat. Do you know how quiet it is in your flat?”
“老实说，我不知道，我只是感觉到了。第六感。金妮耸耸肩，又吃了一叉蛋糕。“在我的肚子里。然后我决定四处闲逛，因为我妈妈在照顾 James，而且你的公寓里很安静。你知道你公寓里有多安静吗？

Slinking into the room, Hermione dropped her bag onto the floor and collapsed onto the sofa beside Ginny with her eyes closed. There was a brief pause and a sweet lemony smell drifted under Hermione’s nose. When she opened her eyes, she found that Ginny had lifted the plate of cake up to her face. 
赫敏溜进房间，把包丢在地板上，闭着眼睛瘫倒在金妮旁边的沙发上。短暂的停顿，一股甜美的柠檬味在赫敏的鼻子下飘荡。当她睁开眼睛时，她发现金妮已经把蛋糕盘举到了她的脸上。

“You look like you need some,” she said gently.
“你看起来需要一些，”她温柔地说。

With a sideways glare in Ginny’s direction, Hermione picked up a loose lump of cake and dropped it into her mouth. “I do.”
赫敏侧头瞪了金妮一眼，捡起一块松散的蛋糕，丢进了嘴里。“我愿意。”

“Where were you?”
“你在哪儿？”

“Malfoy Manor.”
“马尔福庄园。”

Ginny’s expression darkened. “Oh.” She withdrew the plate of cake to cradle it protectively between her chest and stomach. “So you did meet him, then?”
金妮的脸色变得阴沉起来。“哦。”她抽出那盘蛋糕，把它安全地抱在她的胸口和腹部之间。“那么，你真的见过他吗？”

Hermione nodded wearily.
赫敏疲惫地点点头。

“Based on your general demeanour I’m going to guess that he’s just as much of a knob as he’s always been.”
“根据你的一般举止，我猜他和以前一样是个笨蛋。”

“ Ding ding ,” Hermione said. “Correct. You don’t win a prize.” 
“叮叮，”赫敏说。“是的。你不会赢得奖品。

“Thought so,” Ginny said through a mouthful of cake. “Merlin forbid a Malfoy be humbled.” 
“是这么想的，”金妮含着一口蛋糕说。“梅林禁止马尔福谦卑。”

Nodding in agreement, Hermione rolled her head to the side to fix Ginny with a pleading look. “I’m going to tell you something and I don’t want you to be angry at me.”
赫敏点头表示同意，然后把头转向一边，用恳求的眼神看着金妮。“我要告诉你一些事情，我不想让你对我生气。”

“Why would you say the word ‘angry’ and therefore make me think of anger if you don’t want me to be angry Hermione?” Ginny asked, her eyes wide. “Honestly, show some sense.” Ginny eyed her penitent friend speculatively. “Go on then, what have you done?”
“如果你不想让我生气，你为什么还要说'生气'这个词，从而让我想起生气呢，赫敏？”金妮睁大了眼睛问道。“老实说，表现出一些理智。”金妮投机地看着她忏悔的朋友。“那么，你做了什么？”

Wearing a thoroughly and appropriately remorseful expression, Hermione explained the request she’d made of Kingsley and the events of her meetings with Lucius Malfoy to Ginny, whose own face did not move through the entire story. Hermione noted, however, that the pace of her cake eating markedly increased.
赫敏带着彻底而恰当的懊悔表情，向金妮解释了她对金斯莱的要求以及她与卢修斯·马尔福会面的事件，而金妮自己的面孔在整个故事中都没有移动。然而，赫敏注意到她吃蛋糕的速度明显加快了。

“I’m not angry,” Ginny said soothingly, though Hermione sensed a biting undertone that grew worse as her friend went on. “I just don’t understand why you’d want to give that pale, pompous arsehole a single inch after everything he’s done! But I’m not angry .”
“我不生气，”金妮安抚地说，尽管赫敏感觉到一种尖锐的语气，随着她朋友的继续，这种语气越来越严重。“我就是不明白你为什么要在他做完所有事情后给那个苍白、浮夸的屁眼一英寸！但我不生气。

Raising an eyebrow, Hermione gave Ginny a thoroughly sceptical look. “Okay,” Ginny acknowledged, pointing her fork in Hermione’s direction. “I am a bit angry. But, honestly, you look so pathetic I’m struggling to work it up into anything significant. And the cake is helping. If I kill you, I don’t get any more. It’s really that simple.”
赫敏挑了挑眉毛，彻底怀疑地看了金妮一眼。“好吧，”金妮承认道，用叉子指着赫敏的方向。“我有点生气。但是，老实说，你看起来太可怜了，我正在努力把它变成任何重要的事情。蛋糕是有帮助的。如果我杀了你，我就得不到更多了。真的就是这么简单。

“I thought if I offered him something he’s likely to want, he’d give me what I want.”
“我想，如果我给他他可能想要的东西，他就会给我我想要的东西。”

“I don’t know why you didn’t just lie to him.”
“我不知道你为什么不直接对他撒谎。”

Frowning, Hermione pushed herself up to sit slightly straighter and fixed Ginny with a curious stare. “What?”
赫敏皱着眉头，把自己撑起来，稍微坐直了一点，用好奇的目光注视着金妮。“什么？”

“When he asked what Kingsley said,” Ginny said as though she was explaining something extremely basic to someone who was being maddeningly obtuse, “you should have just told him what he wanted to hear. ‘Yes, you monstrous blonde prick, if you do this you’ll get your wand back and you’ll be as free as a bird.’ Easy.”
“当他问金斯莱说了什么时，”金妮说，仿佛她在向一个疯狂的迟钝的人解释一些非常基本的事情，“你应该直接告诉他他想听的话。是的，你这个可怕的金发小混蛋，如果你这样做了，你就会拿回你的魔杖，你会像鸟一样自由。很简单。

“I couldn’t do that.”
“我不能那样做。”

“Why? We both know he’d do that.”
“为什么？我们都知道他会那样做。

“Did you just hear yourself? You used the likely behaviour of Lucius Malfoy as a justification for why I should do something.”
“你刚才听到了吗？你用卢修斯·马尔福可能的行为作为我为什么要做某事的理由。

“Don’t tell me you’d feel bad about doing it, Hermione.” Ginny’s lips were curled into a doubtful smirk and Hermione shifted uncomfortably. “Not to him.”
“别告诉我你这样做会觉得很糟糕，赫敏。”金妮的嘴唇弯成一个疑惑的笑容，赫敏不舒服地动了动。“对他来说不是。”

“Well, it wouldn’t really be right, would it?”
“嗯，这真的不对，对吧？”

Clearing her throat, Ginny lowered her fork and placed it on her plate with the purpose of a woman about to deliver a stirring speech. “Was it right when he supported Voldemort? Or when he slipped that Horcrux into my cauldron? Or when he hunted us through the Department of Mysteries? Or when he stood back and allowed you to be tortured—” 
清了清嗓子，金妮放下叉子，把它放在她的盘子里，目的是一个即将发表激动人心的演讲的女人。“他支持伏地魔是对的吗？或者当他把魂器塞进我的大锅里时？或者当他通过神秘事务司追捕我们时？或者当他退后一步，任由你受折磨时——”

Hermione held her hand up. “Alright, alright. Good point, well made.”
赫敏举起了手。“好吧，好吧。说得好，做得很好。

“Honestly, Hermione, fuck him,” Ginny spat, lifting her fork again and stabbing it into the air as though Lucius Malfoy was right in front of her. “I’d have told him whatever he wanted to hear and used him for all he’s worth—which, by the way, is very little. It’s what he’d do and, more to the point, it’s what he deserves.”
“老实说，赫敏，操他，”金妮啐了一口，再次举起她的叉子，把它刺向空中，仿佛卢修斯·马尔福就在她面前。“他想听什么我就告诉他什么，然后用他的一切价值——顺便说一句，这可不值一提。这是他会做的，更重要的是，这是他应得的。

Ginny’s logic was ruthless but Hermione found she couldn’t entirely disagree with it. If she’d only been more willing to lead Lucius Malfoy on a merry dance, she might already be on the road to having what she wanted. The problem was, she wouldn’t feel good about it. It wouldn’t be right . While Hermione contemplated the hurdle of her own soft-heartedness, an owl appeared at her living room window and began tapping at the glass. 
金妮的逻辑很无情，但赫敏发现她不能完全不同意。如果她更愿意带领卢修斯·马尔福跳一场快乐的舞蹈，她可能已经走上了拥有她想要的东西的道路上。问题是，她不会对此感到好受。这不对。当赫敏思考自己心软的障碍时，一只猫头鹰出现在她客厅的窗户前，开始敲打玻璃。

She and Ginny shared a curious look before twisting in the direction of the window as the tapping became more insistent. After a brief delay in which she registered what she was seeing, Hermione jumped to her feet. It was Draco’s owl.
她和金妮好奇地看了一眼，然后随着敲击声变得更加坚持，她扭向窗户的方向。在她记录了她所看到的短暂延迟后，赫敏跳了起来。那是德拉科的猫头鹰。

“Eager,” Ginny murmured, tucking her feet in as Hermione clambered over her to get to the window. 
“急切，”金妮喃喃自语，在赫敏爬过她爬到窗户前时，她把脚塞进去。

The owl hopped onto the windowsill and patiently waited for Hermione to untie the letter it was carrying. She thanked it with a small pat on its head and allowed it to fly away before tearing open the parchment.
猫头鹰跳到窗台上，耐心地等着赫敏解开它手里的信。她轻轻拍了拍它的头，感谢它，让它飞走了，然后撕开了羊皮纸。

“Granger,
“格兰杰，

Come back at the same time next week. We can give this one more try. Please.
下周同一时间回来。我们可以再试一次。请。

D. Malfoy.” 
D. 马尔福。

“Well, what does it say?” Ginny asked, craning her neck as though she might be able to see through the parchment.
“嗯，上面写了什么？”金妮问道，伸长脖子，仿佛她能看穿羊皮纸。

Hermione looked up with a triumphant smile. “It says this isn’t over.”
赫敏抬起头来，露出得意的笑容。“它说这还没有结束。”

Ginny groaned aloud and rolled her neck so that her head was pressed back against the sofa cushion behind her. “You are a glutton for punishment, Hermione Granger.”
金妮大声呻吟着，扭动着脖子，使她的头向后压在身后的沙发垫上。“你是个贪吃惩罚的人，赫敏·格兰杰。”

May 11th
5月11日

“Third time’s the charm,” Hermione said with a toothy grin in the direction of a reluctantly amused Draco Malfoy. 
“第三次是魅力所在，”赫敏对着不情愿地被逗乐的德拉科·马尔福咧嘴一笑。

Once again, she was standing on the front steps of Malfoy Manor, leather satchel slung over her shoulder while the spring sun shone on her back. Technically, this was going to be her third meeting with Lucius Malfoy but she had decided to think of it as their first official meeting. A fresh start. 
她又一次站在马尔福庄园的台阶上，皮包挎在肩上，春日的阳光照在她的背上。从技术上讲，这将是她与卢修斯·马尔福的第三次会面，但她决定将其视为他们的第一次正式会面。一个新的开始。

“Dial down the optimism before you go up there,” Draco said drily, stepping back to welcome her into the hall. “He’ll take it as a challenge.”
“在你上去之前，先把乐观情绪调低一点，”德拉科干巴巴地说，一边退后一步欢迎她进大厅。“他会把它当作一个挑战。”

“I watched footage of flowing water for forty-five minutes before coming here.”
“在来到这里之前，我看了 45 分钟的流水镜头。”

They began to climb the stairs together, Draco throwing Hermione a curious sidelong look as they went. “Er, why?”
他们开始一起爬楼梯，德拉科在他们走的时候好奇地侧头看了赫敏一眼。“呃，为什么？”

“I read somewhere that it makes you serene.”
“我在某处读到，它让你感到平静。”

“Sounds more like a good way to end up needing the loo to me,” he muttered.
“听起来更像是我最终需要厕所的好方法，”他咕哝道。

“Yes,” Hermione said vaguely. “It’s also actually quite annoying; I don’t think meditation is for me.”
“是的，”赫敏含糊地说。“这实际上也很烦人;我认为冥想不适合我。

“I could have told you that, Granger. Really glad you riled yourself up before coming here - such a great idea.”
“我本来可以告诉你的，格兰杰。真的很高兴你在来这里之前激怒了自己——真是个好主意。

“Well, that wasn’t my intention,” Hermione snapped. 
“嗯，那不是我的本意，”赫敏厉声说。

Draco raised his eyebrows at her with a pointed look and she closed her mouth with a click of her teeth, a frustrated blush rising on her cheeks. 
德拉科用尖锐的眼神看着她扬起眉毛，她咔嚓一声咬住了嘴，脸颊上泛起了沮丧的红晕。

“Should I sit in again?”
“我应该再坐一次吗？”

Hermione considered his offer and then shook her head. “No...no. I think perhaps it should just be us. I know he’s your father but having an audience can sometimes make people either hold back or perform. I don’t want him to do that.”
赫敏考虑了一下他的提议，然后摇了摇头。“不......不。我想也许应该只是我们。我知道他是你的父亲，但有观众有时会让人们要么退缩，要么表演。我不希望他那样做。

“Are you sure about that?”
“你确定吗？”

She shot him a grim smile, “Unfortunately, yes.”
她向他露出一个严肃的笑容，“很遗憾，是的。

“Alright then, Granger.” They stopped outside of the study and Draco swept his arm towards the door. “Have fun.” Shoving his hands into his pockets, he turned lightly on his heel and strolled back down the corridor with the carefree gait of a man who had just been gifted an afternoon free of sniping. 
“好吧，格兰杰。”他们在书房外停了下来，德拉科用手臂扫向门口。“玩得开心。”他把手口袋，轻轻地转过身来，以一个刚刚被赐予一个没有狙击的下午的男人的无忧无虑的步态沿着走廊走回去。

Knocking sharply on the door, Hermione didn’t wait for a response before opening it and walking into the room. She stopped short, a puzzled expression on her face as she looked at the desk. There was no one there. Pulling her chin down towards her neck with a frown, Hermione fractionally bent her knees as though preparing to look under the desk.
赫敏猛地敲了敲门，不等回应，就打开门走进了房间。她停了下来，看着桌子，脸上露出困惑的表情。那里没有人。赫敏皱着眉头，把下巴往脖子上拉，微微弯曲了膝盖，仿佛准备看看桌子下面。

“Looking for something, Miss Granger?”
“找什么东西，格兰杰小姐？”

Hermione jumped to attention at the sound of the voice and spun to the right, finding Lucius Malfoy standing by his bookcase on the other side of the room, a book balanced open in his right hand while his left hovered over the pages.
赫敏听到这个声音，猛地转过身来，向右转身，发现卢修斯·马尔福站在房间另一边的书架旁，右手拿着一本书，左手悬停在书页上。

“Oh,” she said, pointing in the direction of his desk and then at him, “But you’re...I didn’t think…”
“哦，”她说，指着他桌子的方向，然后指着他，“但你......我没想过......”

Hermione trailed off, feeling rather stupid as Malfoy’s eyebrows rose up his forehead expectantly. With one hand, he snapped the book closed and returned it to the shelf without taking his eyes from her. What was she going to say? ‘Oh, I thought you only existed in that portion of the room’? Or, ‘Don’t you disintegrate when you move beyond the rug’?
赫敏慢慢走开，当马尔福的眉毛期待地扬起他的额头时，她觉得自己相当愚蠢。他用一只手啪地合上了书，然后把它放回书架上，目光没有从她身上移开。她要说什么呢？“哦，我以为你只存在于房间的那个部分”？“或者，”当你走出地毯时，你不会瓦解吗“？

“Never mind,” Hermione muttered, moving towards her usual chair. “Good afternoon, Mr Malfoy.”
“没关系，”赫敏咕哝着，走向她平常的椅子。“下午好，马尔福先生。”

Sinking into her seat, Hermione bent forwards to open her bag and began pulling out her Wheezebox, quill and parchment. From behind her, she heard the sound of Malfoy crossing the room and she instinctively stiffened when he passed her, coming close enough to send a gust of air that smelled faintly of bergamot in her direction. For some reason, it made her shiver. She preferred it when there was a desk between them.
赫敏一头扎进座位上，弯下腰打开她的包，开始掏出她的喘息盒、羽毛笔和羊皮纸。从她身后，她听到了马尔福穿过房间的声音，当他从她身边经过时，她本能地僵硬了起来，靠得足够近，将一阵散发着淡淡佛手柑气味的空气吹向了她的方向。不知为何，这让她不寒而栗。她更喜欢他们之间有一张桌子的时候。

Sure enough, when he slipped quietly into his chair across from her, Hermione’s shoulders descended an inch or so and the ball of tension in her stomach unwound a degree. She straightened up and arranged her equipment on his desk, avoiding his gaze all the while. 
果然，当他悄悄地溜到她对面的椅子上时，赫敏的肩膀下降了一英寸左右，她肚子里的紧绷球也舒展了一度。她直起身来，把她的设备放在他的桌子上，一直避开他的目光。

“I understand that you weren’t entirely comfortable with the idea of the voice recorder,” Hermione said, fixing her quill into a point on a fresh sheet of parchment. “But I’m happy to do a test and show you how it works. Would you prefer that?”
“我知道你对录音机这个想法并不完全满意，”赫敏说，一边把她的羽毛笔固定在一张新羊皮纸上的一个尖上。“但我很乐意做一个测试，向你展示它是如何工作的。你喜欢吗？

His expression didn’t tell her much at all but deciding she would prefer it if he knew exactly what he was getting into, Hermione touched the Wheezebox with her wand and slid it into the middle of the table. 
他的表情根本没有告诉她什么，但决定她宁愿他确切地知道自己要做什么，赫敏用魔杖碰了碰喘息盒，把它滑到了桌子的中间。

“You can just say something to it,” she prompted. “Anything really.”
“你可以对它说点什么，”她提示道。“真的，任何事情。”

He raised a single eyebrow and offered her one, slow blink that distinctly told her he would do nothing of the sort and he thought her a fool for even trying to persuade him. Hermione sighed.
他扬起一根眉毛，缓缓地眨了眨眼，显然告诉她他不会做这种事情，他认为她是个傻瓜，连试图说服他都行。赫敏叹了口气。

“Okay, I will. Test, test. Testing.”
“好的，我会的。测试，测试。测试。

Reaching out, Hermione touched it with her wand again and Malfoy watched closely as she performed two shorter taps to play the sound of what she had just said back to him.
赫敏伸出手，再次用魔杖碰了碰它，马尔福仔细地看着她轻敲了两下，以播放她刚刚对他说的话。

“That’s really all it is. Are you happy with that?”
“真的就是这样。你满意吗？

He didn’t look happy but he inclined his head slowly and Hermione exhaled, smiling.
他看起来并不高兴，但他慢慢地歪了歪头，赫敏微笑着呼出一口气。

“Good! Great, alright then. Let’s begin.” Hermione returned the voice recorder to the desk and tapped it, shifting in her seat to get comfortable. “So, Mr Malfoy, generally in interviews I start by asking fairly casual questions. That’s primarily just to warm things up and get you used to the kind of speaking and recollection you’ll be doing. You live in Malfoy Manor where our interview is taking place; were you raised here?”
“很好！太好了，好吧。让我们开始吧。赫敏把录音机放回桌子上，敲了敲它，在座位上挪动了一下，让自己舒服些。“所以，马尔福先生，一般来说，在采访中，我都会问一些相当随意的问题。这主要是为了让事情暖和起来，让你习惯你将要做的那种说话和回忆。你住在马尔福庄园，我们的采访正在进行那里;你在这里长大吗？

“Yes.” 
“是的。”

Hermione felt a flood of relief at the sound of his voice, clipped and displeased as it was. It was jarring to want to hear Lucius Malfoy speak.
赫敏听到他的声音，感到如潮水般地松了一口气，尽管它很尖锐，也很不悦。想听卢修斯·马尔福说话真是令人不安。

“Can you tell me something about your childhood here?”
“你能跟我说说你在这里的童年吗？”

A taut silence stretched out and Hermione could tell that Malfoy wasn’t going to respond, either because he did not want to or because he wasn’t sure what to say. Giving him the benefit of the doubt and working on the assumption of the latter, Hermione attempted to show understanding.
一阵紧绷的沉默持续了下来，赫敏看得出来马尔福不打算回答，要么是他不想回答，要么是因为他不知道该说什么。赫敏给了他怀疑的好处，并努力假设后者，试图表现出理解。

“You don’t have to go into any particular detail, Mr Malfoy. Sometimes just some vague memories, particular sights or smells can be evocative.”
“你不必详细讨论任何细节，马尔福先生。有时，只是一些模糊的记忆、特定的景象或气味就可以唤起人们的共鸣。

More silence in which his eyes trailed over her, judgmentally taking in her curls and the floaty arms of her loose-fitting peasant blouse. Probably not the best style to wear around him in retrospect. Her only comfort was that he probably didn’t have the requisite Muggle fashion knowledge to put a name to it himself. 
更多的寂静中，他的目光在她身上扫过，评判性地看着她的卷发和她宽松的农民衬衫飘逸的手臂。回想起来，这可能不是最适合在他身边穿的款式。她唯一的安慰是，他可能没有必要的麻瓜时尚知识来给它起个名字。

“Perhaps you’d like to ask me about my childhood?” Hermione offered. “Sometimes a bit of back and forth can make this feel like more of an equitable relationship. I understand it can feel like I’m pressing you for information and I don’t want that to be the case. I’m more than happy to share with you.”
“也许你想问我关于我的童年？”赫敏提议道。“有时，一点来回会让这感觉更像是一种公平的关系。我理解感觉就像我在催促你提供信息，我不希望这种情况发生。我非常高兴与您分享。

“I don’t particularly care to know anything about your miserable little Muggle life, Miss Granger.”
“我不是特别想知道你那悲惨的小麻瓜生活，格兰杰小姐。”

Hermione pressed her tongue against the roof of her mouth, repressing a million angry retorts. Running water, running water, running water . 
赫敏用舌头抵住她的上颚，压抑着一百万个愤怒的反驳。 流水、流水、流水。

“Very well, Mr Malfoy. Rather than me asking those more narrow questions, why don’t we open it up? Why don’t you tell me what you’re willing to tell me about the childhood you spent here?” 
“很好，马尔福先生。与其我问那些更狭隘的问题，不如我们打开它呢？你为什么不告诉我你愿意告诉我你在这里度过的童年的事情呢？

“There’s very little I wish you to know about my boyhood. That it was spent here is a matter of public record, so I will own to that. I do not understand what that part of my life has to do with the war or why you would include it in your book.”
“我希望你了解的关于我的童年的事情很少。它在这里度过是一个公共记录问题，所以我将承认这一点。我不明白我生命中的那一部分与战争有什么关系，也不明白你为什么要把它写在你的书里。

“I won’t include all of it in the book, you’re right,” Hermione nodded. “But some of it might make its way in for a bit of…background.” 
“我不会把它们都写进书里，你说得对，”赫敏点点头。“但其中一些可能会进入一点......背景。

When he didn’t look convinced, Hermione sighed and crossed, then uncrossed her legs. “Mr Malfoy, the context of who you were before the war, how you were raised, is important to understanding the person you were during it and who you are now that it’s over. I’m here to record your lived experience but I don’t think that’s the kind of thing that can be easily isolated. It’s…connective tissue. That’s why I ask questions that go so far back.”
当他看起来不服气时，赫敏叹了口气，交叉了一下，然后松开了她的双腿。“马尔福先生，你在战前的身份，你是如何长大的，对于理解你在战时的身份以及现在的你是谁很重要。我在这里记录你的生活经历，但我不认为那种可以轻易孤立的事情。它。。。结缔组织。这就是为什么我提出的问题可以追溯到很久以前。

Lucius looked down at the Wheezebox and then up at her. “Miss Granger, I don’t have a pensieve. Do you know why that is?”
卢修斯低头看了看 Wheezebox，然后又抬头看了看她。“格兰杰小姐，我没有钢笔。你知道为什么吗？

Hermione shook her head, thrown by his sudden shift in topic. He leaned forward, elbows on the arms of his chair and hands clasped. “It is because I am protective of my privacy. I keep myself to myself. I do not want my life to be observed by third parties. I have no desire to be understood .” He said the last word with a disdainful dip in his voice. “And I do not want to seek public penance.”
赫敏摇了摇头，被他突然的话题转移吓了一跳。他身体前倾，手肘搭在椅子扶手上，双手紧握。“这是因为我保护自己的隐私。我把自己留给自己。我不希望我的生活被第三方观察。我不想被理解。他说完最后一个字时，声音里带着轻蔑的低沉。“我不想寻求公开的忏悔。”

The sound of the Quick Quotes Quill scratching out his words was the only sound as Hermione mulled over them. He was so certain about what he didn’t want. “Then what do you want?” Hermione asked quietly. 
Quick Quotes Quill 划出他的话的声音是赫敏仔细考虑时唯一的声音。他对自己不想要的东西非常确定。“那你想要什么？”赫敏轻声问道。

Lucius said nothing, unclasping his hands to lean his chin on his fist as he considered her with an appraising look. She didn’t get the impression that he was angry at her, incredibly—he seemed more thoughtful than anything, as though that was a question he had not been asked or even pondered in a long time.
卢修斯什么也没说，松开双手，将下巴靠在拳头上，用赞赏的眼神打量着她。她没有觉得他对她生气，难以置信——他似乎比什么都深思熟虑，仿佛这是一个他很久没有被问过甚至没有思考过的问题。

“That’s really none of your business,” he finally answered. “Like most of the things you ask.”
“那真的不关你的事，”他终于回答。“就像你问的大多数事情一样。”

“I don’t think you know,” Hermione said. “Do you?”
“我想你不知道，”赫敏说。“是吗？”

Again, Lucius made no reply, his face impassive, but Hermione didn’t miss the way the fist holding up his chin tightened fractionally, the tendons on the back of his hand tautening.
卢修斯又一次没有回答，他的脸上无动于衷，但赫敏没有错过托住他下巴的拳头微微收紧，手背上的肌腱绷紧的样子。

“Maybe if you do this – maybe if you bring your freedom a little closer – you’ll figure it out.”
“也许如果你这样做——也许如果你把你的自由拉近一点——你就会弄清楚。”

Crossing her fingers in her lap and pressing her toes down flat in her trainers, Hermione hoped against hope that he wouldn’t throw her out. She had pushed her luck with him there, she knew that. That was, however, the nature of interviewing people, particularly people like Lucius Malfoy – sometimes you had to push your luck, push them , to get what you wanted.
赫敏把手指交叉在膝盖上，脚趾平压在运动鞋里，希望他不会把她扔出去。她在那里和他一起推了她的运气，她知道这一点。然而，这就是采访人的本质，尤其是像卢修斯·马尔福这样的人——有时你得逼运气，逼他们，才能得到你想要的东西。

“Continue with your questions, Miss Granger,” he eventually said, his voice and his brows low. “Just remember that I do not need to answer them.”
“继续你的问题，格兰杰小姐，”他终于说了，他的声音和眉毛都低垂着。“只要记住，我不需要回答他们。”

Heart skipping a beat with relief, Hermione relaxed into her seat. “Why don’t you tell me about your parents?” Hermione noticed his eyebrow rise and realised she’d probably picked another dead end. Conversing with him was like being in a labyrinth. “What was your father’s name?”
心脏松了一口气，赫敏放松地坐在座位上。“你为什么不告诉我你父母的事？”赫敏注意到他的眉毛上扬，意识到她可能又走了一条死胡同。与他交谈就像置身于迷宫中。“你爸爸叫什么名字？”

“Abraxas Malfoy.” 
“阿布拉克萨斯·马尔福。”

Another matter of public record, obviously, Hermione thought bitterly.
另一件公开记录的事情，显然，赫敏苦涩地想着。

“And your mother?”
“那妈呢？”

To her surprise, Lucius looked somewhat reluctant, like he actually wasn’t going to tell her his mother’s name even though Hermione was sure that was bound to be yet another matter of public record that she could easily uncover on her own. Finally, however, he said, “Aurelia. Her name was Aurelia Malfoy.”
令她惊讶的是，卢修斯看起来有些不情愿，就像他真的不打算告诉她他妈妈的名字一样，尽管赫敏很确定这注定是她自己很容易发现的另一件公共记录。然而，最后他说：“奥瑞莉亚。她的名字叫奥瑞莉亚·马尔福。

“Is there anything you wouldn’t mind telling me about them?”
“你有什么不介意告诉我的事吗？”

Silence. Of course .
沉默。 答案是肯定的。

“Mr Malfoy, I appreciate opening up to a complete stranger isn’t always the easiest but I would encourage you to be a touch more forthcoming. I’m not here to catch you out.”
“马尔福先生，我很感激向一个完全陌生的人敞开心扉并不总是最容易的，但我鼓励你多一点坦诚一点。我不是来抓你的。

Seeing that her line of questioning wasn’t going to yield any kind of result, Hermione decided to change tack. “We’ll move forward some, then. You attended Hogwarts?”
赫敏看到她的提问不会产生任何结果，她决定改变策略。“那么，我们会向前推进一些。你上过霍格沃茨吗？

“Yes.”
“是的。”

“Do you remember the day you received your letter?”
“你还记得你收到信的那天吗？”

“Vividly.”
“生动。”

Hermione smiled at that. So did she. Leaning forward in her seat to convey her interest, she attempted to encourage him. “Excellent. Maybe you could describe what you felt that day. Or tell me where you were in the manor when the owl arrived?”
赫敏笑了笑。她也是。她在座位上向前倾身以表达她的兴趣，并试图鼓励他。“太好了。也许你可以描述一下你那天的感受。或者告诉我猫头鹰来的时候你在庄园里的什么地方？

“I would rather not.”
“我宁愿不。”

Hermione ran a frustrated hand over her forehead, pushing her wispy fringe askew. “Look...I...I don’t want to push, Mr Malfoy, but if you’re going to be resistant to every question I ask you, this is going to be extremely difficult for both of us.”
赫敏沮丧地用一只手抚摸着她的额头，歪歪扭扭地推开了她纤细的刘海。“看......我。。。我不想强迫你，马尔福先生，但如果你要抗拒我问你的每一个问题，这对我们俩来说都是极其困难的。

“Then perhaps you should give up.”
“那也许你应该放弃。”

There was a gleam of a challenge in his eye. Was that all he wanted? For her to give up? If she was the one to give up, Hermione reasoned to herself, then Draco would have to stop bothering him. A bubble of anger began to expand in Hermione’s stomach.
他的眼中闪过一丝挑战。这就是他想要的吗？让她放弃？赫敏心想，如果她是那个要放弃的人，那么德拉科就得停止打扰他了。一股愤怒的泡沫开始在赫敏的胃里膨胀。

“Why was I asked back here if you’re still resistant to working with me?”
“为什么有人问我，你是否仍然抗拒与我合作？”

“Because my son, like yourself, is quite insistent.”
“因为我儿子和你一样，都挺坚持的。”

“Don’t you want to show Kingsley that you’re interested in getting some kind of reprieve?”
“你不是想告诉金斯莱你有兴趣得到某种缓刑吗？”

“I have no interest in performing for rewards like some kind of captive beast .”
“我没有兴趣像某种被俘虏的野兽一样为了奖励而表演。”

“那不是我——”赫敏摇摇头。“德拉科显然很想让你找回一些自由，你不想为他尝试吗？还是你未来的孙子？

“我未来的孙子，再一次，不关你的事，”他说，语气冰冷。

“嗯，你也表现得好像他们不属于你一样，”赫敏厉声说。

There was a pause in which Lucius sat back in his seat, his eyes narrowed. “You are quite quick to anger, Miss Granger, did you know that? It makes you careless with your words. I wouldn’t think you would wish to speak in such a manner to a man you are attempting to coax – I am far from charmed.”
卢修斯坐回座位上，眯起了眼睛。“你真容易生气，格兰杰小姐，你知道吗？它让你的言语粗心大意。我想你不会愿意用这种方式和一个你试图哄骗的男人说话——我一点也不被迷住。

Bloody same , Hermione thought ferociously.
的一样，赫敏凶狠地想着。

“Mr Malfoy, I’m growing tired of trying to persuade you to do something that will help you in addition to helping me. I don’t particularly care if you ever step over the threshold of this manor again but Draco clearly does.” Where he had leaned back, Hermione moved forward and stopped the Wheezebox. “We haven’t done a full hour this week but I think we should leave it there.”
“马尔福先生，我已经厌倦了试图说服你做一些除了帮助我之外还能帮助你的事情。我不是特别在乎你是否会再次跨过这座庄园的门槛，但德拉科显然是这样。赫敏向后靠的地方，向前移动，停下了喘息盒。“我们这周还没有做一整小时，但我认为我们应该就此结束。”

“So you are giving up?” he said and Hermione thought she heard something almost accusatory in the words.  
“所以你要放弃了？” 他说，赫敏觉得她从这些话中听到了什么近乎指责的东西。

“No,” she replied with as much patience as she could muster. “I’m just not going to push you any harder than I need to – I’ve never been one for torture, funnily enough.” His hand squeezed the arm of his chair, a flash of white appearing through the skin over his knuckles. “I’ll be back at the same time next week.” 
“不，”她尽可能耐心地回答。“我只是不会把你逼得太紧——有趣的是，我从来就不是一个喜欢折磨的人。”他的手捏了捏椅子的扶手，一抹白色从他指关节上的皮肤中闪过。“我下周同一时间回来。”

Dropping her equipment into her bag, Hermione closed the flap and stood up, looking down at where he remained seated behind his desk. “I think, perhaps, in the intervening period you should genuinely think about what you want, Mr Malfoy. I have no intention of tripping you up or trying to make your punishment any worse . But I also can’t make it better unless you cooperate.”
赫敏把她的设备放进包里，合上翻盖，站起来，低头看着他坐在桌子后面的地方。“我想，也许，在这段时间里，你应该真心想想你想要什么，马尔福先生。我无意绊倒你或试图让你的惩罚变得更糟。但除非你合作，否则我也无法让它变得更好。

At that, Hermione turned and made for the door, feeling his eyes on her back the entire way across the room. “I’ll see you next week,” she said, not bothering to look back.
听到这话，赫敏转身向门口走去，感觉到他的眼睛在房间的另一边一直盯着她的背影。“下周见，”她说，懒得回头看。

On leaving Malfoy Manor, Hermione didn’t go straight home as she’d originally intended. Instead, she took herself to the Ministry. 
离开马尔福庄园后，赫敏并没有像她最初打算的那样直接回家。相反，她把自己带到了魔法部。

Lucius Malfoy was going to be a challenge for her, that much was clear, so she was going to respond to this challenge the way she did any other: she would arm herself with knowledge. Outside of the notes and books she already had, the Ministry archives felt like a good place to start looking for information on Malfoy. She’d get his trial notes, records of his donations, details of the issues that prompted him to lobby ministers and she’d spend every available moment of the next week reading about him and all of his horrid little ancestors. 
卢修斯·马尔福对她来说将是一个挑战，这一点很清楚，所以她要像对待其他任何人一样来应对这个挑战：她要用知识武装自己。除了她已经拥有的笔记和书籍之外，魔法部档案馆感觉像是开始寻找关于马尔福的信息的好地方。她会得到他的审判记录、他的捐款记录、促使他游说牧师的问题的细节，她会在接下来的一周里利用每一个空闲的时间阅读关于他和他所有可怕的小祖先的故事。

Stepping out of the lift and into the archive, Hermione breathed deep the calm, comforting smell of old parchment and the slightly woody scent of the various shelves and storage cabinets. There was no natural light in the archive, just hundreds of floating candles, all encased in bubble charms to reduce the risk of a fire. It was one of her favourite places in the Ministry, though between the sterile cafeteria and the awful worn tartan carpets that spanned the identikit departmental cubicles, it didn’t have much competition.
走出电梯，走进档案馆，赫敏深深地呼吸着旧羊皮纸平静、令人欣慰的气味，以及各种架子和储物柜的略带木质香味。档案馆里没有自然光，只有数百支漂浮的蜡烛，都包裹在泡泡护身符中，以降低火灾的风险。这是她在魔法部最喜欢的地方之一，尽管在空荡荡的自助餐厅和横跨同一部门隔间的破旧格子呢地毯之间，它并没有太多的竞争。

The welcome desk was empty but, feeling in no particular rush, Hermione hovered around it, folding and refolding the access slip that Kingsley had signed and presented to her at the beginning of her sabbatical. 
迎宾台空无一人，但赫敏并不觉得特别匆忙，她在它周围徘徊，折叠又折叠金斯莱在休假开始时签署并提交给她的访问单。

“Hullo, Hermione Granger.”
“哈洛，赫敏·格兰杰。”

Hermione started and turned to see Terry Boot emerging from a corridor of shelves, a box of documents in his hands. Immediately remembering what Ginny had relayed about him asking Harry about her, Hermione couldn’t seem to stop a small amount of heat rising to her cheeks.
赫敏起身，转过身来，看到特里·布特从书架走廊里走出来，手里拿着一箱文件。赫敏立刻想起了金妮转述的关于他向哈利询问她的事情，她似乎无法阻止一丝热气升到她的脸颊上。

“Hello, Terry. Long time no see.”
“你好，特里。好久不见。

“Indeed,” he grunted, depositing the box of documents on his desk with a heavy thump . Satisfied that they were stable, he gave her a wide smile. “What can I do for you today?”
“确实，”他咕哝着，重重地把一箱文件放在他的桌子上。他对他们很稳定感到满意，对她露出了一个灿烂的笑容。“今天我能为你做些什么？”

Handing over her slip for Terry to stamp, Hermione sidled closer to the desk and lifted her bag up onto it, extracting some parchment and a standard Muggle pencil from within. “I’m looking for material relating to the Malfoy family.”
赫敏把她的纸条递给泰瑞盖章，然后悄悄地靠近桌子，把她的包举到上面，从里面拿出一些羊皮纸和一支标准的麻瓜铅笔。“我在找和马尔福家族有关的材料。”

Terry’s eyebrows were raised as he handed Hermione’s slip back to her. “That’s a surname that appears in plenty of the boxes in here.” Terry ducked down behind the desk and opened a drawer. Hermione could hear him flipping through folders until he emerged with a long leaf of parchment identifying all of the records tied to the Malfoys. “You’ve got a long afternoon ahead of you.”
特里扬起眉毛，把赫敏的纸条还给她。“这个姓氏出现在这里的很多盒子里。”Terry躲在桌子后面，打开了一个抽屉。赫敏可以听到他翻阅文件夹的声音，直到他拿着一长长的羊皮纸出现，上面写着所有与马尔福家族有关的记录。“你有一个漫长的下午在等着你。”

“More than one afternoon by the looks of it,” Hermione said with a smile, taking the parchment from Terry and giving it a once over before rolling it into a tight scroll.
“看样子不止一个下午，”赫敏笑着说，从泰瑞手中接过羊皮纸，看了一遍，然后把它卷成一个紧紧的卷轴。

“Well, you know I’m always glad to see you here.” Terry took her bag and placed it in one of the storage boxes that personal belongings were kept in. “You follow the rules, for one thing.” He nodded at her pencil. 
“嗯，你知道我总是很高兴在这里见到你。”特里拿起她的包，把它放在一个存放个人物品的储物箱里。“一方面，你要遵守规则。”他对着她的铅笔点点头。

Always pleased to have her archive etiquette praised, Hermione grinned at him and he responded with a more shy smile. Terry was quite good looking, she realised with a start. She liked his short, slightly curly hair and, she noticed, he had perfect dimples. His eyes were so brown so as to be almost black and in the candlelit archives they practically glimmered. Why had she never noticed that before? At the start of her project she’d been an almost constant presence in the archives and he’d always been helpful but never anything more than that. Probably because she didn’t really want him to be. 
赫敏总是很高兴她的档案礼仪受到称赞，她对他咧嘴一笑，他以更害羞的笑容回应。特里长得挺好看的，她吓了一跳才意识到。她喜欢他那一头略带卷曲的短发，而且，她注意到，他有完美的酒窝。他的眼睛是如此的棕色，几乎是黑色的，在烛光下的档案中，它们几乎闪闪发光。为什么她以前从来没有注意到这一点？在她的项目开始时，她几乎一直出现在档案中，他总是乐于助人，但从来没有超过此。可能是因为她真的不想让他成为这样的人。

“你上次来这里已经有一段时间了，”他在赫敏转身离开之前说。“我想知道你的项目进展如何。”

“Oh,” Hermione tucked her hair behind her ear. It was rare that anyone asked her that anymore – most people just wanted her to finish it. “It’s coming along. I’ve completed most of my interviews and I’m pulling together my transcripts, trying to organise some kind of structure, you know.”

Terry nodded at the parchment she was holding. “Why the sudden interest in the Malfoys?”
特里对着她手里的羊皮纸点点头。“为什么突然对马尔福家族感兴趣？”

“我现在正在采访卢修斯·马尔福，”赫敏说，轻声补充道，“或者我正在尝试。

Terry的额头上皱起了一丝眉头，他把头歪向一边。“食死徒？”

“是的，”赫敏说，她的语气有些简洁。她并不是真的想向另一个人证明她采访食死徒的愿望是合理的。然而，令她惊讶的是，特里只是点了点头。

“Thorough,” he nodded approvingly. 
“彻底，”他赞同地点点头。

赫敏发出一声短促的、喘息的笑声。拉文克劳。“谢谢。好吧，我最好是......”赫敏慢慢走开，转头指着书架。

“呃，赫敏？”特里在她转身要走时喊道。赫敏停了下来，渴望地皱起眉头，望着黑暗、孤立的一排排，然后再次面对他。他看起来很紧张，抬起一只手挠了挠他的卷发。“我想知道你是否愿意......”

Hermione swallowed, not sure whether she wanted to encourage what she thought he might be attempting to ask. Bloody Ginny .
赫敏咽了口口水，不确定她是否想鼓励她认为他可能试图提出的问题。 血腥金妮 .

“如果你能问我是否需要更多的帮助，”Terry说完，考虑到他刚刚提出了一个非常友好的提议，他看起来有些不和谐地恼怒。

Hermione assumed his irritation was at himself rather than her but she smiled, aware that she probably looked more relieved than she should by a simple offer of help. “I will.” 
赫敏以为他的生气是针对他自己而不是她，但她笑了笑，她知道她看起来可能比简单的帮助更像是松了一口气。“我会的。”

当她再次转身离开时，她听到他喃喃自语着什么，听起来很奇怪，就像“哦，他妈的”，然后又叫了她的名字。

“赫敏，你想出去玩吗？”

赫敏停了下来，沮丧地短暂地闭上了眼睛，慢慢地转过身来面对他，当她看到他看起来如此充满希望时，她的胃一沉。“哦......特里，我真的很受宠若惊。真诚地。只是......我现在很忙，忙于所有的事情......”她可怜地绝望地耸了耸肩，把羊皮纸卷轴举起来。“我只是不确定我有没有时间。”

Terry睁大了眼睛，不知怎么的，他设法同时摇了摇头和点头。“不，绝对。我明白这一点。完全。这是完全公平的。

赫敏带着感激的笑容，觉得她应该离开他，但随后他只是继续说话。“只是......我知道你刚才真的很忙，但也许......不要直接说“不”。如果我稍后再问怎么办？你觉得当你稍微自由一点时，你可能会......？

He trailed off hopefully and Hermione bit her lip as she considered him. Ginny would kill her when she told her about this encounter. Maybe she could reduce her almost certain death sentence to a severe glare and punch on the arm if she said yes. He might not even ask her again. Besides, it wasn't like she even needed to say yes the next time either.
他满怀希望地走开了，赫敏咬着嘴唇，看着他。当金妮告诉她这次遭遇时，她会杀了她。如果她同意的话，也许她可以将她几乎可以肯定的死刑判决减少为严厉的瞪眼和一拳打在手臂上。他甚至可能不会再问她了。此外，她下次也不需要说“是”。

“Yes, why not? I think...that would be lovely.”
“是的，为什么不呢？我认为。。。那太好了。

A relieved smile broke out across Terry’s face and Hermione saw the dimples more clearly than ever. She couldn’t help but return it, though somewhat more wearily. “Brilliant,” he said, slightly breathless. “Great, yeah. Okay, well...I’ll owl you. 泰瑞的脸上露出如释重负的笑容，赫敏比以往任何时候都更清楚地看到了那些酒窝。她忍不住把信还了回去，虽然有点疲惫了。“太棒了，”他说，有点喘不过气来。“太好了，是的。好吧......我来找你。显然，在你去把你的东西还给你之前，我会见你。但我会猫头鹰你。

“Perfect.” Just perfect .
“完美。” 简直完美。

Impatiently combing a stray curl from her face, Hermione squinted at a 1688 tract penned by one Florian Malfoy that argued against the Statute of Secrecy. Noting down some of its points, she found it hard not to shake her head in disbelief. A Malfoy arguing against the greater separation of the wizards and Muggles, when only a year later the records showed they had voted in favour of it. They really would twist themselves into any shape they had to. After poring over Lucius Malfoy’s trial notes from the first war, she could tell it was hereditary.
赫敏不耐烦地梳理着脸上的一缕飘发，眯着眼睛看着弗洛里安·马尔福（Florian Malfoy）在1688年写的一本反对保密法规的传单。记下其中的一些要点后，她发现很难不敢置信地摇头。一个马尔福反对巫师和麻瓜进一步分离，而仅仅一年后，记录显示他们已经投了赞成票。他们真的会把自己扭成任何他们必须的形状。在仔细研究了卢修斯·马尔福在第一次战争中的审判记录后，她可以看出这是遗传的。

Pushing another filled page of parchment to the side, Hermione almost choked when she caught a glimpse of her watch. The problem with the lack of natural light in the archives was that it was kind of hard to tell how much time had passed. Trying to pack away the papers she’d taken out as neatly as she’d found them while still moving quickly, Hermione tutted at herself for being late.
赫敏把另一页装满的羊皮纸推到一边，当她瞥见她的手表时，她差点窒息。档案中缺乏自然光的问题在于，很难判断过去了多少时间。赫敏一边快速移动，一边把她拿出来的文件收拾得像找到它们一样整齐齐，但赫敏嘲笑自己迟到了。

她答应过 8 点在 Hogshead 见金妮、哈利、罗恩、卢娜和纳威，现在已经过去了五点。她已经工作了好几个小时。下次，她必须让 Terry 充当她的计时器。

当她到达猪头时，已经有一杯白葡萄酒在等着她，晚了二十五分钟，金妮立即严肃地指出来。

“就连露娜也比你先到了这里，她不得不在 Pudifoots 夫人停下来帮助他们解决 Nargle 的侵扰！”

“太可怕了，赫敏，”卢娜郑重地点头说。“女服务员真的对整件事感到非常震惊。我真的很同情她。

“我估计她对纳格尔夫妇的惊吓较少，更多的是你把自制的纳格莱杀手洒在她刚刚清理的桌子上，露娜，”罗恩指出，对着他的啤酒嘲笑着。

Hermione had a sudden vision of Luna standing in the centre of Madam Pudifoots, sprinkling Narglecide like a priest with holy water, and choked on her wine. Chuckling to her left, Neville rubbed her back and Hermione threw him a grateful look. 
赫敏突然看到卢娜站在普迪富茨夫人的中央，像牧师一样用圣水洒着纳格莱杀戮剂，然后被她的酒呛住了。纳威朝她的左边笑了笑，揉了揉她的背，赫敏感激地看了他一眼。

They made a habit of having regular drinks at the Hogshead during the school year so that it was easy for Neville to come down from Hogwarts to meet them. He’d once told them that telling his first years that he regularly left the school to meet with Harry Potter, Ron Weasley and Hermione Granger never failed to get him respect. When Ron had pointed out that Neville could get as much, if not more, respect by telling his students that he’d cut the head off of Voldemort’s snake with the sword of Gryffindor, Neville had just gone red around the ears and hidden his face in his pint. 
他们养成了在学年期间定期在霍格黑德喝酒的习惯，这样纳威就很容易从霍格沃茨下来迎接他们。他曾经告诉他们，告诉他一年级的学生，他经常离开学校去见哈利·波特、罗恩·韦斯莱和赫敏·格兰杰，这让他得到了尊重。当罗恩指出纳威告诉他的学生他用格兰芬多的剑砍下了伏地魔的蛇头，可以得到同样多的尊重，如果不是更多的话，纳威刚刚红了耳朵，把脸藏在他的品脱里。

“Where were you, Hermione?” Neville asked once he was sure that she was in a fit state to be able to reply. 
“你在哪儿，赫敏？”纳威在确定她身体状况良好，能够回答后问道。

“At the Ministry archives,” she said apologetically, wiping a droplet of wine from her chin. “Just lost track of time, you know.”
“在魔法部档案馆，”她抱歉地说，擦了擦下巴上的一滴酒。“就是忘记了时间，你知道的。”

“Malfoy research, was it?” Ginny asked, sounding displeased as she picked a congealed strip of cucumber from her gillywater. 
“马尔福研究，是吗？”金妮问道，她从她的吉利水中摘了一条凝结的黄瓜，听起来很不高兴。

“Yes,” Hermione said evasively as Ron narrowed his eyes while Neville and Luna looked on with interest. “But I don’t want to talk about that tonight. How are you, Neville? Luna?”
“是的，”赫敏回避地说，罗恩眯起眼睛，纳威和卢娜饶有兴趣地看着。“但我今晚不想谈论这个。你好吗，纳威？露娜？

“Are you researching the Malfoys too, Hermione?”
“你也在研究马尔福家族吗，赫敏？”

Everyone stared at Luna blankly but, as usual, the blonde girl appeared largely unbothered. “Er, yes, Luna,” Hermione said cautiously, unsure what might come out of pressing Luna for more details. “Are you ?”
每个人都茫然地盯着卢娜，但像往常一样，这个金发女孩似乎基本上不为所动。“呃，是的，卢娜，”赫敏小心翼翼地说，不确定追问卢娜的更多细节会带来什么。“你是吗？”

“Oh, yes,” Luna nodded dreamily and picked the olive out of her martini to pop it in her mouth. “I think I’ve found evidence that they hunted down the last of the Blibbering Humdingers and I’m sure they must still have some of their hides in their manor. They’d be worth a fortune, of course, but I don’t think they should be hidden away. Is that what you’re researching?”
“哦，是的，”卢娜梦幻般地点点头，从马提尼酒中摘下橄榄塞进嘴里。“我想我已经找到了他们追捕了最后一只喋喋不休的喋喋不休的傻瓜的证据，而且我敢肯定他们的庄园里肯定还有一些藏身之处。当然，它们会值一大笔钱，但我认为它们不应该被藏起来。这就是你在研究的东西吗？

Hermione blinked rapidly as Ron shared an incredulous look with a very amused Harry. “No, Luna. I’m interviewing Lucius Malfoy for my oral history. He’s quite...erm...uncommunicative, so I’m researching the family to get some background that I might be able to use to draw him out.” 
赫敏迅速地眨了眨眼，罗恩和哈利分享了一个难以置信的眼神。“不，露娜。我正在采访卢修斯·马尔福（Lucius Malfoy）作为我的口述历史。他相当......呃......不善于交流，所以我正在研究这个家庭，以获得一些背景信息，我可能会用它来吸引他。

“Can’t believe I’m saying something that could be mistaken as a defence of Lucius Malfoy,” said Ron, “but, Hermione, if the bloke really doesn’t want to talk to you, have you considered just leaving him alone?”
“真不敢相信我说的话会被误认为是在为卢修斯·马尔福辩护，”罗恩说，“但是，赫敏，如果那家伙真的不想和你说话，你有没有想过就这样让他一个人呆着？

“Of course she hasn’t, Ron,” Ginny said. “She’s Hermione. She’s a knowledge vampire who’ll suck him dry whether he likes it or not.”
“她当然没有，罗恩，”金妮说。“她是赫敏。她是个知识渊博的吸血鬼，不管他喜欢与否，她都会把他吸干。

Harry laughed loudly over Hermione’s indignant huff while Ron shuddered, his face contorted with disgust. “Can you not talk about sucking Lucius Malfoy dry? Thanks.”
哈利对赫敏的愤怒大笑起来，而罗恩则浑身发抖，他的脸因厌恶而扭曲。“你不能谈谈把卢修斯·马尔福吸干吗？谢谢。

“Fuck, Ron! ” Ginny exclaimed, flinging her cucumber across the table at him and making him cry out in protest. “That’s absolutely disgusting.”
“操，罗恩！”金妮喊道，把她的黄瓜扔到桌子对面，让他大声抗议。“这绝对令人作呕。”

“You said it!”
“你说的！”

“I bloody well did not ! Do not blame me for your sick mind.”
“我没有！不要因为你的病态而怪我。

“Oh my God,” Hermione muttered, dropping her face into her hands as, to her right, Harry sympathetically patted her shoulder. “I have to talk to that man next week so if we could just not that’d be great.”
“哦，我的上帝，”赫敏咕哝着，把脸埋在手里，哈利同情地拍了拍她的肩膀。“我下周必须和那个人谈谈，所以如果我们不能，那就太好了。”

“Why are you bothering, Hermione?” Neville asked quietly, a puzzled frown drawing his brows together. “Isn’t he just awful to you?” 
“你为什么烦恼，赫敏？”纳威轻声问道，困惑的眉头紧锁着他的眉头。“他不是很糟糕吗？”

“Don’t bother, Neville,” Ron interrupted with a dismissive eye roll. “She’ll just rabbit on about thoroughness and academics and getting a fuller picture and blah, blah, blah.”
“别打扰，纳威，”罗恩轻蔑地翻了个白眼打断。“她只会喋喋不休地谈论彻底性和学术性，并获得更全面的画面，等等。”

Hermione flushed an angry red and opened her mouth to protest but, before she could, Luna spoke again. “That makes sense.”
赫敏气得通红，张开嘴想要抗议，但还没等她开口，卢娜又开口了。“这很有道理。”

Everyone looked at Luna and a flicker of dread passed through Hermione. While she appreciated that Luna wasn’t going to be another person jumping down her throat, she wasn’t sure if Luna was the kind of person she wanted to immediately understand what she was doing. Maybe she had lost it.
每个人都看着卢娜，赫敏心中闪过一丝恐惧。虽然她很欣赏 Luna 不会成为另一个从她的喉咙里跳下来的人，但她不确定 Luna 是否是那种她想立即理解自己在做什么的人。也许她已经失去了它。

“What?” Luna asked, actually noticing their stares for once. “If Hermione wants a fuller picture then she’ll need to talk to him, won't she?”
“什么？”卢娜问道，实际上有一次注意到了他们的目光。“如果赫敏想要更全面的情况，那么她需要和他谈谈，不是吗？”

“Yeah,” Ron said, his lips turned down at the corners, “But what’s he going to say? ‘I hate Muggle-borns, end of story’? Great interview.”
“是啊，”罗恩说，他的嘴唇在嘴角下垂，“但他要说什么呢？我讨厌麻瓜出身的人，故事的结尾'？ 很棒的采访。

“That sounds more like the middle of a story to me,” Luna said pensively, taking a sip of her drink. 
“在我看来，这听起来更像是一个故事的中间，”Luna 沉思着说，喝了一口饮料。

Harry raised his eyebrows at Hermione who took a sizeable glug from her wine and shook her head, feeling it slosh in her cheeks. This really wasn’t what she wanted to talk about – it wasn’t exactly pleasant.
哈利向赫敏扬起眉毛，赫敏从她的酒中吸了一大口水，摇了摇头，感觉它在她的脸颊上晃动。这真的不是她想谈论的——这并不完全令人愉快。

“I think I would quite like to know what was happening to the Malfoys while I was in their dungeon,” Luna went on, her gaze unfocused. Everyone tensed up at that. “I heard them screaming sometimes.”
“我想我很想知道当我在马尔福家的地牢里时发生了什么，”卢娜继续说，她的目光没有聚焦。每个人都为此紧张起来。“我有时会听到他们尖叫。”

Hermione’s stomach dropped into the region of her pelvis and she put her wine glass down on the table with a touch more force than was entirely necessary. “I think we should just stop talking about this now. Please.”
赫敏的肚子掉进了她的骨盆区域，她把酒杯放在桌子上，用力大了一会儿。“我认为我们现在应该停止谈论这个。拜托了。

“You’re the one –” Ron started speaking indignantly but managed to cut himself off when Harry gave him a significant look from across the table. A gust of air against Hermione’s leg made her think he might have directed a kick at Ron, too.
“你就是那个——”罗恩开始愤愤不平地说，但当哈利从桌子对面狠狠地看了他一眼时，他设法打断了自己。一阵空气吹在赫敏的腿上，让她觉得他可能也踢了罗恩一脚。

There was a tense silence, broken eventually by Neville who turned to Ron. “How’s Hannah, Ron?”
一阵紧张的沉默，最终被纳威打破，他转向罗恩。“汉娜怎么样，罗恩？”

“Oh,” Ron sounded surprised but pleased. “She’s good, yeah. Studying for her final Healer exams is keeping her pretty busy so she said she’s sorry she couldn’t be here tonight. She told me to tell you she’s asking for you, Neville.”
“哦，”罗恩听起来很惊讶，但很高兴。“她很好，是的。为她的期末治疗师考试而学习让她很忙，所以她说她很抱歉今晚不能来这里。她让我告诉你，她在找你，纳威。

Hermione noticed a pink tinge suffuse Neville’s cheeks. “Tell her thank you,” he said quietly. “That’s very kind.”
赫敏注意到纳威的脸颊上泛起了一丝粉红色。“告诉她谢谢你，”他轻声说。“真是太好了。”

“Yeah, she’s a good’un, Hannah,” sighed Ron fondly, taking a deep drink. “What about you, Neville? Anyone on the go?”
“是的，她是个好人，汉娜，”罗恩深情地叹了口气，深深地喝了一口。“那你呢，纳威？有人在路上吗？

The pink on Neville’s cheeks only deepened and he chucked. “No, no. You don’t get much time for that when you’re teaching at Hogwarts.”
纳威脸颊上的粉红色加深了，他咯咯地笑了起来。“不，不。当你在霍格沃茨教书时，你没有太多时间做这些事情。

Looking over at Ginny, Hermione could see her meddling friend’s eyes moving speculatively between her and Neville. Sensing that Ginny was about to do some very bad maths and propose a very unwelcome solution to Neville’s problem, Hermione blurted out that she’d seen Terry Boot at the archives.
赫敏看着金妮，可以看到她爱管闲事的朋友的眼睛在她和纳威之间投机地移动。赫敏感觉到金妮即将做一些非常糟糕的数学运算，并为纳威的问题提出了一个非常不受欢迎的解决方案，她脱口而出说她在档案馆看到了特里·布特。

“ Really ?” Ginny asked, sounding almost hungry. “And how did that go?”
“真的吗？”金妮问道，听起来几乎饿了。“那进展如何？”

“He asked me out.”
“他约我出去。”

Ron groaned, muttering something about Tedious Terry coming to their pub nights, and Ginny smacked him on the arm without even glancing at him. “And what did you say?”
罗恩呻吟着，嘟囔着关于泰迪斯·特里来他们酒吧之夜的事情，金妮甚至没有看他一眼就打了他的手臂。“你说什么？”

“I said I’m quite busy.”
“我说我很忙。”

Ginny’s smile was fixed, polite and, for that, actually quite threatening. “That’s it?”
金妮的笑容是固定的、有礼貌的，而且，实际上，相当具有威胁性。“就这样？”

“Terry thinks he likes it when girls are smarter than him,” Luna interjected, drawing a stunned stare from Hermione. “It makes sense he would ask you out.”
“特里觉得他喜欢女孩子比他聪明，”卢娜插嘴说，引来了赫敏目瞪口呆的目光。“他约你出去是有道理的。”

“ Thinks he likes…?” 
“觉得他喜欢......？”

“Yes,” Luna said, clearly with no intention of elaborating. 
“是的，”卢娜说，显然无意详细说明。

Ginny widened her eyes at Luna and shook her head aggressively. “ Luna . We’re trying to persuade her to date him.”
金妮瞪大眼睛看着卢娜，咄咄逼人地摇了摇头。“ 露娜 .我们正在努力说服她和他约会。

“I didn’t say no outright ,” Hermione said, holding up a hand. “I just said now isn’t the right time but I hinted I might say yes at some point in the future.”
“我没有直接说不，”赫敏说，举起一只手。“我只是说现在不是合适的时机，但我暗示我可能会在未来的某个时候说是。”

With narrowed eyes, Ginny considered Hermione and then her frosty expression melted into a grin. “Hard to get. Genius, Hermione!”
金妮眯起眼睛，打量着赫敏，然后她冰冷的表情融化成了咧嘴笑。“很难得到。天才，赫敏！

“Your wife is astoundingly meddlesome,” Hermione muttered to Harry who could only grin fondly and shrug. 
“你老婆真是爱管闲事，”赫敏对哈利喃喃自语，哈利只能深情地咧嘴一笑，耸耸肩。

“She just wants everyone to be as happy in love as she is.”
“她只是希望每个人都能像她一样在爱情中快乐。”

“Disgusting.”
“恶心。”

Chapter 9
第 9 章Chapter Summary
本章小结

Hermione and Lucius have another meeting and there is - incredibly - a little more progress than the last.
赫敏和卢修斯又开了一次会，而且——令人难以置信的是——比上一次多了一点进展。

May 18th 
5月18日

“I’m taking you on a detour today.”
“我今天要带你绕道而行。”

Lips pressing into a thin line, Hermione threw an apprehensive glance at Draco as they walked up the stairs to the second floor of Malfoy Manor. “Where to?”
赫敏的嘴唇紧抿成一条细线，在他们走上楼梯来到马尔福庄园的二楼时，他不安地瞥了德拉科一眼。“去哪儿？”

“It’s a surprise.”
“真是个惊喜。”

“Malfoy, I despise surprises. Particularly where your home is concerned.”
“马尔福，我鄙视惊喜。特别是在你的家。

Draco cringed, immediately understanding what she was referencing. “Could you not? You’re ruining it.”
德拉科畏缩了一下，立刻明白了她指的是什么。“你不能吗？你毁了它。

Sighing, Hermione hauled her bag into a more comfortable position on her shoulder. “I don’t want to be late. I’m fairly sure your father will hold that against me until the end of time .”
赫敏叹了口气，把包拖到肩膀上更舒服的位置。“我不想迟到。我相当确定你父亲会一直对我不利，直到时间的尽头。

“He knows I’m doing this. You won’t be late.”
“他知道我在做这件事。你不会迟到的。

Knowing that Lucius Malfoy was also apparently in on the surprise did not serve to make Hermione feel more comfortable. Quite the opposite, in fact. “This is still the way to his study,” she pointed out as though this was a fact worthy of suspicion. 
知道卢修斯·马尔福显然也在寻找惊喜，这并没有让赫敏感到更舒服。事实上，恰恰相反。“这还是去他书房的路，”她指出，仿佛这是一个值得怀疑的事实。

“Our destination is quite close to his study,” Draco said with a shrug. “It’s a surprise, Granger, not a conspiracy.”
“我们的目的地离他的书房很近，”德拉科耸耸肩说。“这是一个惊喜，格兰杰，不是阴谋。”

Sure enough, they walked down the corridor that had become oddly familiar to Hermione but, rather than stop at the usual door, they continued past it, turning left at the end where the large window stood. Within seconds, Hermione found herself in front of a set of towering double doors. 
果然，他们走在赫敏已经变得奇怪熟悉的走廊上，但他们没有在通常的门前停下来，而是继续经过它，在大窗户所在的尽头左转。几秒钟后，赫敏发现自己站在了一组高耸的双门前。

Squinting at a carved band that ran along the centre of both doors, Hermione could make out the Latin words ‘ scientia potentia est ’. Wearing a sly smile, Draco watched her read the words, understand them, and then glance at him with wide eyes. 
赫敏眯着眼睛看着沿着两扇门中央延伸的一条雕刻带子，可以辨认出拉丁文中的“scientia potentia est”。德拉科带着狡猾的笑容，看着她读这些字，理解它们，然后睁大眼睛瞥了他一眼。

“Is this—”
“这是——”

Placing a finger to his lips with raised eyebrows, Draco reached out and opened the doors to the library, throwing them open to her. It was . The library. 
德拉科扬起眉毛，将一根手指放在嘴唇上，伸出手打开了图书馆的门，向她敞开了大门。它是 .库。

“Oh my God, Malfoy.”
“哦，我的上帝，马尔福。”

Hermione stepped over the threshold to the room, feeling like she was entering a dream. A rather cold dream, she thought with an involuntary shiver. A temperature control charm was the likely suspect. 
赫敏跨过房间的门槛，感觉自己仿佛进入了一场梦。一个相当冰冷的梦，她不由自主地颤抖着想。温控咒可能是嫌疑人。

Unlike the archives at the Ministry, the Malfoy’s library was filled with natural light which entered the room through a large glass dome set in the centre of the high vaulted ceiling. Hermione surmised that was a necessity instead of an architectural ostentation because, rather than having windows, every wall was covered with floor to ceiling mahogany bookcases, with more bookcases jutting out to create deep rows. The bookcases were divided into two levels, a small balcony running around each one with a ladder for access. 
与魔法部的档案馆不同，马尔福的图书馆充满了自然光，自然光通过设置在高高的拱形天花板中央的大型玻璃圆顶进入房间。赫敏推测那是必要的，而不是建筑上的炫耀，因为每面墙都没有窗户，而是从地板到天花板的桃花心木书架，更多的书架突出来形成深深的一排。书柜分为两层，一个小阳台围绕着每层，并配有梯子。

“Thought you’d like it.”
“以为你喜欢它。”

“It’s...it’s pretty incredible,” she said, turning on the spot, her eyes on the highest shelves. “I’m not going to lie.”
“这......这真是太不可思议了，“她说，当场转过身来，眼睛盯着最高的书架。“我不会撒谎。”

“You can use it as often as you like.”
“你想怎么用就怎么用。”

Hermione halted, her gaze going from awed to suspicious as she lowered it to land on him. “What are you talking about?”
赫敏停了下来，她的目光从敬畏变成了怀疑，她低下头落在他身上。“你在说什么？”

Malfoy pointed to their left and Hermione spied an enormous stone fireplace. It looked as though it had once been a cosy seating area but any chairs that had been there had been replaced by a large desk. There was a comfortable-looking chair placed in front of it and, on its surface, a selection of ink bottles and quills. 
马尔福指了指他们的左边，赫敏发现了一个巨大的石头壁炉。它看起来好像曾经是一个舒适的休息区，但那里的所有椅子都已被一张大桌子所取代。前面放着一把看起来很舒适的椅子，椅子的表面放着各种墨水瓶和羽毛笔。

“I’ve set up a desk for you here. To get you out of that offensively small kitchen once in a while.”
“我在这里为你安排了一张桌子。偶尔让你离开那个令人反感的小厨房。

“Are you joking?”
“你在开玩笑吗？”

“I know you struggle with humour, Granger, but surely even by your standards that’s a pretty shit joke.” Hermione narrowed her eyes and opened her mouth to say something cutting but Draco jumped in before she could. “I connected your flat to the library Floo so you can come back and forth easily without having to go through the rest of the manor.”
“我知道你很不擅长幽默，格兰杰，但即使按照你的标准，那肯定也是个相当狗屁的笑话。”赫敏眯起眼睛，张开嘴想说些什么，但德拉科在她之前就跳了进来。“我把你的公寓和图书馆连接起来了，飞路，这样你就可以轻松地来回进来，而不必穿过庄园的其余部分。”

Hermione gaped at him, wondering if he knew how intrusive connecting her Floo to his without permission actually was. The triumphant expression on his face suggested that he didn’t. “Malfoy, I really don’t think—”
赫敏目瞪口呆地看着他，想知道他是否知道未经允许将她的飞路和他的连接起来实际上是多么的侵入性。他脸上得意洋洋的表情表明他没有。“马尔福，我真的不觉得——”

He tutted impatiently. “Shut up. You need more space. Desperately. So why don’t you just say thank you and accept the nice offer?”
他不耐烦地啧了一声。“闭嘴。您需要更多空间。拼命地。那么，您为什么不直接说声谢谢并接受这个不错的提议呢？

“You said your father knows about this?”
“你说你爸爸知道这件事？”

“Yes.”
“是的。”

“And he’s happy to allow a Muggle-born to work in his library, is he?” Hermione asked, crossing her arms and raising a skeptical brow. “To touch his things?”
“而且他很高兴让一个麻瓜出身的人在他的图书馆工作，对吧？”赫敏问道，交叉双臂，怀疑地扬起眉毛。“摸他的东西？”

Draco rubbed the back of his neck, his face scrunched up. “Er, not exactly.” Hermione nodded impatiently, hearing exactly what she’d expected. 
德拉科揉了揉他的后颈，他的脸皱了起来。“呃，不完全是。”赫敏不耐烦地点点头，完全听到了她所期望的。

“But,” Draco added brightly, “as I reminded him, this is my home too.” Hermione raised her other brow, reluctantly impressed by his forcefulness. He hadn’t offered his father anything? “ And it’s a good look for Shacklebolt," Draco finished, not even having the grace to look abashed. Ah. Hermione’s lips pressed into a thin line. There it is . “Besides, you’re not really touching his things, are you? You’ll be bringing all your stuff here.”
“但是，”德拉科爽快地补充道，“正如我提醒他的那样，这也是我的家。赫敏扬起另一道眉毛，不情愿地被他的强硬所打动。他什么都没给他爸爸吗？“而且沙克尔博尔这副好看，”德拉科说完，甚至没有表现出羞愧的风度。 啊。赫敏的嘴唇紧贴成一条细线。 就在那里。“再说了，你不是真的在碰他的东西，对吧？你得把你所有的东西都带到这儿来。

Hermione huffed and turned to look covetously at the spacious comfortable set up, content that he could not see her face. It was sorely tempting. 
赫敏气喘吁吁，转过身来，贪婪地看着宽敞舒适的装置，满足于他看不到她的脸。这非常诱人。

“Merlin, just accept it, Granger. I won’t know if you only use it once and then never come back. I just want to give you the option. The three of us barely use this room so someone should.”
“梅林，接受吧，格兰杰。我不知道你是不是只用了一次就再也没有回来了。我只想给你一个选择。我们三个人几乎不用这个房间，所以应该有人用。

On hearing Draco say ‘the three of us’, Hermione recalled what the portrait had said on her last visit to the manor. He was surely referencing himself, his father and Astoria. That surely meant Narcissa Malfoy was the one who had left. Looking at Draco closely, Hermione wondered whether or not that was the kind of thing she could ask him. It felt like something that would have come up by now if he wanted to talk about it. Closing one of her hands into a fist, Hermione repressed her burning curiosity; Draco was her ally in Malfoy Manor and she didn’t want to do anything that might result in losing him.
听到德拉科说“我们三个”时，赫敏想起了她上次来庄园时那幅画像上说的话。他肯定指的是他自己、他的父亲和阿斯托利亚。那肯定意味着纳西莎·马尔福就是那个离开的人。赫敏仔细地看着德拉科，想知道她是否可以问他那种事情。如果他想谈论它，那感觉就像现在就会出现的事情。赫敏将一只手握成拳头，压抑着她燃烧的好奇心;德拉科是她在马尔福庄园的盟友，她不想做任何可能导致失去他的事情。

“You really don’t come in here?”
“你真的不进来吗？”

“It’ll be all yours.”
“一切都是你的。”

Hermione glanced back at the cosy desk and then nodded, first to herself and then to Draco, a smile spreading over her face. “Alright then. Thank you, Malfoy. This is...generous.”
赫敏回头看了一眼那张舒适的书桌，然后点了点头，先是对自己点了点头，然后又点了点头，脸上露出了笑容。“好吧。谢谢你，马尔福。这是。。。慷慨。

“You can put a dedication to us in the book. ‘ A special thank you to the Malfoys, who finally provided me with a desk that isn’t absurdly close to an atrociously loud fridge.’ ”
“你可以在书中写下对我们的奉献。'特别感谢马尔福一家，他们终于给了我一张桌子，这张桌子离一个吵得离谱的冰箱并不近。”

Shooting him a wry look, Hermione turned towards the door. “You are foolishly ignoring the advantages that come from working beside a fridge.”
赫敏讽刺地瞪了他一眼，然后转身朝门口走去。“你愚蠢地忽视了在冰箱旁边工作的好处。”

“Enjoy the tour?” Lucius asked acidly from behind his desk when Hermione entered his office twenty minutes later than usual. 
“喜欢这次旅行吗？”卢修斯在办公桌后面尖酸刻薄地问道，这时赫敏比平时晚了二十分钟进入他的办公室。

“Yes, thank you.” Hermione replied primly, closing the door to his study behind her. “Your library is marvellous.”
“是的，谢谢。”赫敏严肃地回答，关上了她身后书房的门。“你的图书馆真棒。”

Malfoy’s eyebrows lifted a fraction before he fixed her with a haughty look. “I should think so; it’s the work of dozens of generations.”
马尔福的眉毛扬起了一点，然后用一种傲慢的眼神盯着她。“我想是的;这是几十代人的工作。

“And what would all of those ancestors say if they could see me in it, hm?” Hermione asked breezily, setting her bag down on the floor by her chair and flipping it open. 
“如果那些祖先能在里面看到我，他们会怎么说，嗯？”赫敏轻快地问道，把包放在椅子旁的地板上，然后翻开。

When she received no response, Hermione peeked up over the edge of his desk to look at him while she pulled out her equipment. “Nothing to say to that? Really?”
当她没有得到回应时，赫敏从他的桌子边缘偷看了他一眼，同时她拿出了她的设备。“没什么好说的吗？真的吗？

“Draco has suggested that when I think I am going to say something that may upset you, I should opt for silence instead,” Lucius responded stiffly. 
“德拉科建议，当我认为我要说的话可能会让你不高兴时，我应该选择沉默，”卢修斯生硬地回答。

Hermione genuinely laughed, her eyes crinkling as she leaned her head back. “Your silence is the problem , Mr Malfoy. If it means I get something worthwhile out of you, give me your worst. It’ll be nothing I haven’t heard before.”
赫敏真诚地笑了起来，她的眼睛皱了起来，把头向后仰。“你的沉默才是问题所在，马尔福先生。如果这意味着我从你身上得到了一些有价值的东西，那就把你最坏的事告诉我。这不会是我以前没听说过的。

His expression flickered and Hermione got the impression her insouciance irritated him. Good . Men like Lucius Malfoy liked to feel like they had the upper hand and she wasn’t particularly keen on just giving him that. 
他的表情忽悠，赫敏觉得她的漫不经心激怒了他。 好。像卢修斯·马尔福这样的男人喜欢觉得自己占了上风，而她并不是特别热衷于给他这种东西。

Sliding the Wheezebox into the centre of his desk, she adjusted her Quick Quotes Quill, addressing him as she did so. “Prejudice like yours is repetitive and frightfully unoriginal. You’ll have to get creative if you really want to hurt me.”
她把喘息盒滑到他的桌子中央，调整了一下她的快速引文羽毛笔，一边对他说话。“像你这样的偏见是重复的，而且非常没有原创性。如果你真的想伤害我，你就得有创意。

She glanced up in time to catch a gleam in his eye, which made her wish she hadn’t just effectively issued a challenge to him. As Draco had suggested to her, he was the kind of man that would rise to meet it. Before he could try, she continued speaking.
她及时抬头瞥了一眼，捕捉到他眼中的光芒，这让她希望自己没有有效地向他发出挑战。正如德拉科向她建议的那样，他是那种会挺身而出迎接它的人。在他尝试之前，她继续说话。

“Have you given thought to what I said last week?” she asked, drawing out her wand. “Are you willing to be more open?”
“你有没有想过我上周说的话？” 她问道，一边抽出魔杖。“你愿意更开放吗？”

“I am willing to try ,” he said. His tone suggested he was anything but, yet Hermione noticed the way his eyes lingered on her wand. It was possible Lucius Malfoy missed his magic more than he’d been letting on. Without it, after all, he was practically just a wealthy Muggle. Not that she’d dare to point that out to him.
“我愿意尝试，”他说。他的语气表明他绝非如此，但赫敏注意到他的目光在她的魔杖上徘徊。卢修斯·马尔福可能比他一直放的更想念他的魔法。毕竟，没有它，他实际上只是一个富有的麻瓜。她不敢向他指出这一点。

“That’s all I can ask for.” With an encouraging smile, Hermione tapped her wand to the Wheezebox. “Alright, let’s pick up where we left off last time, Mr Malfoy. You were raised here in Malfoy Manor?”
“这就是我所能要求的。”赫敏带着鼓励的微笑，用魔杖敲了敲Wheezebox。“好了，我们继续上次离开的地方吧，马尔福先生。你是在马尔福庄园长大的？

“Yes.”
“是的。”

“Can you tell me about your childhood here?”
“你能告诉我你在这里的童年吗？”

“I struggle to imagine what you could possibly want to know, Miss Granger.”
“我很难想象你会想知道什么，格兰杰小姐。”

“Well, what was it like being raised in such a large house as an only child? Was it lonely?”
“嗯，作为独生子，在这么大的房子里长大是什么感觉？是不是很孤独？

“I was never alone,” he said, his voice and face hardening so fast Hermione had to resist the urge to look over her shoulder for Medusa.
“我从来都不孤单，”他说，他的声音和脸色都变得如此迅速，以至于赫敏不得不忍住回头寻找美杜莎的冲动。

That’s not what I asked , Hermione thought. But she let it slide; he was talking. “Your parents were attentive then?”
那不是我问的，赫敏想。但她让它滑落了;他在说话。“那你父母很细心吗？”

“I had multiple nannies, tutors and servants.”
“我有多个保姆、家庭教师和仆人。”

“Oh, so your parents were…” Hermione trailed off, not entirely sure what they could have been. Too wealthy to work but too busy to spend time with their only son? Even Hermione knew that was insensitive phrasing. 
“哦，所以你的父母是......”赫敏慢慢走开，不完全确定他们是什么。太富有而无法工作，但又太忙而无法陪伴他们唯一的儿子？就连赫敏也知道那是麻木不仁的措辞。

“Doing what was expected of them.” 
“做对他们的期望。”

On seeing her surprise, Lucius sighed tersely. “Draco said you are quite thorough in your research but clearly you are not if you have not bothered to take the time to familiarise yourself with Pure-blood customs. How incredibly typical of your kind to revel in your own ignorance.”
看到她的惊讶，卢修斯简短地叹了口气。“德拉科说你的研究相当彻底，但如果你没有花时间去熟悉纯血统的习俗，显然你就不是。你们这种人陶醉于自己的无知是多么典型啊。

Hermione flushed, embarrassed and incensed by his criticism. She hadn’t really given much thought to Pure-blood customs. They were archaic and pointless, weren’t they? But, she considered, they had created the man before her. Hermione made a mental note to do some additional reading.   
赫敏脸红了，被他的批评弄得尴尬又生气。她并没有真正考虑过纯血统的习俗。他们很古老，毫无意义，不是吗？但是，她想，他们创造了她之前的那个男人。赫敏在心里记下要多读一遍。

“Perhaps you could enlighten me then, Mr Malfoy.”
“也许你能开导我，马尔福先生。”

Lucius pursed his lips and inclined his head. He probably relished the idea of schooling her in all the ways his upbringing was more unnecessarily elaborate than hers.
卢修斯抿起嘴唇，歪着头。他可能很喜欢用他的教养方式比她更不必要地复杂来教育她。

“In Pure-blood circles, it is not usually considered necessary for parents to be overly concerned with their children when they are very young. My mother left my care to those who were professionally qualified to provide it and my father entered my life as a guiding influence at the age of ten, in preparation for my attendance at Hogwarts. As is proper.”
“在纯血统圈子里，通常认为父母没有必要在孩子很小的时候过分关心他们。我母亲把我的照顾交给了那些有专业资格的人照顾，我父亲在我十岁时作为指导影响进入了我的生活，为我进入霍格沃茨做准备。这是正确的。

She had always slightly resented the idea that children with magical parents might have gotten that kind of advantage but, then again, it had only served to make her work harder. A lack of complacency and never taking her magic for granted had worked well for her.
“你爸爸教了你什么样的东西来准备进入霍格沃茨？”赫敏问道，期待着某种一年级前的魔法课程。她一直有点讨厌有魔法父母的孩子可能会得到那种好处，但话又说回来，这只会让她更加努力地工作。不自满，从不把她的魔法视为理所当然，这对她来说效果很好。

“如何成为马尔福。”

Hermione tried to turn her laugh into a cough but the way Malfoy’s lips narrowed into a thin line told her she hadn’t quite succeeded. “And that takes a lot of guidance, does it?” she asked with what she thought was an impressively straight face.
赫敏试图把她的笑声变成咳嗽，但马尔福的嘴唇眯成一条细线的方式告诉她，她还没有完全成功。“这需要很多指导，对吧？”她问道，她认为这是一张令人印象深刻的板脸。

“这是一个责任重大的角色，”卢修斯带着坚如磐石的尊严说。“他在教学中很勤奋。”

Hermione heard something in Malfoy’s tone that caused a tug of curiosity. Following her instinct against her better judgement, she asked, “Did you like your father, Mr Malfoy?”
赫敏从马尔福的语气中听到了什么，引起了一阵好奇。她凭直觉反对自己的判断力，问道，“你喜欢你的父亲吗，马尔福先生？

Lucius Malfoy drummed his fingers against the arm of his chair once and then stilled them. “I don’t see how my feelings for my father can be at all pertinent to your history of the war or my experience of it.” 
卢修斯·马尔福用手指敲了一下椅子的扶手，然后让它们安静下来。“我看不出我对我父亲的感情怎么会与你的战争历史或我的经历有任何关系。”

“他们不是，我想，”赫敏承认道，略微犹豫了一下。“只是......在我们早期的采访中，Draco 总是给我的印象是你从一开始就非常参与他的生活。他没有说任何关于纯血统规则或保姆大军的事情。

Shifting in his seat, Lucius looked to the side of Hermione’s eyes rather than in them. “Young men should fear their fathers.”
卢修斯在座位上挪动了一下，看向赫敏的眼睛一侧，而不是眼睛。“年轻人应该敬畏他们的父亲。”

“但德拉科似乎并不害怕你，”赫敏悄悄地指出。“我的意思是，我想他并没有减少恐惧，但他并不完全是恐惧。”

“I said they should , Miss Granger.” His eyes flicked back to hers, cold and hard like his voice. “Not that they all do. I hardly think your project will be a success if you do not listen carefully.”
“我说他们应该这样做，格兰杰小姐。”他的眼睛又瞥向她，就像他的声音一样冰冷而坚硬。“不是他们都这样做。如果你不仔细倾听，我几乎不认为你的项目会成功。

Biting down on her tongue hard enough to taste the tang of blood, Hermione attempted to compose herself. “Why doesn’t Draco fear you then?”
赫敏用力地咬住自己的舌头，尝到血的味道，试图让自己冷静下来。“那德拉科为什么不怕你呢？”

“Several reasons,” Lucius said with a careless wave of his hand. “Clearly I was wrong in allowing it.”
“有几个原因，”卢修斯漫不经心地挥了挥手。“显然，我允许这样做是错误的。”

“Why?”
“为什么？”

“Well, I wouldn’t be suffering through this indignity if I had ruled with an iron fist as I should have.”
“嗯，如果我本该用铁腕统治的话，我就不会遭受这种侮辱。”

Not entirely sure how to reply to that, Hermione left a brief pause which was, to her horror, filled by the sound of her stomach rumbling loudly. Lucius gave her a look which made her want to curl up in a ball.  
赫敏不完全确定该如何回答这个问题，她短暂地停顿了一下，令她惊恐的是，她的肚子大声咕咕叫的声音填补了这个停顿。卢修斯瞪了她一眼，让她想蜷缩成一团。

“I’m sorry,” Hermione said, her hand instinctively coming down to cradle her stomach. “I was in the archives this morning and I lost track of time. Completely missed lunch.” 
“对不起，”赫敏说，她的手本能地伸下来抱住了她的肚子。“今天早上我在档案馆里，我忘记了时间。完全错过了午餐。

Ducking under the desk and into her bag, Hermione rose again with a small plastic lunchbox in her grip. She lifted it up above the side of the desk so that he could see it. “Do you mind if I…?”
赫敏躲进桌子底下，钻进她的包里，手里拿着一个小塑料饭盒，再次站起来。她把它举到桌子的一侧，这样他就能看到它。“你介意我......？”

“What is that ?”
“那是什么？”

Rolling her eyes, Hermione cracked open the lunchbox and took out a small square of bread. “It’s a sandwich.” She raised it up to her lips and paused before taking a bite. “Can I?”
赫敏翻了个白眼，劈开饭盒，拿出一小块面包。“这是一个三明治。”她把它举到嘴边，停顿了一下，然后咬了一口。“我可以吗？”

“My options appear to be to allow you to drop crumbs all over my floor or listen to your stomach loudly protest your inability to adequately provide for yourself.” 
“我的选择似乎是让你把面包屑丢在我的地板上，或者听你的肚子大声抗议你无法充分养活自己。”

As though on cue, Hermione’s stomach gave a long whine and Lucius uttered a long-suffering sigh, raising a finger to rub the corner of his eye. “Just eat.” 
仿佛是受到了暗示，赫敏的肚子发出了长长的呜呜声，卢修斯发出了一声长长的痛苦叹息，抬起一根手指揉了揉他的眼角。“吃吧。”

He seemed unable to look at her as she took an eager bite of her sandwich, as though it was something indecent. Perhaps he couldn’t reconcile himself with the idea that Muggle-borns would do something as human as eat. That was, admittedly, something she struggled to picture him doing. 
当她急切地咬着她的三明治时，他似乎无法看她一眼，仿佛这是一件不雅的事情。也许他无法接受麻瓜出身的人会做一些像吃东西一样人的事情。“诚然，她很难想象他会这样做。

“I wish I could solely subsist on all the disdain you throw my way, Mr Malfoy,” Hermione said, giving him a sarcastic smile. “But unfortunately Muggle-borns don’t work like that. I’m sure that’s a surprise to you.”
“我真希望我能靠你对我的轻蔑来维持生计，马尔福先生，”赫敏说，对他露出一个讽刺的笑容。“但不幸的是，麻瓜出身的人不是那样工作的。我敢肯定，这对你来说是一个惊喜。

He raised a thin eyebrow. “What exactly were you doing in the archives that occupied you to the point of forgetting to eat ?”
他扬起了一道细眉。“你到底在档案里做什么，让你忘了吃饭？”

“Researching.” 
“研究。”

He left a questioning pause but Hermione did not fill it, instead looking at him with wide eyes as she chewed. He sighed, realising he was going to have to suffer the further indignity of having to ask a question that betrayed he was interested in anything about her. “Researching what ? It obviously was not Pure-blood customs, as we’ve covered.”
他留下了一个质疑的停顿，但赫敏没有填补，而是睁大眼睛看着他，咀嚼着。他叹了口气，意识到他将不得不承受进一步的羞辱，因为他不得不问一个暴露了他对她的任何事情都感兴趣的问题。“研究什么 ？这显然不是我们已经介绍过的纯血统习俗。

“I was researching you.“
“我在研究你。”

He blinked. 
他眨了眨眼。

“And your family.”
“还有你的家人。”

“And that occupied you for hours?”
“那让你忙了好几个小时？”

“Days,” she corrected him. “You’re an active bunch, aren’t you?”
“几天，”她纠正他。“你们是一群活跃的人，不是吗？”

Something passed over his face then but, not being especially well versed in Lucius Malfoy’s facial expressions, Hermione struggled to identify what it was. If the notion didn’t strike her as ridiculous, she could have sworn he was pleased by what he’d heard. 
然后有什么东西从他的脸上掠过，但是，由于不是特别熟悉卢修斯·马尔福的面部表情，赫敏很难弄清楚那是什么。如果这个想法不让她觉得很荒谬，她可以发誓他对他所听到的感到满意。

“Would you like a glass of water, Miss Granger?”
“要一杯水吗，格兰杰小姐？”

Hermione swallowed her sandwich with a loud gulp and hesitated. Unprompted generosity from Lucius Malfoy. It felt like a trap. Unless he actually was pleased that she’d spent days researching his family and this was some kind of sad reward. Considerate acts didn’t strike her as Lucius Malfoy’s bag, after all. While Hermione would eat her wand if Lucius Malfoy had heard of Pavlov she didn’t think it was impossible that he had developed a similar approach to conditioning.

Oh . “接下来的六天里，我不会再想任何事情了，”他抽搐着，把自己从座位上推开，转身看向窗外。

“Wonderful,” Hermione said, sticking her tongue out at his back before pulling the Wheezebox over to her side of the desk. Satisfied that her things were neatly packed away, Hermione rose to her feet and pulled her bag up with her.
“太好了，”赫敏说，把舌头伸到他的背上，然后把喘息盒拉到她这边的桌子上。赫敏对她的东西收拾得整整齐满意，站起来，把她的包拉了起来。

"Miss Granger, before you go." Hermione stilled. He had turned away from the window to face her with his hands clasped behind his back, his broad shoulders pulled back. "I am led to understand that you will soon be making use of my library." 
“格兰杰小姐，在你走之前。”赫敏安静了下来。他转过身去，双手紧握在背后面对她，宽阔的肩膀向后拉。“我明白了你很快就会使用我的图书馆。”

Hermione didn’t miss the way he lingered on the word ‘my’. It made her reluctant to tell him that she had given into Draco's aggressive generosity.
赫敏没有错过他在“我的”这个词上徘徊的方式。这让她不愿意告诉他，她已经屈服于德拉科咄咄逼人的慷慨。

"The offer was extended," Hermione said, raising her chin and jutting her jaw. "I haven’t yet decided if I’m going to accept it."
“提议延长了，”赫敏说，抬起下巴，突出下巴。“我还没有决定是否要接受它。”

His left eyebrow twitched briefly upwards. "If you do use it, I would recommend that you do not, ah…go a-wandering around it unsupervised."
他的左眉毛短暂地向上抽搐了一下。“如果你真的用它，我建议你不要，啊......在无人看管的情况下在它周围闲逛。

Hermione froze while adjusting the strap of her bag and met his eyes. "Are you threatening me, Mr Malfoy?” she asked, her voice low.
赫敏在调整包包的带子时愣住了，与他的眼睛相遇。“你在威胁我吗，马尔福先生？” 她低声问道。

"Certainly not," he said, tilting his head to the side with what Hermione could only identify as an utterly false display of polite confusion. "It’s nothing but a friendly warning. I have been reliably informed of how curious and hungry for knowledge you are. Some of the books in there do not appreciate such...insatiability."
“当然不是，”他说，把头歪向一边，赫敏只能认为这是完全错误的礼貌困惑。“这只不过是一个友好的警告。我被可靠地告知你是多么的好奇和渴望知识。那里的一些书并不欣赏这样的......贪得无厌。

Swallowing, Hermione took a step backwards towards the door. "I thought the Aurors cleared all the dark artefacts out of your home." 
赫敏咽了口口水，向后退了一步，朝门口走去。“我以为傲罗已经清除了你家里所有的黑暗文物。”

"Magic does not necessarily need to be explicitly dark in order to be harmful, Miss Granger, surely you know that," he said with a condescending smile. "Perhaps consider that some of my ancestors were rather creative with their prejudice."
“魔法不一定非得是明显的黑暗才有害的，格兰杰小姐，你肯定知道这一点，”他带着居高临下的笑容说。“也许想想我的一些祖先对他们的偏见相当有创意。”

Hermione bit down, her jaw clenched to the point of pain, and glared at him. Her mind was made up; if he didn’t want her in his library then she was sure as hell going to use it. Regularly. 
赫敏咬了下去，下巴紧紧咬到疼痛的程度，瞪着他。她已经下定决心;如果他不想让她在他的图书馆里，那么她肯定会使用它。定期。

“Thank you, Mr Malfoy," she said, her smile sour and strained. "I’ll bear that in mind.” 
“谢谢你，马尔福先生，”她说，她的笑容酸涩而紧张。“我会记住这一点。”
