May 21st
5月21日

Hands on her hips, Hermione assessed the mounds of parchment on her kitchen table with a critical eye. She was going to take some of them to Malfoy Manor and set up her desk there so that she could divide her work into two locations. If nothing else, the Malfoy’s library seemed like it would be a good place for distraction-free research, note-taking and hand-written editing of her transcripts, mostly because she didn’t have any intention of wandering around to any great degree after Lucius Malfoy’s ‘not-threat’. 
赫敏双手叉腰，用挑剔的眼光打量着厨房桌子上的羊皮纸堆。她打算带他们中的一些人去马尔福庄园，在那里设立她的办公桌，这样她就可以把她的工作分成两个地方。如果不出意外的话，马尔福的图书馆似乎会是一个无干扰的研究、记笔记和手写编辑她的成绩单的好地方，主要是因为在卢修斯·马尔福的“非威胁”之后，她无意四处游荡。

With a purposeful nod, Hermione lifted all of her books into a cardboard box. Next went the folders containing her interviews. 
赫敏故意点了点头，把她所有的书都举进了一个纸板箱里。接下来是包含她采访的文件夹。

When the box was full, Hermione heaved it from the chair on which she’d placed it and walked it through to the living room to dump it onto the floor in front of the fireplace. Wiping her hands on her denim shorts, she caught her breath and wiped the moisture forming at her hairline. 
当盒子装满后，赫敏把它从她放它的椅子上拿起来，然后走到客厅，把它倒在壁炉前的地板上。她用手在牛仔短裤上擦了擦，喘了口气，擦去了发际线处形成的湿气。

It was an unseasonably warm May day and she was starting to regret her decision to do anything even slightly physical. One of her least favourite quirks of her flat was that its temperature dropped to freezing in the winter but it somehow managed to be swelteringly hot in spring and summer. As a result, Hermione was either swaddled in multiple layers or wearing next to nothing. She couldn’t remember a time when it’d been a happy medium. 
那是一个不合时宜的温暖的五月天，她开始后悔自己决定做任何事情，哪怕是轻微的体力活动。她最不喜欢她公寓的一个怪癖是，冬天的温度会降到冰点，但不知何故，春天和夏天却闷热得要命。结果，赫敏要么被襁褓包裹着好几层，要么什么都没穿。她不记得有什么时候这是一个快乐的媒介。

Grabbing her bag of Floo Powder from the mantlepiece, Hermione stepped into the grate and reached out to pull the heavy box in with her. Satisfied that everything was in order, Hermione dropped a handful of Floo Powder and called for the Malfoy library. 
赫敏从壁炉架上拿出她的飞路粉袋，走进炉排，伸手把沉重的盒子拉了进去。赫敏对一切都井井有条感到满意，丢下了一把飞路粉，打电话给马尔福图书馆。

As soon as she stepped out of the green flames at Malfoy Manor, dragging her box after her, Hermione remembered the temperature control charm. Goosebumps rippled up her legs and across her arms despite the sun beaming through the glass dome above her. Really, it was something she should have considered for her own home. Groaning through gritted teeth, Hermione lifted the box onto the desk and set about removing her materials. The desk was so much more spacious than her kitchen table that she was able to set her folders side by side rather than on top of one another; it had an absurdly soothing effect on her mind. Fifteen or twenty minutes had gone by when a silvery voice spoke from the doorway.
当她从马尔福庄园的绿色火焰中走出来，拖着她的盒子跟在身后时，赫敏就想起了温控咒。鸡皮疙瘩在她的腿上和手臂上荡漾，尽管阳光透过她头顶的玻璃穹顶照射进来。真的，这是她应该为自己的家考虑的事情。赫敏咬牙切齿地呻吟着，把盒子举到桌子上，开始拿走她的材料。这张桌子比她的厨房桌子要宽敞得多，以至于她能够将她的文件夹并排放置，而不是彼此重叠;它对她的心灵产生了一种荒谬的舒缓作用。十五、二十分钟过去了，一个银色的声音从门口传来。

“Hermione Granger.”
“赫敏·格兰杰。”

Hermione flinched, momentarily clutching the folder in her hands more tightly, and looked up to see a very pretty and petite brunette standing at the entrance to the library. She was dressed in a long plum-coloured dress with sweeping, gold-clasped robes to match it. 
赫敏畏缩了一下，瞬间把手里的文件夹攥得更紧了，抬头看到一个非常漂亮娇小的黑发女郎站在图书馆的门口。她穿着一件紫红色的长裙，搭配宽大的金色长袍。

“Astoria?” Hermione asked, knowing it couldn’t really be anyone else. 
“阿斯托利亚？”赫敏问道，她知道这不可能真的是其他人。

“Do you mind if I…?” Astoria trailed off, gesturing into the room.
“你介意我......？”阿斯托利亚慢慢走开，向房间里打了个手势。

“Oh my God, no. Please,” Hermione said, setting her folder down on the table and stepping around it towards Astoria. “This is your home.”
“哦，天哪，不。拜托，“赫敏说，把她的文件夹放在桌子上，绕着它走向阿斯托利亚。“这是你的家。”

“Well,” Astoria said with a friendly smile, heels clicking sharply on the floor beneath her robes as she approached. “It’s my husband and father-in-law’s home but I’m told that I’m very welcome to treat it like it's my own.”
“嗯，”阿斯托利亚友好地笑着说，当她走近时，高跟鞋在她长袍下的地板上发出尖锐的咔哒声。“这是我丈夫和岳父的家，但有人告诉我，我非常欢迎像对待自己的家一样对待它。”

That sounded very much like the kind of thing that Lucius Malfoy would say, Hermione mused with a grim expression. Even ‘good’ Pure-blood women weren’t safe from his snide disapproval, apparently – he just couched it in more backhanded terms. 
这听起来很像卢修斯·马尔福会说的那种话，赫敏沉思着，脸色阴沉。显然，即使是“好”的纯血统女性也无法避免他的冷嘲热讽——他只是用更反手的措辞来表达。

“I just wanted to make sure you were getting on okay. The wards let me know someone had arrived in the library and I assumed it would be you.”
“我只是想确保你过得好。病房让我知道有人来到了图书馆，我以为会是你。

It was only when Astoria was a couple of feet away from Hermione that it became clear that she was pregnant. It wasn’t just that it was obscured by her robes and dress; Astoria’s belly, like Astoria overall, was very small. As far as Hermione could remember from her conversations with Draco, she must have been around 6 months along. The pregnant woman glow was something Hermione had heard Ginny aggressively deride as utter nonsense but even with that, Astoria looked, to Hermione’s eye, unusually pale and tired. 
只有当阿斯托利亚离赫敏只有几英尺远时，她才清楚地知道她怀孕了。这不仅仅是因为它被她的长袍和裙子遮住了;阿斯托利亚的肚子，就像整个阿斯托利亚一样，非常小。就赫敏和德拉科的谈话记忆中，她肯定已经有六个月左右了。赫敏听到金妮咄咄逼人地嘲笑说，那孕妇的光芒完全是胡说八道，但即便如此，阿斯托利亚在赫敏的眼中，还是显得异常苍白和疲惫。

Her breathing somewhat shallow, Astoria reached the desk and gently leaned her fingertips against its surface. Hermione wondered how much she was resisting the urge to flatten her whole palm down. Draco had told Hermione of the Greengrass family blood curse and how Astoria’s frailty concerned him but this was the first time she was seeing it for herself. The fact she was wearing what sounded like bloody stilettos probably wasn't helping.
阿斯托利亚的呼吸有些浅促，她走到桌子前，轻轻地将指尖靠在桌子表面。赫敏想知道她有多抗拒想要压平整个手掌的冲动。德拉科告诉赫敏格林格拉斯家族的血诅咒，以及阿斯托利亚的虚弱如何让他感到担忧，但这是她第一次亲眼看到。她穿着听起来像是血腥细高跟鞋的事实可能无济于事。

Hermione pulled around the desk chair. “Would you like to sit down?”
赫敏在桌椅上拉了一圈。“你想坐下吗？”

“No, thank you,” Astoria said with a polite but firm smile. “I’m quite alright. You’re getting on okay?”
“不，谢谢你，”阿斯托利亚带着礼貌而坚定的微笑说。“我还好。你还好吗？

Glancing at the chair and wondering whether this was a scenario where she ought to persist, Hermione hesitated before relenting. She would hate it if someone treated her like she was made of glass, after all.  “I’m getting on very well. Thank you for arranging this.” Hermione swept her hand over the large desk. “It's generous of you to welcome a stranger into your home.”
赫敏瞥了一眼椅子，想知道这是不是她应该坚持的情况，她犹豫了一下，然后才心软了。毕竟，如果有人把她当作玻璃做的事来对待，她会讨厌的。“我过得非常好。谢谢你安排这个。赫敏用手扫过大桌子。“欢迎陌生人到你家里来真是太慷慨了。”

“Oh, well, I know we've never met but I don't really consider you a stranger,” Astoria replied with a shy smile. “I actually rather feel like I know you. Draco speaks so highly of you and you made that divine lemon cake.” Astoria paused and considered Hermione for a moment. “I rather feel that when you've eaten something someone has made for you, you're bonded in a way. Particularly if you enjoyed it.”
“哦，好吧，我知道我们从未见过面，但我并不真的认为你是陌生人，”阿斯托利亚害羞地笑着回答。“我其实更觉得我了解你。德拉科对你评价很高，你做了那个神圣的柠檬蛋糕。阿斯托利亚停顿了一下，思考了赫敏一会儿。“我宁愿觉得，当你吃了别人为你做的东西时，你们在某种程度上是紧密相连的。特别是如果你喜欢它。

Noticing that Astoria glanced searchingly around the boxes, Hermione smiled. “I don’t have any right now but I’ll pop back to the flat and make sure I leave some before I go.”
注意到阿斯托利亚四处寻找地扫视着盒子，赫敏笑了。“我现在没有，但我会回到公寓，确保在我走之前留下一些。”

A tinge of pink appeared high on Astoria’s cheeks. It was absurd that Draco Malfoy had managed to make a woman this sweet a Malfoy. “Thank you. If you need anything while you’re here don’t hesitate to call on Letty; she’ll be very happy to help you.” She rubbed her belly and added, “I’m rather slow at the moment or I’d do it myself.”
阿斯托利亚的脸颊上高高地浮现出一抹粉红色。德拉科·马尔福竟然能让一个如此甜美的女人成为马尔福，这真是荒谬。“谢谢你。如果您在这里需要什么，请随时致电 Letty;她会很乐意帮助你。她揉了揉自己的肚子，补充道，“我现在挺慢的，要不然我自己就自己做。

Hermione nodded with a smile, though she made a mental note not to call on Letty unless she desperately needed to. The elf was lovely but Hermione wasn’t sure she could take another curtsey like the first one she’d received. 
赫敏微笑着点点头，尽管她在心里记下了除非她迫切需要，否则不要打电话给莱蒂。这个小精灵很可爱，但赫敏不确定她能不能再行一次像她第一次那样的屈膝礼。

Astoria stood up straight as though she was preparing to leave but Hermione could see from her face that she wanted to say more. It was the kind of internal struggle Hermione thought it best to wait out. Finally, Astoria said confidingly, “Draco and I are very glad you’re talking to Lucius, you know.”
阿斯托利亚站直了身子，仿佛正准备离开，但赫敏从她的脸上看出她还想说更多。赫敏认为这种内心的挣扎最好还是等下去。最后，阿斯托利亚自信地说，“德拉科和我很高兴你和卢修斯说话，你知道的。

“Well, he’s doing most of the talking, really,” Hermione shrugged. “Now, at least. I'm grateful to Draco for advocating for me.”
“嗯，他大部分都在说话，真的，”赫敏耸耸肩。“至少现在。我很感谢 Draco 为我辩护。

“We just think it’ll be good for him.” 
“我们只是认为这对他有好处。”

Frowning at the hopeful earnestness on Astorias face, Hermione tilted her head, wondering just what would be good about it. “Astoria, you know I’m not a therapist, don’t you? I’m just interviewing him for academic purposes.”
赫敏对阿斯托利亚脸上充满希望的真诚皱起眉头，歪着头，想知道这有什么好处。“阿斯托利亚，你知道我不是治疗师，不是吗？我只是出于学术目的采访他。

“A...therapist?” Astoria’s confusion was polite but plain on her face.
“一个......治疗师？阿斯托利亚的困惑是礼貌的，但她的脸上却很清楚。

“Ah,” Hermione hesitated. “I suppose it’s like a kind of...Muggle mind healer?” Hermione inwardly cringed at the wholly inadequate description. 
“啊，”赫敏犹豫了。“我想这就像一种......麻瓜心灵治疗师？赫敏在心里对这个完全不恰当的描述感到畏缩。

“Oh,” Astoria laughed lightly and waved a hand, “of course not, of course not. We’re not expecting you to do anything. I just think…” Astoria glanced over her shoulder towards the door and lowered her voice when she turned back to Hermione. “He’s been locked in this house for eight years and each passing year he talks to Draco and I less and less. We barely get any visitors. Draco is worried he's giving up and I think taking part in your project could be just the social rejuvenation he needs.”
“哦，”阿斯托利亚轻轻地笑了笑，挥了挥手，“当然不是，当然不是。我们不希望您执行任何操作。我只是觉得......”阿斯托利亚回头看了一眼门口，当她转身看向赫敏时，她压低了声音。“他被锁在这所房子里八年了，每年他和德拉科和我说话的次数越来越少。我们几乎没有访客。Draco 担心他会放弃，我认为参与你的项目可能正是他需要的社交活力。

“A social...rejuvenation,” Hermione said slowly. 
“一个社交......恢复活力，“赫敏缓缓地说。

“Yes, you're an entirely new kind of company!”
“是的，你们是一家全新的公司！”

Blinking, Hermione realised she wasn't entirely sure what to say to that. It was so odd to hear a woman younger than herself talk about former Death Eater Lucius Malfoy like he was a child showing cause for concern. 
眨了眨眼，赫敏意识到她并不完全确定该说什么。听到一个比她年轻的女人谈论前食死徒卢修斯·马尔福，就像他还是个孩子一样，表现出了担忧，这真是太奇怪了。

In some senses, Hermione supposed, she was an entirely new kind of company for him. She thought it unlikely, after all, that Malfoy had ever spent more than thirty voluntary seconds in the company of a Muggle-born. Whether that was good for him was another matter. He didn't seem to think so. In fact, all the horrible things he’d been saying to her suggested to Hermione that he was less in need of new company than new victims.
从某种意义上说，赫敏想，她对他来说是一种全新的陪伴。她觉得，毕竟，马尔福不可能在一个麻瓜出身的男人的陪伴下自愿地花了超过三十秒的时间。这对他有没有好处是另一回事。他似乎不这么认为。事实上，他对她说的所有可怕的话都告诉赫敏，他不需要新的陪伴，而是新的受害者。

“Is he being nice?”
“他很好吗？”

“Nice?” Hermione choked out.
“好吗？”赫敏哽咽着说。

“He can be very…” Astoria winced and Hermione mentally filled in the gaps. Cruel ? Awful ? Evil ? “Blunt.” 
“他可以非常......”阿斯托利亚皱起了眉头，赫敏在心里填补了这些空白。 残酷？ 可怕？ 邪？“直率。”

“Yeah, he's blunt alright,” muttered Hermione. He’s something that sounds like that, anyway . 
“是啊，他直言不讳，没事，”赫敏咕哝道。 无论如何，他听起来就像那样。

Astoria's brow furrowed with concern. “Draco and I have tried so hard to talk him around after the war, we really did. To make him less...well, you know. Suffice it to say he is not my greatest fan after that.”
阿斯托利亚担忧地皱起了眉头。“战后，Draco 和我努力说服他，我们真的做到了。为了让他不那么......嗯，你知道的。可以说，在那之后他不是我最大的粉丝。

That made Hermione smile. Based on her conversations with Draco, Astoria had had a very positive effect on him, not least in relation to his openness and tolerance. She made him more kind. It wasn't all that surprising that Lucius Malfoy would resent his daughter in law for driving that particular kind of change. 
这让赫敏笑了。根据她与德拉科的谈话，阿斯托利亚对他产生了非常积极的影响，尤其是他的开放和宽容。她让他变得更加善良。卢修斯·马尔福会因为他的儿媳妇推动了这种特殊的改变而怨恨，这并不奇怪。

“We have that in common,” Hermione said with a wry smile. “Any tips?”
“我们有这个共同点，”赫敏苦笑着说。“有什么提示吗？”

Astoria giggled guiltily. “Certainly not. I think the only thing I've done that's pleased him is get pregnant.” Her smile faltered somewhat and she looked around at the door again, a hand coming up to rest on her belly protectively. “Although maybe...you haven't mentioned Narcissa in front of him have you?”
阿斯托利亚愧疚地咯咯笑着。“当然不是。我认为我做过的唯一让他高兴的事情就是怀孕了。她的笑容有些动摇，她再次环顾四周，一只手伸过来保护性地放在她的肚子上。“虽然也许......你没在他面前提到过纳西莎吗？

Hermione shook her head, trying not to show how much her curiosity about the matter was burning in her.
赫敏摇了摇头，尽量不表现出她对这件事的好奇心有多大。

“Perhaps avoid her wherever possible.”
“也许尽可能地避开她。”

Hermione raised her eyebrows. “Why?”
赫敏扬起眉毛。“为什么？”

“It's not really my place to say.” Astoria looked pained. “I probably shouldn't have even said what I've said but I just think, you know, given you're going over his past you deserve some kind of warning. She's a rather large part of it, after all. Just tread carefully.”
“这真的不是我该说的。”阿斯托利亚看起来很痛苦。“我可能甚至不应该说出我所说的话，但我只是想，你知道的，鉴于你要回顾他的过去，你应该得到某种警告。”毕竟，她是其中相当大的一部分。小心行事。

“I will,” Hermione said, frowning, “or I’ll try. Thank you.”
“我会的，”赫敏皱着眉头说，“或者我会试试。谢谢你。

“Anyway,” Astoria said, a smile returning to her face with a clap of her hands. “I’ll leave you to get on with what you were doing!”
“总之，”阿斯托利亚说，她拍了拍手，脸上又露出了笑容。“我让你继续你刚才的事！”

Hermione thanked Astoria and, rather lost in thought, waited for her to leave the library before she continued unpacking her things. So she'd been right in her thinking; Narcissa Malfoy had left the manor. It was hard to blame her. Who wanted to be locked up with a man who did nothing but scowl and snap every second of the day?
赫敏感谢了阿斯托利亚，陷入了沉思，等她离开图书馆后，才继续收拾行李。所以她的想法是对的;纳西莎·马尔福已经离开了庄园。很难责怪她。谁愿意和一个每时每刻都皱着眉头和啪的男人一起被关起来呢？

Satisfied that everything was neat and in order, Hermione lowered her box to the floor and settled in at her desk. It was ludicrously spacious; there was room for her elbows to sit on the wood rather than just on piles of parchment. Spreading six pages of one of her interviews with Professor Flitwick out across the desk, Hermione shuddered at the luxury. 
赫敏对一切都井井有条感到满意，她把箱子放到地板上，在她的书桌前坐下。它非常宽敞;她的胳膊肘有空间坐在木头上，而不仅仅是放在成堆的羊皮纸上。赫敏把她对弗立维教授的一次采访摊开了六页，对这种奢侈感到不寒而栗。

The glow of the additional space began to fade when Hermione grew increasingly cold and thirsty. Working beside her fridge was a positive, no matter how noisy Draco thought it was. Looking down at the gooseflesh skin on her legs, Hermione decided that a cup of tea was in order. 
当赫敏变得越来越寒冷和口渴时，额外空间的光芒开始消退。在她的冰箱旁边工作是一件好事，不管Draco觉得它有多吵。赫敏低头看着腿上的鸡皮，决定喝杯茶。

Opening her mouth to call for Letty, she abruptly closed it again. She wasn’t sure she wanted to hear the shrill praise from Letty again, even if it was fantastic news. Besides, what if the elf was engaged with helping Lucius Malfoy and then decided to prioritise Hermione’s request over his? He’d have her out on her rear before she could ask for a splash of milk for her tea. 
她张开嘴想呼唤莱蒂，但她突然又闭上了嘴。她不确定自己是否想再次听到 Letty 尖锐的赞美，即使这是个好消息。此外，如果这个小精灵正在帮助卢修斯·马尔福，然后决定优先考虑赫敏的要求而不是他的请求呢？他会让她躺在后面，然后她才能要一点牛奶来喝茶。

Standing and pressing her hands into her lower back, Hermione rolled onto the balls of her feet and back down again. She’d be able to find the kitchen. It was likely on the ground floor and she knew where that was. 
赫敏站起来，双手按在她的下背部，滚到她的脚掌上，然后又滚了下来。她能找到厨房。它可能在一楼，她知道那在哪里。

The warmth of the corridor outside the library made Hermione shudder with pleasure. As she made her way around the corner to the stretch where Lucius Malfoy’s office was located, she stopped by the expansive window at the end and simply stood in the rays of sunlight that were coming through it, basking like a cat.
图书馆外走廊的温暖让赫敏高兴得不寒而栗。当她绕过拐角，来到卢修斯·马尔福的办公室所在的那段路时，她在尽头的宽大窗户前停了下来，只是站在从窗户射进来的阳光下，像猫一样晒着太阳。

The view over the rear of the manor was impressive. The building led out onto a raised stone terrace where Hermione could imagine plenty of garden parties were once held. Garden parties with undoubtedly nefarious purposes. Wealth combined with evil created that kind of dissonance to Hermione’s mind—dinners for disease, fundraisers for fires, mixers for murder. Civility and inhumanity wrapped in one expensive, incongruous package. Much like Lucius Malfoy, actually.
庄园后面的景色令人印象深刻。这座建筑通向一个凸起的石头露台，赫敏可以想象这里曾经举办过很多花园派对。毫无疑问，具有邪恶目的的花园派对。财富与邪恶的结合在赫敏的心中造成了那种不和谐——疾病的晚餐，火灾的筹款活动，谋杀的混合器。文明和不人道被包裹在一个昂贵、不协调的包装中。实际上，很像卢修斯·马尔福。

A wide set of stairs dropped down into a path and a large, gurgling fountain, which was surrounded by a rolling expanse of green grass. In the distance, Hermione could see what appeared to be a rose garden and the glass roof of what could only be a greenhouse. She had visited public parks with less space. 
宽阔的楼梯向下延伸到一条小路和一个巨大的、潺潺流淌的喷泉，喷泉周围环绕着一片连绵起伏的绿草。在远处，赫敏可以看到一个似乎是玫瑰园的东西和只能是温室的玻璃屋顶。她去过空间较小的公园。

Snorting at the sheer obnoxiousness of it all, Hermione was about to turn away from the window when a figure caught her eye. Squinting through the glass, she realised from the long hair that it was Lucius Malfoy. He was strolling through the sunny grounds in his shirtsleeves, waistcoat and suit trousers. It wasn’t his usual full robes, Hermione conceded, but he must be roasting . 
赫敏对这一切的纯粹令人讨厌哼了一声，正要转身离开窗户，这时一个身影引起了她的注意。透过玻璃眯起眼睛，她从长发中意识到那是卢修斯·马尔福。他穿着衬衫袖子、背心和西装裤，在阳光明媚的草地上漫步。这不是他平时的长袍，赫敏承认，但他一定是在烤。

It was odd witnessing him outside in greenery; almost like seeing a mirage. It was even more odd when a grey, straggly dog ran up alongside him and he leaned down to rub its head, leading it further along the garden with a gentle hand. Head pulled back, Hermione looked at her reflection in the glass and blinked several, befuddled times. Could a man who would treat most people like they were no more than dirt on his shoe really be a dog person? Apparently. 
在外面的绿树丛中目睹他真是奇怪;几乎就像看到海市蜃楼一样。更奇怪的是，一只灰色的、散乱的狗从他身边跑过来，他俯下身来揉它的头，用温柔的手带着它沿着花园走得更远。赫敏把头往后拉，看着镜子里自己的倒影，困惑地眨了几次眼。一个把大多数人当作鞋上的泥土对待的人，真的会是一个爱狗的人吗？显然地。

With a surprised hum , Hermione turned and made her way down the corridor. At least he was outside, she thought as she passed his office door; that meant she didn’t need to worry about bumping into him.
赫敏惊讶地哼了一声，转身沿着走廊走去。至少他在外面，她经过他的办公室门时想;这意味着她不需要担心撞到他。

“Ah, you.”
“啊，你。”

The unexpected voice almost made Hermione trip over her own feet. Looking wildly around, she saw the portrait of the dark-haired Malfoy wife staring at her again. 
这个出乎意料的声音差点让赫敏绊倒自己的脚。她疯狂地环顾四周，看到黑发马尔福妻子的画像再次盯着她看。

“Me.”
“我。”

“Are you lost again ? I do not wish to make you feel like a fool but you’re facing in the wrong direction entirely this time.”
“你又迷路了吗？我不想让你觉得自己像个傻瓜，但这次你完全面对了错误的方向。

“Oh, no. I’m not looking for the study this time I’m—well, I suppose I am trying to get somewhere. Do you think you could show me the way to the kitchen?”
“哦，不。这次我不是在找书房，我是——嗯，我想我是想去某个地方。你觉得你能给我指点去厨房的路吗？

The portrait raised an eyebrow and adjusted her belt with a fussy air. “My dear, you know I am a portrait and not a map, yes?”
这幅画像扬起了眉毛，挑剔地调整了一下她的腰带。“亲爱的，你知道我是一幅肖像而不是地图，对吧？”

Hermione blushed, chastened. “Well, yes but—”
赫敏脸红了，懊恼了。“嗯，是的，但是——”

“And that this family has not yet fallen so far it does not have house elves that are more than equipped to help you?”
“而且这个家族还没有衰落到如此地步，它没有足够能力帮助你的家养小精灵吗？”

“No, I know that, but—”
“不，我知道，但是——”

“So, if you know these things,” the portrait said with an incredulous stare, “why are you asking me ?” 
“所以，如果你知道这些事情，”画像用难以置信的眼神说，“你为什么要问我？

Hermione was asking herself the same question. “I just thought you might know,” she said, rather pathetically.
赫敏也在问自己同样的问题。“我只是觉得你可能知道，”她相当可怜地说。

Clearly unwilling to give the impression that she didn’t know something about her own home, the portrait frowned and adjusted her sleeves. “Well, it’s not that I don’t know… ” 
显然不愿意给人一种她对自己的家一无所知的印象，画像皱着眉头调整了一下袖子。“嗯，不是我不知道......”

“So can you show me?”
“所以你能给我看看吗？”

The portrait eyed Hermione, the very image of irritation, then finally sighed and rolled her eyes. “Oh, very well. Come.”
画像盯着赫敏，正是那个恼怒的形象，然后终于叹了口气，翻了个白眼。“哦，很好。来吧。

They walked in silence for a time, Hermione hearing the occasional shuffle and angry “ move ” as the witch pushed her way into a frame in which she wasn’t welcome. As they made their way down a corridor with more landscapes than other portraits, the witch used the reduction in confrontation to finally speak. 
他们沉默地走了一会儿，赫敏听到了偶尔的拖曳声和愤怒的“移动”声，因为女巫把她推入了一个不受欢迎的框架。当他们走过一条风景比其他肖像更多的走廊时，女巫利用对峙的减少终于开口了。

“Are you a Muggle?”
“你是麻瓜吗？”

“No.” Hermione glanced at the portrait, surprised the word Muggle hadn’t been spat at her like a spoiled bite of food but rather uttered with simple curiosity. “I'm a witch.” On receiving a doubtful look, Hermione reached behind her and slid her wand out from her back pocket, waving it in the air. “I have a wand. See?” 
“不。”赫敏瞥了一眼那幅画像，惊讶于麻瓜这个词并没有像一口变质的食物一样被吐向她，而是带着简单的好奇说出来。“我是个女巫。”赫敏收到了疑惑的眼神，把手伸到她身后，从后兜里掏出魔杖，在空中挥舞着。“我有一根魔杖。看到了吗？

“So you do,” the witch said, lapsing back into silence.
“所以你也知道，”女巫说，又陷入了沉默。

Hermione couldn’t resist investigating as they approached the main stairs. “Why do you think I'm a Muggle?”
赫敏在他们接近主楼梯时忍不住调查。“你为什么觉得我是麻瓜？”

“You don’t wear robes.”
“你不穿长袍。”

“Oh! Well, I feel they get in the way,” Hermione said, specifically thinking of the day at the Ministry when the sleeve of her robe had brushed across the wet ink of one of her proposals and ruined two hours of work. That day had changed everything for her wardrobe when she had a choice over what she could wear.
“哦！嗯，我觉得他们碍事了，“赫敏说，特别想起了在魔法部的那一天，她的长袍袖子拂过了她一个提案的湿墨水，毁了两个小时的工作。那一天改变了她衣橱的一切，因为她可以选择自己可以穿什么。

“Only if you're utterly clumsy,” the portrait replied with a derisive chuckle. “I'm surprised the master allows you to wander his home dressed like that.”
“除非你完全笨拙，”画像嘲讽地笑着回答。“我很惊讶主人允许你穿着那样在他家里闲逛。”

“I think the ‘master’ is surprised he's letting me wander his home full stop. My clothes are the least of his worries.”
“我觉得'主人'很惊讶他让我在他家徘徊。我的衣服是他最不担心的。

They had come to a stop and the portrait cast an assessing eye over Hermione, seemingly oblivious to the irate monk whose prayers she had just interrupted. “You might be right,” she said vaguely. “Anyway, turn right at the bottom of those stairs, right again, through the door, and it’s straight at the end.”
他们停了下来，画像用评估的目光注视着赫敏，似乎没有注意到她刚刚打断了那个愤怒的修道士的祈祷。“你可能是对的，”她含糊地说。“总之，在楼梯的底部右转，再次右转，穿过门，在尽头是笔直的。”

“You’re not coming?”
“你不来？”

“I do not care for the ground floor artwork,” the witch said sniffily. “Good luck.”
“我不在乎底层的艺术品，”女巫轻蔑地说。“祝你好运。”

Watching the witch push the monk to the side, Hermione let out a disbelieving little laugh as she descended the stairs on her own. She was going to find out exactly who she’d been talking to—she had enough Malfoy family trees to hand to do so.
看着女巫把修道士推到一边，赫敏自己走下楼梯时发出了难以置信的笑声。她要弄清楚她到底在和谁说话——她手头有足够多的马尔福家谱可以这样做。

Following the portrait’s instructions, Hermione found the kitchen in a matter of minutes. As she stood in the doorway and stared at the very large room in front of her, Hermione wished she’d also asked for the location of the kettle. And the cups. And maybe the teabags. 
按照画像的指示，赫敏在几分钟内就找到了厨房。当她站在门口，盯着眼前这个非常大的房间时，赫敏希望她也问了水壶的位置。还有杯子。也许还有茶包。

Squaring her shoulders, Hermione began opening cupboards, starting with those closest to her. Very quickly, she managed to find a china cup and a stainless steel teapot. She was bent over, rifling through one of the bottom cupboards looking for a teabag when she heard someone clear their throat. 
赫敏挺直肩膀，开始打开橱柜，从离她最近的人开始。很快，她就找到了一个瓷杯和一个不锈钢茶壶。她弯下腰，在底部的一个橱柜里翻找茶包，这时她听到有人清了清嗓子。

“Can I help you?”
“我能帮你吗？”

Flying upwards into a standing position, narrowly avoiding bashing the back of her head on the underside of the worktop, Hermione spun around to find herself looking at a very irritated Lucius Malfoy. Positively furious Lucius Malfoy, actually. Seething.
赫敏向上飞到一个站着的姿势，勉强避免了后脑勺撞到台面的底部，赫敏转过身来，发现自己正看着非常恼火的卢修斯·马尔福。实际上，卢修斯·马尔福非常生气。沸腾。

“No,” Hermione breathed, shaking her head and taking a step backwards. 
“不，”赫敏喘着气，摇了摇头，向后退了一步。

As though mirroring her, he took a step forward, then another. She was so desperate to keep at least three feet between them, it was mere seconds before she found herself wedged in the corner of the counters. There was no desk between them, she needed the desk between them. A beautifully polished, finely carved no man's land.
仿佛在模仿她，他向前迈了一步，然后又向前迈了一步。她如此拼命地想与他们之间保持至少三英尺的距离，仅仅几秒钟后，她就发现自己被困在柜台的角落里。他们之间没有桌子，她需要他们之间的桌子。一片打磨精美、雕刻精美的无人区。

“So you were just looting my kitchen for no reason, were you? Interviews not enough? You have to find out what I eat for every meal?”
“所以你只是无缘无故地抢劫了我的厨房，是吗？采访还不够？你得弄清楚我每顿饭吃什么吗？

“I was looking for teabags,” Hermione explained hurriedly, gesturing to the cup and teapot she’d left on the kitchen counter. 
“我在找茶包，”赫敏急忙解释道，指着她留在厨房柜台上的杯子和茶壶。

He stopped abruptly, looking in the direction she had pointed and then back at her disbelievingly. “We have a house elf, Miss Granger.”
他突然停了下来，看向她指的方向，然后难以置信地回头看向她。“我们有一个家养小精灵，格兰杰小姐。”

“I know but I didn’t want to bother her and I’m quite particular about brewing...my tea,” Hermione grew quiet when she saw his eyebrows were lowering with every word. 
“我知道，但我不想打扰她，而且我对酿造很讲究......我的茶，“赫敏看到他每说一个字都低下眉毛，她变得安静了下来。

“When I relented to Draco’s badgering it was because I was led to believe that you would be in my library and nowhere else . Being subjected to you at weekly intervals is bad enough; I will not abide you roaming my home, accosting me as I go about my day.”
“当我对德拉科的纠缠心软时，那是因为我被引导相信你会在我的图书馆里，而不是其他地方。每周都受制于你已经够糟糕的了;我不会容忍你在我家里闲逛，在我一天中搭讪。

“I didn’t accost you,” Hermione said indignantly. “I was just looking for a tea bag. If anything, you’re accosting me! ”
“我没有跟你搭讪，”赫敏愤愤不平地说。“我只是在找一个茶包。如果有的话，你是在跟我搭讪！”

If at all possible, he looked even angrier and Hermione hurriedly added, “I thought you’d have known I was here, anyway. Astoria said she sensed my arrival on the wards.”
如果可能的话，他看起来更生气了，赫敏急忙补充道，“反正我以为你早就知道我在这里了。阿斯托利亚说她感觉到我到了病房。

“I am rather disconnected from the wards of Malfoy Manor these days.” He clenched his right hand into a fist and Hermione’s eyes travelled down his arm, landing on his ankle. 
“这些天我和马尔福庄园的守卫们完全脱节了。”他把右手握成拳头，赫敏的目光顺着他的手臂滑过，落在他的脚踝上。

“Does the Magic Dampener do that?” she asked softly, her surprise diluting some of her outrage. It struck her as rather dangerous that he would be unable to sense when the wards of his home were being tampered with. He wasn’t exactly enemy-free, even eight years after the war.
“魔法阻尼器能做到这一点吗？”她轻声问道，她的惊讶冲淡了她的一些愤怒。她觉得相当危险，因为他无法感觉到他家的病房何时被篡改。即使在战后八年，他也不是完全没有敌人。

“You can hardly be connected to magical wards when you have no magic, Miss Granger,” he ground out. “Use your brain .”
“如果你没有魔法，你就很难连接到魔法守卫，格兰杰小姐，”他停下脚步。“用你的脑子。”

“Use your manners,” Hermione snapped, instinctively defending any slight on her intelligence.
“用你的礼仪，”赫敏厉声说，本能地为她的智力辩护。

“I hardly think you are in a position to criticise my manners when you are rifling around my home like a nasty little sneak thief.”
“我不认为你有资格批评我的举止，因为你像个讨厌的小偷偷一样在我家里乱来。”

“I just wanted a cup of tea! ” Hermione exclaimed, painfully aware that his point was actually somewhat valid.
“我只是想喝杯茶！”赫敏惊呼道，痛苦地意识到他的观点其实还有些道理。

A low growl sounded in his throat and he rubbed a hand upwards along his jaw. He moved so suddenly that Hermione automatically went to grip the handle of her wand. Rather than approach her, however, he marched to a cupboard on the opposite side of the kitchen that she hadn’t reached yet and pulled out a metal tin which he slammed onto the counter with enough force to make Hermione cover her ears. 
他的喉咙里发出一声低沉的咆哮，他用一只手顺着他的下巴向上揉了揉。他的动作如此突然，以至于赫敏不由自主地去握住了她的魔杖手柄。然而，他没有靠近她，而是走到厨房对面她还没够到的橱柜前，拿出一个金属罐子，砰的一声砸在柜台上，力气足以让赫敏捂住耳朵。

Opening the tin, he grabbed a teabag from within and threw it into the stainless steel kettle Hermione had found. As she watched him turn the tap on full, Hermione mused to herself that it was the most aggressive tea-making she had ever seen. And a very odd method. When he slammed the kettle down on the stove, he turned to Hermione.
打开罐子，他从里面抓起一个茶包，扔进了赫敏找到的不锈钢水壶里。当她看着他把水龙头开满时，赫敏沉思着，这是她见过的最激进的泡茶。而且是一个非常奇怪的方法。当他把水壶砸在炉子上时，他转向赫敏。

“Brew your tea and. Get. Out.”
“泡好你的茶，然后。出去。

Taking her wand out, eyes on him the entire time, she cautiously approached the stove and lit it with a non-verbal Incendio. 
她拿出魔杖，全程盯着他，小心翼翼地靠近炉子，用非语言的燃烧点燃了它。

“Are you just going to stand there the entire time?” she asked, eyeing his folded arms and angry glare. It could have boiled the water on its own. 
“你打算一直站在那里吗？”她问道，盯着他交叉的手臂和愤怒的目光。它本来可以自己把水煮沸的。

“Yes. You are going to make your tea and get out and I am going to make sure of it.”
“是的。你要泡茶出去，我来确保一下。

The wait for the water to boil was truly agonising. Hermione had never stood in a more tense silence, even when she and Ron had been fighting. Harry’s standoff with Voldemort had been less tense. The Cold War had been less tense and probably hadn’t felt as long, either. Out of the corner of her eye, she saw his gaze was fixed on her and she shuffled on the spot self-consciously. Unable to cope with the silence and judgement anymore, Hermione spoke.
等待水沸腾真的很痛苦。赫敏从来没有像现在这样紧张地沉默过，即使她和罗恩一直在打架。哈利与伏地魔的对峙没有那么紧张。冷战没有那么紧张，可能也没有那么长。她用眼角的余光看到他的目光正盯着她，她不自觉地在原地拖着脚。赫敏再也无法应付这种沉默和评判，开口了。

“Who’s the witch in the blue robes whose portrait is in the corridor outside your study?”
“那个穿蓝色长袍的女巫是谁，她的画像就放在你书房外面的走廊里？”

For a moment, she thought he wasn’t going to reply. In fact, it actually seemed like he really did consider ignoring her but an exasperated little nasal exhale signalled her victory. “Sabine Malfoy. I believe she married my ancestor Magnus Malfoy in the late 17th century. His portrait is on the ground floor somewhere.”
有那么一刻，她觉得他不打算回答。事实上，他似乎真的考虑过无视她，但一声恼怒的小鼻涕呼气标志着她的胜利。“萨宾·马尔福。我相信她在 17 世纪末嫁给了我的祖先马格努斯·马尔福。他的画像在一楼的某个地方。

Remembering what Sabine had told her about not wishing to visit the ground floor artwork, Hermione barely stifled her snort of laughter.
想起萨宾告诉她不想去一楼的艺术品的话，赫敏勉强忍住了她的笑声。

“I fail to see what is amusing in what I just said,” he said coldly.
“我看不出我刚才说的话有什么好笑的，”他冷冷地说。

“Oh, no, it’s...she’s good value.”
“哦，不，这是......她很有价值。

“Good...value?” he asked, his tone making Hermione think of an alien visiting Earth for the first time. “I do not know what it cost to commission her portrait so I hardly think you’re in a position to make such an assessment.”
“很好......值吗？“他问道，他的语气让赫敏想起了第一次访问地球的外星人。“我不知道委托她画像要花多少钱，所以我几乎不认为你有能力做出这样的评估。”

“I mean I like her.”
“我是说我喜欢她。”

“Most visitors find her abrasive and overly forward,” he said and Hermione thought she detected some surprise in his voice.
“大多数来访者都觉得她粗鲁，过于前卫，”他说，赫敏觉得她从他的声音中察觉到了一些惊讶。

“Maybe that’s why I like her.”
“也许这就是我喜欢她的原因。”

A crease appeared between his brows and he titled his head. As soon as the kettle started to whistle, Hermione lifted it from the stove with no small amount of relief and carried it over to her cup to pour. “I think there’s probably enough for two; do you want some?” she asked, forcing a casual nonchalance into her voice to hide how keen she was to leave.
他的眉毛之间出现了一条皱纹，他给自己的头起了个名字。水壶一响起，赫敏就松了一口气，把它从炉子里拿了起来，端到她的杯子里倒了。“我认为可能足够两个人使用;你想要一些吗？“她问道，声音中带着漫不经心的冷漠，以掩饰她有多么渴望离开。

Glancing over her shoulder, Hermione saw he was thin-lipped and absolutely not in the mood. “Just take your tea and get out, Miss Granger.”
赫敏回头瞥了一眼，发现他嘴唇薄薄的，完全没有心情。“拿你的茶出去吧，格兰杰小姐。”

Placing the kettle back on the stove, Hermione extinguished the flame and picked up her cup, gritting her teeth in an attempt to ignore the searing heat emanating from it. Asking for milk would be a mistake. Asking for honey would be even worse. Stepping around Malfoy in a wide circle, Hermione made for the door. 
赫敏把水壶放回炉子上，熄灭了火焰，拿起了她的杯子，咬紧牙关，试图无视它散发出的灼热。要奶是错误的。要蜂蜜会更糟糕。赫敏绕着马尔福绕了一大圈，向门口走去。

“Next time you are tempted to venture forth from the library, Miss Granger,” Lucius began, prompting Hermione to look back at him, “don’t.”
“下次你想从图书馆出去的时候，格兰杰小姐，”卢修斯开始说，让赫敏回头看他，“不要。

With a quiet nod of understanding, she exited the kitchen and didn’t stop walking until she was back in the library with the door shut tight. When she put her cup down and looked at her hands, the scalding cup had left them red raw.
她轻声点头表示理解，走出了厨房，直到她回到图书馆，门紧闭着。当她放下杯子，看着自己的手时，滚烫的杯子已经把它们染红了。

Chapter 11

The interviews continue and Hermione sees something she shouldn't. Uh oh.
采访继续进行，赫敏看到了她不该看到的东西。呃哦。

May 25th  
5 月 25 日

As soon as Hermione arrived in Lucius Malfoy’s study, she could tell something was off. For one thing, there was a faint smell of firewhiskey in the room. For another, the man himself was sitting behind his desk and it looked to Hermione like he could have been there for several days. She got the impression he’d been reading something when she walked through the door but he slammed a sheet of parchment over it at the sight of her.
赫敏一来到卢修斯·马尔福的书房，就看得出来有些不对劲。首先，房间里有一股淡淡的火威士忌气味。另一方面，那个男人自己就坐在他的桌子后面，在赫敏看来，他可能已经在那里呆了好几天了。当她走进门时，她觉得他一直在看什么，但他一看到她，就把一张羊皮纸砸在上面。

“Knock!" he snarled, his hand pressed flat against the parchment.
“咚咚！”他咆哮着，手平压在羊皮纸上。

"I did,” Hermione cried disbelievingly, looking back at the door through which she’d just entered. “Twice!"
“我知道，”赫敏难以置信地喊道，回头看了看她刚刚进来的那扇门。“两次！”

That shut him up , Hermione thought with grim satisfaction. Though it didn't stop him glaring as he muttered, "Well sit down, then."
这让他闭嘴了，赫敏满意地想。不过这并没有阻止他瞪着眼睛，他喃喃自语道，“那么，坐下吧。

While Hermione arranged the equipment, he took a swig from a short crystal glass. A surreptitious glance at its amber contents while she adjusted her quill told Hermione that it was probably firewhiskey. At 2pm? Something was definitely off. 
赫敏在整理设备时，从一个短小的水晶杯中啜饮了一口。赫敏在调整羽毛笔时偷偷地瞥了一眼琥珀色的东西，告诉赫敏这可能是火威士忌。下午 2 点？肯定有什么不对劲。

"What?" he asked. Perhaps her glance hadn't been as covert as she'd thought.
“什么？”也许她的眼神并不像她想象的那么隐蔽。

"Nothing," said Hermione innocently, deciding that bringing up the drinking habits of a man who had possibly been drinking for a while probably wasn't the best idea. 
“没什么，”赫敏天真地说，她觉得提起一个可能已经喝了一段时间酒的男人的饮酒习惯可能不是最好的主意。

Hermione drew her lower lip between her teeth to bite anxiously at it. Recording him wouldn't be the best idea, either. 
赫敏用牙齿咬住下唇，焦急地咬着它。录制他也不是最好的主意。

"Mr Malfoy are you…" Hermione took a fortifying breath and raised her eyes to his. "Are you in a fit state to be interviewed today?"
“马尔福先生，你是......”赫敏深吸一口气，抬起眼睛看向他。“你今天身体状况适合接受采访吗？”

His eyes narrowed dangerously. "What are you insinuating, Miss Granger?"
他危险地眯起了眼睛。“你在暗示什么，格兰杰小姐？”

"I think you've been drinking and I don't want to record you if you're not in a fit state to be recorded." It was direct but it had been him who had previously told her to opt for that over the delicacy she apparently lacked.
“我觉得你一直在喝酒，如果你的身体状况不适合被记录下来，我不想记录你。”这很直接，但之前是他告诉她选择那个，而不是她显然缺乏的美味。

"Ah, am I being treated to your famous academic ethics ?"
“啊，我受到了你著名的学术道德的对待吗？”

"I hardly think they're my–"
“我几乎不认为它们是我的——”

"Draco told me all about them," he said, pausing to take another drink. Of course he had. "I am surprised that you would extend them to me."
“德拉科把他们的事情都告诉我了，”他说，停下来又喝了一杯。他当然有。“我很惊讶你会把它们扩展到我。”

"I’m not here to take advantage of you, Mr Malfoy. I thought I made that perfectly clear."
“我不是来占你的便宜的，马尔福先生。我认为我把这说得非常清楚。

"Crystal," he said, raising his glass in a mocking salute and taking another drink. Oh, he's got to be a little pissed , Hermione thought. "I wish to proceed."
“Crystal，”他说，举起酒杯，嘲讽地敬了个礼，又喝了一杯。 哦，他一定有点生气，赫敏想。“我想继续。”

"If you're sure."
“如果你确定的话。”

"Keep your snide, doubtful little tone to yourself, Miss Granger. I don’t appreciate it."
“把你那冷嘲热讽、怀疑的小语气藏在心里，格兰杰小姐。我不欣赏它。

Hermione was ready to start recording when the crack of apparition caused her to pull her wand back. It was Letty. The house elf was levitating a tray laden with tea and sandwiches above her head, her already wrinkled forehead further creased with concentration as she kept it steady.  
赫敏正准备开始录音，这时幽灵的噼啪声让她把魔杖缩了回来。是莱蒂。家养小精灵将一个装满茶和三明治的托盘悬浮在头顶，她本已布满皱纹的额头在保持稳定时更加专注地皱起了眉头。

Hermione leaned forward to snatch up the Wheezebox as the house elf clicked her fingers to make the tray shoot forward. Malfoy rolled his eyes and lifted his firewhiskey high in the air as the heavily-laden silver slid over the surface of his desk, thoroughly disrupting its former neatness. A couple of sheets of parchment fluttered to the floor but he didn’t even spare them a glance and Hermione wasn’t about to start picking things up for him. 
赫敏向前倾身抢起了喘息盒，而家养小精灵则咔嚓咔嚓地打了个响指，让托盘向前飞去。马尔福翻了个白眼，将他的火威士忌高高举向空中，沉重的银子滑过他的桌子表面，彻底破坏了它以前的整洁。几张羊皮纸飘落在地板上，但他甚至没有看一眼，赫敏也不打算开始为他收拾东西。

"Tea and sandwiches for Master and Miss Granger," said Letty breathlessly, sparing a second to direct a shiny-eyed look at Hermione
“给格兰杰少爷和小姐的茶和三明治，”莱蒂上气不接下气地说，抽出一秒钟的时间，用闪亮的眼睛看了赫敏一眼

And Miss Granger? 
格兰杰小姐呢？

Still clutching the Wheezebox, Hermione blinked down at the tray and then up at Malfoy who seemed wholly unbothered. With a little wave of his hand and a murmured ‘thank you’, he dismissed the bowing Letty.
赫敏仍然抓着喘息盒，对着托盘眨了眨眼，然后又对马尔福眨了眨眼，马尔福似乎完全不在意。他轻轻地挥了挥手，低声说了声“谢谢”，然后打发了鞠躬的莱蒂。

"Is there any particular reason you look so astonished by tea and sandwiches, Miss Granger?” he asked, sounding weary. “I am well aware you have consumed them before. In my home, no less."
“格兰杰小姐，你对茶和三明治感到如此惊讶，有什么特别的原因吗？”“我很清楚你以前吃过它们。在我家，同样如此。

"These are for me?" she asked, carefully setting the Wheezbox back in place.
“这些是给我的吗？” 她问道，小心翼翼地将 Wheezbox 放回原位。

"You are quite self-centred, aren’t you?" he said, shooting her a stern look as he lifted a cup of tea and deposited it on her side of the tray. How odd the moments were, Hermione thought, when his manners overpowered his prejudice. He didn’t seem to notice. "These are as much for myself as they are for you. You’re not the only one who unintentionally abstains from food when occupied by other things."
“你很以自我为中心，不是吗？”他说，一边严厉地瞪了她一眼，一边举起一杯茶，把它放在她这边的托盘上。赫敏想，当他的举止压倒了他的偏见时，这些时刻是多么奇怪。他似乎没有注意到。“这些对我自己和对你一样重要。你不是唯一一个在被其他事情占据时无意中不吃东西的人。

Rubbing his bleary eyes with one hand, he lifted his own cup of tea towards himself with the other. His state of dress was pristine, as usual, but he himself was noticeably not. There was a shadow around his jaw and his complexion had a greyness that tended to follow prolonged periods of little sleep. It was disconcerting to see him so...dishevelled. 
他用一只手揉着朦胧的眼睛，另一只手把自己的茶杯举向自己。他的衣着一如既往地朴素，但他自己显然不是。他的下巴周围有阴影，他的肤色呈灰色，这种灰色往往是由于长时间的睡眠不足造成的。看到他如此......蓬乱。

"I meant what I said, Mr Malfoy; we don't have to talk today."
“我说的是真的，马尔福先生;我们今天不必交谈。

"And I meant what I said," he said coldly. "Begin."
“我说的是真的，”他冷冷地说。“开始。”

Still not entirely in agreement with his insistence, Hermione tapped the Wheezebox and then dropped her wand into her open bag. After a brief hesitation, she lifted a sandwich from the plate on the tray. Smoked salmon – her favourite. 
赫敏仍然不完全同意他的坚持，她敲了敲 Wheezebox，然后将魔杖放进了她敞开的袋子里。犹豫了一会儿，她从托盘上的盘子里拿起了一个三明治。烟熏鲑鱼 - 她的最爱。

"So, we stopped just short of discussing your attendance at Hogwarts in our last meeting. Would you mind giving me a sort of overview of your school career?"
“所以，我们在上次会议中就没有讨论你去霍格沃茨的事情了。你介意给我介绍一下你的学校生涯吗？

Hermione tried not to stare as he poured the remainder of his firewhiskey into his tea and stirred it neatly with a spoon. The spoon didn’t clink loudly against the cup as it did when she stirred her tea. He took a slow sip. Surely that tastes vile . His expression didn’t change if it was.
赫敏尽量不盯着他看，他把剩下的火威士忌倒进茶里，然后用勺子整齐地搅拌。勺子没有像她搅拌茶时那样在杯子上发出响亮的叮当声。他慢慢地啜了一口。 这肯定很糟糕。如果是的话，他的表情也没有改变。

"I was a successful Hogwarts student, overall,” he finally said, lowering his cup with a satisfied sigh. “I was sorted into Slytherin and excelled in my classes. When I reached the upper school, I was made Prefect and became a member of Horace Slughorn's club. The latter was, admittedly, more of a chore than a pleasure but it provided me with the appropriate connections for the role I would play in the Ministry and that pleased my father. ‘Make friends with the right sort’ is something of an unofficial family motto."
“总的来说，我是一个成功的霍格沃茨学生，”他终于说，满意地叹了口气，放下了杯子。“我被分到了斯莱特林，在我的课堂上表现出色。当我进入高中时，我被任命为级长，并成为 Horace Slughorn 俱乐部的成员。诚然，后者与其说是一种乐趣，不如说是一件苦差事，但它为我提供了适当的联系，使我在事工中扮演的角色感到高兴，这让我父亲很高兴。'与正确的人交朋友'是一句非正式的家庭座右铭。

I’m beginning to think ‘Sins of the Father’ could be another , Hermione thought wryly. 
我开始觉得《父之罪》可能是另一部，赫敏讽刺地想。

"I'm surprised you would have wanted to be a Prefect," she said aloud, pursuing the less combative path as she had tried so hard to do in their previous meetings.
“我很惊讶你会想成为一名级长，”她大声说，追求着一条不那么好斗的道路，就像她在之前的会议中努力做到的那样。

"Why exactly?"
“到底为什么？”

"Well, there are an awful lot of rules and responsibilities involved with the role. Forgive me, Mr Malfoy, but you don't strike me as being the rule-obeying type."
“嗯，这个角色涉及很多规则和责任。原谅我，马尔福先生，但你可别觉得我是那种遵守规则的人。

He delicately selected a sandwich from the tray and took an incredibly neat bite. Not a single crumb dropped and had he not been wearing the Magic Dampener, Hermione would have suspected some kind of siphoning spell at work. He chewed slowly, considering her before answering.
他小心翼翼地从托盘中挑选了一个三明治，咬了一口，非常整洁。没有一块面包屑掉下来，如果他没有戴着魔法阻尼器，赫敏会怀疑有什么虹吸咒在起作用。他慢慢地咀嚼着，在回答之前打量着她。

"Surely after our discussion about the Ministry last week you know why I would have wanted to be a Prefect." When Hermione did nothing but shrug he rolled his eyes. "Being in a position of power makes it much easier to break the rules, Miss Granger. It's quite simple."
“当然，在我们上周讨论过魔法部的事情之后，你知道我为什么会想成为一名级长。”赫敏除了耸耸肩什么也没做，他翻了个白眼。“身居高位更容易打破规则，格兰杰小姐。这很简单。

Hermione recalled Ron confiscating items from younger students with a grim expression. She imagined Lucius Malfoy's rule breaking had been a touch more sinister than that.
赫敏回忆起罗恩没收了低年级学生的东西，脸上露出了严肃的表情。她想象着卢修斯·马尔福的违规行为比这更险恶。

“And you didn’t play Quidditch?”
“你没有打魁地奇吗？”

A vaguely offended look passed over his face. “Of course not. I had neither the time nor the inclination. I abhor broomsticks; an utterly inelegant method of travel."
他的脸上掠过一丝隐约的冒犯。“当然不是。我既没有时间，也没有兴趣。我讨厌扫帚;一种完全不优雅的旅行方式。

“Oh!” It was fair enough, Hermione supposed, looking him over. As far as she could tell through the layers of his robes, he was tall and fairly lean—not a bad build for a Chaser she would sure Ron would say—but she still found it rather difficult to imagine Lucius Malfoy on a broomstick. It’d mess up his hair.
“哦！”这很公平，赫敏想，一边打量着他。从他那层层的长袍中可以看出，他个子高大，相当瘦弱——她确信罗恩会这么说，对于一个追逐者来说，这个身材还不错——但她还是觉得很难想象卢修斯·马尔福骑着扫帚的样子。这会弄乱他的头发。

"Why do you sound so surprised?" he asked, eyeing her over the rim of his cup as he raised it for another drink.
“你为什么听起来这么惊讶？”他问道，一边盯着她的杯子边缘，一边举起杯子准备再喝一杯。

Hermione shrugged and crossed her legs. "Well, Mal—I mean, your son was always so keen on Quidditch and I just assumed that, like most things, it was because he wanted to impress you."
赫敏耸耸肩，盘起双腿。“嗯，马尔——我是说，你儿子总是那么热衷于魁地奇，我只是觉得，就像大多数事情一样，那是因为他想给你留下深刻印象。”

"I imagine it was," Malfoy lowered his cup to the desk and sat back, leaning one elbow on the arm of his chair while clasping his hands.
“我想是这样，”马尔福把杯子放到桌子上，坐回去，一只手肘靠在椅子的扶手上，双手紧握。

"Why would he think it would impress you if you’re not interested in it?"
“如果你对它不感兴趣，他为什么会认为它会给你留下深刻印象？”

"Because I let him think I was." His expression said ‘ duh’ so that his mouth didn't have to but Hermione was still visibly puzzled. "He was interested in Quidditch and showed an aptitude for flying," Lucius elaborated as though he was the most patient person in the world speaking to the most dense.
“因为我让他认为我是。”他的表情说“呃”，这样他的嘴就不必了，但赫敏仍然明显感到困惑。“他对魁地奇很感兴趣，并表现出了飞行的天赋，”卢修斯解释道，仿佛他是世界上最有耐心的人，与最密集的人交谈。

"So you just...pretended?"
“所以你只是......假装的？

"Why would I want to discourage my son from pursuing something that he’s good at?"
“我为什么要劝阻我的儿子不要追求他擅长的事情？”

Realising her mouth had dropped open, Hermione closed it with a click of her teeth and swallowed her urge to say 'because you’re Lucius Malfoy'. He raised his eyebrows at her silence, giving her the distinct impression that he was waiting for her to say just that. Still grappling with the revelation that Lucius Malfoy possessed anything close to unselfish fatherly tendencies, Hermione decided to shift the subject to safer ground.  
赫敏意识到自己的嘴巴张开了，咔嚓一声咬紧了嘴，忍住了想说“因为你是卢修斯·马尔福”的冲动。他对她的沉默扬起眉毛，给她一种明显的印象，他在等她说这句话。赫敏仍然在努力应对卢修斯·马尔福拥有任何接近无私的父亲倾向的启示，她决定将话题转移到更安全的领域。

"You seem content with what you got out of school. Did you like Hogwarts?"
“你似乎对你从学校学到的东西感到满意。你喜欢霍格沃茨吗？

"I had a perfectly acceptable experience." That doesn't sound like much fun , Hermione thought. 
“我有一次完全可以接受的经历。” 这听起来没什么好玩的，赫敏想。

“You liked your teachers?”
“你喜欢你的老师吗？”

“Well enough."
“很好。”

“Even Dumbledore?”
“甚至邓布利多？”

He stalled in lifting his cup to his mouth, his eyes flicking up to hers. “I had my reservations there.”
他停滞不前，把杯子举到嘴边，眼睛眨了眨。“我在那里有所保留。”

"Is there any particular reason for that?"
“这有什么特别的原因吗？”

“Several,” he said carefully, setting the cup back down with a faint clink . 
“好几个，”他小心翼翼地说，轻轻地叮当一声把杯子放回去。

“I’d appreciate it if you could give me at least one,” Hermione said, musing that her parents probably had an easier time drawing teeth from recalcitrant children than she had drawing detail from the man in front of her.
“如果你能给我至少一个，我会很感激的，”赫敏说，她沉思着，她的父母可能比她从面前的男人身上画细节更容易。

Lucius tutted, leaning back and twisting his signet ring around his finger. “He could be a very closed-minded man."
卢修斯啧了一声，向后靠着，把他的图章戒指扭在手指上。“他可能是一个非常思想封闭的人。”

If Hermione had been drinking her tea at that moment, she was sure she would have choked on it. Lucius Malfoy calling anyone closed-minded was richer than he was. 
如果赫敏在那一刻正在喝她的茶，她肯定自己会被茶呛到。卢修斯·马尔福称呼任何思想封闭的人比他更富有。

"Any particular examples of that closed-mindedness you can give me?"
“你能给我举个具体的例子来说明这种封闭的思想吗？”

Lucius appeared to ponder her question, his eyes losing focus as he continued to rotate his ring on his finger with an absent air. Finally, his eyes sharpening again, he said, "Once he took the post, the Restricted Section of the library doubled overnight.” 
卢修斯似乎在思考她的问题，他的眼睛失去了焦点，继续用心不在焉的语气转动着手指上的戒指。最后，他的眼睛又变得锐利起来，他说道：“他一上任，图书馆的禁区就在一夜之间翻了一番。

Interesting . “Who told you that?”
有趣。“谁告诉你的？”

“Several older students in Slytherin house as well as my father and his associates.” 
“斯莱特林学院的几个年纪较大的学生，还有我爸爸和他的同事。”

Hermione quietly pondered Malfoy’s criteria for determining a trustworthy source. He struck her as a man who was not lacking intelligence, yet throughout his life he had proven he was not averse to simply believing things he’d been told by his elders with little to no critical engagement. 
赫敏静静地思考着马尔福确定可靠来源的标准。他给她的印象是一个不缺乏智慧的人，但在他的一生中，他已经证明他并不反对简单地相信长辈告诉他的事情，几乎没有批评性的参与。

Was it possible he only used that sharp mind when it suited him? That seemed likely to Hermione. After all, Purebloods like him didn’t tend to ask questions when it was more convenient to believe what they were being told. They didn't need to. To examine anything beyond the surface was to risk finding out they weren’t nearly as special as they thought. 
有没有可能，他只在适合他的时候才使用那敏锐的头脑？在赫敏看来，这似乎是可能的。毕竟，像他这样的纯血统者在更方便相信他们被告知的内容时不会提出问题。他们不需要这样做。检查表面之外的任何东西都是冒着发现它们并不像他们想象的那么特别的风险。

How much of what Lucius Malfoy had believed and done, she wondered, had been borne out of outright wickedness and how much had just been spineless apathy? 
她想知道，卢修斯·马尔福所相信和所做的，有多少是出于彻头彻尾的邪恶，又有多少是毫无骨气的冷漠？

“And that bothered you?” Hermione asked. “That he increased the size of the Restricted Section?”
“这让你很困扰？”赫敏问道。“他增加了限制区的规模？”

“Of course it did,” Lucius said, frowning in a way that suggested he was offended by the implication that it wouldn’t. “Knowledge should not be restricted.” 
“当然是这样，”卢修斯说，皱着眉头，似乎他被这种不会的暗示冒犯了。“知识不应该受到限制。”

Hermione raised her eyebrows. Obviously he only meant with regards to Pure-bloods.
赫敏扬起眉毛。显然，他指的是纯血统。

“Albus Dumbledore warded off entire areas of study to students, attached shame and secrecy to those areas of study, just because he had been unable to control himself where they were concerned,” Lucius continued. “Typical Gryffindor—brave in the face of everything except a mirror.”
“阿不思·邓布利多把整个研究领域都排除在学生之外，给那些研究领域带来羞耻和秘密，只是因为他在他们关心的地方无法控制自己，”卢修斯继续说道。“典型的格兰芬多——勇敢地面对除了镜子之外的一切。”

Gliding over his jibe at Gryffindor with an ease of which she was actually rather proud, Hermione said, “I never had any issue with getting books from the Restricted Section when I was at Hogwarts, Mr Malfoy.” Even if she had been forced to trick Professor Lockhart that time.
赫敏轻松地滑过他对格兰芬多的嘲讽，她实际上相当自豪，她说，“当我在霍格沃茨的时候，我从来没有遇到过从禁区买书的问题，马尔福先生。即使那次她被迫欺骗了洛哈特教授。

“You were not a Slytherin, Miss Granger. When we showed an interest in the books within that section we were watched more carefully than students from other houses.” Hermione searched his face. He looked like he truly believed what he said. Was that true ? “I imagine it was always assumed that your intent was noble . I never appreciated anyone else setting my limits.”
“你不是斯莱特林，格兰杰小姐。当我们对那个部分的书籍表现出兴趣时，我们比其他学院的学生受到更仔细的观察。赫敏搜索了他的脸。他看起来真的相信自己所说的话。这是真的吗？“我想人们总是认为你的意图是高尚的。我从来不欣赏别人为我设定极限。

Yet you would happily set limits for other people , Hermione thought bitterly. He would set limits for people like her, for creatures like Dobby but Merlin forbid that anyone set any for him . Typical bloody Malfoy.
然而，你会很乐意为其他人设定限制，赫敏苦涩地想。他会为像她这样的人，为像多比这样的生物设定限制，但梅林禁止任何人为他设定任何限制。典型的血腥马尔福。

“I’m sure Dumbledore had a good reason for expanding the Restricted Section.” If he even did .
“我敢肯定邓布利多有充分的理由扩大禁区。” 如果他真的这样做了。

“Only if you consider hypocrisy a good reason,” Malfoy said archly. “Restricting access to texts has certainly never stopped those interested in the Dark Arts from learning about them. All it’s ever done is create a false, reductive binary. ‘Restricted’ and ‘permitted’. ‘Dark’ and ‘light’. ‘Good’ and ‘evil’. They are books and the Dark Arts were never going to stop existing merely because one man would rather they didn’t.”
“除非你把虚伪当成一个好的理由，”马尔福拱手说。“限制对文本的访问肯定从未阻止那些对黑魔法感兴趣的人了解它们。它所做的只是创造了一个虚假的、简化的二元论。“受限”和“允许”。“黑暗”和“浅”。“善”和“恶”。它们是书，黑魔法永远不会仅仅因为一个人宁愿他们不这样做就停止存在。

Hermione blinked at Malfoy. More than once, she had grumbled resentfully about the oppressive rules of the Restricted Section. The permission slips; the ban on taking books out lest she share the restricted knowledge; Madam Pince breathing down her neck and checking her notes. It had always felt so ridiculous. Not only that, it hadn’t stopped her from brewing Polyjuice Potion anyway.
赫敏对马尔福眨了眨眼。她不止一次地不满地抱怨禁区的压迫性规则。许可单;禁止带书外出，以免她分享受限知识;平斯夫人顺着她的脖子呼吸，检查她的笔记。这总是让人觉得很荒谬。不仅如此，这并没有阻止她酿造复方汤剂。

When she, Harry and Ron had been looking for information on Horcruxes to destroy them, the books had been nowhere in sight. The knowledge they’d needed had been removed even further than the Restricted Section, taken from those who needed it to do good as much as those who wanted to do evil. Yet a simple Accio had gotten it to her because she’d been determined. Someone looking to make Horcruxes could have been just as determined to try the same thing. Relief and anger had coursed through her in equal measure when the books had come flying through her window that day.
当她、哈利和罗恩一直在寻找魂器的信息以摧毁它们时，那些书已经不见踪影了。他们需要的知识已经被比禁区更进一步地被剥夺了，从那些需要它来行善的人和那些想作恶的人那里被夺走了。然而，一个简单的 Accio 就得到了它，因为她已经下定决心。想要制作魂器的人可能也同样决心尝试同样的事情。那天，当书从她的窗户飞来时，她心中既如释重负，又生气。

“Did you not find it unsatisfying, Miss Granger,” Malfoy continued, blissfully unaware of her resentful musings, “that you were not taught the Dark Arts, yet you spent hours of every week learning to defend against them?”
“难道你不觉得不满意吗，格兰杰小姐，”马尔福继续说道，幸福地没有意识到她那不满的沉思，“你没有学过黑魔法，却每周花几个小时来学习防御它们吗？

“We did learn about the Dark Arts in defence classes, that's hardly acc—”
“我们确实在防御术课上学过黑魔法，这可不是什么——”

“You learned the bare minimum,” he said admonishingly. “And that is not nearly enough. Those classes leave enough mystery around the Dark Arts to ensure that your fear of them grows disproportionately to your understanding of them. You cannot truly defend yourself against the Dark Arts until you understand them. It's arrogant to believe otherwise. And willfully ignorant to frame all other counter-jinxes and defensive spells as ‘good’ or ‘right’ when they can be used to inflict harm as easily as any so-called Dark spell. Malicious intent may power the Unforgivable Curses but it is not as reliant upon them as they are upon it.”
“你学到了最低限度的东西，”他告诫地说。“这还远远不够。这些职业在黑魔法周围留下了足够的神秘感，以确保你对它们的恐惧与你对它们的理解不成比例地增长。除非你理解了黑魔法，否则你无法真正保护自己免受黑魔法的攻击。不这么认为是傲慢的。并且故意无知地将所有其他反恶灵和防御法术框定为“好”或“正确”，因为它们可以像任何所谓的黑暗咒语一样容易地用来造成伤害。恶意可能会为不可饶恕的诅咒提供动力，但它并不像他们那样依赖它们。

Unbidden, a memory of lighting professor Snape’s cloak on fire with the Incendio charm passed through Hermione’s mind; of confunding McClaggen when he was 50 feet in the air on a broomstick; of stunning Death Eaters in mid-air while she clung desperately to Kingsley’s cloak and hoped she wouldn't fall to her death like them. None of those spells were Dark and she hadn't actually wanted to harm anyone but that didn't mean those spells had not been without the potential to cause harm. Somehow that risk hadn’t mattered to her at the time.
不请自来，赫敏的脑海中闪过了用燃烧咒点燃斯内普教授的斗篷的记忆;当 McClaggen 骑着扫帚在 50 英尺高的空中时，他被收养;半空中的食死徒们被击晕，而她拼命地紧紧抓住金斯莱的斗篷，希望她不会像他们一样摔死。那些咒语都不是黑暗的，她实际上也不想伤害任何人，但这并不意味着那些咒语并非没有造成伤害的潜力。不知何故，当时这种风险对她来说并不重要。

“But those spells are legal,” Hermione pointed out. 
“但那些咒语是合法的，”赫敏指出。

“And your personal moral code is entirely bound up in the law, is it?”
“而且你的个人道德准则完全受法律的约束，是吗？”

“Well, yours certainly isn’t,” Hermione said with a frown. He had some cheek to talk to her about moral codes . As if he had one.
“嗯，你的肯定不是，”赫敏皱着眉头说。他有些厚颜无耻地和她谈论道德准则。就好像他有一样。

A hint of a smile passed over his face at that. “You can judge me for my views on magic all you want, Miss Granger. I feel no shame in them. Suffice it to say that, from my perspective, magic is magic. The only limit should be how far you’re willing to go with it. While I could never claim to be a master of the Dark Arts, I certainly understand them enough to know evil intent is not the sole motivation of those who develop an interest in them.”
“说到这里，他的脸上闪过一丝微笑。“你可以随心所欲地评判我对魔法的看法，格兰杰小姐。我对他们并不感到羞耻。可以说，在我看来，魔法就是魔法。唯一的限制应该是你愿意走多远。虽然我永远无法声称自己是黑魔法大师，但我确实足够了解它们，知道邪恶的意图并不是那些对它们产生兴趣的人的唯一动机。

“Just as pure intent isn’t always the sole motivation of people who don’t,” Hermione finished quietly. She’d encountered enough witches and wizards like Gilderoy Lockhart and Rita Skeeter to know that an interest in Dark Magic wasn’t a prerequisite for selfish maleficence. 
“就像纯粹的意图并不总是不这样做的人的唯一动力一样，”赫敏平静地结束了。她见过足够多的女巫和巫师，比如吉德罗·洛哈特和丽塔·斯基特，知道对黑魔法的兴趣并不是自私恶意的先决条件。

“Precisely,” Lucius said and Hermione could hardly believe she heard something that came close to approval in his tone. Even less believable was the fleeting ripple of pleasure that instinctively passed through her – apparently her love of being told she’d successfully grasped an idea hadn’t abandoned her entirely since leaving Hogwarts. 
“正是，”卢修斯说，赫敏几乎不敢相信她从他的语气中听到了近乎赞同的东西。更令人难以置信的是，她本能地闪过一阵快乐的涟漪——显然，自从离开霍格沃茨后，她对被告知她已经成功掌握了一个想法的热爱并没有完全抛弃她。

Stopping to take a sip of tea, Hermione considered the man across from her. It stood to reason that he would have such an ambiguous outlook; it probably made it easier for him to rationalise everything he did. She couldn’t say she entirely disagreed with him but Hermione knew that though her intent while using her magic had not always been pure—far from it—she had never actually wanted to outright kill another person. It seemed unlikely that he would be able to say the same. Undoubtedly he would just tell her that harm borne of her own short-sightedness was still harm. The hot tea burned on its way down.
赫敏停下来喝了一口茶，打量着她对面的男人。按理说，他会有这样一个模棱两可的观点;这可能使他更容易合理化他所做的一切。她不能说她完全不同意他的观点，但赫敏知道，虽然她在使用魔法时的意图并不总是纯粹的——远非如此——但她从来没有真正想过直接杀死另一个人。他似乎不太可能说同样的话。毫无疑问，他只会告诉她，她自己的短视所造成的伤害仍然是伤害。热茶在下山的路上燃烧着。

“But surely you can’t believe the split is even, Mr Malfoy.” He raised his eyebrows, inviting her to go on, and Hermione felt another strange flutter of gratification. “I just mean…well, while I don’t think you’re wrong exactly, surely it’s more likely that the intentions of someone who actively pursues the Dark Arts aren’t going to be particularly noble.”
“但你肯定不敢相信平分秋色，马尔福先生。”他扬起眉毛，邀请她继续说下去，赫敏又感到一阵奇怪的满足感。“我只是说......好吧，虽然我不认为你完全错了，但肯定更有可能的是，积极追求黑魔法的人的意图不会特别高尚。

He nodded slowly, his head leaning to the side as he acknowledged her point. “Certainly it’s more likely but it’s not guaranteed. The exceptions undermine the rule and so absolutism in this area is pointless.”
他缓缓地点了点头，他的头歪向一边，承认了她的意思。“当然，可能性更大，但不能保证。例外情况破坏了规则，因此这一领域的绝对主义毫无意义。

Says the absolutist in so many other areas , Hermione thought grimly.
“那么多其他领域的绝对主义者说，赫敏冷酷地想着。

“Is all this why you wanted to send your son to Durmstrang?”
“这就是你想把你的儿子送到德姆斯特朗的原因吗？”

He cocked his head, giving her an appraising look. “How did you know that?”
他歪着头，给了她一个赞赏的眼神。“你是怎么知道的？”

“It came up,” Hermione said with a shrug, neglecting to specify when. ‘I overheard him bragging about it on the Hogwarts Express’ didn’t exactly sound authoritative.
“它出现了，”赫敏耸耸肩说，忘记了具体是什么时候。“我在霍格沃茨特快列车上无意中听到他吹嘘这件事”听起来并不完全权威。

Malfoy shot her a curious frown and then, perhaps deciding her vagueness wasn’t worth querying, nodded. 
马尔福好奇地皱了皱眉头，然后，也许觉得她的含糊不清不值得质疑，点了点头。

“It is. I felt that Dumbledore would rather his students suffocate their ambition than harness it. He would rather make them fear the Dark Arts than trust them to find their own limits. The man coddled weakness of mind and feared strength. It’s why he filled the halls with Mudbloods and half-breeds. He and Hogwarts were part of the problem that the Dark Lord wished to solve.”
“是的。我觉得邓布利多宁愿他的学生扼杀他们的雄心壮志，也不愿驾驭它。他宁愿让他们害怕黑魔法，也不愿相信他们能找到自己的极限。这个男人溺爱心智的软弱，害怕力量。这就是为什么他把泥巴种和混血儿塞满了大厅。他和霍格沃茨是黑魔王想要解决的问题的一部分。

It was remarkable to Hermione that Lucius Malfoy could preach the virtues of nuance in one breath and then spout such narrow-minded nonsense in another. Did he even hear himself? It was possible she had overestimated her ability to sit in a room with him and listen to him. Pressing her toes down hard into the bottom of her shoes, Hermione asked, “And that was?”
对赫敏来说，卢修斯·马尔福能一口气宣扬细微差别的美德，然后又一口气说出如此狭隘的胡说八道，这真是太了不起了。他甚至听到了自己的声音吗？她可能高估了自己和他坐在一个房间里听他说话的能力。赫敏用力地将脚趾压进鞋底，问道，“那是？

“That Pure-bloods were not getting the respect they were due,” he said simply. “We were being undermined and sidelined in the Ministry for larger but lesser portions of the population.”
“纯血统没有得到应有的尊重，”他简单地说。“我们在事工中被削弱和边缘化，因为人口的比例更大但更少。”

“What gave you the impression you were being sidelined?” Hermione asked with forced politeness that was edged with a sharp sarcasm. “Was it your immense wealth or your immense privilege?”
“是什么让你觉得自己被边缘化了？”赫敏勉强礼貌地问道，但又夹杂着尖锐的讽刺。“是你的巨额财富还是你的巨大特权？”

His eyes narrowed. “It was common knowledge.”
他眯起了眼睛。“这是常识。”

“Given it's hard to imagine you spent much time around the Ministry while at Hogwarts, I'm going to assume that means your father told you and you just believed him without question.”
“鉴于很难想象你在霍格沃茨的时候花了很多时间在魔法部周围，我假设这意味着你爸爸告诉你了，而你只是毫无疑问地相信了他。”

He didn’t say a thing and Hermione smiled, though it was closer to a sneer, and leaned towards the Wheezebox. “For the record, Mr Malfoy looks like he's swallowed a cockroach cluster.”
他什么也没说，赫敏笑了笑，虽然更接近于冷笑，然后靠向了喘息盒。“郑重声明，马尔福先生看起来就像吞下了一簇蟑螂。”

“I do not .”
“我没有。”

Without missing a beat, Hermione pushed forward in her questioning with the mindset of one who might dive into ice cold water rather than suffer a slow descent. “Did your father have you engage in the attacks that Voldemort was launching against Muggles while you were at Hogwarts?”
赫敏没有错过任何一个节拍，以一种宁愿跳入冰冷的水中也不愿缓慢下降的心态向前提问。“你爸爸有没有让你参与伏地魔在霍格沃茨的时候对麻瓜发动的攻击？”

“Certainly not. I was underage, for one thing. From his perspective—and the Dark Lord’s also, I believe—I was more useful within the walls of Hogwarts.”
“当然不是。一方面，我还未成年。从他的角度来看——我相信也是黑魔王——我在霍格沃茨的围墙内更有用。

“In what way?”
“以什么方式？”

“I could identify and recruit future Death Eaters.” 
“我可以识别并招募未来的食死徒。”

“Like Professor Snape? You were at school together, weren’t you?” 
“像斯内普教授一样？你们是一起上学的，不是吗？

Inclining his head, Malfoy took another sip of tea.
马尔福歪着头，又喝了一口茶。

“How did you pick them?”
“你是怎么挑选他们的？”

Lucius looked up and to the left as he set his cup back down, as though searching back through his memories. 
卢修斯抬头看向左看，把杯子放回去，仿佛在回溯他的记忆。

“I preferred to keep things within my own house,” he finally said, with a nod that was more to himself than to her. “Slytherins are more adept at discretion and I understood their motivations better. Snape was a lonely, disaffected young man who felt intensely insecure and inferior. I offered him somewhere he could feel he belonged. A cause that empowered him and gave him a sense of superiority to which he could cling when faced with those who would make him feel less than.” He frowned, adding, “There were quite a few people who enjoyed doing that.”
“我宁愿把东西都放在我自己的房子里，”他终于说，点头更像是对他自己而不是对她。“斯莱特林更善于判断，我更了解他们的动机。斯内普是一个孤独、心怀不满的年轻人，他感到极度不安全感和自卑。我给他提供了一个他能感觉到自己有归属感的地方。这项事业赋予了他力量，给了他一种优越感，当面对那些让他感到不如的人时，他可以依附于这种优越感。他皱起眉头，补充道，“有不少人喜欢这样做。

There was a tightness forming in Hermione’s throat and no amount of swallowing seemed to get rid of it. “You probably ruined his life.”
赫敏的喉咙里一阵紧绷，似乎再多的吞咽都无法摆脱它。“你可能毁了他的一生。”

“I hardly think offering him genuine friendship should be viewed so harshly,” Lucius said, his face tight. “Severus’ problem was always his preference for placing others on pedestals before stepping onto one himself. He ruined his own life, Miss Granger. I didn’t make his decisions for him.”
“我几乎不认为应该如此严厉地看待向他提供真正的友谊，”卢修斯说，脸色紧绷。“西弗勒斯的问题一直是他喜欢先把别人放在基座上，然后再自己踏上一个。他毁了自己的生活，格兰杰小姐。我没有为他做决定。

“Do you have no sense of personal responsibility?” Hermione asked, made slightly breathless by his callousness.
“你没有个人责任感吗？”赫敏问道，他的冷酷无情让她略微喘不过气来。

“If I take all of the responsibility then what’s left for him?”
“如果我承担了所有的责任，那他还剩下什么呢？”

The blitheness of his tone made Hermione grit her teeth and she felt an irrepressible urge to pursue a more reckless course. It rose up her throat like bile, ringing in her ears. 
他轻快的语气让赫敏咬牙切齿，她感到一种无法抑制的冲动，想要走一条更鲁莽的道路。它像胆汁一样上升到她的喉咙里，在她的耳边回响。

“So why didn't you send your son to Durmstrang, then? If Hogwarts was so detestable to you?” She knew the answer to that, of course. The important thing was that Lucius Malfoy didn’t know she knew. 
“那么，你为什么不把你的儿子送到德姆斯特朗去呢？如果霍格沃茨对你来说如此可憎？她当然知道答案。重要的是卢修斯·马尔福不知道她知道。

Just as she expected after Astoria’s warning, this time he really did look as though he had swallowed a cockroach cluster. “His mother.”
正如她在阿斯托利亚警告后所预料的那样，这一次他看起来确实像是吞下了一簇蟑螂。“他的妈妈。”

“She wanted him to stay close to home?”
“她想让他待在离家近的地方吗？”

“Yes.” 
“是的。”

“And you relented?” Hermione asked, somewhat surprised to hear the hint of an unkind taunt in her own voice. 
“你心软了？”赫敏问道，听到她自己的声音里带着一丝不友善的嘲讽，她有些惊讶。

Lucius Malfoy fixed her with a cold look. “I did not agree with her.” He brushed some invisible crumbs from his desk, dropping his gaze. “But I realised very early on, Miss Granger, that I am not the kind of man who finds it gratifying to make it hard for my wife to be a loving mother just so that I can look like a strong husband.” 
卢修斯·马尔福冷冷地看着她。“我不同意她的观点。”他从桌子上拂去一些看不见的碎屑，垂下了目光。“可是我很早就意识到，格兰杰小姐，我不是那种觉得让我的妻子很难成为一个慈爱的母亲，只是为了让我看起来像个强壮的丈夫而感到满足的男人。”

A soft gust of breath escaped between Hermione’s parted lips and she also looked down, his unexpectedly unguarded revelation leaving her feeling discomfited and even a little dirty for having taunted him. 
一阵轻柔的呼吸从赫敏张开的嘴唇之间逸出，她也低下头，他出乎意料的毫无防备的揭露让她感到不安，甚至因为嘲笑他而有点肮脏。

“Please excuse me for a moment,” he said, rising from his seat and striding past her. She heard a gentle clink and realised he was pouring a drink.
“请原谅我一会儿，”他说，从座位上站起来，大步从她身边走过。她听到一阵轻柔的叮当声，意识到他在倒一杯饮料。

Though there was an odd queasiness working its way up her abdomen, Hermione leaned forward to take another sandwich, more for something to do than because she particularly wanted it. Just as her fingers brushed the crust of the bread, she glanced up beyond the tray and noticed that the parchment Malfoy had placed over what he had been reading when she’d entered had shifted in Letty’s accidental rearrangement of the table. It looked like a stack of contracts.
虽然一阵奇怪的恶心感沿着她的腹部蔓延，赫敏还是向前倾身，想再拿一个三明治，更多的是为了做点什么，而不是因为她特别想吃。就在她的手指拂过面包皮的时候，她抬头瞥了一眼托盘外，注意到马尔福在她进来时放在他正在阅读的东西上的羊皮纸在莱蒂不小心重新布置桌子时已经移动了。它看起来像一堆合同。

Stiffening, her hand hovering over the sandwich tray, Hermione lifted her chin slightly to get a glimpse of what the contracts were for. The word ‘divorce’ jumped out at her multiple times in solid black ink. Eyes wide, Hermione snatched her hand back just as Lucius Malfoy began making his way back around the desk.
赫敏僵硬了一下，手悬停在三明治托盘上，微微抬起下巴，想瞥一眼合同的用途。“离婚”这个词用纯黑色墨水多次出现在她面前。赫敏睁大了眼睛，在卢修斯·马尔福开始绕着桌子走回去的时候，她把她的手抢了回来。

As he moved past the side of the desk, his steps faltered and then stalled. Hermione stared resolutely ahead as he slowly set his filled glass down. Risking a glance at him, she saw he was looking down at the uncovered contract, a frown knitting his brows together. He met her eye, realisation setting in, and Hermione, breath held, chewed the inside of her cheek so hard she was worried her teeth would go through the skin.
当他走过桌子的一侧时，他的脚步踉踉跄跄，然后停滞不前。赫敏坚定地盯着前方，慢慢地放下了装满酒的杯子。她冒险地瞥了他一眼，发现他正低头看着那份揭开的合同，皱着眉头。他对上了她的眼睛，恍然大悟，赫敏屏住呼吸，用力地咀嚼着她的脸颊内侧，她担心自己的牙齿会穿过皮肤。

Holding her gaze, he approached her seat, the tip of his finger tapping the desk as he did so. The faint tap tap tap just about matched the beat of Hermione's heart and she wondered if that was just coincidence or if it was because he could hear it smacking against her ribs.
他凝视着她的座位，走近她的座位，同时用指尖敲打着桌子。微弱的咔嚓咔嚓声几乎与赫敏的心跳相匹配，她想知道这只是巧合，还是因为他能听到它敲打她的肋骨。

Stopping beside her chair, Lucius looked down but Hermione broke eye contact to stare determinedly at the window straight ahead of her, as though she could instigate some kind of spontaneous apparation. Then, her eyes darted to the handle of her wand which was sticking out of her open bag by her feet.
卢修斯停在椅子旁，低头看去，但赫敏打破了眼神交流，坚定地盯着她正前方的窗户，仿佛她可以煽动某种自发的幻影。然后，她的眼睛盯着从她脚边敞开的袋子里伸出来的魔杖手柄。

“ Don’t even think about it,” he said, his voice low and dangerous. “Look at me, Miss Granger.”
“别想了，”他说，他的声音低沉而危险。“看着我，格兰杰小姐。”

A horrid twisting in her stomach, Hermione turned her face up to his and saw nothing but cold fury. It was almost funny to her that she’d thought she’d seen Lucius Malfoy at his angriest when he’d caught her rummaging around his kitchen. Almost.
赫敏的胃里一阵可怕的扭曲，她把脸转向他，只看到冰冷的怒火。对她来说，这几乎是个好笑的事情，她以为她看到了卢修斯·马尔福在他厨房里翻找时最生气的样子。几乎。

“Are you absolutely incapable of minding your own business?” he asked. “Do you suffer from some kind of deficiency ?”
“你绝对没有能力管好你自己的事吗？”“你有某种缺陷吗？”

“I didn’t see anything.”
“我什么也没看到。”

“Don't lie to me,” he hissed. “You moved that parchment.”
“别骗我，”他嘶嘶地说道。“你把那张羊皮纸搬走了。”

“I didn't touch it!” Her voice had more force when she was telling the truth, she noticed. “It must have just moved with the tray.”
“我没碰它！”她注意到，当她说出真相时，她的声音更有力。“它一定是刚刚随着托盘移动的。”

“Who are you working for?” he demanded, leaning down to grip the arm of her chair with one hand while the other leaned on the edge of his desk, caging her in from one side. His face was close enough that she could smell the firewhiskey from him. It mixed with the bergamot of his cologne, making her feel slightly light-headed. “The Prophet? Witch Weekly?” Beyond words, Hermione shook her head repeatedly and he paled. “The Quibbler ?” 
“你在为谁工作？”他问道，俯下身子，一只手抓住她的椅子扶手，另一只手靠在桌子的边缘，从一侧把她关进去。他的脸离得足够近，她能闻到他身上的火威士忌味。它与他的古龙水的佛手柑混合在一起，让她感觉有点头晕目眩。“先知？女巫周刊？赫敏一再摇头，脸色苍白。“狡辩者？”

“I'm not working for anyone,” Hermione finally bit out, leaning back from him, desperate to create some distance. “I'm here on my own!” 
“我不是为任何人工作，”赫敏终于咬了一口，向后靠了靠，不顾一切地想要拉开一些距离。“我一个人在这里！”

Seeming not to hear her, he glanced down at her lap where her hands were clenched into fists and Hermione saw his eyes land on the faint scar on her inner forearm. The scar she’d gotten when she’d first visited Malfoy Manor. 
他似乎没有听到她的话，低头瞥了一眼她的腿，她的双手紧握成拳头，赫敏看到他的目光落在她前臂内侧的淡淡疤痕上。她第一次造访马尔福庄园时留下的伤疤。

“So it's revenge then, is it?” he asked softly, meeting her eyes.
“所以这就是报复，是吗？” 他轻声问道，与她的眼睛相遇。

“ What ?”
“什么？”

“My sister-in-law: dead. My wife :” he spat the word, “gone. So you want to get revenge on me. Revenge for what happened to you, is that it? I've not been brought low enough, you want to reveal this to the world and bring me lower.”
“我的嫂子：死了。我妻子：“他吐出一个字，”走了。所以你想报复我。为发生在你身上的事情报仇，就这样吗？我还没有被降低到足够低的位置，你想向世界揭示这一点，让我更低。

The ringing in Hermione’s ears was starting to make her head hurt. For what happened to her. As though her torture in his home had just been a happening . As though he hadn’t been directly involved. Incensed, Hermione pushed the arms of the chair and propelled herself to her feet, forcing him to straighten up and away from her. She backed around the chair so that it stood between them, a pathetic barricade. 
赫敏耳鸣的声音开始让她的头疼。为了发生在她身上的事情。就好像她在他家里的折磨才刚刚发生一样。就好像他没有直接参与一样。赫敏被激怒了，推着椅子的扶手，把自己撑起来，迫使他直起身来，远离她。她绕着椅子往后退，让它站在他们之间，就像一个可悲的路障。

“I don't need to do anything to make you the lowest kind of person there is,” she spat, relieved that her voice only shook once. “I don't want revenge, Mr Malfoy. And if I did, I wouldn't need your divorce to get it.” She pointed down at the wand poking from her bag, her eyes still fixed on his. “I've got a wand and you don't. Remember?”
“我不需要做任何事情来让你成为最卑微的人，”她啐了一口，因为她的声音只颤抖了一次而松了一口气。“我不想报复，马尔福先生。如果我这样做了，我就不需要你离婚了。她低头指着从包里探出的魔杖，眼睛仍然盯着他。“我有一根魔杖，而你没有。记得吗？

His eyes widened fractionally before narrowing, a sneer curling his lips. “Are you threatening me in my own home?”
他的眼睛微微睁大，然后眯起，嘴唇弯起一丝冷笑。“你在我自己家里威胁我吗？”

"Certainly not,” Hermione said in a mocking imitation of him. “It’s simply a friendly warning.”
“当然不是，”赫敏嘲讽地模仿他说。“这只是一个友好的警告。”

He started forward so suddenly that Hermione gasped and stumbled back, her heart in her throat. Just as suddenly, he stopped, his hand gripping the back of her chair in a way that made her suspect he’d been about to push out of the way to get to her. Visibly unsettled, his chest rising and falling rapidly, Malfoy looked around himself, anywhere but at her, and flexed his hand as he relinquished the chair.
他突然向前走，以至于赫敏喘息着，踉跄着向后退去，她的心都提到了嗓子眼。同样突然，他停了下来，他的手紧紧抓住她的椅背，让她怀疑他正要推开她。马尔福显然很不安，他的胸膛迅速起伏，他环顾四周，除了她之外，任何地方都看了看，并在让出椅子时弯曲了一下手。

“I want you out,” he muttered, turning away from her and sweeping his arm to the door. “Get out.” 
“我要你出去，”他咕哝着，转过身去，用手臂扫向门口。“滚出去。”

Without another word, Hermione scrambled to throw her things in her bag, unable to look at him. As he moved around his desk towards his window, she slammed the door to his study shut behind her and sprinted down the corridor, her bag cradled in her arms.
赫敏一言不发，手忙脚乱地把东西扔进包里，看不见他。当他绕过书桌走向窗户时，她砰的一声关上了书房的门，然后抱着包冲下走廊。

Chapter 12
第十二章Chapter Summary
本章小结

Hermione has a pep talk with Ginny and an unexpected encounter with Lucius Malfoy.
赫敏与金妮进行了一次鼓舞人心的谈话，并与卢修斯·马尔福意外相遇。

Chapter Notes
章节注释

In a total fluster at the nice comments I've been left for this story. Thank you <3
我对这个故事留下的好评论感到非常慌乱。谢谢 <3

The weight and warmth of James Potter was utterly comforting to Hermione. Though he wriggled and fidgeted, he gurgled happily in her lap and allowed her to cuddle him, her arms wrapped around his middle. It was actually the first time he'd seemed even slightly comfortable in her arms—usually he stretched away from her, consumed with shyness and a desire to explore—and Hermione wondered if that was because he could sense that she needed comfort. 
詹姆·波特的沉重和温暖让赫敏感到非常安慰。虽然他扭动着坐立不安，但他在她的腿上快乐地咯咯笑着，让她拥抱他，她的手臂搂着他的中间。这实际上是他第一次在她的怀里显得哪怕是一点点舒服——通常他会从她身边伸开，被害羞和探索的欲望所吞噬——赫敏想知道那是不是因为他能感觉到她需要安慰。

"Are you going to tell me what happened?" Ginny asked from the other side of the sofa, wearing her most motherly expression. 
“你要告诉我发生了什么事吗？”金妮从沙发的另一边问道，露出她最慈母的表情。

"Nothing," Hermione murmured, pressing a gentle kiss into James’ soft hair. He kicked his legs and grabbed his feet, his little brow furrowed in concentration.
“没什么，”赫敏喃喃自语，在詹姆斯柔软的头发上轻轻地吻了一下。他踢着自己的腿，抓住自己的脚，小眉头全神贯注地皱起。

"’Nothing’ doesn’t usually leave you looking like you’ve walked through a ghost."
“'什么都没有'通常不会让你看起来像是走过了鬼魂。”

Hermione had come straight to the Potters from Malfoy Manor. It probably hadn't been the best idea—she'd arrived in a fit of a pique, rather alarming Ginny—but the thought of going home to sit on her own had been even less appealing. Ginny had talked her down, first by pushing a cup of tea into her hands and then, when that was finished, by pushing a happy baby into her arms. It had, Hermione conceded, been an effective approach. She felt better.
赫敏是从马尔福庄园直接来到波特家的。这可能不是个好主意——她来的时候是一怒之下，让金妮感到相当惊慌——但回家独自坐着的想法就更不那么吸引人了。金妮劝说她，先是把一杯茶塞到她手里，然后，当茶喝完后，把一个快乐的婴儿推到她的怀里。赫敏承认，这是一个有效的方法。她感觉好多了。

"Mr Malfoy and I had a...disagreement."
“马尔福先生和我有过一次......分歧。

"Did he do something to you?" Ginny asked sharply, leaning forward, her eyes scanning Hermione for signs of harm. 
“他对你做了什么吗？”金妮尖锐地问道，身体前倾，眼睛扫视着赫敏是否有受伤的迹象。

"No." Even if I’m fairly sure he wanted to , Hermione thought, recalling his face so close to hers and so angry. Even if it was only in her head, she could still smell the firewhiskey. “We just argued.”
“不。” 即使我相当确定他想，赫敏想着，回想起他的脸是那么靠近她，那么生气。即使只是在她的脑海中，她仍然能闻到火威士忌的味道。“我们只是争论了。”

“About?”
“大约？”

Hermione shot Ginny a sidelong look and raised an eyebrow. “What do you think? Anything and everything.”
赫敏侧头看了金妮一眼，扬起了眉毛。“你怎么看？任何事情。

Hermione wasn’t entirely sure why she wasn’t immediately telling Ginny about what she’d seen on Malfoy’s desk. No doubt Ginny would be delighted to share in the gossip of a Malfoy divorce. Yet the words wouldn’t come. Perhaps because Malfoy was right: it really wasn’t any of her business. She didn’t think it was anyone else’s either. With a surge of regret, Hermione wished she’d never bothered to read stupid the parchment. Her only comfort was that even if she hadn’t, he likely wouldn’t have believed her anyway. At least this way she knew why he was furious.
赫敏不完全确定她为什么不立即告诉金妮她在马尔福的桌子上看到的东西。毫无疑问，金妮会很高兴分享马尔福离婚的八卦。然而，这些话并没有来。也许是因为马尔福是对的：这真的不关她的事。她也不认为这是别人的。赫敏一阵遗憾，希望她从来没有费心去读那张愚蠢的羊皮纸。她唯一的安慰是，即使她没有，他也可能也不会相信她。至少这样她知道他为什么生气。

“Suffice it to say, I don’t think I’ll be going back to Malfoy Manor to interview him next week.,” Hermione said, raising her wrist so that James could more easily inspect her watch, his fingerprints fogging the face of it. “I’ll have to pick up the things I’ve left in their library but I’m fairly sure it’s done.”
“我只想说，我不认为我下周会回马尔福庄园去采访他，”赫敏说，抬起手腕，让詹姆斯可以更容易地检查她的手表，他的指纹在手表的脸上起雾。“我得把留在他们图书馆里的东西拿起来，但我相当确定它已经完成了。”

Ginny gave a low whistle and collapsed back into the sofa. "That bad? What did you say to him? Did you make him cry? Oh, I wish I could see that."
金妮低沉地吹了一声口哨，瘫倒在沙发上。“那么糟糕？你对他说了什么？你让他哭了吗？哦，我希望我能看到这一点。

Hermione chuckled. “I don’t think Lucius Malfoy cries, Ginny.” Bouncing her legs up and down to make James giggle, she added quietly, “I don’t think he feels guilt, either.”
赫敏咯咯地笑了起来。“我不认为卢修斯·马尔福会哭泣，金妮。”她上下摆动双腿，让James咯咯地笑，然后轻声补充道，“我也不觉得他有内疚感。

A soft sigh prompted Hermione to look up at Ginny who was watching her with an exasperated but loving expression. “You are such a div. Of course he doesn’t. He doesn’t feel anything , I’d wager. If you ask me, this is for the best.”
