“是的，但我永远不会试图羞辱你，对吧？”赫敏严肃地说，向金妮摇了摇手指。“这不是活动，而是人。”

A lewd grin spread across Ginny’s face and Hermione could hardly help but share it. “Saucy,” Ginny said, swiping at Hermione’s arm. “That’s more like it.”
金妮的脸上露出的笑容，赫敏忍不住分享了它。“俏皮，”金妮说，一边扫了一下赫敏的手臂。“那更像是这样。”

“If this date is terrible, I want you to promise that you’ll get off my back for a while,” Hermione said, approaching James and sinking onto her knees beside him to help him with his blocks. 
“如果这个约会很糟糕，我希望你保证你会暂时离开我，”赫敏说，走近詹姆斯，跪在他身边，帮助他挡住。

“Well,” Ginny muttered, lowering herself back onto the sofa, “if it’s good I want you to promise that you’ll get on it yourself.” 
“嗯，”金妮咕哝着，把自己放回沙发上，“如果好的话，我希望你保证你会自己上去的。

“Ginny!”
“金妮！”

May 30th
5月30日

Hermione was curled up on her sofa, staring into the fireplace and contemplating when she should return to Malfoy Manor to collect her things from the library. At first, she’d told herself she would simply go when the time felt right but, since that was proving to be never , she was coming to the realisation that she’d just have to go when she felt like she could. 
赫敏蜷缩在沙发上，盯着壁炉，思考着什么时候应该回到马尔福庄园去图书馆收拾她的东西。起初，她告诉自己，她会在时机合适的时候去，但因为事实证明这是不可能的，她逐渐意识到，她必须在她觉得可以的时候去。

It was past 8pm but it was still light and pleasantly warm outside. Her cold glass of white wine was sweating, the condensation dribbling over her fingers. Glancing down into it, Hermione raised the glass to her lips and took a long drink. 
虽然已经晚上 8 点多了，但外面仍然很轻松，温暖宜人。她冰凉的白葡萄酒杯出汗了，冷凝水滴落在她的手指上。赫敏低头看了一眼，把杯子举到嘴边，喝了一大口。

It wasn't like she was scared to go back to Malfoy Manor. Not really. Sure, Lucius Malfoy had almost definitely wanted to hurt her but he hadn't and, deep down, she was certain he wouldn't. It was too much of a risk given he was still serving his sentence. She just couldn't be worth it—worth the additional punishment—to him. He thought so little of her, after all. 
她并不是害怕回到马尔福庄园。没有。当然，卢修斯·马尔福几乎肯定想伤害她，但他没有，而且，在内心深处，她确信他不会。考虑到他还在服刑，风险太大了。她就是不值得——值得额外的惩罚——对他来说。毕竟，他对她的看法太少了。

Hermione flushed with embarrassment recalling the way she had flinched back when she'd thought he was going to come at her. He'd been unarmed and instead of diving for her wand she'd panicked . Clearly she was out of practice. Ugh . 
赫敏尴尬得满脸通红，回想起当她以为他会来找她时，她退缩的样子。他手无寸铁，她没有跳下去抢她的魔杖，反而惊慌失措。显然她没有练习。 呸。

Hermione glanced around for the bottle of wine and saw that she'd left it all the way across the room on the windowsill. Not worth it. Raising the glass to her lips again, she drained it, holding the glass up so that the last droplets had time to make their way into her mouth. 
赫敏环顾四周寻找那瓶酒，发现她一直把它放在了房间对面的窗台上。不值得。她再次将杯子举到嘴边，喝干了它，举起杯子，让最后一滴水有时间进入她的嘴里。

Allowing her head to fall back onto the sofa, Hermione sighed. It wasn't so shameful, was it? The war was long over. Surely a benefit of peacetime was forgetting some of the tightly coiled fear that meant one always felt the need to be armed and primed to fight.
赫敏让她的头靠回沙发上，叹了口气。这没那么可耻，不是吗？战争早已结束。当然，和平时期的一个好处是忘记了一些紧紧缠绕的恐惧，这意味着一个人总是觉得需要武装并准备好战斗。

Recalling the cold fury that had been on Malfoy’s face, Hermione tapped her finger against her wine glass and frowned. She wasn’t afraid to go back to Malfoy Manor but in that specific moment, when he'd moved so suddenly, a part of her mind had gone back in time. He had been unarmed but he was still Lucius Malfoy. A man that hated her and would once not have hesitated to kill her. Maybe still wouldn't, if he could guarantee no consequences. 
回想起马尔福脸上冰冷的怒火，赫敏用手指敲了敲她的酒杯，皱起了眉头。她并不害怕回到马尔福庄园，但在那个特定的时刻，当他如此突然地移动时，她的一部分思绪已经回到了过去。他手无寸铁，但他仍然是卢修斯·马尔福。一个恨她，曾经毫不犹豫地杀死她的男人。如果他能保证不承担任何后果，也许现在还是不会。

Hermione contemplatively rolled the stem of the wine glass between her fingers. In some ways, men like Lucius Malfoy managed to scare her just that little bit more than Voldemort because they looked utterly human while still being monsters. 
赫敏沉思着用手指滚动着酒杯的杆。在某些方面，像卢修斯·马尔福这样的男人比伏地魔更能吓到她，因为他们看起来完全是人类，但仍然是怪物。

Voldemort had looked evil to her. Maybe he hadn't always been snakelike but his cruel preoccupations had caught up with him. But Lucius Malfoy...an instinctive, delicate shiver passed through Hermione’s body. He had a polished veneer that was so shiny he'd been able to hide behind it for years. They had known for centuries about werewolves but Lucius Malfoy made her wonder if there were not wolves that became men.
伏地魔在她看来是邪恶的。也许他并不总是像蛇一样，但他残酷的关注已经赶上了他。但是卢修斯·马尔福......一种本能的、微妙的颤抖穿过赫敏的身体。他有一个抛光的单板，非常闪亮，他已经躲在它后面很多年了。几个世纪以来，他们就知道狼人了，但卢修斯·马尔福让她怀疑，难道没有变成人的狼吗。

Yet, still, he interested her. Still she wanted to finish their interviews. Everyone she'd interviewed had been fascinating in their own way, certainly, but her last discussion with him had held her attention in a way that she hadn't anticipated. He struck her as a mess of contradictions and that made the problem solver in her sit up just a little straighter. He was perfect for her project. Maybe that was part of why she hadn't collected her things – if they were still at the manor it meant there was still a chance he'd give in.
然而，他仍然引起了她的兴趣。她还是想完成他们的采访。当然，她采访过的每个人都以自己的方式令人着迷，但她与他的最后一次讨论以一种她没有预料到的方式吸引了她的注意力。他觉得她是一团乱七八糟的矛盾，这让她的问题解决者坐直了一点。他非常适合她的项目。也许这就是她没有收拾东西的部分原因——如果它们还在庄园里，那就意味着他还有可能屈服。

But, she thought with a grim finality, he wasn’t going to. So she'd just have to give up like he wanted. Grunting, Hermione leaned forward and deposited her wine glass on the coffee table before heaving herself to her feet. If there wasn't a good time to go to Malfoy Manor then she'd just have to go now. Use the momentum. And the wine. 
但是，她冷酷地想，他不会这样做的。所以她只能像他想要的那样放弃。赫敏咕哝了一声，身体前倾，把酒杯放在咖啡桌上，然后站了起来。如果不是去马尔福庄园的好时机，那她现在就得走了。利用势头。还有葡萄酒。

When Hermione eventually Floo’d into the Malfoy library, the sun had finally set and she found it in almost-darkness. The only light source was the steadily dimming glow of the low flames in the fireplace. Glancing around, she approached the desk and withdrew her box from beneath it, glad that she’d not bothered to take it home. There was just enough light to see what she was packing up so she didn't bother to light her wand. The bright glow of a Lumos spell only made it more likely that someone would come to investigate the room and she didn't want that. The plan was to get in, get her things, and get out. 
当赫敏最终飞路走进马尔福图书馆时，太阳终于落山了，她发现它几乎是黑暗的。唯一的光源是壁炉里低火逐渐变暗的光芒。她环顾四周，走近桌子，从桌子下面拿出她的盒子，庆幸自己懒得把它带回家。光线刚好够看清她正在收拾的东西，所以她懒得点燃她的魔杖。Lumos 咒语的明亮光芒只会让有人更有可能来调查这个房间，而她不希望这样。计划是进去，拿她的东西，然后出去。

Brushing her hair over her shoulders, Hermione got to work re-organising her sheets of notes into the correct folders, the soft crackles of the fire and flicking sounds of parchment the only sounds. It was almost peaceful and she managed to lose herself in the repetition of it.
赫敏把头发拂过肩膀，开始把她的笔记重新整理到正确的文件夹中，火堆的柔和噼啪声和羊皮纸的轻弹声是唯一的声音。这几乎是平静的，她设法在它的重复中迷失了自己。

“Did you know, Miss Granger.” Hermione’s head shot up at the sound of the drawl from the direction of the door and a folder slipped from her hands to land with a smack on the desk. “That I have spent the last few days waiting for the sordid details of my personal life to appear in one, or several, of our illustrious news outlets. And yet it hasn’t happened. Why?” 
“你知道吗，格兰杰小姐。”赫敏听到门口传来的拉砸声，一个文件夹从她手中滑落，砰的一声落在桌子上。“在过去的几天里，我一直在等待我个人生活中的肮脏细节出现在我们杰出的新闻媒体中。然而，这并没有发生。为什么？

Lucius Malfoy was standing in the entrance to the library, his neat black robes just about blending in with the shadows in the dark corridor behind him. His hands were behind his back, his posture straight, and, unlike the last time Hermione had seen him, his face was a mask of calm rather than cold with rage. 
卢修斯·马尔福站在图书馆的门口，他整洁的黑色长袍几乎与他身后黑暗走廊中的阴影融为一体。他的双手背在背后，姿势笔直，与赫敏上次见到他不同，他的脸上是一副平静的面具，而不是愤怒的冰冷。

Regardless, Hermione reached blindly to her right, refusing to take her eyes from him. Patting her hand along the smooth table, she finally brushed the carved handle of her wand with her fingertips and seized it to point, unwavering, in his direction. To her frustration, he simply smiled and tilted his head to the right. Admittedly, she had no intention of cursing the man in his own home but he had no way of knowing that.
无论如何，赫敏盲目地把手伸向她的右侧，拒绝将目光从他身上移开。她用手在光滑的桌子上轻拍，终于用指尖拂过魔杖的雕花手柄，然后抓住它，坚定不移地指向他的方向。令她沮丧的是，他只是微笑着，把头向右歪了歪。诚然，她无意在自己家里诅咒这个男人，但他无从得知。

“Lower your wand, silly girl,” he said, shaking his head with a condescending smile. “I have no intention of harming you.”
“放下你的魔杖，傻姑娘，”他说，一边摇着头，露出居高临下的笑容。“我无意伤害你。”

As though she didn’t hear him, Hermione kept the wand up and gripped it tighter. He sighed, dropping his hands from behind his back so that they hung by his sides. It was a small source of pride to her that she exhausted him.
就像她没有听到他的声音一样，赫敏一直举起魔杖，握得更紧了。他叹了口气，把手从背后垂下来，挂在他的身体两侧。她让他筋疲力尽，这让她感到骄傲。

“What do you want, Miss Granger?” he asked shortly.
“你想要什么，格兰杰小姐？”

Hermione blinked a couple of times, not sure she’d heard properly. “What do you mean what do I want?” she asked, eyeing him warily. “I’m packing my things up. I want to go. What do you want?”
赫敏眨了眨眼，不确定自己是否听错了。“你什么意思，我想要什么？” 她问道，警惕地盯着他。“我正在收拾我的东西。我想去。你想要什么？

“I mean ,” he said, taking a slow step forward, “why are you sitting on the story of my divorce? What do you want from me? Money?”
“我是说，”他说，慢慢地向前迈了一步，“你为什么坐视我离婚的故事呢？你想从我这里得到什么？钱？

That surprised Hermione so much she dropped her wand arm limply by her side and cocked her head at him. “I don't want your money .”
这让赫敏大吃一惊，她无力地把魔杖的手臂垂在身侧，歪着头看着他。“我不要你的钱。”

With an oddly nervous flutter in her stomach, Hermione allowed him to take in her faded t-shirt, low-rise jeans and her off-white trainers, before his doubtful eyes flicked back up to meet hers. “Are you sure about that?”
带着赞赏的神情，他垂下了目光，顺着她的身体向下拖拽。赫敏的肚子里奇怪地紧张地颤抖着，让他看她褪色的T恤、低腰牛仔裤和她的米白色运动鞋，然后他怀疑的眼睛又抬起头来与她对视。“你确定吗？”

It bothered her that while his words didn’t affect her, the looks he gave her could. They always had. “I wasn't lying to you. I'm not going to tell anyone. I haven't. I don't care .”
“我对你血腥的离婚没兴趣，马尔福，”赫敏厉声说，不自觉地把双臂交叉在胸前。让她感到困扰的是，虽然他的话没有影响她，但他给她的眼神却能。他们一直都是这样。“我没有骗你。我不会告诉任何人。我没有。我不在乎。

His eyes narrowed with suspicion and Hermione laughed incredulously, sounding slightly mad as it echoed in the large library. “I don't understand why you're finding it so hard to believe.”
他怀疑地眯起了眼睛，赫敏难以置信地笑了起来，听起来有点疯狂，因为它在大图书馆里回荡。“我不明白你为什么觉得这么难以置信。”

“It’s leverage,” he said quietly, “and you are not using it.”
“这是杠杆，”他轻声说，“你没有使用它。

“It's not leverage.” Hermione shook her head, disgusted that he would suggest she might see it that way. “It's your private life. I didn’t come here because I want to spread gossip; I want to write an oral history.”
“这不是杠杆。”赫敏摇摇头，厌恶他会暗示她可能会这样看。“这是你的私生活。我来这里不是因为我想传播八卦;我想写一段口述历史。

“Are you trying to tell me that if we don’t resume our meetings, you will leak it?”
“你是想告诉我，如果我们不恢复会议，你就会泄露它吗？”

“Oh my God, no!” Hermione raised her arms wide in an attempt to throw some of her rapidly rising frustration out of her body. “That is not what I said. Why would I?”
“哦，天哪，不！”赫敏张开双臂，试图将她迅速上升的挫败感从她的身体中释放出来。“我不是这么说的。我为什么呢？

Malfoy placed his hands in the pockets of his robes and took another few steps towards her, shrugging. “Payback.”
马尔福把手长袍的口袋里，耸了耸肩，又向她走了几步。“报复。”

As he walked into the low light cast by the fire, Hermione could see that his face didn’t appear quite as bleary and grey as it had on their last meeting. Clearly, he had pulled himself together somewhat. Maybe just one or two firewhiskeys today.
当他走进火堆投下的昏暗灯光时，赫敏可以看到他的脸不像上次见面时那样朦胧和灰暗。显然，他已经稍微振作起来了。也许今天只有一两杯火威士忌。

“Yeah.” Hermione shook her head. “That's not my style.” 
“是的。”赫敏摇摇头。“那不是我的风格。”

“I would do it.”
“我会这样做的。”

With an impatient tut , Hermione dropped her wand onto the desk with a clatter and put her hands on her hips. “You’ve just given me yet another reason to not want to do it.” 
赫敏不耐烦地啧啧一声，咔嚓一声把魔杖扔在桌子上，双手放在臀部上。“你刚刚给了我另一个不想做这件事的理由。”

他走近桌子，站在一边的角落里，而赫敏则站在他对面的另一边。事实证明，他没有德拉科那么高，但只相差几厘米。她抬起头仔细地看着他。“你看，这是某种奇怪的逆向心理学斯莱特林游戏吗？你真的想让我把这个故事卖给先知吗？你似乎很奇怪地对它有意。

“No.” He said it so quickly that she believed him. 
“不。”他说得如此之快，以至于她相信了他。

“Then stop harassing me about it,” Hermione said with a roll of her eyes. She picked up the folder she had dropped when he’d come in and placed it carefully into her box, feeling his eyes on her the whole time. “You’re getting exactly what you want, aren’t you?”
“那就别再骚扰我了，”赫敏翻了个白眼说。她捡起他进来时丢下的文件夹，小心翼翼地放进她的盒子里，感觉他的眼睛一直盯着她。“你得到了你想要的，不是吗？”

“I am finding you hard to understand, Miss Granger.” 
“我觉得你很难理解，格兰杰小姐。”

“The feeling’s bloody mutual,” she muttered, depositing another folder into the box. All too aware that he wasn’t leaving, Hermione glanced up at him and saw he was staring at her intently. Her stomach flipped like a half-done pancake and she straightened up. “How did you know I was here?”
“这种感觉是血腥的相互的，”她咕哝着，把另一个文件夹放进盒子里。赫敏太清楚他不会离开了，抬头看了他一眼，发现他正目不转会地盯着她。她的肚子像吃了一半的煎饼一样翻动着，她直起身来。“你怎么知道我在这里？”

“I knew you would need to collect your things so I asked Astoria to inform me when the wards signalled an arrival,” he said, finally dropping his gaze and glancing around the dimly lit room. “It’s somehow very typical of you to interrupt my nightcap.”
“我知道你需要收拾你的东西，所以我让阿斯托利亚在病房发出到来的信号时通知我，”他说，终于垂下了视线，环顾了一下昏暗的房间。“你打断我的睡前酒有点很典型。”

Shuffling awkwardly, Hermione pushed down her instinct to apologise. She hadn’t asked him to leave his stupid study for Merlin’s sake, what was wrong with her? Perhaps sensing her discomfort, he returned his attention to her. “You may continue to use the library. You have exhibited…discretion. Something I would not have imagined you capable of.” 
赫敏尴尬地拖着脚，压抑住了道歉的本能。她没有让他为了梅林而离开他那愚蠢的书房，她怎么了？也许是感觉到她的不安，他又把注意力转向了她。“你可以继续使用这个库。您展出了...自由裁量权。我从来没有想过你能做到。

Offering him a sarcastic smile, Hermione returned to packing up her things. “Don't really want to use the library of a man who does nothing but insult me, thanks.” 
赫敏向他露出一个讽刺的笑容，然后继续收拾她的东西。“我真的不想使用一个除了侮辱我什么都不做的人的图书馆，谢谢。”

“Don’t be petulant,” he said with a sigh, raising a hand to rub at his temple. “I am apologising.”
“别撒脾气，”他叹了口气说，抬起一只手揉了揉自己的太阳穴。“我很抱歉。”

“Apologies usually have the word sorry in them.” Hermione punctuated the word ‘sorry’ by dropping a particularly heavy folder in the box.
“道歉通常带有对不起这个词。”赫敏把一个特别重的文件夹扔进盒子里，打断了“对不起”这个词。

“I would like to point out that you still took it upon yourself to read something that was none of your business.” 
“我想指出，你仍然主动阅读了一些与你无关的东西。”

Hermione’s shoulders dropped and she raised her head to look at him. He was still standing by the desk, one fingertip now leaning on it, watching her carefully. 
赫敏的肩膀垂下来，她抬起头看着他。他仍然站在桌子旁，一根指尖现在靠在上面，仔细地看着她。

“You want to keep doing the interviews?” she asked, her brow furrowed with doubt.
“你想继续做采访吗？” 她问道，疑惑地皱起了眉头。

“You may return at the usual time next week.”
“你下周可以照常的时间回来。”

Drawing her bottom lip between her teeth, Hermione considered him as she gnawed at it. His face was utterly unreadable but he did not blink, holding her gaze steadily. A part of her thought Ginny was right—ending the interviews probably was for the best. But there was still that other part of her that was desperately keen to finish what she’d started. Hermione Granger always saw things through to the bitter end.
赫敏用牙齿咬住下唇，一边啃着一边看着他。他的脸完全看不清，但他没有眨眼，稳稳地凝视着她。她有一部分认为金妮是对的——结束采访可能是最好的。但她还有另一部分拼命渴望完成她开始的事情。赫敏·格兰杰总是把事情看到底。

“Alright,” she said quietly. He nodded, turning away, and with a sharp exhale Hermione began taking things out of the box again to return them to the desk. 
“好吧，”她轻声说。他点点头，转过身去，赫敏猛地呼出一口气，又开始从盒子里拿出东西，把它们放回桌子上。

“I'm sorry, by the way, Mr Malfoy,” she said to his retreating back. Halting, he turned on his heel to give her a curious look. “About your marriage,” she explained.
“对不起，顺便说一句，马尔福先生，”她对他后退的背影说。停下脚步，他转过身来，好奇地看了她一眼。“关于你的婚姻，”她解释说。

He tilted his head, his eyes cold. “Do not pity me, Miss Granger. I neither want it nor need it.” 
他歪着头，眼神冰冷。“别可怜我，格兰杰小姐。我既不想要也不需要。

“Oh, I really don't.” Hermione gave a small laugh which made him frown. “ At all . But that doesn't mean I can't offer my condolences.”
“哦，我真的不知道。”赫敏轻轻地笑了起来，这让他皱起了眉头。“一点也不。”但这并不意味着我不能表示哀悼。

Rather than continue his exit, he took another few steps towards her again. “She left for France almost five years ago,” he said. “At this point the papers are nothing more than a formality that will complete her transition into a new life. My concern largely revolves around the fact that divorces are not the kind of thing that happens in the Pure-blood world. Of course, I doubt that's something you —”
他没有继续离开，而是再次向她走了几步。“她差不多五年前去了法国，”他说。“在这一点上，这些文件只不过是一种形式，将完成她向新生活的过渡。我的担忧主要围绕着这样一个事实，即离婚不是纯血统世界中发生的那种事情。当然，我怀疑你是不是——”

He broke off as Hermione held up a dusty guide to Pure-blood customs. "I know,” she said. “I took your recommendation for additional reading. Despite the rude manner in which it was given.”
当赫敏举起一本尘封的纯血统习俗指南时，他打断了他。“我知道，”她说。“我接受了你的建议，以便进一步阅读。尽管它被以粗鲁的方式给出。

Hermione wasn’t sure if it was a shadow cast from the flickering flames in the fireplace but she could have sworn his lips quirked at the corners ever so slightly. It disappeared as quickly as it came. 
赫敏不确定那是不是壁炉里摇曳的火焰投下的影子，但她可以发誓他的嘴唇微地抽搐了一下。它消失得和来得一样快。

“So you understand why I would prefer that the matter remains private.” 
“所以你明白为什么我宁愿这件事保密。”

“I suppose I do.” She lowered the book and shrugged. “Your pride.”
“我想我记得。”她放下书，耸了耸肩。“你的骄傲。”

“The Malfoy name has suffered quite enough,” he said tersely. “Do not talk about pride as though it is a trivial trifle. It's one of the few things I have left.”
“马尔福这个名字已经受够了，”他简洁地说。“不要把骄傲当作一件小事来谈论。这是我剩下的为数不多的东西之一。

“I don't think pride is trivial. We all have it on some level and I actually think it has its virtues on occasion.” He raised his chin, glaring down his nose at her. Looking away towards the fire, Hermione thoughtfully added, “Though I also think it can stand in the way of a reconciliation."
“我不认为骄傲是微不足道的。我们都在某种程度上拥有它，我实际上认为它有时也有它的优点。他抬起下巴，顺着鼻子瞪着她。赫敏望向火堆，若有所思地补充道，“虽然我也认为它会阻碍和解。

“Your liking for Sabine makes more sense every day,” he said drily.
“你对萨宾娜的喜欢一天比一天更有意义，”他冷淡地说。

Hermione’s eyes snapped back to his face and she shook her head hurriedly. That had definitely slipped out on the current of wine coursing through her system. “I'm sorry, I shouldn't have—”
赫敏的眼睛猛地回到他的脸上，她急忙摇了摇头。这肯定是在她体内流淌的酒流中溜走的。“对不起，我不该——”

“I don’t want a reconciliation, Miss Granger.”
“我不想和解，格兰杰小姐。”

Swallowing her trepidation, Hermione dropped her gaze and ran a finger along the edge of the desk. “Are you angry at her for leaving?”
赫敏吞下了她的恐惧，垂下了目光，用一根手指在桌子的边缘滑了一下。“你对她的离开生气吗？”

Risking a glance up, Hermione found he was scanning the table warily. “I’m not recording,” she said, feeling that she was reading him correctly for once. 
赫敏冒险抬头看了一眼，发现他正在小心翼翼地扫视着桌子。“我没有录音，”她说，感觉自己有一次读对了他。

His eyes snapped to hers. “Then why are you asking?”
他的眼睛猛地盯着她。“那你为什么要问？”

Hermione shrugged. “I’m interested.”
赫敏耸耸肩。“我很感兴趣。”

Had he ever talked to anyone about the disintegration of his marriage? There was something about his raised shoulders and clenching and unclenching fists that told Hermione no. But she had proven herself to be a relatively trustworthy third party—discreet, as he said—so it was perhaps with that in mind that he didn’t immediately shout her down.
他有没有和任何人谈过他婚姻的破裂？他抬起的肩膀和紧握和松开的拳头在告诉赫敏不。但她已经证明自己是一个相对值得信赖的第三方——正如他所说，很谨慎——所以也许是考虑到这一点，他没有立即把她喊下来。

"Interested,” he repeated with a frown. “Miss Granger, you really do seem to have an irrepressible fascination with things that are none of your concern.”
“感兴趣，”他皱着眉头重复道。“格兰杰小姐，你似乎真的对那些不关心的事情有一种无法抑制的迷恋。”

“You don’t have to tell me but I won’t tell anyone else if you do.”
“你不必告诉我，但如果你告诉我，我不会告诉其他人。”

Managing to keep her face entirely blank, Hermione withstood the scrutiny of his gaze. For one wild moment, she read Malfoy’s silence as him actually considering telling her something. Then he turned on his heel and said over his shoulder, “I will see you on Thursday at 2, Miss Granger. Don’t be late.”
赫敏设法让她的脸完全空白，经受住了他的目光审视。有那么一刻，她读到马尔福的沉默，因为他真的在考虑告诉她什么。然后他转过身来，转过头来说：“我星期四两点见，格兰杰小姐。不要迟到。

Watching Malfoy go with a sinking feeling, Hermione remembered her date with Terry Boot. She’d just have to make it work.
看着马尔福带着一种沉重的感觉离去，赫敏想起了她和特里·布特的约会。她只需要让它发挥作用。

6 月 1 日

On the morning of her date with Terry, Hermione stood in front of her wardrobe tapping her foot as she assessed its contents. Generally, she didn’t think all that hard about what she was going to wear but Ginny had made the mistake of asking her what she was planning to wear and it had set off a spiral of overthinking. Glancing over her shoulder out of the window, Hermione could see that it was another warm, sunny day. 
在她和特里约会的那天早上，赫敏站在她的衣柜前敲打着她的脚，一边打量着里面的东西。一般来说，她不会那么认真地考虑她要穿什么，但金妮犯了一个错误，问她打算穿什么，这引发了一场过度思考的漩涡。赫敏回头瞥了一眼窗外，发现这又是一个温暖、阳光明媚的日子。

Rifling through her clothes, Hermione dismissed items one by one. Jeans might end up being too warm; shorts felt too casual; that skirt didn’t feel casual enough ; she suddenly hated every single other skirt she had. Finally, Hermione landed on a pale blue cotton summer dress with a broderie anglaise pattern. Pulling it out, she held it up to herself. Short without being too short, very thin straps but it wouldn’t cling to her body too much. Perfect. Throwing it on the bed, she pulled a pair of sandals from the floor of her wardrobe and set about getting ready for the day. 
赫敏翻阅着她的衣服，一个一个地扔掉了这些东西。牛仔裤最终可能会太暖和;短裤感觉太随意了;那条裙子感觉不够随意;她突然讨厌她拥有的每一条裙子。最后，赫敏找到了一件带有马德拉刺绣图案的淡蓝色棉质夏装连衣裙。她把它，举到自己面前。短而不短，非常细的带子，但不会太紧地贴在她的身上。完善。她把它扔在床上，从衣柜的地板上拿出一双凉鞋，开始为这一天做准备。

Just as Hermione was settling down at her kitchen table to have some toast and coffee, an owl arrived at the window. Rising to let it in, Hermione took the letter from its leg and immediately recognised Terry’s writing. Rolling her eyes, Hermione ripped it open, fully expecting it to be a cancellation.
正当赫敏在厨房的桌子旁坐下来吃吐司和咖啡时，一只猫头鹰来到了窗前。赫敏起身让它进来，从它的腿上拿走了信，立刻认出了特里的字。赫敏翻了个白眼，把它扯开了，完全以为它会被取消。

"It’s a beautiful day so let’s meet at the new ice cream shop on Diagon Alley. I’ve heard they’ve got a new butterbeer flavour with chunks of butterscotch in and I’m desperate to try it . Terry ."
“今天天气晴朗，让我们在对角巷的新冰淇淋店见面吧。我听说他们有一种新的黄油啤酒口味，里面有大块的奶油糖果，我迫切地想尝试一下。 特里。

Smiling, Hermione reached over to her plate for some toast and took a hearty bite. She would never admit it to Ginny but she was a little bit excited. Going for ice cream was a nice date. It would be nice . Nice things were nice. If she just kept telling herself that over and over then maybe she’d believe it. 
赫敏微笑着伸手到她的盘子里吃了点吐司，然后丰盛地咬了一口。她永远不会向金妮承认，但她有点兴奋。去吃冰淇淋是个不错的约会。那就太好了。美好的事物就是美好的。如果她只是一遍又一遍地告诉自己，也许她会相信。

It was true that she hadn’t dated after Ron but it wasn’t that Ron had put her off, exactly. It was just that she’d thought a relationship was something she didn’t really need. She didn’t need to be worrying about another person or about fitting them into her life. So far, though, Terry hadn’t been doing too badly. He was keen to meet her but he hadn’t been constantly trying to get in contact with her in the interim. That was a good start. Maybe, even if she didn’t need him, she might end up wanting him. Unthinkable, really. 
的确，她没有在罗恩之后约会过，但并不是罗恩完全推迟了她。只是她认为一段关系并不是她真正需要的东西。她不需要担心另一个人或让他们融入她的生活。不过，到目前为止，特里的情况还不错。他很想见她，但在此期间他并没有一直试图与她取得联系。这是一个好的开始。也许，即使她不需要他，她最终也可能想要他。真的，不可思议。

After depositing her plate and cup in the sink, Hermione pulled her satchel onto a chair and made sure everything she needed for the day was there. She’d decided that she would turn up to Malfoy Manor slightly earlier than usual so that she could leave early for her date. Mr Malfoy had only said “don’t be late”, after all. He’d said nothing about being just over half an hour early. Counting the times on her fingers, she figured that if she arrived at Malfoy Manor just before 1.30 rather than at 2, she’d be able to get to apparate to meet Terry just after 2.30 as promised.
把盘子和杯子放进水槽后，赫敏把她的书包拉到椅子上，确保她今天需要的所有东西都在那里。她决定比平时早一点来到马尔福庄园，这样她就可以早点出发去约会了。毕竟，马尔福先生只说了一句“别迟到”。他什么也没说要提前半个多小时。她用手指数着时间，心想如果她在1点30分之前到达马尔福庄园，而不是在2点钟，她就能像承诺的那样在2点30分之后幻影去见特里。

When Hermione knocked on the door of Lucius Malfoy’s study at 1.25, she received no reply. Counting to twenty, nodding her head in a metronomic beat to ensure accuracy, she knocked again. Nothing. Sighing, Hermione tapped her foot and glanced down at her watch. With Malfoy, it was hard to tell whether he was genuinely not there to answer her or whether he was remaining silent to torment her. The only way to find out was to open the door for herself.
当赫敏在 1.25 敲响卢修斯·马尔福书房的门时，她没有收到任何回复。数到二十，她以节拍器点头以确保准确性，然后她再次敲门。无。赫敏叹了口气，敲了敲她的脚，低头看了一眼她的手表。对马尔福来说，很难说他是真的不是来回答她，还是他保持沉默来折磨她。找出答案的唯一方法就是为自己打开门。

Steeling herself to be snapped at for entering without explicit permission, Hermione turned the handle to his study and pushed her way into the room. 
赫敏强忍着自己没有得到明确允许就进去而被打伛，她转动了书房的把手，推门走进了房间。

Opening her eyes, which had closed in a dread-induced cringe as she crossed the threshold, Hermione glanced around the room, her shoulders dropping as she took it all in. It was empty. Feeling somewhat stumped, Hermione drew her lower lip between her teeth thoughtfully. 
赫敏睁开眼睛，在她跨过门槛时，眼睛因恐惧而畏缩着，她环顾了一下房间，她的肩膀垂了下来，把这一切都看进去了。里面空无一人。赫敏感到有些难住，若有所思地把下唇夹在牙缝里。

Where was he likely to be except in his study? More importantly, how could she find out quickly? There was really only one way in a house so large and unfamiliar.
除了他的书房，他可能在哪儿呢？更重要的是，她怎么能快就发现呢？在如此大和陌生的房子里，真的只有一条路。

“Letty?” Hermione asked, her voice hesitant as she spoke to the empty room. 
“莱蒂？”赫敏问道，她的声音在对着空荡荡的房间说话时犹豫不决。

A crack rent the air, signalling Letty’s arrival and Hermione found herself faced with a beaming elf who, on seeing who had called her, immediately dipped a reverential curtsey that made Hermione want to squirm.
空气中响起了裂缝，标志着莱蒂的到来，赫敏发现自己面对的是一个喜气洋洋的精灵，她一看到是谁叫她，立即行了一个虔诚的屈膝礼，这让赫敏想扭动一下。

The master will not be pleased. Master doesn't like snooping. Miss should go. Go, go, go.”
“赫敏·格兰杰小姐！”莱蒂喊道，她的声音高亢而高兴，指向马尔福书房的地板。然而，当莱蒂从屈膝礼中站起来时，她看起来有些不安，她网球大小的眼睛在观察周围的环境时变得更像餐盘。“小姐在主人的书房里，”莱蒂缓缓地说。“小姐一个人。”妖精开始烦恼，把她布满皱纹的双手扭在一起。“小姐不应该——不好，小姐。主人不会高兴的。师父不喜欢窥探。小姐该走了。走，走，走。

莱蒂急忙向赫敏走去，弯下身子，把瘦骨嶙峋的手放在赫敏的后背上，把她推向门口，一遍又一遍地喃喃自语着“走”。赫敏大喊着，她的整个身体向前颤抖着，这个精灵的力量让她大吃一惊。不知道还能做什么，赫敏跳到一边，以便将莱蒂的手从她身上移开。

“Thank you, Letty,” she said with a smile down at the elf. “I can take it from here.”
“谢谢你，莱蒂，”她低头对精灵微笑着说。“我可以从这里拿走它。”

With another low curtsey, Letty backed into the house, clearly glad not to be asked to go any further. Taking a fortifying breath, Hermione began to wander over the grass towards Malfoy who, facing away from her, was blissfully unaware that his early afternoon was about to be interrupted. 
莱蒂又低低地行了个屈膝礼，回到屋子里，显然很高兴没有被要求再往前走。赫敏深吸一口气，开始在草地上向马尔福走去，马尔福背对着她，幸福地没有意识到他的午后即将被打断。

The dog scrambled around his feet before shooting off after it and Lucius rolled his shoulders as his arm fell back down by his side. Hermione’s gait stuttered at the sight. It was odd to see Lucius Malfoy do anything remotely physical; he and energetic movement did not go together in her mind. 
就在她靠近他的时候，他抽回了手臂，把一个看起来像微型的夸夫饼的东西扔到了花园的远处。那条狗在他的脚上爬来爬去，然后追了上去，卢修斯扭了摇肩膀，手臂又落在了身边。赫敏的步态在看到这一幕时结结巴巴。看到卢修斯·马尔福做任何与身体无关的事情都很奇怪;他和充满活力的运动在她的脑海中并不相伴。

“Mr Malfoy,” Hermione called, picking up her pace to a slight jog as she crossed the grass towards him. 
“马尔福先生，”赫敏喊道，加快了脚步，轻轻地向他走来。

When she finally reached him, she planted her hands on her hips, her cheeks flushed and a smile on her face as she caught her breath. 
他当场转过身来，看到赫敏小跑穿过他的地面向他走来，他的眉毛竖了起来，一只手稳住她的包，以免它撞到她的侧面。当她终于找到他时，她把手放在臀部上，脸颊通红，屏住呼吸，脸上露出笑容。

“你在这里做什么？”他问道，他的眼睛在花园里扫视，仿佛在寻找他必须要咒语的人，因为他把她带到了他身边。好吧，她不会让莱蒂受到责备。

“I’m here to interview you,” Hermione said brightly, as though she was playing along with some kind of deliberate silliness. “You know that.”
“我是来采访你的，”赫敏爽朗地说，仿佛她在玩弄某种故意的愚蠢。“你知道的。”

“不，”他说，眼睛短暂地闭上了。“我是说，你现在在这里做什么？”他把手伸到裤子的口袋里，掏出一块老式的手表，深深地皱着眉头看了看。“你早到了半小时。”

“You only said don’t be late.”
“你刚才说过别迟到。”

Lucius tutted, dropping the watch back into his pocket. “That’s not explicit permission to show up whenever you like before that.”  
卢修斯啧了一声，把手表放回了口袋里。“在那之前，你可以随时出现。”

“Sorry, I just—”
“对不起，我只是——”

“Assumed I’d have nothing to do and would therefore be eagerly awaiting your arrival?” His voice was light but laced with a dangerous amount of sarcasm. 
“假设我无事可做，因此会热切地等待你的到来？”他的声音很轻，但夹杂着危险的讽刺。

“No,” Hermione said, a heat that had nothing to do with the sun rising in her cheeks. She wouldn’t have phrased it quite like that, anyway. True, she hadn’t fully considered that Malfoy might have other plans, locked in his house as he was.
“不，”赫敏说，这种热度与她脸颊上升起的太阳无关。反正她不会这么说。没错，她没有完全考虑到马尔福可能还有其他计划，像他一样被锁在他的房子里。

“Why are you inflicting yourself upon me half an hour before you need to?”
“你为什么在你需要的时候半小时就对我下手呢？”

“Oh,” Hermione said, tucking her hair behind her ear and feeling exceptionally awkward, “well… “
“哦，”赫敏说，把头发掖到耳后，感觉特别尴尬，“嗯......“

The sound of four padding paws and loud panting signalled the arrival of Malfoy's dog, saving Hermione the trouble of answering. The dog was shaggy, grey and fairly large, coming up to just above Hermione’s knee, though she got the feeling it still had further to grow. With its ball in its mouth, the dog ran around her in a tight circle, its tail wagging and bashing against her legs. Hermione laughed, turning in a circle to watch its progress before it stilled enough to snuffle her hand with its cold, wet nose. 
四只拍打爪子的声音和响亮的喘息声预示着马尔福的狗到来了，省去了赫敏回答的麻烦。那条狗毛茸茸的，灰色的，相当大的，刚好超过赫敏的膝盖，尽管她觉得它还要进一步长大。这只狗嘴里叼着球，绕着她绕着她跑，尾巴摇晃着，撞击着她的腿。赫敏笑了起来，转了一圈观察它的进展，然后它才平静下来，用它冰冷、湿润的鼻子捏住了她的手。

“Oh!” she exclaimed. Allowing her bag to slip from her shoulder onto the grass, Hermione got down to her knees and buried her hands in the dog’s coat, letting it sniff her properly. She would never have expected Lucius Malfoy to have a dog so affectionate. “What’s their name?”
“噢！”赫敏让她的包从肩膀上滑到草地上，跪下来，把手埋在狗的外套里，让它好好地闻她。她从来没有想过卢修斯·马尔福会养一只如此深情的狗。“他们叫什么名字？”

Hermione looked up at Malfoy and saw his expression was tight, his lips thin. He looked like he wanted to drag the dog away by its tail. “Cato. He’s a Scottish deerhound.”
赫敏抬头看向马尔福，看到他的表情紧绷，嘴唇薄薄的。他看起来好像想拽着狗的尾巴把狗拖走。“卡托。他是一只苏格兰猎鹿犬。

“He’s just lovely,” Hermione said, her eyes leaving Malfoy as she used both hands to scratch around the panting dog’s ears.
“他就是很可爱，”赫敏说，她的眼睛离开了马尔福，用双手挠了挠这只气喘吁吁的狗的耳朵。

“He’s not fully trained yet. He’s still quite young.”
“他还没有完全训练。他还很年轻。

Cato hopped around Hermione as she clambered back to her feet and she reached down to clap his head again. “He seems very friendly to me.” Tearing her eyes away from the dog, she glanced at Lucius. “Or is that the problem?”
卡托在赫敏爬回去站起来时，在赫敏周围跳来跳去，她又伸手拍了拍他的头。“他似乎对我非常友好。”她把目光从狗身上移开，瞥了卢修斯一眼。“或者这就是问题所在？”

Malfoy arched an eyebrow and said nothing more which Hermione took as confirmation that, yes, that was the problem. Any dog of Lucius Malfoy’s would not be friendly with a Mudblood was surely the implication. It was, at least, Hermione’s inference. 
马尔福扬起眉毛，没有再说什么，赫敏认为这是对，是的，这就是问题所在。卢修斯·马尔福的任何一条狗都不会对泥巴种友好，这肯定是言下之意。至少，这是赫敏的推断。

“You didn’t answer my question,” he said. “Why are you here early?”
“你没有回答我的问题，”他说。“你怎么来得早？”

Eyes on Cato as he gathered his ball between his teeth, Hermione adjusted her bag back onto her shoulder. “I have a date,” she mumbled, “and the timings sort of…overlapped.”
赫敏盯着卡托，把他的球夹在牙缝里，把她的包调整回她的肩膀上。“我有个约会，”她喃喃自语，“时间差不多......重叠。

“A date,” came Malfoy's blank reply.
“约会，”马尔福茫然地回答。

Hermione’s eyes flicked to his and defensiveness bubbled up in her chest at the look of surprise on his face. “ Yes , a date.  It’s an appointment between two people hoping to make a romantic connection.”
赫敏的眼睛瞥向他，他脸上惊讶的表情让她的胸口冒出了防御的气息。“是的，一个约会。 这是两个人之间的约会，希望建立浪漫的联系。

“I know what a date is, Miss Granger.”
“我知道什么是约会，格兰杰小姐。”

“Well then, don’t say it like you don’t,” she snapped, embarrassed. “There wasn’t anything about them in the Pure-blood customs book, was there? Plenty of things about chaperoned meetings, mind,” she added with an eye roll.
“那么，别说得像你没说的那样，”她尴尬地厉声说。“纯血统的海关簿上没有关于他们的任何事情，对吧？很多关于有人陪伴的会议的事情，介意，“她翻了个白眼补充道。

“That book is rather old,” Malfoy said, looking down his nose at her. “I started at Hogwarts in the 1960s, not the 1860s.”
“那本书相当古老，”马尔福说，低头看着她。“我从 1960 年代开始在霍格沃茨上学，而不是 1860 年代。”

Hermione’s blush deepened. “Well, it’s at 2.30 so I was kind of hoping you wouldn’t mind starting a little bit earlier today. I don’t even mind recording out here; I’m sure the Wheezebox will be fine outside if I’m careful.” 
赫敏的脸红得更深了。“嗯，现在是 2.30，所以我有点希望你不介意今天早一点开始。我什至不介意在这里录音;如果我小心的话，我敢肯定 Wheezebox 在外面会没事的。

Rummaging through her bag, Hermione withdrew the tiny gramophone and balanced it in the palm of her hand as she looked up at him hopefully. 
赫敏在包里翻找着，拿出那台小小的留声机，用手心平衡着它，满怀希望地抬头看着他。

With a sharp exhale through his nose, Lucius Malfoy’s gaze travelled from the Wheezebox to Hermione and then back again. “Very well. But do not make a habit of this, Miss Granger. I find it disrespectful in the extreme.”
卢修斯·马尔福从鼻子里猛地呼出一口气，目光从喘息盒移到赫敏身上，然后又移回来。“很好。但不要养成这种习惯，格兰杰小姐。我觉得这是极不尊重的。

Muttering ‘sorry’ under her breath, Hermione hastened to withdraw her wand from her bag and considered the Wheezebox for a moment. To make walking easier, she waved her wand in a small spiral above the Wheezebox so that it rose into the air and floated between them at head height. That would surely get the sound better. She would just have to have her Quick Quotes Quill work from the recording later. With a self-satisfied smile, Hermione cut her eyes to Malfoy who gazed stonily back at her. 
赫敏低声喃喃道“对不起”，赶紧从包里拿出魔杖，考虑了一会儿喘息盒。为了方便行走，她在 Wheezebox 上方以一个小螺旋形挥舞魔杖，使其上升到空中，并以头部高度漂浮在他们之间。那肯定会让声音变得更好。她只需要让她的 Quick Quotes Quill 稍后从录音中工作。赫敏得意地笑了笑，把目光投向马尔福，马尔福则目不转睛地看着她。

“What are you doing on this date that makes it essential that it take place in the middle of the day?” he asked, his eyes dropping to her summer dress. Hermione couldn’t tell if he was judging it or not.
“你在这个约会里做了什么，让它必须在中午进行？” 他问道，他的眼睛落在她的夏装上。赫敏不知道自己是在评判还是不是在评判。

“We’re going for ice cream,” she said, pulling at the dress from behind and hoping he wouldn’t notice. Maybe it was too short. 
“我们要去吃冰淇淋，”她说，从后面拉着裙子，希望他不会注意到。也许它太短了。

“Ice cream,” he replied with that same blankness as he had said ‘date’. Before Hermione could speak he held up a hand, his face pained. “I know what ice cream is.”
“冰淇淋，”他回答道，语气和他说“约会”时一样茫然。赫敏还没来得及说话，他就举起了一只手，脸上带着痛苦。“我知道冰淇淋是什么。”

Hermione shrugged. “It’s only a first date.”
赫敏耸耸肩。“这只是第一次约会。”

“Clearly,” he murmured and, without another word, began walking in the direction that Cato had run. Hermione jogged forwards to join him and the Wheezebox floated through the air alongside them. 
“显然，”他喃喃自语，一言不发，开始朝着Cato跑的方向走去。赫敏小跑着向前走，加入了他的行列，喘息盒在他们旁边漂浮在空中。

“Draco once led me to believe that you were with the Weasley boy.” He said ‘Weasley’ as though it tasted off in his mouth, like something curdled.
“德拉科曾经让我相信你和那个韦斯莱男孩在一起。”他说“韦斯莱”，仿佛在他嘴里尝起来很臭，就像什么凝结的东西一样。

“No,” Hermione said, her voice rising with surprise that Malfoy might have listened to anything about her from his son. “That didn’t work out. It ended quite a long time ago.”
“不，”赫敏说，她的声音提高了，惊讶于马尔福可能从他儿子那里听到了关于她的任何事情。“那没有成功。它很久以前就结束了。

Malfoy didn’t say anything in response and they fell into an awkward silence, through which Hermione bit down her urge to explain why she and Ron didn't work out. It didn't seem like the kind of thing Lucius Malfoy would care to know.
马尔福没有回应，他们陷入了尴尬的沉默，赫敏忍住了她想要解释为什么她和罗恩没有解决的冲动。这似乎不是卢修斯·马尔福（Lucius Malfoy）关心的那种事情。

Hermione was relieved when the sound of panting signalled the return of Cato. Bounding up to her, the dog dropped its ball at her feet. Pausing, she looked up at Malfoy who raised his eyebrows and said nothing. Bending down, Hermione lifted the ball and grinned as Cato jumped excitedly around her until she finally drew her arm back and threw the ball as hard as she could. Once Cato had taken off again, barking all the while, they carried on walking. 
当喘息声表明卡托回来时，赫敏松了一口气。狗跳到她身边，把球丢在了她的脚边。停顿了一下，她抬头看向马尔福，马尔福扬起眉毛，什么也没说。赫敏弯下腰，举起球，咧嘴一笑，卡托兴奋地在她周围跳来跳去，直到她终于把手臂缩回来，用尽全力把球扔了出去。当卡托再次起飞时，他们一直在吠叫，继续走着。

“I don’t think he needs any more training,” Hermione said fondly as the dog’s excitable yelps drifted back on the warm breeze in the grounds.
“我觉得他不需要更多的训练，”赫敏深情地说，狗兴奋的叫声在院子里温暖的微风中飘回去。

“It’s just as well that what you think doesn’t matter then, isn’t it?” Lucius said quietly.
“那你的想法也无关紧要，不是吗？”卢修斯轻声说道。

“Let’s just begin,” she replied, rolling her eyes. 
“我们开始吧，”她翻了个白眼回答。

“Let’s.” 
“我们走吧。”

Reaching up, Hermione tapped the floating Wheezebox with her wand, sliding it into her bag afterwards. “So, what happened when you left school?”
赫敏伸手用魔杖敲了敲漂浮的喘息盒，然后把它滑进了她的包里。“那么，你离开学校时发生了什么？”

“Several things in quick succession,” Lucius said, shoving his hands into his pockets as he walked, “the most important amongst them being that I took the mark and my father died.”
“接二连三，”卢修斯说，边走边把手塞进口袋里，“其中最重要的是我拿了标记，我爸爸死了。

“Oh,” Hermione said, thrown by the cold casualness with which he spoke of such significant life events. “I'm sorry.”
“哦，”赫敏说，他谈到如此重大的生活事件时，用一种冷淡的随意态度感到困惑。“对不起。”

“别撒谎，”他抽搐着，弯起嘴唇低头瞥了她一眼。“我没有。”

“他死于龙痘，不是吗？”

“报告是这么说的。”

There was something in the indifference of Malfoy’s tone that made Hermione give him a sidelong look but his face was inscrutable. “Did you continue to live with your mother?”
马尔福语气中的冷漠让赫敏侧头看了他一眼，但他的脸色却高深莫测。“你继续和妈住在一起吗？”

Hermione subtly leaned forward to look past him and follow his gaze but she couldn’t see anything that seemed likely to be holding his attention. “It was only my father and I for much of my school career.”
“那时她已经死了好几年了，”他说，瞥了一眼他们左边的灌木丛。赫敏巧妙地向前倾身，想越过他，顺着他的目光看去，但她看不到任何似乎可能引起他注意的东西。“在我学校生涯的大部分时间里，只有我和我爸爸。”

赫敏停顿了一会儿，想知道他是否要详细说明他母亲的死，但他的沉默是坚决的，他的目光也看向了她的对面。那个领域的具体感觉并不是特别相关，尽管个人很好奇，但赫敏还是决定顺利地继续前进。

“So you inherited his estate and took the mark after his death?”
“所以你继承了他的财产，并在他死后继承了这个印记？”

“Yes,” Malfoy said, his eyes now returning straight ahead. “I replaced him in the inner circle. It made sense.”
“是的，”马尔福说，他的眼睛现在直直地回到前方。“我取代了他在核心圈子里的位置。这是有道理的。

“Can you tell me about getting the Dark Mark?” Hermione asked, her eyes raking the crisp white sleeves of his shirt. It was usually the left arm, the arm that was farthest from her. As though sensing her stare, he looked down and withdrew his hands from his pockets. 
“你能跟我说说关于得到黑暗印记的事情吗？”赫敏问道，她的眼睛耙着他衬衫清爽的白色袖子。通常是左臂，离她最远的手臂。仿佛感觉到她的凝视，他低下头，从口袋里抽出双手。

“If you want to see it you need only ask, Miss Granger,” he said with a knowing look, bringing his hand up to toy with his cufflinks. 
“如果你想看，你只需要问就知道了，格兰杰小姐，”他带着会心的眼神说，同时抬起手来玩弄他的袖扣。

“Oh,” Hermione flushed a deep pink and looked away. “I, er – I wasn’t sure if that’s–”
“哦，”赫敏脸红了一脸深红，把目光移开了。“我，呃——我不确定那是不是——”

“Invasive and rather presumptuous? Well, I’d say that’s you to a tee.”
“侵略性，而且相当自以为是？好吧，我想说这就是你。

Hermione turned her head round to glare at him so fast that her long curls swept off one shoulder and down her back. “Go on, then. Let me see.”
赫敏转过头来瞪着他，速度如此之快，以至于她的长卷发从一侧肩膀滑落到她的背部。“那么，请继续。让我看看。

A smirk on his face, Malfoy stopped walking, forcing Hermione to stop with him. He undid his cufflink, slid it into his pocket and began rolling up his shirt sleeve to reveal the pale skin of his forearm, Hermione carefully inspecting his every move. When his shirt was around his elbow, he turned towards Hermione properly, revealing his inner forearm. 
马尔福脸上露出得意的笑容，停下了脚步，迫使赫敏和他一起停下来。他解开袖扣，把它塞进口袋里，开始卷起衬衫袖子，露出前臂苍白的皮肤，赫敏仔细地检查着他的一举一动。当他的衬衫套在肘部时，他适当地转向赫敏，露出了他的前臂内侧。

She’d never really looked at the Dark Mark before. Not up close and with no sense of impending doom. Stepping closer to him, Hermione bent forward slightly to inspect it. Her face came close enough to his arm that her breath ghosted over it and he clenched his fist in response to the sensation, his tendons flexing. 
她以前从来没有真正看过黑暗标记。不是近距离的，也没有即将到来的厄运的感觉。赫敏靠近他，微微向前弯下腰来检查它。她的脸贴得足够近，以至于她的呼吸在上面鬼魂般地喘息着，他紧握着拳头作为回应，他的肌腱弯曲着。

The mark was very faded, closer to a scar than a tattoo. Her fingers twitched with the urge to touch it but one glance up at Malfoy’s stony face reminded her who she was with and how very unwelcome that would likely be.
那个印记很褪色，更像是疤痕，而不是纹身。她的手指抽搐着，想触摸它，但抬头看了一眼马尔福那张坚硬的脸，她想起了她和谁在一起，以及那可能是多么不受欢迎。

“How did he do it?” she asked, straightening up and giving Malfoy the signal that he could roll his sleeve back down. 
“他是怎么做到的？”她问道，直起身来，向马尔福示意他可以把袖子卷回去。

“That was a very secret ritual, Miss Granger,” he said, securing his sleeve again. “I will not divulge the details, even now.”
“那是一个非常秘密的仪式，格兰杰小姐，”他说，又把袖子拉上了。“即使是现在，我也不会透露细节。”

Hermione pursed her lips, frustrated. “Well, is there anything you can tell me about it?”
赫敏沮丧地抿了抿嘴唇。“嗯，你有什么可以告诉我的吗？”

“It was extremely painful.”
“这非常痛苦。”

He was so matter-of-fact about it that Hermione couldn’t help but scour his face for any other information. As usual, it gave nothing away so she turned and re-started their progress across the lawns. “How did it feel to join Voldemort’s inner circle, Mr Malfoy?”
他实事求是，以至于赫敏忍不住在他的脸上搜寻任何其他信息。像往常一样，它什么都没有泄露出去，所以她转身重新开始他们在草坪上的前进。“加入伏地魔的核心圈子是什么感觉，马尔福先生？”

“Exhilarating.” His voice was soft but Hermione was sure the Wheezebox would be able to pick it up. “I was thrilled that the wizarding world was going to change and I was going to be a part of that.”
“令人振奋。”他的声音很轻柔，但赫敏确信Wheezebox能接住它。“我很高兴魔法世界将发生变化，我将成为其中的一部分。”

“你相信你会成为让纯血统再次登上顶峰的努力的一部分，”赫敏问道，回想起了他上次见面时告诉她的话。

“Yes,” he said, glancing over at her with cold eyes. “No Mudbloods. Or at the very least, servile Mudbloods.”
“是的，”他说，用冰冷的眼神瞥了她一眼。“没有泥巴种。或者至少，奴性地 Mudbloods。

“你真是太好了，”赫敏说，她的语气干涩到足以让她感到口渴。

“It was. I was the youngest member of the Dark Lord’s inner-circle at that time and he trusted me implicitly.”
“是的。当时我是黑魔王核心圈子里最年轻的成员，他暗中信任我。

“And why was that? What prompted him to put that trust in you?”
“为什么呢？是什么促使他把这种信任放在你身上？

“I was willing to do anything,” Lucius said, his expression distant. 
“我愿意做任何事情，”卢修斯说，他的表情很遥远。

“What constitutes anything?”
“什么构成了任何东西？”

他的嘴角露出苦涩的笑容，他用眼角的余光怀疑地看了赫敏一眼。“我想你不想知道这个问题的答案，格兰杰小姐。”他摇摇头。“不是。”

“我不会问我不想得到答案的问题，”赫敏冷冷地说。

“Mm, but you never seem to have any compunctions when it comes to answering questions nobody asked,” Lucius murmured. He looked down at her properly then and Hermione met his eyes, unblinking. It was fortunate that the Malfoy’s gardens were so well-kept, otherwise she would have run the risk of tripping over something. 
“嗯，但你似乎在回答没人问的问题时从来没有任何自责，”卢修斯喃喃自语道。然后他低头看着她，赫敏与他的眼睛对上，一眨不眨。幸运的是，马尔福家的花园打理得如此完好，否则她会冒着被什么东西绊倒的风险。

“I gave him my time,” he finally said on an exhale, “as well as a great deal of my fortune. I blackmailed, threatened and tortured both inside and outside the Ministry, though mostly inside. I was most useful there thanks to my inherited connections.”
“我把我的时间给了他，”他终于呼出一口气说，“还有我的大部分财富。我在魔法部内外都进行了勒索、威胁和折磨，尽管主要是在内部。多亏了我继承的人脉，我在那里最有用。

Cato returned to them with a happy bark and Hermione tore her gaze away from Malfoy, feeling somewhat queasy. The presence of a happy dog, its tail wagging in the bright sunshine did not fit their conversation. Malfoy stopped his walking so that Hermione could bend down to pick up the ball and throw it again, though she did so with a touch less enthusiasm than before and no smiles.
卡托高兴地吠叫着回到他们身边，赫敏把目光从马尔福身上移开，感到有些恶心。一只快乐的狗在明亮的阳光下摇晃着尾巴，这与他们的谈话格格不入。马尔福停下了他的脚步，这样赫敏就可以弯下腰捡起球再扔一次，尽管她这样做时比以前少了一点热情，也没有笑容。

“你肯定在 18 岁左右，”当 Cato 高速起飞时，她的耳朵在风中飘动。“当你开始做这一切的时候。”

"Yes."
“是的。”

"That's very young, don't you think?"
“那还很年轻，你不觉得吗？”

“I'd wager that's around the age you joined the war, yes?"
“我敢打赌，那大概是你参战的年龄，对吧？”

“Yes, I suppose it was." 
“是的，我想是的。”

He simply nodded and didn’t add anything more. Hermione cleared her throat, struggling to look at him. “Did you…enjoy doing those things?”
他只是点点头，没有再多说什么。赫敏清了清嗓子，挣扎着看他。“你是不是......喜欢做那些事情吗？

I did what was necessary to serve a cause that was larger than myself. I wasn’t weak. That is why the Dark Lord trusted me and that is why I rose through the ranks.”
“这与享受无关，格兰杰小姐。”他不耐烦地摇摇头。“他们是我们努力破坏魔法部和当时秩序的必要条件。我做了必要的事情来服务于一个比我自己更大的事业。我并不弱。这就是黑魔王信任我的原因，也是我晋升的原因。

“Because you weren’t weak,” she repeated, wondering if he would notice the doubt and anger creeping into her voice. 
“因为你并不软弱，”她重复道，想知道他是否会注意到她声音中悄悄流露的怀疑和愤怒。

She thought she’d done rather well to keep it down thus far but the feelings were rising like bile in her throat and it was only a matter of time before they came out in her words. To her mind, the things he had done did not constitute strength. “Why were the Muggle attacks necessary, if you don’t mind me asking?”
她认为到目前为止她已经很好地控制住了它，但这种感觉像胆汁一样在她的喉咙里上升，它们在她的话语中出来只是时间问题。在她看来，他所做的事并不构成力量。“如果你不介意我问的话，为什么麻瓜的袭击是必要的？”

“Excuse me?”
“什么？”

“That’s what you lot did, wasn’t it? You and the other Death Eaters. You attacked Muggles. For sport, I heard. Saw, even, at the Quidditch World Cup. I don’t think attacking defenceless Muggles makes you particularly strong and, while I’m sure it depends on who you ask, I don’t think sport is particularly necessary either. They didn’t even know you existed and you punished them for…what? Being less powerful than you?”
“你们就是这么做的，不是吗？你和其他食死徒。你攻击了麻瓜。对于运动，我听说。甚至在魁地奇世界杯上。我不认为攻击手无寸铁的麻瓜会让你特别强壮，虽然我确定这取决于你问谁，但我也不认为运动是特别必要的。他们甚至不知道你的存在，你惩罚他们......什么？不如你强大？

“Less powerful, lesser overall. We were going to take over and they had to learn what their place would be in the new order. They had to learn to fear us.”
“力量较弱，整体较差。我们要接管，他们必须了解他们在新秩序中的位置。他们必须学会害怕我们。

“Yeah, okay. Sure.” Hermione snorted gracelessly, drawing a disgusted look from Malfoy. “That’s all any of this is, really, isn’t it? Fear.”
“是的，好的。当然。赫敏优雅地哼了一声，引来了马尔福厌恶的眼神。“这就是这一切，真的，不是吗？恐惧。

“I’m sure I don’t know—”
“我确定我不知道——”

“You’re afraid. Always have been.”
“你害怕。一直都是。

As though he’d hit a brick wall, Malfoy stopped dead and looked at her with the expression of a man who could hardly believe what he was hearing. Somewhere overhead a bird trilled and the sound of the bubbling fountain was soft behind them. 
就像他撞到了一堵砖墙一样，马尔福停了下来，用一个几乎不敢相信自己所听到的男人的表情看着她。头顶上的某个地方，一只鸟儿颤抖着，他们身后传来潺潺流淌的喷泉的声音。

“I am not —”
“我不是——”

“Not of anyone in particular,” Hermione carried on. “It’s a different kind of fear—it’s so instilled in you it probably feels natural. I mean, fear is natural, I suppose, but it’s not always rational and I—” Hermione huffed out a sigh, brows low in a frown. “I’m not explaining myself very well, am I?”
“不是特别的，”赫敏继续说。“这是一种不同的恐惧——它如此灌输给你，它可能感觉很自然。我的意思是，恐惧是自然的，我想，但它并不总是理性的，我——“赫敏叹了口气，眉头低垂着。“我没有很好地解释自己，对吧？”

He swallowed, his jaw jutted to the side. “You are doing the opposite and I think you had best explain yourself to my satisfaction or this meeting will end shortly and you will not return here.”
他咽了口口水，下巴向一侧突出。“你做的事反了，我想你最好把自己解释得令我满意，否则这次会议很快就会结束，你不会再回来了。”

“Mr Malfoy, I’ve spent weeks studying your family.” He nodded approvingly, his chin raised in a prideful way that made Hermione want to roll her eyes. “The Malfoy name goes quite far back and it’s been involved in the development of the British Wizarding World almost from the beginning.”
“马尔福先生，我花了好几个星期来研究你的家庭。”他赞同地点点头，骄傲地抬起下巴，让赫敏想翻白眼。“马尔福这个名字可以追溯到很久以前，它几乎从一开始就参与了英国魔法世界的发展。”

“I’m very aware of this, Miss Granger. It’s hardly news to—”
“我非常清楚这一点，格兰杰小姐。这不是什么新闻——”

“My research has allowed me to…see certain things,” Hermione continued, ignoring him entirely. She started walking again, more slowly this time, her hands moving as she spoke. After a moment, he fell into step beside her, his longer legs making it easy for him to catch up. “It’s allowed me to make certain connections. Did you know, for instance, that before the Statute of Secrecy, your family was more than happy to interact with Muggles?”
“我的研究使我能够......看到某些东西，“赫敏继续说，完全无视他。她又开始走路了，这次走得更慢了，她的手随着她说话而移动。过了一会儿，他倒在了她身边，他较长的双腿让他很容易追上。“它让我能够建立某些联系。例如，你知道吗，在保密法规之前，你的家人非常乐意与麻瓜互动？

Malfoy stopped again and Hermione turned to look at him, seeing his lips pressed thin. Cato came bounding up to them, this time dropping the ball closer to Malfoy and panting up at him. It took Malfoy a moment to notice that his dog was even there but as he bent down to pick up the ball, he didn’t take his eyes from Hermione.
马尔福又停了下来，赫敏转过头看着他，看到他的嘴唇紧紧地抿着。卡托跳向他们走来，这一次把球丢得离马尔福更近了，气喘吁吁地看着他。马尔福花了一点时间才注意到他的狗甚至在那里，但当他弯下腰捡球时，他的眼睛没有从赫敏身上移开。

“Not ordinary Muggles, of course,” Hermione waved a hand, sweeping the notion away for being so ridiculous. “They were rich and powerful Muggles. The cream of the crop, really. Your own namesake, Lucius Malfoy the first, was in the position to try to win the hand of a Muggle queen, or so I read.”
“当然不是普通的麻瓜，”赫敏挥了挥手，把这个想法扫除了，因为太荒谬了。“他们是有钱有势的麻瓜。真的，这是最精华的。你自己的名字，卢修斯·马尔福一世，正处于试图赢得麻瓜女王之手的位置，至少我是这么读的。

Lucius gripped the ball, his eyes blazing. “That is debated and I—”
卢修斯紧紧抓住球，眼睛炯炯有神。“那是有争议的，我——”

“I’m sure your family saw these Muggles as inferior to them because of their lack of magical power but their wealth and influence redressed the balance somewhat. In a world where Wizarding and Muggle societies weren’t rigidly divided, those Muggles were useful; they sat at the top and the Malfoys sat on top of them. But then, of course, the Statute of Secrecy was passed.”
“我敢肯定，你的家族认为这些麻瓜不如他们，因为他们缺乏魔法力量，但他们的财富和影响力在一定程度上改变了这种平衡。在一个巫师和麻瓜社会没有严格划分的世界里，那些麻瓜是有用的;他们坐在上面，马尔福一家坐在他们上面。但后来，当然，保密法规通过了。

“As was right.”
“说得对。”

“嗯，你的祖先弗洛里安·马尔福不这么认为。”赫敏扬起眉毛。“他有一段时间非常反对。你能想象为什么吗？

Malfoy said nothing, his eyes fixed on her as he remained oblivious to Cato’s whining and snuffling at his hand. 
马尔福什么也没说，他的眼睛盯着她，对卡托的抱怨和抽搐他的手视而不见。

“I have some theories," Hermione continued archly. "Largely, the Statute of Secrecy was for the protection of witches and wizards at risk of persecution in the Muggle witch hunts but, as those disproportionately victimised the poor and powerless, I suppose Malfoys never really had to worry about them. Florian Malfoy didn’t really like the idea of his family losing their useful foothold in the Muggle world. Still, when it became clear the Statute couldn’t be stopped and that a new seat of power would be formed in the Ministry of Magic, your family got on board with the new world."
“我有一些理论，”赫敏继续说道。“在很大程度上，保密法规是为了保护在麻瓜猎巫行动中面临迫害风险的女巫和巫师，但是，由于这些行为不成比例地伤害了穷人和无权无势的人，我想马尔福从来就不需要真正担心他们。”弗洛里安·马尔福并不喜欢他的家人在麻瓜世界失去有用的立足点。尽管如此，当法规显然无法阻止，魔法部将形成一个新的权力宝座时，你的家人就加入了这个新世界。

Hermione watched Cato’s desperate attempts to get his owner's attention but Malfoy couldn't seem to tear his eyes away from her, held still by some kind of horrified fascination. 
赫敏看着卡托不顾一切地试图引起他主人的注意，但马尔福似乎无法将目光从她身上移开，被某种惊恐的迷恋所束缚住。

"Problem was, it was a new world where everyone was magical. For a family that had become used to deriving their power from their wealth and their magic that must have been rather jarring. Suddenly, retaining that generational wealth became key to keeping power and influence. But how to justify having such exorbitant sums when you were witches and wizards just like everyone else? I think your family probably looked to their aristocratic Muggle friends for tips at this point.”
“问题是，这是一个每个人都很神奇的新世界。对于一个已经习惯了从财富和魔法中获取力量的家族来说，这一定是相当不和谐的。突然之间，保留世代财富成为保持权力和影响力的关键。但是，当你和其他人一样是女巫和巫师时，如何证明拥有如此高昂的金额呢？我想你的家人现在可能向他们的贵族麻瓜朋友寻求建议。

Life seemed to jolt back into Malfoy and he raised his hand to point aggressively in Hermione's direction. “Miss Granger, you are goin—”
生活似乎又回到了马尔福的心中，他抬起手，咄咄逼人地指向赫敏的方向。“格兰杰小姐，你要去——”

“They weaponised ancestry and class,” Hermione said staunchly, her lips pursed and her hands on her hips. “To be at the top you need to establish a bottom, so to justify their wealth and self-professed superiority, your family championed arbitrary sub-divisions of the magical community. Magic was not just magic and all magical people weren’t made equal. Old, pre-existing prejudices, certainly, but those are easy to dust off and re-fashion as the need arises. I imagine the pervasive negative feelings towards Muggles in the aftermath of the Statute and the witch hunts really helped make it all stick. When Muggles are mistrusted and disliked, it’s rather easy to make it so that any witch or wizard born in connection with them should also be mistrusted and disliked. It makes it so easy to believe that Muggleborns are lesser, that their magic is somehow tainted as a result of their heritage, and the Malfoys were able to set themselves up as the opposite. Because, of course, Malfoy’s didn't mix with Muggles. Anymore, at least. Perish the thought. They’re the best .” Hermione’s expression was fierce as she added, “The best at hypocrisy, anyway.”

“You will stop right now, Miss Granger, or I will stop you," Malfoy snarled, stepping towards her but finding his path impeded by the whining Cato.
“你现在就停下来，格兰杰小姐，或者我就拦住你，”马尔福咆哮着，向她走来，却发现他的去路被抱怨的卡托挡住了。

“All that Pure-blood superiority is,” Hermione pressed on, caught up in her own rant, her eyes gleaming, “is a narrative designed to keep all the wealth and power flowing through a small circle of the wizarding community. It’s a way to create the impression that you deserve all the advantages you have when, really, you and your family aren't any more remarkable than anyone else. It’s all just fear and greed. A convenient lie told through enough generations that people began to take it for truth. I’m not surprised you wouldn’t question it; why would you? It got you all this.” Hermione threw an arm out to indicate the verdant, sweeping grounds of Malfoy Manor.
“纯血统的优越感，”赫敏继续说，沉浸在自己的咆哮中，她的眼睛闪闪发光，“只是一个旨在让所有财富和权力在巫师界的小圈子里流动的叙事。这是一种给人留下印象的方式，即您应该拥有所有优势，而实际上，您和您的家人并不比其他人更出色。这一切都只是恐惧和贪婪。一个方便的谎言经过了足够多的世代传播，以至于人们开始将其视为真理。你不会质疑它，我并不感到惊讶;你为什么会呢？它让你得到了这一切。赫敏伸出一只手臂，指着马尔福庄园青翠、广阔的土地。

Cato was jumping around Malfoy’s feet, desperately signalling that he wanted the ball thrown, but Malfoy was clutching it tightly in one hand, his jaw clenched and his gaze fixed on Hermione with such intensity she rather thought he was trying to overcome the restrictions of his Magic Dampener to make her burst into flame. Slowly, she approached him and reached out to take the ball from his hands. As her fingers closed over his, his entire arm tensed and he jerked it away, dropping the ball into her waiting hand. 
卡托在马尔福的脚边跳来跳去，拼命示意他想把球扔出去，但马尔福一只手紧紧地抓着球，他的下巴紧紧地咬着，他的目光如此强烈地盯着赫敏，她宁愿以为他是在试图克服他的魔法阻尼器的限制，让她燃烧起来。她慢慢地靠近他，伸手从他手中接过球。当她的手指合拢在他的手指上时，他的整个手臂都绷紧了，他猛地把它抽开，把球丢进了她等待的手里。

“Thank you,” Hermione said softly. Turning away, she drew her arm back and threw the ball hard so that Cato could chase it. When she turned back, he was still staring at her, his eyes narrowed. 
“谢谢你，”赫敏轻声说。她转过身来，把手臂往后拉，用力把球扔出去，这样卡托就可以追球了。当她回头时，他仍然盯着她，眼睛眯了起来。

“Perhaps what you’re telling yourself is the convenient lie,” Lucius said, his eyes sliding to the retreating figure of Cato. “A way to make yourself feel better about your innate inferiority.”
“也许你对自己说的只是一个方便的谎言，”卢修斯说，他的眼睛滑向逐渐撤退的卡托身影。“一种让自己对自己天生的自卑感觉更好的方法。”

Huffing a sigh through her nose, Hermione tilted her head. “Superiority and inferiority aren’t innate. They’re…self-asserted and projected. That you would suggest otherwise shows how disconnected from reality you are; how fully you bought into the lie. It goes some way to explaining—to me at least—why you find it so easy to hate.”
赫敏从鼻子里叹了口气，歪了歪头。“优越和自卑不是与生俱来的。他们是......自我断言和投影。你不这么说表明你与现实有多么脱节;你是多么完全地相信了这个谎言。这在某种程度上解释了——至少对我而言——为什么你觉得讨厌这么容易。

His eyes snapped back to hers but for the first time he didn’t try to stop her speaking. 
他的眼睛猛地回到她的身上，但这是他第一次没有试图阻止她说话。

“That’s what I mean, Mr Malfoy. We hate what we fear and we fear what we hate. I mean…do you really think I’m filthy?” Hermione held out her arms so that he could look at her pristine dress in the sun. “Do I look dirty? Smell dirty?”
“我就是这个意思，马尔福先生。我们憎恨我们害怕的，我们害怕我们憎恨的。我的意思是。。。你真的觉得我很脏吗？赫敏伸出双臂，这样他就可以在阳光下看着她那件质朴的裙子。“我看起来很脏吗？闻起来很脏？

A single jerk of his head that was neither up and down, nor left and right, was all she got but she interpreted it as a 'no' because she knew she didn’t.  
他头上下不上下，也不左右地抽搐，就是她所能得到的，但她把它解释为“不”，因为她知道她没有。

“And how do you think I got my magic? Do you think I stole it?
“那你觉得我是怎么得到魔法的呢？你觉得我偷了它吗？

“No,” he spat. “That was some ridiculous pamphlet cobbled together by Umbridge as though magic can be—”
“不，”他啐了一口。“那是乌姆里奇拼凑起来的一本荒谬的小册子，仿佛魔法可以——”

“Then why do you think I have magic?”
“那你为什么觉得我有魔法？”

“You are an accident, an aberration.”
“你是个意外，一个反常。”

“An aberration.” Hermione nodded, her expression grave. “I see. So as an aberration—a departure from the norm— I suppose you could say I’m an exception to the rule that says magic belongs to purely magical families.” Malfoy’s eyes narrowed into slits and Hermione continued, satisfied that he knew exactly where she was going. “Someone once told me that exceptions undermine rules and so absolutism is pointless. Have you ever heard that?”
“一个反常。”赫敏点点头，表情严肃。“我明白了。所以作为一个反常——背离常态——我想你可以说我是魔法属于纯粹魔法家族的规则的例外。马尔福的眼睛眯成一条缝，赫敏继续说，满意他确切地知道她要去哪里。“有人曾经告诉我，例外会破坏规则，所以绝对主义毫无意义。你听说过吗？

“It’s different,” he said, his face cold and furious.
“不一样，”他说，脸色冰冷而愤怒。

“Oh, I’m sure it is. Squibs from ancient Pure-blood families, witches and wizards from Muggle families—all just freak accidents rather than proof that magic doesn’t accumulate in the blood to be either strengthened or diluted. Isn’t that right?”
“哦，我确定是这样。来自古代纯血统家庭的哑炮，来自麻瓜家庭的女巫和巫师——所有这些都只是怪异的意外，而不是证明魔法不会在血液中积累以加强或稀释。不是吗？

“Your magic has not been refined over centuries of good breeding.”
“你的魔法在几个世纪的良好繁殖中还没有得到提炼。”

“That’s not how it works, I’m afraid. I have magic just like yours and I’ve honed it through years of practice…just like you. If anything, when you’re wearing that.” Hermione gestured to his ankle, knowing the Magic Dampener lay under the leg of his trousers. “My magic is undeniably more powerful than yours. So where does that leave us? When I have the magic and you don’t? Does that make me better than you now? I suppose you still have the money…” She looked around the grounds appraisingly and then back at Malfoy, one eyebrow raised. 
“恐怕不是这样运作的。我有和你一样的魔法，我通过多年的练习磨练了它......就像你一样。如果有的话，当你穿着它时。赫敏指了指他的脚踝，知道魔法阻尼器就在他的裤腿下。“不可否认，我的魔法比你的更强大。那么，这给我们留下了什么呢？当我有魔法而你没有？那我现在比你更好吗？我想你还有钱......”她赞赏地环顾了一下场地，然后又看向马尔福，扬起了一根眉毛。

“You will leave, Miss Granger,” Lucius said, his hands clenched tight into fists. “Right now.”
“你会走的，格兰杰小姐，”卢修斯说，他的双手紧紧地握成拳头。“现在。”

Hermione didn’t care that he was clearly barely restraining himself, she just had to push. “How did you feel when you found out Voldemort was a Half-blood, Malfoy? That you’d unquestioningly served a man who had a Muggle father? Or is that the kind of thing that it’s actually fairly easy to gloss over when power and wealth are at stake? Because what does blood purity actually matter when it’s all fake?”
赫敏不在乎他显然是在勉强克制自己，她只需要推挤。“当你发现伏地魔是个混血儿时，你感觉如何，马尔福？你毫无疑问地为一个有麻瓜父亲的男人服务？或者，当权力和财富受到威胁时，这种事情实际上很容易被掩盖吗？因为当血液都是假的时，血液纯度实际上又有什么关系呢？

“Leave!” he barked, raising his voice to the loudest point Hermione had ever heard it reach.
“走！”他吼道，把声音提高到了赫敏听过的最响亮的程度。

With as much dignity as she could muster, Hermione drew her wand from her bag and tapped the Wheezebox to stop its recording. Grabbing it from the air, she shoved it into her bag. “My notes on your family are in the library if you care to look, Mr Malfoy. I have no interest in lying to you. Or for you.”
赫敏尽可能地鼓起尊严，从包里掏出魔杖，敲打着喘息器，停止了录音。她从空中抓起它，把它塞进了她的包里。“如果你愿意看的话，我关于你家庭的笔记就在图书馆里，马尔福先生。 我没兴趣对你撒谎。或者为了你。

With that, Hermione turned on her heel and made her way back to the house, her heart hammering as it sank its way down into her stomach. She’d fucked it again and almost certainly wasted her last chance. Despite that, she thought with a bitter smirk on her face, it felt worth it. Nothing about what he believed made sense to her and she was almost relieved by that.
说完，赫敏转身回到了房子里，她的心跳加速，沉入了她的胃里。她又操了一次，几乎可以肯定她浪费了最后的机会。尽管如此，她还是带着苦涩的笑容想，这感觉很值得。他所相信的东西对她来说毫无意义，她几乎因此松了一口气。
