更多注释见本章末尾“I mean, honestly, some of the things he’s said to me,” Hermione fumed, stabbing her tiny plastic spoon into a pale scoop of lavender ice cream. “No intelligent person could surely think that way. As though having a gene pool so shallow it needs a ‘no diving’ sign is somehow a mark of superiority.”
“我是说，老实说，他对我说的一些话，”赫敏生气地把她的小塑料勺子捅进了一勺苍白的薰衣草冰淇淋里。“没有一个聪明人肯定能这样想。就好像基因库如此浅以至于需要一个'禁止潜水'的标志在某种程度上是一种优越感的标志。

Hermione shovelled the ice cream into her mouth, barely tasting the flavour, and jabbed her spoon in the direction of a bewildered Terry Boot. “And I think that might be the worst thing, you know. I’m fairly sure he is intelligent. He’s just never bothered to question anything he’s been told because the lies suit him; they’re advantageous to him. The apathy ! The selfishness!”
赫敏把冰淇淋铲进嘴里，勉强尝到了味道，然后用勺子戳向困惑的特里靴的方向。“我认为这可能是最糟糕的事情，你知道的。我相当确定他很聪明。他只是从来懒得质疑他被告知的任何事情，因为谎言适合他;他们对他有利。冷漠！太自私了！

“The Slytherinness?” Terry interjected with a hesitant smile. 
“斯莱特林？”特里犹豫地笑着打断了他。

Mouth open, spoon in the air, Hermione stopped and looked at him. “Yes,” she said. “The Slytherinness.” Looking down at her almost finished ice cream, Hermione felt a burning shame and met Terry’s eye. “I’m so sorry, I’ve done nothing but rant at you since I got here.”
赫敏张着嘴，勺子在空中，停了下来，看着他。“是的，”她说。“斯莱特林。”赫敏低头看着她快吃完的冰淇淋，感到一阵灼热的羞耻，与特里的眼睛相遇。“我很抱歉，自从我来到这里以来，除了对你咆哮之外，我什么也没做。”

"That’s alright, I don’t mind listening."
“没关系，我不介意听。”

"No, you shouldn't have to listen to that. This should be nice." Hermione sighed and attempted to form something close to a smile. "How’s the butterbeer flavour?"
“不，你不应该听那个。这应该很好。赫敏叹了口气，试图形成一个接近微笑的东西。“黄油啤酒的味道怎么样？”

Terry smiled and pushed his tub towards Hermione, angling it so that the spoon was closer to her side. "Why don’t you try it?"
泰瑞微笑着把他的浴缸推向赫敏，调整它的角度，让勺子更靠近她的身边。“你为什么不试试呢？”

"Oh." Hermione hesitated. Ron had never shared and when he had offered it was always with the understanding that you wouldn't accept. "Are you sure?" 
“哦。”赫敏犹豫了。罗恩从来没有分享过，当他提出时，他总是明白你不会接受。“你确定吗？”

"It’s ice cream, Hermione." Terry gestured to the pastel surroundings of the ice cream parlour. "Not a finite resource here." 
“是冰淇淋，赫敏。”特里指了指冰淇淋店柔和的环境。“这里的资源不是有限的。”

Blushing, Hermione slid her own tub towards him. "Then you try some of mine."
赫敏脸红了，把自己的浴缸滑向他。“那你尝尝我的。”

"Deal." 
“成交。”

Their eyes met as they tried each other’s flavours and Hermione grinned, feeling unusually shy. It seemed ridiculous that something so innocuous could feel intimate, and yet. "Hey, it is good," she said.
他们的目光相遇，尝试着彼此的味道，赫敏咧嘴一笑，感觉异常害羞。如此无害的事情会让人感到亲密，这似乎很荒谬，然而。“嘿，这很好，”她说。

Terry stuck out his tongue, his face screwed up, and pushed her chosen ice cream back across the table. "I don’t think I’m a lavender guy."
Terry伸出舌头，脸上一团糟，把她选好的冰淇淋推回桌子对面。“我不认为我是一个喜欢薰衣草的人。”

Hermione quietly snorted a laugh. "You have no idea how much I’d have killed to hear that in school."
赫敏悄悄地哼了一声笑。“你不知道如果我在学校听到这些话，会付出多少代价。”

"What?"
“什么？”

"Er, never mind. Stupid joke," Hermione said with an apologetic grin. She was so unused to spending time outside of their group, where their private jokes actually were private.
“呃，没关系。愚蠢的笑话，“赫敏带着歉意的笑容说。她太不习惯在他们的小组之外花时间了，他们的私人笑话实际上是私人的。

"Don’t think you could ever do anything stupid."
“别以为你永远都能做任何蠢事。”

Well , Hermione thought with an astonished blink, that’s overt . Looking down because eye contact felt like a touch too much after quite possibly the most flirtatious compliment she’d heard in years, Hermione said, "You’ve had to listen to me go on and on about my work, as much as it is. Why don’t you tell me about the Archives?"
嗯，赫敏惊讶地眨了眨眼想，这太明显了。赫敏低下头，因为眼神交流感觉有点太过分了，这很可能是她多年来听到的最轻浮的赞美，赫敏说，“你得听我滔滔不绝地谈论我的工作，尽管它就是这样。你为什么不告诉我关于档案馆的事呢？

"Oh, it’s not exciting at all," he said with a self-effacing grin. 
“哦，一点也不刺激，”他带着自谦的笑容说。

"But it must be so interesting! Having access to all of that information."
“可是，这一定很有趣！可以访问所有这些信息。

"Interesting for sure but not exciting. I don’t know if it’s what I want to do forever."
“当然很有趣，但并不令人兴奋。我不知道这是否是我想永远做的事情。

"It can be hard to know that," Hermione said sympathetically. "So many options."
“知道这一点可能很难，”赫敏同情地说。“这么多选择。”

"Exactly! There’s so much to see and do. It feels a shame to spend my life in a windowless room."
“正是！有很多东西可以看和做。在没有窗户的房间里度过我的一生，感觉很可惜。

"A big change from Ravenclaw tower."
“与拉文克劳塔楼相比，这是一个很大的变化。”

"Yeah," he laughed, revealing his dimples again. Rubbing the back of his neck, Terry looked off to the side. "Er, look, I know you said you’re quite busy these days but do you want to go for a drink after this? There’s a new place down by Gringotts."
“是啊，”他笑了起来，再次露出了他的酒窝。Terry揉了揉他的后颈，看向一边。“呃，你看，我知道你说你这几天很忙，但之后你想去喝一杯吗？古灵阁那边有个新地方。

Hermione shifted her legs under the table, crossing one ankle over the other as she considered him. She was having a nice time, wasn’t she? And she certainly wasn’t going to be back at Malfoy Manor in any great hurry. "Sure. I’d love that."
赫敏把双腿移到桌子下面，一边打量着他，一边把一只脚踝交叉在另一只脚踝上。她玩得很开心，不是吗？而且她肯定不会匆忙回到马尔福庄园。“当然。我会喜欢的。

Lucius clutched his glass of firewhiskey, pressing his fingertips hard enough into the glass that his nails turned white. He'd done it every 5 minutes for an hour and he couldn't rid himself of the feeling of Granger's fingers ghosting over his own as she'd taken Cato’s ball from his hands. That she would dare to touch him.
卢修斯紧紧握着他的火威士忌杯，指尖用力地按在玻璃杯里，指甲都发白了。他每五分钟做一次，持续了一个小时，他无法摆脱格兰杰的手指在他自己的手指上滑过的感觉，因为她从他手中夺走了卡托的球。她敢碰他。

Impudent little Mudblood.  
无耻的小泥巴种。

Setting the glass down, Lucius flexed his fingers outwards to try something else. Standing in his grounds in her unaccountably short dress with her wild curls like some chaotic, troublemaking pixie. He should never have allowed Draco to convince him. He should never have allowed her back . Who was she to come to his home with all her self-righteousness and tell him that he was wrong? That generations of Malfoys were wrong ?
放下杯子，Lucius 向外弯曲手指，尝试其他东西。她穿着她那莫名其妙的短裙，狂野的卷发像什么混乱的、捣蛋的小精灵。他绝对不应该让德拉科说服他。他永远不应该让她回来。她是谁，竟然带着她所有的自以为是来到他家，告诉他他错了？几代马尔福都错了？

“My notes on your family are in the library if you care to look, Mr Malfoy. I have no interest in lying to you.” 
“如果你愿意看的话，我关于你家庭的笔记就在图书馆里，马尔福先生。 我没兴趣骗你。

No interest in lying indeed. Lucius scoffed and snatched up the glass to take a swig of his firewhiskey. 
确实没有兴趣撒谎。卢修斯嗤之以鼻，抓起酒杯，喝了一口他的火威士忌。

When she had kept the story of his divorce to herself he had been reluctantly impressed, if he was being generous. He thought that he had discovered a very rare thing indeed: a discreet Gryffindor. Rare things interested him. They were worthy of further study, at least, to see if they held any value. However, she had proven since then that she was everything else he hated about that forsaken house: self-righteous, indelicate, stubborn, hot-headed. And she wasn’t wrong when she said she had pride. It was undeserved. 
当她把他离婚的故事藏在心里时，如果他慷慨的话，他就不情愿地留下了深刻的印象。他以为自己确实发现了一件非常罕见的东西：一个低调的格兰芬多。很少有东西让他感兴趣。至少，它们值得进一步研究，看看它们是否有任何价值。然而，从那时起，她就证明了她就是他讨厌的那个被遗弃的房子的一切：自以为是、不成熟、固执、头脑发热。她说她有骄傲并没有错。这是不应该的。

Gritting his teeth, Lucius pushed himself from his chair and swept out of his study, firewhiskey in hand. The sun was low in the sky, making a show in its final hours by casting a blood red glow over his face as he marched along the corridor in the direction of the library. He wasn’t afraid of her notes. As though a Mudblood brain was really all that capable of grasping the complexity of the Malfoy family and the history of a world in which she didn’t even belong. 
Lucius咬紧牙关，从椅子上站起来，手里拿着火威士忌，大步走出了书房。太阳低垂在天空中，在最后的几个小时里，当他沿着走廊向图书馆的方向走去时，他的脸上投下了血红色的光芒。他不怕她的笔记。仿佛一个泥巴种的大脑真的能够理解马尔福家族的复杂性，以及一个她甚至不属于这个世界的历史。

Marching through the library doors, Malfoy shuddered at the sudden drop in temperature. The fire was burning itself out, its glow providing just enough light to see while barely making a difference to the temperature of the room. A feeling of frustrated impotence made him take another long drink. Letty was at a different house, as Granger’s stupid act permitted, and he didn’t have the magic to light the fire himself. He’d be damned before he got on his knees and did it the Muggle way. 
迈步穿过图书馆的门，马尔福对突然下降的气温感到不寒而栗。火势正在自行燃烧，它的光芒刚好提供了足够的光线，同时对房间的温度几乎没有影响。一种沮丧的无能为力的感觉使他又喝了一大口酒。莱蒂在另一所房子里，正如格兰杰的愚蠢行为所允许的那样，他没有自己点火的魔法。在他跪下来像麻瓜一样做这件事之前，他就该死了。

He was still haunted by the time, not long after Narcissa’s departure, that he had found himself desirous of tea and Draco had entered the kitchen to find him utterly stumped before the stove, unable to light the fire without his magic. Draco had done him the kindness of wordlessly lighting it and immediately leaving so that he could attempt to wrangle with the stovetop kettle on his own. Never having suffered the indignity of making his own tea, he hadn’t been entirely sure how to go about it. He’d barely ever stepped foot in the manor’s kitchen. The entire process had taken him an hour and the tea hadn’t even tasted good, which was infuriating because how difficult could it possibly be ? 
在纳西莎离开后不久，他发现自己很想喝茶，而德拉科走进厨房，发现他在炉子前完全被难住了，没有魔法就无法生火。德拉科好心地点燃了它，然后立即离开，这样他就可以自己尝试与炉灶水壶争论了。他从来没有因为自己泡茶而遭受过羞辱，所以他并不完全确定该怎么做。他几乎从未踏入过庄园的厨房。整个过程花了他一个小时，而且茶的味道甚至都不好，这很令人愤怒，因为这有多难？

The next day Lucius had found a box of matches on his desk, obviously left there by Draco. He had encountered the things before, of course; in his first year at Hogwarts he’d been tasked with transfiguring them into needles and he’d proven rather adept at it. But he’d never had to use them to light a fire like the Muggles. It struck him as primitive. He’d spent hours attempting to use them, with sporadic success. More than once he had burned his fingers and when he’d finally taken the matches to the kitchen to attempt another pot of tea it still hadn’t come out right. 
第二天，卢修斯在他的桌子上发现了一盒火柴，显然是德拉科留在那里的。当然，他以前也遇到过这些事情;在霍格沃茨的第一年，他的任务是把它们变成针，事实证明他相当擅长这件事。但他从来没有像麻瓜那样用它们来点火。这让他觉得很原始。他花了几个小时尝试使用它们，但偶尔取得了成功。他不止一次烫伤了手指，当他终于把火柴带到厨房再泡一壶茶时，还是没有流出来。

If the Ministry had been trying to make him more understanding of Muggles by taking his magic away they’d utterly failed. As far as he was concerned, a life in which something as basic as making tea was so unnecessarily laborious, never mind fraught with opportunities to turn oneself into an inferno, was a life that was hardly worth living. 
如果魔法部一直试图通过剥夺麻瓜的魔法来让他对麻瓜有更多的了解，那他们就彻底失败了。对他来说，泡茶这样基本的事情是如此不必要地费力，更不用说充满了把自己变成地狱的机会，这种生活几乎不值得过。

He’d barely been able to believe his ears when Granger had told him that she was voluntarily making her own tea when he’d found her rummaging around his kitchen like a Niffler. Surely just more proof that she didn’t deserve the magic she had.
当格兰杰告诉他她是自愿自己泡茶时，他几乎不敢相信自己的耳朵，而他发现她像个嗅嗅一样在他的厨房里翻找。当然，这只是更多的证据，证明她不配拥有她所拥有的魔法。

He matched his tea-drinking routine to Letty’s work routine now and if the elf had noticed she had the sense not to mention it. 
他现在把自己的喝茶习惯和莱蒂的工作习惯相匹配，如果那个小精灵注意到了，她就有意识不提这件事。

Casting a dark look at the embers, Lucius exhaled sharply through his nose. The firewhiskey would keep him warm. 
卢修斯阴暗地看着余烬，从鼻子里猛地呼出一口气。火威士忌会让他保持温暖。

Approaching Granger’s desk, Lucius set his glass on one of the few slivers of wood not covered by parchment or books. He was ready to sneer at her messiness when he saw evidence of a colour-coded system and rolled his eyes. Organised chaos made a lot more sense given her hair. 
走近格兰杰的书桌，卢修斯把酒杯放在为数不多的几块没有被羊皮纸或书本覆盖的木条上。当他看到颜色编码系统的证据时，他准备嘲笑她的凌乱，并翻了个白眼。考虑到她的头发，有组织的混乱更有意义。

Scanning the table, he saw a thick folder bearing his own name and a black sticker. Arching his eyebrow, he lifted the folder and dropped it with a heavy thud in front of himself before flicking it open disdainfully. With a sinking feeling, Lucius picked through her mounds of research. She was…thorough. 
扫视着桌子，他看到一个厚厚的文件夹，上面写着他自己的名字和一张黑色的贴纸。他扬起眉毛，举起文件夹，砰的一声丢在自己面前，然后轻蔑地打开了它。带着一种沉重的感觉，卢修斯在她的一堆研究中挑选。她是。。。彻底。

Extracts from Florian Malfoy’s 1693 anti-Statute of Secrecy tract; eye-witness writings in early modern English from various foreign ambassadors describing Lucius Malfoy I’s designs on Elizabeth the Muggle; long-buried copies of the Malfoy family tree which included the Squibs that they had attempted to hide. There were more of those than he’d realised, he thought as he lifted the parchment and squinted at the crossed-off names. 
摘自弗洛里安·马尔福 （Florian Malfoy） 1693 年的反保密法规小册子;多位外国大使用早期现代英语撰写的目击者著作，描述了卢修斯·马尔福一世对麻瓜伊丽莎白的设计;埋藏已久的马尔福家谱副本，其中包括他们试图隐藏的哑炮。那些人比他意识到的要多，他想着，一边掀起羊皮纸，眯着眼睛看着那些被划掉的名字。

Lucius pulled out another sheet, his attention drawn by the way it was stamped red with Copy Approved By Ministry Archive. Lucius scanned it and found it was a court record of an impassioned speech made by Sabine Malfoy in 1655. Slowly, he sank into Granger’s seat as he pored over the parchment. The speech, he discovered, was testimony in defence of her lady’s maid. Her Muggle lady’s maid. 
卢修斯拿出另一张纸，他的注意力被上面印着魔法部档案馆批准的红色印章所吸引。 卢修斯扫描了一下，发现这是萨宾娜·马尔福在 1655 年发表的一次慷慨激昂的演讲的法庭记录。他慢慢地坐在格兰杰的座位上，仔细研究着羊皮纸。他发现，这番话是为她女士的女仆辩护的证词。她的麻瓜女士的女仆。

Reading quickly, Malfoy surmised that the maid had been on trial in the Muggle court, accused of witchcraft. He'd always found it infuriating that the Ministry kept records of such Muggle barbarity but so often real witches and wizards had been dragged into proceedings. Apparently the maid had been accused by—Malfoy gripped the parchment more tightly, reading and re-reading the name as though it would somehow change if he willed it—Sabine’s husband, Magnus Malfoy. 
马尔福快速阅读，推测这个女仆是在麻瓜法庭上受审的，被指控使用巫术。他总是觉得很生气，魔法部保留了这种麻瓜野蛮行为的记录，但真正的女巫和巫师经常被拖入诉讼程序。显然，那个女仆被——马尔福把羊皮纸抓得更紧了，一遍又一遍地读着这个名字，仿佛如果他愿意，它就会以某种方式改变——萨宾的丈夫，马格努斯·马尔福。

Lucius swallowed and, finding his mouth very dry, reached out to take a drink of his firewhiskey. His ancestors involved in petty Muggle trials? Petty Muggle witch trials? He squinted at Hermione’s cramped footnotes that linked the case with other historical records and hurriedly dug through to find them. They were extracts from magical history books, Muggle records and Sabine Malfoy’s own diaries that she had apparently left to the Ministry archive for posterity. It was well seeing she had outlived her husband – that was not a particularly Malfoy thing to do.
卢修斯咽了口口水，发现自己口干舌燥，伸手喝了一口他的火威士忌。他的祖先卷入了麻瓜的小审判？小规模的麻瓜女巫审判？他眯着眼睛看着赫敏狭窄的脚注，这些脚注将这个案子与其他历史记录联系起来，然后匆匆忙忙地翻找着。它们是魔法历史书、麻瓜记录和萨宾娜·马尔福自己的日记的摘录，显然她已经留给了魔法部的档案，供后人使用。看到她比她的丈夫活得更久，这真是太好了——那可不是马尔福特别擅长做的事情。

In the end, the lady’s maid had been saved from death, not by Sabine’s defence, but by the discovery that she was pregnant. After that she disappeared from public records. Pushing the diary extracts Granger had obviously deemed the most pertinent closer to the weak glow of the fire, Lucius read. 
最后，这位女士的女仆免于死亡，不是因为萨宾娜的辩护，而是因为发现她怀孕了。在那之后，她从公共记录中消失了。卢修斯把格兰杰显然认为最相关的日记摘录推到离火光微弱的地方，读道。

“October 30  
“10 月 30 日

Took Annabel and the child food and warm clothing for the winter today. Magnus still unaware and will remain so. The child has his eyes. A kind version of them. Annabel told me strange things have been happening since the child’s fifth birthday. I fear the worst. 
今天带了 Annabel 和孩子们过冬的食物和保暖的衣服。马格努斯仍然不知道，而且会一直如此。孩子有他的眼睛。他们的善良版本。安娜贝尔告诉我，自从孩子五岁生日以来，奇怪的事情一直在发生。我担心最坏的情况。

January 5
一月 5

The child is undoubtedly magical, I have seen it with my own eyes. Annabel is frightened. Understandably so, after her own experience. The boy is all she has now. The witch hunts continue but my wards are keeping them safe. I have vowed to protect them. After what Magnus inflicted on her, it is the least I can do.  
这个孩子无疑是神奇的，我亲眼见过。安娜贝尔很害怕。根据她自己的经历，这是可以理解的。这个男孩就是她现在所拥有的一切。猎巫行动仍在继续，但我的守护者正在保护他们的安全。我发誓要保护他们。在马格努斯对她造成了伤害之后，这是我至少能做的了。

April 18
四月 18

The boy’s magic is showing itself with increasing frequency and I fear what will happen if he is not taught to control it. Forced to tell Magnus of his abilities. Misguided of me to think that such a revelation would prompt him to be more generous. Magnus does not know the meaning of the word.  
这个男孩的魔法越来越频繁地显现出来，我担心如果不教他如何控制它会发生什么。被迫告诉卡尔森他的能力。我误以为这样的启示会促使他更加慷慨。马格努斯不知道这个词的含义。

For the first time, it appears he is interested in the living consequences of his actions. He is taking the child and intends to name him Cyrus. When I protested, he reminded me that he was merely taking what I have thus far been unable to give him. Annabel devastated and I am responsible. We have ruined her. He has ruined me.” 
他似乎第一次对自己行为的活生生的后果感兴趣。他正在带走这个孩子，并打算给他取名赛勒斯。当我抗议时，他提醒我，他只是拿走了我迄今为止无法给他的东西。安娜贝尔悲痛欲绝，我有责任。我们毁了她。他毁了我。

Setting the parchment down, Lucius brushed his fingers over it thoughtfully. He thought he knew Sabine. Any time he'd been forced to stand outside his father’s office, waiting for his punishment for some kind of wrongdoing, Sabine had been the only portrait that had talked to him. She didn't comfort him, exactly – that was not her way – but she'd distracted him. His father had moved her but as soon as the manor became his, Lucius had put her right back where she belonged – in a prime position to irritate anyone who dared to bother him in his private study. 
放下羊皮纸，卢修斯若有所思地用手指抚摸着它。他以为自己认识萨宾。每当他被迫站在他父亲的办公室外，等待他因某种错误行为而受到惩罚时，Sabine 是唯一一个和他说话的肖像。她没有安慰他，确切地说——那不是她的方式——但她分散了他的注意力。他的父亲把她搬走了，但庄园一变成他的，卢修斯就把她放回了属于她的地方——处于一个有利的位置，可以激怒任何敢在他的私人书房里打扰他的人。

Lifting one of the family trees, Lucius surveyed the names, running his finger through history until he found it. Magnus Malfoy, Sabine Malfoy: married. One child: Cyrus. No mention of Annabel the Muggle. How long had this information sat in the Ministry’s archives uninvestigated? 
卢修斯拿起其中一棵家谱，仔细研究了这些名字，用手指在历史中摸索，直到找到它。马格努斯·马尔福，萨宾娜·马尔福：已婚。一个孩子：赛勒斯。没有提到麻瓜安娜贝尔。这些信息在国防部的档案中存放了多长时间没有被调查？

An odd queasiness rising up his throat, Lucius turned his attention to the rest of Hermione’s notes, not covering just his own family but the other witches and wizards she’d interviewed, as well as the records from the first and second wizarding wars. It was…sprawling. Beyond his expectations. Beyond what he had ever studied of his own world. Beyond absolutes. 
一阵奇怪的恶心从他的喉咙里升起，卢修斯把注意力转向了赫敏的其余笔记，不仅包括他自己的家人，还包括她采访过的其他女巫和巫师，以及第一次和第二次巫师战争的记录。那是......广阔。超出他的预期。超越了他对自己世界的研究。超越绝对。

Lucius gripped the edge of the table. Perhaps she was intelligent. Draco's never-ending complaints about her during their school days had made it clear to Lucius that she was teachable but this was different. By all accounts she knew more about the wizarding world, more about the dirty secrets of his family, than he did. Everyone knew there were darker aspects of the Malfoy family’s history; they’d never tried particularly hard to hide it because it gave them an intimidating edge. Granger had found the kinds of things that they did hide.  
卢修斯紧紧抓住桌子的边缘。也许她很聪明。德拉科在学生时代对她无休止的抱怨让卢修斯清楚地知道她是可以教的，但这次不同。从各方面来看，她比他更了解魔法世界，更了解他家庭的肮脏秘密。每个人都知道马尔福家族的历史有更黑暗的一面;他们从来没有特别努力地隐藏它，因为这给了他们一种令人生畏的优势。格兰杰发现了他们隐藏的那些东西。

Yet, somehow, he didn’t think he had to worry about her telling anyone. She just wanted him to know she knew. Now, so did he. Except he wasn’t entirely sure how to feel about it. Angry? Embarrassed? Both with a dash of something else? He thought he rather wanted to kill Granger but that instinct was tempered by a desire to find out what else she knew.
然而，不知何故，他认为他不必担心她会告诉任何人。她只是想让他知道她知道。现在，他也这样做了。只是他不完全确定该如何看待它。生气？尴尬？两者都有一点其他东西？他以为他宁愿想杀了格兰杰，但这种本能被想知道她还知道什么的愿望所缓和。

A newspaper clipping sandwiched between two booklets of parchment caught Malfoy’s eye and he pulled it out, taking great care not to rip it. 
夹在两本羊皮纸小册子之间的剪报引起了马尔福的注意，他把它掏了出来，小心翼翼地不把它撕掉。

Miss Aurelia Rosier weds Mr Abraxas Malfoy in the society wedding of the summer. 
奥雷莉亚·罗西尔小姐在夏季的社交婚礼上与阿布拉克萨斯·马尔福先生结婚。

A picture of his mother and father sat below the faded black text of the headline. They stood side by side, not touching. His mother, beautiful with her large eyes and soft features. She was much smaller than his father, who sneered haughtily into the camera. Neither of them looked happy, even then.
他父母的照片放在标题褪色的黑色文字下方。他们并排站着，没有接触。他的母亲，美丽的大眼睛和柔和的五官。她比他的父亲小得多，他的父亲对着镜头傲慢地嘲笑。即使在那时，他们俩看起来都不高兴。

Their marriage had been… convenient , a voice that sounded startlingly like Granger’s whispered in his head. Just who it had been convenient for, he wasn't sure. Certainly not him. Or his mother. Who was any of it for ?
他们的婚姻一直......方便，一个听起来像格兰杰的声音在他的脑海中低语。至于对谁来说很方便，他不确定。当然不是他。或者他的母亲。这是为了谁的？

Slamming the newspaper clipping down under his palm, Lucius bent his head and took several deep breaths before pulling the folder back towards himself to continue reading.
卢修斯将剪报砸在手心下，低下头，深呼吸了几次，然后将文件夹拉回自己身边继续阅读。

Hermione sipped her fourth Mopsus Martini and leaned into the corner of the booth in which she and Terry had been talking for several hours. They were both growing tipsy, Hermione probably far closer to drunk, but she’d been having just enough fun that she didn’t really want to be the one to call it a night. 
赫敏啜了她的第四杯莫普苏斯马提尼酒，靠在她和泰瑞已经聊了几个小时的卡座角落里。他们俩都喝得酩酊大醉，赫敏可能快喝醉了，但她已经玩得够开心了，她真的不想成为那个收工的人。

The bar he’d taken them to was decent enough. Below street level, it was fairly dark with low lighting that made it feel cosy and intimate. Not particularly summer-y, Hermione thought, but certainly suitable for a date. Being close to Gringotts, it seemed to be a popular haunt for goblins and curse breakers whose quiet, intense conversations actually made for the kind of atmosphere that Hermione preferred. 
他带他们去的酒吧还不错。在街道以下，它相当黑暗，光线昏暗，让人感觉舒适和亲密。不是特别的夏日气息，赫敏想，但肯定适合约会。靠近古灵阁，这里似乎是妖精和破诅者的热门出没之地，他们安静、激烈的对话实际上营造出赫敏喜欢的那种氛围。

Feeling like she had to let off some steam and seize an opportunity for some levity, Hermione had opted to try the cocktail menu which was, based on the bartender’s reaction when they’d ordered, largely ignored by the bar’s usual customer base. Hermione had stuck to the one drink while Terry had tried a few, allowing her to sip them so that they could debate the merits of each. His choice of a Lychee Love Potion had led them into a debate over love potions generally.  
赫敏觉得她必须发泄一下，抓住一个轻松的机会，她选择尝试鸡尾酒菜单，根据调酒师点菜时的反应，酒吧的普通客户群基本上忽略了这个菜单。赫敏坚持喝一杯，而泰瑞则试了几杯，让她啜饮一口，这样他们就可以争论每杯酒的优劣。他选择的荔枝爱情药水让他们陷入了一场关于爱情药水的普遍争论。

“I just think they’re wrong,” Hermione said, shaking her head more vehemently than she would have if she hadn’t been drinking, her curls bouncing against her flushed cheeks. “I overheard some girls plotting to slip Harry love potion in sixth year. I was furious.”
“我只是觉得他们错了，”赫敏说，比她没有喝酒时更猛烈地摇头，她的卷发在她通红的脸颊上弹跳。“我无意中听到一些女孩在六年级时密谋偷偷服用哈利爱情魔药。我很生气。

“Yeah, but the effects are only temporary and did anything bad happen to him?”
“是的，但影响只是暂时的，他身上发生了什么不好的事情吗？”

“Well, no,” Hermione said slowly, frowning and electing to gloss over what had happened to Ron in the aftermath for the sake of keeping things relatively light. “But he didn’t like that girl so why should she take it on herself to make him?”
“嗯，没有，”赫敏缓缓地说，皱着眉头，为了让事情相对轻松，她选择掩盖罗恩在事后发生的事情。“可是他不喜欢那个女孩，为什么她要自己动手来造就他呢？”

“It wouldn’t have lasted forever, Hermione,” Terry said, laughing. “He’d have snapped out of it and she’d have had the night she wanted. I reckon Harry wouldn’t be half as annoyed as you are on his behalf.”
“它不会永远持续下去的，赫敏，”特里笑着说。“他会突然从中走出来，她会度过她想要的夜晚。我估计哈利不会像你代表他那样生气。

Slowly setting her drink down, Hermione gave Terry a sidelong look. “I don’t think that makes it okay , Terry. Where was Harry’s say in the matter? That’s not consensual. Love potions are no better than the Imperius Curse, if you ask me and I bet you wouldn't defend that.”
慢慢地放下她的饮料，赫敏侧头看了特里一眼。“我不认为这很好，特里。哈利在这件事上有什么发言权呢？这不是双方同意的。爱情药水并不比帝王诅咒好，如果你问我的话，我敢打赌你不会为此辩护。

Terry raised his eyebrows at Hermione over the rim of his glass. “That’s a bit of an extreme equivalence, don’t you think?” he asked, setting his glass down. “Imperius is an Unforgivable and love potions are legal. Even the Weasleys sell them.” He gave her a lopsided grin. “Don’t tell me you’d lock up the Weasleys.”
泰瑞对着玻璃杯边缘的赫敏扬起眉毛。“这有点极端的等同，你不觉得吗？”“Imperius 是不可饶恕的，爱情药水是合法的。就连韦斯莱家也卖它们。他朝她露出一个不平衡的笑容。“别跟我说你会把韦斯莱家关起来。”

“I’ve made my feelings on that front quite clear to George and Ron,” Hermione said shortly. “Love potions being legal doesn’t make them right . Sometimes I wonder if their risks aren’t given due consideration purely because of their cultural association with lovelorn teenage girls but they’re far more sinister than that and I think it’s silly just to…”
“我已经把我在这方面的感受告诉了乔治和罗恩，”赫敏很快说。“爱情药水合法并不意味着它们是正确的。有时我在想，她们的风险是否仅仅因为她们与失恋少女的文化联系而没有得到应有的考虑，但她们远比这险恶得多，我认为仅仅这样做是愚蠢的......”

Hermione trailed off as she noticed Terry was leaning closer to her. At first she’d thought it was that the martinis were having a fishbowl effect on her vision but, no, he was definitely getting closer. His hand came to rest on her knee and Hermione twitched like a cornered animal, looking down at it and then back up at him. In that second, he’d come even closer. His eyelids were heavy over his deep brown eyes. They were warm. They were also getting larger with every second. If Hermione didn't close hers, they'd meet in the middle trying to keep him in sight.

他说格兰杰小姐又忘了吃饭了。他怎么知道的？大概是阿斯托利亚告诉了他她的到来。也许他只是在他们在厨房里意外对峙后要求 Astoria 这样做。更有可能的是，他把莱蒂送上去，期待着她再次流浪。

Frowning, Hermione lifted another sandwich, feeling like a hamster that was being fed in its cage. Some crumbs fell onto her skirt and she automatically brushed them onto the floor. Tensing on realising what she’d done, Hermione drew her wand and vanished evidence of her mess with a nervous glance at the door. 
赫敏皱着眉头，举起了另一个三明治，感觉就像一只在笼子里被喂食的仓鼠。一些面包屑掉在她的裙子上，她自动地把它们刷到地板上。赫敏意识到自己做了什么，紧张地抽出魔杖，紧张地看了一眼门口，消失了她混乱的证据。

She’d just reached for the tea and was pouring some into her cup when a voice spoke from across the room. 
她刚伸手去拿茶，正往杯子里倒了一些，这时一个声音从房间的另一头传来。

“I see Letty has done as I asked.”
“我看莱蒂已经按照我的要求做了。”

Hermione started at the unexpected noise, slopping some tea over the edge of her cup and onto the tray. Looking up, she saw Lucius Malfoy standing in the doorway, watching her with raised eyebrows. 
赫敏被这意想不到的声音吓了一跳，把一些茶从杯子的边缘倒到托盘上。她抬起头，看到卢修斯·马尔福站在门口，扬起眉毛看着她。

“You’re very jumpy for a Gryffindor, aren’t you?” he drawled.
“你对格兰芬多来说很跳动，不是吗？”

“You did that on purpose.” Hermione scowled, lifting her wand to clean up the mess. 
“你是故意这样做的。”赫敏皱起眉头，举起魔杖收拾烂摊子。

“Yes, I suppose it does make sense that I would have tea brought to you by my house elf just so that I could make you spill it later.”
“是的，我想我让我的家养小精灵给你端茶确实是有道理的，这样我以后就可以让你把茶洒出来。”

“I don’t know how Slytherin minds come up with their diabolical plans.”
“我不知道斯莱特林是怎么想出他们邪恶的计划。”

“That is not diabolical, Miss Granger, it is convoluted.” He gave her a stern look. “And you are welcome for the food.”
“那不是恶魔，格兰杰小姐，这很复杂。”他严厉地看了她一眼。“不客气。”

“Thank you,” Hermione said quickly, a blush suffusing her cheeks. “I did miss lunch again, as it happens. How did you know?”
“谢谢你，”赫敏很快地说，脸颊上泛起了红晕。“碰巧我又错过了午餐。你怎么知道的？

"I merely assumed," he said, folding his hands behind his back. "Astoria mentioned your arrival at breakfast and it has been some time since then."
“我只是假设，”他说，双手交叉在背后。“阿斯托利亚在早餐时提到你的到来，从那时起已经有一段时间了。”

An awkward silence fell. Hermione wasn’t sure whether he would mention the note he had sent her or if she should do it. Surely if he wanted to talk about it he would; Lucius Malfoy wasn’t exactly the shy type. 
尴尬的沉默降临。赫敏不确定他是否应该提到他寄给她的那张纸条，或者她是否应该这样做。如果他想谈论这件事，他肯定会的;卢修斯·马尔福并不是那种害羞的类型。

“Aren’t you cold?” he asked, nodding his head at her with a frown. 
“你不冷吗？” 他问道，皱着眉头朝她点头。

Hermione looked down at her bare legs under the desk and pressed her knees together tightly, her face growing warm. It felt like a roundabout criticism of the way she dressed—it probably was—but her skirt was actually a perfectly acceptable length and just because he was quasi-Victorian with his suits and cravats didn’t mean she had to be. 
赫敏低头看着桌子下她光秃秃的双腿，双膝紧紧地靠在一起，脸上暖和起来。这感觉像是对她穿着方式的迂回批评——可能是这样——但她的裙子实际上是完全可以接受的长度，仅仅因为他穿着西装和领结是准维多利亚时代的人，并不意味着她必须如此。

“Why would I be?” she asked, sitting up straighter and doing a bad job at dampening her defensiveness.
“我为什么会这样？” 她问道，坐直了身子，在抑制她的防御性方面做得很糟糕。

“The temperature control charms in this room are set quite cold. It’s for the good of the books but not for the people reading them.”
“这个房间里的温度控制咒设置得很冷。这是为了书本的利益，而不是为了阅读它们的人。

“Oh.” Some of the tension seeped out of Hermione and her shoulders dropped as she gave him an abashed grin. “No, I’m okay. I used an imperturbable charm to contain a second temperature control charm under the desk. It keeps me warm without affecting the rest of the room.”
“哦。”赫敏身上渗出了一些紧张感，她的肩膀垂了下来，羞愧地对他咧嘴一笑。“不，我没事。我用了一个不动声色的咒语，在桌子下面装了第二个温度控制咒。它让我保持温暖，但不影响房间的其他部分。

Malfoy stared at her, his jaw clenched. It was hard to tell if he was annoyed or not. Hermione was about to offer to lift the spell when he finally murmured, “clever”, before looking off to the side. Mildly astonished, Hermione’s instinctive reaction was to smile at the compliment, regardless of how unwillingly given it was, but he didn’t smile back. If anything he appeared pained. 
马尔福盯着她，咬紧了下巴。很难说他是否生气。赫敏正要提议解除咒语，这时他终于喃喃自语道，“聪明”，然后看向一边。赫敏略显惊讶，他的本能反应是对这句赞美微笑，不管它有多么不情愿，但他没有回应。如果有的话，他看起来很痛苦。

“Would you like to join me?” Hermione asked, gesturing to the tea. “Letty left two cups.”
“你愿意和我一起吗？”赫敏问道，指着茶。“莱蒂留下了两个杯子。”

Malfoy blinked, his brows drawing together in a frown. “She did not leave two chairs, Miss Granger. I merely came to ensure she did as I asked.”
马尔福眨了眨眼，眉头紧锁。“她没有留下两把椅子，格兰杰小姐。我只是来确保她按照我的要求去做。

Before Malfoy could turn, Hermione picked up her wand and conjured a comfortable chair that was much like the one on which she was already sitting. Shifting her own chair over, she pulled the other one in towards the desk and turned to give Malfoy an expectant look. 
在马尔福转身之前，赫敏拿起她的魔杖，变出了一把舒适的椅子，这把椅子很像她已经坐过的那把椅子。她把自己的椅子挪过来，把另一把椅子拉到桌子上，转身期待地看了马尔福一眼。

Though it was a strange notion for her to contend with, she wanted him to join her. The note he sent her had piqued her curiosity. Just what had he thought about what he’d read?
虽然这对她来说是一个奇怪的想法，但她希望他能加入她。他寄给她的纸条激起了她的好奇心。他对自己读到的东西有什么看法？

Sighing through his nose, his hands dropping to his sides, he approached the desk and lowered himself regally into the chair. With a narrow-eyed look at her he slid one of his legs experimentally under the desk. On feeling the heat there, his eyes widened fractionally and Hermione grinned. 
他从鼻子里叹了口气，双手垂到身体两侧，走近桌子，庄重地坐在椅子上。他眯着眼睛看着她，实验性地将一条腿滑到桌子下面。感觉到那里的热度，他微微睁大了眼睛，赫敏咧嘴一笑。

“See? It works!”
“看到了吗？它有效！

He sighed and there was something almost wistful in it. “I suppose there is some relief in knowing that you do actually use magic.”
他叹了口气，里面有某种近乎渴望的东西。“我想知道你真的会使用魔法会让人松一口气。”

“And what’s that supposed to mean?” Hermione asked, her tone sharpening in line with her expression. 
“那应该是什么意思？”赫敏问道，她的语气随着她的表情而变得尖锐。

“It means that I think a witch who would dig through my kitchen cupboards in order to make tea the Muggle way may not fully appreciate what she has.”
“这意味着，我认为一个女巫会翻遍我的厨房橱柜，以便用麻瓜的方式泡茶，她可能并不完全欣赏她所拥有的。”

Hermione frowned, bringing the spare cup down to pour him some tea. “Just because I don’t whip my wand out for everything doesn’t mean I don’t appreciate my magic, Mr Malfoy,” she said, shooting him an irate glance. “I consider it a gift.”
赫敏皱起眉头，把备用的杯子拿下来给他倒了点茶。“仅仅因为我不为一切而动用魔杖，并不意味着我不欣赏我的魔法，马尔福先生，”她说，愤怒地瞥了他一眼。“我认为这是一份礼物。”

“Better than taking it as a given, I suppose,” he murmured, his expression distant as he took the tea from her with a vague nod of thanks. "Rather easy to do."
“我想，总比把它当作理所当然要好，”他喃喃自语，一边从她手中接过茶，含糊地点头表示感谢。“挺容易做到的。”

“Do you miss your magic then?”
“那你怀念你的魔法吗？”

Lucius’ eyes flicked upwards in a fleeting, irritated roll. “I see you are moving through the ‘i’s with your questions.” When Hermione merely raised her eyebrows with polite inquisitiveness over the rim of her teacup, he said, “First ‘invasive’, now ‘inane’. Perhaps one day you might accidentally veer into ‘interesting’ or ‘intelligent’, though I doubt it.”
卢修斯的眼睛向上眨了眨，转瞬即逝，恼怒地转动了一下。“我看到你正在用你的问题通过'我'。”当赫敏只是礼貌地好奇地抬起眉毛看着她的茶杯边缘时，他说，“先是'侵入性的'，现在是'无聊的'。也许有一天你可能会不小心转向'有趣'或'聪明'，尽管我对此表示怀疑。

Hermione choked on her tea, her nose wrinkling as the hot liquid splashed the tip of it. Lowering the cup, she fixed him with a glare. “There’s no need to be so rude .”
赫敏被茶呛住了，热液体溅到茶尖时，她的鼻子皱了起来。她放下杯子，瞪着他。“没必要这么粗鲁。”

“Well, of course I miss my magic. It’s barely a question worth asking.”
“嗯，我当然想念我的魔法。这几乎不是一个值得问的问题。

Hermione flushed a deep pink, clutching her teacup in her lap tightly. Perhaps he was right: it had been a silly question to ask, especially of him. She was also right, though: there hadn’t been any need for him to be so rude.
赫敏脸红了，紧紧地把茶杯攥在腿上。也许他是对的：这个问题一直很愚蠢，尤其是对他来说。不过，她也是对的：他没有必要这么粗鲁。

“Alright then,” Hermione said, proud of the calm control she managed to exercise over her tone. “What do you miss about it?”
“好吧，”赫敏说，为她设法控制自己的语气而感到自豪。“你很想念它吗？”

He blinked at her, perhaps not having anticipated the persistent immediacy of the shift in her line of questioning. They were, after all, not having a recorded conversation. Then he went quiet, frowning thoughtfully at her before allowing his gaze to be drawn down into the full cup of tea that he held in his lap. 
他朝她眨了眨眼，也许没有预料到她提问方式的持续转变会如此迅速。毕竟，他们没有录音谈话。然后他安静了下来，若有所思地皱着眉头看着她，然后让他的目光落在他腿上的满杯茶上。

Hermione was considering politely moving the conversation on, assuming he wasn’t going to answer, when he finally replied. “My magic is an intrinsic part of myself. I miss feeling whole.” 
赫敏正在考虑礼貌地转移话题，以为他不会回答，这时他终于回答了。“我的魔力是我自己内在的一部分。我想念完整的感觉。

His eyes flicked up to hers and Hermione swallowed, her tongue feeling oddly thick when she saw the truth of what he was saying written on his face. 
他的眼睛眨向她，赫敏咽了口口水，当她看到他脸上写着的话的真实性时，她的舌头感觉奇怪地厚。

“The Magic Dampener is a straitjacket, Miss Granger. A bridle.” He cleared his throat and straightened his waistcoat using his free hand. “A humiliation.”
“魔法阻尼器是一件束缚衣，格兰杰小姐。缰绳。他清了清嗓子，用空出来的手拉直了背心。“一种羞辱。”

Hermione felt locked in place by his gaze. She knew Lucius Malfoy was a proud man – if she hadn’t already witnessed it for herself, he had told her as much. He was proud in himself; in his heritage; in his magic. Pride was simply a facet of human nature, wasn’t it? They'd agreed on that. Funny, then, that Hermione thought he was displaying more humanity in this admission that his pride was injured than she had ever seen from him. 
赫敏感觉被他的目光锁定在原地。她知道卢修斯·马尔福是个骄傲的人——如果她没有亲眼目睹的话，他已经告诉了她同样的事情。他为自己感到自豪;在他的遗产中;在他的魔法中。骄傲只是人性的一个方面，不是吗？他们已经同意了这一点。那么，有趣的是，赫敏认为他承认自己的自尊心受到了伤害，比她从他身上看到的还要多。

"It's not especially nice when other people decide to make your magic – or your right to use it – their business, is it?" she asked with a pointed look.
“当其他人决定把你的魔法——或者你使用它的权利——当作他们的事时，这不是特别好的事情，不是吗？”

Lucius arched an eyebrow and Hermione thought she saw the corner of his lips twitch. "I cannot pretend it doesn't rankle."
卢修斯扬起眉毛，赫敏觉得她看到他的嘴角抽搐了一下。“我不能假装它不吵。”

“I appreciate your honesty,” she said.
“我很欣赏你的诚实，”她说。

“I’ve never been anything but honest with you, Miss Granger,” he said, his tone clipped. “Rightfully reticent on occasion, yes, but I don’t believe I've ever intentionally lied.”
“我对你从来都不是诚实的，格兰杰小姐，”他说，语气变得尖锐起来。“有时理所当然地保持沉默，是的，但我不相信我曾经故意撒谎。”

“I imagine that’s been a real challenge for you.” 
“我想这对你来说是一个真正的挑战。”

What was it about Lucius Malfoy that made it so hard for her to contain the mean-spirited jabs that so often passed through her mind?
卢修斯·马尔福究竟是什么让她如此难以控制那些经常在她脑海中闪过的卑鄙的刺痛呢？

Despite her rudeness, this time she definitely did see a hint of a smile from him, though it was fleeting. “Not as much as you might think.” On seeing Hermione’s doubtful expression, he added, “The best lies tend to contain at least a grain of truth, Miss Granger. If one can even be certain of what the ‘truth’ actually is.”
尽管她很粗鲁，但这一次她确实从他身上看到了一丝微笑，尽管那是转瞬即逝的。“没有你想象的那么多。”看到赫敏怀疑的表情，他又补充道，“最好的谎言往往至少包含一丝真相，格兰杰小姐。如果一个人甚至可以确定'真相'到底是什么。

Hermione’s warm brown eyes flicked between the grey coldness of his. “With that in mind.” She set her cup down on the table and, encouraged by his openness, decided to throw caution to the wind. “You read my notes.” 
赫敏温暖的棕色眼睛在他灰色的冰冷之间闪烁。“考虑到这一点。”她把杯子放在桌子上，受到他坦诚的鼓励，决定把谨慎抛诸脑后。“你读我的笔记。”

They were sitting fairly close. Close enough that Hermione could see Malfoy tense in response to her words. It was such a small movement and it struck her as something she would never have noticed if they’d been sitting their usual distance from one another. He took some time drinking his tea before lowering his own cup and looking at her. “You are a thorough researcher.”
他们坐得相当近。近到赫敏能看到马尔福对她的话的回应而紧张。这是一个如此小的动作，她觉得如果他们平时坐在彼此之间的距离，她永远不会注意到。他喝了一会儿茶，然后放下自己的杯子，看着她。“你是一个彻底的研究者。”

“That somewhat avoidant answer makes me think you don’t want to talk about any of it.”
“那个有点回避的回答让我觉得你不想谈论任何事情。”

“I would prefer not to for now,” Malfoy said with a nod and Hermione tried to hide her frustration and disappointment. He looked off to the side and then back at her. “Though, I wonder if I might read further through some of your other folders.”
“我现在宁愿不要，”马尔福点点头说，赫敏试图掩饰她的沮丧和失望。他看向一边，然后又看向她。“不过，我想知道我是否可以进一步阅读你的其他文件夹。”

Hermione hesitated and glanced down at the other piles of work on the desk. Everyone had given her permission for full publication so she supposed it wasn’t really an invasion of privacy to let Malfoy have a look before any publishers. That didn’t make it any less curious. “Why?”
赫敏犹豫了一下，低头看了一眼桌上的其他一堆作业。每个人都允许她完整地出版，所以她认为让马尔福在任何出版商之前看一看并不是真的侵犯隐私。这并没有减少它的好奇心。“为什么？”

“Do I need a reason?”
“我需要理由吗？”

“I suppose not, it’s just—”
“我想不是，只是——”

“Might I remind you whose home you are in?” Malfoy asked, his voice light but his eyes sharp. “I was merely asking out of politeness.”
“我能提醒你你在谁家吗？”马尔福问道，他的声音很轻，但眼神很锐利。“我只是出于礼貌而问。”

“Oh, alright,” Hermione snapped. “Pick one.”
“哦，好吧，”赫敏厉声说。“选一个。”

Rising to his feet, he set his tea down on the tray and selected a folder at random. With it in hand, he lowered himself back down into the chair, crossed one leg over the other and flipped the folder open. The purple sticker just visible on the cover identified it as Neville’s folder. 
他站起来，把茶放在托盘上，随意选了一个文件夹。拿着它，他把自己放回椅子上，一条腿交叉在另一条腿上，翻开了文件夹。封面上刚好可见的紫色贴纸表明这是 Neville 的文件夹。

“You’re going to sit here and do it?” 
“你要坐在这里做这件事吗？”

He glanced up from his reading and raised an eyebrow. “I wouldn’t like to take your things away from you. Besides." He gestured to the table with a lazy twirl of his fingers. "I’m sure there is some kind of order here even if it is difficult to identify.”
他从阅读中抬起头来，扬起了眉毛。“我不想把你的东西从你身边拿走。此外。他懒洋洋地转动着手指，指着桌子。“我敢肯定这里有某种秩序，即使很难识别。”

Rolling her eyes, Hermione waved a hand telling him to carry on and turned back to her own work, not missing his victorious smirk as she did so. 
赫敏翻了个白眼，挥了挥手，让他继续，然后转身回到自己的工作中，没有错过他胜利的笑容。

For a time, he read quietly while Hermione scoured Sprout’s interview, marking out pertinent sections. Technically, she supposed, he was a quiet, well-behaved library companion but she couldn’t help but be very aware of him. Usually there was a desk between them, for one thing. When she found herself glancing at him out of the corner of her eye for the sixth or seventh time, Hermione sighed with frustration.
有一段时间，他静静地阅读，而赫敏则翻阅着斯普劳特的采访，标出相关的部分。她想，从技术上讲，他是一个安静、乖巧的图书馆伙伴，但她忍不住非常了解他。一方面，他们之间通常有一张桌子。当她发现自己第六次或第七次用眼角的余光瞥了他一眼时，赫敏沮丧地叹了口气。

“Mr Malfoy,” she said abruptly, setting her quill down so that she could turn to look at him, “can I ask you something?”
“马尔福先生，”她突然说，放下羽毛笔，让她可以转身看着他，“我能问你点什么吗？

He glanced up at her from under his brows, looking wary. “I’ve never been able to stop you before.”
他从眉毛下抬头瞥了她一眼，看起来很警惕。“我以前从来没有阻止过你。”

“Have you ever really spent time in the company of a Muggle-born?”
“你真的有没有和一个麻瓜出身的人在一起？”

“Miss Granger, I have been locked up in this manor for eight years, not my entire life. I would think it a great achievement not to encounter at least one of your kind in the course of living in our world.”
“格兰杰小姐，我已经被关在这个庄园里八年了，不是我这辈子。我认为在我们的世界生活中没有遇到至少一个同类是一种了不起的成就。

“No,” Hermione shook her head, “I don’t mean just being around us. I mean…like this.” She waved her hand back and forth between them and he looked at it askance, drawing back slightly. “Talking. Sitting together.”
“不，”赫敏摇摇头，“我不是说只在我们身边。我的意思是。。。就像这样。她在他们之间来回挥舞着手，他疑惑地看着它，微微缩回去。“说话。坐在一起。

Slowly, he closed the folder to give her his full attention but he kept his place in it with his forefinger. “I have never needed to.”
他慢慢地合上文件夹，全神贯注地关注她，但他用食指保持着自己的位置。“我从来不需要。”

“You don’t really need to now,” Hermione pointed out.
“你现在真的不需要，”赫敏指出。

“No.”
“不。”

There was a beat of silence in which they assessed one another, both absorbing the strange shift towards stilted civility that was taking place. 
他们一阵沉默，互相打量着彼此，都吸收了正在发生的奇怪的转向生硬的礼貌。

“It’s not so bad, is it?” Hermione asked, a small smile quivering at the corners of her mouth.

“Thank you!” Hermione cried, her arm reaching across the table to gesture gratefully at Harry. “Anyway, I called it after that. I wasn’t particularly in the mood to talk anymore.”
“谢谢你！”赫敏喊道，她的手臂伸过桌子，感激地向哈利打了个手势。“不管怎样，我在那之后叫了它。我不是特别想再说话了。

Ginny patted Hermione’s other hand sympathetically from across the table. “I think maybe you’re just not meant to date Ravenclaws,” she said with her best ‘I’m being kind’ voice. “It’s a lot of desire to be right in one relationship. Maybe a nice, agreeable Hufflepuff next time.”
金妮从桌子对面同情地拍了拍赫敏的另一只手。“我想也许你只是不适合和拉文克劳约会，”她用她最好的“我是好心的”声音说。“在一段关系中，人们非常渴望正确。也许下次会是一个不错的、和蔼可亲的赫奇帕奇。

“You can have Hannah if you want,” Ron muttered. “Maybe you’d be able to browbeat her into staying.”
“如果你愿意，你可以拥有汉娜，”罗恩咕哝道。“也许你能劝她留下来。”

“I don’t browbeat people,” Hermione said, pulling her hand from under Ginny’s to cross her arms. 
“我不会责怪别人，”赫敏说，从金妮的手下抽出来，交叉着她的手臂。

“Sure you don’t,” Ginny said happily. 
“你当然不知道，”金妮高兴地说。

“I think I’d be wary of anyone that tries to defend love potions anyway,” said Harry as he picked up his wine. “Probably a good call, Hermione.” 
“我想无论如何我都会警惕任何试图为爱情魔药辩护的人，”哈利拿起他的酒说。“也许是个好主意，赫敏。”

“They’re good sellers, you know,” Ron grumbled, his ears turning red. “I mean, I’d never use one but—”
“他们很畅销，你知道的，”罗恩抱怨道，他的耳朵变得通红。“我是说，我永远不会用，但是——”

“Besides,” Ginny interrupted, rolling her eyes at Ron, “didn’t Luna say Terry only thinks he likes girls that are more clever than him? You need a man that knows he likes clever girls.” Ginny nodded sagely at Hermione, then at Harry who nodded back. “He is out there.”
“再说了，”金妮打断了她，对罗恩翻了个白眼，“卢娜不是说过特里只觉得他喜欢比他聪明的女孩吗？你需要一个知道他喜欢聪明女孩的男人。金妮睿智地向赫敏点了点头，然后又向哈利点了点头。“他在外面。”

“Somewhere,” added Harry with a wavering, mystical voice like Professor Trelawney and a distant look on his face that made Ron and Ginny laugh uproariously. 
“在某个地方，”哈利补充道，他的声音像特里劳尼教授一样摇摆不定，神秘得脸上带着遥远的表情，这让罗恩和金妮大笑起来。

“You’re all prats,” Hermione said, her arms still crossed but a wide grin spreading over her face.
“你们都是小子，”赫敏说，她的手臂仍然交叉着，但脸上却露出了灿烂的笑容。

“Speaking of prats: how are the Malfoys?” Ron asked through a mouthful of mash. 
“说到小子：马尔福家怎么样？”罗恩一口泥问道。

“Oh, she’s stopped going there,” Ginny said with an assured smile which dimmed on seeing Hermione's responding grimace. “You have stopped going there?” 
“哦，她已经不去了那里，”金妮带着自信的笑容说，但看到赫敏回应的鬼脸，笑容变得黯淡了。“你已经不去那里了？”

Hermione didn’t reply, her lips pressed tight and Ginny made a frustrated noise in the back of her throat. “You went back ? After the argument you had?”
赫敏没有回答，她的嘴唇紧紧地抿着，金妮的喉咙后部发出了沮丧的声音。“你回去了？在你吵架之后？

“Argument?” asked Harry, sitting up straighter. 
“争论？” 哈利问道，坐直了身子。

“We had an argument,” Hermione said, waving her hand dismissively. “It’s over now; the interviews are back on.”
“我们吵架了，”赫敏说，不屑地挥了挥手。“现在已经结束了;采访又开始了。

“Argument about what?” Harry was frowning, worried and looking from Hermione to Ginny. Hermione got the feeling he was going to have a stern word with Ginny about sharing everything with him. He had once told her that gossip was one of the pillars of marriage and she fully believed him.
“争论什么？”哈利皱着眉头，担心着，从赫敏看向金妮。赫敏有一种感觉，他要和金妮说一句严厉的话，要把一切都分享给他。他曾经告诉她，八卦是婚姻的支柱之一，她完全相信他。

“She wouldn’t tell me,” Ginny said, shrugging. “Such a non-story. Had her furious, whatever it was, mind.” 
“她不会告诉我的，”金妮耸耸肩说。“真是个没故事。让她生气，不管是什么。

“We just, you know, had an argument,” Hermione said, raising her hands in the air in a ‘who cares’ way. “We’re very different people so it’s bound to happen. It’s fine now.”
“我们刚刚，你知道的，吵了一架，”赫敏说，以一种“谁在乎”的方式将双手举向空中。“我们是非常不同的人，所以这肯定会发生。现在没事了。

“What, so, Daddy Malfoy has suddenly stopped being mean?” asked Ginny doubtfully. 
“什么，所以，马尔福爸爸突然不再刻薄了？”

“ Don’t call him ‘Daddy Malfoy’, Ginny,” Ron said with an exasperated sigh.
“别叫他'马尔福爸爸'，金妮，”罗恩恼怒地叹了口气。

“What? He is Malfoy’s dad. And he’s a Malfoy. Ergo, Daddy Malfoy.”
“什么？他是马尔福的爸爸。而且他是马尔福。呃，马尔福爸爸。

“Yeah, but it’s just a bit—”
“是啊，但只是有点——”

“Mr Malfoy is co-operating,” Hermione said, her tone broaching no further argument. “That’s all I need from him. Today he was actually fairly—”
“马尔福先生在合作，”赫敏说，她的语气没有进一步的争论。“这就是我从他那里需要的。今天他其实还算——”

“Today?” Harry asked, voice lilting with surprise. “I thought you met on Thursdays.”
“今天？”哈利问道，声音里带着惊讶。“我以为你在星期四见面。”

“Okay, Mr Auror," Hermione said with a sidelong look at Harry. "He came into the library while I was working.” 
“好的，傲罗先生，”赫敏侧头看了哈利一眼。“他在我工作的时候进了图书馆。”

“To…” Ginny said, rolling her hand in a circle to encourage explanation.
“去......”金妮说，用手转圈鼓励解释。

“To make sure I got the tea he asked his house elf to bring me.”
“为了确保我喝到茶，他让他的家养小精灵带我来。”

“What the fuck is going on in that house?” asked Ron, his tone equal parts horrified and mystified. 
“那他妈的房子里怎么了？” 罗恩问道，他的语气既惊恐又困惑。

“Did he, like, pour it on you?” Ginny asked, peeking under the table as though looking for burns on Hermione’s legs.
“他有没有，比如，把酒倒在你身上？”金妮问道，一边偷看桌子底下，好像在寻找赫敏腿上的烧伤。

“What? No!” Hermione shook her head, laughter bubbling up. “It was just polite, I’m sure. And probably to keep me in the library and out of his kitchen.”
“什么？不！赫敏摇摇头，笑声不断涌现。“我敢肯定，这只是礼貌。可能是为了让我留在图书馆和他的厨房里。

“Right,” Ron said, giving Hermione a sidelong look that made her hit back with a perfected ‘oh shut up’ look of her own. “Watch your back Hermione.”
“好吧，”罗恩说，侧头看了赫敏一眼，让她用自己完美的“哦，闭嘴”的表情回击。“小心你的背影，赫敏。”

“What do you think he’s going to do, hospitality me to death?”
“你觉得他会怎么做，把我款待得死去活来？”

“Wouldn’t put it past him to try. Dobby almost saved Harry to death, didn't he. Maybe he learned a few things about that from his master at the time.”
“不会让他尝试。多比差点把哈利救死了，不是吗。也许他当时从他的师父那里学到了一些东西。

Hermione looked at Harry disbelievingly, inviting him to interject and decry the idiocy of Ron’s theory, but he merely shrugged. 
赫敏难以置信地看着哈利，邀请他插嘴，谴责罗恩的理论是愚蠢的，但他只是耸了耸肩。

“Let’s move on,” she said, pinching the bridge of her nose, “shall we?”
“我们继续吧，”她捏着鼻梁说，“好吗？
