June 8th
6月8日

Lucius stood with his hands on his hips, eyeing the gnarled Snargaluff stump apprehensively. It wasn't really a one man job and he knew it. 
卢修斯双手叉腰站着，忧心忡忡地盯着那根多节的斯纳加洛夫树桩。这并不是一个人的工作，他知道这一点。

He supposed he could call Draco but it was such a pointless musing because he wasn’t going to. Draco was probably only still living in the manor because of him, he would not ask him for more. Certainly, it was Draco who needed the Snargaluff pod for his potion but that was even less reason to ask him. He could do things for his son alone .
他以为他可以给德拉科打电话，但那是毫无意义的沉思，因为他不打算这样做。德拉科可能只是因为他才还住在庄园里，他不会再向他要求更多了。当然，是德拉科需要斯纳加洛夫胶囊来装他的药水，但那更不是问他的理由。他可以独自为儿子做事。

Hooking the collar of his shirt with his finger, Lucius tugged at it to allow some air to circulate around his neck. The sun was pressing against the glass panes of the greenhouse, creating an oppressive heat. He'd spent the entire morning in it doing various jobs and he was starting to wish he hadn't left this particular one for last.
卢修斯用手指勾住衬衫的领子，拉扯它，让一些空气在他的脖子上循环。阳光压在温室的玻璃板上，产生一种闷热的热量。他花了一整个上午的时间在里面做各种工作，他开始希望自己没有把这个特别的工作留到最后。

Lucius was so lost in thought, he didn't hear the rustles and murmurs of a person approaching him through the greenhouse. Nor did he see Hermione duck under a large, overhanging leaf to his left and stop suddenly at the sight of him.
卢修斯陷入了沉思，他没有听到一个人从温室里向他走来的沙沙声和低语声。他也没有看到赫敏躲在他左边一片悬垂的大叶子下，一看到他就突然停了下来。

"Do not tell me you're going to try and tackle that on your own."
“别告诉我你要自己去搞定。”

Rolling his eyes, Lucius turned his head and saw that, as he had thought, the gratingly familiar voice did indeed belong to Granger. She was standing with her arms crossed, leaning her weight on one leg so that her hip jutted out. 
卢修斯翻了个白眼，转过头来，发现正如他所想的那样，那个熟悉的嗓音确实属于格兰杰。她双臂交叉站着，将体重靠在一条腿上，使臀部突出。

“And what if I am?”
“如果我是呢？”

“Then you're an idiot who deserves the thorny vine to the face that he's inevitably going to get.”
“那你就是个白痴，活该被荆棘藤打脸，他不可避免地会得到。”

Lucius tutted and turned to face her fully. “What are you doing here?”
卢修斯啧了一声，转过身来完全面对她。“你在这里做什么？”

Straightening up and uncrossing her arms, Hermione held up her wrist and jabbed a finger at the watch she was wearing. “Meeting time. You're late and I was told I'd find you here.” 
赫敏直起身来，松开双臂，举起手腕，用手指戳了戳她戴着的手表。“见面时间。你迟到了，我听说我会在这里找到你。

“By?” Lucius asked, his voice low and angry.
“靠？”卢修斯问道，他的声音低沉而愤怒。

“None of your business,” Hermione said primly, clasping her hands behind her back as she rose up briefly on her toes.
“不关你的事，”赫敏一本正经地说，双手紧握在背后，踮起脚尖短暂地站了起来。

Letty, he thought venomously. That house elf was the bane of his life. Well, actually, Granger was the bane of his life but the elf was clearly determined to assist her in that through her sheer inability to deny the girl anything.
莱蒂，他恶毒地想。那个家养小精灵是他一生的祸根。嗯，实际上，格兰杰是他生命中的克星，但这个精灵显然决心通过她完全无法否认这个女孩的任何事情来帮助他们。

“Nice apron, by the way.”
“顺便说一句，漂亮的围裙。”

Lucius dropped his head so that his chin almost touched his chest and squeezed the bridge of his nose between his thumb and forefinger. “Miss Granger, you are…” He sighed and shook his head, lifting it to look at her again. “Return to the manor. Now. I will meet you in my study shortly. And don’t touch anything while you’re in there.”
卢修斯低下头，下巴几乎碰到他的胸口，用拇指和食指挤压着他的鼻梁。“格兰杰小姐，你是......”他叹了口气，摇了摇头，抬起头再次看着她。“回到庄园去。现在。我很快就会在我的书房里见到你。你在里面的时候不要碰任何东西。

No longer interested in her, Lucius turned away dismissively but from the corner of his eyes he could see she still hadn’t moved. 
卢修斯不再对她感兴趣，轻蔑地转过身去，但从他的眼角余光中，他可以看到她仍然没有动。

“I'm not leaving you if you're going to try to deal with that thing on your own,” she said.
“如果你打算尝试自己处理那件事，我不会离开你，”她说。

“Fine,” he snapped, barely turning his head in her direction. “I'm not. Now leave.”
“好吧，”他厉声说，勉强把头转向她的方向。“我没有。现在走吧。”

“That was so unconvincing, I now think this might be a cry for help.”
“这太没有说服力了，我现在认为这可能是一个求救。”

“Miss Granger —”
“格兰杰小姐——”

“Oh, I'm kidding .” Hermione dropped her bag onto the floor and walked towards him, shrugging off her light cardigan as she went to reveal a thin-strapped top beneath. “I'll help you,” she said, shoving the cardigan into an empty compartment beneath the table. She peered around the wooden surface and then up at him. “No other aprons?”
“哦，我在开玩笑。”赫敏把包丢在地上，向他走来，耸了耸肩，脱掉了她的轻便开衫，露出了下面的一件细带上衣。“我来帮你，”她说，把羊毛衫塞进桌子下面的一个空隔间里。她环顾着木头表面，然后抬头看向他。“没有别的围裙吗？”

“I don’t like other people being here.”
“我不喜欢其他人在这里。”

“Clearly,” she said, not taking his hint. Instead she shook her hair over her shoulders and placed her hands on her hips in the manner of a woman ready for a challenge. “Right, who's doing what?”
“显然，”她说，没有接受他的暗示。相反，她把头发甩到肩膀上，双手放在臀部上，就像一个准备好迎接挑战的女人一样。“对，谁在做什么？”

“You are returning to the manor and I am dealing with this.” 
“你要回庄园去了，我正在处理这件事。”

“Sure, okay." She was nodding her head like she had listened. She had not. "So, you deal with the vines and I'll stick my arm in?” She raised a hand and wriggled her fingers at him. “I think mine are smaller.”
“当然，好吧。”她点点头，就像她听了一样。她没有。“所以，你处理藤蔓，我就把我的胳膊伸进去？”她抬起一只手，朝他扭动着手指。“我觉得我的更小。”

“You are utterly impossible,” he snapped. Granger was a dangerous catalyst for the steady smouldering of his patience that had been taking place in the heat. A combustion was liable to take place in her presence. 
“你完全不可能，”他厉声说。格兰杰是一个危险的催化剂，导致他在高温下不断的耐心。在她面前很容易发生燃烧。

“High praise from the current most impossible person in this greenhouse.” Audible aggravation was beginning to creep into her voice.
“来自这个温室里目前最不可能的人的高度赞扬。”她的声音里开始传来一丝恼怒。

Hermione sighed sharply and tilted her head, her shiny curls falling back over her shoulder. “Mr Malfoy, just let me help. I won’t tell anyone. Besides, the sooner we do this, the sooner we do the interview, and the sooner I am out of your hair for another week.” 
赫敏猛地叹了口气，歪了歪头，她闪亮的卷发垂在肩膀上。“马尔福先生，让我来帮忙。我不会告诉任何人。再说了，我们越早做这件事，我们就越早做采访，我就越早离开你的头发再过一个星期。

He contemplated her set jaw and gleaming eyes and came to the rather depressing realisation that there was going to be no arguing with her. Particularly because she was actually right. It would only end badly for him if he did it alone and the visible results of that would be more embarrassing than allowing her to help him in secret. 
他凝视着她坚定的下巴和闪闪发光的眼睛，然后相当沮丧地意识到，不会再和她争论了。特别是因为她实际上是对的。如果他一个人做这件事，对他来说只会很糟糕，而这样做的明显结果比让她偷偷帮助他更尴尬。

“Fine,” he snapped. “Come here.” 
“好吧，”他厉声说。“过来。”

Hands still clasped behind her back, Hermione got even closer, closing the gap between them in two large steps to stand directly beside him. 
双手仍然紧握在背后，赫敏靠得更近了，用两大步缩小了他们之间的差距，直接站在了他身边。

“Do you agree with me?” she asked. “I'll get the pod? You're taller so stand behind me, just to the side, and grab the vines. Tying them—”
“你同意我的看法吗？”“我来拿豆荚？你个子高，所以站在我身后，就靠一边，抓住藤蔓。把他们绑起来——”

“In a knot is best. Yes, Miss Granger, I too attended sixth year Herbology classes.” He had never met anyone quite so bossy in his life.
“打结是最好的。是的，格兰杰小姐，我也上过六年级的草药学课。他这辈子从来没有见过这么专横的人。

Hermione blushed and shrugged. “It helps to talk things through out loud. “
赫敏脸红了，耸了耸肩。“大声说出来很有帮助。”

“Perhaps it helps you," he said, glaring down at her from the corner of his eyes. "It gives me a headache”. 
“也许这对你有帮助，”他说，用眼角的余光低头瞪着她。“这让我很头疼。”

“I'm sure lots of things give you a headache.” She looked up at him with a sarcastic smile.
“我敢肯定，很多事情都会让你头疼。”她抬头看着他，露出讽刺的笑容。

“Yes." He turned his head towards her to make his glare more pointed.
“是的。”他把头转向她，使他的目光更加尖锐。

Without even a moment of hesitation, Hermione slipped from her place beside him to move even closer, stopping just in front of him. 
赫敏没有片刻的犹豫，从他身边的位置滑了下来，进一步靠近，停在了他的面前。

Not expecting her to move so quickly, Lucius hesitated and fell back, looking down at the top of her head as though it was an ancient rune he'd never encountered. She was smaller than he’d initially thought – she moved through the world with the ferocity of someone twice her height.
没想到她动作这么快，卢修斯犹豫了一下，向后退去，低头看着她的头顶，仿佛那是他从未见过的古老符文。她比他最初想象的要小——她以两倍于她身高的人的凶猛穿越世界。

Collecting himself and moving forward to assume the position she had suggested – demanded – Lucius inhaled deeply in an effort to get a handle on his temper only to find himself taking in an unexpectedly sweet and floral scent. He wrinkled his nose. Was that…her? Given ordinary flowers weren’t something he kept in the greenhouse, it could only be. He looked down at her head again, frowning slightly. Such a delicately feminine scent didn't strike him as fitting for a harridan.
卢修斯镇定下来，向前走去，采取她建议——要求——的姿势，他深深地吸了一口气，试图控制住自己的脾气，却发现自己吸入了一股出乎意料的甜美和花香。他皱了皱鼻子。那是......她？鉴于普通的花不是他放在温室里的东西，那只能是。他又低头看了看她的头，微微皱起眉头。如此淡淡的女性气味让他觉得自己并不适合 harridan。

He'd been close to her but never for long enough to actually look . He was close enough to see the blonde in her curls, the faint constellation of freckles that spanned her shoulders, and a purple-ish mark that cut through the middle of them. The shape of it suggested it had been left behind by her heavy satchel. He vaguely wondered, with a contemplative tilt of his head, if it was painful, even if he didn't really care if it was.
他一直靠近她，但从来没有足够长的时间真正去看。他离得足够近，可以看到她卷发中的金发女郎，她肩膀上淡淡的雀斑群，以及从它们中间划出的紫色印记。它的形状表明它是她沉重的背包留下的。他隐约地想着，沉思地歪着头，这是否痛苦，即使他并不真的在乎是不是。

“Ready?” she asked, turning to look at him over her shoulder and drawing him out of his own head. She wasn’t perturbed by his proximity at all. So why was he?
“准备好了吗？”她问道，转身看着他，把他从自己的脑海里拉了出来。她一点也不因为他的靠近而感到不安。那么他为什么呢？

Blinking once, slowly, Lucius realised her nose had a slight upturn to it. It was smattered with freckles similar to the ones on her shoulders. Like someone had flicked her with a paintbrush.
Lucius缓缓地眨了眨眼，意识到她的鼻子微微上扬。它上面散布着类似于她肩膀上的雀斑。就像有人用画笔弹了她一样。

It had never occurred to him that Granger had…details. Then again, one didn't usually look for details in an effigy.
他从来没有想过格兰杰已经......详。话又说回来，人们通常不会在肖像中寻找细节。

Malfoy cleared his throat as she raised her eyebrows expectantly, realising he hadn't responded to her question. “I feel I should warn you, Miss Granger, that this Snargaluff recently suffered a cold, so I wouldn't linger in there.”
马尔福清了清嗓子，她期待地扬起眉毛，意识到他没有回答她的问题。“我觉得我应该警告你，格兰杰小姐，这个斯纳加洛夫最近感冒了，所以我不会在那儿逗留。”

“Interesting,” she turned back, leaning her elbows on the table and bending forwards on her tiptoes to peer more closely at the dormant stump. Looking back over her shoulder at him, she added, “I didn’t know they could get colds. What happens?”
“有意思，”她转过身来，将手肘靠在桌子上，踮起脚尖向前弯腰，更仔细地观察着休眠的树桩。她回头看着他，补充道，“我不知道他们会感冒。会发生什么事？

“They become more sensitive to intrusion,” Lucius replied, taking a subtle half-step back from her to establish a more appropriate distance between himself and her new position. 
“他们对侵入变得更加敏感，”卢修斯回答道，巧妙地从她身边后退了半步，在他和她的新位置之间建立了更合适的距离。

Hoping they could just get on with it and get her out of his way, he lifted some gloves from the pocket of his apron and put them on, drawing Hermione’s attention. 
希望他们能继续下去，让她离开他，他从围裙的口袋里掏出一些手套戴上，引起了赫敏的注意。

“Don’t suppose you’ve got any of those spare?” she asked, straightening up to turn around.
“你觉得你没有多余的吗？” 她问道，直起身来转身。

He shook his head and she sighed. “ Goggles , at least?”
他摇摇头，她叹了口气。“至少是护目镜？”

This time he was able to help and drew two sets from the pocket of his apron. The Venomous Tentacula had a penchant for stealing them so spares were necessary. Hermione snatched a pair from his hand, quite strongly reminding him of said plant, and put them on her face. 
这一次他能够提供帮助，从围裙的口袋里抽出两套。Venomous Tentacula 喜欢偷走它们，所以备用的是必不可少的。赫敏从他手里抢过一双，非常强烈地让他想起了那种植物，然后把它们戴在她的脸上。

“I feel so safe,” she said drily. “You should really make this greenhouse more helper friendly, you know.”
“我感觉很安全，”她冷淡地说。“你知道的，你真的应该让这个温室对帮手更友好。”

“You are not making a good case for that,” he murmured. 
“你没有提出一个很好的理由，”他喃喃自语道。

Rolling her eyes, Hermione turned back around and asked him if he was ready. He replied in the affirmative and she reached for the stump which immediately sprang to life. 
赫敏翻了个白眼，转过身来问他准备好了吗。“他回答说是肯定的，她伸手去摸树桩，树桩立刻就活了起来。

The thorny vines moved quickly, viciously, but Lucius grabbed as many as he could in each hand, knotting them together with enough force that the Snargaluff reluctantly opened. 
带刺的藤蔓快速而恶狠狠地移动着，但卢修斯用每只手都抓住了尽可能多的藤蔓，用足够的力气将它们打结在一起，以至于斯纳加洛夫不情愿地打开了。

Without any hesitation, Hermione rose onto her tiptoes and shoved her arm into it up to the elbow, just as Lucius stopped another vine from knotting itself in her hair. 
赫敏毫不犹豫地踮起脚尖，把她的手臂塞进去，一直到肘部，就在卢修斯阻止另一根藤蔓在她的头发上打结的时候。

“Do try to hurry up, Miss Granger. I told you not to linger,” Lucius grunted as a vine wrapped itself around his hand and attempted to tug at his glove. His forearms were covered in tiny cuts and he didn’t relish the idea of the same happening below his wrist. 
“快点吧，格兰杰小姐。我告诉过你不要逗留，“卢修斯咕哝着，一根藤蔓缠住了他的手，试图拉扯他的手套。他的前臂上布满了细小的伤口，他不喜欢手腕以下发生同样的事情。

“I’m trying,” Hermione said, her voice strained as she pulled at something within the stump. “It’s stuck.”
“我在努力，”赫敏说，她的声音在拉扯树桩里的某个东西时变得紧张。“它卡住了。”

“It can’t be stuck it—”
“不能卡住——”

Hermione yelped and managed to wrench her arm free, her shoulder smacking against Lucius' chest hard enough to knock the air out of him. 
赫敏大喊着，设法把她的手臂扭开，她的肩膀狠狠地撞在卢修斯的胸口上，足以把他的空气打得喘不过气来。

Just as she lifted the pulsing green pod on her hand with a triumphant 'ha!', the Snargaluff made an ominous retching sound. 
就在她得意洋洋地“哈”一声举起手上跳动的绿色豆荚时，斯纳加洛夫发出了不祥的干呕声。

Instinctively, Lucius leapt to the side, narrowly managing to avoid the splatter of green mucus which erupted from the centre of the Snargaluff. 
卢修斯本能地跳到一边，勉强躲过了从 Snargaluff 中心喷出的绿色粘液飞溅。

Hermione was less lucky; it went up her right arm, over her shoulder and into the ends of her hair. The Snargaluff coughed in a satisfied way and its vines immediately retracted, leaving it looking like a harmless, dead stump once more. 
赫敏就没那么幸运了;它沿着她的右臂，越过她的肩膀，一直到她的发梢。斯纳加洛夫满意地咳嗽着，它的藤蔓立即缩回，让它看起来又像一个无害的死树桩。

“ Ugh! ” Hermione cried, dropping the pod into the waiting bowl with a clatter and looking down at her mucus covered arm. 
“呃！”赫敏喊道，咔嚓一声把豆荚扔进等待的碗里，低头看着她沾满粘液的手臂。

Lucius raised a hand to his mouth but it did nothing to conceal the growing smile there. Oh, it was too perfect.
卢修斯抬起一只手捂住嘴巴，但这丝毫没有掩盖他脸上日益增长的笑容。哦，这太完美了。

Hermione looked over at him and, seeing the tell-tale crinkling of his eyes and the shake of his shoulders, her eyes narrowed. 
赫敏看着他，看到他眼中明显的皱纹和肩膀的颤抖，她的眼睛眯了起来。

“Don’t you dare,” she snapped. “Or I’ll—” 
“你不敢，”她厉声说。“或者我就——”

She raised her arm threateningly and when he realised she was preparing to fling some of the mucus in his direction he took a swift step back, his amusement snuffing out with the ease of a candle.
她威胁地举起手臂，当他意识到她正准备向他的方向扔一些粘液时，他迅速后退了一步，他的乐趣就像蜡烛一样轻松地熄灭了。

“Don’t you dare,” he growled, pointing a finger in warning. “You wanted to help, that’s what you get.”
“你不敢，”他咆哮着，用手指警告道。“你想帮忙，这就是你得到的。”

“Mucus,” Hermione said blankly, lowering her arm so that some of the mucus dripped from her fingertips onto the floor. “I get mucus for helping. You’re twisted .” 
“粘液，”赫敏茫然地说，放下手臂，让一些粘液从她的指尖滴到地板上。“我帮忙会沾满粘液。你被扭曲了。

He shrugged, not particularly inclined to disagree, and she sighed deeply, her attention drawn back to her arm. “Look, just…just pass me my wand from my bag, will you?”
他耸了耸肩，并没有特别不同意，她深深地叹了口气，她的注意力又回到了她的手臂上。“你看，只是......你就把我包里的魔杖递给我吧，好吗？

Lucius looked down in the direction she’d indicated and saw he was standing beside her satchel. Her wand was sticking out of the side so he bent down, still with a wary eye on her in case of a mucus missile, and lifted the wand. 
卢修斯低头看向她所指的方向，发现他正站在她的书包旁边。她的魔杖从侧面伸出来，所以他弯下腰，仍然警惕地看着她，以防被粘液导弹击中，然后举起了魔杖。

As soon as his fingers made contact with the smooth wood, there was a swift swoop in his stomach. It was familiar and strange, thrilling and dread-inducing. The Magic Dampener hummed threateningly around his ankle. 
当他的手指接触到光滑的木头时，他的胃里迅速地猛扑过来。它既熟悉又陌生，既惊心动魄又令人恐惧。魔法阻尼器在他的脚踝上发出威胁性的哼唱。

Gripping the wand tighter, Lucius took a sharp intake of breath as a rush of… something went up his arm, while the Magic Dampener pulsed warningly around his leg, growing unbearably hot. Taken together, the sensations crossed pleasure and pain, making him feel light-headed and physically sick. 
卢修斯把魔杖握得更紧了，猛地吸了一口气......有什么东西顺着他的手臂爬上去，而魔法阻尼器在他的腿上警告性地跳动着，变得热得难以忍受。总而言之，这些感觉跨越了快乐和痛苦，使他感到头晕目眩，身体不适。

Spying a look of alarm from Hermione, he remembered that he was holding her wand. The Magic Dampener squeezed, moving beyond threat of pain to the real thing and he hurriedly threw the wand at her like it had grown white hot. On his loss of contact with the wand, the Magic Dampener stilled and died, leaving a warm, pulsing pain to linger in his leg. 
他偷偷地从赫敏那里看到警惕的眼神，想起他正拿着她的魔杖。魔法阻尼器挤压着，超越了痛苦的威胁，变成了真正的东西，他急忙将魔杖扔向她，就像它已经变得白热一样。在他失去与魔杖的接触后，魔法阻尼器静止并死去，留下一种温暖的、搏动的疼痛在他的腿上挥之不去。

Hermione rose from her haunches, having been forced to pick up the wand, giving him a discomfited look. He wondered what his face must look like. It had all been but the work of a few seconds and yet he was breathing heavily like he’d run a long distance.
赫敏从她的臀部站起来，被迫拿起魔杖，不安地看了他一眼。他想知道自己的脸一定是什么样子。这一切都只是几秒钟的工作，但他却像跑了很长一段距离一样喘着粗气。

"Mr Malfoy, are…are you okay?"
“马尔福先生，是......你还好吗？

Lucius swallowed, flexing his hand to try and rid it of the curious, painful tingle dancing down his palm to his fingertips. “Fine," he said shortly, his throat dry. Lucius leaned his neck to one side and then the other, forcing it to crack. "Your wand, Miss Granger, what core does it use?”
卢修斯咽了口口水，弯曲他的手，试图摆脱从他的手掌到指尖跳动的奇怪、痛苦的刺痛感。“好吧，”他很快说，喉咙发干。卢修斯把脖子靠向一边，然后又靠向另一边，迫使它裂开。“你的魔杖，格兰杰小姐，它用的是什么芯子？”

“Dragon heartstring,” she said, eyes running over him apprehensively. Clearly satisfied he wasn't about to drop dead, she turned them to her arm to begin syphoning the mucus away.
“龙之心弦，”她说，眼睛忧虑地扫视着他。显然，她很满意他不会死去，于是把它们转向她的手臂，开始吸走粘液。

He hummed in response, clenching and unclenching his fist again. That had been the core of his wand, no doubt the source of the curious familiarity that he had felt when holding hers. 
他哼了一声作为回应，再次握紧又松开了拳头。那一直是他魔杖的核心，毫无疑问，这是他握着她的魔杖时感到奇怪的熟悉感的来源。

Once the mucus was gone, Hermione shoved her wand in her back pocket and hesitantly sniffed at her arm. “Oh for—” She sighed, and looked at him with pleading eyes. “Please tell me there’s a sink with some soap or something in here where I can wipe this down. It really doesn’t smell great.”
粘液消失后，赫敏把魔杖塞进后兜，犹豫地嗅了嗅她的手臂。“哦，因为——”她叹了口气，用恳求的眼神看着他。“请告诉我这里有一个水槽，里面有一些肥皂什么的，我可以在那里擦干净。它真的闻起来不太好闻。

Still occupied by the overwhelming sensation that had come with holding a wand after more than eight years, Lucius mumbled about there being a sink around the corner, pointing vaguely in the right direction. 
八年多后，卢修斯仍然被拿着魔杖带来的压倒性感觉所占据，他喃喃自语着拐角处有一个水槽，模糊地指出了正确的方向。

Hermione disappeared and once she had, Lucius rolled his ankle, feeling the weight of the Magic Dampener on his calf and the pulsing pain it had left behind. It rippled up to his knee and he winced.
赫敏消失了，她一消失，卢修斯就转动了他的脚踝，感受着魔法阻尼器在他小腿上的重量和它留下的搏动般的疼痛。它波及到他的膝盖，他畏缩了起来。

The Ministry had told him that the Magic Dampener would act if he appeared to be at risk of circumventing the terms of his imprisonment but he hadn't thought it would be quite so immediate. Or quite so painful.
魔法部告诉他，如果他看起来有规避监禁条件的风险，魔法阻尼器就会采取行动，但他没想到会这么快。或者说非常痛苦。

Really, he had only touched the wand. It wasn't even his . Lucius huffed and tugged at his collar again, this time undoing the top button.
真的，他只碰过魔杖。这甚至不是他的。卢修斯气喘吁吁地再次扯了扯他的衣领，这一次解开了顶部的纽扣。

The Ministry always did like its little cruelties, though. It revelled in its own inflexibility. He preferred when he wasn’t on this side of it. He felt drained and empty. Even vulnerable. He missed his magic more than ever. At the very least, this served to remind him why he put up with Granger—getting his wand back and getting the horrendous thing off . 
不过，魔法部总是喜欢它的小残酷。它陶醉于自己的僵化。他更喜欢自己不在这边的时候。他感到筋疲力尽，空虚。甚至脆弱。他比以往任何时候都更想念他的魔法。至少，这提醒了他为什么忍受格兰杰——拿回他的魔杖，把那个可怕的东西拿下来。

Grumbling, Lucius approached the Snargaluff pod, a slight limp in his step, and occupied himself with extracting the disgusting green tubers from within. 
卢修斯咕哝着走近斯纳加洛夫豆荚，脚步略微跛行，忙着从里面拔出那些令人作呕的绿色块茎。

Getting Granger’s help probably had been the right approach; certainly, it meant that he hadn’t had to take a faceful of Snargaluff mucus. Lucius snorted at the memory of her disgusted, angry face.
获得格兰杰的帮助可能是正确的方法;当然，这意味着他不必吃一脸 Snargaluff 的粘液。卢修斯想起她那张厌恶、愤怒的脸，哼了一声。

He couldn’t pretend he didn’t find a quiet kind of enjoyment in riling her up but having the plant do it for him was also satisfying. Low effort, high reward. She had a tendency to lash out when she was angry, to forget to moderate her tone. Witnessing it was cathartic in a way. The pink on her cheeks made him feel like he was having an impact on something, at least.
他不能假装自己在激怒她时没有找到一种安静的乐趣，但让植物为他做这件事也很令人满意。低努力，高回报。她生气时倾向于大发雷霆，忘记了缓和自己的语气。目睹这一切在某种程度上是一种宣泄。她脸颊上的粉红色让他觉得自己至少对什么产生了影响。

Frowning, Lucius looked up and then around him, turning on the spot. Granger was still gone. How long had she been gone? 
Lucius皱着眉头，抬头看了看，又环顾四周，当场转过身来。格兰杰还是走了。她走了多久了？

Wiping his hands on his apron, he hurriedly walked in the direction of the sink. The last thing he needed was for Granger to be throttled to death by his Venomous Tentacula. The Aurors would just jump straight to killing him. He was sure a few of them would seize on any minor excuse and Granger's death probably wouldn't be considered minor by most.
他用围裙擦了擦手，急忙朝水槽的方向走去。他最不需要的就是让格兰杰被他的毒触手掐死。傲罗们会直接跳起来杀了他。他确信他们中的一些人会抓住任何一个小借口，而格兰杰的死可能不会被大多数人认为是小事。

Rounding the corner, Lucius exhaled in relief as he heard the sound of running water and distracted humming. She was alive. Utterly incapable of carrying a tune but alive. Pushing an overhanging leaf to the side, his eyes landed on her and his purposeful stride stuttered and halted. Granger was standing at his sink, her back to him, wiping her shoulder down with a damp rag. 
绕过拐角，卢修斯听到流水的声音和分心的嗡嗡声，松了一口气。她还活着。完全无法承载一首曲子，但还活着。他把一片悬垂的叶子推到一边，目光落在她身上，他坚定的步伐结结巴巴地停了下来。格兰杰站在他的水槽旁，背对着他，用湿抹布擦着她的肩膀。

The strap of her top had been lowered to loop her arm, her hair draped over the opposite shoulder. She held the rag under the running water briefly and swiped it across the bar of lemon soap sitting by the tap before she scrubbed at her skin. 
她上衣的带子被放低以环绕她的手臂，她的头发垂在对面的肩膀上。她把抹布放在流水下短暂地滑过，在水龙头旁的柠檬皂上擦过，然后擦洗自己的皮肤。

Lucius frowned and politely looked to the side as she lifted the strap of her top back into place. 
卢修斯皱着眉头，礼貌地看向一边，同时将上衣的带子拉回原位。

It wasn’t really appropriate for him to be watching her when she didn’t know he was there. Admittedly, she was only wiping her shoulder –  hardly a salacious display – but it made him feel uncomfortable; like he was intruding on her privacy.
当她不知道他在那儿时，他看着她真的不太合适。诚然，她只是在擦她的肩膀——算不上什么淫秽的展示——但这让他感到不舒服;就像他侵犯了她的隐私一样。

He was opening his mouth to tell her to hurry up when she gathered the ends of her hair and bent at the waist over the sink to hold them under the water. 
他正张开嘴告诉她快点，这时她捡起发梢，弯下腰在水槽上把它们放在水下。

Lucius’ eyes drifted back over to her and trailed up the length of her legs to the wand that was sticking out the back pocket of her shorts. Slowly he closed his mouth, swallowing his words and struggling to find new ones.
卢修斯的目光又回到她身上，沿着她的双腿一直滑到从她短裤后袋伸出的魔杖上。他慢慢地闭上了嘴，吞下了他的话，努力寻找新的词。

Reaching up, she turned off the tap and straightened up, turning before Lucius could leave. As he came into her line of vision she started, backing up into the sink in her surprise. "Oh! Mr Malfoy, I was just–"
她伸手关掉了水龙头，直起身来，在Lucius离开之前转身。当他进入她的视线时，她开始了，惊讶地向水槽里倒退。“哦！马尔福先生，我只是——”

"Taking an eternity?" 
“需要永恒？”

"–finishing up." 
“——结束了。”

Hermione flushed with annoyance as she heard what he said. Her hair was still wet at the ends and Lucius spied droplets of water running over her clavicle, leaving a damp, glistening trail.
赫敏听到他说的话，恼火地涨红了脸。她的头发发梢仍然湿漉漉的，卢修斯发现水滴流过她的锁骨，留下了一条潮湿、闪闪发光的痕迹。

"I was gone for five minutes," she said. 
“我走了五分钟，”她说。

"Five minutes of my time," came his stiff response. "It's not yours to waste."
“我有五分钟的时间，”他生硬地回答。“这不是你的浪费。”

A disbelieving scoff escaped her mouth as she marched towards and then past him, returning in the direction of the work table. 
她不敢置信地嘲笑着，走向他，然后越过他，朝着工作台的方向走去。

"I hardly think you'd want me trailing Snargaluff mucus into your precious manor."
“我几乎不认为你会希望我拖着 Snargaluff 的粘液进入你珍贵的庄园。”

Lucius rolled his eyes and followed her, pulling his apron over his head and folding it as he went. It would be too easy to tell her that he’d rather have a thousand mucus-spitting Snargaluffs in his home than her. He was more creative than that. 
卢修斯翻了个白眼，跟着她，把围裙拉到头上，边走边折叠。告诉她他宁愿家里有一千个吐着粘液的 Snargaluffs，也不愿让她来，这太容易了。他比那更有创造力。

"Would you?" she asked over her shoulder, yanking her cardigan out from where she'd unceremoniously stuffed it in the workbench. 
“你愿意吗？”她转过头问道，从她毫不客气地塞在工作台上的地方扯出她的羊毛衫。

Lucius didn’t deign to answer as he pointedly, carefully placed his neatly folded apron back in its slot. 
卢修斯没有屈尊回答，他小心翼翼地将他折叠整齐的围裙放回了插槽中。

"Didn't think so," she said in response to his silence. 
“我不这么认为，”她回应他的沉默说。

Exhaling sharply through his nose, Lucius straightened up to ask her if she could, for once in her life, shut up when he spied the cardigan folded over her forearm. Two drops of water from the ends of her hair landed on it. The rest continued to glisten on her skin.
卢修斯从鼻子里猛地呼出一口气，直起身来问她，当他看到折叠在她前臂上的羊毛衫时，她是否可以闭嘴，这是她这辈子的第一次。两滴水从她的发梢落在上面。其余的继续在她的皮肤上闪闪发光。

“Aren’t you putting that on?”
“你不是戴上了吗？”

Hermione frowned, following the direction of his gaze before glancing up at him from under her brow. “Well, it’s warm in here and my hair is still a bit wet." She lifted a strand to show him. “So I'll just leave it for now.”
赫敏皱起眉头，顺着他的目光方向看去，然后从眉毛下抬头看了他一眼。“嗯，这里很暖和，我的头发还是有点湿。”她掀起一根绳子给他看。“所以我现在就先不说了。”

“Are you a witch or not?”
“你是不是女巫？”

Turning her head to eye him apprehensively, she said, “Er, yes?”
她转过头来，忧心忐忡地看着他，说：“呃，是吗？

“Then why can’t you just dry your hair with a spell?” he asked impatiently. Honestly, here he was standing here lamenting the loss of his magic and she wouldn't even use hers. She would rather stand there damp and half-dressed.
“那你为什么不能用咒语把头发吹干呢？”老实说，他站在这里哀叹失去了他的魔法，而她甚至不会使用她的魔法。她宁愿浑身湿漉漉、衣衫褴褛地站在那里。

“They all make it really frizzy.” Seeing his sceptical look she crossed her arms, folding the cardigan between them. “Yes, it can get frizzier.”
“他们都让它变得非常毛躁。”看到他怀疑的眼神，她交叉双臂，将开衫折叠起来。“是的，它会变得更毛躁。”

Lucius sighed and rolled his neck back to look up at the blue sky through the roof of the greenhouse. Nope, no patience up there either. “Try ‘Sericum’,” he muttered. 
卢修斯叹了口气，把脖子向后转，透过温室的屋顶仰望着蓝天。不，那里也没有耐心。“试试'Sericum'，”他咕哝道。

Hermione mouthed the word quizzically and shook her head. “I haven’t—”
赫敏疑惑地说了这个词，摇了摇头。“我没有——”

“It’s a drying charm,” he snapped, bringing his head back down. “Just try it.” 
“这是个干燥的咒语，”他厉声说，把头低了下来。“试试吧。”

Looking at him askance, Hermione slowly withdrew her wand from her back pocket and paused, the expectation of instruction clear on her face.
赫敏疑惑地看着他，慢慢地从后兜里掏出魔杖，停顿了一下，脸上露出对指示的期待。

“Drag the wand downwards in a smoothing motion as you say the spell,” he directed. “Like you’re brushing your hair.” 
“当你说出咒语时，以平滑的动作将魔杖向下拖动，”他指示道。“就像你在梳头一样。”

Following his guidance exactly, Hermione cast the spell and looked at the ends of her hair in wonder, her mouth slightly agape. Her curls were smooth and shiny, the blonde he'd noticed earlier running through them like melted caramel.
赫敏完全按照他的指引施展了咒语，惊奇地看着她的发梢，她的嘴巴微微张大。她的卷发光滑有光泽，他之前注意到的金发像融化的焦糖一样穿过它们。

“How did you—?” She cut herself off when she looked at him and he saw her eyes scan his hair. A small, knowing smile pulled at the corners of her lips. “Never mind.”
“你怎么——？”当她看着他时，她打断了自己，他看到她的眼睛扫视着他的头发。她的嘴角勾起一丝会心的微笑。“算了。”

Lucius grit his teeth, a muscle twitching in his jaw. “Do not share that spell.”
卢修斯咬紧牙关，下巴的肌肉抽搐着。“不要分享那个咒语。”

“Oh, I won’t,” Hermione said, her smile widening into a beaming grin as she pulled her cardigan back over her shoulders. “You can trust me, you know that. I'm discreet .” 
“哦，我不会的，”赫敏说，当她把开衫拉回肩膀上时，她的笑容灿烂成灿烂的笑容。“你可以相信我，你知道的。我很谨慎。

“Just get your bag, Miss Granger, and let’s go.”
“拿你的包吧，格兰杰小姐，我们走吧。”

“Who casts that spell for you now you can’t use your magic?” she asked slyly, pulling her bag up onto her shoulder. “Is it Draco?”
“现在你不能使用魔法了，谁为你施放了那个咒语？”她狡猾地问道，把包拉到肩上。“是德拉科吗？”

“Do shut up .”
“闭嘴。”

“Our last meeting didn’t go quite according to plan,” Hermione said once they were settled in his study in their usual places. The Wheezebox was recording and her Quick Quotes Quill was in motion. 
“我们上次的会议并没有完全按计划进行，”赫敏在他们平常的书房里安顿下来后说。Wheezebox 正在录音，她的 Quick Quotes Quill 正在移动。

“I believe you rather dominated the conversation as you are so wont to do," Lucius replied with a long-suffering expression.
“我相信你宁愿像你那样主导了谈话，”卢修斯用一种长期忍耐的表情回答。

“I said things you needed to hear.”
“我说了你需要听的话。”

“No, you said things you needed to say, Miss Granger. The difference is vast.”
“不，你说了你该说的话，格兰杰小姐。差异是巨大的。

Hermione drew in a deep breath, her shoulders rising, and then let it go slowly, placing her hands in her lap. 
赫敏深吸一口气，肩膀抬起，然后慢慢地放开，双手放在膝盖上。

“Are you struggling to breathe?” Lucius drawled, glancing uninterestedly down at his nails. "Because I should warn you, I don't think the mediwizards from St Mungo's would be tripping over themselves to get to this address. And I certainly won’t be helping."
“你呼吸困难吗？”卢修斯抽了抽身子，不感兴趣地低头瞥了一眼他的指甲。“因为我应该警告你，我不认为圣芒戈的医疗巫师会为了到达这个地址而绊倒自己。我当然不会帮忙。

“No,” she snapped. “I’m taking a moment before replying.”
“不，”她厉声说。“我先花点时间再回答。”

“Ah, so you are struggling for control . I don’t know why I didn’t come to that conclusion first.”
“啊，所以你在为控制权而挣扎。”我不知道为什么我没有先得出那个结论。

“Stop poking at me,” Hermione said, crossing her arms defensively. “I helped you today. The least you could do is not be such an…an arse .” 
“别戳我了，”赫敏说，防御性地交叉着双臂。“我今天帮了你。你至少能做的就是不要成为这样的......一个屁股。

“I did not ask for your help,” Lucius hissed, leaning forward and placing his arms on the desk. Her gaze flicked down to his forearms and she spied the small cuts that the Snargaluff had peppered along them. 
“我没有找你帮忙，”卢修斯嘶嘶地说道，身体前倾，双臂放在桌子上。她的目光扫向他的前臂，她注意到了斯纳加洛夫在他们身上留下的小伤口。

“Do you need some essence of Murtlap?” she asked, pointing. “For those. Which, might I add, would have been much worse had I not been there.”
“你需要一些 Murtlap 的精华吗？”“为了那些。我还要补充一点，如果我没有在那儿，情况会更糟。

“No,” he replied through gritted teeth. They stung but barely. He’d experienced far worse and he would never give her the satisfaction. 
“没有，”他咬牙切齿地回答。他们刺痛了，但几乎没有。他经历过更糟糕的事情，他永远不会给她满意。

“If anyone ever tries to tell me that I’m stubborn again, I will point them in your direction for an example of what that truly is.”
“如果有人试图告诉我我又很固执，我会给他们指出你的方向，让他们知道那到底是什么。”

“Just get on with it, Miss Granger.”
“继续吧，格兰杰小姐。”

“That’s what I was trying to—” Hermione broke off and lowered her head with her eyes closed. When she looked up a moment later he found her expression was unexpectedly serene. “What were you doing in the greenhouse anyway?”
“这就是我想要的——”赫敏打断了她的话，闭着眼睛低下了头。片刻后，当她抬起头时，他发现她的表情出乎意料地平静。“你到底在温室里做什么？”

“And this is relevant to where we left off…how?”
“这与我们上次中断的地方有关......怎么做到的？

“Just answer the question, Malfoy.”
“就回答这个问题吧，马尔福。”

His jaw jutted to the side and he lifted the tip of his tongue to the roof of his mouth as he leaned back in his chair. “I grow ingredients for Draco’s potions in the greenhouses. Herbology is one of the few ways I can still interact with magic as it so rarely requires a wand.”
他的下巴向一侧突出，他向后靠在椅子上，将舌尖抬到上颚。“我在温室里种植了 Draco 的魔药原料。草药学是我仍然可以与魔法互动的少数方式之一，因为它很少需要魔杖。

Hermione recalled Draco telling her that his father supported his potion making in his own way and nodded in understanding. “Don’t you think Draco should help you? Particularly in situations like that.”
赫敏记得德拉科告诉她，他爸爸以自己的方式支持他的魔药制作，并点头表示理解。“你不觉得德拉科应该帮你吗？尤其是在这样的情况下。

“I do not want him to,” Lucius said shortly. “Just as I did not want you to. Moving on, Miss Granger.”
“我不想让他这样做，”卢修斯很快说。“就像我不希望你这样做一样。继续前进，格兰杰小姐。

Hermione clamped her jaw tight and exhaled through her nose. “Right, so, from last time; you had left Hogwarts and you didn’t need to work so you were free to serve Voldemort. You rose through his ranks and I imagine he was pleased by the recruits that followed you out of the school?”
赫敏紧紧地夹住下巴，用鼻子呼气。“对，所以，从上次开始;你已经离开了霍格沃茨，你不需要工作，所以你可以自由地为伏地魔服务。你是一路升迁的，我想他对那些跟着你走出学校的新兵感到高兴吧？

“Yes.”
“是的。”

“I sometimes wonder: were you all there for the same reasons? Did everyone believe like you?”
“我有时在想：你们都是出于同样的原因吗？大家都像你一样相信吗？

“We did not often discuss our motivations, Miss Granger. In the earliest days we were barely allowed to speak without the Dark Lord present and our masks made it hard to be certain about the identities of our fellows.”
“我们不常讨论我们的动机，格兰杰小姐。在最初的日子里，如果没有黑魔王在场，我们几乎不被允许说话，而且我们的面具让我们很难确定我们同伴的身份。

“Why?”
“为什么？”

“It stopped us forming loyalties in-rank. We were supposed to be there for him and no one else.”
“它阻止了我们在级别上形成忠诚度。我们应该在他身边，而不是其他人。

“But surely, in time, you must have come to know other Death Eaters.”
“但可以肯定的是，随着时间的推移，你一定已经了解了其他食死徒。”

He inclined his head in reluctant acknowledgement. “Enough to betray their names to the Aurors,” Hermione added pointedly. He raised an eyebrow and leaned his head back to study her. 
他不情愿地歪着头承认。“足以把他们的名字出卖给傲罗，”赫敏尖锐地补充道。他扬起眉毛，把头向后仰，打量着她。

“Now who’s poking?” he asked. 
“现在谁在戳？”

A small smile flickered on Hermione’s lips but she quickly flattened it. Lucius raised his fist under his chin and leaned the weight of his head on it. “But you're right. In both senses. I came to know some of my fellow Death Eaters and no, we were not all there for the same reasons.”
赫敏的嘴唇上闪过一丝微笑，但她很快就把它压平了。卢修斯将拳头举到下巴下，将头的重量靠在上面。“但你是对的。在这两种意义上都是如此。我认识了一些食死徒同伴，不，我们并不是因为同样的原因而去那里。

“Can you tell me some of them?”
“你能告诉我其中的一些吗？”

“And here I thought you came here with the intent of discovering everything there is to know about me . Not enough for you, am I?”
“我以为你来到这里是为了发现关于我的一切。对你来说还不够，对吧？

Hermione fixed him with an impatient, narrow-eyed look that raised a smirk to his lips. “Very well.” He sighed and lifted his head to lean it against the back of his chair, his eyes directed towards the ceiling. 
赫敏用不耐烦的、眯起的眼睛盯着他，嘴角扬起一丝得意的笑容。“很好。”他叹了口气，抬起头靠在椅背上，眼睛直视着天花板。

“Some, like me, believed in ‘the cause’, as we called it. Some…well, some were afraid of the Dark Lord and so scurried towards him in the hope that would spare them.”
“有些人，比如我，相信我们所说的'事业'。一些。。。嗯，有些人害怕黑魔王，所以急忙向他跑来，希望能饶过他们。

 He was counting off the reasons on his fingers, still not looking at her. 
他用手指头数着原因，仍然没有看她。

“Others respected his power and hoped he would share it. Some were simply rather violent and appreciated that the Dark Lord encouraged their proclivities. And many were outcasts who hated the Ministry and wanted to watch the world burn so that they could remake it anew.”
“其他人尊重他的权力，希望他能分享它。有些人只是相当暴力，并感谢黑魔王鼓励他们的癖好。许多人是被抛弃的人，他们憎恨魔法部，想看着世界燃烧，这样他们就可以重新塑造它。

 He raised his head and gave her a tight smile. “Satisfied?”
他抬起头，对她露出一个紧绷的笑容。“满意吗？”

“Outcasts,” Hermione repeated, the doubt heavy in her voice. Voldemort’s limited view of who should be allowed to wield magic did not, from her perspective, leave much room for outcasts.
“被抛弃的人，”赫敏重复道，她的声音里带着沉重的疑惑。在她看来，伏地魔对谁应该被允许使用魔法的有限看法并没有给被抛弃的人留下太多空间。

“Miss Granger, the Dark Lord promised a new world. Do you know how appealing that is as a concept to those for whom the current world does not work? Giants were relegated to their settlements; werewolves ostracised from society; and Dementors were never particularly keen on employment. The Dark Lord vowed to give them a place and they thought him ruthless enough to carve it out.”
“格兰杰小姐，黑魔王承诺了一个新世界。你知道这个概念对那些当前世界不起作用的人来说是多么有吸引力吗？巨人被降级到他们的定居点;被社会排斥的狼人;摄魂怪从来都不是特别热衷于就业。黑魔王发誓要给他们一个位置，他们认为他无情到可以把它瓜分出去。

“But he deplored non-wizards! He was just using them,” Hermione burst out angrily. 
“可是他可怜非巫师！他只是在利用它们，“赫敏生气地爆发。

Lucius raised a finger with a quiet “ah ah” to halt her. “Whether or not he was actually going to do as he said is another matter but the promise was enough for them. Desperation is an excellent motivator. At least, I’ve always found that.”
卢修斯抬起一根手指，轻声地“啊啊”一声阻止了她。“他是否真的会按照他说的去做是另一回事，但这个承诺对他们来说已经足够了。绝望是一个很好的动力。至少，我一直都觉得这样。

He seemed somewhat amused by her simmering anger and pouted at her condescendingly. “So enraged on their behalf when they would have torn you limb from limb, given half the chance. Didn’t anyone ever tell you to be wary of monsters, Miss Granger?”
他似乎被她酝酿的怒火逗乐了，居高临下地朝她撅起嘴。“当他们给一半的机会，就把你撕成碎片，真是太生气了。难道没有人告诉你要小心怪物吗，格兰杰小姐？

Hermione pursed her lips. "They're not 'monsters'," she said. "Wizards treating them like they are is part of the problem." She paused thoughtfully, her lips pursed. Except the Dementors,” she added. “Awful things.”
赫敏抿了抿嘴唇。“他们不是'怪物'，”她说。“巫师像对待他们一样对待他们是问题的一部分。”她若有所思地停顿了一下，抿起了嘴唇。除了摄魂怪，“她补充道。“可怕的事情。”

“Quite,” Malfoy concurred quietly, contemplatively. His gaze was piercing enough to make Hermione look down into her lap for some relief from it. “Have you always been so…intent on finding the good in others, Miss Granger?”
“没错，”马尔福平静地、沉思着地同意道。他的目光锐利到足以让赫敏低头看向她的腿，以寻求一些缓解。“你一直都是这样......打算在别人身上找到优点，格兰杰小姐？

Hermione shifted in her seat and her eyes flicked up to his to find his gaze was still unwavering. He wasn’t really supposed to ask her personal questions – that wasn’t how the interviews worked. Her tongue darted out to wet her lips as she considered him. “I like to find it when it’s there to be found.”
赫敏在座位上动了动，她的眼睛瞥向他，发现他的目光仍然坚定不移。他真的不应该问她的私人问题——那不是采访的运作方式。她伸出舌头打湿了她的嘴唇，同时她打量着他。“我喜欢在它在那里被发现的时候找到它。”

“That suggests you think it isn’t in everyone to be found,” he said softly. “Is my understanding correct?”
“那说明你觉得不是每个人都能找到它，”他轻声说。“我的理解正确吗？”

Hermione frowned, drawing both of her hands into fists in her lap so that she felt her fingernails dig into her palms – she didn’t like the idea of that. That wasn’t what she thought. Was it? “I don’t know.” Lucius raised his eyebrows to hear her admit such a thing. “Maybe goodness is just harder to find in some than in others.”
赫敏皱起眉头，双手握成拳头放在膝盖上，这样她就能感觉到指甲深深地扎进了她的手掌——她不喜欢这种想法。她不是这么想的。是吗？“我不知道。”卢修斯扬起眉毛，听她承认了这样的事情。“也许有些人比其他人更难找到善良。”

“I’m surprised you don’t think yourself capable of manifesting it in others.”
“我很惊讶你不认为自己有能力在别人身上表现出来。”

The overt mockery in his words drew Hermione’s brow low in a frown. “I’m not sure that’s how it works.”
他话语中明显的嘲讽使赫敏皱起了眉头。“我不确定它是怎么运作的。”

“And how do you think it works?” The mockery was suddenly absent, as though he might genuinely want to hear her perspective. For some reason, this irritated Hermione more. Perhaps, in part, because while she had definitive answers for many things, how being good worked was not one of them.
“那你觉得它怎么运作？”嘲讽突然消失了，仿佛他可能真的想听听她的观点。不知为何，这让赫敏更加恼火了。也许，部分原因是虽然她对很多事情都有明确的答案，但好是如何运作并不是其中之一。

“Well,” she said, falteringly. “It’s all choices, isn’t it? We tend to make those ourselves.”
“嗯，”她踌躇不安地说。“这都是选择，不是吗？我们倾向于自己制作这些。

Lucius’ responding smile was mild but his eyes were probing. “Mmm, we must all make choices.” He nodded slowly. “Of course, sometimes the challenge lies in identifying when we’re making them, doesn’t it? Or even recognising that we have them.” 
卢修斯回应的笑容很温和，但他的眼睛却在探查。“嗯，我们都必须做出选择。”他缓缓地点了点头。“当然，有时挑战在于确定我们何时制作它们，不是吗？甚至认识到我们拥有它们。

Lucius’ smile dimmed as Hermione tilted her head, her warm eyes thoughtful as they inspected him. 
当赫敏歪着头时，卢修斯的笑容变得黯淡，她温暖的眼睛在打量他时若有所思。

"Are you trying to tell me that was your experience, Mr Malfoy?"
“你是想告诉我那是你的经历吗，马尔福先生？”

"No," he said tightly. "I am merely pointing out that just because you describe something with reductive simplicity does not mean that it is, in fact, simple.”
“不，”他紧紧地说。“我只是指出，仅仅因为你用简化的简单性来描述某件事，并不意味着它实际上很简单。”

“I didn’t—”
“我没有——”

"Perhaps consider that making choices is not always simply a matter of putting one foot in front of the other in an act of repetitious clarity," he said. "Sometimes it is descending a staircase in the dead of night, unable to see beyond your own hands. Sometimes you think you know exactly where the next step is until your heel just clips its edge and you fall, unable to grab ahold of anything except a faint hope that you will still be alive when you land."
“也许可以考虑一下，做出选择并不总是简单地将一只脚放在另一只脚前面，以重复的清晰行为，”他说。“有时是在夜深人静的时候从楼梯上下来，无法看到自己的双手以外的东西。有时你认为你确切地知道下一步在哪里，直到你的脚后跟夹住了边缘，你摔倒了，什么都抓不住，只能微弱地希望着陆时你还活着。

Hermione opened her mouth, drawing in a sharp breath as though intending to snap at him. But she didn't. Instead she stopped, exhaling quietly through her nose. That was a very specific metaphor offered up with an unusual degree of emotiveness.
赫敏张开嘴，猛地吸了一口气，仿佛打算对他发脾气。但她没有。相反，她停了下来，用鼻子轻声呼气。这是一个非常具体的比喻，以不同寻常的情感程度提供。

“Carry on with your questions, Miss Granger," Malfoy said, waving a hand, his voice quiet and irate. "I have dragged us off track.”
“继续你的问题，格兰杰小姐，”马尔福说，挥了挥手，他的声音平静而愤怒。“我把我们拖离了轨道。”

"I think I'd actually rather dig a little further into what you just said, Mr Malfoy."
“我想我其实更愿意更深入地研究你刚才说的话，马尔福先生。”

"I would not."
“我不会。”

"Then why did you say it?" she asked, her voice rising with impatience again. Impossible man .
“那你为什么这么说呢？” 她问道，她的声音又因不耐烦而提高了。 不可能的人。

"Because you needed to hear it," he said, levelling her with a steady gaze and the weight of her own words.
“因为你需要听到它，”他说，用坚定的目光和她自己话语的重量来平定她。

There was a tense pause in which Hermione closed her eyes tight, her lips pressed thin and her heart thumping. Why couldn't he just be straightforward? Why did he have to make everything a struggle? Why he just assume the choices she had made were easy? Why did he –
赫敏紧紧地闭上了眼睛，嘴唇紧紧地抿着，心砰砰直跳。为什么他不能直截了当呢？为什么他必须让一切都变得艰难呢？为什么他只是认为她所做的选择很容易？他为什么——

"Are you actually going to carry on?" His drawling voice broke into her internal tirade. "Or are you granting me the small mercy of finishing early?" 
“你真的要继续吗？”他拖沓的声音打破了她内心的长篇大论。“还是你给了我提前完成的小小怜悯？”

Clearing her throat, Hermione opened her eyes to glower at him. He was inspecting the small cuts on his arms. One of them had started to bleed lightly and he wiped it with his thumb, smearing a faint red streak over the pale skin of his forearm. Hermione sighed, some of her anger leaving her.
清了清嗓子，赫敏睁开眼睛瞪着他。他正在检查自己手臂上的小伤口。其中一个已经开始轻微流血，他用拇指擦了擦，在他前臂苍白的皮肤上涂抹了一条淡淡的红色条纹。赫敏叹了口气，她的一些愤怒离开了她。

"Please let me help you heal those."
“请让我帮你治愈那些。”

"Please just continue , Miss Granger," he said, glancing up at her with impatient eyes. He lifted his thumb absently to his mouth and sucked the streak of blood from it. Hermione's eyes were drawn to his mouth as he drew his thumb away from it. Was it the blood or had his lips always been quite red? His tongue flicked out, wetting his lips, before he said, "I won't tell you again."
“请继续，格兰杰小姐，”他说，用不耐烦的眼神抬头瞥了她一眼。他心不在焉地把拇指举到嘴边，吸吮着拇指上的血迹。赫敏的眼睛被吸引到他的嘴上，同时他把拇指从嘴上抽了出来。是血还是他的嘴唇一直很红？他的舌头伸了出来，弄湿了他的嘴唇，然后他说，“我不会再告诉你了。

“Fine," Hermione said, dragging her eyes away from his mouth with a defeated sigh. "Fine, let's just…" She cast around, trying to find a thread of questioning she could grab onto while he bent his head, attention back on his arm. "I’m assuming you…got married around the time of your formal entry into the Death Eaters?” 
“好吧，”赫敏说，把眼睛从他的嘴里拖开，沮丧地叹了口气。“好吧，我们就......”她四处张望，试图找到一丝可以抓住的提问线索，而他则低下了头，注意力又回到了他的手臂上。“我假设你......在你正式加入食死徒的时候结婚了？

As soon as she asked the question, Hermione internally cringed when she saw his head slowly rise, his lips forming a thin line. “You don’t have to talk about that if you’d rather not,” she added hurriedly. 
她一问这个问题，赫敏看到他的头慢慢抬起，嘴唇形成一条细线，内心就畏缩了起来。“如果你愿意的话，你就不必谈论这个，”她急忙补充道。

Lucius studied her for a moment and then exhaled softly, lowering his arms to his desk. “No," he said. "I think you and I have rather gotten past that particular point of reticence. Yes, I married Narcissa relatively early in my time with the Death Eaters.”
卢修斯端详了她一会儿，然后轻轻地呼出一口气，将手臂垂到桌子上。“不，”他说。“我想你和我都已经越过了那个特定的沉默点。是的，我在与食死徒在一起的时候就嫁给了纳西莎。

“What age were you?”
“你几岁了？”

“I was 22, she had just turned 21.”
“我当时 22 岁，她刚满 21 岁。”

“I assume, based on the book you ‘encouraged’ me to read, that it was arranged?”
“我猜，根据你'鼓励'我读的那本书，它是被安排好的？”

“Yes. My father had organised the contract with the Blacks before his death and it was one of his few final wishes that I was willing to see through. Narcissa and I knew of one another from Hogwarts, of course. We knew we were to be wed and we liked one another well enough.”
“是的。我父亲在去世前与布莱克队签订了合同，这是我愿意实现的他为数不多的遗愿之一。当然，纳西莎和我在霍格沃茨就认识了。我们知道我们要结婚了，我们很喜欢彼此。

“Did you have any say in the matter?”
“你对这件事有什么发言权吗？”

“No,” he said with a careless shrug. “But I didn’t particularly care to. I believe I was originally supposed to be married to the middle Black daughter, Andromeda, but of course she ran off with that Mudblood—” 
“不，”他漫不经心地耸耸肩说。“但我并不是特别在乎。我相信我本来应该嫁给中间的黑人女儿，仙女座，但她当然带着那个泥巴种跑了——”

His eyes met Hermione's as ‘Mudblood’ left his lips and he faltered, as though anticipating that she was going to tell him off. Instead, Hermione raised her eyebrows expectantly, inviting him to carry on, and he quietly cleared his throat, a small frown creasing his forehead. “...She ran off. I knew it was going to happen regardless of my input.”
当“泥巴种”离开他的嘴唇时，他的目光与赫敏的目光相遇，他颤抖着，仿佛预料到她会告发他。相反，赫敏期待地扬起眉毛，邀请他继续，他悄悄地清了清嗓子，额头上皱起了小皱眉。“...她跑掉了。我知道无论我的意见如何，它都会发生。

“Didn’t that bother you, though?”
“不过，你不介意吗？”

“Miss Granger…” he trailed off looking exasperated. “ No . Why would it? I didn’t know any different.”
“格兰杰小姐......”他一脸恼怒地走开了。“ 不 .为什么会这样呢？我不知道有什么不同。

“But surely you saw different kinds of relationships at Hogwarts. Didn’t you ever think about one of those?”
“但你肯定在霍格沃茨看到了各种各样的关系。你从来没有想过其中之一吗？

“I’m afraid I was far more fixated on other things. Things that weren’t as trivial as relationships that could never last. If anything, having Narcissa preparing to be my wife was…” he winced and rolled his eyes, “somewhat convenient.”
“恐怕我更专注于其他事情。这些事情不像永远不会持久的关系那样微不足道。如果有的话，让 Narcissa 准备成为我的妻子就是......”他皱起眉头，翻了个白眼，“有点方便。

“How romantic.”
“多么浪漫。”

“Pure-blood marriages are not based on romance; they are transactions. You of all people obviously know that after your little diatribe in the grounds.” Hermione looked grim but far from embarrassed. “But I came to love her. Sincerely, in my own way. Partly that was because of who she was as a person but it was also because I had already decided that I would respect and cherish my wife, whoever she ended up being.” 
“纯血统婚姻不是基于浪漫;它们是交易。 在你那小小的谩骂之后，你显然知道这一点。赫敏看起来严肃起来，但一点也不尴尬。“但我开始爱她。真诚地，以我自己的方式。部分原因是她作为一个人，但也因为我已经决定要尊重和珍惜我的妻子，无论她最终成为谁。

Hermione sat back, her head tilted as she took him in. His gaze was unfocused and she found herself wishing she'd included a Pensieve in their interviews, so keen was she to see whatever was passing through his head. 
赫敏坐回去，歪着头把他带进去。他的目光没有聚焦，她发现自己希望自己在他们的采访中包括一个 Pensieve，她是如此热衷于看到他脑海中闪过的一切。

It seemed he had decided from a young age exactly what kind of wizard he was going to be and had spent his life building towards it. He struck her as very…structured. Perhaps overly so. To the point of being brittle? For all his efforts, everything had shattered. Hermione wasn't sorry that it had – where would she be if everything had worked out as he’d wanted it?
他似乎从很小的时候就决定了他要成为什么样的巫师，并为此付出了一生的努力。他觉得她非常......结构。也许有点过分了。到了脆的地步？尽管他付出了所有努力，但一切都碎了。赫敏并不为此感到遗憾——如果一切都按照他的意愿进行，她会在哪里呢？

“Did respecting and cherishing your wife affect your work with the Dark Lord?”
“尊重和珍惜你的妻子是否影响了你与黑魔王的工作？”

“ Well .” Lucius came back into himself and he fixed her with a rather tired look. “As much as Narcissa, like myself, agreed with the Dark Lord’s views on Pure-bloods and our society, she had no interest in following her sister into the Death Eaters.” 
“嗯。”卢修斯回过神来，用一种相当疲惫的眼神注视着她。“尽管纳西莎和我一样，都同意黑魔王对纯血统和我们社会的看法，但她没有兴趣跟着她的姐姐加入食死徒。”

He paused and rested his left hand on the desk, drumming his fingers and drawing Hermione’s eyes to the rings there. He’d never been wearing a wedding ring, she suddenly realised, and she’d never noticed it.
他停了下来，把左手放在桌子上，敲打着手指，把赫敏的眼睛吸引到那里的戒指上。他从来没有戴过结婚戒指，她突然意识到，而且她从来没有注意到。

“She never really explained why . I remember her once feeding me a line that she had sworn loyalty to only one man and she would stand by that.” He smiled and there was a sadness in it that made Hermione feel… weird . Like she’d seen something she shouldn’t have. “But I don’t know the real reason. Perhaps she knew something I didn’t.”
“她从来没有真正解释过为什么。我记得她曾经给我说过一句话，她发誓只效忠一个男人，她会坚持下去。他笑了笑，里面有一种悲伤，让赫敏觉得......奇怪。就像她看到了不该看到的东西。“但我不知道真正的原因。也许她知道一些我不知道的事情。

“Did Voldemort try to recruit her?”
“伏地魔有没有想招募她？”

“Of course. She’s a talented witch. But she refused and I stood by her. The Dark Lord didn’t look particularly kindly on that. Certainly, he took note. A line was drawn that day, I believe.” 
“当然。她是一个有才华的女巫。但她拒绝了，我站在她身边。黑魔王对此并不特别友好。当然，他注意到了。我相信那天划定了一条线。

“What was the line?”
“那是什么线？”

“For me,” Lucius said, raising an indicative hand to his chest, “it was a line between the Dark Lord and my family. I placed myself on it, separating him from them. For him…I think it was the line marking the limit of my loyalty to him. I’d never had one before. He didn’t tend to like them.”
“对我来说，”卢修斯说，将一只手举到他的胸前，“这是黑魔王和我家人之间的一条线。我把自己放在上面，把他和他们分开。对他来说......我认为这是标志着我对他的忠诚极限的界限。我以前从来没有过。他不太喜欢他们。

“I suppose that line only became more distinct when your son was born. 1980, wasn’t it?”
“我想，当你的儿子出生时，这条界限才变得更加明显。1980 年，不是吗？

“Yes.” He nodded. “Narcissa could spout about loyalty to only one man but if it ever was me that changed when Draco was born. As I would have expected.”
“是的。”他点点头。“纳西莎可以滔滔不绝地谈论对一个男人的忠诚，但如果真的是我的话，当德拉科出生时，情况发生了变化。正如我所料。

He seemed barely aware of the softness that had taken residence on his face. Weirdly human , Hermione thought with a twinge of discomfort. He loved his son, she could tell. He loved him as more than an heir or a vessel for the family name. 
他似乎几乎没意识到自己脸上的柔软。 奇怪的人类，赫敏带着一丝不适想着。她看得出来，他爱他的儿子。他爱他，而不是一个继承人或家族的容器。

For a time, even during their interviews, she had thought Draco’s insistent loyalty to his father foolish and misguided. It was possible there was more to their relationship than she had thought. More than she could ever really understand.
有一段时间，甚至在他们的采访中，她都认为德拉科对他父亲的执着忠诚是愚蠢和误导的。他们的关系可能比她想象的要多。比她真正理解的要多。

“Something else happened in 1980, though.” Lucius frowned and Hermione elaborated: “The prophecy.”
“不过，1980 年还发生了另一件事。”卢修斯皱起眉头，赫敏解释道：“预言。

Lucius’ eyes rolled to the ceiling and he leaned both of his elbows on the arms of his chair, sinking down in a way that was uncharacteristically undignified. “Ah, yes. The prophecy .” 
卢修斯的眼睛翻向天花板，他的双手肘靠在椅子的扶手上，以一种异常不体面的方式沉了下去。“啊，是的。预言 .

“You don’t sound taken with it,” Hermione said, not bothering to restrain her smirk. 
“你听起来没什么好意思，”赫敏说，懒得抑制自己的笑容。

His responding glare was venomous and Hermione’s smirk turned into a full grin. 
他回应的目光是恶毒的，赫敏的笑容变成了一个完整的笑容。

“Don’t look so pleased with yourself, Miss Granger,” he said. "You have an immensely irritating habit of acting like you know all the ins and outs of a story before you actually hear it."
“不要看起来对自己那么满意，格兰杰小姐，”他说。“你有一个非常令人讨厌的习惯，在你真正听到一个故事之前，你就表现得好像你知道它的所有来龙去脉。”

“Well, tell me about it, then,” she prompted, allowing the slight to brush past her like a poorly aimed hex.
“好吧，那么，跟我说说吧，”她提示道，让那微小的一丝光芒像一个瞄准不佳的六角一样从她身边擦过。

Lucius sighed deeply through his nose. “I know the story now, of course, but at the time the prophecy was made, the Dark Lord didn’t divulge the details to the majority of his Death Eaters. The information was too sensitive, so he simply became erratic, obsessive and even more secretive. Over the course of a year, he withdrew from every active operation.” Lucius lifted his hand to his face, running his forefinger along his lower lip. “Rather alarming for me, I must say.”
卢修斯从鼻子里深深地叹了口气。“我现在当然知道这个故事了，但在预言出来的时候，黑魔王并没有把细节透露给他的大多数食死徒。信息太敏感了，所以他就变得飘忽不定、强迫症，甚至更加隐秘。在一年的时间里，他退出了所有活跃的行动。卢修斯把手举到他的脸上，食指滑过他的下唇。“我必须说，这让我相当惊慌。”

“以什么方式？”

“It’s somewhat difficult to give commands when there aren’t any to give. There was a noticeable…loss of momentum, shall we say. It was enough to cause rumbles of dissatisfaction through the ranks and those made my life less than easy. 
“当没有命令可下达时，下达命令有点困难。有一个明显的......失去动力，容我们说。这足以在队伍中引起不满的隆隆声，这让我的生活变得不那么轻松。

"I pressed Severus, of course. He was behaving as oddly as the Dark Lord and I knew he knew something but, for the first time, I think, he wasn’t particularly forthcoming with me.” 
“当然，我催促了西弗勒斯。他的行为举止和黑魔王一样古怪，我知道他知道一些事情，但我想，这是第一次，他并不是特别愿意对我说。

Lucius pursed his lips, clearly irked by the memory of Snape's avoidance.
卢修斯抿了抿嘴唇，显然对斯内普的回避感到恼火。

“And then the Dark Lord vanished. Our marks faded instantaneously. We… felt the loss of him. His power.” 
“然后黑魔王就消失了。我们的印记瞬间消失了。我们。。。感到失去了他。他的力量。

Lucius clicked his tongue against the roof of his mouth, his jaw sliding to the side as he fixed Hermione with a stare.
卢修斯用舌头抵住他的上颚，他的下巴滑向一边，盯着赫敏。

“你知道的，事后一片混乱。我们谁也不知道发生了什么。指控满天飞，派系在几个小时内形成。然后有报道说他被一个婴儿毁了。一个婴儿。

Lucius sighed and lifted a hand to rub his eyes, appearing exhausted by the mere memory of that time. 
卢修斯叹了口气，抬起一只手揉了揉眼睛，似乎仅仅因为那段时间的记忆而筋疲力尽。

“显然，他很害怕。如果他不想失去所有的力量，他就必须认真对待所有风险。

“更多的恐惧。”卢修斯嗤之以鼻。“你眼里每个人都害怕吗？想想除了你之外的每个人都在恐惧中四处乱窜，这让你觉得自己更像一个勇敢的小格兰芬多吗？

“Gryffindors still feel fear,” Hermione said loftily. “We just act in spite of it rather than allow ourselves to be led by it.” 
“格兰芬多们还是感到恐惧，”赫敏高傲地说。“我们只是无视它而行动，而不是让自己被它引导。”

Malfoy narrowed his eyes at that, sensing her underlying accusation.
马尔福眯起眼睛，感觉到她潜在的指责。

"You don't set much store by prophecy,  then?" Hermione asked, the almost eager interest in her voice making his head tilt curiously. 
“那么，你不怎么看重预言吗？”赫敏问道，她声音中近乎热切的兴趣让他好奇地歪了歪头。

"I think Divination is one of our most ancient branches of magic and should, therefore, be extended some respect," he said slowly, his voice considering. Hermione bit back a derisive scoff. "But I also think interpreting something as ambiguous as a prophecy or tea leaves through a single, highly personal lens is a recipe for disaster."
“我认为占卜是我们最古老的魔法分支之一，因此，应该给予一些尊重，”他缓缓地说，他的声音深思熟虑。赫敏嘲讽地嘲讽地回了一句。“但我也认为，通过一个单一的、高度个人化的镜头来解释像预言或茶叶这样模棱两可的东西，是灾难的根源。”

"Yes, imagine allowing your personal biases to cloud your judgment," Hermione said flatly. 
“是的，想象一下让你的个人偏见蒙蔽了你的判断，”赫敏平淡地说。

Lucius' nostrils flared and Hermione offered him a tight smile.
卢修斯的鼻孔张开，赫敏向他露出一个紧绷的笑容。

“So what did you do the night he fell?" Hermione asked. "Amidst the chaos?”
“那么，他坠落的那天晚上你做了什么？”赫敏问道。“在混乱中？”

Lucius looked like he might not answer her as punishment for her cheek but, after a moment of tight-faced contemplation, he sighed. “I got my story straight.”
卢修斯看起来可能不会回答她，以惩罚她的脸颊，但在紧绷的脸上沉思了一会儿后，他叹了口气。“我把我的故事说清楚了。”

“You didn’t go looking for him at Godric’s Hollow? You didn't join the Death Eaters who desperately searched for him?" Lucius shook his head. "Your sister-in-law was so sure he wasn't dead she destroyed the Longbottoms," Hermione added, a slight waver in her voice. "Why didn't you?"
“你不是去戈德里克山谷找他吗？你不是加入了拼命寻找他的食死徒吗？卢修斯摇摇头。“你嫂子这么确定他没死，她毁了隆巴顿一家，”赫敏补充道，她的声音略带颤抖。“你为什么不呢？”

"Bella was a fanatic, Miss Granger. I consider myself to be a touch more pragmatic and, as a pragmatist, I cannot pretend my faith wasn't shaken by the Dark Lord's apparent defeat by a baby ."
“贝拉是个狂热分子，格兰杰小姐。我认为自己更务实一些，作为一个实用主义者，我不能假装我的信仰没有被黑魔王明显地打败一个婴儿所动摇。

"So you believed he was gone?"
“所以你相信他已经走了？”

"It certainly appeared that way and so I acted accordingly. I told you, Miss Granger, my family came first. I had to protect their— our —interests before anything else. Going looking for the Dark Lord would not have been in keeping with the behaviour of a man who had just snapped out of years spent under the Imperius curse. I am many things but I am not a fool.”
“事情确实是这样的，所以我采取了相应的行动。我告诉你，格兰杰小姐，我的家人先来了。我必须先保护他们——我们的——利益。去寻找黑魔王与一个刚刚在帝王诅咒下度过的岁月中醒来的人的行为不符。我有很多东西，但我不是傻子。

“No,” she said thoughtfully, her eyes raking over him, lingering on his scratched arms and rumpled shirt long enough that he shifted, feeling a curious vulnerability. “I don’t suppose you are. I think we can leave it there for today, Mr Malfoy.”
“不，”她若有所思地说，她的眼睛扫视着他，在他被划伤的手臂和皱巴巴的衬衫上徘徊了足够长的时间，以至于他动了动，感到一种奇怪的脆弱。“我想你不是。我想我们今天就在这里吧，马尔福先生。

“Very well.”
“很好。”

As Malfoy straightened up, inspecting the cuts on his arm more closely, Hermione tapped the Wheezebox with her wand and proceeded to pack her things away. “I'll be working in the library for a while tonight,” she said. “Just so you're aware.”
当马尔福直起身来，更仔细地检查他手臂上的伤口时，赫敏用魔杖敲了敲喘息盒，然后开始收拾她的东西。“我今晚会在图书馆工作一会儿，”她说。“只是让你知道。”

Lucius made a dismissive noise and rose out of his chair to turn and face the window. He continued looking away until he heard the door close, at which point he sighed and allowed his shoulders to drop under the weight of his tiredness.
卢修斯轻蔑地发出声音，从椅子上站起来，转身面对窗户。他继续移开视线，直到听到门关上的声音，这时他叹了口气，让自己的肩膀在疲惫的重压下垂下。

"Letty," he said into the empty room, hoping the elf would be quick with the essence of Murtlap. His cuts were beginning to sting. 
“莱蒂，”他对着空荡荡的房间说，希望这个妖精能快点掌握穆特拉普的精华。他的伤口开始刺痛。

June 8th - continued
6 月 8 日 - 续

Lucius didn’t often eat dinner with Draco and Astoria but after Granger’s departure he felt an unusual need to be around people. More specifically, to be around his son. 
卢修斯不经常和德拉科和阿斯托利亚一起吃晚饭，但在格兰杰离开后，他觉得自己不寻常地需要和人在一起。更具体地说，就是在他儿子身边。

He didn’t say that, of course. In fact, he sat at the dining table in stony silence, barely looking at either of them, but their presence soothed the uncomfortable itching that had developed in the back of his brain. 
当然，他没有这么说。事实上，他静静地坐在餐桌旁，几乎不看他们中的任何一个人，但他们的存在缓解了他大脑后部产生的不舒服的瘙痒。

“The wards noted Hermione’s arrival today but I’m not sure she’s actually left,” Astoria said to Draco, glancing over at the grandfather clock in the corner. It read 8.10 pm. “Shouldn’t we send something up with Letty if she's still here?”
“病房注意到赫敏今天到了，但我不确定她真的已经离开了，”阿斯托利亚对德拉科说，瞥了一眼角落里的老爷钟。上面写着晚上 8 点 10 分。“如果 Letty 还在这里，我们难道不应该给她寄点东西吗？”

“Miss Granger is perfectly capable of feeding herself, Astoria,” Lucius said crisply, dabbing the corner of his mouth with a napkin. 
“格兰杰小姐完全有能力自己吃饭，阿斯托利亚，”卢修斯干脆地说，用餐巾纸擦了擦嘴角。

Astoria looked reproachfully at Lucius and appeared ready to respond when Draco set a cautioning hand on her arm. The sight of the action made Lucius grit his teeth. Sometimes they treated him like something to be handled. Like some kind of fanged creature that wouldn't bite if you could only tread carefully enough around it. It made him want to bite more. 
阿斯托利亚责备地看着卢修斯，当德拉科用一只警告的手搭在她的手臂上时，她似乎准备回应。看到这一幕，卢修斯咬牙切齿。有时他们把他当作需要处理的东西。就像某种长着獠牙的生物，如果你能小心翼翼地绕过它，它不会咬人。这让他想咬得更多。

Granger was the only other person with whom he had any interactions and she didn’t treat him like that, he realised with a dissatisfied tug in his stomach. She just…what? Lucius adjusted his napkin, frowning at it. What did she do? Well, she didn't tread carefully, at the very least.
格兰杰是他唯一一个和他有任何互动的人，她也没有那样对待他，他意识到，肚子里不满地拉扯着。她只是......什么？卢修斯调整了一下餐巾纸，皱着眉头。她做了什么呢？好吧，至少她没有小心翼翼。

 “She's a guest, father,” said Draco, his tone carefully measured.
“她是客人，爸爸，”德拉科说，他的语气小心翼翼地衡量着。

“Not a dinner guest,” Lucius responded, taking a sip of his wine. “She has the freedom to go back and forth between the library and her own kitchen. I do not see why she should make so much use of ours.”
“不是晚餐的客人，”卢修斯回答道，啜了一口他的酒。“她可以自由地在图书馆和自己的厨房之间来回切换。我不明白她为什么要这么多地利用我们。

Draco frowned at him but didn’t argue back, instead turning to Astoria. “She’ll probably leave soon, anyway. I’ve told you what she gets like when she’s head down into things.” Draco jerked his head in the direction of his father. “It’s like him.”
德拉科皱着眉头看着他，但没有反驳，而是转向阿斯托利亚。“反正她可能很快就会走了。我已经告诉过你，当她埋头做事时，她会是什么样子。德拉科猛地把头转向他父亲的方向。“就像他一样。”

“There is nothing of a likeness between myself and Miss Granger,” Lucius said stiffly, setting down his knife and fork, his appetite rapidly vanishing. 
“我和格兰杰小姐之间一点也不像，”卢修斯僵硬地说，放下了他的刀叉，他的胃口很快就消失了。

“Funny,” Draco said, a smirk quivering around his mouth, “I’m sure she’d say that too. You seem to be especially annoyed by her today, what’s she done?”
“好笑，”德拉科说，嘴角一抹得意的笑容颤抖着，“我敢肯定她也会这么说的。你今天好像特别生她的气，她做了什么？

“Nothing.” Lucius removed his napkin from his lap and dropped it onto his plate, crossing his legs and folding his arms.
“没什么。”卢修斯从腿上取下餐巾纸，把它放在盘子里，交叉双腿，交叉双臂。

Draco raised his eyebrows and took a large bite of mashed potato as he dispassionately contemplated Lucius’ pretzel-like body language. “Never heard ‘nothing’ sound so much like ‘something’.”
德拉科扬起眉毛，咬了一大口土豆泥，冷静地思考着卢修斯那类似椒盐卷饼的肢体语言。“从来没有听过'什么都没有'听起来这么像'有东西'。”

Lucius tutted and looked away, deciding that he would opt for a dignified silence over a snappish response. He was rather regretting his decision to join his son for dinner. 
卢修斯啧了一声，移开了视线，决定他会选择庄重的沉默，而不是生硬的回应。他相当后悔自己决定和儿子一起吃晚饭。

Despite not getting a reply, Draco didn’t let up. Their spoiling of him had ensured that wasn't in his nature and Lucius quietly lamented himself and Narcissa's short-sightedness. “She’s not what you thought she’d be, is she?”
尽管没有得到回复，德拉科并没有松懈。他们对他的宠坏确保了这并不是他的本性，卢修斯悄悄地哀叹自己和纳西莎的短视。“她不是你想象的那个样子，对吧？”

Slowly, Lucius’ head turned back towards his son and he rolled his tongue in his mouth for a moment in an effort to stop himself answering. 
慢慢地，卢修斯的头转向他的儿子，他在嘴里滚动了一会儿舌头，试图阻止自己回答。

“What exactly do you mean by that?” he finally asked, his voice pleasant and his face placid, while he internally cursed himself to the ends of the earth for engaging.
“你这到底是什么意思？”他终于问道，他的声音悦耳动听，脸色平静，同时他在心里咒骂自己，直到天涯海角。

“She’s a person.”
“她是一个人。”

This time, Lucius didn’t actually have a reply to repress. Perhaps sensing that, Draco just smiled and dropped his gaze to his dinner. Astoria looked back and forth between them, her lips slightly parted and her cod forgotten. Lucius didn’t say a word for the rest of the meal.  
这一次，卢修斯实际上并没有回应压抑。也许是感觉到了这一点，德拉科只是笑了笑，把目光投向了他的晚餐。阿斯托利亚在他们之间来回打量，她的嘴唇微微张开，忘记了她的鳕鱼。卢修斯在剩下的饭菜中一言不发。

The sun had set but the evening was still pleasantly warm enough for Lucius to stand on the terrace with his after-dinner brandy. Swirling it in the glass, he turned his head up to the sky and inhaled the summer night air, his eyes fluttering closed. It smelled fresh and there was something floral from the gardens that reminded him of…
太阳已经落山，但傍晚仍然温暖宜人，卢修斯可以站在露台上喝着他的餐后白兰地。他在玻璃杯里旋转着，抬头望向天空，吸入夏夜的空气，颤抖着闭上了眼睛。闻起来很清新，花园里有一些花香让他想起......

Lucius’ eyes snapped open and he took a large gulp of his brandy, coughing when some of it went down the wrong way. 
卢修斯猛然睁开眼睛，他大口大口地喝了一大口白兰地，当一些白兰地流错方向时，他咳嗽了起来。

“Need some company?” Draco’s voice came from behind him but Lucius didn’t bother to turn around, still rubbing his chest to help the rest of his brandy go down. “I’ll take your silence as an invitation.”
“需要一些陪伴吗？”德拉科的声音从他身后传来，但卢修斯懒得转身，仍然揉着胸口，帮助他剩下的白兰地喝下去。“我会把你的沉默当作一种邀请。”

“Of course you will,” Lucius muttered as Draco appeared by his shoulder, clutching a matching glass of brandy. 
“你当然会的，”卢修斯咕哝着，德拉科出现在他的肩膀上，手里拿着一杯相配的白兰地。

露台一片漆黑，但房子的光线足够强，足以照亮周围的环境，给一切都带来朦胧的背光。卢修斯用眼角的余光瞥了一眼他的儿子。他经常忘记德拉科已经长得比他高了。他经常忘记德拉科已经长大了。

“Are you being nice to her?” Draco asked, looking out over the grounds and taking a sip of his brandy. 
“你对她好吗？”德拉科问道，一边望着外面的地面，啜了一口他的白兰地。

Lucius didn’t need to ask who he was talking about—they both knew perfectly well. “I am doing as asked. Stop adding increasingly restrictive parameters to what is already a hateful experience.” 
卢修斯不需要问他在说谁——他们都非常清楚。“我正在按照要求去做。停止在已经是仇恨的经历中增加越来越严格的参数。

德拉科一定是笑了，因为他的肩膀在颤抖。“她还在这里，”他说，瞥了一眼卢修斯。“我让莱蒂检查一下。”

Lucius reached down and drew out his pocket watch. Ludicrous . “Is she ever in her own home?”
卢修斯伸手掏出他的怀表。 荒唐的。“她曾经在自己家里吗？”

“She cares about what she does,” Draco said, shrugging. “I thought passion and drive were things you always admired. You banged on enough about the importance of working hard when I couldn’t beat her marks at school.”

Lucius quietly tutted at the memory of his borderline distraught son, presenting him with acceptable grades and excuses for why they weren’t the best in his year. “I deplore complacency, Draco, you know that. And excuses.” Lucius sighed deeply, adding with a murmur, “I do recall you being alarmingly fixated on her. It did somewhat concern me for a time.”
卢修斯悄悄地啧啧了一声，回忆起他那几乎心烦意乱的儿子，向他展示了可以接受的成绩和借口，解释为什么他们在他的一年里不是最好的。“我惋惜自满，德拉科，你知道的。还有借口。卢修斯深深地叹了口气，喃喃自语地补充道，“我记得你曾经对她产生了惊人的关注。这确实让我有一段时间有点担心。

So that’s what I tried to be. Except she beat me in every class. The only place she couldn’t beat me was the Quidditch pitch but Potter did that for her. Half-blood Potter with his Muggle-born mother.”

Except she wasn’t anything like what you told me a Mudblood was. What was I supposed to do with that? I hated her so much that Pansy accused me of some kind of…repressed… fascination .”

Had you pursued that path our diplomatic strategy would be chaotic."

卢修斯脸色发白。“她跟你说的吗？”

“为什么？”卢修斯咬牙切齿地问道。为什么当他已经受到惩罚时，他自己的儿子却认为应该进一步惩罚他呢？

“我正在努力联系你并关心你。”德拉科的声音里有一丝微妙的裂缝，毫无疑问，其中充满了委屈。

His only son, who he had been keeping at arm’s length since the end of the war out of a combination of shame at what he had done to him and fear of being a burden to him. “当我在温室里需要帮助时，”他轻声说，“我会来找你的，德拉科。

Couldn't he, for once in his life, do something selfless for Draco?

德拉科的叹息很轻柔，但在夏日傍晚的宁静中，还是可以听到的。在他痛苦、烦躁的状态下，卢修斯本可以抓住它来进一步激怒自己，但他却闭上了眼睛，稳住了呼吸。这似乎对格兰杰有用。有时。

“我们都爱你，德拉科，”卢修斯轻声说，睁开眼睛，抬起头。“这不会改变。”

“我知道。”

为了补充能量，卢修斯转身朝房子的方向走去，留下德拉科一个人在露台上。他没有回到外面。

晚上 10 点多，卢修斯穿过走廊，朝着他的书房方向走去。他感觉相当沉思，完全打算再喝几杯火威士忌来浅浅他心灵的漩涡深处。

“卢修斯，你今晚看起来特别闷闷不乐。”

“谢谢你，Sabine，”他说，放慢脚步停下，转身看着Sabine靠在她身上的熟悉景象。

“你那个麻瓜出身的人还来探望吗？”她问道，眼睛扫视着卢修斯，仿佛他可能在躲着赫敏。“我已经有一段时间没有和她说话了。”

“她不是我麻瓜出身的，”卢修斯说，他的眉头深深地皱了起来。

“嗯，她不是我的。”

卢修斯交叉双臂。“那她就不是任何人的了。”

“多么可悲，”Sabine 撅着嘴，把她的肩膀靠在框架上，让她站直。

“你为什么想认识萨宾？你对麻瓜和泥巴种有特别的依恋吗？

He knew he was probably pushing her buttons. Quite meanly, actually, given her history. But a part of him resented her for never telling him about her husband, about their maid, about the child they had adopted—stolen—from its Muggle mother. Besides, she was a painting .
他知道他可能在按她的按钮。实际上，考虑到她的历史，这相当卑鄙。但他有一部分怨恨她，因为她从来没有告诉他关于她的丈夫，关于他们的女仆，关于他们从麻瓜母亲那里收养——偷来——的孩子。此外，她是一幅画。

萨宾的戏谑表情消失了，她交叉着自己的手臂，与卢修斯相映成趣。“当你还是个孩子的时候，我告诉过你不要在我身边使用这个词。你听起来像你爸爸。

The problem with pressing Sabine’s buttons was that she knew how to press his right back. Lucius raised his eyebrows in challenge. “You never gave me a good enough reason.”
按下 Sabine 按钮的问题在于她知道如何按下他的右背。卢修斯挑起眉毛。“你从来没有给我一个足够好的理由。”

“我反对它应该有足够的理由，卢修斯;要尊重一些。她严肃的表情无限地柔和了下来。“她看起来是个足够体面的女孩。 没错，她对方向无可救药，但她很漂亮，以一种不加修饰的方式。无罪。当然不配这个贬义词，“萨宾娜精明地补充道。“你不必这么残忍。”

卢修斯咬住舌头，阻止自己说出他可能会后悔的话，然后放下手臂，转向他的办公室。

当他到达办公室时，他停了下来，把手放在门把手上，沿着走廊向图书馆的方向看去。

You needn’t be so cruel . He hesitated, turning back towards the corridor and then back towards the library a few times before stopping with a deep, resigned sigh.

“莱蒂，”他轻声说。

精灵发出一声响亮的噼啪声，卢修斯皱起眉头，从门口回头看，确认格兰杰没有动弹。

卢修斯做了个手势让精灵安静下来，然后指着图书馆的方向，低声说道。“莱蒂，带格兰杰小姐到走廊对面的客房去。尽量不要吵醒她。

莱蒂热切地点点头，她的耳朵拍打着。卢修斯没有等她听从他的命令，而是沿着走廊向他的书房走去，他的脚步很沉重。

Her bed wasn’t very soft and large; it was rather small and there was a strange lump in the mattress down by her lower back. Dazed and groggy from sleep, she used her elbows to push herself up into a sitting position and looked around. 
赫敏惊醒了，猛地吸了一口气。她躺在床上。一张非常柔软的大床。她的床不是很柔软，也不是很大;它相当小，在她下背部的床垫上有一个奇怪的肿块。她睡着了，头晕目眩，昏昏沉沉的，她用手肘把自己推到坐姿，环顾四周。

Lots of floral patterns and dusky rose shades, a thick carpet, heavy curtains and bed hangings. Overall, it was a room that looked like it should be very dusty but, based on the fresh smell, Hermione was fairly certain that it was sparklingly clean.

Oh , she thought, seeing the large window at the end. She was still in the corridor with the library and Malfoy’s study. Kept her out of bother.” Malfoy took another drink and then looked over at Hermione with a bitter smile as he swallowed. “She was such a bother,” he said, his voice weighed down with sarcasm.

赫敏的嘴巴干涩。她不该来的。如果她以前认为他喝醉了，那么他现在更接近喝醉了。他可能不是想告诉她他是什么的一半，他想起来后会让她付出代价。 如果他记得的话。

赫敏回头看了他一眼，然后朝书架走去，不完全确定自己在找什么。它会说 'photo album' 吗？也许最好找个书脊上根本没有文字的东西。想起马尔福说过他家里不那么友好的书，她对拿出任何东西感到有些犹豫。

赫敏难以置信地笑了起来。“嗯，不，这不是问题。只是......嗯，很多，不是吗？

她的语气比她本来想的更具有挑战性，更具侵略性，她用牙齿咬住了舌头。他的嘴角勾起一丝微笑。一个戏谑的、好奇的微笑。

“没有，”赫敏很快说，肚子紧紧地捏着。她在撒谎吗？或。不，这并没有困扰她，只是让她觉得——

她的胃一沉。 嫉妒。“我不嫉妒。当然不是你。赫敏转过身来，又开始在书架上找找，她的脸颊温暖，她的眼睛实际上什么也没看。

He’d probably had a million tutors growing up and Hogwarts didn't even offer to teach magical languages which was, frankly, ludicrous.
他可能在成长过程中有一百万个导师，而霍格沃茨甚至没有提出教授魔法语言，坦率地说，这很荒谬。

他在学校也只有时间进行这种个人研究;没有邪恶的阴谋需要挫败。当然不是每一年都是血腥的一年。

她甚至直到 11 岁才知道美人鱼是真实的，更不用说她们有自己的语言了。

她怎么能——

他和她的距离并不比在温室里时更近，但房间里昏暗的灯光和最近醒来的脆弱感让他感觉更亲近了。

无。她什么都不打算做。这不是第三年。他不是德拉科。她不会让他满意。她只是幻想着用她能鼓起的所有力量把她的肘部放回他的肚子里。赫敏把头转回她一直在做的事情上，马尔福的念头翻了个身，喘息着给了她一种奇怪的平静。

当有人把你肺里的空气都打掉时，他不会说任何语言，马尔福。

她拖着脚步靠近书架，双脚几乎不离开地面，以便在他的胸部和她的背部之间拉开一些距离。

赫敏抬起自己的手，把它们压在她的臀部上，不知为何，她想感受一下他会有什么感受。只是粗糙的牛仔布和挥之不去的......东西。瘙痒。

Lowering her hands and raising her eyes, she watched him reach up, pull a book halfway out and then push it back with a dissatisfied mutter. 
她垂下双手，抬起眼睛，看着他伸出手，把一本书拉了一半，然后不满地咕哝着把它推了回去。

“I think I should probably go, Mr Malfoy. It’s late… early. It’s…” she trailed off into a mumble because he clearly wasn’t listening anyway. 
“我想我可能应该走了，马尔福先生。已经很晚了......早。这是......”她喃喃自语起来，因为他显然根本没在听。

Malfoy glanced over at her, brow furrowed, apparently hearing her on a delay. He waved a dismissive hand. “Yes, off you go. I’ll tell you next week if I find the thing.”
马尔福瞥了她一眼，皱起了眉头，显然听到了她的延迟。他不屑一顾地挥了挥手。“是的，你走吧。如果我找到那东西，我下周再告诉你。

When Hermione closed the door behind her, Malfoy was still scouring his bookcase. She stopped outside in the corridor, trying to wrestle with the strangeness of the conversation they’d just had. 
当赫敏在她身后关上门时，马尔福还在翻找他的书柜。她停在外面的走廊上，试图与刚才他们谈话的奇怪作斗争。

Absolutely certain that she wouldn’t be able to sleep in Malfoy Manor, Hermione leaned into the guest room to collect her bag and returned to her own flat through the library Floo. In the end, she couldn’t get to sleep there either.
赫敏绝对确定自己无法在马尔福庄园睡觉，她靠进客房收拾行李，然后通过图书馆飞路回到了自己的公寓。最后，她也没能在那里睡觉。

“When Voldemort returned, how did you feel?”

Hermione reclined in her seat and crossed her legs, fixing Malfoy with an expectant look. They were back in his study, this time in the bright light of day. He didn’t look like he’d been drinking and Hermione silently noted that there were no bottles or empty glasses on his desk. 
赫敏斜靠在座位上，盘起双腿，用期待的眼神注视着马尔福。他们回到了他的书房，这一次是在明亮的阳光下。他看起来不像是在喝酒，赫敏默默地注意到他的桌子上没有瓶子或空杯子。

She’d managed to avoid bumping into him for the week following their conversation in his study, keeping herself cloistered in the library and hoping he wouldn’t seek her out to make her pay for what he’d told her. Now that she was sitting across from him and he wasn’t treating her any differently than usual, she wondered if he even remembered it at all.
在他们在他的书房里谈话后的一周里，她设法避免了碰到他，把自己关在图书馆里，希望他不会找到她，让她为他告诉她的事情付出代价。现在她坐在他对面，他对她没有和平时有任何不同，她想知道他是否还记得这件事。

“你当时就意识到了？”赫敏疑惑地皱起眉头问道。

赫敏张开嘴，犹豫了一下，皱着眉头看着马尔福。“我真的看不清你在哪儿——”

赫敏盯着他，睁大了眼睛，难以置信。这个男人什么都不尊重。

Oh . Hermione’s stomach dropped. 
哦。赫敏的肚子一沉。
