“多亏了那个男人的《麻瓜保护法》，我没能把几百年前的无价传家宝放在自己家里，但他的儿子冒着我们世界安全的风险，把他改装的汽车开到了全国各地，他被罚款五十加隆，还被问了一遍。我问你！

A smile trembled at Hermione’s lips. “This is obviously a sore point.” 
赫敏的嘴唇上闪过一丝笑容。“这显然是一个痛点。”

Malfoy’s expression was scathing.“Don’t start. Miss Weasley was not strictly responsible for her father’s idiocy, it’s true, but my family heirlooms were not baiting Muggles any more than his headline-making car.”
马尔福的表情很严厉。不要开始。韦斯莱小姐并没有对她父亲的愚蠢负严格责任，这是真的，但我的传家宝并没有像他那辆成为头条新闻的汽车那样诱饵麻瓜。

“If she wasn’t responsible then why give her an obviously dark object?”
“如果她不负责任，那为什么要给她一个明显黑暗的东西？”

“Well, I didn’t expect her to actually be able to use it,” he snapped. “The Dark Lord informed me he could use the book to open the Chamber of Secrets but he never explained how . He just told me to wait for his instructions and, as far as I was concerned, he was dead. I combed the blasted thing looking for any hidden text and found nothing. How was I supposed to expect that chit of a girl would tap into Dark Magic that I couldn’t? She wasn’t even a Slytherin.”
“嗯，我没想到她真的能用它，”他厉声说。“黑魔王告诉我，他可以用这本书来打开密室，但他从未解释过怎么做。他只是告诉我等待他的指示，就我而言，他已经死了。我梳理了那个被炸毁的东西，寻找任何隐藏的文本，但什么也没找到。我怎么能指望那个女孩的闲聊会利用我无法利用的黑魔法呢？她甚至都不是斯莱特林。

Lucius looked away from her, smoothing the legs of his trousers. He appeared agitated and uncomfortable which took Hermione rather by surprise. It was a sign he might actually feel something even if he didn’t ever intend to acknowledge it.
卢修斯把目光从她身上移开，抚平了他的裤腿。他显得焦躁不安，这让赫敏颇为惊讶。这是一个迹象，即使他从来没有打算承认，他也可能真的感觉到了什么。

“What on earth did you think would happen?”
“你到底觉得会发生什么？”

“I thought she’d be caught with it!” he said, his voice rising. “Even I didn’t anticipate that security was so lax under Albus Dumbledore that a dark object like that would get into the school. I planned to demand that the board of governors launch an investigation and use the news that Arthur Weasley’s daughter had been discovered with a mysteriously dark magical object that could easily be picked up by a Muggle to quash the credibility of his absurd Muggle Protection Act.”
“我以为她会被抓住呢！”“就连我都没想到，在阿不思·邓布利多的治下，安保如此松懈，以至于像这样的黑暗物体会进入学校。我打算要求理事会展开调查，并利用亚瑟·韦斯莱的女儿被发现携带了一个神秘的黑色魔法物品的消息，这个物品很容易被麻瓜捡到，来推翻他荒谬的麻瓜保护法的可信度。

Hermione curled her lip, making it perfectly clear that she didn’t approve of his aims or his methods in the least. “And when the Chamber actually opened, you didn’t think you should help? You just decided to take advantage of the situation and get rid of Dumbledore instead?”
赫敏抿起嘴唇，清楚地表明她丝毫不赞成他的目的或方法。“当商会真正开放时，你不觉得你应该帮忙吗？你只是决定趁势除掉邓布利多？

“Was he helping?” Malfoy asked lightly.
“他在帮忙吗？”马尔福淡淡地问道。

Hermione paused, her mouth opening and then closing as she absorbed his audacity. “You know fine well he was the best chance of stopping those attacks.”
赫敏停顿了一下，她的嘴巴张开又闭上，吸收了他的大胆。“你很清楚，他是阻止那些攻击的最佳机会。”

“To my eyes, he hadn’t been any more capable of stopping the attacks that were taking place during your school years than he had been fifty years previously, Miss Granger. I’m afraid I wasn’t blessed with the baseless faith in Albus Dumbledore possessed by so many of my peers in the Ministry so, no, I didn't think him especially worth keeping.”
“在我看来，他没有比五十年前更有能力阻止你们学生时代发生的袭击，格兰杰小姐。恐怕我没有像魔法部里那么多同僚那样对阿不思·邓布利多毫无根据的信仰，所以，不，我不认为他特别值得留着。

Hermione scoffed, crossing her arms tightly over her chest. “Don’t try to pretend you got rid of him because you thought you might find a replacement more capable of protecting the Muggleborns.”
赫敏嘲笑着，双臂紧紧地抱在胸前。“别想假装你摆脱了他，因为你觉得自己可能会找到一个更能保护麻瓜出身的人。”

“I’m not,” Lucius said, his eyebrows rising as though he thought her suggestion ludicrous. “I was merely pointing out that his absence didn’t actually change anything. In fact, I do believe it was in his absence that your Mr Potter successfully indulged his incorrigible habit of heroism.”
“我不是，”卢修斯说，他的眉毛扬起，仿佛他觉得她的建议很荒谬。“我只是指出他的缺席实际上并没有改变任何事情。事实上，我确实相信，正是在他不在的时候，你们的波特先生成功地放纵了他那不可救药的英雄主义习惯。

Hermione glowered furiously at Malfoy but he merely offered her a bland smile and a careless half shrug. “Did you know that I was attacked?” she asked tightly. 
赫敏愤怒地瞪着马尔福，但他只是给了她一个平淡的微笑和漫不经心的半耸肩。“你知道我被袭击了吗？”

“Were you indeed?” He sat up slightly straighter, an interested gleam in his eye that sent a flash of disgust through Hermione. He was making her feel like a morbidly fascinating museum exhibit. “I confess, that news passed me by. The names, you know.” He waved a dismissive hand. “It’s so hard to take them in when you’re not actually listening.”
“你真的吗？”他稍微坐直了身体，眼中闪过一丝兴趣的光芒，让赫敏心中闪过一丝厌恶。他让她感觉像一个病态迷人的博物馆展品。“我承认，这个消息我过去了。那些名字，你知道的。他不屑一顾地挥了挥手。“当你没有真正倾听时，很难接受他们。”

Hermione gripped her biceps with painful tightness and his eyes flicked down to her white knuckles, a similarly white smile ghosting across his face. “And how did you survive, if it’s not too rude to ask such a thing?”
赫敏痛苦地紧紧地抓住她的二头肌，他的眼睛向下瞥向她白皙的指关节，同样的白色笑容在他的脸上浮现。“如果问这种事不是太粗鲁的话，你是怎么活下来的？”

Nostrils flared, Hermione raised her chin proudly. “I worked out that the creature in the Chamber was a Basilisk. I was using a mirror to look around corners when it attacked.”
赫敏张开了鼻孔，骄傲地抬起了下巴。“我发现房间里的生物是蛇怪。当它攻击时，我正在用镜子环顾四周。

A small smile tugged at the corners of Malfoy’s lips and his eyes swept over her appraisingly. “You really have always been a very clever girl, haven't you?"
马尔福的嘴角勾起一丝微笑，他的眼睛赞赏地扫过她。“你真的一直都是个很聪明的姑娘，不是吗？”

There was bald admiration in his words but Hermione also detected a faintly mocking undertone that raised a sneer to her lips. “Your selfishness could have killed me.” 
他的话语中带着光秃秃的钦佩，但赫敏也察觉到一种淡淡的嘲讽意味，她的嘴角扬起了一丝冷笑。“你的自私可能会杀了我。”

“But it didn’t, did it? You made sure of that yourself. Quite cleverly, as I said.”
“但事实并非如此，是吗？你自己确定了这一点。正如我所说的，相当聪明。

“What if it had?”
“如果真是这样呢？”

“Killed you?” he asked, pushing out his lower lip thoughtfully. “Well, my afternoon would look very different right now, wouldn’t it? Far more peaceful.”
“杀了你吗？” 他问道，若有所思地伸出下唇。“嗯，我现在的下午看起来会很不一样，不是吗？要平静得多。

There was a tense pause, suddenly broken when Hermione huffed out a disbelieving laugh that could have transitioned quite easily into a scream of frustration and rage if she’d let it. 
一阵紧张的停顿，赫敏哼出一声难以置信的笑声，如果她允许的话，这笑声很容易就会变成沮丧和愤怒的尖叫。

Collapsing heavily against the back of her seat, arms still crossed, Hermione eyed Malfoy across the desk. He returned her stare boldly, unblinking, his face a mask. Hermione knew at that moment that she wouldn’t be able to extract anything else honest from him when it came to his memories of the Chamber of Secrets. There was barely any point in trying.
赫敏重重地瘫倒在椅背上，双臂仍然交叉着，盯着桌子对面的马尔福。他大胆地回以她的目光，一眨不眨，他的脸上戴着面具。赫敏在那一刻知道，当涉及到他对密室的记忆时，她无法从他那里提取出任何其他诚实的东西。尝试几乎没有任何意义。

“Were you not familiar with Horcruxes at all , Mr Malfoy? Couldn’t you even hazard a guess at what Voldemort had given you?”
“你对魂器一点也不熟悉吗，马尔福先生？你连猜猜伏地魔给你的是什么吗？

“No. Dark Magic is a vast and varied field and I never had any particular interest in the branches relating to mortality.”
“不。黑魔法是一个广阔而多样的领域，我从来没有对与死亡有关的分支有任何特别的兴趣。

“Why?”
“为什么？”

“Magic of that nature always requires an exchange—a significant exchange—and I do not see how it could be ever worthwhile. I have no interest in living forever, Miss Granger. I am not supposed to; it’s my role as a Malfoy to pass the family name and fortune along to my child and heir. That's our version of immortality.”
「那种性质的魔法总是需要交换-一次重要的交换-而且我看不出这怎么可能值得。我对永远活着没有兴趣，格兰杰小姐。我不应该这样做;作为马尔福，我的职责是将家族的姓氏和财富传给我的孩子和继承人。这就是我们的不朽版本。

Hermione’s lips quirked. “That’s rather arrogant.”
赫敏的嘴唇抽搐了一下。“这真是太傲慢了。”

“Perhaps but you have spent weeks of your life reading about us, have you not?” he asked with a self-satisfied smile. It faded as he continued speaking. “The Dark Lord never liked arrogance, you know; mine or anyone else's. Pitiful subservience was his preference, much as he’d deny it. Just look at Pettigrew.” Lucius flicked his fingers out as though clearing a pest from the air, his lip curled. “He loved to hate us, to look down on us. He never wanted an equal and in the first war I’d been young and foolish enough to think that he might have.”
“也许吧，但你花了好几个星期的时间来阅读关于我们的文章，不是吗？”随着他继续说话，它消失了。“你知道的，黑魔王从来不喜欢傲慢;我的或其他任何人的。可怜的顺从是他的偏好，尽管他会否认这一点。看看小矮星就知道了。卢修斯伸出手指，仿佛要从空气中清除了一只害虫，他的嘴唇卷曲着。“他又爱恨我们，又看不起我们。他从来不想要平等的人，在第一次战争中，我还年轻又愚蠢，以为他可能会这样做。

“ Was he angry at you, then? When he returned?”
“那么，他对你生气了吗？”他什么时候回来的？

“Oh, furious ,” he said lightly but Hermione thought she could hear an undertone of something else. Retrospective agitation, perhaps. “Hence my being tasked to lead the break in at the Department of Mysteries.”
“哦，生气了，”他淡淡地说，但赫敏觉得她能听到别的东西。也许是回顾性的激动。“因此，我的任务是领导神秘事务司的闯入。”

Hermione pulled her head back. “That was…a punishment?”
赫敏把头往后拉。“那是......惩罚？

“It was certainly a fool’s errand. I attempted to avoid going myself by placing viable targets within the Ministry under the Imperius curse but those plans failed because of the ludicrous condition that the prophecy can only be taken by those about whom it is made.” Lucius huffed out an irate sigh. “Of course, then the Dark Lord made it quite clear I would need to do the work myself. In person. By that point he had very little patience left so I had to cobble together a plan.”
“这当然是个愚蠢的差事。我试图通过在魔法部内放置可行的目标来避免自己去，但这些计划失败了，因为预言只能被那些预言所针对的人接受的荒谬条件。卢修斯愤怒地叹了口气。“当然，然后黑魔王很明确地表示我需要自己做这项工作。躬。到那时，他已经没有多少耐心了，所以我不得不拼凑出一个计划。

Lucius leaned an elbow on his chair and frowned down at the surface of his desk. “I knew the Ministry better than any of them, so I understood that it was very unlikely that we would be able to infiltrate the Department of Mysteries and get everyone out. Not in one piece. Then he insisted that Bellatrix join me as my second and my fate was sealed.”
卢修斯用手肘靠在椅子上，皱着眉头看着他的桌子表面。“我比他们任何人都更了解魔法部，所以我明白我们不太可能渗透到神秘事务司并把所有人都救出来。不是一体的。然后他坚持让贝拉特里克斯加入我，成为我的第二个孩子，我的命运就注定了。

At Hermione’s questioning look Lucius rolled his eyes impatiently. “You did not send Bellatrix to do infiltration and persuasion, Miss Granger. She was always so horrifically unpredictable and uncontainable—the exact opposite of what I needed in a room filled with fragile glass. She also unrelentingly resented me for having avoided Azkaban after the first war and made it clear she’d never follow my orders. I didn’t need a prophecy to know it was destined to be a complete fuck up .” 
面对赫敏质疑的眼神，卢修斯不耐烦地翻了个白眼。“你没有派贝拉特里克斯去进行渗透和劝说，格兰杰小姐。她总是那么可怕、不可预测和无法控制——这与我在一个装满易碎玻璃的房间里所需要的完全相反。她也无情地怨恨我在第一次战争后避开了阿兹卡班，并明确表示她永远不会听从我的命令。我不需要预言就知道这注定是一场彻头彻尾的混乱。

Hermione blinked. He so rarely swore, never mind with such vehemence. “But you still did it.”
赫敏眨了眨眼。他很少发誓，更不用说这么激烈了。“但你还是做到了。”

“Of course I did,” he snapped. “What else could I do? He would have liked us to succeed, I'm sure, but he did very little to make it easy. I suspect he wanted to show me that I couldn’t slither my way out of everything.” He narrowed his eyes on her. “Thank you for making absolutely certain of that.” 
“我当然知道，”他厉声说。“我还能做什么呢？我敢肯定，他希望我们成功，但他几乎没有做任何事情来让它变得容易。我怀疑他想告诉我，我不能从所有事情中溜走。他眯起眼睛看着她。“谢谢你绝对确定这一点。”

“你会杀了我们，”赫敏喊道，几乎不敢相信他真的会责怪她试图活下去。

He nodded. “And I’d have killed every single Death Eater I was with to try and get back to my wife and son. After my death, my capture was the next best way to leave them exposed.”
他点点头。“而且我会杀掉和我在一起的每一个食死徒，以试图回到我的妻子和儿子身边。在我死后，我的被捕是让他们暴露的下一个最佳方式。

Taking in a deep breath and holding it in an attempt to control her temper, Hermione eyed his face, finding nothing but sincerity there. He was ruthlessly protective but she couldn’t say she found it all that unrelatable. It disconcerted her.
赫敏深吸一口气，屏住呼吸，试图控制自己的脾气，她盯着他的脸，发现里面只有真诚。他无情地保护着她，但她不能说她觉得这一切那么不相关。这让她感到不安。

“What was Azkaban like for you?”
“阿兹卡班对你来说是什么样子的？”

“After such a catastrophic failure, it was probably the safest place for me. Though I suppose that’s not really saying much, is it?”
“在经历了如此灾难性的失败之后，它对我来说可能是最安全的地方。虽然我想这并没有说明什么，是吗？

“The Dementors still affected you?”
“摄魂怪还影响着你？”

“When you’re in Azkaban you’re fair game, Miss Granger. Dementors do not see sides as we do.” He pursed his lips and Hermione could see him picking absently at the skin beside his thumbnail with his forefinger. “It was my first real encounter with them, you know. “当你在阿兹卡班的时候，你是公平的，格兰杰小姐。摄魂怪不像我们一样看到任何一方。他抿了抿嘴唇，赫敏可以看到他心不在焉地用食指抠着拇指旁边的皮肤。“这是我第一次真正遇到他们，你知道的。我从来没有体会过......他们太糟糕了。

Lucius dropped into silence, a thoroughly introspective closedness behind his eyes. ”I’d never really considered my soul before,” he said quietly, almost to himself. If you are to retain even a fraction of your sanity, it's imperative that you establish one precious thing to which you can cling.”
卢修斯陷入了沉默，他的眼睛后面是彻底的内省。“我以前从来没有真正考虑过我的灵魂，”他轻声说，几乎是对自己说的。然后他抬头看向赫敏。“如果我能说一件事对他们有利的话，那就是他们帮助一个人找到某种观点。如果你要保持哪怕一点点的理智，就必须建立一件你可以依附的珍贵东西。

"What did you cling to?" Hermione asked, a slight hush to her voice as though she hoped asking quietly wouldn't scare him away from providing an answer. 
“你坚持什么？”赫敏问道，她的声音略带小声，仿佛她希望悄悄地问不会吓到他而放弃回答。

“我的家人。”他的声音很沉重，然后随着他的表情而变得僵硬，他补充道，“显然。你总是可以告诉那些一无所有的人——他们是第一个离开的。

“你知道他会在你不在的时候招募德拉科吗？”赫敏问道，回想起她花了整整一年的时间来否定哈利关于那件事的理论。现在感觉真是太愚蠢了; 她觉得自己很傻，因为她从来没有想过连伏地魔也不会这么低头。

“I strongly suspected he would,” he said, dipping his head. “Not least because I'd made it clear that I didn't want my son to receive the mark while still at school. It was his way of teaching me a further lesson.”
“我强烈怀疑他会，”他低着头说。“尤其是因为我已经明确表示，我不希望我的儿子在上学时就收到分数。这是他给我上了一课的方式。

“And what was that?”
“那是什么？”

“That I was as replaceable as my father.”
“我和我父亲一样可以被替代。”

Lucius uncrossed his legs and leaned forward to set his forearms on the desk in front of him. “Of course, he broke me out of Azkaban and I was supposed to be grateful for that.” His mouth tightened at the corners. “In some ways I actually was. And I expressed my gratitude by opening up my home to him. 
卢修斯松开双腿，身体前倾，将前臂放在他面前的桌子上。“当然，他把我从阿兹卡班解救出来，我应该为此心存感激。”他的嘴角紧闭着。“在某些方面，我实际上是。我向他敞开了我的家门，以表达我的感激之情。

“他是巫师的魔鬼圈套;总是想方设法让你更进一步、更接近。挣扎只会更快地杀死你，所以你保持不动并希望。

“Do you think he was planning to kill you?” Hermione asked, her voice quiet.
“你觉得他打算杀你吗？”赫敏问道，她的声音很平静。

Lucius’ eyes flicked to hers, the corners of his lips turned downwards. “It was a very popular view amongst my fellow Death Eaters that I would be better off dead, so killing me would have appeared dangerously close to kindness. 里面有一本书，她必须读。

一个只为她。

赫敏摇了摇头，对自己不合逻辑的思路感到恼火。她对房间的这一边一无所知——那里有一本书专门为她准备的想法是荒谬的。

但那本书就在那里。就一本书。

她确信，这也很有趣。

她怎么能确定呢？

它砰的一声掉在了地板上。

卢修斯看着她咽了口口水，低着头揉搓着她的网球鞋，突然间，他压倒性地意识到自己相对年轻了。

Would she tell the Aurors if he made no attempt at amends? They’d make his life barely worth living and he was already at a rather low ebb.
如果傲罗没有试图和好，她会告诉傲罗吗？他们会让他的生活变得几乎不值得活下去，而他已经处于相当低谷。

“Miss Granger.” Lucius clasped his hands behind his back and raised his eyes to the domed ceiling as he took in a deep, steadying breath. “I am…sorry.” 
“格兰杰小姐。”卢修斯双手紧握在背后，抬起眼睛看向圆顶天花板，深深地吸了一口气。“我......对不起。

The word felt unfamiliar on his tongue, especially in her company. The ‘r’s weren’t right somehow. Too many of them, maybe; why make that word longer than it had to be? 
这个词在他的舌头上感觉很陌生，尤其是在她的陪伴下。'r'不知何故不对。也许他们太多了;为什么要让这个词比它必须的长呢？

“I didn’t think—” He stopped and repressed a wince when she lifted her head to reveal sorrowfully large eyes. At least they’d stopped glistening. “I will have Draco comb the library tomorrow. We’ll make it safe and you can…explore freely going forward.”
“我没想过——”他停了下来，当她抬起头露出那双悲哀的大眼睛时，他压抑住了一丝畏缩。至少他们不再闪闪发光了。“我明天会让德拉科梳理图书馆。我们会确保安全，您可以...自由探索未来。

Rubbing at her eyes, she cleared her throat and nodded. He spied red marks on her wrist and scrapes on the backs of her hands that made him feel, dare he say it, uncomfortable. 
她揉了揉眼睛，清了清嗓子，点了点头。他发现她手腕上的红色印记和手背上的擦伤让他感到，他敢说，不舒服。

“Did I hurt you?” he asked. 
“我伤害了你吗？”

“Not really,” she looked down at her wrists and offered him a tremulous smile. “You helped me, I suppose.”
“不是真的，”她低头看着自己的手腕，向他露出一个颤抖的微笑。“我想，你帮了我。”

He blinked at that. He had helped her. Had he? Instinctively, he’d tried to, at least. How novel.
他眨了眨眼。他帮助了她。是吗？至少，本能地，他试过这样做。多么新奇。

“Allowing you to just take the bloody book would have been less physically harmful to both of us,” he grumbled, bringing a hand behind him to rub at his aching back. 
“让你拿走那本的书对我们俩的身体伤害会小一些，”他抱怨道，将一只手放在身后揉了揉他酸痛的背部。

He could still hear the smack of her hands hitting the floor. He’d been rather fortunate it hadn’t been her head. That would have been another reason for the Aurors to descend on him in a rather spectacular, murderous fashion.
他仍然能听到她的手敲打地板的声音。他很幸运，不是她的头。那将是傲罗以相当壮观、杀戮的方式降临到他身上的另一个原因。

“I think this is preferable to the humiliation of being forced to read about how to be an obedient little Mudblood, don’t you?”
“我觉得这比被迫阅读如何成为一个听话的小泥巴种的羞辱要好，不是吗？”

Looking around at the surrounding shelves, he muttered noncommittally, well aware that he wouldn’t have been the one reading about how to be an obedient little Mudblood, yet he was the one with a bruised spine. When he turned back to her, he found she was watching him intently. Too intently. It was making him uncomfortable.
环顾周围的书架，他漫不经心地咕哝着，很清楚他不会是那个读到如何成为一个听话的小泥巴种的人，但他却是那个脊椎瘀伤的人。当他转身看向她时，他发现她正聚精会神地看着他。太专注了。这让他很不舒服。

“Would you like tea?” he asked, the question falling out of his lips for a lack of anything else to say. Everyone offered tea after everything, whether it was a trying day or a minor trauma. “You can take it on the terrace.”
“你想喝茶吗？” 他问道，因为没什么可说的了，这个问题从他的嘴里说了出来。每个人都在一切之后提供茶水，无论是艰难的一天还是轻微的创伤。“你可以在露台上带它。”

“We haven’t found the—” she gestured to the wider library, clearly meaning the album they’d been looking for in the first place.
“我们还没找到——”她指了指更广阔的图书馆，显然是指他们一开始一直在寻找的专辑。

“I think that can wait, somehow,” he said, trying to keep his impatience out of his voice.
“我觉得那可以等一等，不知怎么的，”他说，试图把不耐烦从他的声音中挤出来。

Hesitating for only a second, she nodded. “Will you come?”
她只犹豫了一秒钟，就点了点头。“你会来吗？”

Eyeing the earnestness on her face, Lucius grimaced and swallowed his immediate urge to decline. “Very well.”
看着她脸上的认真，卢修斯做了个鬼脸，吞下了他立即想要拒绝的冲动。“很好。”

Eyes closed, enjoying the heat of the sun on her skin, Hermione breathed in the summer breeze. It smelled particularly nice in the Malfoys’ garden. Fresh, clean air, with a hint of something floral alongside freshly cut grass. The faint gurgle of the fountain nearby only added to the peace. She felt fractionally better now that she was out of that house. 
赫敏闭上眼睛，享受着阳光照在她皮肤上的热量，呼吸着夏日的微风。它在马尔福家的花园里闻起来特别好闻。清新、干净的空气，在新鲜割下的草地上带有淡淡的花香。附近喷泉微弱的潺潺流淌，更增添了宁静。现在她离开了那所房子，感觉好多了。

Opening her eyes, she found Lucius Malfoy looking at her rather oddly. Both like he didn’t want to be there and like he was waiting to have to catch her if she toppled suddenly from her chair. It was nicer than disdain and dislike, she supposed, but still quite irritating.
睁开眼睛，她发现卢修斯·马尔福正相当奇怪地看着她。既像他不想在那里，又像他在等着如果她突然从椅子上摔下来就必须接住她。她想，这比轻蔑和厌恶要好得多，但还是很烦人。

“I’m fine , Mr Malfoy. I feel much better. You were right in your choice of the terrace. It’s lovely.”
“我很好，马尔福先生。我感觉好多了。你选择的露台是对的。这很可爱。

He nodded curtly and added a splash of milk to his tea before taking a sip. She wasn’t sure why she’d asked him to join her; he wasn’t what anyone would call comforting company. It had just come out. 
他匆匆地点了点头，在茶里加了一点牛奶，然后喝了一口。她不知道自己为什么让他加入她;他不是任何人所说的安慰伙伴。它刚刚出来。

Presumably, she’d simply wanted him there at that moment. He had helped her after all, even if it had been in a somewhat aggressive fashion. Hermione rolled her wrists experimentally. They were fine. The growing ache in all of her muscles was more annoying. She arched her back, cringing at the pain. What on earth had he done?
大概，她只是想让他在那一刻就在那里。毕竟他帮助了她，即使它以一种有点咄咄逼人的方式。赫敏实验性地转动着手腕。他们很好。她所有肌肉越来越痛，这更令人讨厌。她弓起背，因疼痛而畏缩。他到底做了什么？

Relaxing gingerly into her seat again, she took a drink of tea and eyed him over the rim of the cup. The last thing she remembered was wandering down that row, an intangible force leading her along. Then she’d come to and found herself pressed to the ground by Lucius Malfoy. Not a standard Thursday.
她小心翼翼地再次放松到座位上，喝了一口茶，透过杯子的边缘看着他。她记得的最后一件事是沿着那排徘徊，一股无形的力量引导着她前进。然后她回过神来，发现自己被卢修斯·马尔福压在了地上。不是一个标准的星期四。

Awareness had all come rather back slowly. First she’d felt the pain of his hand gripping her wrist, then the press of his legs against her hips, then the solid stone under her back. As the room had come into focus, she’d come face to face with his utterly unreadable expression. An embarrassed warmth spread over Hermione’s cheeks as she imagined that scene from an outsider’s perspective. Trying to explain that to Draco if he’d wandered in would have been interesting.
意识都恢复得相当缓慢。首先，她感觉到他的手抓住她的手腕的疼痛，然后是他的双腿压在她的臀部上，然后是她背下坚硬的石头。当房间成为焦点时，她面对着他完全无法理解的表情。赫敏的脸颊上蔓延着一股尴尬的温暖，她从一个局外人的角度想象着那一幕。如果 Draco 走进来了，试着向他解释这一点会很有趣。

Horrified by the idea that she might have damaged them, Hermione had immediately set about picking up the fallen books from the library floor but when she’d straightened up and found Lucius gone, she’d felt unexpectedly uncertain. He hadn’t said he was going anywhere. He hadn’t told her if he thought there would be any more harmful books. Still feeling delicate, she’d decided to wait for him and the relief when he’d finally turned the corner had completely thrown her for a loop. 
赫敏害怕自己可能损坏了它们，她立即着手从图书馆地板上捡起掉落的书，但当她直起身来发现卢修斯不见了时，她感到意外的不确定。他没有说他哪儿也要去。他没有告诉她，如果他认为还会有更多有害的书。她仍然觉得很脆弱，她决定等他，当他终于转过拐角时，她松了一口气，这让她完全陷入了困境。

Imagine feeling relief at the sight of Lucius bloody Malfoy. 
想象一下，看到卢修斯血腥的马尔福时，你会感到如释重负。

“They’ll likely bruise,” he said, nodding to her wrists.
“他们可能会有瘀伤，”他说，一边朝她的手腕点点头。

She nodded, rubbing her thumb softly over one of the scrapes. They probably would. Most of her probably would. And he would be worried about anyone connecting that back to him. 
她点点头，用拇指轻轻地擦过其中一处擦痕。他们可能会。她中的大多数人可能会。他会担心有人把这件事和他联系起来。

“Don’t worry, I’ll be discreet ,” she said, a conspiratorial dip in her tone as she used his favourite word. “I’ll just tell Ginny I had a particularly amorous night.” 
“别担心，我会小心翼翼的，”她说，当她使用他最喜欢的词时，她的语气中带着阴谋论的语气。“我就告诉金妮，我度过了一个特别多情的夜晚。”

Her intention had been to be funny because Ginny would obviously never believe that of her but his expression turned stony and her smile slipped. “I’m joking,” she said quickly. “I’ve got bruise removal balm.”
她本来是想搞笑的，因为金妮显然永远不会相信她这样，但他的表情变得坚硬，她的笑容也消失了。“我在开玩笑，”她很快说。“我有瘀伤去除膏。”

He nodded once and she rolled her eyes. And people called her uptight.  
他点了点头，她翻了个白眼。人们说她很紧张。

“Will you really have Draco comb the library?” she asked. He nodded solemnly and she pursed her lips. “I thought you didn’t want me exploring?”
“你真的会让德拉科梳理图书馆吗？”他郑重地点点头，她抿起嘴唇。“我以为你不想让我去探究？”

“Miss Granger, you are drawn to trouble like a Bowtruckle to a wand tree, so I think it best if I remove all immediately obvious sources of danger while you’re in my home. I don’t particularly relish the idea of Aurors being able to accuse me of murder by negligence.”
“格兰杰小姐，你就像 Bowtruckle 对魔杖树一样被麻烦所吸引，所以我认为最好趁你在我家的时候消除所有显而易见的危险源。我不是特别喜欢傲罗能够指控我因疏忽而谋杀的想法。

Hermione snorted softly into her tea and shook her head. Of course that was his main motivation. Still, at least he hadn’t just left her. If she was honest with herself that’s exactly what she’d have expected him to do. That book wouldn’t have killed her but the idea that she’d have been imprisoned in a cycle of reading it, her mind subjected to its poison, made her feel sick.
赫敏轻轻地哼了一声，然后摇了摇头。当然，这是他的主要动机。不过，至少他没有就这样离开她。如果她对自己诚实，那正是她期望他做的事情。那本书不会杀死她，但一想到她会被囚禁在阅读它的循环中，她的心灵受到它的毒药，她就感到恶心。

“Thanks for helping me, anyway. Your father was a piece of work.”
“总之，谢谢你帮助我。你爸爸是个活头。

His cold, grey eyes cut to hers and she held her breath, worried she’d stepped over the line while wishing that he’d just make it more obvious where it was. 
他冰冷、灰色的眼睛直视着她，她屏住呼吸，担心自己越过了界线，同时希望他能把事情说得更清楚。

“Yes, he was,” Lucius said with a single, slow nod and Hermione immediately exhaled, offering him a weak smile which he didn’t return. 
“是的，他是，”卢修斯缓缓地点了点头，赫敏立即呼出一口气，向他露出一个虚弱的微笑，但他没有回应。

They sat in silence for a while, drinking their tea and looking out across the grounds. Outside that one meeting where Malfoy had ignored her for a full hour, it was the longest they’d ever sat in silence together without being occupied by other things. And it was…nice. Certainly not taut with fractious tension the way that early meeting had been. 
他们静静地坐了一会儿，喝着茶，望着外面的花园。除了马尔福无视她整整一个小时的那次会议之外，这是他们一起静坐的时间最长的一次，没有被其他事情占据。而且它是......好。当然不像早期见面那样因紧张而紧张。

Sliding her eyes from the bird hopping along the stone wall of the terrace over to Malfoy, Hermione covertly inspected him. He appeared deep in thought, his eyes fixed on a point some way in the distance, a finger stroking absently against the rim of his teacup. There had, she was sure, been a time when he would have found it amusing to leave her to that book but apparently they were no longer living in it. Suddenly, his touch that evening in his study didn't seem like such an unsolvable puzzle anymore. At some point, something had simply shifted. At some point, their fear of one another, their desire to hurt one another, had taken a back seat.
赫敏的目光从那只沿着露台石墙跳来跳去的鸟儿身上滑过，看向马尔福，偷偷地打量着他。他似乎陷入了沉思，眼睛盯着远处的某个点，一根手指心不在焉地抚摸着他的茶杯边缘。她敢肯定，曾经有一段时间，他会觉得把她留给那本书很有趣，但显然他们已经不在书里了。突然间，那天晚上他在书房里的触碰似乎不再是一个无法解开的谜题。在某个时候，有些事情发生了变化。在某个时候，他们对彼此的恐惧，他们想要伤害彼此的愿望，已经退居二线。

“Mr Malfoy,” Hermione began, toying with the handle of her teacup, “if you don’t—didn’t—like your father, why did you listen to so much of what he told you? Why did you do what he wanted?”
“马尔福先生，”赫敏开始玩弄她的茶杯把手，“如果你不像——没有——像你爸爸那样，你为什么听他告诉你这么多话呢？你为什么做他想做的事？

Coming back into himself, Malfoy turned to face her with a thoughtful frown. His finger that had been running along the rim of his teacup stopped and hovered over it for a moment before settling on it again, still this time. 
马尔福回过神来，转过身来面对她，皱着若有所思的眉头。他一直沿着茶杯边缘滑行的手指停了下来，在上面盘旋了一会儿，然后又停了下来，这一次还是。

“I didn’t like my father, Miss Granger, no,” he said with a brief shake of his head. “I couldn’t abide by his view of what it meant to be a father and a husband. He was cruel, even to those who would have loved him, had he let them.” 
“我不喜欢我的父亲，格兰杰小姐，不，”他短暂地摇了摇头说。“我无法接受他对成为父亲和丈夫意味着什么的看法。他很残忍，即使对那些本来会爱他的人，如果他允许的话。

He exhaled softly through his nose. “But he was good at being a Malfoy and that was what I, too, had to be – wanted to be. No matter how much I hated him, I wanted the Malfoy name and the things that came with it: power, influence, wealth. Success, in other words. He had everything I wanted and so I was sure that, detestable as he was, he must have been right about some things. Or at the very least doing some things right. He was a piece of work, as you say, but he was a hard man to dismiss entirely.”
他从鼻子里轻轻地呼出一口气。“但他很擅长成为一个马尔福，而那也是我必须成为的——想成为。无论我多么讨厌他，我都想要马尔福的名字和随之而来的东西：权力、影响力、财富。换句话说，成功。他拥有我想要的一切，所以我确信，尽管他很可憎，但他在某些事情上一定是对的。或者至少做一些正确的事情。正如你所说，他是一件工作，但他是一个很难完全忽视的人。

Hermione nodded and looked out over the grounds, feeling Malfoy’s eyes still on the side of her face. In that moment, in her tired state, it felt needlessly combative to ask him if he regretted wanting what his father had. A pointless question , he would tell her. And she wouldn’t disagree.
赫敏点点头，望向外面的地面，感觉到马尔福的眼睛仍然盯着她的脸。在那一刻，在她疲惫的状态下，问他是否后悔想要他父亲所拥有的东西，感觉毫无必要地好斗。 一个毫无意义的问题，他会告诉她。她不会不同意。

“I think I might go,” Hermione said when her tea cup was empty and the breeze had picked up just enough to be chilly. 
“我想我可能会走，”赫敏说，这时她的茶杯是空的，微风已经吹得足够冷了。

Malfoy nodded and got to his feet. Hermione looked down at the ground and realised she didn’t have her bag. “My bag,” she said, looking up at him. “I must have left it in your—”
马尔福点点头，站了起来。赫敏低头看了看地面，意识到她没有带包。“我的包，”她说，抬头看着他。“我一定是把它留在你的——”

“I’ll get it,” he said sharply. “I left the book in there and I’d rather you didn’t…I’ll get it.”
“我会得到的，”他尖锐地说。“我把书留在那儿，我宁愿你不要......我会得到的。

Nodding, Hermione settled back into her seat and watched him as he disappeared into the manor, her left thumb absently brushing over the scrapes on the back of her right hand.
赫敏点点头，坐回座位上，看着他消失在庄园里，左手拇指心不在焉地抚摸着右手背上的擦伤。

Chapter 19
第十九章Chapter Summary
本章小结

Hermione finally gets to look through the photo album.
赫敏终于可以翻看相册了。

Chapter Notes
章节注释

Thank you all for your kind comments on the last chapter. Wonderful people!
感谢大家对上一章的友好评论。很棒的人！

June 17th  
6 月 17 日

The photo album and a note were waiting for Hermione when she arrived in the Malfoy library. Lucius Malfoy was nowhere in sight. Picking up the note first, however, Hermione recognised his neat, sweeping handwriting. 
相册和一张纸条正在等着赫敏来到马尔福图书馆。卢修斯·马尔福不见了。然而，赫敏先拿起那张纸条，认出了他工整、流畅的笔迹。

The library is now safe for unbearably nosy wanderers.
图书馆现在对那些爱管闲事的流浪者来说是安全的。

Hermione grinned at the note, practically able to hear the lilting drawl he used when he wanted to cut but not deeply. Setting the sheet of parchment down, she turned her attention to the second thing he’d left.
赫敏对着这张纸条咧嘴一笑，几乎能听到他想切的时候用的轻快的拖曳声，但又听不见。放下那张羊皮纸，她把注意力转向他留下的第二样东西。

It was a thick album, bound in a deep green, soft leather. Hermione ran her hand over it, her fingers brushing under the edge of the cover. It didn't feel quite right to her that she would look through it alone. Obviously, though, he had left it there for that very purpose.
这是一本厚厚的专辑，装订在深绿色的柔软皮革中。赫敏用手抚摸着它，她的手指在盖子的边缘下抚摸着。她觉得自己一个人看完它不太对劲。不过，显然他把它留在那里就是为了这个目的。

Slowly opening the album, Hermione peered down at the early pictures. A pretty young woman Hermione recognised from news clippings as Aurelia Malfoy blinked up at her from a posed scene. Turning the page, Hermione saw her seated in the same scene with a woman and a man standing on either side of her, their hands on her shoulders. She assumed they were her parents. 
赫敏慢慢地打开相册，低头凝视着早期的照片。一个漂亮的年轻女子赫敏从新闻剪报中认出，奥瑞莉亚·马尔福从一个摆姿势的场景中向她眨了眨眼。翻开书页，赫敏看到她坐在同一个场景中，一个女人和一个男人站在她的两侧，他们的手搭在她的肩膀上。她以为他们是她的父母。

Flicking a few pages forward, Hermione recognised the original version of the photo she’d seen in the newspaper announcement of her wedding to Abraxas Malfoy. Gazing into the man’s eyes, cold even in a photograph, Hermione frowned. Initially she’d thought Lucius Malfoy was an exact replica of his father but now that she’d spent time with him she could recognise differences. His brows were less severe and heavy—they had some of Aurelia’s softness—and his lips were the same. When he wasn’t sneering, of course.
向前翻了几页，赫敏认出了她在报纸上看到的她和阿布拉克萨斯·马尔福结婚时看到的照片的原始版本。看着男人的眼睛，即使在照片中也显得冰冷，赫敏皱起了眉头。起初，她认为卢修斯·马尔福是他父亲的精确复制品，但现在她和他相处了一段时间，她就能认出不同之处。他的眉毛不那么严肃和沉重——它们有一些奥瑞梨的柔和——他的嘴唇也是一样的。当然，当他没有冷笑的时候。

On another page Aurelia and Abraxas were pictured at what appeared to be a garden party in the manor. There were other figures milling around but Hermione didn’t know enough about Pure-blood circles at that time to be able to identify them. Glancing over at the back of the page, Hermione looked for any names or notes but found nothing. It wasn’t especially useful if she didn’t know who she was looking at. 
在另一页上，奥雷利亚和阿布拉克萨斯被拍到似乎在庄园里参加花园派对。还有其他人在周围转来转去，但赫敏当时对纯血法阵的了解还不够多，无法识别它们。赫敏瞥了一眼书页的背面，寻找任何名字或笔记，但什么也没找到。如果她不知道自己在看谁，那就不是特别有用了。

A few more photos of unidentifiable figures later, Hermione closed the album, her lips scrunched in thought. Surely Mr Malfoy wouldn’t mind telling her? He had left the album out, after all. Lifting it into her arms, Hermione began carrying the album towards the door before stalling just short of it. Maybe he had left it out for her because he didn’t want to talk over it with her.
又拍了几张无法辨认的人的照片后，赫敏合上了相册，她的嘴唇因沉思而皱起。马尔福先生肯定不介意告诉她吧？毕竟，他把这张专辑忘在了外面。赫敏把它抱在怀里，开始把相册拿向门口，然后在它附近停了下来。也许他没有给她看，因为他不想和她谈论这件事。

With a shake of her head, Hermione carried on her way to his study. He had to realise by now that he couldn’t just give her something like this and not expect questions. The album cradled in one arm, Hermione knocked on his study door and waited. There was a long stretch of silence and she was considering turning around when he finally spoke.
赫敏摇了摇头，继续向他的书房走去。他现在必须意识到，他不能只给她这样的东西，而不期待问题。赫敏一只胳膊抱着相册，敲响了他的书房门，等待着。沉默了很长一段时间，当他终于开口时，她正在考虑转身。

“What do you want, Miss Granger?” came his muffled voice. Even through the wood Hermione could hear his weary exasperation and grinned. That sounded like an invitation to her. 
“你想干什么，格兰杰小姐？”即使隔着木头，赫敏也能听到他疲惫的愤怒，咧嘴一笑。这听起来像是对她的邀请。

Entering the study, Hermione found Malfoy sitting on his sofa before the fire. He turned to look over the back of the sofa when she entered, his eyes following her as she walked around it to come to a stop in front of him. There was a book open in his lap and the sight of it made her feel a tiny twinge of guilt. Interrupting private reading time was an unforgivable social sin.
走进书房，赫敏发现马尔福坐在火堆前的沙发上。当她进来时，他转身看向沙发的靠背，他的眼睛跟着她绕着沙发走，在他面前停了下来。他的腿上打开着一本书，看到它让她感到一丝愧疚。打断私人阅读时间是一种不可原谅的社会罪恶。

“I’m sorry, I didn’t realise you were reading,” she said, trying to convey that she was genuinely apologetic. “I can come back later.”
“对不起，我没意识到你在读，”她说，试图表达她是真诚的歉意。“我可以晚点回来。”

“No,” he said, his voice resigned as he closed the book and sat it on the small table beside the sofa. “You’re here now so tell me what you want. ”
“不，”他说，他合上书，坐在沙发旁边的小桌子上。“你现在在这里，所以告诉我你想要什么。”

Holding the album up in front of her face, Hermione lowered it to her chin to peer down at him. “You left this for me I assume?”
赫敏把相册举到面前，把它放到下巴上，低头看着他。“我想，这是你留给我的吧？”

“I did.”
“我做到了。”

“ Well .” Hermione turned on the spot and lowered herself onto the sofa beside him, pressing the album into his lap as she went. “I hoped you might be able to take me through some of the photos and provide me with some names and context.”
“嗯。”赫敏当场转过身来，坐到他旁边的沙发上，一边走一边把相册压在他的腿上。“我希望你能带我浏览一些照片，并为我提供一些名字和背景。”

Lucius blinked down at the album and then looked her in the face. “I thought it’d all be rather obvious.”
Lucius低头看着相册，然后看着她的脸。“我以为这一切都会很明显。”

“Not for every photo.” Hermione shook her head and scooted closer to him until the sides of their legs were touching, flipping the cover of the album open as she did so. His entire body was tense as she leaned forward and flicked over a few pages, eventually reaching the garden party. “This photo, for instance. I’m not really sure who everyone else is.”
“不是每张照片。”赫敏摇了摇头，快步靠近他，直到他们的腿两侧接触，同时掀开了专辑的封面。当她身体前倾并翻阅了几页时，他的整个身体都紧绷着，最终到达了花园派对。“比如这张照片。我不太确定其他人是谁。

Brushing her hair over her shoulder, Hermione turned her head to look up at him and found his expression muddled, like he’d short-circuited. “If you’d rather not, it’s okay. As nice as the thought was, I don’t need these, really; it’s more of a personal curiosity.”
赫敏把头发拂过肩膀，转头看他，发现他的表情很混乱，就像他短路了一样。“如果你不想，那也没关系。尽管这个想法很好，但我真的不需要这些;这更多的是个人的好奇心。

“No,” he said after a beat. “No, I can…” He cleared his throat and pointed through the faces, grouping the couples with his fore and middle fingers. “The Blacks; the Lestranges; the Greengrasses; the Notts; the Averys; and the Parkinsons.”
“不，”他打了一会儿后说。“不，我可以......”他清了清嗓子，指着他们的脸，用食指和中指把这对夫妇分组。“黑人;莱斯特兰奇一家;格林格拉斯夫妇;诺茨;艾弗里斯;和帕金森氏症。

“Ah." Hermione peered closer at the photo, looking over Malfoy’s finger. “Yes, she does look like Pansy.”
“啊。”赫敏仔细地看着那张照片，越过马尔福的手指。“是的，她确实长得像潘西。”

“That doesn’t sound like a compliment,” Malfoy said, giving her an amused sidelong look. 
“这听起来不像是恭维，”马尔福说，好笑地侧头看了她一眼。

“That’s because it isn’t.”
“那是因为事实并非如此。”

Malfoy laughed once through his nose and continued to turn the pages, quietly naming the inhabitants of the photos and explaining to Hermione where they were. They seemed to mostly have been taken at the various estates of the Pure-blood families. It struck Hermione as an active but extremely limited social circle and Aurelia Malfoy's smile appeared pretty but practised. Abraxas Malfoy did not smile. Ever. None of the men in the photos seemed to, actually.
马尔福从鼻子里笑了一下，继续翻页，悄悄地说出照片里的居民的名字，并向赫敏解释他们在哪里。他们似乎大部分是在纯血统家族的各个庄园被带走的。赫敏觉得她是一个活跃但极其有限的社交圈子，而奥瑞莉亚·马尔福的笑容看起来很漂亮，但很老练。阿布拉克萨斯·马尔福没有笑。曾。实际上，照片中的男人似乎都没有。

"Pure-blood men don't smile very much, do they?"
“纯血统的男人很少笑，对吧？”

Malfoy's fingers stuttered at the corner of a page and he turned his head fractionally towards her.
马尔福的手指在一页纸的一角结结巴巴地抽搐着，他微微地把头转向她。

"Why would they?"
“他们为什么会呢？”

"I don't know," Hermione mumbled, feeling silly for her observation in the face of his perplexity. "To communicate their happiness to be with the ones they love?"
“我不知道，”赫敏喃喃自语，面对他的困惑，她觉得自己的观察很傻。“传达他们和他们所爱的人在一起的快乐？”

Malfoy's single raised eyebrow in response made her blush and feel even sillier. As though her brain was determined to make things worse, she tried to explain herself further, the words coming in a rush. "Well, it might make them look a bit friendlier. I prefer it when you smile and don't do that awful sneer thing. It makes your lips softer. Your face, too."
马尔福的回应是抬起的眉毛让她脸红了，感觉更傻了。仿佛她的大脑决心让事情变得更糟，她试图进一步解释自己，话语匆匆忙忙。“嗯，这可能会让他们看起来更友好一些。我更喜欢你微笑的时候，不要做那种可怕的冷笑。它让你的嘴唇更柔软。你的脸也是。

Hermione could tell by the expression on his face that Malfoy was willing her to shut up and she couldn't say she disagreed with him. 'It makes your lips softer' would haunt her until her dying day. Even if it was true and she did prefer it.
赫敏从他脸上的表情可以看出，马尔福愿意她闭嘴，她不能说她不同意他。“它让你的嘴唇更柔软”会一直困扰着她，直到她临终的那一天。即使这是真的，而且她确实更喜欢它。

"Softness isn't a trait we value, Miss Granger."
“柔软不是我们重视的特质，格兰杰小姐。”

Risking a glance up at his face, Hermione was pleased to see that while he wasn't smiling, he wasn't sneering either. He was just inspecting her thoughtfully. Her eyes flicked down to his lips and back up. They were definitely more like his mother's than his father's; she could see that now. They weren't made for sneering.
赫敏冒险抬头看了一眼他的脸，很高兴地看到他虽然没有笑，也没有冷笑。他只是若有所思地打量着她。她的眼睛向下扫向他的嘴唇，然后又向上看。他们肯定更像他母亲的，而不是他父亲的;她现在能看到这一点。他们不是为讥讽而生的。

"Let's move on, Miss Granger," he said quietly, turning his attention back to the album.
“我们继续吧，格兰杰小姐，”他轻声说，把注意力转回那张专辑上。

As Malfoy turned another page Hermione gripped her own knees with delight. "That's you, isn't it? Please tell me that's you."
当马尔福翻开另一页时，赫敏高兴地紧紧抓住自己的膝盖。“就是你，不是吗？请告诉我那是你。

The photo was of Aurelia, her eyes lovingly fixed on a baby she was gently rocking in her arms. For the first time, her smile looked genuine. Hermione heard Malfoy sigh. 
那张照片是 Aurelia 的，她的眼睛深情地注视着她怀里轻轻摇晃的婴儿。她的笑容第一次显得真诚。赫敏听到马尔福叹了口气。

"I can and will end this."
“我可以而且一定会结束这一切。”

"I was just—"
“我只是——”

"It is me. And you will comment no further."
“是我。你不会再多说了。

Hermione pressed her lips flat between her teeth and bit down. The further they moved through the photos, the older Malfoy got and the more difficult Hermione found it to contain herself. 
赫敏把嘴唇贴在牙齿之间，咬了下去。他们越看照片，马尔福就越老，赫敏发现自己也就越难控制自己。

"You are vibrating ," Malfoy said, his voice heavy with disdain as he looked down to see her arm repeatedly brushing against his as she shook with laughter.
“你在颤抖，”马尔福说，他低头看到她的手臂反复擦过他的手臂，她笑得发抖。

"I'm sorry," she breathed, her eyes shimmering with mirth. "It's just...look at what you're wearing."
“对不起，”她喘着气，眼睛里闪烁着欢笑的光芒。“只是......看看你穿的是什么。

A toddler Malfoy dressed in absurdly frilly formal robes scowled out at them. He was held in his mother's arms while his father stood beside them in the adult version of those same robes. Aurelia, Hermione couldn't help but notice, looked far thinner and more drawn than she had at the start of the album. It dampened some of her glee.
一个蹒跚学步的马尔福穿着荒谬的褶边正装长袍，向他们怒目而视。他被母亲抱在怀里，而他的父亲则穿着同样的成人版长袍站在他们身边。赫敏忍不住注意到，奥瑞梨看起来比专辑开始时瘦得多，也更吸引人。这让她的一些喜悦有所减弱。

"I didn't exactly have a choice," Malfoy said through gritted teeth, struggling to maintain his air of stoic dignity. 
“我完全别无选择，”马尔福咬牙切齿地说，努力保持他坚忍不拔的尊严。

When Hermione failed to stifle her next laugh, Lucius gave a long-suffering sigh and moved to close the album. Hermione’s hand shot out and seized his wrist. “No, don’t!” she insisted, her eyes still watering. “I’m sorry, I swear I’ll stop.”
当赫敏没能抑制住她的下一个笑声时，卢修斯长忍着叹了口气，然后合上了相册。赫敏的手猛地伸出，抓住了他的手腕。“不，不要！” 她坚持说，她的眼睛仍然在流泪。“对不起，我发誓我会停下来。”

Eyebrows raised, Lucius looked down at her hold on his wrist and then back up to her face. Hermione’s cheeks burned and she relinquished him, her hands coming back into her lap, clenched. “You don’t need to take it so seriously,” she said. “It’s not like you dress like that now .” She directed a hand at him. “You dress very well.”
卢修斯扬起眉毛，低头看了看她握住他的手腕，然后又抬头看向她的脸。赫敏的脸颊灼热起来，她放弃了他，她的手又回到了她的腿上，紧握着。“你不需要这么认真，”她说。“你现在可不是穿成那样的。”她用一只手指着他。“你穿得真好。”

Lucius scoffed but reopened the album to where they’d been. “You are just full of observations about me today, aren’t you?”
Lucius 嗤之以鼻，但还是把相册重新打开了，回到了他们刚才去的地方。“你今天对我充满了观察，不是吗？”

“All complimentary,” Hermione pointed out primly. It was only when the words had left her mouth that she blinked, realising the truth of them. Eyes sliding over to him, Hermione observed the pressed sleeves of his shirt and the perfect fit of his waistcoat. No cravat again, she noted, just the open neck of his shirt. His manner of dress was formal but she did like it. She liked neatness, smartness. She liked attention to detail and Lucius Malfoy certainly had that. He dressed to his own advantage.
“都是赞美的，”赫敏一本正经地指出。直到这些话从她嘴里说出来时，她才眨了眨眼，意识到了这些话的真实性。赫敏的眼睛滑向他，观察着他衬衫的压袖和背心的完美合身。她注意到，又没有领结了，只有他衬衫敞开的领口。他的着装很正式，但她确实喜欢。她喜欢整洁、聪明。她喜欢注重细节，卢修斯·马尔福当然有这种感觉。他穿着对自己有利。

“All unnecessary ,” Malfoy responded, breaking her train of thought. Hermione cleared her throat and turned her attention back to the album, blinking rapidly. 
“都是不必要的，”马尔福回答道，打断了她的思路。赫敏清了清嗓子，把注意力转回相册上，快速眨了眨眼。

A few pages on, there was another garden party but this one was populated by young children. Lucius Malfoy, still dressed formally, stood beside three young girls in frilly dress robes and one boy. 
几页后，又有一场花园派对，但这次派对上都是年幼的孩子。卢修斯·马尔福仍然穿着正式，站在三个穿着褶边长袍的年轻女孩和一个男孩旁边。

"The Blacks," he said. "Our families were quite close in these years at our parents' insistence. I imagine marriage contracts were being discussed."
“黑人，”他说。“这些年，在父母的坚持下，我们的家庭非常亲密。我想他们当时正在讨论婚约。

"That's Sirius, isn’t it?" Hermione asked with surprise, pointing to the familiar young boy furthest to the left with long messy hair and mischievous eyes. He continually sidled out of the frame only to be shoved back in by a disembodied hand. 
“那是小天狼星，不是吗？”赫敏惊讶地问道，指着左边最远的那个熟悉的小男孩，他有一头凌乱的长发和调皮的眼睛。他不断地从画面中溜出来，却被一只没有实体的手推了回来。

"Yes, his mother thought it best that he spend more time with myself and his cousins. An attempt at establishing some corrective influences. I hated when he visited,” Malfoy added darkly. “Nowhere ever felt safe to sit down."
“是的，他妈妈认为他最好多花点时间陪伴我和他的表兄弟姐妹。试图建立一些纠正影响。我讨厌他来的时候，“马尔福阴沉地补充道。“从来没有任何地方觉得坐下来很安全。”

Hermione giggled at the thought of Sirius leaving a whoopie cushion down in every room of Malfoy Manor and received a glare for it. ”What age were you here?” she asked, straightening her face out.
赫敏一想到小天狼星在马尔福庄园的每个房间里都留下了一个百合垫子，就咯咯地笑了起来，并因此受到了一瞪。“你几岁了？” 她问道，直起脸来。

“I was 9, or thereabouts,” he said, tilting his head as he inspected the photo. “That would make Black around 4 or 5. Bellatrix…possibly 11? She was already at Hogwarts, anyway.” Hermione inspected the heavy-lidded eyes of the young Bellatrix with distaste. Even then she looked haughty and annoyed to be there, her hands on her hips, her chin raised and her eyes staring disdainfully out of the page. 
“我当时 9 岁左右，”他说，一边歪着头看照片。“这将使黑方在 4 或 5 左右。贝拉特里克斯。。。可能是 11 个？反正她已经在霍格沃茨了。赫敏厌恶地打量着年轻的贝拉特里克斯沉重的眼睑。即便如此，她还是显得傲慢而恼火，双手叉腰，下巴抬起，眼睛轻蔑地盯着书页。

“Andromeda.” He pointed at a brunette girl who was holding her hand out to Sirius, encouraging him to take it. “Was the same age as myself. Narcissa must have been eight.”
“仙女座。”他指着一个黑发女孩，她正向小天狼星伸出手，鼓励他握住手。“和我同龄。纳西莎肯定是八岁。

Hermione looked at the little blonde girl who would lean around Bellatrix at regular intervals to gaze with wide-eyed admiration at an utterly oblivious and visibly bored Lucius. It was so odd to her to see them all like this; to see proof that they'd all been children once. 
赫敏看着那个金发小女孩，她会每隔一段时间就靠在贝拉特里克斯身边，睁大眼睛羡慕地注视着一个完全忘乎所以、明显无聊的卢修斯。看到他们全都这样，她觉得太奇怪了;看到他们都曾经是孩子的证据。

"It must be quite nice to have all of these,” Hermione said. “Especially because they move. I’ve always liked wizard photos.”
“拥有这些一定很不错，”赫敏说。“特别是因为他们会移动。我一直很喜欢巫师照片。

“You don’t have such things?”
“你没有这些东西吗？”

“Muggle photos don’t move,” Hermione explained. “And I don’t have any. Not of my family, anyway. Well,” she said hesitantly, “that’s not strictly true, actually. I kept one but I sent the rest away with mum and dad and destroyed all of the photos I was in.”
“麻瓜的照片不会移动，”赫敏解释道。“而我没有。反正不是我家的。嗯，“她犹豫地说，”实际上，这并不严格地说。我保留了一个，但我把剩下的和爸爸妈妈一起送走了，并销毁了我拍摄的所有照片。

“You really were thorough, then,” he said quietly, watching her from the corner of his eyes.
“那么，你真的很彻底，”他用眼角的余光看着她，轻声说。

“Mmm,” Hermione nodded, a grim smile on her face. “I was just about to properly join the war and I spent my last few evenings in my parents’ home destroying all evidence of my childhood. It was all a bit too on the nose to be genuinely upsetting, actually.”
“嗯，”赫敏点点头，脸上露出阴森的笑容。“我正准备正式参战，我在父母家里度过了最后几个晚上，销毁了我童年的所有证据。实际上，这一切都有点太令人沮丧了。

“Which photo did you keep?”
“你保留了哪张照片？”

Hermione turned her head and found he was looking at her intently, unusually sincere interest on his face. For some reason it made her face grow warm.
赫敏转过头，发现他正专注地看着她，脸上异常真诚地感兴趣。不知为何，这让她的脸变得温暖起来。

“Just one of me with my mum and dad,” she said, breaking eye contact to fiddle with her fingers in her lap. “We were on holiday in France and we’d spent the whole day building a sandcastle on the beach. It was so impressive that someone offered to stop and take a photo of us with it.”
“就我和我爸爸妈妈的一个，”她说，中断了眼神交流，把手指放在膝盖上摆弄。“我们在法国度假，我们花了一整天的时间在海滩上建造了一座沙堡。这太令人印象深刻了，以至于有人主动提出停下来，用它拍张照片。

Hermione’s happy smile faded somewhat as she recalled the rest of the day. “Mum and dad said they think that was the first day I showed signs of magic. The tide came in and swept the castle away. I was distraught, of course. But then the castle sort of…reformed in the sand. As though it’d never been touched.”
赫敏快乐的笑容在回忆起那天剩下的时间时有些褪去。“爸爸妈妈说，他们认为那是我第一次表现出魔法迹象。潮水来了，把城堡冲走了。当然，我心烦意乱。但后来城堡有点......在沙子里改过自新。就好像它从来没有被碰过一样。

Hermione frowned at her knees. “Mum and dad didn’t really know what to do about it. Think they thought for a long time it was some kind of shared hallucination from spending too much time in the sun.”
赫敏皱着眉头跪在地上。“爸爸妈妈真的不知道该怎么做。想想他们长期以来一直认为这是由于在阳光下度过太多时间而产生的某种共同幻觉。

Malfoy scoffed but cut it short at a sharp look from Hermione. He frowned and pursed his lips, looking both puzzled and annoyed by his own instinctive self-censure.
马尔福嗤之以鼻，但被赫敏锐利的眼神打断了。他皱着眉头，抿着嘴唇，看起来对自己本能的自我谴责既困惑又恼火。

“They were—are—wonderful, intelligent, accepting people,” she said. “They didn’t always understand the wizarding world but they tried, even when I would choose it over spending time with them. I was always choosing magic over them,” she added regretfully.
“他们曾经——现在是——很棒的、聪明的、善于接受的人，”她说。“他们并不总是了解魔法世界，但他们尝试了，即使我会选择它而不是花时间与他们在一起。我总是选择魔法而不是他们，“她遗憾地补充道。

“You are a witch,” Malfoy said shortly, earning himself a surprised look from Hermione. “To reject magic for them would be to deny a part of yourself and you, Miss Granger, have made it quite clear that you’re incapable of making yourself smaller for the comfort of anyone else.”
“你是个女巫，”马尔福很快说，赫敏给了他一个惊讶的眼神。“对他们来说，拒绝魔法就是否认你自己的一部分，而你，格兰杰小姐，已经很清楚地表明，你不能为了别人的舒适而让自己变小。”

Hermione locked eyes with him, a rapid flutter passing through her stomach when he didn't look away. It reminded her of two days before, when she’d been lying under him and he, with a tight grip on her chin, had been inspecting her for any lingering bewitchment. Suddenly very aware of the feeling of Malfoy’s leg against her own, Hermione shifted under the pretence of getting more comfortable and moved hers away. “Let’s look at some more.”
赫敏与他对视相接，当他没有移开视线时，一阵快速的颤动从她的肚子中掠过。这让她想起了两天前，当时她躺在他身下，他紧紧地抓住她的下巴，一直在检查她是否有任何挥之不去的蛊惑。突然间，赫敏非常清楚马尔福的腿抵在自己腿上的感觉，她假装变得更舒服了，把她的腿移开了。“我们再看看一些。”

The final photo was of Aurelia and Lucius sitting together on a sofa much like the one Hermione was sitting on with him. Aurelia looked incredibly ill and barely present to Hermione, her cheeks hollow while her eyes sat large and sunken in her face. Her tiny arm was around Lucius' shoulder and he looked sad and anxious, gripping her hand in his lap. Hermione glanced at the adult Lucius as he took the photo in with thin lips. 
最后一张照片是奥瑞梨和卢修斯一起坐在沙发上，很像赫敏和他一起坐的那张。奥瑞梨看起来病得非常严重，几乎不在赫敏面前，她的脸颊凹陷，而她的眼睛则睁大而凹陷。她的小胳膊搂着卢修斯的肩膀，他看起来悲伤而焦虑，把她的手紧紧地抱在腿上。赫敏瞥了一眼成年的卢修斯，他用薄薄的嘴唇把照片接了进去。

"This was shortly before her death,” he said, his voice flat. “I was 14 here in the summer after my third year. She was 34."
“那是在她去世前不久，”他说，声音平淡。“我三年级后的夏天在这里 14 岁。她当时 34 岁。

34 . Before Hermione could truly register how young that was, Lucius closed the album, his hand remaining on the cover as though determined to keep it closed. 
34 .在赫敏真正意识到那是多么年轻之前，卢修斯合上了专辑，他的手一直放在封面上，似乎决心要把它关上。

"Thank you for showing me, Mr Malfoy," Hermione said quietly, her eyes flitting over his profile. 
“谢谢你带我看，马尔福先生，”赫敏轻声说，她的眼睛在他的侧脸上扫过。

He nodded and looked around at her, his eyes lowering to her hands in her lap. “Your wrists…” he began, trailing off inquisitively. 
他点点头，环顾四周，目光垂向她放在膝盖上的双手。“你的手腕......”他开始说话，好奇地慢慢走开。

Hermione followed his gaze and, assuming he was attempting to ask how she was after their misadventure in the library, rolled them gently before lifting one so that he could see it. 
赫敏顺着他的目光看去，以为他是想问她在图书馆的不幸之后过得怎么样，轻轻地滚动了一下，然后举起了一个，让他能看到。

“They’re fine,” she said, smiling at him. “I promise.”
“他们没事，”她对他微笑着说。“我保证。”

Though she’d moved away, Hermione could still somehow feel his leg against hers. He didn’t say anything more, simply looking at her narrow wrists with a faint frown between his brows as though he was considering reaching out to inspect them for himself. 
虽然她已经走开了，赫敏仍然能感觉到他的腿抵在她的腿上。他没有再说什么，只是看着她狭窄的手腕，眉间微微皱起眉头，仿佛在考虑伸手亲自检查它们。

Instinctively, Hermione’s attention was drawn to his hands atop the photo album and she found herself wondering, if she did offer her wrists up for his inspection, how gentle he would be. How gentle a man like him was capable of being. 
本能地，赫敏的注意力被相册上的他的手吸引了，她发现自己在想，如果她真的把手腕伸出来让他检查，他会有多温柔。像他这样的人，竟然能表现得多么温柔啊。

Rather than find out, Hermione averted her eyes uncomfortably, tucking her hair behind her ear just to occupy her hands.
赫敏没有发现，而是不自在地移开了她的眼睛，把头发塞到耳后，只是为了占据她的手。

The moment passed and, quietly, Lucius rose to his feet, the album in his grip. Hermione turned in her seat, arm leaning on the back of the sofa, to watch him as he took it to his desk and deposited it on the surface. 
这一刻过去了，Lucius 悄悄地站了起来，手里拿着相册。赫敏在座位上转过身来，胳膊靠在沙发靠背上，看着他把它带到书桌上，放在桌面上。

"I don't have any more recent albums for you, I'm afraid,” he said. “Narcissa was more interested in those things and she took ours with her."
“恐怕我没有更多最近的专辑给你了，”他说。“纳西莎对那些东西更感兴趣，她把我们的东西都带走了。”

"Do you think she'd send them if you asked her?"
“如果你问她，你觉得她会送他们来吗？”

"I doubt it; the divorce has been finalised. She need not have anything to do with me anymore and I mean no offence, Miss Granger, when I say she’d certainly want nothing to do with you." 
“我怀疑;离婚已经敲定。她不需要再跟我有任何关系了，我没有冒犯的意思，格兰杰小姐，我说她肯定不想和你有任何关系。

Hermione didn't miss the bitterness in his voice even if he managed to keep it off his face. "Are you angry that she left?"
赫敏并没有错过他声音中的苦涩，即使他设法把它从他的脸上压住了。“你对她的离开感到生气吗？”

“I sent her away, Miss Granger,” he said, leaning his knuckles on his desk. “Society here was unkind to her and I didn’t want her to waste the best years of her life and her freedom roaming the halls of the manor when she didn’t have to.”
“我把她送走了，格兰杰小姐，”他说，一边把指关节靠在桌子上。“这里的社会对她不友善，我不希望她浪费她生命中最美好的岁月和自由，在她不需要的时候在庄园的大厅里漫游。”

Frowning, Hermione tilted her head. “It surprises me that after everything she would have left Draco behind.”
赫敏皱着眉头歪了歪头。“我很惊讶，毕竟她会留下德拉科。”

“He wouldn’t go,” Lucius replied, a bite of frustration in his voice. “No matter how much we tried to make him. She still writes, I believe. Badgering him. He is, however, a grown man free to make his own decisions. These days I owe it to him to let him, regardless of how questionable I believe them to be.”
“他不会去的，”卢修斯回答，声音里带着一丝沮丧。“无论我们多么努力地塑造他。我相信她仍然在写作。缠着他。然而，他是一个可以自由做出自己决定的成年人。这些天来，我欠他让他走的，不管我认为他们有多么可疑。

Eyes flicking over Lucius’ irate face, Hermione bit her tongue. Obviously Draco thought his father needed him more than his mother. She didn’t think he was wrong.
赫敏的眼睛在卢修斯愤怒的脸上扫过，咬住了她的舌头。显然，德拉科认为他的父亲比他的母亲更需要他。她不认为他错了。

“Just say what you want to say, Miss Granger.”
“就说你想说的话吧，格兰杰小姐。”

Hermione blinked, her mouth opening for a second before she snapped her teeth together and shook her head. “I don’t want to say anything.”
赫敏眨了眨眼，张大了嘴巴一秒钟，然后她咬紧牙关，摇了摇头。“我什么都不想说。”

“The expression on your face says otherwise,” Lucius replied. “I’m afraid all the time you spend with books has made you rather easy to read. Say it.”
“你脸上的表情说明不是这样，”卢修斯回答。“恐怕你花在书上的时间都使你变得相当容易阅读。说出来。

Hermione rubbed her finger over the soft leather of the back of the sofa, not meeting Malfoy’s eyes as she said,  “It seems to bother you that she left even though you told her to. Is that really fair?”
赫敏用手指在沙发靠背柔软的皮革上摩擦，没有与马尔福的眼睛对视，她说道，“你告诉她，她还是走了，这似乎让你很困扰。这真的公平吗？

“It didn’t bother me that she left,” he said with a sharp, defensive edge to his voice. “It bothered me that she never seemed to miss me enough to want to come back."
“她走了我并不在意，”他的声音里带着尖锐的、防御的锋芒。“让我感到困扰的是，她似乎从来没有想念过我，以至于想回来。”

Hermione didn’t know what to say to that and, when she glanced up, she thought Malfoy looked like he wished he’d never said it in the first place. 
赫敏不知道该说什么，当她抬起头时，她觉得马尔福看起来就像他希望他一开始就没有说过这句话。

Part of Hermione thought that Malfoy had maybe got what he wanted in his wife’s leaving. Or what he thought he wanted. Draco had told her that he’d been closed off, barely speaking to him and Astoria. Putting together the pieces, it sounded like Lucius Malfoy had pushed his wife away until eventually she’d stopped pushing back and just allowed him to shove her out of his life entirely. Perhaps she resented him for doing it. Perhaps he resented her for letting him. But saying that aloud was out of the question. At the same time, offering comforting but meaningless platitudes did not seem like the kind of thing he would want either. 
赫敏的一部分认为马尔福也许在他妻子的离开中得到了他想要的东西。或者他认为他想要什么。德拉科告诉她，他一直被封闭起来，几乎不和他和阿斯托利亚说话。把这些碎片拼凑起来，听起来卢修斯·马尔福把他的妻子推开了，直到最后她才停止反抗，只是让他把她完全赶出自己的生活。也许她怨恨他这样做。也许他怨恨她让他。但大声说出来是不可能的。与此同时，提供安慰但毫无意义的陈词滥调似乎也不是他想要的那种东西。

"It’s not particularly pleasant to feel unwanted," he said with a calm detachment that made Hermione think he could have been observing an odd turn in the weather. A turn in the weather, however, would not have made Hermione’s heart skip a beat the way his disarmingly honest admission had.
“感觉不受欢迎并不是特别令人愉快，”他以一种平静的超然态度说，这让赫敏觉得他可能一直在观察天气的奇怪变化。然而，天气的转变并不会像他坦率的承认那样让赫敏的心跳加速。

Keen to inject a bit of levity into their afternoon, Hermione crossed her arms in a show of faux irritation. “Well, don’t think you’re going to get any sympathy from me on that front.” 
赫敏热衷于为他们的下午注入一点轻松，她交叉双臂，假装生气。“嗯，别以为你在这方面会从我这里得到任何同情。”

Lucius raised his eyes to hers and blinked once as though surprised she’d heard what he’d said. “Have you ever had your face slapped on a poster that says 'Undesirable' in huge letters?” she asked, eyebrows raised. “And then discovered that you’re not even number one ?” 
卢修斯抬起眼睛看着她，眨了眨眼，似乎很惊讶她听到了他说的话。“你有没有被一张用大字写着'不受欢迎'的海报打脸？”她扬起眉毛问道。“然后发现你甚至不是第一名？”

His face warmed into a smile as he cottoned on. That softness again, Hermione noted with a swoop low in her stomach. If she wasn’t mistaken, it was growing more frequent.
他的脸上暖和地笑了起来。又是那种柔软，赫敏在她的肚子上猛地一跳。如果她没记错的话，这种情况越来越频繁。

“Touché.” Lowering his tone as though asking her a daring question, he added, “Tell me, did being Undesirable Number Two make you more Undesirable than Potter or less Undesirable?”
“Touché。”他压低了语气，仿佛在问她一个大胆的问题，然后补充道，“告诉我，作为不受欢迎的二号人物，是你比波特更不受欢迎，还是不那么不受欢迎？

“Good question,” Hermione replied, rising to her feet and lifting her finger to her chin in a mocking imitation of pondering. “I mean, if Harry was Undesirable Number One then he was, by all rights, the most undesirable.” Lucius nodded. “But, then,” Hermione continued, walking around the sofa towards his desk with her hands clasped behind her back, “as Undesirable Number Two then surely I was a less desirable undesirable and, by extension, more undesirable overall.”
“好问题，”赫敏回答，站起来，把手指举到下巴上，嘲弄地模仿着沉思。“我的意思是，如果哈利是不受欢迎的一号人物，那么他就是，按理说，他就是最不受欢迎的。”卢修斯点点头。“但是，那么，”赫敏继续说，双手紧握在背后，绕过沙发走向他的书桌，“作为不受欢迎的二号人物，我肯定是一个不那么受欢迎的不受欢迎的人，推而广之，总体上更不受欢迎。

“Perhaps we didn't think it through,” Lucius said. “Dolores Umbridge never was the sharpest quill in the drawer.”
“也许我们没有想清楚，”卢修斯说。“多洛雷斯·乌姆里奇从来都不是抽屉里最锋利的羽毛笔。”

“An understatement,” Hermione said drily. “I think Desirable posters would have been better.” She came to a stop in front of his desk, rising onto her tiptoes and lowering again. “Y’know, ‘Hermione Granger: Desirable’. Much more palatable.” 
“轻描淡写，”赫敏冷淡地说。“我认为 Desirable posters 会更好。”她在他的书桌前停了下来，踮起脚尖，又放下了脚步。“你知道的，'赫敏·格兰杰：令人向往'。更可口。

She nodded authoritatively and smiled at Malfoy who, this time, barely lifted his lips in return, his face tight. Perhaps she’d overstayed her welcome. “Anyway, I'll get back to work. Thanks, Mr Malfoy.”
她权威地点了点头，对马尔福微笑，而马尔福这一次，几乎没有抬起嘴唇作为回应，他的脸紧绷着。也许她逾期了。“不管怎样，我会回去工作。谢谢你，马尔福先生。

Hermione left the room with a wave and Lucius listened to her footsteps travel back along the corridor, his fingers dancing an unsettled pattern along his leg that had been pressed against hers.
赫敏挥手离开了房间，卢修斯听着她的脚步声沿着走廊往回走，他的手指在压在她腿上的腿上跳动着不安的图案。

注释见本章末尾June 18th
6月18日

The summer punch was alarmingly pink and toe-curlingly strong and Hermione knew that it was entirely down to Ginny. During the latter weeks of her first pregnancy, Ginny had opted to drink vicariously and clearly that was happening again.
夏日的潘趣酒是令人震惊的粉红色，脚趾卷曲得非常结实，赫敏知道这完全是金妮的功劳。在她第一次怀孕的最后几周，金妮选择间接饮酒，很明显这种情况又发生了。

"Watch yourself," Hermione said to Ron handing him a cup, "it's—" Ron choked and dribbled some of the liquid down his chin while spraying Hermione's face with more. "Strong," she finished, wiping her cheek. 
“小心点，”赫敏对递给他杯子的罗恩说，“这是——”罗恩哽咽着，把一些液体滴到他的下巴上，同时又喷了赫敏的脸。“强壮，”她说完，擦了擦脸颊。

"There must be a bottle of vodka in this cup alone," Ron rasped, holding it under his nose for a smell test. 
“光是这个杯子里肯定有一瓶伏特加，”罗恩嘶哑地说，把它放在鼻子下试了试气味。

"Well, it's a baby shower. What do you expect?" Hermione asked drily, taking a far more careful sip through tightly pursed lips.
“嗯，这是个婴儿送礼会。你期待什么？赫敏干巴巴地问道，通过紧闭的嘴唇更小心地啜了一口。

They'd all gathered at the Burrow for Ginny's baby shower—a summer barbecue in the garden. There were faces milling around that Hermione hadn't seen in months but, growing exhausted by the repetitive small talk, she’d gravitated towards Ron because interactions with him and Harry never felt forced. 
他们都聚集在陋居参加金妮的婴儿送礼会——在花园里进行夏日烧烤。赫敏已经好几个月没见过一些面孔了，但是，由于重复的闲聊，她越来越疲惫不堪，她被罗恩所吸引，因为与他和哈利的互动从来没有感觉是被迫的。

"Is Hannah coming?"
“汉娜来了吗？”

"Yeah." Ron looked at his watch. "Should arrive any time. She was up visiting Neville yesterday and she stayed in Hogsmeade overnight. Said she felt bad that she kept missing our drinks nights with him."
“是的。”罗恩看了看手表。“应该随时到。她昨天去看望纳威，在霍格莫德住了一夜。她说她一直想念我们和他的酒会之夜，这让她感到很遗憾。

Hermione nodded, taking a sip of her punch through pursed lips and wondering if Neville’s being at Hogwarts—the school where a certain matron post was still being advertised—also had something to do with Hannah's visit. It felt more sensible not to comment and Hermione was grateful she’d not yet had enough punch to dull her instincts in that area.
赫敏点点头，抿着嘴唇啜了一口她的潘趣酒，心想纳威在霍格沃茨——那所学校还在发布某个校长职位的公告——是否也与汉娜的来访有关。不发表评论感觉更明智，赫敏很庆幸她还没有得到足够的冲击来削弱她在这方面的直觉。

“I mean, I tried to tell her that term ends next week and she’ll see him then but she—”
“我是说，我试着告诉她，这个学期下周结束，她那时会见到他，但她——”

“Hermione, Hermione, Hermione.”
“赫敏，赫敏，赫敏。”

The voice of George Weasley drifted over from their left and both Ron and Hermione turned to see him leaning against a nearby tree, shaking his head in disappointment. 
乔治·韦斯莱的声音从他们的左边飘过来，罗恩和赫敏都转过身来，看到他靠在附近的一棵树上，失望地摇了摇头。

“What?” Hermione asked, her eyes narrowing. 
“什么？”赫敏眯起眼睛问道。

“I heard from a little birdie called Ronnie that you've been using the Weasley’s Wizard Wheezebox to record Malfoys.” Hermione internally groaned and threw a glare in Ron’s direction but he was looking up at the paper chains in the tree above George as though they had asked him a very thought-provoking question. “Why must you use my creation for evil?”
“我从一个叫罗尼的小鸟那里听说，你一直在用韦斯莱的巫师喘息器来记录马尔福。”赫敏在心里呻吟着，瞪了罗恩一眼，但他正抬头看着乔治头顶树上的纸链，仿佛它们问了他一个非常发人深省的问题。“为什么你必须用我的创造来作恶？”

“Oh stuff it, George,” Hermione said sniffily. “I heard that mixtape you made Angelina; they were used for evil from the off.”
“哦，塞进去吧，乔治，”赫敏轻蔑地说。“我听说你做的那张混音带 Angelina;他们从一开始就被用来作恶。

George looked at Ron disbelievingly and held a hand up to his chest, choking out a gasp. “Clearly they're rubbing off on you, Hermione.” Ron shot George a sharp look of disgusted warning but he ignored it. “That was mean .”
乔治难以置信地看着罗恩，将一只手举到他的胸前，哽咽着喘息。“显然他们在蹭你，赫敏。”罗恩用厌恶的警告狠狠地瞪了乔治一眼，但他没有理会。“那太刻薄了。”

In her best imitation of Lucius Malfoy, Hermione raised her chin and looked down her nose at George. “And I can get meaner so watch it, Weasley.”
赫敏最好地模仿卢修斯·马尔福，抬起下巴，低头看着乔治。“而且我可能会变得更刻薄，所以看着它，韦斯莱。”

“Uncanny,” George whispered in fascinated horror. “Next you’ll be bleaching your hair and calling us all Blood Traitors.”
“不可思议，”乔治惊恐地低声说。“接下来你要漂白头发，然后叫我们都是血腥叛徒。”

“Oh, ha ha,” Hermione said with a roll of her eyes. She’d tried to play along but the feeling of exhaustion was sneaking back in—making fun of the Malfoys wasn’t quite as enjoyable as it had been in the past. “Burgers?” she asked, pointing in the direction of the grill and surrounding tables.
“哦，哈哈，”赫敏翻了个白眼说。她试着跟着玩，但疲惫的感觉又悄悄地溜进来了——取笑马尔福一家已经不像过去那样愉快了。“汉堡？” 她问道，指着烤架和周围桌子的方向。

“Ah, Hermione,” George said, with a pitying shake of his head, “a Malfoy would never eat a burger. Everyone knows they only consume souls. You’ve spoiled the illusion.”
“啊，赫敏，”乔治可怜地摇摇头说，“马尔福永远不会吃汉堡。每个人都知道他们只消耗灵魂。你破坏了这种幻觉。

Hermione laughed a little too heartily and turned away, her smile slowly fading from her face as she approached the food. It felt like a good time to sit alone for a while. Taking a burger and another punch, she slipped out of the crowd and found a quiet table under a tree where she'd be able to eat undisturbed. 
赫敏笑得有点太爽朗了，转过身去，当她走近食物时，她的笑容慢慢地从她的脸上消失了。感觉是独自坐一会儿的好时机。她吃了一个汉堡，又喝了一拳，从人群中溜了出来，在一棵树下找到一张安静的桌子，在那里她可以不受打扰地吃饭。

As she tucked into her meal, Hermione scanned the party crowd, spying various familiar faces. Lee Jordan was desperately trying to extricate himself from an intense conversation with Percy Weasley; Arthur and Molly Weasley were welcoming a gift-bearing Kingsley to the party with wide smiles and open arms; Dean Thomas and Seamus Finnegan were huddled together and giggling about something, approximately ten cups of punch littering the table between them.
当她大口吃东西时，赫敏扫视着派对的人群，窥视着各种熟悉的面孔。李·乔丹拼命想从与珀西·韦斯莱的激烈谈话中解脱出来;亚瑟和莫丽·韦斯莱带着灿烂的笑容和张开的双臂欢迎带着礼物的金斯莱参加派对;Dean Thomas 和 Seamus Finnegan 挤在一起，咯咯地笑着说着什么，他们之间的桌子上散落着大约十杯潘趣酒。

Hermione's eyes landed on Ron and she saw that Hannah had arrived. Except Ron didn't look pleased at all. They were gathered under a tree that was distant from the party and therefore not too far from Hermione. Though Hannah’s back was to her, Hermione could see Ron was speaking in an angry undertone, his ears growing pink in a way that had nothing to do with all the time he’d spent in the afternoon sun. 
赫敏的目光落在罗恩身上，她看到汉娜已经到了。只是罗恩看起来一点也不高兴。他们聚集在一棵树下，这棵树离派对很远，因此离赫敏不太远。虽然汉娜背对着她，但赫敏能看到罗恩在用愤怒的语气说话，他的耳朵变得粉红色，这与他在午后阳光下度过的所有时间无关。

Sighing, Hermione tore her eyes away from them. For one thing, it was obviously personal and she ought not to pry. For another, it wouldn’t look great to be caught dissecting her ex-boyfriend's arguments with his current girlfriend. It might give the wrong impression.
赫敏叹了口气，把目光从他们身上移开。首先，这显然是私人的，她不应该窥探。另一方面，如果被发现剖析前男友与现任女友的争论，那看起来就不是一件好事了。它可能会给人留下错误的印象。

Hermione had finished her burger and was just about through with her punch when Harry slid into the seat next to her with a fresh cup. “Just call me Trelawney,” he said, peering into the almost-empty cup in her hand before pushing the new one towards her.
赫敏吃完了她的汉堡，正要打完她的一拳，哈利就拿着一个新鲜的杯子滑到她旁边的座位上。“叫我特里劳尼就好了，”他说，瞥了一眼她手里几乎空的杯子，然后把新杯子推向她。

"Oh, Harry, I really don't think I should have any more of this." Hermione lifted a hand to her mouth as a distinctly punch-flavoured burp rose in her throat.
“哦，哈利，我真的觉得我不应该再有这些了。”赫敏抬起一只手捂住嘴巴，喉咙里发出一声明显的潘趣味的打嗝。

"Go on, Hermione,” Harry said bracingly. “You know Ginny will be gutted if at least one person hasn't puked in a bush by the end of the night. It’s her baby shower!"
“继续说，赫敏，”哈利振作起来。“你知道，如果到晚上结束时至少有一个人没有在灌木丛里呕吐，金妮会很伤心的。这是她的迎婴派对！

“I hope it's you,” Hermione said, taking the cup with a dark glare at her friend.
“我希望是你，”赫敏说，接过杯子，阴暗地瞪着她的朋友。

“Well, I'm on my fifth,” Harry responded, raising his cup in a ‘cheers’ salute, “so it probably will be.”
“嗯，我已经第五次了，”哈利回答，举起杯子“干杯”敬礼，“所以可能会这样。

“I take it you saw Ron and Hannah?” Hermione asked in an undertone. 
“我猜你看到了罗恩和汉娜吗？”赫敏低声问道。

“Yeah. It was kind of hard to miss it after a while,” Harry said, looking solemn. “But I pretended I did miss it, which is the important thing.”
“是的。过了一会儿，我很难错过它，“哈利说，看起来很严肃。“但我假装我确实错过了它，这才是重要的事情。”

“Do you think we should say something to him?” Hermione asked, though she was at a loss for what they actually could say.
“你觉得我们应该对他说点什么吗？”赫敏问道，尽管她不知道他们到底能说什么。

“And say what?” Harry asked, reflecting her thoughts back at her. “He’ll figure it out.” Hermione gave Harry a doubtful look and he laughed. “Or it’ll work itself out. For better or worse.”
“然后说什么？”哈利问道，把她的想法回想起来。“他会想办法的。”赫敏疑惑地看了哈利一眼，哈利笑了起来。“或者它会自行解决。无论好坏。

Glancing in the direction of a sullen Ron and seeing Hannah was nowhere in sight, Hermione felt less sure.
赫敏看了一眼闷闷不乐的罗恩的方向，看到汉娜不见了，赫敏觉得不太确定了。

“It's best not to get overly involved in each other's relationships, Hermione,” Harry said, following her gaze. “I tried to keep out of it when it was you and Ron.” 
“最好不要过度参与彼此的关系，赫敏，”哈利顺着她的目光说。“我试图避开只有你和罗恩的时候。”

It was true, Hermione thought. Even when she and Ron had been at their worst in the last six months of their relationship, Harry had been there for her without meddling or proffering any kind of unhelpful opinion. It had actually been…comforting in some ways. In their early school years, he’d tended to side with Ron during their arguments but as they’d grown and their dynamic had grown more complex, Hermione had noticed a change in Harry. It’d made her less worried about losing Harry’s friendship in the event of a break-up and, sure enough, they’d all gotten through it. It had all worked out.
这是真的，赫敏想。即使在她和罗恩的最后六个月里，他们处于最糟糕的状态时，哈利也一直在她身边，没有插手或提出任何无益的意见。它实际上是......在某些方面令人欣慰。在他们上学的早期，他倾向于在他们争吵时站在罗恩一边，但随着他们的成长和他们的动态变得更加复杂，赫敏注意到哈利的变化。这让她不那么担心在分手时失去哈利的友谊，果然，他们都度过了难关。一切都成功了。

“I knew there were parts of your relationship that I'd never understand or see,” Harry explained. “It didn’t feel right to offer a comment on it. So I figured I should just be there for you, not judge you, and not pretend I knew your relationship better than you did just because I was looking at it from the outside. With Hannah, we'll just be his friends and he'll come to us about it when he needs us.”
“我知道你们关系中有些部分我永远不会理解或看到，”哈利解释道。“对此发表评论感觉不对。所以我想我应该在你身边，而不是评判你，也不应该因为我是从外面看的，就假装我比你更了解你的关系。和 Hannah 在一起，我们就是他的朋友，当他需要我们时，他会来找我们。

“You're a wise man, Harry Potter,” Hermione said, sighing and tipping her head back. 
“你是个聪明人，哈利·波特，”赫敏说，叹了口气，把头向后仰。

“A wise man wouldn’t have given Ginny full control over the decor,” Harry replied, his eyes following the path of a group of mischief-making golden cherubs as they stole cherries from the cake, stuffing their tiny glowing faces. “That's a choking incident waiting to happen,” he sighed. Sure enough, within a minute, one cherub had a hold of another and was performing the heimlich manoeuvre.
“一个聪明人不会让金妮完全控制装饰，”哈利回答，他的眼睛跟着一群恶作剧的金色小天使的轨迹，他们从蛋糕里偷走樱桃，塞满了他们发光的小脸。“那是一场等待发生的令人窒息的事件，”他叹息道。果然，在一分钟内，一个小天使抓住了另一个小天使，并正在进行海姆立克急救法。

“How goes it with the Malfoys?” Harry asked distractedly, eyes still fixed on his decorations to make sure they wouldn’t choke to death. Obviously the deposit had been sizeable.
“马尔福家怎么样？”哈利心不在焉地问道，眼睛仍然盯着他的装饰品，确保它们不会窒息而死。显然，这笔押金是相当大的。

“It's…” Hermione shrugged and took a drink. “You know it's okay, actually. I've almost been enjoying myself recently.”
“这是......”赫敏耸耸肩，喝了一口。“你知道这没关系，其实。我最近几乎过得很愉快。

Harry’s eyebrows rose over the rim of his cup as he took a drink. “Really?” Hermione couldn’t blame him for the doubt in his voice. The last he’d heard she’d just had a storming argument with Malfoy that had almost ended their interviews.
哈利喝了一口水，眉毛从杯沿上扬起。“真的吗？”赫敏不能因为他声音中的怀疑而责怪他。他最后一次听到她刚刚和马尔福发生了一场激烈的争吵，几乎结束了他们的采访。

“Yes, it's...I don't really know how to explain it.” Hermione watched a cherub dip its head in a cup of punch and then topple off the edge of a table while its fellows cheered raucously. “I don't know if I could honestly say he's gotten a whole load nicer but he's not been quite as…” Hermione shook her head, the memory of his almost concerned gaze when they’d taken tea on the terrace burned into her brain. “Maybe I've just gotten used to him.”
“是的，这是......我真的不知道怎么解释。赫敏看着一个小天使把头浸进一杯潘趣酒里，然后从桌子的边缘摔下来，而它的伙伴们则大声欢呼。“我不知道我是否能诚实地说他变得更好了，但他并没有完全......”赫敏摇了摇头，当他们在露台上喝茶时，他几乎是关切的目光的记忆深深地烙印在她的脑海中。“也许我已经习惯了他。”

“They do say we can adapt to anything.”
“他们确实说我们可以适应任何事情。”

“Yeah...maybe,”  Hermione murmured. Adapting didn't feel like quite the right word to her but given she didn't know what did , she couldn't exactly correct him.
“是啊......也许吧，“赫敏喃喃自语。适应对她来说并不是一个完全正确的词，但鉴于她不知道什么，她无法完全纠正他。

"He showed me a photo album yesterday, actually, and there was a photo of Sirius in it. You'd have loved it, Harry; he was trying to escape the camera and I feel like even then he terrorised everyone with his pranks.”
“实际上，他昨天给我看了一本相册，里面有一张 Sirius 的照片。你会喜欢的，哈利;他试图逃避镜头，我觉得即便如此，他还是用他的恶作剧吓坏了所有人。

Harry smiled fondly into the distance. “It's weird to think of him as a kid, isn’t it?” His eyes refocused and he gave Hermione a curious look. “Not as weird as thinking of you sitting with Lucius Malfoy looking at a photo album, right enough.”
哈利深情地向远方微笑。“把他当成个孩子很奇怪，不是吗？”他的眼睛重新聚焦起来，好奇地看了赫敏一眼。“不像想到你和卢修斯·马尔福坐在一起看相册那么奇怪，就够了。”

“Yeah,” Hermione said noncommittally. Her leg felt warm with the memory of being pressed against Malfoy’s as they’d looked at the photos. The more she thought it about it, the more the heat spread through her.  Swirling her punch, she threw the last of it down her throat. “Sometimes he's not what I expected.” 
“是的，”赫敏不置可否地说。她的腿因为在他们看照片时被压在马尔福的腿上的记忆而感到温暖。她越想越觉得热度在她身上蔓延得越多。她挥舞着她的拳头，将最后一拳扔进了她的喉咙。“有时他不是我所期望的。”

“How so?”
“怎么会这样？”

“I dunno because in a lot of ways he’s exactly what I expected.” Hermione dropped her chin into her hand. “I guess it's that he…” she trailed off and looked into the distance, frustrated by her inability to organise her thoughts. Harry peered curiously at the side of her face. “He feels things that aren't just disdain and disgust. It’s...he’s…a proper person . Recently there've been moments where it's almost as if he – as if I – as if we –”
“我不知道，因为在很多方面他正是我所期望的。”赫敏把下巴放在她的手里。“我猜是他......”她慢慢地走开，望向远方，因为她无法组织自己的思绪而感到沮丧。哈利好奇地盯着她的脸侧。“他感受到的东西不仅仅是轻蔑和厌恶。它。。。他......一个合适的人。最近有些时候，他——好像我——好像我们——”

Harry’s brow was furrowed as he looked at Hermione closely. “Hermione, are you okay?”
哈利紧紧地看着赫敏，皱起了眉头。“赫敏，你还好吗？”

Hermione opened her mouth, not really even sure what she was going to say, when Kingsley appeared at Harry’s shoulder, making her close it with a snap. 
赫敏张了张嘴，甚至不确定自己要说什么，这时金斯莱出现在哈利的肩膀上，让她啪地一声合上了嘴。

“Hermione, Harry, I'm sorry to interrupt.” Kingsley’s deep voice was genuinely apologetic and he offered them a smile. “I wonder if I might have a private word with Hermione.”
“赫敏，哈利，很抱歉打扰。”金斯利低沉的声音是真诚的歉意，他向他们微笑。“我想知道我能不能和赫敏私下谈谈。”

Harry grinned and stood up to shake Kingsley's hand enthusiastically. “Of course, Minister. Always an honour to have you here.” 
哈利咧嘴一笑，站起来热情地握住了金斯莱的手。“当然，部长。有你在这里总是很荣幸。

"An excellent party, Harry,” Kingsley said warmly, “but I do feel I should warn you there's a group of rather inebriated cherubs floating alarmingly close to the grill. I got the impression a game of chicken was about to begin.”
“真是个很棒的派对，哈利，”金斯莱热情地说，“但我确实觉得我应该警告你，有一群喝得酩酊大醉的小天使在烤架附近飘来飘去。我有一种感觉，一场懦夫游戏即将开始。

Harry swore and took off at a run while Hermione chuckled. “I thought he would have learned that cherubs are the wrong choice after the coconut incident the last time.”
哈利咒骂着跑了起来，赫敏咯咯地笑了起来。“我以为他会在上次椰子事件之后明白小天使是错误的选择。”

“他们上演了一副真心实意的样子，赫敏，”金斯莱说，把自己放到哈利刚刚空出的座位上。“忘记他们的过错很容易。”

Turning her cup with her fingers, Hermione suddenly wished she hadn’t allowed herself to drink quite so much. Even slight insobriety felt like a massive disadvantage when in a conversation with Kingsley. 
赫敏用手指转动杯子，突然希望她没有让自己喝那么多。在与 Kingsley 交谈时，即使是轻微的不清醒也感觉像是一个巨大的劣势。

“I just wanted to ask you how your most recent batch of interviews are going.”
“我只是想问你最近一批的面试进展如何。”

“Surprisingly well,” Hermione said. “I was just talking to Harry about it, actually. Lucius Malfoy has been quite communicative recently. Helpful, dare I say it.”
“出乎意料的好，”赫敏说。“实际上，我只是在和哈利谈论这件事。卢修斯·马尔福最近一直很善于交际。有帮助，我敢说。

“Is that so?”
“是这样吗？”

“And the Malfoys have provided me with a space to work. In their library.”
“马尔福家族给了我一个工作的空间。在他们的图书馆里。

Draco had offered her the space to help but he'd also hoped to impress Kingsley. Hermione thought she might as well let him do that.
德拉科给了她帮助的空间，但他也希望能给金斯莱留下深刻印象。赫敏觉得她不如让他这样做。

“I see.” Kingsley fiddled with his earring and leaned back in his chair to observe the wider garden while they talked. “Well, that is somewhat surprising to hear. Pleasing, certainly, but…do you feel safe?”
“我明白了。”金斯利摆弄着他的耳环，靠在椅子上，一边交谈一边观察着更广阔的花园。“嗯，这听起来有点令人惊讶。当然令人高兴，但是......你觉得安全吗？

His eyes slid to her and noted the way she seemingly unconsciously rubbed one wrist and then the other. They appeared fine to his eyes. She appeared fine. 
他的眼睛滑向她，注意到她似乎无意识地揉了揉一只手腕，然后又揉了揉另一只手腕。在他看来，他们看起来还不错。她看起来还不错。

"Yes." She placed her hands on the table and turned her head to meet his eyes. "I do. Have you been sounding out what I asked of you?”
“是的。”她把手放在桌子上，转过头来与他的眼睛对视。“我愿意。你有没有把我对你的要求都说出来？

Kingsley inclined his head and crossed one leg over the other. “I have and it has been an enlightening experience."
金斯莱歪着头，把一条腿交叉在另一条腿上。“我有，这是一次有启发性的经历。”

"How so?"
“怎么会这样？”

"There are some who’d see him locked up for longer, as you’d expect. Mostly Aurors.” 
“正如你所料，有些人会看到他被关得更久。主要是傲罗。

Hermione nodded. She could understand that; the Aurors had spent years of their lives chasing the glory that would come with finally taking down Lucius Malfoy and in the end he had come quietly. She wondered if he'd taken some pleasure in knowing that he'd disappointed them. He was vindictive enough for that. 
赫敏点点头。她能理解这一点;傲罗们花了好几年的时间去追逐最终打倒卢修斯·马尔福所带来的荣耀，而他最终还是悄无声息地来了。她想知道他是否因为知道自己让他们失望而感到高兴。他对此已经足够报复了。

"Harry is less opposed than most."
“哈利比大多数人都少反对。”

Hermione looked up sharply to find Kingsley already looking at her knowingly. "Harry?"
赫敏猛地抬起头，发现金斯莱已经明知故犯地看着她。“哈利？”

"Yes." Kingsley nodded. "He told me he trusted your judgement."
“是的。”金斯莱点点头。“他告诉我他相信你的判断。”

A squirm of guilt worked its way through Hermione’s stomach. She wished she'd taken the chance to tell Harry the full extent of what she'd asked of Kingsley. She knew, of course, that Ginny would have told him after it had been revealed to her but talking about it personally was preferable. That would have to be a conversation for later.
一阵愧疚感在赫敏的肚子里蔓延。她希望自己能抓住这个机会把她对金斯莱的要求全部告诉哈利。她当然知道，金妮会在她知道这件事后告诉他，但最好还是亲自谈论这件事。那得等到以后再谈。

“And there are others," Kingsley continued, "who are similarly lacking vehemence. A few of the more administrative types said they wouldn’t mind him back in the Ministry for a while if he behaved himself.” Kingsley chucked at the sight of Hermione’s barely concealed disbelief. “I confess, you look how I felt. Apparently he was quite…effective. Dealt with red tape the way he did everything else.”
“还有其他人，”金斯利继续说，“他们同样缺乏热情。一些更行政的人说，如果他表现得好的话，他们不会介意他回到魔法部一段时间。金斯莱看到赫敏几乎无法掩饰的怀疑，咯咯笑了起来。“我承认，你看看我的感受。显然他相当......有效。处理繁文缛节的方式就像他处理其他所有事情一样。

“Like it was beneath him?”
“就像在他下面一样？”

卢修斯在最躲避睡眠的那个晚上一直在阅读她的工作。这很有趣，可能部分原因是它充满了她对自己所做的事情的持久兴趣。

Granger was just so interested in everything with that keen little brain of hers. Right now, she was interested in him. There was something about being the focus of Hermione Granger's interest that was both alarming and gratifying. It was a long time since he'd seen passion not borne from a desire to do harm, to destroy, but he was beginning to think it was no less potent for that.
格兰杰对她那敏锐的小脑袋对一切都如此感兴趣。现在，她对他感兴趣。成为赫敏·格兰杰感兴趣的焦点，这既令人担忧又令人欣慰。他已经很久没有见过激情不是源于伤害、破坏的欲望了，但他开始认为这种激情对这种欲望的效力并不逊色。

He'd been trying to figure out what it was that he enjoyed about interacting with her when he had spent so long closing himself off. He was starting to think that it was because she didn't make him feel like a problem. He was a solution for her – the person she wanted and needed to get something right – and it had been so long since he'd been that for anyone.
他一直在试图弄清楚，当他花了这么长时间把自己封闭起来时，他喜欢和她互动是什么。他开始认为这是因为她没有让他觉得自己是个问题。他是她的解决方案——她想要和需要把事情做好的人——而且他已经很久没有成为任何人了。

Of course, her interest wouldn't last. She'd get what she needed from him and then leave and his days would go back to what they'd been before her arrival: peaceful, long and empty. Good. Good? Yes, good. Definitely good. The sooner the better.
当然，她的兴趣不会持续下去。她会从他那里得到她需要的东西，然后离开，他的日子会回到她到来之前的样子：平静、漫长和空虚。好。好？是的，很好。绝对不错。越早越好。

It was best that he prepared for that day. It was, perhaps, even better that he expedite its arrival. Lucius’ eyes slid to the fire where the last of the parchment was burning up. No more teasing notes, no more tea on the terrace, no more warmth. No more.
他最好为那一天做好准备。也许，他能加快它的到来是更好的。卢修斯的眼睛滑向火堆，最后一块羊皮纸正在燃烧。不再有挑逗的音符，不再有露台上的茶，不再有温暖。没有了。
