June 22nd
6月22日

Hermione was surprised when Letty directed her to the greenhouse for her meeting with Malfoy. After the last time they'd been in there together she hadn't expected that he would ever let her return and she told him just that when she found him standing by his workbench, a pestle in hand. 
赫敏对莱蒂带她去温室与马尔福会面感到惊讶。上次他们一起进去之后，她没想到他会让她回来，当她发现他站在他的工作台旁，手里拿着杵时，她只是告诉他。

"I'm not asking for your help, Miss Granger," he said, barely looking up from what he was doing. "So you can rid yourself of that notion. I’m simply asking that we conduct our interview here today so that I can do this at the same time."
“我不是在找你帮忙，格兰杰小姐，”他说，几乎没从他正在做的事情中抬起头来。“所以你可以摆脱这种想法。我只是要求我们今天在这里进行采访，这样我就可以同时进行采访。

Hermione walked towards him and deposited her bag on the clear half of the workbench. "And what is 'this'?" she asked, removing the Wheezebox and Quick Quotes Quill from her bag. 
赫敏走向他，把她的包放在工作台的空旷半边。“那'这个'是什么？”她问道，从包里拿出 Wheezebox 和 Quick Quotes Quill。

"I'm powdering the asphodel roots for Draco's potions and it must be done before this evening," he murmured, pressing the pestle into the mortar. "Does that explanation meet your satisfaction?"
“我正在给德拉科的药剂做石槐根磨粉，今天晚上必须做完，”他喃喃自语着，一边把杵压进研钵里。“这个解释让你满意吗？”

"Yes," Hermione said, giving him a friendly smile as his head turned and his eyes rose to hers. Not seeing a seat, Hermione lowered her bag to the floor and, turning, lifted herself up onto the workbench so that she was sitting near where Malfoy was working but facing in the opposite direction. His movements stuttered and he glanced down at her legs swinging near him.
“是的，”赫敏说，给了他一个友好的微笑，他转过头来，目光抬起来看她。赫敏没有看到座位，她把包放到地板上，转身把自己抬到工作台上，这样她就坐在马尔福工作的地方附近，但面向相反的方向。他的动作结结巴巴，他低头瞥了一眼她在他身边摆动的双腿。

"Sorry," she muttered, stilling the movement of her legs. He didn't say anything but resumed powdering the roots with a little more force than before. Moody today , Hermione mentally noted. 
“对不起，”她咕哝着，让双腿的动作静止下来。他什么也没说，只是继续用比以前更大的力气给根部撒粉。 今天穆迪，赫敏在心里记下。

Placing the Wheezebox in the space between where she was sitting and he was working, Hermione tapped it with her wand. 
赫敏把喘息盒放在她坐的地方和他正在工作的地方之间的空隙里，用魔杖敲了敲它。

"I thought maybe we could talk about the period Voldemort spent in your home, after you'd been broken out of Azkaban."
“我想也许我们可以谈谈伏地魔在你家度过的那段时间，那时你被解救出阿兹卡班之后。”

"Oh, goody," he muttered with one particularly vehement twist of the pestle.
“哦，天哪，”他咕哝着，杵特别猛烈地扭动着。

"In our last meeting, you suggested he was reluctantly welcomed."
“在我们上次见面时，你说他很不情愿地受到了欢迎。”

"Yes."
“是的。”

"He was an unpleasant guest?"
“他是个不愉快的客人吗？”

Malfoy stopped what he was doing and gave Hermione an utterly incredulous look that distinctly asked her if she was joking. She shrugged in response, having received the reponse she expected, and he rolled his eyes. 
马尔福停下了手头的事情，用完全难以置信的眼神看了赫敏一眼，显然是在问她是不是在开玩笑。她耸了耸肩作为回应，因为她已经收到了她所期望的回应，他翻了个白眼。

"He had nothing on you, but yes."
“他对你什么都没有，但是是的。”

Hermione grinned and it only got wider when she saw the corners of Malfoy's mouth twitch. She got great enjoyment out of his reluctant pleasure in her company. In part because it made her feel better about the increasing amount she enjoyed his.
赫敏咧嘴一笑，当她看到马尔福的嘴角抽搐时，她的嘴角才变得更大了。她从他不情愿地享受她的陪伴中获得了极大的乐趣。部分原因是这让她对他越来越喜欢的感觉更好。

"Did the rest of the Death Eaters stay?"
“其余的食死徒都留下来了吗？”

His face dropped into tiredness and he returned to his powdering. "We were the headquarters, primarily for gatherings. They dropped in and out; we fed them if they needed to be fed, gave them a bed if they needed to sleep. The Dark Lord was an almost permanent fixture. As were myself, Narcissa and Draco. And dear Bellatrix, of course."
他的脸上陷入了疲惫，他又开始涂粉了。“我们是总部，主要是聚会的。他们进进出出;如果他们需要吃饭，我们就给他们喂食，如果他们需要睡觉，我们就给他们一张床。黑魔王几乎是永久的固定人物。我、纳西莎和德拉科也是。当然还有亲爱的贝拉特里克斯。

"He didn't send you back out to do work for him?" Hermione asked, thinking most specifically of the night they'd removed Harry from the Dursleys. 
“他不是派你出去为他干活的吗？”赫敏问道，特别想起了他们把哈利从德思礼家带走的那个晚上。

"No. He was at pains to make it clear that I was, without my influence in the Ministry, quite useless to him. Doubly so as an Azkaban escapee."
“不。他煞费苦心地表明，如果没有我在魔法部的影响力，我对他来说完全没有用处。作为一个阿兹卡班的逃亡者更是如此。

"So, what did you do?"
“那么，你做了什么？”

"Waited for any chance to prove myself and told Narcissa and Draco to do the same. Returning to his favour felt like the only way to survive but opportunities were increasingly hard to come by."
“等待任何证明自己的机会，并告诉纳西莎和德拉科也这样做。回到他的青睐似乎是生存的唯一途径，但机会越来越难获得。

"Didn't you consider turning? Even just for protection?"
“你没想过转身吗？哪怕只是为了保护？

Lucius kept his head down but shook it, his shoulders lifting with a single humourless chuckle. "No. It was well past that point, Miss Granger."
卢修斯一直低着头，但还是摇了摇，他的肩膀抬起，发出一声毫无幽默感的笑声。“不。早就过了那个时候了，格兰杰小姐。

Hermione inspected his firm, forceful movements with the pestle. He had removed his rings to do the work and she spied them on the far side of the table, far from what he was doing. 
赫敏用杵检查着他坚定而有力的动作。他摘下了他的戒指来做这项工作，她在桌子的另一边偷看它们，离他正在做的事情很远。

“你是个很小心的人，马尔福先生，不是吗？”

"I would hardly rush to describe myself as care less ."
“我几乎不会急于将自己描述为不在乎。”

"You couldn't see any way of reaching out to the Order that wasn't careless?"
“你看不出有什么办法可以不粗心地联系教团吗？”

Malfoy stilled and raised his head to give her a sidelong look. "Even if I had wanted to do such a thing, which I most certainly did not , we were quite closely watched. We had to move up in the Dark Lord's esteem or not at all. I had chosen my path, Miss Granger, and it narrowed and shortened with each passing day."
马尔福静了下来，抬起头来，斜头看了她一眼。“即使我想做这样的事情，但我肯定没有，我们还是受到了相当密切的监视。我们不得不在黑魔王的尊重中上升，或者根本不在乎。我选择了自己的路，格兰杰小姐，它一天比一天变窄，越来越短。

"But you were tortured by him." She said it as a statement rather than a question. There was no point pretending she didn't know. "All of you."
“但你被他折磨了。”她说这句话是为了陈述，而不是一个问题。假装她不知道是没有意义的。“你们所有人。”

Lucius set his pestle down on the workbench entirely, his hand still resting on it as he turned to observe her fully. "And I suppose Draco told you that, did he?" The question was perfectly polite but there was an edge to his tone, as though he thought she might be making fun of him. 
卢修斯把杵完全放在工作台上，他的手仍然放在上面，转过身来仔细观察她。“我想德拉科是告诉你的，是吗？”“这个问题非常有礼貌，但他的语气里却带着一丝锋芒，仿佛他觉得她可能在取笑他。

"He did," Hermione said, nervously swinging her legs once before halting when she remembered how much it annoyed him. And Luna. "But he wasn't willing to say much."
“他做到了，”赫敏说，紧张地摆动了一下双腿，然后当她想起这让他有多恼火时，她停了下来。 还有 Luna。 “但他不愿意说太多。”

Snatching up the pestle, Malfoy began powdering with more force than ever. Hermione half expected him to go through the mortar to the table.
马尔福抓起杵，开始用比以往任何时候都大的力气给杵上粉。赫敏半信半疑地希望他能穿过砂浆走到桌子上。

"He said that was more your story to tell."
“他说那更像是你的故事。”

"Did he now?"
“他现在呢？”

"Yes." 
“是的。”

Lucius' chest swelled and his movements steadily slowed until they came to a stop. He took a moment before looking up at her, an unusually earnest tilt to his eyebrows. "I tried to protect Narcissa and Draco. I did. I always placed myself between him and them."
卢修斯的胸口膨胀，他的动作稳步减慢，直到停了下来。他过了一会儿才抬头看着她，眉毛异常认真地歪了歪。“我试图保护纳西莎和德拉科。我做了。我总是把自己放在他和他们之间。

"But he still…?"
“但他还是......？”

"I...failed,” he said, looking down at the asphodel blankly as though he could still hardly believe it. “I couldn't always stay conscious through the pain and when I couldn't he would move on. To them."
“我......失败了，“他说，茫然地低头看着 Asphodel，仿佛他仍然难以置信。“我无法在痛苦中始终保持清醒，当我不能时，他会继续前进。对他们来说。

Hermione set her hand flat on the workbench, her fingers twitching as though desperate to move. But she didn't extend her hand towards him as she would have done with Draco. Something held her back.
赫敏把手平放在工作台上，手指抽搐着，仿佛急于移动。但她没有像对德拉科那样向他伸出手。有什么东西阻碍了她。

"Why did he do it?"
“他为什么要这样做？”

"He didn't need a reason, Miss Granger. We were there for every piece of news. Good and bad. Both elicited…reactions."
“他不需要理由，格兰杰小姐。我们在那里听到每一条新闻。好与坏。两者都引起了......反应。

Hermione's fingers pressed against the table and, against her better judgement, she allowed her hand to inch towards him. It sounded like Voldemort had used the entire Malfoy family as a stress ball and sympathy was her natural reaction.
赫敏的手指按在桌子上，与她更好的判断相反，她让她的手慢慢地向他靠近。听起来像是伏地魔把整个马尔福家族当作压力球，而同情是她的自然反应。

"What did he do to you?"
“他对你做了什么？”

"The Cruciatus curse, mostly." Malfoy glanced down at her hand and returned to his work with an indifferent shrug but Hermione suspected it was an affected indifference. "The Dark Lord wasn't hugely creative in that area. He much preferred efficiency. Anything else would be wasting time on people who didn't deserve it."
“主要是十字架诅咒。”马尔福低头看了一眼她的手，冷漠地耸了耸肩，继续他的工作，但赫敏怀疑那是一种受影响的冷漠。“黑魔王在这方面没有很大的创造力。他更喜欢效率。其他任何事情都会在不值得的人身上浪费时间。

"Did you have to see him—"
“你得见他吗——”

"Yes, I had to see him perform the curse on my family, Miss Granger. No, I did not enjoy it. Yes, I still think about it."
“是的，我必须看到他对我的家人施行诅咒，格兰杰小姐。不，我不喜欢它。是的，我仍然在想。

"How did it feel?"
“感觉如何？”

"You're no stranger to the Cruciatus curse," he pointed out coldly. "Surely you don't need to ask that." His eyes met hers and his lip curled. “It hurt.”
“你对十字架诅咒并不陌生，”他冷冷地指出。“你当然不需要问那个。”他的眼睛与她的目光相遇，嘴唇弯起。“好痛。”

Hermione frowned at his flippant reference to her own torture and turned the question. "Then how did it feel to go through what you'd put so many other families through? Did you ever think about them when you watched him torture your own family?"
赫敏对他轻率地提到她自己的折磨皱起了眉头，然后转过了问题。“那么，你让这么多其他家庭经历了这一切，感觉如何？当你看到他折磨你自己的家人时，你有没有想过他们？

Lucius narrowed his eyes at her and returned them to the mortar, dragging his teeth along his bottom lip. "Taking no prisoners today, hm? Well, no. I did not. I'm sure it would be satisfying for you to hear that I wept and beat my breast, drowning in the collective pain of all those I wronged. But I didn't actually have a great deal of clarity in those moments to consider anything except what was in front of me and how helpless I was to stop it. If I was even conscious in those moments at all."
卢修斯眯起眼睛看着她，把眼睛放回砂浆上，用牙齿咬着下唇。“今天不抓俘虏，嗯？嗯，不是。我没有。我相信，如果听到我哭泣、捶胸顿足，淹没在所有我冤枉的人的集体痛苦中，你会感到满足。但在那些时刻，我实际上并没有很清晰的思路去考虑任何事情，除了眼前的事情以及我是多么无助地阻止它。如果我在那些时刻还有意识的话。

"What do you think of it now?"
“你现在觉得怎么样？”

He took a deep breath, his shoulders rising, and then leaned his hands on the workbench, the pestle clutched in his fist. "I wasn't actually ever a very big proponent of the Cruciatus curse so I don't think it was a particularly poetic form of justice."
他深吸一口气，肩膀抬起，然后双手靠在工作台上，杵紧握在拳头里。“实际上，我从来都不是十字架诅咒的大力支持者，所以我不认为这是一种特别诗意的正义形式。”

Hermione was stunned into a silence, faint disgust at his coldness clear on her face. Seeing it, he smiled unpleasantly. Not his soft smile, she noted. Not a real smile. He looked like the old Lucius Malfoy. It was strange that there was an old Lucius Malfoy to her. Stranger that she could miss the one she felt she was getting to know. "I always favoured the Imperius curse."
赫敏惊呆了，沉默了下来，脸上对他的冷漠感到淡淡的厌恶。见状，他不悦地笑了笑。不是他温柔的笑容，她注意到。不是真正的微笑。他看起来像老卢修斯·马尔福。奇怪的是，她竟然有一个老卢修斯·马尔福。更奇怪的是，她会错过她觉得自己正在了解的那个人。“我一直都喜欢帝王诅咒。”

"For torture?"
“为了折磨？”

If Malfoy heard the doubt in her voice, he didn't acknowledge it. "Of course."
如果马尔福听到了她声音中的疑惑，他并没有承认。“当然。”

"You can't torture with the Imperius curse, Mr Malfoy." Hermione said it but even to her own ears she didn't sound certain. 
“你不能用不死咒来折磨人，马尔福先生。”赫敏说了，但即使她自己听来，她听起来也不太确定。

"Can't you?" he asked, his eyebrows rising. "It has many benefits over the Cruciatus curse or vulgar physical torture. For one thing, it doesn’t leave a mark. Nor does it push the body to the brink, so it can be used for a prolonged period."
“你不能吗？” 他问道，眉毛扬起。“它比十字架诅咒或粗俗的身体折磨有很多好处。首先，它不会留下任何痕迹。它也不会将身体推向边缘，因此可以长时间使用。

“那么它有什么作用呢？”

"It gives you a certain power to humiliate and bend the mind without risk of breakage. People can only ever take so much of that."
“它给了你某种力量来羞辱和扭曲思想，而不会有破裂的风险。人们只能承受这么多。

Said with the authority of a man who knows.
“以一个知情人的权威说。

"But they wouldn't remember," she said. 
“但他们不会记得，”她说。

He relinquished the pestle and straightened up, his eyes fixed on hers. Despite the heat of the greenhouse, a chill passed through Hermione and the hairs on her arms stood on end. 
他放下杵，直起身来，眼睛盯着她。尽管温室很热，但一股寒意传遍了赫敏，她手臂上的汗毛都竖了起来。

"There’s always some awareness in the Imperius Curse, though it varies from person to person. Often, it’s like watching oneself from behind thick glass or underwater. But for clarity’s sake, there's no reason why you can't show their memories—or yours—back to them," he said with the tone of a teacher explaining a simple concept. "Make them watch the things they've done for a few hours, maybe days."
“冥王诅咒中总有一些意识，尽管它因人而异。通常，这就像从厚玻璃后面或水下看着自己。但为了清楚起见，你没有理由不把他们的记忆——或者你的——还给他们看，“他用老师解释一个简单的概念的语气说。“让他们花几个小时，也许几天来观察他们所做的事情。”

“It's a far more intimate form of torture and leaves a more...lasting impression than the Cruciatus curse. Done right it can make a person begin to doubt who they truly are at their core. The self is a very fragile thing. Even the strongest person will break when you have them hurt their own family."
“这是一种更亲密的酷刑形式，留下了更......比十字架诅咒更持久的印象。如果做得好，它会让一个人开始怀疑他们的核心到底是谁。自我是非常脆弱的。即使是最强壮的人，当你让他们伤害自己的家人时，也会崩溃。

Breathing hard through her nose, Hermione inspected his face. She believed what he was telling her, believed that if he hadn't done this then he had seen it done.

赫敏的手臂在他的握里不由自主地抽搐了一下，但她没有抽离。“不。”

Slap .
打。

Lifting her hand hadn’t been a conscious action. She didn’t even feel it as her palm connected with his face. It was only the stinging across her fingers and the faint pink mark appearing on his cheek in the aftermath that made her realise that, yes, she had actually slapped him. Clenching her hand into a regretful fist, Hermione breathed hard through her nose, her chest heaving, as she waited for his reaction. Against her expectations, however, he didn’t look angry at all. If anything, he appeared almost satisfied. That concerned her more.  
抬起她的手并不是一个有意识的动作。当她的手掌碰到他的脸时，她甚至没有感觉到。只是她手指上的刺痛和他脸颊上出现的淡淡的粉红色印记，才让她意识到，是的，她真的打了他一巴掌。赫敏遗憾地握紧了手，用鼻子用力呼吸，胸口起伏，等待他的反应。然而，出乎她意料的是，他看起来一点也不生气。如果有什么不同的话，他看起来几乎是满意的。这让她更担心。

“Did that make you feel better, Miss Granger?”
“那让你感觉好些了吗，格兰杰小姐？”

“No.” The shake of her head was slow after her words. Her truthful words. She felt worse than she had in months and there was a painful stinging in her nose that contained the threat of angry tears. 
“不。”她的话后，缓慢地摇了摇头。她诚实的话语。她感觉比几个月前都糟糕，鼻子里有一阵痛苦的刺痛，里面有愤怒的眼泪威胁。

“Perhaps you'd like to try again.”
“也许你想再试一次。”

There was something taut in the air, something Hermione couldn’t quite identify but her gut told her it was dangerous. Her eyes searched Malfoy’s and she found they were gleaming, as though he had relished her outburst. 
空气中有什么东西绷紧了，赫敏不太清楚，但她的直觉告诉她这很危险。她的眼睛扫视着马尔福的眼睛，发现它们闪闪发光，仿佛他很享受她的爆发。

“No.”
“不。”

“No?” he asked, his tone rising derisively. “How else are you supposed to show me how much you hate me?”
“没有？” 他问道，语气里带着嘲讽。“不然你怎么能向我表明你有多恨我？”

“I don't hate you,” she said, her voice dazed. He was trying to upset her. Going to quite a lot of effort to do it, too. After all the pleasantness that had developed between them, he was pushing back violently. Coward , she thought.
“我不恨你，”她说，她的声音有些茫然。他想让她难过。也要付出相当大的努力来做到这一点。在他们之间产生了所有的愉快之后，他猛烈地反击。 懦夫，她想。

“Don't. Lie,” he said, barely parting his lips to let the words through. 
“不要。撒谎，“他说，勉强张开嘴唇让这些话说出来。

“I don't hate you nearly as much as you hate yourself.”
“我恨你，也不像你恨自己。”

A heavy silence fell and then Malfoy huffed out a single humourless laugh. Hermione watched him lower his face into his hands, dragging them down until his fingertips sat in the corners of his eyes.
一阵沉重的沉默，然后马尔福发出了一声毫无幽默感的笑声。赫敏看着他把脸埋进手里，把脸往下拖，直到指尖停在眼角。

"You feel guilty, Mr Malfoy. About your son."
“你感到内疚，马尔福先生。关于你的儿子。

He glared at her over his fingertips. "What a perceptive girl you think you are, Miss Granger. So certain, too."
他用指尖瞪着她。“你觉得你是个多么有洞察力的女孩，格兰杰小姐。也很确定。

"Do you feel guilty about me? Or anyone else?"
“你对我感到内疚吗？还是其他任何人？

He didn't respond to that, instead planting his hands on his hips and rolling his head back so that his nose was directed at the glass roof. Hermione heard him take in a slow, deep breath. His eyes were probably closed.
他没有回应，而是把手放在臀部上，把头向后仰，这样他的鼻子就对准了玻璃屋顶。赫敏听到他缓缓地深吸了一口气。他的眼睛可能是闭着的。

"You don't know how to deal with it. It's why you're pushing everyone out. You're trying to do it with your son and you succeeded with your wife. You think it's easier if everyone hates you."
“你不知道该怎么处理。这就是你把所有人都赶出去的原因。你试图和你的儿子一起做这件事，你和你的妻子成功了。你觉得如果每个人都讨厌你，那就容易多了。

"Isn't it?" he asked, his face still directed upwards.
“不是吗？” 他问道，他的脸仍然向上。

"I don't hate you."
“我不恨你。”

"Yes, you’ve said that," he said, dropping his head to throw her a look that bordered on accusatory. 
“是的，你说过了，”他说，低下头，向她投来一个近乎指责的眼神。

"I probably should," she said, more to herself than to him. Everyone she knew would tell her she should. 
“我也许应该，”她说，与其说是对他，不如说是对自己。她认识的每个人都会告诉她应该这样做。

"Then why won 't you?"
“那你为什么不呢？”

"I don't want to." As she said it, Hermione knew it was true. At some point, and she didn’t know exactly when, she’d stopped hating him and she didn’t really want to start again. "Not anymore. Hating you wouldn't make me any happier, even if I would be well within my rights to do it."
“我不想。”当她说这句话时，赫敏知道这是真的。在某个时候，她不知道确切的时间，她已经不再讨厌他了，她真的不想重新开始。“现在不会了。恨你不会让我更快乐，即使我完全有权利这样做。

"What if I want you to hate me?"
“如果我想让你恨我怎么办？”

"Why?"
“为什么？”

"Because it might finally stop you pushing in where you're not wanted."
“因为它可能最终会阻止你推到你不想要的地方。”

Not because he hated her . There was a half-heartedness to his glare that encouraged Hermione to slide from the workbench onto her feet. He retreated a step to give her space but not a great deal, so she was forced to crane her neck to look up at him. He stayed very close for a man so insistent that he wanted her far away.
不是因为他恨她。他的目光中带着一种半心半意的神情，鼓励赫敏从工作台上滑到她的脚上。他后退了一步，给她留出空间，但不是很大，所以她被迫伸长脖子抬头看他。他离得非常近，因为这个男人如此执着，以至于他想让她离得很远。

"You said you were on a narrow path under Voldemort. He's dead now—definitely this time—so why are you acting like you're still on it? You talk about the fragility of the self so why not break it entirely and forge something new? Something stronger?”
“你说你在伏地魔手下走的是一条狭窄的道路。他现在已经死了——肯定是这次——那么你为什么表现得像你还在吃呢？你谈到了自我的脆弱性，那么为什么不完全打破它并打造新的东西呢？更强大的东西？

Hesitantly, Hermione reached out to his left forearm hanging by his side. She brushed the backs of her fore and middle fingers against the soft, inner part of his arm that bore the Dark Mark, observing the slight tremor that passed through him. "You don't have to be this anymore. Not if you don't want to be."
赫敏犹豫了一下，伸手摸了伸手去拿挂在他身边的左前臂。她用食指和中指的背拂过他手臂上带有黑暗印记的柔软内侧，观察着他身上的轻微颤抖。“你不必再这样了。如果你不想的话，就不要。

"It's not that simple, Miss Granger."
“没那么简单，格兰杰小姐。”

"It's not that complicated either. Stop drawing your self-worth from things that exist outside of yourself. Stop thinking about yourself as a Pure-blood or a Malfoy or anything like that and start showing who you are through the things that you do. Our actions show us more clearly than anything else."
“这也不复杂。停止从存在于你之外的事物中汲取自我价值。不要再把自己看作是纯血统或马尔福或类似的东西，开始通过你做的事情来展示你是谁。我们的行动比其他任何事情都更清楚地表明我们。

"Yes, your insistence on discussing this, for instance, shows me just how irritating you truly are."
“是的，例如，你坚持讨论这件事，向我展示了你到底有多烦人。”

"You chose to try to upset me today," Hermione pressed on past his pathetic attempt to deter her, "but you also chose to help me in your library rather than leave me. I'd encourage you to lean towards the latter instinct more regularly." 
“你今天选择让我难过，”赫敏压制住了他可怜的阻止尝试，“但你也选择在你的图书馆里帮助我，而不是离开我。我鼓励你更经常地倾向于后一种直觉。

"Of course you would,” he said venomously. “In case you haven't noticed, my world is currently very small and will continue to be so for the next...oh, twelve years, give or take a few weeks. What I choose to do hardly matters."
“你当然会，”他恶毒地说。“如果你没有注意到，我的世界目前非常小，明年将继续如此......哦，十二年了，或多或少几周。我选择做什么几乎无关紧要。

"It matters to me. I told Kingsley that I'll personally advocate for a reduction in your sentence to make sure it happens." Malfoy blinked, taken aback by the revelation, and Hermione nodded firmly. "I'll stick to my word because thus far you've stuck to yours. I want you to have another chance and I hope you'll see it as an opportunity."
“这对我来说很重要。我告诉金斯利，我会亲自倡导减轻你的刑期，以确保它发生。马尔福眨了眨眼，被这个发现吓了一跳，赫敏坚定地点了点头。“我会信守诺言，因为到目前为止你一直信守诺言。我希望你有另一个机会，我希望你能把它看作是一个机会。

"To do what , exactly?" 
“到底做什么？”

"To look outwards and find a way to deal with your guilt that isn't just allowing it to consume you."
“向外看，找到一种方法来处理你的内疚感，而不仅仅是让它吞噬你。”

Hermione lifted a hand to his chest, hovering only a moment before she pressed it flat, pushing him back to give herself some more space. The rapid beat of his heart was faint but perceptible through the thin layer of his shirt and she met his eyes before he stepped out of her reach. 
赫敏将一只手抬到他的胸前，在她把它压平之前只悬停了一会儿，把他往后推，给自己更多的空间。他心跳的急促虽然微弱，但透过他薄薄的衬衫可以察觉到，在他走出她的手之前，她与他的眼睛相遇。

"Hatred is easy, Mr Malfoy," she said, her hand lingering in the air between them before she let it fall. "But I’d be amazed if you haven’t noticed by now that it doesn't ever get you very much in return. You don't strike me as a man that would do something for nothing."
“仇恨很容易，马尔福先生，”她说，她的手在他们之间的空气中徘徊，然后放下手来。“但如果你现在还没有注意到，它不会给你带来多少回报，我会感到惊讶。你不会觉得我是一个不劳而获的人。

Lucius looked at the space where her hand had been, his own hands clenching and unclenching by his sides. With a suddenness that made Hermione sharply inhale and hold her breath, he closed the space between them, forcing her lower back against the workbench, his hips just touching hers.
卢修斯看着她手所在的空间，他自己的手在他的身体两侧紧握又松开。突然间，赫敏猛地吸了一口气，屏住了呼吸，他拉近了他们之间的空间，迫使她的下背部靠在工作台上，他的臀部刚好碰到她的臀部。

"Forgive me, Miss Granger, if I find your advocacy of looking to the future hard to swallow when you spend your days here, with me, dredging up the past."
“请原谅我，格兰杰小姐，如果你在这里度过你的日子，和我一起，挖掘过去的时候，你对未来的倡导让人难以接受。”

Hermione swallowed, looking up into his angry eyes and shook her head weakly. Abruptly, Malfoy turned on his heel and marched out of the greenhouse without another word. Hermione heard the door slam, the glass rattling, and sighed, her shoulders slumping as she looked over at her still-recording Wheezebox. She wasn’t sure that was a conversation she’d ever want to listen to again.
赫敏咽了口口水，抬头看着他愤怒的眼睛，虚弱地摇了摇头。突然，马尔福转过身来，一言不发地走出了温室。赫敏听到门砰的一声，玻璃嘎嘎作响，叹了口气，她的肩膀耷拉着，看着她那仍在录音的喘息器。她不确定这是一场她是否还想再听一遍的对话。

6 月 29 日

Lucius Malfoy stabbed his fork into his scrambled eggs, a dark expression on his face. It was Thursday. Granger visited on Thursdays. 
卢修斯·马尔福用叉子刺进了他的炒鸡蛋里，脸上露出阴沉的表情。那天是星期四。格兰杰周四来访。

“If you don’t like your eggs just don’t eat them, father,” Draco chided from across the table. “There’s no need for violence at the breakfast table.”
“如果你不喜欢你的鸡蛋，就别吃它们，爸爸，”德拉科在桌子对面斥责道。“早餐桌上没有必要使用暴力。”

“Shut up, Draco,” Lucius muttered, actually somewhat grateful to his son for interrupting his thoughts. 
“闭嘴，德拉科，”卢修斯咕哝道，实际上是有点感谢他的儿子打断了他的思绪。

For the first time in years, he was regularly eating his meals with Draco and Astoria. It was almost pleasant but it had been a long week and he was irritable. Granger had said he was trying to push his son out so he was going to show her that she was wrong. Even though she was right. She was always fucking right. Or she thought she was. 
多年来，他第一次定期与德拉科和阿斯托利亚一起吃饭。这几乎是愉快的，但这是漫长的一周，他很烦躁。格兰杰说他试图把他的儿子赶出去，这样他就要让她知道她错了。即使她是对的。她总是他妈的对。或者她认为她是。

After their little encounter the previous week, he’d told Astoria he didn’t want to know when Granger was in the library. He’d endeavoured to avoid her completely, locking himself in his study or the greenhouse and hoping against hope that she wouldn’t seek him out. She hadn’t. And a part of him—a stupid, spineless, pathetic part—had been disappointed by that. 
在上周他们短暂的相遇之后，他告诉阿斯托利亚，他不想知道格兰杰什么时候在图书馆里。他努力完全避开她，把自己锁在书房或温室里，希望她不会找到他。她没有。而他的一部分——一个愚蠢的、没有骨气的、可悲的那一部分——已经为此感到失望了。

Where did she get off, though? Pushing and pushing and pushing her way into his life like a fucking emotional Reducto and then, without a word, just stopping? Disappearing? He thought he’d been good at torture but she was certainly teaching him a thing or two.
不过，她是从哪里下来的呢？像一个该死的情绪化的 Reducto 一样推啊推、推、推，闯进他的生活，然后，一言不发，就停下来了？消失？他认为他很擅长折磨，但她肯定是在教他一两件事。

Well, she'd be back at the manor within a few hours anyway and when she arrived she'd have to look him in the face again. Lucius' fork hovered threateningly over his eggs as he considered the approaching meeting. He was framing it as though she should have trouble looking at him. It was the other way around. 
好吧，反正她几个小时内就会回到庄园，当她到达时，她得再看一眼他的脸。卢修斯的叉子威胁性地悬在他的鸡蛋上，他思考着即将到来的会议。他把这句话说得好像她看他时应该很麻烦。但情况正好相反。

The fork descended with force and missed the eggs entirely, screeching across his plate. He barely heard it. 
叉子用力下降，完全错过了鸡蛋，在他的盘子里发出尖锐的声音。他几乎没听见。

"Father!"
“爸爸！”

She'd told him she still dreamed about what happened to her, the way he still dreamed about what happened to his family, and instead of reaching across that connection he'd just…
她告诉他，她仍然梦见发生在她身上的事情，他仍然梦见他家人发生的事情，他没有跨越那种联系，而是......

Blinking away the memory of her large, trusting eyes as he'd held her scarred arm in his hand, he pondered the merits of fried mushrooms for stabbing rather than eggs. Smaller surface area but a more satisfyingly fleshy solidity. 
当他用手握住她伤痕累累的手臂时，他眨了眨眼，抹去了她那双大而信任的眼睛的记忆，他思考着炸蘑菇比鸡蛋更能刺伤。较小的表面积，但更令人满意的肉质固体。

Of course, she'd seen right through his attempt to upset her. He'd weaved together a combination of things that seemed likely to rile and scare her and used them ruthlessly because he’d decided it was just easier if she hated him like everyone else. Hatred doesn’t get you much, she’d said, patently oblivious to the fact that it had actually once given his life a great deal of simplicity. 
当然，她已经看穿了他试图惹她不安的企图。他把一些看起来可能会激怒和吓唬她的东西编织在一起，并无情地使用它们，因为他认为如果她像其他人一样讨厌他，那就更容易了。憎恨对你没有多大好处，她说，显然忘记了它实际上曾经给他的生活带来了许多简单。

Lucius sighed through his nose and lowered his fork to the table, his breakfast demolished but uneaten. She still refused to hate him. After all that, she'd suggested she had some kind of absurd faith in him. She was going to personally advocate for him to give him a chance. Look outwards, she'd said. Consider his future in a world he hadn't actually ever seriously entertained seeing again.
卢修斯从鼻子里叹了口气，把叉子放到桌子上，他的早餐被毁了，但还没有吃完。她仍然拒绝恨他。毕竟，她暗示她对他有某种荒谬的信仰。她打算亲自为他辩护，给他一个机会。她曾说过，要向外看。想想他的未来，在一个他实际上从未真正喜欢再看到的世界里。

Consider his actions. And their effects.
想想他的行为。以及它们的影响。

He swallowed. Objectively he knew what the right action was in this instance. An apology. He'd been inappropriate. He actually hadn't anticipated she'd let him get as close as she had. She'd always been on the edgy side when their meetings first started but obviously, at some point, proximity and even touch had become acceptable. When exactly did that happen? It was all so unclear. Every meeting blended in his head, just becoming a blur of her .
他咽了口口水。客观地说，他知道在这种情况下什么是正确的行动。道歉。他太不合适了。他其实没想到她会让他像她一样靠近。当他们的会议刚开始时，她一直很前卫，但显然，在某个时候，接近甚至触摸已经变得可以接受。这究竟是什么时候发生的？一切都是那么不清楚。每一次会面都混在他的脑海中，只是变成了她的模糊。

He detested inexactitude; it led to mistakes. He detested those even more because he'd made quite enough of them. Clearing his throat, Lucius glanced up in the direction of his son, Granger’s face still looming in his mind.
他讨厌不精确;它导致了错误。他更讨厌那些，因为他已经受够了。清了清嗓子，卢修斯抬头看了一眼儿子的方向，格兰杰的脸仍然在他的脑海中若隐若现。

"Draco, would you like to join me on my walk with Cato this afternoon?"
“德拉科，你愿意今天下午和我一起和卡托一起散步吗？”

Across the breakfast table, past the floral centrepiece, the Daily Prophet that had been covering his son's face flopped in half, revealing a startled expression. 
在早餐桌对面，经过鲜花中央，一直遮住儿子脸的《预言家日报》瘫成两半，露出惊讶的表情。

"Of – of course."
“当然。”

"Good. Be ready by 12.45, please."
“很好。请在 12.45 之前准备好。

Draco nodded several times before saying, "Yes. Yes, I will."
德拉科点了好几次头，然后说，“是的。是的，我会的。

Depositing his napkin on the table, Lucius rose from his seat with a stately dignity and quietly exited the room. Half-rising in his seat, Draco peered over the centrepiece at his father's barely-touched breakfast and then at the door through which he had just exited. Something had ruffled Lucius Malfoy.
卢修斯把餐巾纸放在桌子上，庄重地从座位上站起来，悄悄地走出了房间。德拉科半站着坐在座位上，从中央看了一眼他父亲几乎没碰过的早餐，然后又看了看他刚刚走出去的门。卢修斯·马尔福有些生气了。

Lucius Malfoy's hands were haunting Hermione's dreams. 
卢修斯·马尔福的手在赫敏的梦中萦绕。

Ripping off a chunk of toast with her teeth, Hermione scowled at the bright summer sky outside of her kitchen window with tired eyes. She could sit at the kitchen table now – it was clear enough as most of her things were at Malfoy Manor. Odd that when the table had been at its messiest, her life had been at its most simple. 
赫敏用牙齿撕下一大块吐司，疲惫的眼睛看着厨房窗外明亮的夏日天空。她现在可以坐在厨房的桌子旁了——这已经足够清楚了，因为她的大部分东西都在马尔福庄园。奇怪的是，当桌子最混乱的时候，她的生活却是最简单的。

Another roar rent the air, the loudest sound coming from a financially devastated Ron. Hermione laughed loudly and rose from her seat, moving around the table to hug Ron from behind and plant a kiss on the top of his head before wrapping Harry and James in a hug. She kissed Harry’s cheek and did the same to James but far more gently, feeling that his soft face was still warm from his crying.
另一声咆哮划破了空气，最响亮的声音来自经济崩溃的罗恩。赫敏大声笑了起来，从座位上站起来，绕着桌子从后面拥抱罗恩，在他的头顶上亲了一下，然后把哈利和詹姆斯抱在了一起。她亲吻哈利的脸颊，对詹姆斯做同样的事情，但要温柔得多，感觉到他柔软的脸上仍然因哭泣而温暖。

"Congratulations," she said softly, her eyes shining as they met Harry’s. 
“恭喜你，”她轻声说，当他们与哈利的眼睛相遇时，她的眼睛闪闪发光。

The rest of the table followed suit, rising and queuing to embrace Harry and wish he and Ginny the best. It was something of a shame, Hermione thought, that Draco Malfoy probably wouldn’t have quite the same reception when he announced the birth of he and Astoria’s child.
桌子上的其他人也纷纷效仿，起身排队拥抱哈利，祝他和金妮一切顺利。有点遗憾，赫敏想，当德拉科·马尔福宣布他和阿斯托利亚的孩子出生时，他可能不会受到同样的接待。

It was just before midnight by the time Hermione arrived back at her flat. After everyone had congratulated Harry, forcing a port into his hand and another down his throat, they had left Mr and Mrs Weasley and James to be the first to see Ginny and the new baby. 
赫敏回到她的公寓时，已经是午夜前了。在大家都向哈利道过祝贺之后，他们把一个端口塞进了他的手里，又塞进了他的喉咙，他们让韦斯莱先生和夫人以及詹姆成为第一个看到金妮和新生儿的人。

Hermione, Fleur and the other Weasleys, agreeing that Ginny would be far too tired to see everyone, had departed for a Muggle pub and toasted to Albus Severus. They'd had fun at first, advising an agitated Percy on how to converse with people he fancied about things that weren’t work or general Ministry policy, but they called it a night when Ron reached an exceptionally morose state and declared he was almost certain Hannah was going to leave him for Hogwarts. 
赫敏、芙蓉和其他韦斯莱一家都认为金妮会太累了，无法见到大家，于是他们去了一家麻瓜酒吧，向阿不思·西弗勒斯敬酒。起初他们玩得很开心，建议激动的珀西如何与他喜欢的人交谈，谈论那些不是工作或魔法部一般政策的事情，但他们称那天晚上，罗恩达到了异常忧郁的状态，并宣布他几乎可以肯定汉娜会离开他去霍格沃茨。

Knowing that she wanted to make up for her day of missed work on Friday, Hermione had tried to stop drinking fairly early but she still felt a touch unsteady as she wound her way through the hallway of her flat and into her bedroom. 
赫敏知道她想弥补周五错过的一天，她试图早点停止喝酒，但当她穿过公寓的走廊进入她的卧室时，她仍然感到有点不稳定。

Not bothering to close the door, Hermione stepped out of her clothes, leaving them in a bundle on her floor, and pulled her oversized Chudley Cannons t-shirt on over her comfiest knickers. It was a hot night and it was a relief to get some air around her legs.
赫敏懒得关门，从衣服里走出来，把它们一捆一捆地放在地板上，把她超大号的查德利大炮T恤套在她最舒适的短裤外面。那是一个炎热的夜晚，她的腿周围有一些空气，真是让人松了一口气。

Leaving her bedroom, her bare feet padding across the wooden floor of her hall, she peeked into the living room in the direction of the window. A small part of her was disappointed not to see the bright orange eyes of Lucius Malfoy's owl waiting for her. When he hadn't sent a reply to the hospital, she'd told herself it was more likely that he'd sent his owl to her flat. Apparently not. What she was even expecting from him she didn't know. Lucius Malfoy didn't send notes of comfort and understanding. He was probably furious at her. 
她走出卧室，光着脚踩在走廊的木地板上，朝窗户的方向偷看了一眼客厅。她有一小部分人因为没有看到卢修斯·马尔福的猫头鹰那双明亮的橙色眼睛在等着她而感到失望。当他没有给医院回复时，她告诉自己，他更有可能把他的猫头鹰送到了她的公寓。显然不是。她甚至不知道她对他有什么期望。卢修斯·马尔福没有送来安慰和理解的信。他可能对她很生气。

Hermione was just making her way across the hall in the direction of the kitchen to get a drink of water when a loud bang at her front door made her stop dead in her tracks. Feeling suddenly very sober, she turned in the direction of the door and held her breath, staying completely still and silent. Her wand wasn't on her; it was on her bedroom floor with her clothes. 
赫敏正穿过走廊，朝着厨房的方向去喝水，这时一声巨响传来，她的前门砰的一声让她停在了原地。她突然感到非常清醒，她转向门的方向，屏住呼吸，完全静止不动，一言不发。她的魔杖不在她身上;它和她的衣服一起在她卧室的地板上。

Another loud bang made Hermione jump and scamper back into her bedroom. Snatching her wand up from the pile on the floor, she moved back through the doorway with it held aloft. 
又一声巨响让赫敏跳了起来，蹦蹦跳跳地回到了她的卧室。她从地板上的一堆魔杖中抓起魔杖，高举着魔杖从门口向后移动。

"Granger! Open this door!"
“格兰杰！打开这扇门！

The command was followed by another loud bang and Hermione's mouth dropped open. She knew that voice. That absurdly entitled voice. Surely not . It was impossible. Not just conceptually; it was physically impossible. Wasn't it? Lowering her wand, her heart hammering so hard she thought it might be able to knock the door right back, Hermione approached her front door at a creep to peer through the eye hole. 
命令之后是另一声巨响，赫敏张大了嘴巴。她认识那个声音。那个荒谬的标题。 当然不是。这是不可能的。不仅仅是概念上;这在物理上是不可能的。不是吗？赫敏放下魔杖，她的心跳得如此剧烈，她觉得它也许能把门敲回去，赫敏悄悄地靠近她的前门，从眼孔里窥视。

Just as she expected, Lucius Malfoy was leaning his shoulder against the frame of her front door looking exhausted, frustrated and almost certainly like he'd been drinking. 
正如她所料，卢修斯·马尔福正把肩膀靠在她前门的框架上，看起来筋疲力尽，沮丧，几乎可以肯定他就像在喝酒一样。

更多注释见本章末尾Hermione wrenched open her front door and grabbed Malfoy by the arm, hauling him into her flat without a second thought. Poking her head into the outer hallway, she turned left and right. Seeing no one, she closed the door tight and turned to find him with his back to her, using the palm of his hand to support his weight against her wall.
赫敏拧开她的前门，抓住马尔福的胳膊，不假思索地把他拖进了自己的公寓。她把头探进外面的走廊，左右转过身来。没有看到任何人，她把门关紧，转身发现他背对着她，用他的手掌将他的重量支撑在她的墙上。

“What is this?” she asked, furious and disbelieving, as she walked around him to look him in the face. “What the fuck are you doing ? You’re under house arrest, Mr Malfoy, you can’t be here!”
“这是什么？”她问道，愤怒而难以置信，同时绕过他，看着他的脸。“你他妈在干什么？你被软禁了，马尔福先生，你不能在这里！

His eyes were closed, a frown creating a deep crease in the skin between his brows. He seemed to be breathing deeply through his nose as though steadying himself. If he was sick in her hall she’d hex him into oblivion.
他闭着眼睛，皱眉在眉间的皮肤上形成了深深的皱纹。他似乎在用鼻子深呼吸，仿佛在稳住自己。如果他在她的大厅里生病了，她就会把他咒语遗忘。

“Are you even listening to me?” she asked, stepping closer to him, her wand gripped tight in her fist. “Have you been drinking? Mr Malfoy, you’re under house arrest. The Aurors will know you’ve left. Doesn't the Magic Dampener also—”
“你有没有听我说话？”她问道，一边靠近他，手里紧紧地握着魔杖。“你喝酒了吗？马尔福先生，你被软禁了。傲罗们会知道你已经走了。魔法阻尼器不也是——”

"Don’t give them so much credit. It doesn’t tell them when I leave,” Malfoy said through gritted teeth, squeezing his eyes more tightly shut as though the words were costing him a great deal of effort. “It suppresses my magic so as far as they're concerned I can't apparate, or use the Floo, or go far .” He took a deep, shuddering breath. “It's supposed to incapacitate me in the highly unlikely event I breach the wards which match its magical signature so they can find me when they realise I’m gone.”
“不要给他们太多的荣誉。它不会告诉他们我什么时候离开，“马尔福咬牙切齿地说，把眼睛紧紧地闭着，仿佛这些话让他费了很大的力气。“它压制了我的魔法，所以就他们而言，我不能幻影，也不能使用飞路，也不能走得太远。”他深深地吸了一口气，颤抖着。“它应该在我突破符合其魔法特征的守卫时使我失去行动能力，这样当他们意识到我走了时就可以找到我。”

“Incapacitate…?” Hermione trailed off wonderingly, properly taking in his contorting face and crumbling posture. There was, she realised, a faint shimmer of sweat across his brow and suddenly she didn’t see drunkenness but – “Mr Malfoy, are you in pain?”
“丧失能力......？”赫敏疑惑地走开了，适当地观察了他扭曲的脸和摇摇欲坠的姿势。她意识到，他的额头上闪过一丝淡淡的汗水，突然间她没有看到醉酒，而是——“马尔福先生，你痛吗？

“Some,” he said, his hand sliding further down the wall as he folded into himself. 
“一些，”他说，他的手在折叠自己时进一步滑下墙壁。

Rushing forward, Hermione planted her hands on his shoulders to steady him, her anger temporarily forgotten. “How did you get here?” she demanded. “If you can’t apparate or Floo, tell me. I need to get you home.”
赫敏冲上前去，双手搭在他的肩膀上稳住他，她的愤怒暂时忘记了。“你是怎么到这儿的？”“如果你不能幻影或飞路，就告诉我。我得送你回家。

“The elf,” he said, his voice catching in his throat.
“那个妖精，”他说，他的声音卡在了喉咙里。

“Letty,” Hermione called, her voice rising with panic as more of Malfoy’s weight fell on her hands. “Letty!”
“莱蒂，”赫敏喊道，随着马尔福的更多重量落在她的手上，她的声音因恐慌而提高。“莱蒂！”

“LETTY!” Malfoy barked, his voice straining.
“莱蒂！”马尔福吼道，他的声音很紧张。

A crack rent the air and an audibly anxious Letty appeared in Hermione’s hall, her eyes wide and brimming with tears. “Master is in pain,” the elf cried, twisting her left wrist with her right hand like she was trying to unscrew it. “Letty tried to tell the master that he shouldn’t! Letty told master that miss—”
一阵裂缝划破了空气，听见焦虑的莱蒂出现在赫敏的大厅里，她的眼睛睁得大大的，泪流满面。「主人很痛，」妖精喊道，一边用右手扭动着她的左手腕，彷佛她正试图拧开它。“莱蒂试图告诉主人，他不应该这样做！莱蒂告诉主人，那个小姐——”

“Letty,” Hermione interrupted forcefully, barely managing to keep her tone even as Malfoy clutched her upper arm tightly to stay upright. “Letty, it’s not your fault. You only did as he asked you. And now you need to do as I’m asking you. Take us back to your master’s study. Please. Right now.”
“莱蒂，”赫敏用力打断了她，即使马尔福紧紧地抓住她的上臂以保持直立，她也勉强保持了自己的语气。“莱蒂，这不是你的错。你只是按照他的要求做了。现在你需要按照我的要求去做。带我们回到你的师父书房。请。 现在。

Taking a gasping, teary breath, Letty nodded and rushed forward, grabbing both Hermione and Lucius by their legs to transport them to his study with a crack . 
莱蒂喘着粗气，泪流满面，点点头，冲上前去，抓住赫敏和卢修斯的腿，啪啪一声把他们送到了他的书房。

They appeared in the centre of the room, between the sofa and the crackling fireplace. Supporting Malfoy, Hermione helped him towards the sofa as Letty stood to the side, tears openly pouring down her wrinkled cheeks. Ignoring Letty’s choked apologies, Hermione lowered Malfoy into a sitting position on the sofa. He groaned as the weight came off his feet and reached down to hold the leg fitted with the Magic Dampener. 
他们出现在房间的中央，在沙发和噼啪作响的壁炉之间。赫敏扶着马尔福，扶着他走向沙发，而莱蒂则站在一边，泪水从她布满皱纹的脸颊上流下来。赫敏无视莱蒂哽咽的道歉，将马尔福放到沙发上坐下。当重量从脚上脱落时，他呻吟着，伸手握住了装有魔法阻尼器的腿。

“Move,” Hermione snapped, batting away his hand and dropping to her knees between his legs, her large Chudley Cannons t-shirt pooling on the floor around her. It said a lot to her about the pain he must be in that he immediately relented and fell back into the sofa, his body slumped.
“动，”赫敏厉声说，拍开他的手，跪在他的两腿之间，她的大 Chudley Cannons T 恤在她周围的地板上积落。这对她来说，他一定很痛苦，他立即心软了，倒在沙发上，身体瘫软了下来。

Not bothering to waste time trying to roll them up, Hermione used a severing charm to open the leg of his trousers from the knee to the hem. Folding the material over his knees, she set her eyes on the Magic Dampener for the first time. 
赫敏懒得浪费时间试图把它们卷起来，他用了一个切断咒，从膝盖到下摆打开了他的裤腿。将材料折叠在他的膝盖上，她第一次将目光投向了 Magic Dampener。

It was an unremarkable, solid iron cuff, clamped around his calf just above where his sock ended. It wasn’t moving or even emitting any kind of sound so Hermione could only assume that whatever it had been doing had stopped. But it had clearly been doing something because its effects were lingering. The muscles in Malfoy’s calf—and possibly further up his leg—were visibly straining and spasming. Touching a finger to the device, Hermione gasped and pulled her hand back. It was burning hot. 
那是一个不起眼的、结实的铁铐，夹在他的小腿上，就在他袜子末端的上方。它没有移动，甚至没有发出任何声音，所以赫敏只能假设它一直在做什么已经停止了。但它显然一直在做一些事情，因为它的影响挥之不去。马尔福小腿上的肌肉——可能还有他腿上的肌肉——明显地绷紧和痉挛。赫敏用一根手指碰了碰设备，喘着粗气，把手抽了回来。天气很热。

赫敏咬着嘴唇，从地板上的位置抬头看了卢修斯一眼，看到他的胸膛迅速起伏，一只手捂住了眼睛。她唯一能真正看到他脸上的部分是他紧紧咬着的下巴。

小精灵打了个嗝，默许了她，消失了，终于给了赫敏思考所需的安静。

It might work . Exhaling slowly through her nose, Hermione pressed the tip of her wand into the side of knee and wordlessly cast a cooling charm. A quiet intake of breath from above her told her it had done something. Focused on his leg, she turned the wand in a clockwise direction and murmured the sing-song incantation of a relaxation charm that she’d taught herself when the Ministry had become particularly stressful. The muscles in Malfoy’s legs began to loosen and, out of the corner of her eyes, she saw his hand that had been gripping the edge of the sofa relinquish its hold. He didn’t make a single sound otherwise. 
它可能会奏效。赫敏从鼻子里缓缓地呼出一口气，将魔杖的尖端压在膝盖侧面，无言地施展了一个冷却咒。她从头顶轻轻地吸了一口气，告诉她它做了什么。她专注于他的腿，将魔杖顺时针方向转动，喃喃自语着一种放松咒语的歌唱咒语，这是她在魔法部变得特别紧张时自学的。马尔福腿上的肌肉开始松弛，她用眼角的余光看到他一直抓着沙发边缘的手松开了。他没有发出任何声音。

赫敏刚完成咒语，莱蒂就回到了房间，毛巾在她的手臂上堆得很高，以至于遮住了她的脸。赫敏站起来，带着善意但紧张的微笑从小精灵手中接过毛巾。

“谢谢你，莱蒂。你做得很好。你现在可以离开了;主人会没事的。

Letty peered around Hermione to look at Lucius who, while still in exhausted repose on the sofa, did seem more at peace than when she had left. “I promise,” Hermione added quietly. “I’ll take care of him.”
莱蒂环顾赫敏，看着卢修斯，卢修斯虽然仍然在沙发上疲惫不堪地休息着，但看起来确实比她离开时更加平静。“我保证，”赫敏悄悄地补充道。“我会照顾他的。”

Surely a tracking spell, or some kind of variation on the trace, would have made more sense. Lower lip caught between her teeth, Hermione glanced up at him and found he was watching her, his face utterly unreadable.

“好些吗？” 她问道，她的声音奇怪地嘶哑到她耳中。

“Marginally.” 
“稍微。”

His voice was muted and tired but the fact that the word was not being spoken through gritted teeth suggested to Hermione that the improvement was more than marginal and he was just an ungrateful bloody git. Secure in that knowledge, she allowed her tone to harden again.
他的声音低沉而疲惫，但事实上，这个词没有咬牙切齿地说出来，这让赫敏觉得这种改善不仅仅是微不足道的，他只是一个忘恩负义的的家伙。确信了这一点，她让自己的语气再次变得坚硬。

“那不客气。”

他低头瞪着她，平常的力量被他瘫软的姿势稍微削弱了。“这是我的错，我一开始就处于那个位置。”

赫敏哽咽着发出难以置信的笑声。“什么？”

“你没有来参加我们的会议。”

“我写信给你解释为什么。”

“不，你没有。”

“是的，我做到了;我派了一只猫头鹰。

“但你没有解释为什么。”

You know, because sometimes it’s nice to be around people that you like. Does that explanation meet your satisfaction despite probably being an utterly foreign concept to you?”
“好吧，”赫敏厉声说。“金妮·波特正在分娩，我和韦斯莱一家一起在医院，因为我想在那里和他们一起庆祝。”你知道的，因为有时候和你喜欢的人在一起是件好事。尽管这个解释对你来说可能是一个完全陌生的概念，但你满意吗？

“I was angry at you.”
“我对你生气。”

“Couldn’t you just have written to me to tell me that?”
“你不能写信给我告诉我吗？”

“No.”
“不。”

“ Why ?”
“为什么？”

“Because I wanted to see you,” he barked, his voice rising with impatience as he pushed himself up into a straight sitting position. 
“因为我想见你，”他吼道，他的声音因不耐烦而提高，同时把自己推到一个笔直的坐姿。

Oh . Hermione fell silent, her heart hammering in her chest, in her ears, all around the room and in the walls themselves for all she knew. The fire behind her back suddenly felt incredibly warm and she sank further down onto her heels. 
哦。赫敏沉默了，她的心在胸口、耳边、房间周围和墙壁上都砰砰作响。她背后的火突然感到无比温暖，她进一步沉入了她的脚后跟。

“为什么？” 她问道，声音很平静。

If he hadn’t been having dreams as she had, there was still every chance something had shifted for him too. The looks, the touches, the softening —surely it all had to add up to something that wasn’t completely one-sided.  But she wasn’t entirely sure that she wanted to hear it because acknowledging it would make it real and it couldn’t be real. “是的。你这周几乎没有离开过你的书房！

“As you have barely left the library?”
“你刚离开过图书馆？”

They glared at one another, faces tight, Hermione kneeling on the floor and Lucius looking down at her from his position on the sofa. 他沉默了一会儿，看着她避开他的目光，然后他说，“你喜欢这样，不是吗？

Before Hermione could even turn her head in his direction, Malfoy had reached out and grabbed her forearm, pulling her up into a tall kneel so that her face was almost level with his. Hermione cried out, tugging her arm but he held tight, jerking her closer so that their faces were mere inches apart.
赫敏甚至还没来得及把头转向他的方向，马尔福就伸手抓住了她的前臂，把她拉起来，高高地跪了下来，让她的脸几乎和他的脸齐平。赫敏大声喊道，拉着她的胳膊，但他紧紧地抓住了她，猛地把她拉得更近，以至于他们的脸相距只有几英寸。

赫敏停止了试图从他身边抽离的企图，她被激怒了，僵在了原地。“我什么时候给你留下过我喜欢那样的印象？”

“别，”他说，嘴巴几乎一动不动。“不敢动。”

To an onlooker, Hermione could have just been struck by a stray Petrificus Totalus. He wanted forgiveness. For what? For his treatment of her in the distant past? The recent past? Right now? All of the above? Maybe he didn’t even know. It was so bloody typical of him to ask for forgiveness without an overt apology – to leave the legwork to somebody else.
在旁观者看来，赫敏可能只是被一只流浪的 Petrificus Totalus 击中了。他想要宽恕。为什么？因为他在遥远的过去对她的对待？最近的过去？马上？以上所有？也许他甚至不知道。他请求原谅而不公开道歉是如此血腥的典型——把跑腿的工作留给别人。

赫敏的肚子紧紧地握紧，仿佛握成拳头，她的眼睛瞪向他，发现眼睛已经盯着她。她的名字从他嘴里说出来听起来很奇怪，但她并不完全不喜欢。“晚安，卢修斯。”

He inclined his head and stood watching her until she had left the study, afterwards sinking onto the sofa with a relieved groan as he lifted his weight off his leg. 
他歪着头站着看着她，直到她离开书房，然后瘫倒在沙发上，松了一口气，把重心从腿上移开。

Hermione stepped into the hallway, her bare feet sinking into the plush carpet. She was planning to Floo from the library to return home but she stood for a few moments outside his study door attempting to process what had just happened. Not able to hear any movement from within, she rather thought he was doing the same thing. 
赫敏走进走廊，赤脚陷进毛绒地毯里。她本来打算让飞路从图书馆回家，但她在他的书房门外站了一会儿，试图理解刚刚发生的事情。她听不到里面的任何动静，宁愿以为他在做同样的事情。

"Baaaaad! Baaaaaaad!"

赫敏愧疚地颤抖着，被詹姆·波特响亮的哭声从她对卢修斯·马尔福的思绪中拉了出来。当她低头看着坐在马车里的他时，她松了一口气，发现他实际上并不是某种 Legilimens 神童。

相反，她发现他实际上是在咆哮，因为他指着远处站在公园对面的一只大而特别毛茸茸的白狗。

一声可爱而轻柔的“他们哇”让赫敏咧嘴一笑。“干得好，”她说。“没错。”

Inevitably her thoughts drifted back to him in any quiet moment and had insisted on doing so since their kiss. 
赫敏特地去了波特家，带詹姆斯出去玩一个下午，希望能给哈利和金妮一点时间，让他们只剩下阿不思·西弗勒斯要应付。这也是让自己忙碌的一种方式，这样她醒着的每一刻都不会花在想卢修斯·马尔福上。嗯，应该是这样。在任何安静的时刻，她的思绪都不可避免地飘回到了他身上，自从他们接吻后，她就一直坚持这样做。

She’d tried tackling her increasingly perilous ‘to read’ pile, cooking meals for the Potters, and taking James out for hours here and there to give them breaks. She’d even joined Neville on one of his bi-weekly summer holiday visits to the Hogwarts greenhouses. None of those activities had kept her mind off Malfoy for quite long enough. 她试过处理她那堆越来越危险的“阅读”堆，为波特家做饭，带詹姆斯到处出去几个小时让他们休息。她甚至和纳威一起参加了他每两周一次的暑假霍格沃茨温室之旅。这些活动都没有让她的注意力从马尔福身上离开足够长的时间。事实上，纳威的温室实际上激发了特别生动的回忆。

赫敏叹了口气，继续推着詹姆斯和他的马车沿着公园里蜿蜒的小路走。每次她认为自己有效地分散了自己的注意力，把马尔福从她的脑海中抹去时，最后感觉就像她只是把他塞进了一个小小的心理橱柜里，他在那里等着她的戒备放松，然后才倒下。

她很感激他给她时间来思考她想要什么;出乎意料地迁就了他。结果，有一些怀疑和感激交织在一起，但那只是对他和他的动机的健康警惕。

In the end, coming to terms with the fact that she was attracted to him hadn’t been all that painful. 最后，接受她被他吸引的事实并没有那么痛苦。毕竟，自从他们在温室里争吵以来，她就一直在考虑这个问题，而且她怀疑甚至在那之前它就已经在表面下冒泡了。所以她想要他。好。正是这种新的、持续的想要拥有他的冲动带来了一个问题。尤其是因为他已经明确表示她可以。

In her more even-minded moments over the week, Hermione had truly considered the idea of pursuing something with him and the various ways it could go. None of her projections ended particularly well. Someone always ended up getting hurt. 在她这一周比较平静的时刻，赫敏真正考虑了和他一起追求某件事的想法，以及它可能走的各种路。她的预测都没有特别好的结局。总有人受伤。也不总是她或卢修斯;在一个投影中，她想象了罗恩在与重新武装的卢修斯对峙的错误尝试后特别不幸的命运。

It was hard to imagine how they fit into one another’s lives. Sure, when she was interviewing him, being around one another made sense. When they weren’t continually in one another’s presence, though, how would it work? 很难想象他们如何融入彼此的生活。当然，当她采访他时，彼此在一起是有道理的。然而，当他们不是经常在彼此面前时，它会如何运作呢？不仅如此，整件事难道不是只是由于接近和缺乏其他选择而产生的短暂幻想吗？

There was not giving a jot about the opinions of strangers and then there was not being receptive to the concerns and feelings of the people she loved and respected. Two very different things.
虽然赫敏不认为自己是一个太在意别人怎么想的人，但不可否认的是，她和马尔福一起会画画......评论。她的朋友会说什么，他的儿子——一个非常新的朋友——会说什么。她没有对陌生人的意见开玩笑，也没有接受她所爱和尊重的人的关心和感受。两件截然不同的事情。

然后是先知。直到最近，它才开始接受她真的像她一直坚持的那样无聊。与卢修斯·马尔福的关系会让该出版物的每一位记者都来到她家门口，打破她来之不易的平静。

赫敏的脚步放慢了，她的大脑进入了新的、危险的领域。但她把它看作是一种关系。他从来没有提到过。他只是问她想要什么。谁能说他们不会简单地睡在一起然后继续前进呢？抓痒。赫敏咽了口口水，她的脸颊因为她正在考虑和卢修斯·马尔福发生——一个秘密的——而感到温暖。他们能做到吗？他会想要那样吗？

Would she have to disclose the extent of their relationship to the Wizengamot and would it consider her judgement clouded? Was her judgement clouded? 但是魔法部。她曾承诺为他辩护，但如果她是......与他纠缠在一起——无论是过去还是现在——嗯，那会是什么样子？她是否必须披露他们与威森加摩的关系程度，它会认为她的判断蒙上了阴影吗？ 她的判断是否蒙上了阴影？如果她的证词不是来自客观的战争女英雄赫敏·格兰杰，而是来自与上诉人上床的女巫赫敏·格兰杰，那么她的证词真的可信度如何？

She should never have let him lift her into his lap, or kiss her neck, or push up her t-shirt in that ridiculously teasing – Hermione clenched her jaw and sharply shook her head. Stop it . 
这是不可能的。这一切都太他妈的不可能了，这让她想尖叫。她绝对不应该让他吻她。她永远不应该回吻他。她绝对不应该让他把她抱到自己的腿上，或者亲吻她的脖子，或者用那种荒谬的挑逗来掀起她的T恤——赫敏咬紧了下巴，猛地摇了摇头。 停下。

“Kingsley told me he spoke to you about what I asked him to do for Lucius Malfoy.”
“金斯莱告诉我，他跟你谈过我让他为卢修斯·马尔福做些什么。”

哈利快速眨了眨眼，显然没想到这是赫敏为她打开厨房门时第一个从她嘴里说出来的话。

Hermione’s smile was tight in return. “I sincerely hope that won't be necessary.”
赫敏的笑容也紧紧地回应。“我真诚地希望那没有必要。”

7 月 6 日

“Lucius, I wondered if you’d mind discussing some things we didn't quite get to in our last meeting?”
“卢修斯，我想知道你是否介意讨论一下我们上次会议中没有完全谈到的一些事情？”

Telling Hermione Granger to use his given name had been one of Lucius Malfoy’s better decisions; each and every time, she said it with a subtle hesitation that had not yet failed to amuse him. The girl said ‘Voldemort’ with more brazen confidence. 
告诉赫敏·格兰杰使用他的名字是卢修斯·马尔福更好的决定之一;每一次，她说这句话时，都带着一种微妙的犹豫，但还没有不让他感到高兴。女孩说“伏地魔”时更加自信。

“Whatever you like, Hermione.”
“随你便吧，赫敏。”

Saying her name was even better. He appreciated that it had so many syllables, allowing him to draw it out and savour the faint blush that rose to her cheeks. 
说出她的名字就更好了。他很欣赏它有这么多的音节，让他可以把它抽出来，细细品味她脸颊上升起的淡淡的红晕。

“So, you said you were wandless and useless to Voldemort.” Lucius’ smirk slipped slightly; she was still irritatingly, and he sometimes suspected deliberately, indelicate for all her attractive blushes. “You also said you no longer had any interest in the war. Why did he bring you to the Battle at Hogwarts?”
“所以，你说你没有魔杖，对伏地魔毫无用处。”卢修斯的笑容微微滑落;她仍然令人恼火，他有时故意怀疑，尽管她脸红迷人，但并不雅致。“你还说你对战争不再有任何兴趣。他为什么带你去参加霍格沃茨之战？

“I rather think I inflated the numbers,” Lucius drawled with a dissatisfied purse of his lips. “Or perhaps he thought I’d make a useful shield.”
“我宁愿觉得我夸大了数字，”卢修斯不满地抿起嘴唇。“或者他认为我会做一个有用的盾牌。”

“I suppose you wanted to be there anyway,” Hermione said. “Even if he thought it was punishing you.”
“我想你无论如何都想去那里，”赫敏说。“即使他认为这是在惩罚你。”

“Yes.” Lucius leaned his elbows on his desk and clasped his hands in a bridge beneath his chin. “Draco was at Hogwarts.”
“是的。”卢修斯将胳膊肘靠在桌子上，双手紧握在下巴下的桥上。“德拉科在霍格沃茨。”

“Did you have a plan to reach him?”
“你有没有找到他的计划？”

“No. I was in a rather…reactive state by that stage, Hermione. I intended to take an opportunity to get to my son if it presented itself but I was in no position to create one.”
“不。我处于一个相当......反应状态，赫敏。如果它出现，我打算抓住机会去找我的儿子，但我没有资格创造一个。

“You must have been delighted when one did present itself, then. Harry told me that Voldemort chose Narcissa to check that he was still alive after the encounter in the forest. Why was she chosen?”
“那么，当一个出现时，你一定很高兴。哈利告诉我，伏地魔选择纳西莎是为了在森林里遭遇后检查他是否还活着。为什么她被选中？

“She caught his eye first,” Lucius said with a shrug. “She was disposable to him. And I’m sure he thought she’d always tell the truth as a dutiful Pure-blood witch should.” Leaning back in his chair, he rested his elbows on its arms. “He didn’t know Narcissa very well.”
“她先引起了他的注意，”卢修斯耸耸肩说。“她对他来说是一次性的。而且我敢肯定，他认为她总是会像一个尽职尽责的纯血统女巫一样说真话。他靠在椅子上，胳膊肘靠在它的手臂上。“他不是很了解纳西莎。”

“Obviously. Because she did lie. Are you glad she did?”
“显然。因为她确实撒了谎。你高兴她这样做了吗？

Lucius rubbed his forefinger along his lower lip thoughtfully, his eyes fixed on the patiently waiting witch across from him. “Yes, I think I am,” he finally said. “She took a risk and while I’m not sure how exact she was when she calculated it, I can appreciate it paid off in many ways.”
卢修斯若有所思地用食指在下唇上摩擦，眼睛盯着对面耐心等待的女巫。“是的，我想我是，”他终于说。“她冒了风险，虽然我不确定她计算时的准确性如何，但我可以体会到它在很多方面都得到了回报。”

“Would you have done as she did?”
“你会像她那样做吗？”

Scoffing and rolling his eyes, Lucius dropped his arm so that his hand dangled over the arm of his chair, his rings glinting. “I doubt the Dark Lord would have trusted me to find my own pulse by that point, never mind Harry Potter’s.”
卢修斯嘲笑着翻了个白眼，放下了他的手臂，让他的手悬在椅子的扶手上，他的戒指闪闪发光。“我怀疑黑魔王会相信我会在那个时候找到自己的脉搏，更不用说哈利波特的脉搏了。”

“That’s not what I asked, Lucius,” Hermione said sternly.  
“那不是我问的，卢修斯，”赫敏严肃地说。

“Well, I don’t know . I like to think I’d have had the foresight that Narcissa did but I’ll confess my reserve of hope was rather lower than hers. I can’t discount the possibility that I’d have given Potter away in a last ditch attempt at returning to the Dark Lord’s favour.”
“嗯，我不知道。我喜欢认为我有像纳西莎那样的先见之明，但我承认我的希望储备比她低得多。我不能打折扣，我可能会把波特送走，以换回黑魔王的青睐。

Seeing Hermione’s disbelieving and faintly disgusted look, Lucius shifted irritably in his seat. She wasn’t supposed to be looking at him like that; she was supposed to be looking at him with attraction and lust. At the very least, she was supposed to be looking at him in a way that didn’t make him feel like something mounted on the walls of Borgin and Burkes. 
看到赫敏难以置信和略带厌恶的眼神，卢修斯在座位上烦躁地挪动了一下。她不应该那样看着他;她应该用吸引和欲望看着他。至少，她应该以一种不会让他觉得自己像是挂在博金和伯克斯墙上的东西的方式看着他。

“Stop asking absurd hypotheticals,” he snapped. “They help no one.” 
“别再问荒谬的假设了，”他厉声说。“他们帮不了任何人。”

“Why do you think she did it?” Hermione asked. It had never really been explained to her satisfaction through the trials. The action had been used as evidence in and of itself; the motive hadn’t really mattered. Given Lucius and Draco had both expressed that they didn’t think Narcissa would want to have anything to do with Hermione herself, she thought she’d better ask while she could. 
“你觉得她为什么这么做？”赫敏问道。通过试验，她从来没有真正满意地解释过这一点。这个行动本身就被用作证据;动机并不重要。鉴于卢修斯和德拉科都表示他们不认为纳西莎会想和赫敏本人有任何关系，她认为她最好趁早问问。

Crossing one leg over the other, Lucius lifted his arm and leaned the side of his head on his fist, inspecting Hermione. He didn’t think he should speak for his ex-wife; she had never appreciated it when they’d been married and she would appreciate it even less when they were divorced. 
卢修斯把一条腿交叉在另一条腿上，抬起手臂，把头的一侧靠在拳头上，打量着赫敏。他认为自己不应该为他的前妻说话;当他们结婚时，她从来没有欣赏过，当他们离婚时，她会更不欣赏。

“I cannot tell you that with any authority, Hermione. It’s not my place.” Hermione’s face fell, a crestfallen slump lowering her shoulders, and Lucius sighed through his nose. 
“我不能用任何权威告诉你，赫敏。这不是我的地方。赫敏的脸沉了下来，一阵瘫倒的垂头丧气垂下了她的肩膀，卢修斯从鼻子里叹了口气。

“If I had to truly hypothetically put myself in her place as you asked me to,” he said reluctantly, prompting her to fix him with a look of wide-eyed curiosity that he found begrudgingly appealing, “and contrive some kind of in-the-moment train of thought, I would say that my family and I did not stand to thrive if Voldemort won. We were as low in his favour as it was possible to be while remaining alive. Had I approached Potter and found him still alive after being struck with the killing curse for the second time, my already fractured faith in the Dark Lord might have…taken a further hit, shall we say.” 
“如果我真的必须按照你的要求，假设自己在她的位置上，”他不情愿地说，促使她用一种他觉得勉强吸引人的睁大眼睛的好奇眼神来注视他，“并想出某种当下的思路，我会说，如果伏地魔赢了，我和我的家人就不能茁壮成长了。我们在活着的时候，尽可能地对他有利。如果我找到波特，发现他在第二次被杀戮诅咒击中后还活着，我对黑魔王已经支离破碎的信仰可能会......受到了进一步的打击，容我们说。

Hermione blinked and Lucius raised an eyebrow. “I might have even dared to think that Potter stood a chance. And while a world in which Potter was a winner would be a world in which I had chosen the wrong side, even I would have understood that my family and I stood a far greater chance of staying alive in such a world.”
赫敏眨了眨眼，卢修斯扬起了眉毛。“我甚至敢认为波特有机会。虽然一个波特是赢家的世界会是一个我选错了一边的世界，但即使是我也会明白，我和我的家人在这样的世界里活下去的机会要大得多。

“And if Voldemort had managed to kill Harry in the end? He’d have realised you lied. He’d have realised Narcissa lied.”
“如果伏地魔最后成功杀死了哈利呢？他会意识到你在撒谎。他会意识到纳西莎撒谎的。

“And there is the risk,” Lucius said with a wry smile. “I suppose I could have comforted myself with the thought that if he had won, my life would not have been especially worth living anyway. If you’re going to lose you might as well do so in a way that is as much to your advantage as possible.”
“而且有风险，”卢修斯苦笑着说。“我想我本可以安慰自己，如果他赢了，我的生活无论如何都不会特别值得活着。如果你要输，你还不如以尽可能对你有利的方式去做。

“So neither of you fought.”
“所以你们俩都没有打架。”

“No. After what Narcissa did it was certainly not in our interests to help the Dark Lord win. We took what we knew was our one and only chance to find Draco. And if I had managed to lay my hand on a wand I would not have raised it to do anything other than protect my wife and child. So, you see, they were right to mention it to my credit in the trials,” Lucius said with a bitter smile, recalling her anger in the greenhouse. “Not that it made a huge amount of difference to my sentence in the end.”
“不。在纳西莎所做的一切之后，帮助黑魔王获胜肯定不符合我们的利益。我们抓住了我们知道的唯一机会来找到 Draco。如果我设法将我的手放在一根魔杖上，我就不会举起它来做任何事情，除了保护我的妻子和孩子。所以，你看，他们在试验中提到我是对的，“卢修斯苦笑着说，回忆起她在温室里的愤怒。“并不是说它最终对我的判决产生了很大的影响。”

“I remember seeing the three of you in the Great Hall afterwards, you know,” Hermione said. “I was surprised you didn’t run.”
“我记得后来在礼堂里看到你们三个，你知道的，”赫敏说。“我很惊讶你没有跑。”

Lucius shook his head. “Staying was a statement of intent, though more for Draco than either of us—I knew the optics were good for him. Besides that, we felt relatively safe. For the first time in quite a while.”
卢修斯摇摇头。“留下来是一种意向声明，尽管对Draco来说比我们中的任何一个人都重要——我知道这些眼光对他有好处。除此之外，我们感到相对安全。很长一段时间以来的第一次。

“You felt safe?” Hermione asked, a smile twitching at her lips. “Surrounded by the enemy?”
“你觉得安全吗？”赫敏问道，嘴角的笑容抽搐着。“被敌人包围了？”

Lucius hummed, balancing his chin on his fist, his eyes flicking up and to the left in an almost-roll. “Well, you all have that tedious attachment to honour , don’t you? I thought it unlikely I was going to receive an unannounced killing curse to the back—I’d at least get a trial first.”
卢修斯哼了一声，用拳头固定着下巴，他的眼睛几乎是滚动地向上和向左眨了眨。“嗯，你们都对荣誉有那种乏味的执着，不是吗？我以为我不太可能在背后受到一个突如其来的杀戮诅咒——我至少会先得到一个试炼。

“You call that tedious ?”
“你说这很乏味？”

“I suppose at that specific moment it was refreshing. A temporarily welcome dissimilarity.”
“我想在那个特定的时刻，它令人耳目一新。暂时受欢迎的不同。

With a disbelieving scoff, Hermione reached forward to give the Wheezebox a perfunctory tap with her wand. “Thank you, Lucius. That’ll do for this week.”
赫敏带着难以置信的嘲笑，伸手上前用魔杖敷衍地敲了敲Wheezebox。“谢谢你，卢修斯。这周就这样了。

“A rather short chat today,” Lucius said, his eyebrows raised as he tried to keep any resentment out of his voice.
“今天聊得相当短，”卢修斯说，他扬起眉毛，试图让声音中流露出任何怨恨。

“Mostly I just wanted to fill in some gaps from our last interview. I won’t be able to use some of that,” Hermione said with a wry smile. “It turned rather personal, if you recall.”
“大多数情况下，我只是想填补我们上次采访中的一些空白。我不能用一些，“赫敏苦笑着说。“如果你还记得的话，它变得相当私人。”

“Vaguely,” he said, lifting one of his shoulders in a shrug. Lowering his eyes to inspect his fingernails, he added, “I can’t imagine we have much left to discuss.”
“隐约地，”他说，耸耸肩，抬起他的一个肩膀。他低下眼睛检查自己的指甲，补充道，“我无法想象我们还有很多事情要讨论。

“No,” Hermione said slowly, thumbing through the transcript on his desk before slotting them into her bag. “I think next week might be our final interview.” Their eyes met and Lucius held her gaze intently until she broke it, clearing her throat with a discomfited shift. “Though I hope you’ll still let me use your library.”
“不，”赫敏缓缓地说，用拇指翻阅桌上的文字记录，然后把它们塞进她的包里。“我认为下周可能是我们的最后一次面试。”他们的目光相遇，卢修斯专注地注视着她，直到她打断了它，不安地清了清嗓子。“不过我希望你还是让我使用你的图书馆。”

“I got the impression you were tired of using it,” he said. “It’s been quiet.”
“我感觉你已经厌倦了使用它，”他说。“一直很安静。”

It had been. When Granger had said she’d be back for their next meeting, he had rather thought she would still show up to work in the library in the meantime. Instead, she’d practically vanished. It was strange for him to think that there was once a time when he’d have been delighted by such a turn of events. Now, as a man who had finally come to terms that he liked her company, that he liked her , he found her prolonged absences just as, if not more, frustrating than her presence.
它曾经是。当格兰杰说她会回来参加他们的下一次会议时，他宁愿认为她在此期间还会出现在图书馆工作。相反，她几乎消失了。他想到曾经有一段时间他会为这样的转变感到高兴，这真是奇怪。现在，作为一个终于接受他喜欢她的陪伴，他喜欢她的男人，他发现她长时间的缺席与她的存在一样令人沮丧，如果不是更令人沮丧的话。

“I took a few days off to help Ginny and Harry settle in with the new baby. And to think.”
“我请了几天假，帮助金妮和哈利安顿好新生儿。并思考。

To think. That was what she’d said she would do. Unsurprisingly, he had been doing the same thing. 
思考。这就是她说她会做的。不出所料，他一直在做同样的事情。

Initially, the morning after their kiss in particular, he’d damned himself as an old fool who had finally succumbed to the madness he’d always suspected would eventually seize him as a result of his house arrest. She was young – arguably too young – and not really anything like what he thought he’d want in a lover; stubborn, proud, argumentative. Infuriating, in other words. But Merlin help him if it didn’t have an effect on him. After eight years of stultifying boredom she was not so much a breath of fresh air as a fucking hurricane.
最初，特别是在他们接吻后的那个早晨，他诅咒自己是个老傻瓜，最终屈服于他一直怀疑的疯狂最终会因为他的软禁而夺走他。她很年轻——可以说太年轻了——根本不像他认为他想要的情人;固执、骄傲、好争论。换句话说，这很令人愤怒。但是如果这对他没有影响，梅林会帮助他。在经历了八年令人窒息的无聊之后，她与其说是一股清新的空气，不如说是一场该死的飓风。

He’d found himself wondering to what extent prolonged exposure was the primary cause of his feelings and whether or not he would simply be cured of them once she finally, inevitably, disappeared out of his life. It was easy to think with that kind of clarity when one was strolling around bright sunlit grounds. 
他发现自己在想，长时间的暴露在多大程度上是他感情的主要原因，以及一旦她最终不可避免地从他的生活中消失，他是否会简单地治愈这些情绪。当一个人在阳光明媚的地面上漫步时，很容易以这种清晰的方式思考。

But then night fell and he’d returned to being ensconced in his study before the fire. Clarity was harder to find then, replaced by memories of her kneeling between his legs, her face drifting so close to his that he rather thought he could have counted each of the freckles on her nose with his mind’s eye if he’d cared to do so. Her stubbornness, pride and argumentativeness added up to passion and, it turned out, that could manifest in rather more appealing ways. Recollections of soft lips, softer skin and breathless moans tended to make rational, measured thoughts roll their eyes and declare that a holiday was in order. 
但后来夜幕降临，他又回到了火灾前的书房里。那时，他更难找到清晰的信息，取而代之的是她跪在他的两腿之间，她的脸离他如此之近，以至于他宁愿认为如果他愿意的话，他可以用心灵的眼睛数出她鼻子上的每一个雀斑。她的固执、骄傲和争论加起来就是激情，事实证明，这可以以更吸引人的方式表现出来。回忆起柔软的嘴唇、柔软的皮肤和喘不过气来的呻吟，往往使理性、有分寸的思考翻白眼，宣布假期已经准备好了。

After a week, he had come to the conclusion that he didn’t regret what had happened. Not a moment of it. He regretted it so little that he was more than willing to do it again. It had been a long time since he'd had an encounter like that but even he could still recognise when it was worth repeating. 
一周后，他得出结论，他并不后悔所发生的事情。一刻也没有。他后悔得如此之少，以至于他非常愿意再做一次。他已经很久没有遇到过这样的遭遇了，但即使是他也能意识到什么时候值得重蹈覆辙。

Besides, he considered himself to be something of a goal driven individual and it had been quite some time since he’d had anything approaching a goal. The idea of what Granger would do to him if she ever got an inkling that he had, even in passing, thought of her as a goal, however, made him cross his legs protectively.
此外，他认为自己是一个目标驱动型的人，他已经有很长一段时间没有接近目标了。然而，如果她知道他曾经把她当作目标，格兰杰会怎么对待他，这让他保护性地交叉着双腿。

“And how did all of that go?”
“那这一切进展如何？”

“The baby is doing very well.”
“宝宝情况很好。”

卢修斯忍住了他对她的混淆的不耐烦。这就是和他说话的感觉吗？多么令人愤怒。“那想法呢？”

“Less well.”
“不太好。”

Good , he thought viciously . It served her right for disappearing. He hoped it had been an unbearable week for her. A week of acute emotional suffering. Pain, sleepless nights, wistful daydreams. All of it. 
好，他恶狠狠地想着。 她有权利消失。他希望这对她来说是难以忍受的一周。一周的剧烈情绪痛苦。痛苦、不眠之夜、渴望的白日梦。所有这一切。

“Still struggling to come to terms with what you want?” he asked, purposely keeping his tone airy and conversational. She could load his question with meaning herself; he was sure she would. 
“还在努力接受你想要的吗？”他问道，故意保持语气轻快和对话。她自己也能把他的问题装满意思;他确信她会的。

赫敏抿着嘴唇，选择完全避开它。“你的腿怎么样了？”她问道，她的声音里异常浓郁的毒液，他实际上觉得挺可爱的。“还在挣扎着站起来，却没有怨恨地激励你？”

“It’s fine,” he said with a sardonic smile. “Thank you for such sincere concern; it does you credit. Such a good, kind-hearted girl.”
“没事，”他带着讽刺的笑容说。“感谢你们如此真诚的关心;它值得称赞。真是个善良、善良的姑娘。

Huffing a sigh through her nose, Hermione dropped some of her defensiveness and adopted an expression that actually did seem close to concerned. “Do you want me to have a look at it?”
赫敏从鼻子里叹了口气，放下了一些防御，采取了一种实际上看起来确实近乎担忧的表情。“你想让我看看吗？”

“Do you want to have a look at it?”
“你想看看吗？”

“Lucius,” she said, weighing his name down with warning. 
“卢修斯，”她说，警告地压低了他的名字。

“ Hermione ,” he responded mockingly.
“赫敏，”他嘲讽地回答。

There was a tense silence in which they eyed one another, Lucius at his ease and Hermione fidgeting with her wand. 
他们面面相觑，一阵紧张的沉默，卢修斯轻松自在，赫敏则摆弄着她的魔杖。

“I’m going to the library,” she said, lunging forward to grab the Wheezebox from his desk. 
“我要去图书馆，”她说，一边冲上前去，从他的书桌上拿起了 Wheezebox。

Lucius watched with a complacent smile as she tidied away her things. Getting to her feet and hauling her bag up, she looked at him and opened her mouth as though she was considering speaking but then closed it again.
卢修斯得意地笑着看着她收拾自己的东西。她站起来，把包拽起来，看着他，张开嘴，好像在考虑说话，但又闭上了嘴。

“Bye,” she mumbled, leaving his study with her head down. 
“再见，”她喃喃自语，低着头离开了他的书房。

July 7th
7 月 7 日

The flat was still and quiet, as was the street outside, with the exception of a bird twittering in a tree somewhere. Hopefully that meant she hadn’t slept too late—she’d agreed the previous week to meet Neville at Hogwarts for another jaunt around the greenhouses and she had no intention of missing it. Especially not if her only truthful excuse was ‘sorry, Neville, overslept after spending most of the night with Lucius Malfoy. No, don’t worry, we only shagged once.’
公寓寂静无声，外面的街道也一样，除了一只鸟在某处的树上叽叽喳喳。希望这意味着她没有睡得太晚——她上周已经约定在霍格沃茨和纳威见面，再去温室里闲逛，她不想错过这个机会。尤其是如果她唯一真实的借口是“对不起，纳威，在和卢修斯·马尔福度过了大半夜之后睡过头了。不，别担心，我们只打过一次。

Snorting out a soft laugh, Hermione burrowed her face further into her pillow and closed her eyes. She was trying extremely hard not to beat herself up about it. They’d done it and she’d enjoyed it. 
赫敏轻声笑了起来，把脸进一步钻进枕头里，闭上了眼睛。她非常努力地不为此自责。他们做到了，她很享受。

Not only that, she’d enjoyed the rest of the night too. After he’d talked her through the various mirrors of the manor, detailing the ones he thought she really ought to avoid while vowing to show her the books containing the theory of their magic, they’d simply continued to talk. Mostly about nothing. Inane things; the books she’d read during her week off, the plants he was growing for Draco, food, magic. It had been oddly easy but, then, they’d practised talking with the most difficult topics first, so was it really so surprising that when they finally moved onto things they enjoyed it felt relatively frictionless? 
不仅如此，她还享受了这个夜晚的剩余时间。在他通过庄园的各种镜子与她交谈，详细说明了他认为她真正应该避免的那些镜子，同时发誓要给她看包含他们魔法理论的书之后，他们只是继续交谈。基本上什么都没有。无聊的东西;她在休息一周里读的书，他为德拉科种的植物，食物，魔法。这本来很容易，但是，他们先练习了谈论最困难的话题，所以当他们最终转向他们喜欢的事情时，感觉相对来说没有摩擦，这真的是不是很令人惊讶？

They even had things in common; he had no patience for divination—though she rather suspected that after his disapproval of the prophecy—and shared her appreciation for Arithmancy; he agreed that white wine was more enjoyable in the heat of the summer but assured her that the only reason she didn’t like Riesling was because she’d been given all the wrong ones, something he was more than happy to fix; and when he’d risen to take some of the books he tended to return to from his personal shelves, they’d both been pleased to find she’d already read most of them. He’d offered to let her spend time in his study to read the others.
他们甚至有一些共同点;他对占卜没有耐心——尽管在他不赞成这个预言之后，她宁愿怀疑这一点——并分享了她对算术的欣赏;他同意白葡萄酒在炎热的夏天更令人愉快，但向她保证，她不喜欢雷司令的唯一原因是她得到了所有错误的雷司令，他非常乐意解决这个问题;当他起身从个人书架上拿起一些他经常回头的书时，他们都很高兴地发现她已经读完了其中的大部分。他提议让她花时间在他的书房里读其他的。

The only reason she’d decided to leave was because she’d found her eyelids drooping against her wishes. As far as she’d been able to tell, Lucius hadn’t been tired at all but, then, she supposed he was very used to keeping unusual hours. She found herself wondering when he actually did sleep and how much of it he tended to get. Would she ever be lying beside him when he did it?
她决定离开的唯一原因是她发现自己的眼睑违背了她的意愿而下垂。据她所知，卢修斯一点也不累，但是，她认为他已经非常习惯了保持不寻常的时间。她发现自己在想他什么时候真的睡着了，他往往会睡多少。当他这样做时，她会躺在他身边吗？

He hadn’t objected when she’d declared her intention to return to her own bed. He hadn’t offered his or another at the manor either and Hermione had actually been glad of that. He’d simply let her go, with a murmured acknowledgement that he’d see her again soon. 
当她宣布打算回到自己的床上时，他并没有反对。他也没有在庄园里提出过他或那个，赫敏实际上很高兴。他只是放开了她，喃喃地承认他很快就会再见到她。

Rolling over, Hermione grabbed her watch from her bedside table and peered at it. 10am and she was meeting Neville at 11. Perfect. Swinging her legs over the side of her bed, she groaned at the ache in her limbs. Glancing down at her bare legs, she saw faint marks on her thighs and, pulling up her t-shirt, her hips. Exhaling shakily, she placed her fingertips against them, imagining they were Malfoy’s. It was going to be hard to keep a clear head.
赫敏翻了个身，从床头柜上拿起她的手表，凝视着它。上午 10 点，她在 11 点与 Neville 见面。完善。她把双腿摆动到床边，四肢的疼痛让她呻吟起来。她低头瞥了一眼她光秃秃的双腿，看到她的大腿上有淡淡的痕迹，拉起她的 T 恤，她的臀部。她颤抖地呼出一口气，将指尖贴在他们身上，想象着他们是马尔福的。要保持清醒的头脑会很困难。

Bending at the waist, Hermione inspected the velvety leaves of Neville’s many dittany plants. She hadn’t spotted any of those in the Malfoy greenhouse. As a plant with healing properties, it would surely be useful to Draco for his potions. On top of that, the idea of presenting Lucius Malfoy with a healing plant that he would have to care for and nurture made a sly smile creep over Hermione’s face. It was so easy to imagine his lip curling before he unleashed some snide comment about sentimentality or a lack of subtlety. 
赫敏弯下腰，检查着纳威的许多白叶植物的天鹅绒般的叶子。她还没在马尔福的温室里看到任何那些东西。作为一种具有治疗特性的植物，它肯定对德拉科的魔药有用。最重要的是，向卢修斯·马尔福赠送一株他必须照顾和培育的治疗植物的想法让赫敏的脸上露出了狡猾的笑容。很容易想象他弯起嘴唇，然后才说出一些关于多愁善感或缺乏微妙的讥讽评论。

“Neville,” Hermione asked, turning her head to look over her shoulder, “is there any chance I could take a cutting of this dittany?”
“纳威，”赫敏问道，转头看向她的肩膀，“我有机会把这个小东西剪下来吗？

“You’re growing?” Neville asked, his voice brimming with enthusiasm as he marched across the room to join her, watering can in hand.
“你在长大吗？”纳威问道，他的声音充满了热情，手里拿着喷壶，穿过房间加入她。

“I’m not,” Hermione said, hesitating. “It’s…er, well, it’d be for the Malfoys. Draco is making potions for St. Mungo’s and his father is growing ingredients in their greenhouse.”
“我不是，”赫敏犹豫着说。“这......呃，嗯，那会是给马尔福家的。德拉科正在为圣芒戈制作药水，他的父亲在他们的温室里种植配料。

“Lucius Malfoy is running a greenhouse?” Neville asked blankly. 
“卢修斯·马尔福在经营一个温室？”纳威茫然地问。

“Well, it’s relatively small. Not as impressive as the Hogwarts greenhouses, that's for sure, but bigger than you’d expect to find in someone’s back garden, if that makes sense.”
“嗯，它相对较小。肯定没有霍格沃茨的温室那么令人印象深刻，但比你想象的在别人的后花园里找到的要大，如果这有意义的话。

“No,” Neville shook his head. “It’s just…I guess I’m surprised that he has the disposition for it, that’s all.”
“不，”纳威摇摇头。“只是......我想我很惊讶他有这样的性格，仅此而已。

Tilting her head, Hermione considered Lucius’ disposition in the context of gardening. He didn’t really strike her as the most natural gardener now that she thought about it. After all, he wore what appeared to be fairly expensive clothes while doing it and he wasn’t exactly a nurturing presence – more of a frost. “I reckon it’s probably touch and go sometimes, to be honest,” Hermione said thoughtfully, “but he seems pretty committed to it. Has an apron and everything.”
赫敏歪着头，思考着卢修斯在园艺方面的性格。现在她想想，他并没有真的觉得她是最自然的园丁。毕竟，他在做这件事时穿着看起来相当昂贵的衣服，而且他并不完全是一个有教养的存在——更像是一个冰霜。“老实说，我估计有时可能是一碰就走，”赫敏若有所思地说，“但他似乎很投入。有围裙和一切。

Neville eyed his dittany with loving concern and glanced up at Hermione. “I suppose I could give you a cutting,” he said, sounding less than certain. “I have some seeds, too, but he’ll need to wait until next spring before planting them.”
纳威用慈爱的眼神看着他的小家伙，抬头看了赫敏一眼。“我想我可以给你剪个剪子，”他说，听起来不太确定。“我也有一些种子，但他需要等到明年春天才能播种。”

“Oh, Neville, that’s so kind of you,” Hermione replied, rising onto the balls of her feet with a smile. 
“哦，纳威，你真是太好了，”赫敏回答，微笑着站起脚掌。

“It’s your kindness,” he assured her. “I’m just facilitating it.” Neville’s face grew troubled as he gazed down at the dittany and back up at Hermione, seemingly internally debating over just how willing he was to part with it for someone like Lucius Malfoy. Sighing through his nose, Neville lifted one shoulder. “It’s kind of hard to do wrong with dittany isn’t it? “
“这是你的好意，”他向她保证。“我只是在促进它。”纳威的脸色变得不安起来，他低头看了看那件小事，又抬头看向赫敏，似乎在心里争论他到底有多愿意为了卢修斯·马尔福这样的人而放弃它。纳威从鼻子里叹了口气，抬起了一侧的肩膀。“用 dittany 做错事有点困难，不是吗？”

Rather than ruin the moment and tell Neville that if anyone could find a way it’d be Lucius Malfoy, Hermione decided to assure him that it’d probably find its way into Draco’s potions and that those definitely were doing good. Setting his watering can down and removing his wand from his pocket, Neville jerked his head at a workbench. 
赫敏没有毁掉这一刻，告诉纳威，如果有人能找到办法，那就是卢修斯·马尔福，而是决定向他保证，它可能会进入德拉科的魔药中，而且那些药剂肯定是好的。放下喷壶，从口袋里掏出魔杖，纳威猛地把头撞向工作台。

“Put some compost in one of those smaller pots. I can take a basal cutting.” 
“在其中一个较小的罐子里放一些堆肥。我可以进行基部切割。

When Hermione had done as Neville asked, she returned to find he’d made a clean cut at the base of the plant. Placing it towards the edge of the pot, he began to pat fresh compost down around it to keep it in place. With a thoughtful frown, Neville picked up his wand again and murmured a couple of spells, making swirling motions over the plant. 
当赫敏按照纳威的要求做了时，她回来发现他在植物的底部做了一个干净的切口。他把它放在花盆的边缘，开始在它周围拍打新鲜的堆肥，以保持它的位置。纳威若有所思地皱起眉头，再次拿起魔杖，喃喃自语了几个咒语，在植物上做出了旋转的动作。

“What are you doing?” Hermione asked, truly interested as an iridescent border formed around the pot and plant.
“你在干什么？”赫敏问道，对花盆和植物周围形成的彩虹色边界感到非常感兴趣。

“We need to keep it kind of moist until you can get it to his greenhouse. That should do it but it’ll only last for a couple of days so try not to hang about.”
“我们需要保持湿润，直到你能把它送到他的温室里。这应该可以，但它只会持续几天，所以尽量不要闲逛。

Hermione nodded fervently, keen to show Neville that she was taking the responsibility seriously. It was rare he was so authoritative and Hermione knew that meant she should listen. He cast a last longing look at the dittany before glancing up at her. 
赫敏热切地点点头，热衷于向纳威表明她正在认真对待这个责任。他很少这么权威，赫敏知道这意味着她应该听。他最后渴望地看了一眼那只小鸡巴，然后抬头看了她一眼。

“I have some books I think he should have as well; they have tips specific to caring for magical herbs for potions. I’ll dig them out when we go up for tea.”
“我有一些书，我想他也应该有;他们有专门照顾药水魔法草药的提示。我们上去喝茶的时候，我会把它们挖出来。

“Oh…er,” Hermione smiled hesitantly, not entirely sure how Lucius would react to receiving instructional books from Neville. Probably not all that well. “That’s nice, thanks Neville.”
“哦......呃，“赫敏犹豫地笑了笑，不完全确定卢修斯收到纳威的指导书会有什么反应。可能不是那么好。“太好了，谢谢纳威。”

“It’s for the plants,” he said firmly. “I want to be sure he’s taking care of them.”
“这是给植物的，”他坚定地说。“我想确保他正在照顾他们。”

“Of course.”
“当然。”

Neville eyed Hermione quietly for a moment. “You said he has an apron,” he said, a small frown pulling his brows together. “For the greenhouse?”
纳威静静地盯着赫敏看了一会儿。“你说他有围裙，”他说，微微皱起眉头。“为了温室？”

“Yes,” Hermione replied, not entirely sure where he might be going with such a question.
“是的，”赫敏回答，不完全确定他会问这样的问题去哪里。

“You actually saw it?”
“你真的看到了？”

“The greenhouse…?”
“温室......？”

“No, the apron.”
“不，围裙。”

“Yes,” Hermione said, even more confused and wondering if greenhouse aprons had to be made from a certain material or ought to meet some kind of quality standard.
“是的，”赫敏说，更加困惑了，想知道温室围裙是不是必须用某种材料制成，或者应该满足某种质量标准。

“And he let you live?”
“他让你活着？”

Hermione’s clouded expression was immediately cleared by the appearance of her wide, bright grin which Neville returned, his shoulders shaking with barely-repressed mirth.
赫敏朦胧的表情立刻被她灿烂而灿烂的笑容所掩盖，纳威回来了，他的肩膀因几乎无法抑制的笑容而颤抖。

“I have been considering having them rewrite my Chocolate Frog card,” Hermione said, leaning forward with a confiding tone, “but I don’t think anyone would believe it. Best just stick with all the Horcrux destroying and dragon riding stuff.”
“我一直在考虑让他们重写我的巧克力蛙卡，”赫敏说，用一种倾诉的语气向前倾，“但我想没有人会相信。最好还是坚持使用所有摧毁魂器和骑龙的东西。

Neville nodded gravely, wearing a look of deep sympathy. “They say it’s the greatest achievements that are the hardest to believe.”
纳威严肃地点点头，露出深深的同情。“他们说，最伟大的成就是最难相信的。”

Catching one another’s eyes they snorted and descended into peels of laughter, Hermione throwing her head back and Neville curling over into himself.
他们四目相接，哼了一声，大笑起来，赫敏把头向后仰，纳威蜷缩着身体。

Straightening up, Neville wiped his shimmering eyes and gave a loud satisfied sigh that suggested he hadn’t laughed so much in a while. For a wild moment, Hermione wondered what would happen if she told him what else she’d seen of Lucius Malfoy. Well, a highly edited version of it. But she couldn’t – keeping it from the Wizengamot meant secrecy overall, even if Neville was kind and understanding. He wouldn’t hate her. Maybe. Or maybe even if she could tell him, it wasn’t worth the risk that he would.  
纳威直起身来，擦了擦他闪闪发光的眼睛，满意地大声叹了口气，这表明他已经有一段时间没有笑了。有那么一刻，赫敏在想，如果她告诉他她还看到了卢修斯·马尔福的什么，会发生什么。嗯，这是它的高度编辑版本。但她不能——不让威森加摩知道这件事意味着总体上是保密的，即使纳威是善良和善解人意的。他不会恨她的。或。或者，即使她能告诉他，他也不值得冒险。

“Tea?” he asked, carefully lifting the dittany pot into his arms and cradling it against his stomach.
“茶吗？”他问道，小心翼翼地把小罐子抱在怀里，把它抱在肚子上。

“Sure,” Hermione said, a somewhat defeated edge to her voice as the moment passed. She wouldn’t—couldn’t—tell him. Not today, at least. 
“当然，”赫敏说，随着时间的流逝，她的声音里有些挫败。她不会——不能——告诉他。至少今天不会。

They moved from the greenhouses to Neville’s office, walking through the empty entrance hall of the castle to get to it. It was so strange to be in Hogwarts during the holidays—the big stone halls were meant to echo with loud, excitable student voices and thundering footsteps moving between classes, rather than quiet conversations between two subdued adults. 
他们从温室搬到了纳威的办公室，穿过城堡空荡荡的门厅才到达办公室。假期里在霍格沃茨真是太奇怪了——巨大的石头大厅里本来是回荡着响亮、兴奋的学生声音和课间雷鸣般的脚步声，而不是两个被压制的成年人之间安静的对话。

Despite knowing that, Hermione wasn’t sure she could ever comfortably return to her schooldays. She thought of walking to classes, anxiously looking back to make sure Ron and Harry were keeping up and not making her late. Or fighting through throngs of other houses on the way out of dinner, trying to make herself heard above the noise, the thought of holding herself up in the quiet of the library or her favourite corner of the common room keeping her sane. 
尽管知道这一点，赫敏还是不确定她是否能舒适地回到她的学生时代。她想着走路去上课，焦急地回头看，确保罗恩和哈利能跟上，不要让她迟到。或者在吃完晚饭的路上穿过成群结队的其他房子，试图让自己的声音盖过喧嚣，一想到要在安静的图书馆或她最喜欢的公共休息室角落里站起来，就能保持理智。

They were fond memories but she wasn’t particularly keen on reliving them. Somehow there was something comforting about that—even if she wasn’t sure exactly what she was supposed to be doing, she’d firmly moved past what she had been doing.
这些都是美好的回忆，但她并不是特别热衷于重温它们。不知何故，这其中有一些令人欣慰的东西——即使她不确定自己到底应该做什么，她已经坚定地超越了她一直在做的事情。

Neville’s office was cosy and warm with squashy chairs and a large number of plants dotted around. It was almost like another greenhouse. The entire wall behind his desk had been taken over by an ivy which, to Hermione’s eye, looked like it was attempting to crawl onto the ceiling, too. He’d probably have to watch that, she thought, having visions of it one day crawling around to block his door.
内维尔的办公室舒适而温暖，有一把南瓜椅子和大量的植物。它几乎就像另一个温室。他桌子后面的整面墙都被一棵常春藤占据了，在赫敏看来，它看起来也好像也想爬到天花板上。他可能得看着那个，她想，有一天他看到它爬来爬去堵住他的门。

Depositing a tray of tea on his desk, Neville shuffled over towards his bookcase and began to pick out the books he’d told her about, occasionally having to gently lift the leaf of a plant out of the way of a title. While he searched, Hermione set about pouring their tea. Neville only took milk but he always had honey for her.
纳威把一盘茶放在书桌上，拖着脚步走向他的书架，开始挑选他告诉她的书，偶尔不得不轻轻地把植物的叶子从书名上掀开。在他寻找的时候，赫敏开始给他们倒茶。纳威只喝牛奶，但他总是给她吃蜂蜜。

“I think these should do the trick,” Neville said, setting four thick tomes on the desk beside her and the still-shimmering dittany cutting. 
“我觉得这些应该能解决问题，”纳威说，把四本厚厚的书放在她旁边的桌子上，还有仍然闪闪发光的碎屑。

“Wonderful. I’ll make sure he gets them.”
“太好了。我会确保他得到它们。

Apparently satisfied that he’d done all he could for Lucius Malfoy’s plants, short of going to Malfoy Manor himself, Neville settled into his chair and pulled his tea towards himself with a murmur of thanks to Hermione for preparing it. They sat in a comfortable silence for a while, Hermione stirring honey into her tea while Neville drank his.
纳威显然对自己为卢修斯·马尔福的植物所做的一切感到满意，除了亲自去马尔福庄园之外，纳威坐在椅子上，把茶拉向自己，低声感谢赫敏准备了茶。他们舒服地沉默了一会儿，赫敏在她的茶里搅拌蜂蜜，而纳威则喝他的茶。

“Hermione,” he said eventually, “can I talk to you about something?”
“赫敏，”他终于说，“我可以和你谈谈什么吗？

Setting her spoon down carefully on her saucer, Hermione nodded and smiled. “Of course, Neville. You don’t have to ask; we can talk about anything.”
赫敏小心翼翼地把勺子放在她的碟子上，点点头，微笑着。“当然，纳威。你不必问;我们可以谈论任何事情。

“It’s about Ron and Hannah.”
“这是关于 Ron 和 Hannah 的。”

Oh . Except that. Don’t get involved, Harry had said. She still agreed with him. “Actually, Neville, I don’t know if that’s the best—”
哦。除了那个。不要卷入其中，哈利说。她还是同意他的看法。“其实，纳威，我不知道那是最好的吗——”

“求求你了，赫敏，”纳威说，他的声音带着绝望的边缘。“我需要和某人谈谈这件事，因为我不能再把它藏在心里了，我就是不能，而且我——”

“纳威，”赫敏惊恐地说，伸出一只安抚他的手。“纳威，没事。没事的。我们可以交谈。我可以听。

“纳威，就好像我永远都不会评判你一样，”赫敏说，感觉越来越不安。纳威可能做了什么让他如此紧张？

“我一直在帮汉娜申请霍格沃茨的护士长工作，”纳威说，他的脸扭曲了起来，就像他刚刚告诉赫敏，他已经把汉娜斩首了，而且已经把她的头放在他的枕头上一个星期了。

作为回应，赫敏只是点了点头。这正是她认为正在发生的事情。纳威并没有因为她完全没有惊讶而感到安慰，反而似乎变得更加焦虑了。
