“Your favourite mug,” Hermione said, handing it to Draco with a smile when she thought she had got her point across. Twin pink spots appeared high on Draco’s pale cheeks as he took it from her with a murmur of thanks. 
“你最喜欢的杯子，”赫敏说，当她认为自己已经说得明白时，微笑着把它递给德拉科。德拉科苍白的脸颊上高高地出现了两个粉红色的斑点，他从她手中接过它，低声表示感谢。

“He has a favourite mug here?” Ginny asked, the mild disgust in her voice drawing a dark scowl from Draco. 
“他这儿有个最喜欢的杯子吗？”金妮问道，她声音中略带的厌恶让德拉科皱起了眉头。

“It’s the biggest one,” he said, drawing his shoulders back and raising his pointed chin to look down his nose at Ginny.
“这是最大的一个，”他说，把肩膀往后拉，抬起尖尖的下巴，低头看着金妮。

“Of course it is,” Ginny replied, rolling her eyes as she took her own usual Holyhead Harpies-branded mug from Hermione with a fleeting, tense smile of thanks. 
“当然是，”金妮回答道，翻了个白眼，从赫敏手中接过她自己平常的霍利黑德鹰身女妖牌杯子，脸上露出一闪而过的感谢微笑。

Hermione returned to the table with her own tea and slid into her seat, clutching it in her hands. “So,” she said with exaggerated brightness, looking back and forth between the reluctant faces of Ginny and Draco. “How are you both?”
赫敏端着自己的茶回到桌子旁，滑进了她的座位，手里紧紧地攥着它。“所以，”她夸张地说，在金妮和德拉科不情愿的面孔之间来回打量。“你们俩都好吗？”

“Fine,” they muttered together, quite obviously avoiding looking at one another. Draco opted to stare into his tea while Ginny poked her fork sullenly into her cake.
“好吧，”他们一起咕哝着，显然避免看彼此。德拉科选择盯着他的茶，而金妮则闷闷不乐地把叉子戳进她的蛋糕里。

“That doesn’t tell me much, does it?” asked Hermione bracingly. “Some specifics might do the trick.”
“这没什么大不了的，对吧？”“一些细节可能会奏效。”

“Well, I take it you heard about Ron and Hannah?” Ginny asked, shaking her head pityingly as she broke off a piece of cake with her fork.
“嗯，我想你听说过罗恩和汉娜的事吧？”金妮问道，一边用叉子掰开一块蛋糕，一边可怜地摇摇头。

“Lost another one has he?” Draco said, raising an eyebrow. “That’ll be another pointless story fuelling the Prophet’s gossip columns for a month. Weasley is very careless for a man who can’t really afford to lose anything.”
“他又丢了一个，是吗？”德拉科说，扬起了一道眉毛。“这将是另一个毫无意义的故事，让先知的八卦专栏持续一个月。韦斯莱对一个真的不能失去任何东西的人非常粗心。

“That's my brother, Malfoy,” Ginny growled, her grip on her fork fractionally tightening.
“那是我哥哥，马尔福，”金妮咆哮着，她握着叉子的手稍微收紧了。

“Then surely,” Draco said, with an affected shrug, “as his sister, you are immune to the incomprehensible physical charm he seems to have for some witches and are able to see that he's utterly bloody hopeless.”
“那么肯定，”德拉科耸了耸肩说，“作为他的妹妹，你对他似乎对某些女巫所具有的难以理解的身体魅力免疫，并且能够看到他完全没有希望。

Ginny narrowed her eyes at Draco and jabbed her fork back into her cake. “Well, yes, but you're not allowed to say that.”
金妮眯起眼睛看着德拉科，把叉子插回了她的蛋糕里。“嗯，是的，但你不能这么说。”

“I did know,” Hermione finally said, setting her tea down and clutching the mug between her palms. “He came here the night it happened, actually. Quite drunk.”

“你能怪我吗？”“你真的可以责怪我怀疑吗？还是生气？那一年是——那一年——在我的脑海中——“金妮的声音颤抖着，她松开双臂，用拳头狠狠地擦过她满是雀斑的脸颊，仿佛在警告她的眼睛，它们可能会保持干燥，否则就会面临暴力。他欠我一年的生命。那可不是你就能从家族金库里拿出来还的债，马尔福，不管里面有多么满满的金子。

Draco’s face was always pale but Hermione thought it looked even paler as he assessed Ginny across the table. Glancing down at James, still content in his lap, Draco cleared his throat. “We can’t, you’re right. I’m sorry, Weasley. I am.” Ginny visibly stiffened, her back straightening as Draco met her eyes. “A year of… him in your house is bad enough. A year in your head, I struggle to imagine.”
德拉科的脸总是苍白的，但赫敏觉得当他打量着桌子对面的金妮时，脸色更加苍白了。德拉科低头看了一眼仍然满足地坐在他腿上的詹姆斯，清了清嗓子。“我们不能，你说得对。对不起，韦斯莱。我是。金妮明显地僵硬了起来，当德拉科与她的眼睛对上时，她的背挺直了。“一年...... 他在你家里已经够坏的了。在你的脑海中，我很难想象一年。

When she’d asked them both to stay for tea, she hadn’t expected it to be quite so confrontational. Even in the silence, they hadn’t broken eye contact. 
赫敏几乎不敢在寂静中呼吸，寂静从几秒变成了几分钟，她把她的背靠在椅子上，仿佛她可能会从椅子上沉下去，消失不见。当她邀请他们俩留下来喝茶时，她没想到会如此对抗。即使在寂静中，他们也没有中断眼神交流。

Lowering her hands and her eyes into her lap, Ginny finally made a small noise in the back of her throat and brushed down her long dress, straightening out the creases. “I suppose I got the pretty version,” she eventually said, flicking her hair over her shoulder. “If we’re looking for small mercies.”
金妮垂下双手，眼睛盯着她的膝盖，终于在她的喉咙后部发出了一个小小的声音，然后拂过她的长裙，理顺了折痕。“我想我得到了漂亮的版本，”她最终说，把头发甩到肩膀上。“如果我们在寻找小小的怜悯。”

Draco’s shoulders dropped as he let go of a breath and Hermione exhaled a single faint laugh. Ginny smiled, though it was closer to a pained grimace, and she gave Hermione a sidelong look that told her this small surrender was for her and no one else. 
德拉科的肩膀垂下来，他松了一口气，赫敏发出一声淡淡的笑声。金妮笑了，虽然更像是一个痛苦的鬼脸，她斜头看了赫敏一眼，告诉她这个小小的投降是为了她自己，而不是其他人。

“And I’ll have to wait for my apology from your father, will I?” Ginny asked Draco, eyes flicking to him. “I’m sure he has plenty of people to get around.”
“我得等你爸爸道歉，对吧？”金妮问德拉科，眼睛眨着他。“我敢肯定他有很多人可以四处走动。”

Draco tilted his head and lifted his shoulders which Ginny seemed to take for a yes. James bashed the tail of his phoenix toy excitedly against the table, just catching Draco’s hand. With a small ‘oh’, James then lay the toy’s head down softly against where he had made contact with Draco, as though soothing him.
德拉科歪着头，抬起肩膀，金妮似乎把这当作是肯定的。詹姆斯兴奋地把他的凤凰玩具的尾巴砸在桌子上，刚好抓住了德拉科的手。詹姆斯轻轻地“哦”了一声，然后把玩具的头轻轻地靠在他和德拉科接触的地方，仿佛在安抚他。

“How’s Potter?” Draco asked, turning his eyes up from James to Ginny, who appeared fixated on what her son was doing with the phoenix. 
“波特怎么样？”德拉科问道，把目光从詹姆斯转向金妮，金妮似乎正专注于她儿子对凤凰做什么。

“He’s…he’s fine. Thank you.” Her eyes darted up to Draco’s. “He’s with Albus today. And your…” Ginny shook her head, as though forcing the next word to come loose. “Wife?”
“他......他没事。谢谢你。她的眼睛瞪向德拉科的眼睛。“他今天和阿不思在一起。而你的......”金妮摇了摇头，仿佛在强迫下一个词松动。“老婆？”

“Astoria,” he proffered graciously.
“阿斯托利亚，”他亲切地提议。

“Astoria,” Ginny said, her tone experimental, like she was tasting the name for the first time and wasn’t sure if she’d like it.
“阿斯托利亚，”金妮说，她的语气带着实验性，就像她第一次品尝这个名字，不确定自己是否喜欢它。

“She’s well enough,” Draco said. “Very pregnant. Very keen to impress on me that our children will be attending Hogwarts together.”
“她已经很好了，”德拉科说。“非常怀孕。我非常想让我印象深刻，我们的孩子会一起在霍格沃茨上学。

Ginny’s eyes travelled back to James who had started pecking his phoenix toy into Draco’s cake, pretending it was eating. Hermione thought she saw something in Ginny soften ever so slightly.
金妮的目光又回到了詹姆斯身上，詹姆斯开始把他的凤凰玩具啄进德拉科的蛋糕里，假装它在吃东西。赫敏觉得她在金妮身上看到了什么，稍微软化了一点。

“Not for a while,” she finally said. “Gives us some time, I suppose.”
“暂时没有，”她终于说。“我想，给我们一些时间。”

Draco huffed out a laugh, his shoulders jumping once. “That it does.”
德拉科哼哼大笑，他的肩膀跳了一下。“确实如此。”

7月31日

Hermione Granger was angry. Hermione Granger was furious. Hermione Granger was barging into Lucius Malfoy’s study with a letter clutched so tightly in her fist that the ink on the parchment was in danger of tattooing her skin. 
赫敏·格兰杰很生气。赫敏·格兰杰大发雷霆。赫敏·格兰杰闯进卢修斯·马尔福的书房，拳头里紧紧地攥着一封信，羊皮纸上的墨水有纹身的危险。

“Ridiculous!” she spat from the wide open doorway. 
“荒谬！” 她从敞开的门口吐了一口唾沫。

With the delicate care of a man who had just been told it was rigged to blow, Lucius set the quill he had been using back in its well in his desk and, clasping his hands together, looked up at Hermione with a patient, expectant expression. 
在一个刚刚被告知它纵起来会爆炸的男人的细心照顾下，卢修斯将他一直在使用的羽毛笔放回办公桌的井中，双手紧握，抬头看着赫敏，露出耐心、期待的表情。

“Aren’t you going to ask me what’s ridiculous?” she said after a beat of silence.
“你不打算问我什么荒谬吗？”

“You are going to tell me whether I ask or not, Hermione. I thought it foolish to risk an interruption when you’re so…” He pushed his lower lip out, his eyes running down her tense stance. “Piqued.”
“你得告诉我我问不问，赫敏。我觉得冒着被打扰的风险是愚蠢的，因为你是......”他把下唇往外推，眼睛顺着她紧张的姿势扫过。“生气了。”

Hermione chewed the inside of her cheek, her eyes narrowing, and entered Lucius’ study properly, closing the door behind her with what he felt was a touch more force than entirely necessary. 
赫敏咬了咬她的脸颊内侧，眯起了眼睛，然后正确地走进了卢修斯的书房，用他觉得比完全必要的力气更强的触碰关上了她身后的门。

“This,” she said, raising the letter in her clenched fist, “is another rejection.”
“这个，”她说，用紧握的拳头举起那封信，“又一次被拒绝。

Ah . Lucius nodded. The rejections. This must have been her fourth? No, fifth. He was beginning to see that Hermione Granger did not take non-constructive criticism especially well. The last rejection had come the day before and it had ended up taking most of his stamina and a lot of faith in the structural integrity of his study sofa to distract her and ease her frustration. He wasn’t sure he had the energy on this particular afternoon for a repeat performance and he rather suspected she was too angry for it to work anyway.
啊。卢修斯点点头。拒绝。这一定是她的第四次吧？不，第五。他开始看到赫敏·格兰杰并没有特别好地接受非建设性的批评。最后一次被拒绝是在前一天，结果他花了大部分的耐力和对书房沙发结构完整性的很大信心来分散她的注意力，缓解她的挫败感。他不确定自己在这个特别的下午是否有精力再演一遍，他宁愿怀疑她太生气了，无论如何都不起作用。

“And do you know what it says? Do you know what it has the cheek to say?”
“你知道它说什么吗？你知道它有什么厚脸皮要说的吗？

Lucius raised his eyebrows and blinked away the pleasant memory of Hermione bent over his sofa, dress rucked up around her waist and knickers around her spread knees. “I can use my imagination,” he said. “The word ‘rejection’ is fairly self-explanatory, Hermione, and there hasn’t been a great deal of variation in the letters.”
卢修斯扬起眉毛，眨了眨眼，赫敏弯下腰，裙子围在腰间，短裤围在她张开的膝盖上。“我可以发挥我的想象力，”他说。“'拒绝'这个词是不言自明的，赫敏，而且信件中没有太大的变化。”

“No, this one is different.”
“不，这个不一样。”

Lucius leaned back in his chair, waving an imperious hand that invited her to continue. “It says that they won’t publish my book because…” Some of her rage dimmed as she met his eyes and she lowered the hand wielding the parchment, keeping her fist clenched tight. “Because you’re included.”
卢修斯靠在椅子上，挥舞着一只专横的手，邀请她继续说下去。“它说他们不会出版我的书，因为......”当她与他的眼睛相遇时，她的愤怒消退了一些，她放下了挥舞着羊皮纸的手，紧紧握着拳头。“因为你被包括在内。”

A tight smile spread across Lucius’ face. So one of them had finally said it. “What’s their view on Draco?” he asked.
卢修斯的脸上绽放出紧绷的笑容。所以他们中的一个人终于说了出来。“他们对德拉科有什么看法？”

“They don’t seem to have as much of an issue with him," she said, glancing down at the letter. "At least, he’s not mentioned.”
“他们似乎对他没有那么大的问题，”她说，低头看了一眼那封信。“至少，他没有被提及。”

Lucius nodded, satisfied. “Well, then, you know what you have to do then, don’t you?” he said lightly, sitting forward again to lift his quill back out of its well. “Remove me.” 
卢修斯满意地点点头。“那么，你知道你该怎么做，不是吗？”他淡淡地说，又坐了起来，把羽毛笔从井里拿了出来。“把我移开。”

The rejection letter slammed down on his desk under Hermione’s palm. Lucius looked at it from under his brow and slowly lifted his eyes up her tense arm, over the grim set of her jaw and up to her furiously gleaming eyes. “I will not,” she said.

Their director is a tasteless moron. And quite tactless, apparently.”

赫敏的另一只手放在他的桌子上，她向他靠了靠。“你为什么不更生气呢？”她问道，她歪着头，眯着眼睛看着他，就像她正试图从远处看出一个标志。“你不觉得这很荒谬吗？”

With a soft sigh, Lucius placed the quill back in its well. His letter to the estate manager could wait because his witch could not. “I think,” he began carefully, “that it’s not particularly surprising, actually. And I don’t say that to disparage your surprise. I say it to balance your righteousness with some realism.”
卢修斯轻轻叹了口气，将羽毛笔放回了井中。他写给庄园经理的信可以等一会儿，因为他的女巫不能。“我想，”他小心翼翼地开始说，“其实这并不特别令人惊讶。我这么说并不是为了贬低你的惊讶。我说这句话是为了平衡你的正义和一些现实主义。

卢修斯看着赫敏的一根眉毛扬起，她把手从他的桌子上推开，直起身来，低头看着他，让信皱成一团。

“但他们甚至没有读你说的话，”她坚持说，她的手放在臀部上。“他们甚至不知道，他们只是一发不可收拾地不屑一顾。”

He gave her a searching look. It was, admittedly, quite nice to have someone be so outraged on his behalf but really her naivety was astounding. 
他探寻地看了她一眼。诚然，有人为他如此愤怒是件好事，但实际上她的天真令人震惊。

“那是他们的特权，”他摇着头说。“他们是一门生意，赫敏。他们必须赚钱。显然，他们认为我参与你的书可能对销售不利。

“我想你会发现我可以。”

“像贝拉特里克斯甚至克劳奇的儿子这样的人都被描绘成伏地魔的暴力狂热分子。遥不可及。但是你。 “赫敏呼出一口气，摇了摇头，她的卷发弹跳着。”凭借你的财富和影响力，你和其他像你一样的人就这样溜走了。你自己说过：你很务实。在第二次战争中，正是这种实用主义让你回到了他身边。而你的沉默并不是因为你看到了任何重大错误。

Lucius remained silent this time, his jaw tight shut and his tongue pressed to the roof of his mouth as he watched her grow more distressed. He had somehow forgotten, in gaining so much from them, that their interviews weren’t for him. They were for her and she had aims that pre-dated their closeness. 
这一次卢修斯保持沉默，他的下巴紧闭着，舌头贴在嘴巴上颚，看着她变得更加痛苦。他不知怎么的忘记了，虽然从他们那里得到了这么多，但他们的采访并不适合他。他们是为了她，她的目标早于他们的亲密。

“And now that they’ve figured you out, they’ve just locked you up and I bet they over time they lump you in with the rest of them. They’ll say ‘ah, we saw through him in the end’.” She laughed mirthlessly and pushed herself off the desk, throwing a hand out. “But they didn’t! Not really; you just made it impossible for them not to see. They’ll forget everything that went before and never learn the lesson from it. Well, I won’t let them.”
“现在他们已经弄清楚了你，他们就把你关起来了，我敢打赌，随着时间的推移，他们会把你和其他人混在一起。他们会说'啊，我们最终看穿了他'。她无情地笑了起来，把自己从桌子上推开，伸出一只手。“但他们没有！没有;你只是让他们不可能看不到。他们会忘记之前的一切，永远不会从中吸取教训。好吧，我不会让他们的。

She took a deep breath, her eyes gleaming. “And I know you’re different now, Lucius. I know it. But you… you’re proof that evil and cruelty aren't just found in mad wizards who want to live forever and rule the world. Sometimes cruelty and evil worm their way into seemingly respectable, otherwise intelligent people who are too apathetic to question what they've been told and too selfish to see beyond how things affect just them.”
她深吸一口气，眼睛闪闪发光。“我知道你现在不一样了，Lucius。我知道。但是你。。。你证明了邪恶和残忍不仅仅存在于想要长生不老并统治世界的疯狂巫师身上。有时，残忍和邪恶会蠕动到看似受人尊敬、本来聪明的人身上，他们太冷漠了，不敢质疑他们被告知的事情，也太自私了，不敢看到事情如何影响他们自己。

“That’s quite enough, Hermione,” Lucius said, his voice sharp. “Thank you. Your point has been sufficiently pressed.”
“够了，赫敏，”卢修斯说，他的声音很尖锐。“谢谢你。你的观点已经被充分地抓住了。

“I know that’s not all you are.”
“我知道那不是你的全部。”

“I’m so very glad.” Lucius could not help the sarcasm that crept in.
“我非常高兴。”卢修斯忍不住悄悄溜进来的讽刺。

“I know you feel differently now.” 
“我知道你现在的感觉不一样了。”

“I do.” 
“我愿意。”

“And that’s important for people to know too! I’ll make sure they know it. But our problems didn’t just disappear with Voldemort and what you’ve told me about you, your father, that circle , shows that they didn’t just start with him either.”  
“人们知道这一点也很重要！我会确保他们知道。但是我们的问题并没有随着伏地魔而消失，你告诉我的关于你、你父亲、那个圈子的事情表明，这些问题也不只是从他开始的。

Tapping his fingers once, twice on his desk, Lucius inspected her earnest face. “The wizarding world doesn’t want to hear that right now, Hermione.”
卢修斯用手指敲了一下，在他的桌子上敲了两下，打量着她认真的脸。“魔法世界现在不想听这些，赫敏。”

Lucius uncrossed his legs to lean forward and pushed himself to his feet, his fingertips coming to barely lean on his desk. Having her speak all those words down to him had had an aggravating effect and he rather felt that standing to face her was the only solution. 
卢修斯松开双腿，身体前倾，站起来，指尖勉强靠在桌子上。让她对他说所有这些话已经产生了加重的效果，他宁愿觉得站着面对她是唯一的解决办法。

“It wants to hear that everything is fine. That everything is better. You need to accept that not everyone is like you – not everyone wants to reflect and not everyone wants to hear from me. In fact, you must be aware that most people will see my name and put your book straight back on the shelf.”
“它想听到一切都很好。一切都变得更好了。你需要接受不是每个人都像你一样的事实——不是每个人都想反思，也不是每个人都想听我说话。事实上，你必须意识到，大多数人会看到我的名字，然后直接把你的书放回书架上。

“You should give people more credit, Lucius.”
“你应该给人们更多的荣誉，卢修斯。”

“You give them more than enough for both of us, I think,” he replied, eyebrows rising admonishingly as he slipped his hands into his pockets, his shoulders drawing back. 
“我想，你给他们俩的钱已经绰绰有余了，”他回答道，双手口袋，肩膀向后缩，眉毛告诫地扬起。

Her nostrils flared, her lips pressing thin. “I think someone will publish me,” she said firmly. “ With your contribution. I just have to push.”
她的鼻孔张开，嘴唇紧紧地抿着。“我想有人会把我公布出来，”她坚定地说。“凭借您的贡献。我只需要推动。

Eyes flicking briefly upwards, like he had spied his patience evaporating, Lucius exhaled sharply. “And I think you are setting yourself up for disappointment. Your work will still be an achievement without me in it. It will still have an impact.”
卢修斯的眼睛短暂地向上眨了眨，就像他发现自己的耐心正在蒸发一样，卢修斯猛地呼出一口气。“而且我认为你正在让自己失望。没有我的参与，你的工作仍然是一项成就。它仍然会产生影响。

“It won't be what I want,” she said, her tone sharpening. 
“这不会是我想要的，”她说，语气变得尖锐起来。

“You're being a stubborn fool,” Lucius said, unable to keep the sharpness from his own voice. “Either you want to be published or you don't. If it's the former, then you should do whatever is necessary to make it happen. If it's the latter…well, by all means continue what you’re doing.”
“你是个顽固的傻瓜，”卢修斯说，无法抑制自己声音的尖锐。“要么你想被发布，要么你不想。如果是前者，那么您应该采取一切必要措施来实现它。如果是后者......好吧，一定要继续你正在做的事情。

“Well, what about you?” Hermione demanded, jabbing an aggressive hand towards him across the desk that felt like an increasing gulf between them. “Do you ever want to leave this manor or not? Do you want your magic back or not? It feels like you don’t. It feels like you don’t even want to try.”
“嗯，那你呢？”赫敏质问道，一只咄咄逼人的手隔着桌子戳向他，感觉他们之间的鸿沟越来越大。“你有没有想离开这个庄园？你想要不要拿回你的魔法？感觉你没有。感觉你甚至都不想尝试。

How had he forgotten how irritating she could be? “Do you really want your cautionary tale walking free?” he asked, his lip curling. “What kind of message does that send?”
他怎么忘记了她有多么令人恼火呢？“你真的想让你的警世故事自由行走吗？”“这传达了什么样的信息？”

“Lucius, don’t,” Hermione said firmly. “You know I’ve advocated for you. You’ve helped me like you promised and I think if we just pushed the publishers –”
“卢修斯，别这样，”赫敏坚定地说。“你知道我一直在为你辩护。你像你承诺的那样帮助了我，我想如果我们只是推动出版商——”

“You tried, Hermione,” he interrupted shortly, “but it hasn’t worked. You will be published without my contribution or not at all and the former is clearly the better option. I can tell you right now, I am not the kind of wizard who is going to facilitate any of your absurd plots of noble self-sacrifice for some wizarding world greater good –"
“你试过了，赫敏，”他很快打断了他，“但没用。你将在没有我的贡献的情况下被发布，或者根本没有，前者显然是更好的选择。我现在可以告诉你，我不是那种会为了魔法世界更大的利益而为你任何高尚的自我牺牲的荒谬阴谋提供便利的巫师——”

“What,” she said with a scoff, crossing her arms, “and I'm supposed to just facilitate yours for me?”
“什么，”她交叉双臂嘲讽地说，“我就该帮你忙吗？

“I am not being noble you daft witch,” he snapped, clenching his hands into fists in his pockets. “I am pointing you towards the path where you stand to gain at least something .”
“我不是高贵的，你这个女巫，”他厉声说，双手紧握成口袋里的拳头。“我为你指明了一条道路，在那里你至少可以获得一些东西。”

“I don't care about gaining anything.” 
“我不在乎得到任何东西。”

"What else is there to care about?”
“还有什么好关心的？”

Incensed, Hermione opened her mouth to argue back and then seemed to think twice. Closing her mouth tight, she shot him an exasperated glare, nodded once like his words had reminded her of something unpleasant and marched away from him. 
赫敏被激怒了，张开嘴想反驳，然后似乎又想了三思。她紧紧地闭上嘴巴，恼怒地瞪了他一眼，点了点头，仿佛他的话让她想起了什么不愉快的事情，然后大步离开了他。

Lucius let her go, not even looking as she slammed the door behind her. When he was quite sure she was down the corridor, he withdrew his clenched fists from his pockets and slammed one firmly on the table, just to the left of the rejection letter she had left behind. 
卢修斯放开了她，甚至没有看她一眼，她砰地一声关上了身后的门。当他非常确定她在走廊上时，他从口袋里掏出紧握的拳头，用力地将一个拳头砸在桌子上，正好在她留下的拒绝信的左边。

Lucius swirled his firewhiskey in its glass, watching the amber liquid churn with unfocused eyes. Darkness pressed at the windows of his study but the low-burning embers in his fireplace just about kept it at his back. 
卢修斯在玻璃杯中旋转他的火威士忌，用无神相看的眼睛看着琥珀色的液体翻腾。黑暗压在他书房的窗户上，但壁炉里低矮燃烧的余烬几乎把它挡在了他的背后。

Hermione was right – he didn’t think the Wizengamot would be interested in granting him any kind of clemency if it thought he wasn’t able to see the one bit of good he was supposed to be doing to the end. 
赫敏是对的——他不认为威森加摩会有兴趣给予他任何形式的宽大处理，如果它认为他看不到他应该做的一点点好事。

But even with her expert skills in badgering, he doubted any publisher would have him in her book if they thought it would be bad for sales or their reputation. He detested the idea that he was impeding her. Of course, she was also impeding herself in her refusal to simply drop him. 
但即使她精通缠斗，他也怀疑任何出版商如果认为这对销售或声誉不利，就会让他出现在她的书中。他讨厌他阻碍她的想法。当然，她也阻碍了自己拒绝简单地放弃他。

She wouldn't, either; drop him. Not when she had a point that she wanted to put across. She was relentless. A stampede of Hippogriffs couldn't stop Hermione Granger when she had a point to prove and Lucius rather suspected that the defeat of the Dark Lord owed as much to that as it did to Potter.
她也不会;放弃他。当她有一个她想表达的观点时，就不会了。她是无情的。当赫敏·格兰杰需要证明一点时，一群骏鹰的狂奔并不能阻止她，卢修斯宁愿怀疑黑魔王的失败与波特的失败一样多。

Instinctively he'd wanted to be angry at what she'd said. Evil and cruelty. Apathy and selfishness. Ugly words and certainly not how he'd viewed himself at the time. Instead, though, he'd allowed himself to ruminate on them and it had made a strange kind of regretful exhaustion seep into his very bones. 
他本能地想对她说的话生气。邪恶和残忍。冷漠和自私。难听的话语，当然不是他当时如何看待自己。然而，相反，他允许自己沉思它们，这让一种奇怪的遗憾疲惫渗入了他的骨子里。

Once he'd wanted her removed from the wizarding world entirely and would have been happy to be the one to make it happen. Now, he disliked the idea that she wasn't achieving her potential within it and the idea that it was in some way down to him made it worse. His current feelings certainly weren't rooted in any kind of selfishness or cruelty and that made the unproductive, poisonous nature of his old feelings all the more clear.
他曾经想把她从魔法世界里完全赶出去，并且会很高兴成为实现这一目标的人。现在，他不喜欢她没有发挥她的潜力的想法，而这在某种程度上取决于他的想法使情况变得更糟。他现在的感情当然不是植根于任何形式的自私或残忍，这使得他旧感情的无益、有毒的本质更加明显。

He thought she was wrong. He thought she didn’t really stand much of a chance. But he didn’t take much satisfaction in telling her that. It was, he had spent the evening reasoning to himself, surely better to try to help her. Maybe that would go some way towards mitigating the frustrated guilt he was feeling. 
他认为她错了。他觉得她真的没有多少机会。但他对告诉她这件事并不感到满意。是的，他花了一整晚的时间自言自语，最好还是试着帮助她。也许这会在某种程度上减轻他感到的沮丧内疚。

So, he had sent a letter to the one contact he’d made in the media who had been brought almost as low as him and was, therefore, likely to reply without an expectation of anything in return: Barnabus Cuffe, the former and extremely disgraced editor of the Daily Prophet. 
因此，他给他在媒体上结识的一位联系人写了一封信，这个人几乎和他一样被贬低，因此，他很可能不求任何回报就回复了：巴纳布斯·库姆（Barnabus Cuffe），《预言家日报》（Daily Prophet）的前任编辑，也是极度耻辱的编辑。

Cuffe was a man without scruples but Lucius thought he was oddly boyish about it. Everything was important and worthy of his unrestrained enthusiasm but only insofar as it contained potential for “good copy”. He didn’t actually take anything seriously, including himself or his work. To do so would have risked feeling any kind of responsibility for the power and influence that he and the Prophet had once had in the wizarding world. He had seen himself as the caretaker of the Prophet, not the people who read it. 
库尔普是一个毫无顾忌的人，但卢修斯认为他对此感到奇怪的孩子气。一切都很重要，值得他无拘无束的热情，但前提是它包含着“好副本”的潜力。他实际上并没有把任何事情当回事，包括他自己或他的工作。这样做就有可能对他和先知曾经在魔法世界中拥有的权力和影响力承担任何责任。他把自己看作是先知的看护人，而不是阅读先知的人。

Cuffe had never cared about the actual news, he had cared about stories and sales. He had always been able to justify publishing anything as long as he thought it would serve his newspaper well and keep it in print. It had made things very easy when the Dark Lord had returned to power; no bribes were ever required to make the Daily Prophet print in line with the power of the day. 
Cuffe 从不关心实际的新闻，他关心的是故事和销售。他总是能够证明出版任何东西是合理的，只要他认为它对他的报纸有好处并保持印刷。当黑魔王重新掌权时，事情变得非常容易;不需要贿赂就能使《预言家日报》的印刷符合当时的权力。

Yes, Cuffe was spineless and, like anyone who had been on the wrong side of his poisonously impartial quill, Lucius didn’t especially like him but he was one of the few people from whom Lucius thought he might get an honest assessment of Hermione’s chances. 
是的，库普没有骨气，就像任何一个在他那有毒的公正的羽毛笔上站在错误一边的人一样，卢修斯并不特别喜欢他，但他是卢修斯认为他可能会从中得到对赫敏机会的诚实评估的少数人之一。

Lucius had sent the owl three hours ago, which had been three hours after Hermione had marched out of his study. After an hour without a reply, he had grown irate. After two, that melted into a paranoia about the extent of his own irrelevance. And here he was at hour three: drinking.
卢修斯在三个小时前送来了猫头鹰，也就是赫敏走出书房的三个小时后。一个小时没有回答后，他变得愤怒起来。两次之后，这就融化成了对他自己无关紧要程度的偏执狂。而他在第三个小时：喝酒。

He was just beginning to ponder how he might further spiral in hour four when his owl, Nuncio, returned to peck imperiously at his window, a letter tied neatly around his leg. Setting his drink on his desk, Lucius pushed himself out of his seat with a grunt and allowed Nuncio in. Unfurling the parchment, he absently stroked a hand over the owl’s head before reading.
他刚开始思考如何在第四个小时里进一步螺旋式上升，这时他的猫头鹰 Nuncio 回来了，威风凛凛地啄着他的窗户，一封信整齐地系在他的腿上。卢修斯把饮料放在桌子上，咕哝着从座位上站起来，让努西奥进来。他展开羊皮纸，心不在焉地用一只手抚摸着猫头鹰的头，然后读了起来。

“Lucius, 
“卢修斯，

My good man, I cannot tell you what a shock it is to receive a letter from you; I rather thought you hated my guts. Although you were always meticulously polite, so perhaps you do and just write a marvellous letter when you want to.  
我的好人，我无法告诉你收到你的来信是多么的震惊;我宁愿以为你讨厌我的胆量。虽然你总是一丝不苟地彬彬有礼，但也许你这样做了，只是在你想写一封很棒的信的时候写一封很棒的信。

After all, I don’t think anyone who actually likes me would ask how my enforced retirement is going. Don’t think I didn’t notice that little jab, you snake. How would you feel if I asked you how house arrest is treating you? 
毕竟，我认为任何真正喜欢我的人都不会问我强制退休的情况如何。别以为我没注意到那个小戳，你这个蛇。如果我问你软禁对你有什么影响，你会有什么感觉？

Retirement is utterly bloody miserable, as I’m sure you well know. Just the other day, while I was taking my morning walk, I considered divorcing Mabel. Nothing she’s done, of course — marvellous woman — but I thought it might shake things up. Don’t know why I’m bothering, mind, because she’ll take every galleon I’ve got and my balls to boot. Not that they’re much to boast about these days. Time does a number on every wizard, Lucius, just you wait.  
退休是极其悲惨的，我相信你很清楚。就在前几天，当我早上散步时，我考虑过要和梅布尔离婚。当然，她什么都没做——了不起的女人——但我认为这可能会改变一切。不知道我为什么这么烦，注意，因为她会把我的每一艘大帆船和我的蛋蛋都带走。这几天他们没什么好夸耀的。时间对每个巫师都产生了影响，卢修斯，你等着。

I toyed with writing a memoir but, truly, there is nothing more dull than writing about oneself. Even a man who regards himself as highly as you would struggle with it, I’m sure. I’ve tried writing anonymous letters to the Prophet, too, but that hoity toity little fucker that Shacklebolt brought in to replace me has returned every one. My views are ‘not conducive to pleasant reading’ apparently.  
我曾想写一本回忆录，但说真的，没有什么比写自己更乏味的了。我敢肯定，即使是一个和你一样把自己看得很重的人也会为此而挣扎。我也试过给先知写匿名信，但沙克尔博尔特带来的那个用来代替我的那个神圣的小混蛋已经把一封信都退回来了。我的观点显然“不利于愉快的阅读”。

Now, onto your predicament because I am very aware that you don’t give a toss about me, even if I do appreciate that you went to the effort to pretend to care. As I said: meticulously polite. 
现在，说说你的困境，因为我非常清楚你不会对我发呆，即使我真的很感激你不遗余力地假装关心。正如我所说：一丝不苟的礼貌。

I’m no longer publicly welcome in the old circles but I still have my contacts in private and I can honestly tell you it doesn’t shock me in the least that they’re not willing to take on Granger’s book with you included. You’re just not the mood these days, Lucius. You’re the bad times; the enemy vanquished. No one wants to think about you, never mind read about you. Shacklebolt is telling the wizarding world to look forward and, by gum, it’s happy to do it. 
我不再在旧圈子里公开受欢迎，但我仍然私下里有我的联系人，我可以诚实地告诉你，他们不愿意和你一起接受格兰杰的书，这丝毫没有让我感到震惊。你这几天的心情不太好，Lucius。你是糟糕的时代;敌人被击败了。没有人想着你，更不用说阅读你的信息了。沙克尔博尔特告诉魔法世界要向前看，而且，它很高兴这样做。

If Granger wants a hit, she’d be better served leaning into the heroics. That’s what everyone wants right now. A heroic Golden Girl who tells them they were worth every sacrifice she and her little friends made. Golden Girls don’t talk to Death Eaters, Lucius, you know that.  
如果格兰杰想要一击，她最好靠向英雄主义靠拢。这就是现在每个人都想要的。一个英勇的金童玉女，告诉他们她和她的小朋友们所做的每一次牺牲都是值得的。黄金女郎不和食死徒说话，卢修斯，你知道的。

That said… gold is still valuable, even when it’s tarnished. You aren’t a man known for allowing his words to be written down and people are naturally curious. Even a little morbid. They might well buy it just to confirm to themselves that you’re as bad as they thought. I’m in no position to publish her but I would if I could. She might find someone like me, although it’s possible that you wouldn’t be overly enamoured with the marketing angle I’d take. 
可是。。。黄金仍然很有价值，即使它被玷污了。你不是一个以允许他的话被写下来而闻名的人，人们天生好奇。甚至有点病态。他们很可能只是为了向自己确认你和他们想象的一样糟糕。我没有资格发表她，但如果可以的话，我会的。她可能会找到像我这样的人，尽管你可能不会对我所采取的营销角度过于着迷。

I won’t even ask how you and Granger have come to be acquainted. Merlin knows, I can appreciate what a highly restricted social circle can do to a man’s standards and I –” 
我什至不会问你和格兰杰是怎么认识的。梅林知道，我能体会到一个高度受限的社交圈对一个男人的标准有什么影响，而我——”

With an irate grumble, Lucius crumpled Cuffe’s letter in his fist and threw it aimlessly across his desk. It soared over Hermione’s abandoned rejection and landed on the floor. Cuffe was a boor. But he had a point – people were naturally curious. Nosy, he’d call it. A publisher might be convinced to see value in that but that suggested to Lucius that anyone who would publish Hermione wouldn’t do it because they shared her integrity. She was unlikely to get along with a publisher like that.
卢修斯愤怒地咕哝着，用拳头揉搓着库姆的信，漫无目的地把它扔在桌子上。它飞过赫敏被遗弃的拒绝，落在地板上。库尔普是个粗鲁的人。但他有一点——人们天生好奇。爱管闲事，他会这么称呼。出版商可能会被说服看到其中的价值，但这向卢修斯表明，任何想要出版赫敏的人都不会这样做，因为他们和她一样正直。她不太可能与这样的出版商相处。

A knock at the door jerked Lucius out of his reverie and he sat up straighter as it creaked open, a shaft of light from the brightly lit hallway leaking into the room. Draco’s head poked through the gap in the door and he blinked at the relative darkness of the study. “Father?”
一阵敲门声将卢修斯从遐想中拉了出来，当门吱吱作响时，他坐直了身子，一束光从灯火通明的走廊射进了房间。德拉科的头从门的缝隙里探了出来，他对着相对黑暗的书房眨了眨眼。“爸爸？”

“Come in, Draco.”
“进来吧，Draco。”

Draco pushed the door open fully and stepped into the room properly. “Are you…sulking?” he asked, withdrawing his wand from his pocket to point it over the sofa at the fire. 
德拉科把门完全推开，稳稳地走进了房间。“你是......生闷气吗？“他问道，从口袋里掏出魔杖，对准沙发上的火堆。

The low-burning embers burst into writhing flames that lit up the room more fully and Lucius squinted instinctively. “No,” he grumbled, rubbing his eyes with his forefinger and thumb. “I was brooding. Obviously.”
低矮燃烧的余烬迸发出扭动的火焰，将房间更加充分地照亮，卢修斯本能地眯起了眼睛。“不，”他抱怨道，用食指和拇指揉了揉眼睛。“我在沉思。显然。

“Obviously,” Draco repeated dryly, approaching his desk. It was only when Draco was standing across from him that Lucius noticed he was holding a plate. 
“显然，”德拉科干巴巴地重复道，走向他的桌子。直到德拉科站在他对面时，卢修斯才注意到他手里拿着一个盘子。

“You missed dinner,” Draco explained, setting the plate down, followed by some cutlery. Lucius blinked down at the plain fare of meat and potatoes that his son had placed in front of him and then over to the grandfather clock.
“你错过了晚饭，”德拉科解释道，放下盘子，然后是一些餐具。卢修斯对着儿子放在他面前的普通肉类和土豆眨了眨眼，然后转向了老爷爷钟。

“So I did,” he said quietly. “You couldn’t have had Letty bring it?”
“所以我就这样做了，”他轻声说。“你不能让莱蒂带来它吗？”

“That’d be rather impersonal, don’t you think?” Draco asked with a shrug. 
“那会很没有人情味，你不觉得吗？”德拉科耸耸肩问道。

Lucius raised an eyebrow. “And how else would you be able to pry into the reason for my absence, hm?”
卢修斯扬起眉毛。“那你怎么能打探我不在的原因，嗯？”

“Exactly.” Draco had the grace to give him an abashed smile. “It’s been a while since you missed dinner.”
“没错。”德拉科优雅地给了他一个羞愧的微笑。“你已经有一段时间没有错过晚饭了。”

“You couldn’t have brought the wine too?” Lucius muttered, pulling the plate towards himself. He wasn’t especially hungry and the smell of the meat turned his stomach but he picked up the fork and speared a potato anyway.
“你不能也带酒来吧？”卢修斯喃喃自语着，把盘子拉向自己。他不是特别饿，肉的气味让他胃里一阵，但他还是拿起叉子，用长矛刺了一个土豆。

“I think you’re all set,” Draco said, his voice less inclined towards good humour as he gestured towards the glass of firewhiskey sitting more than half-full by Lucius’ elbow. 
“我想你都准备好了，”德拉科说，他的声音不那么幽默了，他指了指坐在卢修斯胳膊肘边的那杯已经装满了一半多的火威士忌。

As Draco stepped back from the desk, his heel caught the crumpled up ball that was Cuffe’s letter. With a curious glance at his father, Draco bent over to pick it up. He hesitated before opening it but, when Lucius didn’t bother to stop him and instead opted to finally eat the potato he’d been torturing, Draco read what Cuffe had written. Lucius watched with interest as his son’s smooth forehead creased with surprise and then collapsed into outrage. 
当Draco从桌子上退后时，他的脚后跟碰到了那个皱巴巴的球，那是Cuffe的信。德拉科好奇地看了他父亲一眼，弯下腰把它捡起来。他在打开门前犹豫了一下，但是，当卢修斯懒得阻止他，而是选择最终吃掉他一直在折磨的土豆时，德拉科读了库姆写的东西。卢修斯饶有兴趣地看着儿子光滑的额头因惊讶而皱起，然后愤怒地瘫倒在地。

Draco looked up sharply, the letter held tightly. “Cuffe dares to suggest that you’re going to be an issue for G–”
德拉科猛地抬起头，紧紧地握着那封信。“Cuffe敢说你会成为G的麻烦——”

Still chewing, Lucius held up a finger to call for pause and nodded once towards the rejection on the desk, drawing Draco’s attention to it. Abandoning Cuffe’s letter, Draco flattened the rejection letter under his hand to read it, sinking into the chair in front of the desk as he did so. When he had finished reading, Draco looked up at his father from under his brow.
卢修斯仍然在咀嚼，他举起一根手指要求暂停，然后朝桌子上的拒绝点了点头，引起了德拉科的注意。Draco放弃了Cuffe的信，将拒绝信压平在手下阅读，一边读一边瘫坐在桌子前面的椅子上。读完后，德拉科从眉毛下抬头看向他的父亲。

“Ridiculous,” he said faintly. 
“荒谬，”他淡淡地说。

Setting his fork down with a defeated air, Lucius pushed his mostly-full plate to the side. “You sound rather like Hermione.”
卢修斯带着挫败的气息放下叉子，将他几乎装满的盘子推到一边。“你听起来挺像赫敏的。”

“Well, she’s right.”
“嗯，她说得对。”

“No, she is not,” Lucius said patiently. “She is upset. As are you. But this is not ridiculous; it is to be expected.”
“不，她不是，”卢修斯耐心地说。“她很不高兴。你也是。但这并不荒谬;这是意料之中的。

“What’s she going to do?” Draco asked, because naturally his son knew she was going to do something.
“她要做什么？”德拉科问道，因为他的儿子自然知道她要做什么。

“She is going to fight tooth and nail against every publisher in the wizarding world until she alienates everyone and leaves herself with no options,” Lucius said, tiredly reclining in his seat, his elbow leaning on its arm. “That is what she is going to do.”
“她要与魔法世界的每一个出版商拼尽全力，直到她疏远了所有人，让自己别无选择，”卢修斯说，疲惫地斜靠在座位上，手肘靠在它的手臂上。“这就是她要做的。”

“You don’t sound very happy about that.”
“你听起来不太高兴。”

“I am far from it.”
“我离它很远。”

Draco frowned, shaking his head. “What, you think she should just drop you? That’s not Granger.”
德拉科皱着眉头，摇了摇头。“什么，你觉得她应该丢下你？那不是格兰杰。

“I’m discovering that.”
“我发现了这一点。”

Eyeing his father, Draco added, “It’s not very you either. If she drops you, her deal with Shacklebolt – your agreement with her –”
看着他的父亲，德拉科补充道，“你也不是很。如果她抛弃了你，她和沙克尔博尔的交易——你和她的协议——”

“Won’t matter if the book never sees the light of day anyway,” Lucius said sharply. "The Wizengamot doesn't set much store by incomplete actions and broken promises."
“反正这本书永远不会见天日也没关系，”卢修斯尖锐地说。“威森加摩并不重视不完整的行动和违背的承诺。”

Following Lucius’ example, Draco fell back in his seat and anchored his elbows on the arms of it. He eyed his father and raised a hand, running the edge of his forefinger along his lips. “Then what are you going to do about it?"
以卢修斯为榜样，德拉科坐回座位上，用手肘固定在椅子的扶手上。他看着他的父亲，抬起一只手，食指的边缘滑过他的嘴唇。“那你打算怎么做？”

“I’m going to ask for your help.” 
“我要请你帮忙。”

Draco’s eyebrows jumped up his forehead and he removed his forefinger from his lip to point it directly at his own face. “My help?” 
德拉科的眉毛跳上了额头，他把食指从嘴唇上移开，直接指向了自己的脸。“我的帮助？”

“Cuffe’s letter was irritating but it suggested that she’s not entirely without hope.” At Lucius’ words, Draco picked the letter up again and skim-read it, his eyes flicking up over the edge of the parchment to fix meet Lucius' with a serious look.
“库姆的信令人恼火，但它表明她并非完全没有希望。”听到卢修斯的话，德拉科又拿起那封信，略读了一遍，他的眼睛在羊皮纸的边缘上瞥了一眼，以严肃的眼神与卢修斯对视。

“I’m not sure I like his reasoning. Using people’s hatred of you to induce them to read Granger’s book doesn’t sound like a good approach at all. For you or her.”
“我不确定我是否喜欢他的理由。利用人们对你的仇恨来诱使他们阅读格兰杰的书，这听起来根本不是一个好方法。为了你或她。

Lucius nodded his agreement and reached for his firewhiskey. “No, but he’s right that I don’t speak out often and that people are naturally curious. If she finds the right person…” Taking a long drink, Lucius mulled over his next steps and when he lowered his glass he found his son’s attention was still on him. “Hermione is more…persuasive in person than she is by letter.”
卢修斯点头表示同意，然后伸手去拿他的火威士忌。“不，但他是对的，我不经常说出来，而且人们天生就很好奇。如果她找到合适的人......”卢修斯喝了一大口酒，思考着下一步该怎么做，当他放下酒杯时，他发现儿子的注意力仍然在他身上。“赫敏更......当面比她写信更有说服力。

Draco’s head tipped to the side in a way that indicated agreement laced with doubt. “Less easily stopped, I’d say. You can’t fold her up and put her in a drawer when she’s standing ranting in front of you.”
德拉科的头歪向一边，似乎同意并带有怀疑。“我想说，不太容易停下来。当她站在你面前咆哮时，你不能把她折叠起来放在抽屉里。

“Precisely,” Lucius said with a small smile. “I need to head her off before she begins firing out abrasive letters to every contact she’s ever had the fortune to make. She needs to have some in-person meetings if she’s ever going to make any headway.”
“正是，”卢修斯微微一笑。“我需要在她开始向她有幸接触的每一个联系人发出粗暴的信件之前阻止她。如果她要取得任何进展，她需要举行一些面对面的会议。

Draco was quiet for a moment, watching as his father took a long drink. “How?”
德拉科沉默了一会儿，看着他的父亲喝了一大口酒。“怎么做到的？”

“We’ll have an event for her,” Lucius replied, setting his glass back down. “Here.” Draco opened his mouth to interrupt but Lucius pressed on. “People are naturally curious, as I said. Even the publishers who have rejected her are unlikely to turn down a chance to have a peek inside Malfoy Manor.”
“我们会为她举办一场活动，”卢修斯回答道，同时放下了他的酒杯。“给你。”德拉科张开嘴想要打断，但卢修斯继续说下去。“正如我所说，人们天生就好奇。即使是那些拒绝了她的出版商，也不太可能拒绝窥探马尔福庄园的机会。

“But–”
“但是——”

“I won’t be attendance, of course, but I’m sure we can have a word with Potter and arrange for the ballroom to be isolated by the Aurors for public use. He’ll have to be here anyway.”
“我当然不会出席，但我相信我们可以和波特谈谈，安排傲罗把舞厅隔离起来供公众使用。无论如何他都必须在这里。

“Potter?” Draco asked, his voice rising with surprise.
“波特？”德拉科问道，他的声音因惊讶而提高。

“Yes. He’s one of her interviewees. Invite them, her friends. And the publishers. I’ll leave those letters to you, I think, given –” Lucius broke off to gesture at the rejection with a dismissive twirl of his fingers. “With all of these people together I think she might stand a chance of persuading someone .”
“是的。他是她的受访者之一。邀请他们，她的朋友们。还有出版商。我想，我会把那些信留给你的——“卢修斯打断了他，用轻蔑的手指旋转着，示意他拒绝了。“有这么多人在一起，我认为她可能有机会说服某人。”

Squinting his eyes like he wasn’t entirely sure he was seeing his father properly, Draco asked, “What exactly will this event involve?”
德拉科眯起眼睛，仿佛不完全确定自己是否正确地看待了他的父亲，他问道，“这件事到底会涉及什么？

“Her recordings are all still in the library, yes? And her transcripts?”
“她的录音都还在图书馆里，对吧？她的成绩单呢？

“I –” Draco blinked, shrugging. “I think so, I don’t –”
“我——”德拉科眨了眨眼，耸了耸肩。“我想是的，我不——”

“Good.” Lucius nodded, businesslike. “Bring them to me in the morning. I have an idea but I’ll need you for the magic.” 
“很好。”卢修斯点点头，很公事公办。“早上把它们带到我这里来。我有个主意，但我需要你来施展魔法。

“Father, this is…” Draco seemed to be at a loss for what it was and Lucius was sure he could see his son mentally picking up words and discarding them as insufficient or incorrect. “Does Granger know about this?”
“爸爸，这是......”德拉科似乎对这是什么感到困惑，卢修斯确信他能看到他的儿子在心里拾取单词，然后把它们当作不足或不正确而丢弃。“格兰杰知道这件事吗？”

“No, it’s a very recent idea. I could tell her I suppose but I rather think she’d find the idea of an event dedicated to her a rather unseemly waste of time. I’m sure she’d find a way to avoid it so that she can sit in the library and fire out letters. Hermione favours efficiency and hard work to get things done but I think she would benefit from learning the value of charm.”
“不，这是一个非常新的想法。我想我可以告诉她，但我宁愿认为她会觉得为她举办活动的想法是相当不体面的浪费时间。我敢肯定她会想办法避免这种情况，这样她就可以坐在图书馆里写信了。赫敏喜欢效率和努力工作来完成事情，但我认为她会从学习魅力的价值中受益。

“You’re going to spring this on her?” It was almost amusing to Lucius that Draco sounded frightened by the idea.
“你要对她下手吗？”对卢修斯来说，德拉科听起来被这个主意吓坏了，这几乎是一件好笑的事情。

“Well, she can hardly avoid it then.”
“嗯，那她就几乎无法避免了。”

A mildly alarmed look at Lucius’ audacity passed over Draco’s face. “When exactly do you want to do this?”
对卢修斯的大胆，德拉科的脸上掠过一丝警惕。“你到底想什么时候做这个？”

Pushing out his lower lip thoughtfully, Lucius slowly turned his glass on the table. “Next week would be best, I think.”
卢修斯若有所思地伸出下唇，慢慢地将酒杯放在桌子上。“我认为下周会是最好的。”

“Next week?” Draco’s voice was choked with incredulity as he sat forward. “A week to organise a whole event? To invite people? To get permission from the –”
“下周？”德拉科坐向前方，声音因难以置信而哽咽。“一周时间组织一整场活动？邀请他人？要从 –”

“Draco, please.” Lucius waved a hand as though pushing Draco’s fears aside. “I watched your mother organise events with as little as an afternoon’s notice. It's perfectly possible when you have the funds. Astoria will be more than equipped to assist.”
“Draco，拜托了。”卢修斯挥了挥手，仿佛将德拉科的恐惧推到一边。“我看着妈组织活动，只用了一个下午的通知。当你有资金时，这是完全可能的。Astoria 将完全有能力提供帮助。

“She’s eight months pregnant.”
“她已经怀孕八个月了。”

“Then I’m sure she will relish a distraction.”
“那我敢肯定她会喜欢分散注意力的。”

Scoffing, Draco dropped back in his seat and glared at his father who simply smiled blandly back. “This is a lot of effort for someone that’s probably going to curse us for going to it.”
德拉科嗤之以鼻，坐回座位上，瞪着他的父亲，而父亲只是淡淡地回以微笑。“对于一个可能会诅咒我们去做的人来说，这是很大的努力。”

“I’m sure she will thank us when it helps her to get what she wants.”
“我相信当它帮助她得到她想要的东西时，她会感谢我们。”

There was a pause in which Lucius took another drink and as he set the glass down, Draco asked, “Why do you care ? Why do you care if she gets what she wants?”
停顿了一会儿，卢修斯又喝了一口，当他放下杯子时，德拉科问道：“你为什么在乎？你为什么在乎她是否得到她想要的东西呢？

Lucius was quiet as he relinquished his hold on his glass and sat up slightly straighter in his seat. “I never said anything about caring, Draco.”
卢修斯安静地放开了对玻璃杯的控制，在座位上坐得稍微挺直了。“我从来没有说过任何关心的事情，德拉科。”

The sound of a quiet, doubtful laugh in the back of Draco’s throat made Lucius look up. “You didn’t need to,” Draco said, frowning. “You’re exposing yourself to help her and running the risk of her hexing your bollocks off to do it. You don’t do that because you don’t care.”
德拉科的喉咙后部发出一声安静而疑惑的笑声，让卢修斯抬起头来。“你不需要，”德拉科皱着眉头说。“你冒着自己去帮助她，冒着她把你的肮脏弄掉的风险来做这件事。你不这样做是因为你不在乎。

Pressing his lips together, Lucius met Draco’s scrutinising gaze. His son wasn’t stupid. He hadn’t raised him to be. “I won’t get what I want — my magic and my freedom — if she doesn’t get what she wants.”
卢修斯紧紧抿着嘴唇，与德拉科审视的目光相遇。他的儿子并不傻。他没有把他培养成这样。“如果她得不到她想要的，我就得不到我想要的——我的魔法和我的自由。”

It made sense, Lucius thought, but Draco didn’t seem entirely satisfied. Instead his son’s scrutiny only seemed to intensify. “She said you apologised to her,” Draco finally said. 
这很有道理，卢修斯想，但德拉科似乎并不完全满意。相反，他儿子的审视似乎越来越严厉。“她说你向她道歉了，”德拉科终于说了。

Lucius gazed down at his glass with only a few mouthfuls left in it and decided he was really going to have to have a word with Hermione about what she and Draco discussed when he wasn’t there. “Yes.”
卢修斯低头看着他的杯子，杯子里只剩下几口了，他决定他真的得和赫敏谈谈他不在的时候她和德拉科讨论的事情。“是的。”

“She said she believed you were sincere.” 
“她说她相信你是真诚的。”

Lucius looked up at his son from beneath his brows. “I was.”
卢修斯从眉毛下抬头看着他的儿子。“我是。”

Draco’s nod was barely perceptible, like he had ascertained a previously questionable fact and was satisfied by it. “Did she forgive you?”
德拉科的点头几乎看不见，就像他已经确定了一个之前有问题的事实并对此感到满意。“她原谅你了吗？”

At the memory of his apology, a wry smile crept over Lucius’ face without his permission. It felt like a long time ago given how much had changed. “No. I believe that’s something she would like me to earn.”
想起他的道歉，卢修斯的脸上未经他的允许就悄悄地露出了苦笑。考虑到变化有多大，感觉就像是很久以前的事情了。“不。我相信这是她希望我赚到的。

There was a pause in which Draco studied his father’s smile and then he asked, “And you intend to try?”
德拉科停顿了一下，端详着他父亲的笑容，然后他问道，“你打算试试吗？

Lucius sighed and pressed his back into his chair, raising his head to look his son fully in his face. This conversation wasn’t ending and there was little he could do but attempt to see it through with his head held high. “It may take some time. But yes. Perhaps helping her with this event will help.”
卢修斯叹了口气，把背靠在椅子上，抬起头，全神贯注地看着儿子的脸。这次谈话并没有结束，他也无能为力，只能昂首挺胸地尝试完成它。“这可能需要一些时间。但是是的。也许帮助她参加这次活动会有所帮助。

“Father,” Draco began slowly. “What – just how exactly –” Draco exhaled sharply through his nose and took the dive. “What is Granger to you?”
“爸爸，”德拉科缓缓地开口。“什么——到底是怎么——”德拉科从鼻子里猛地呼出一口气，然后俯冲起来。“格兰杰对你来说是什么？”

After that question, even the dinner plate felt like an oppressive presence in the room and Lucius found himself pushing it closer to the edge of his desk as though to put it out of earshot. Swallowing, he clasped his hands in front of himself and leaned forward towards his son. “If I knew that with any certainty Draco, I assure you I would tell you.”
在这个问题之后，就连餐盘在房间里也感觉像是一种压迫感，Lucius 发现自己把它推得更靠近桌子的边缘，仿佛要把它放在听不见的地方。他咽了口口水，双手紧握在身前，身体前倾，朝着儿子。“如果我知道的话，德拉科，我向你保证，我会告诉你的。”

Eyes widening, Draco said, “I don’t need certainty. I just want to know what…give me an approximation.”
Draco睁大了眼睛，说，“我不需要确定性。我只是想知道什么......给我一个近似值。

Give an approximation of his feelings for Granger. Now there was a challenge he hadn’t anticipated facing any time soon. “She is…” Lucius tilted his head, lowering his eyes to his clasped hands. “More to me than I ever thought she would be.” His gaze rose swiftly and pinned his shell-shocked son with a severe look. “And far less to me than you.” 
请大致描述他对格兰杰的感情。现在，他没有预料到很快就会面临一个挑战。“她是......”卢修斯歪着头，低头看着他紧握的双手。“对我来说，她会比我想象的要多。”他的目光迅速抬起，用严厉的眼神注视着他震惊不醒的儿子。“而且对我来说远不如你。”

“Does she know ?” Draco’s voice was choked, breathless.
“她知道吗？”德拉科的声音哽咽着，喘不过气来。

Lucius flexed his fingers against one another and lifted a shoulder. “I’ve given her reason to suspect as much.”
卢修斯用手指相互弯曲，抬起了一个肩膀。“我已经给了她同样怀疑的理由。”

“And does she –”
“她——”

“I don’t think she’s displeased by it.”
“我不认为她对此感到不满。”

“Merlin,” Draco said on an exhale. Raising a hand to cup it over his mouth, he curled his body forward so that his elbows came to rest on his knees. Folding his fingers into a fist at his chin to reveal his lips, Draco looked up at Lucius from across the desk. “Merlin's fucking –” He blinked, squeezing his eyes tight like he thought it might wake him up from a dream. “Father. When were you going to tell me?”
“梅林，”德拉科呼出一口气说。他抬起一只手捂住嘴巴，身体向前蜷缩，使他的肘部停在膝盖上。德拉科将手指握成拳头，露出嘴唇，从桌子对面抬头看着卢修斯。“梅林他妈的——”他眨了眨眼，紧紧地眯着眼睛，仿佛他觉得这会把他从梦中惊醒。“爸爸。你打算什么时候告诉我？

In response to Draco’s physical cringe, Lucius felt himself instinctively sit up straighter, his pride not allowing him to be ashamed. “When I had a better understanding of what it was,” he said, a slight defensiveness to his tone as he attempted to reassert his position as the father in the room. “When it became any of your business, Draco.” 
作为对德拉科身体畏缩的回应，卢修斯感觉到自己本能地坐直了，他的骄傲不允许他感到羞耻。“当我对那是什么有了更好的理解时，”他说，当他试图重申他作为房间里父亲的地位时，他的语气中带着一丝防御。“当它变成你的事的时候，德拉科。”

“I just don’t understand when – how –” Still curled over towards his knees, Draco lowered his head and covered his face with his hands.
“我就是不明白什么时候——怎么——”德拉科仍然蜷缩着膝盖，低下头，用手捂住脸。

“We have spent months in one another’s company.”
“我们在彼此的陪伴下度过了几个月。”

“Well, yeah.” Draco’s voice was faint and muffled. “But I didn’t think – the way it started –” He looked up through his fingers at his father, torn. “You’ve been…different lately.” 
“嗯，是的。”德拉科的声音微弱而低沉。“但我没想——事情是这样开始的——”他透过手指抬头看着他的父亲，心里很伤心。“你一直......最近不同了。

“I hadn’t noticed,” was Lucius’ stiff response. 
“我没注意到，”卢修斯僵硬地回答。

“I have.” Draco lowered his hands so that his arms were crossed over his knees. “And she's been here a lot more. It just never occurred to me that –” Suddenly, Draco sat up and dropped back in his chair, his hands coming up to clutch at his hair. “Oh, fuck, a glow —"
“我有。”德拉科放下双手，双臂交叉在膝盖上。“她在这里的时间更长。我从来没有想过——“突然，Draco坐了起来，坐回了椅子上，他的手伸过来抓着他的头发。“哦，操，一阵光芒——”

"A glow?"
“发光？”

"Weasley said she has a glow. Have you –”
“韦斯莱说她有光泽。 你——”

“ Weasley ?” Lucius asked sharply. “What have you been –”
“韦斯莱？”卢修斯尖锐地问道。“你最近怎么了——”

Draco pointed an accusing finger at him. “What have you been –”
德拉科用指责的手指指着他。“你最近怎么了——”

“Draco.”
“德拉科。”

Lunging out of his seat across the table, Draco snatched up Lucius’ firewhiskey and downed the last of it as he dropped back into a sitting position. “I don’t want to know,” he said, staring into the empty glass with a haunted expression, his hair messy and flopping over his forehead. “No, I don’t want to know. I can’t know. I never wish to know.”
德拉科从桌子对面的座位上冲了出来，一把抢过卢修斯的火威士忌，喝掉了最后一瓶，然后他又坐了回去。“我不想知道，”他说，一脸懊恼地盯着空杯子，头发凌乱，垂在额头上。“不，我不想知道。我不知道。我从来不想知道。

“Draco –”
“德拉科——”

“Bloody hell,” Draco continued, ignoring him. “I want to be angry at you. Both of you. I want to tell you to just…not but you have been different.” Their eyes met again and Lucius saw that Draco’s expression was almost desperate. “You’ve been…happier. Have you been happier?”
“的，”德拉科继续说，无视他。“我想对你生气。你们俩。我想告诉你只是......不是，但你一直不同。他们的目光再次相遇，卢修斯看到德拉科的表情几乎是绝望的。“你一直......快乐。你更快乐了吗？

Lucius pondered. “I’ve been diverted.” Draco choked and looked at the empty glass as though willing it to refill. “I never thought about it in terms of happiness.” 
卢修斯沉思着。“我被转移了。”德拉科哽咽着看着空杯子，仿佛希望它能重新装满。“我从来没有想过幸福。”

Happiness wasn’t really a singular feeling to his mind – it was a collage of feelings and circumstances. It was comfort, security, connection, a sense of achievement. Lucius considered the previous months – the times he had made Hermione laugh, his openness with her and Draco, the general contentment that seemed to permeate his recent days. He didn’t feel like he was missing much. 
在他的心中，幸福并不是一种真正的单一感觉——它是情感和环境的拼贴。这是舒适、安全、联系、成就感。卢修斯回想着之前的几个月——他逗赫敏笑的时候，他对她和德拉科的坦诚，以及似乎弥漫在他最近几天的普遍满足感。他并不觉得自己缺少什么。

“Perhaps I am.” He fixed Draco with a serious look and took in a slow, deep breath through his nose. “Your happiness means more to me Draco.” He hoped that put across what he meant; what he would sacrifice for his son now after so many years of not sacrificing enough. 
“也许我是。”他用严肃的眼神盯着德拉科，然后用鼻子缓缓地深吸了一口气。“你的快乐对我来说更有意义，德拉科。”他希望这能说明他的意思;在这么多年没有做出足够牺牲之后，他现在会为他的儿子牺牲什么。

A sad, huffing laugh made Draco’s shoulders jump up. He shook his head. “I don’t think I’d ever be happy if I knew I was standing in the way of yours. That’s not what I want. I just…did it have to be Granger?”
一阵悲伤的、喘息的笑声让德拉科的肩膀跳了起来。他摇摇头。“如果我知道我挡住了你的路，我想我永远不会高兴。那不是我想要的。我只是。。。一定是格兰杰吗？

“I have asked myself that multiple times,” Lucius said dryly.
“我已经问过自己好好几次了，”卢修斯干巴巴地说。

Draco scoffed. “I can only assume she appreciates your sense of romance – no, I can’t. I thought I could joke about it but I can’t.” Draco set the empty glass on the desk with a heavy clunk and stared at it for a moment. “I’ll just…we’ll talk in the morning,” he said, pushing himself to his feet and looking down at Lucius. “I’ll bring those Wheezebox things from the library and we’ll just…yeah. We can talk about it then.”
德拉科嗤之以鼻。“我只能假设她欣赏你的浪漫感——不，我不能。我以为我可以开玩笑，但我不能。德拉科把空杯子放在桌子上，发出沉重的哐当声，盯着它看了一会儿。“我就......我们早上再谈，“他说，站起身来，低头看着卢修斯。“我会从图书馆带来那些 Wheezebox 的东西，然后我们就......是的。那我们就可以谈谈了。

“Draco –” Lucius said as his son turned away.
“德拉科——”卢修斯说，他的儿子转过身去。

Turning back, Draco raised a hand to stop his father. “Just let me –” He sighed and dragged a hand through his hair to push the loose strands back from his forehead. “You know you spent most of your life and pretty much all of mine calling people like her Mudbloods behind closed doors, right? Not to mention everything else. You understand why this is so surprising to me?”
德拉科转过身来，举起一只手阻止了他的父亲。“就让我——”他叹了口气，用一只手拽过他的头发，把散乱的发丝从额头上推开。“你知道你一生中的大部分时间，几乎都是在闭门造车地打电话给像她这样的泥巴种人，对吧？更不用说其他一切了。你明白为什么我这么惊讶吗？

“Did you not tell me yourself that she’s not what that word means?” 
“你不是自己告诉我，她不是那个词的意思吗？”

“I did but –”
“我记得，但是——”

“And did you not say that you hoped that she would help me to see that the world would not necessarily be better without Muggleborns?”
“你不是说过，你希望她能帮我看到，没有麻瓜出身的人，世界不一定会变得更好吗？”

“Well, I did –”
“嗯，我做到了——”

“Then perhaps take a moment to savour your success.”
“那么，也许花点时间细细品味你的成功。”

“My success,” Draco said faintly, flatly.
“我的成功，”德拉科淡淡而平淡地说。

“This would never have been possible without you, Draco.”
“没有你，这绝对不可能，德拉科。”

Draco scowled. “Are you really going to blame me f–”
德拉科皱起眉头。“你真的要怪我吗——”

“Perhaps I’m thanking you.”
“也许我是在感谢你。”

A surprised laugh bubbled out of Draco but it sounded almost pained. “Father, I know being locked up in the Manor has perhaps made it easy to forget but there’s a world out there beyond you, me and Granger and –”
德拉科发出一阵惊讶的笑声，但听起来几乎是痛苦的。“爸爸，我知道被关在庄园里可能很容易让人忘记，但在你之外还有一个世界，我和格兰杰，还有——”

“I am very aware of the world out there, Draco,” Lucius said coldly, gesturing to the crumpled collection of parchment littering his desk. “I had a run in with it only today.”
“我非常了解外面的世界，德拉科，”卢修斯冷冷地说，指着散落在他桌上的皱巴巴的羊皮纸。“我今天才遇到了它。”

Draco cringed. “I just mean…Granger’s friends. Weasley especially – the girl one. I’m not sure they’re ever likely to accept whatever –”
德拉科畏缩了。“我只是说......格兰杰的朋友们。尤其是韦斯莱——那个女孩。我不确定他们是否可能接受任何东西——”

“They are not to know anything," Lucius said sternly. "And if they ever do find out..." He shrugged. "I don’t care what they think.”
“他们什么都不知道，”卢修斯严肃地说。“如果他们真的发现了......”他耸耸肩。“我不在乎他们怎么想。”

Draco looked almost sad, like Lucius had said something particularly disappointing. “She might. She cares about a lot of things, including them. I’ve seen that more than you. Just…bear that in mind, okay?”
德拉科看起来几乎是伤心的，就像卢修斯说了什么特别令人失望的话。“她可能会。她关心很多事情，包括它们。我比你见过得更多。只。。。记住这一点，好吗？

Without another word, Draco turned and left the study. Lucius sat in the silence for a time, staring at his empty firewhiskey glass. Then, with a heavy sigh, he got to his feet, swiped it from the desk and crossed the room to refill it.
德拉科一言不发，转身离开了书房。卢修斯在寂静中坐了一会儿，盯着他空的火威士忌杯。然后，他重重地叹了口气，站起来，从桌子上刷了一下，穿过房间重新装满了它。

Chapter End Notes
章节结束注释

So Draco finally knows! And he and Lucius still have a little more to discuss. Writing Draco's reaction was always going to be tough. In my previous story he was really angry but that didn't feel like the right approach for this Draco. He's been so exhausted by his father's withdrawal and so pleased by his recent opening up that I think he would have to see some of the benefits of his closeness with Hermione, even if he can't really understand it and doesn't wholly approve of it. I hope you all enjoyed and thank you so much for still being on this journey :D
所以 Draco 终于知道了！他和 Lucius 还有更多的事情要讨论。写 Draco 的反应总是很艰难的。在我之前的故事中，他真的很生气，但那感觉不像是这个 Draco 的正确方法。他父亲的退缩让他筋疲力尽，又因为他最近的敞开心扉而感到高兴，我想他必须看到他和赫敏亲密的一些好处，即使他不能真正理解，也不完全赞成。我希望你们都喜欢并非常感谢你们仍然在这段旅程中:D

注释见本章末尾August 1st 
8 月 1 日

Draco lazily flicked his wand and sent a box filled with Wheezeboxes sliding onto his father’s desk. “Here,” he said, tucking his wand away. “All of her interviews. Labelled, of course – we’re talking about Granger here.”
德拉科懒洋洋地弹了弹魔杖，把一个装满喘息盒的盒子滑到了他爸爸的桌子上。“给你，”他说，把魔杖收起来。“她所有的采访。当然是有标签的——我们在这里谈论的是格兰杰。

Eyeing the mound of devices, Lucius nodded with satisfaction. “Good,” he said, setting his hand on top of another box. “I have the transcripts here.” He didn't mention, though he eyed the space in the air where Draco's wand had just been, that he'd been forced to carry them. 
看着那堆设备，卢修斯满意地点了点头。“很好，”他说，把手放在另一个盒子上。“我这里有文字记录。”他没有提到，尽管他盯着Draco的魔杖刚才所在的空中空间，他是被迫携带它们的。

“Is this really a good idea?” Draco asked with a small frown. “I can’t see her being too happy with us riffling through her things if she comes by to work.”
“这真的是个好主意吗？”德拉科皱着眉头问道。“如果她来上班，我看不出她会对我们吵闹她的东西太高兴。”

“Oh, I can’t see her coming by,” Lucius said lightly, picking up a sheaf of parchment to peruse it. “Not this morning, at least.”
“哦，我看不见她走过来，”卢修斯淡淡地说，拿起一捆羊皮纸仔细阅读。“至少今天早上不会。”

Draco’s frown deepened. “Err, why?”
德拉科的眉头皱得更深了。“呃，为什么？”

“She’s quite annoyed at me, I think,” Lucius said, lowering the parchment to look over it at his son with a wry smile. “I imagine she’ll want to cool off.”
“我想她对我很生气，”卢修斯说，放下羊皮纸，苦笑着看着他的儿子。“我想她会想冷静下来。”

“Do I want to know?”
“我想知道吗？”

“It’s nothing lascivious, I assure you.” Lucius didn’t miss Draco’s cringe and snorted softly to himself. “She’s just annoyed that I tried to withdraw my interview. And that I told her she was wrong.” He placed the transcript neatly back in the box and tilted his head thoughtfully before adding, “There’s a good chance that she’s annoyed by the general tone I used too.”
“我向你保证，这没什么的。”卢修斯没有错过德拉科的畏缩，轻声哼了一声。“她只是对我试图撤回采访感到恼火。我告诉她她错了。他把笔录整齐地放回盒子里，若有所思地歪着头，然后补充道，“她很有可能也对我用的那种一般语气感到恼火。

Draco blinked and shook his head with a bewildered air. “Rather you than me. So what are we doing with these?” he asked, waving a hand over the box of Wheezeboxes. 
德拉科眨了眨眼，带着困惑的神情摇了摇头。“宁愿你，也不愿我。那么我们要用这些做什么呢？“他问道，一边在一盒 Wheezebox 上挥了挥手。

Lucius tapped the box of transcripts. “Each interviewee has a dedicated recording device and a matching transcript. I want to find the most interesting sections of their conversations and charm the devices to play them on a loop.” Lifting a transcript up, he held it out so Draco could take it. “You’ll notice that Hermione has already done most of the work for us by underlining the pertinent sections of her interviews – I suggest that we make use of the best of them.” 
卢修斯敲了敲那盒文字记录。“每个受访者都有一个专用的录音设备和一份匹配的文字记录。我想找到他们对话中最有趣的部分，并吸引设备循环播放它们。他拿起一份成绩单，把它拿出来，让Draco可以拿走。“你会注意到赫敏已经为我们完成了大部分工作，强调了她采访的相关部分——我建议我们利用它们中最好的。”

“And what will you do with them?”
“那你打算怎么处理他们？”

“If we disperse them around the ballroom, with the application of some sound containment charms we should be able to create listening stations for people to hear her work. I think it could have a striking effect.”
“如果我们把它们分散在宴会厅周围，应用一些隔音咒，我们应该能够创建倾听站，让人们听到她的作品。我认为它可能会产生惊人的影响。

“It just might,” Draco said thoughtfully, flipping over a sheet of parchment to continue reading the interview. 
“也许吧，”德拉科若有所思地说，翻开一张羊皮纸继续阅读采访。

“Have you started sending the letters?”
“你开始寄信了吗？”

“I’ve started with Potter,” Draco said, looking up from the parchment and appearing suddenly quite tired. “I didn’t see the point in doing anything if the Aurors weren’t going to give us permission to use the manor.”
“我从波特开始，”德拉科说，从羊皮纸上抬起头来，突然显得相当疲惫。“如果傲罗们不同意我们使用庄园，我就看不出做任何事情的意义。”

“He’s responded?”
“他回应了吗？”

“Within an hour, incredibly,” Draco said. “To say he was surprised to hear from me would be an understatement. But he said he would help to make it happen. As long as you’re keeping to your house arrest, he doesn’t see why the other side of the Manor can’t be temporarily publicly accessible. They’ll station Aurors at the doors.”
“在一个小时内，令人难以置信，”德拉科说。“说他对听到我的消息感到惊讶是轻描淡写的。但他表示，他会帮助实现这一目标。只要你一直被软禁，他就不明白为什么庄园的另一边不能暂时公开进入。他们会在门口派驻傲罗。

Lucius nodded, clearly pleased. “And you asked him not to tell her?”
卢修斯点点头，显然很高兴。“你让他不要告诉她？”

“I thought if I did that then he almost certainly would tell her.” Draco shrugged as he set the transcript down and started lifting Wheezeboxes out of the box to lay them on the desk. “So I didn’t say anything and we’ll just hope he’ll assume that she knows because of that.” 
“我想如果我这样做了，那么他几乎肯定会告诉她。”德拉科耸了耸肩，把成绩单放下，开始从盒子里拿出Wheezebox，把它们放在桌子上。“所以我什么都没说，我们只是希望他会因此假设她知道。”

“Very astute,” Lucius said with an approving nod. 
“非常精明，”卢修斯赞许地点点头说。

Draco looked up, his eyebrows raised, and found his father looking at him with something that came close to pride. He tried to look nonchalant, offering Lucius another shrug but he failed to dampen the smile that trembled at the corners of his mouth.

“Astoria 主动提出处理餐饮和装饰，”Draco 补充道。“事实证明你是对的——她很感激这种干扰。”

“哦，不，”德拉科说，不屑一顾地挥了挥手。“她说她觉得这其实很甜蜜。”

卢修斯的动作结结巴巴地停了下来，他抬头一瞥，发现他的儿子正在对他傻笑。“甜蜜的，”卢修斯平淡地重复道。

“你会的。”

“所以，这是一个'可能'？”

“Draco.”
“德拉科。”

“嗯，你觉得它会持续吗？”还是'当我们都在庄园周围时，我们不妨'之类的事情？

“你说那是她的错吗？”

“她想要什么确实对我们如何前进有一定影响，”卢修斯干巴巴地说，睁开眼睛看到德拉科惊讶地向他眨了眨眼，他明白了其中的含义：如果赫敏这样做，卢修斯会继续前进。

德拉科停顿了一下，打量了一下他的父亲，然后他说，“我不认为格兰杰会是个很好的母亲。

Nostrils flaring, Lucius rolled his eyes. “I thought you were unable to joke about this.”

“那是昨晚的事。但我开始认为，对此一笑置之可能是我唯一的前进道路。

“Just get on with what you’re supposed to be doing,” Lucius said, sharply jabbing a hand towards the Wheezebox before picking up the transcript again.  
“继续你该做的事，”Lucius说，用一只手猛地戳了戳Wheezebox，然后又拿起了笔录。

“说到母亲，”德拉科补充道，他的声音突然失去了轻快。“你想过她吗？在别人知道之前告诉她？

“What I do is no longer any of her business.” Lucius didn’t look up at Draco as he said the words, weighing them down with a cold finality that invited no further discussion. 
“我做什么不再是她的事。”卢修斯说这句话时没有抬头看德拉科，以一种冷酷的结局压制着他们，没有再让人进一步讨论。

A muffled sigh signalled Draco’s admission of defeat but, before he carried on with his task at hand, he glanced over at his father and took in his serious, somewhat pinched expression for a moment. “I’m pleased for you,” Draco finally said quietly. “Trying to be.”
德拉科低沉地叹了口气，表示他承认了失败，但在他继续手头的任务之前，他瞥了一眼他的父亲，并注意到了他严肃的、有点紧绷的表情。“我为你感到高兴，”德拉科终于轻声说。“努力成为。”

Lucius’ eyes flicked over to his son, landing on his face and seeing sincerity there. With a barely audible sigh through his nose, Lucius nodded once. “Thank you, Draco.”
卢修斯的眼睛瞥向他的儿子，落在他的脸上，看到了那里的真诚。卢修斯的鼻子里发出一声几乎听不见的叹息，他点了点头。“谢谢你，德拉科。”

August 2nd
8月2日

“Draco: I didn't know what to do when he was arrested. Mother was crying constantly. Auntie Bella was shouting at her and telling her to stop because I don’t think she knew what to do with tears that she hadn't caused. He hadn't told me what to do if he never came back. I honestly think he never thought it would happen. Maybe he couldn't afford to, I don't know. 
“德拉科：他被捕时我不知道该怎么办。妈妈一直在哭。贝拉阿姨对她大喊大叫，让她停下来，因为我认为她不知道该如何处理不是她造成的眼泪。他没有告诉我，如果他再也没有回来怎么办。老实说，我认为他从未想过会发生这种情况。也许他负担不起，我不知道。

赫敏：你做了什么决定？

Draco：显然很糟糕。他还活着。我想念他。那一年他来得少了，但庄园没有他还是感觉不太对劲。感觉就像我穿上了一件不合身的服装。

Draco：更难。如果他在那儿，这一切就不会发生。你随便你怎么看我就怎么看我那怀疑的眼神吧，格兰杰;他不会让这种情况发生。在他允许我之前，他自己会做的。我知道。

突然间，他对喘息盒完全不感兴趣了，德拉科任由他的魔杖手掉下来，抬起脸看着他的父亲。“真的吗？”

That you would suggest otherwise shows how disconnected from reality you are; how fully you bought into the lie. It goes some way to explaining—to me at least—why you find it so easy to hate.”
