说出马尔福名字的潘西漫不以为然地扫视着这群人，然后点头打招呼，把目光放回德拉科身上。卢娜和潘西手牵手，给了他们一个梦幻般的快乐微笑，而纳威则尴尬地挥了挥手，紧张地瞥了罗恩一眼。

“Pans,” Draco said, a surprised lilt to his voice, “I didn’t expect to see you here. Didn’t you tell me – what was it – you don't do soporifics unless they're Healer prescribed?”
“潘斯，”德拉科说，他的声音里带着惊讶的轻快，“我没想到会在这里见到你。你没告诉我——那是什么——除非是治疗师开的处方，否则你不会做催眠药吗？

Rolling her eyes, Pansy inclined her head towards Luna and said, “I was persuaded.”
潘西翻了个白眼，把头歪向露娜说：“我被说服了。

“I see,” Draco replied, an amused smile playing around his lips. “I don’t recall you ever being very easily persuaded.”
“我明白了，”德拉科回答，嘴角浮现出一个有趣的笑容。“我记得你从来没有被轻易说服过。”

“Well, you were never particularly persuasive , Draco,” Pansy said sniffily. "You just liked to think you were."
“嗯，你从来都不是特别有说服力，德拉科，”潘西轻蔑地说。“你只是喜欢认为你是。”

“Your house is nicer up here,” Luna said to Draco suddenly, tearing her eyes away from the sparkling chandelier, clearly not having listened to Draco and Pansy’s exchange at all. “Much less damp.”
“你家这儿比较好，”卢娜突然对德拉科说，把目光从那盏闪闪发光的吊灯上移开，显然根本没有听德拉科和潘西的交流。“不那么潮湿。”

Everyone in the group visibly stiffened at Luna’s declaration – Draco most especially. Everyone, that is, except for Pansy, whose shoulders shook with repressed laughter. Releasing Luna’s hand, Pansy pointed towards a tray bearing champagne flutes and placed a gentle touch on her lower back. 
小组中的每个人都明显对 Luna 的声明感到僵硬——尤其是 Draco。每个人，除了潘西，她的肩膀因压抑的笑声而颤抖。松开 Luna 的手，Pansy 指向一个盛着香槟杯的托盘，轻轻地抚摸着她的下背部。

“Would you mind getting me one, love? We’ll see if we can find a way to get out of here and look for those Blibbering Humdinger hides after that.”
“你介意给我买一个吗，亲爱的？我们看看能不能找到办法离开这里，然后去找那些喋喋不休的Humdinger的藏身之处。

Luna nodded enthusiastically and with another smile at everyone, slipped away from the group towards the tray Pansy had pointed out. 
露娜热情地点点头，又对大家微笑，从人群中溜走，走向潘西指出的托盘。

“I thought you said you were good at curtailing her less tactful declarations,” Draco said through gritted teeth to Pansy, his eyes shifting uneasily to Hermione, Harry and the Weasleys.
“我还以为你说你很擅长克制她不那么委婉的声明，”德拉科咬牙切齿地对潘西说，他的眼睛不安地转向赫敏、哈利和韦斯莱一家。

“I am,” Pansy said with a shrug. “When I want to. I find that’s rare, though. Besides, you should have seen your face. Hilarious.”
“我是，”潘西耸耸肩说。“我想什么时候。不过，我发现这种情况很少见。此外，你应该看到你的脸。太搞笑了。

Ron snorted as pink spots appeared on Draco’s cheeks. “And don’t you dare try to get out of this room,” Draco said, drawing himself up authoritatively. “There are Aurors stationed at the entrance and I don’t know what a bloody Blibbering Humdinger is but I can assure you that we don’t –”
罗恩哼了一声，德拉科的脸颊上出现了粉红色的斑点。“你还敢试着离开这个房间吗，”德拉科说，威严地站起身来。“入口处有傲罗驻扎着，我不知道什么是的喋喋不休的喋喋不休的傻瓜，但我可以向你保证，我们没有——”

“So Malfoy took it on himself to organise all of this?” Ginny murmured to Harry under cover of Draco and Pansy’s argument becoming more heated. “And he said he didn’t have a thing for her.”
“所以马尔福自己承担了组织这一切的责任？”金妮在德拉科的掩护下对哈利喃喃自语，潘西的争论变得更加激烈。“他说他对她没有好感。”

“I don’t think he does, Gin, he just –”
“我不认为他知道，Gin，他只是——”

“Oh, just let her have a look , Draco,” came Pansy’s cajoling voice.
“哦，让她看看吧，德拉科，”潘西哄骗的声音传来。

“No!” Draco snapped. “I have an arrangement with the Department of Magical Law Enforcement and the last thing –”
“不！”德拉科厉声说。“我和魔法执法部有个安排，最后一件事——”

“Oh please, Harry,” Ginny scoffed quietly and waved a hand. “Look at this place. This has come from the mind of someone who either wants to get in, or stay in, Hermione Granger’s knickers.”
“哦，拜托了，哈利，”金妮轻声嘲笑着，挥了挥手。“看看这个地方。这句话出自一个想进或想留在赫敏·格兰杰的短裤里的人的想法。

Harry’s face visibly paled as Ginny pulled a now-quiet but flushed Draco’s attention from Pansy by jutting her chin at him. “So, if Hermione didn’t know about all this,” Ginny said, raising her voice slightly to bring her and Harry back into the group’s conversation, “does that mean it was all your work then, Malfoy?” 
哈利的脸色明显苍白，金妮把现在安静但又冲昏了头脑的德拉科的注意力从潘西身上伸出来。“所以，如果赫敏不知道这一切，”金妮说，稍微提高了声音，让她和哈利回到了小组的谈话中，“那是不是意味着那都是你的工作，马尔福？

Malfoy frowned at Ginny’s smug face as she lifted her champagne flute to her lips. “No,” he said. “It was mostly my father.”
马尔福对着金妮得意的脸皱起眉头，她把香槟酒杯举到嘴边。“不，”他说。“主要是我爸爸。”

If at all possible, Harry’s face went even more pale and Ginny choked on her champagne. Malfoy watched, distaste written over his face, as Ginny coughed while Harry patted her back, giving everyone in the perplexed group an apologetic grimace. 
如果可能的话，哈利的脸色会更加苍白，金妮被香槟呛住了。马尔福看着金妮咳嗽，哈利拍着她的背，让困惑的人群中的每一个人都做了一个抱歉的鬼脸。

“Must have went down the wrong way,” he said with false joviality over the sound of his wife’s spluttering. 
“一定是走错了路，”他对妻子的啪啪声带着假装的欢快说。

Rolling her eyes with disgust, Pansy swept her dark hair over her shoulder and stepped away from the group in the direction of Luna, who was re-approaching with a glass of champagne for her. Hermione watched Pansy place an uncharacteristically warm kiss of thanks on Luna’s lips as she accepted the glass before turning back towards the group. 
潘西厌恶地翻了个白眼，把她的黑发拂过肩膀，离开了人群，朝着露娜的方向走去，露娜正拿着一杯香槟重新走过来。赫敏看着潘西在卢娜的嘴唇上一个异常温暖的感谢之吻，她接过杯子，然后转身走向这群人。

Draco watched Pansy and Luna over Hermione’s head, his eyes narrowed with suspicion. It was abundantly clear he would be surveilling them for the rest of the night. Neville, meanwhile, had turned to Ron with a nervous expression. 
德拉科看着潘西和卢娜越过赫敏的头顶，怀疑地眯起了眼睛。很明显，他会在剩下的晚上监视他们。与此同时，纳威转向罗恩，露出紧张的表情。

“So, er…how you doing, Ron?”
“所以，呃......你好吗，罗恩？

Hermione watched on with exasperation as, shoving his hands in his pockets, Ron barely managed to spare Neville a glance as he grunted and shrugged out a reply that said very little about how he was at all. 
赫敏恼怒地看着罗恩双手插在口袋里，勉强瞥了纳威一眼，他咕哝着耸了耸肩，回答得一点也不清楚。

Just about recovered from her coughing fit, Ginny cast her taciturn brother a disgusted look and moved away from Harry to take Neville by the elbow. 
刚从咳嗽中恢复过来，金妮厌恶地看了她沉默寡言的弟弟一眼，然后离开哈利，抓住纳威的胳膊肘。

“Come on, Neville,” she said, her voice still slightly hoarse. “I don’t think I’ve seen your Wheezebox yet, would you mind showing me it?”
“来吧，纳威，”她说，她的声音仍然略微沙哑。“我想我还没见过你的 Wheezebox，你介意给我看一下吗？”

Draco, who hadn’t taken his eyes from Pansy and Luna for a second, placed a gentle hand on Hermione’s arm. “Excuse me for a moment, Granger,” he said, his eyes dropping briefly to hers. “Talk to some bloody publishers, will you? It’s the entire point.”
德拉科的眼睛一秒钟都没有从潘西和卢娜身上移开，他温柔地把手放在赫敏的手臂上。“对不起，格兰杰，”他说，他的眼睛短暂地落在她的身上。“和一些的出版商谈谈，好吗？这就是重点。

Before Hermione could say a word, Draco had slipped away towards the space in the room from which Luna and Pansy had just managed to vanish without a trace. Huffing out a sigh, Hermione turned back to Harry and Ron and shrugged at them.
赫敏还没来得及说一句话，德拉科就溜向了房间里那个空间，卢娜和潘西刚刚从那里消失得无影无踪。赫敏叹了口气，转身看向哈利和罗恩，对他们耸了耸肩。

“Just the three of us,” she said. Then, turning to Ron, added, “And while it is just the three of us: be nice to Neville.”
“就我们三个人，”她说。然后，转向罗恩，补充道，“趁着只有我们三个人的时候，对纳威好一点。

“Why should I?” Ron asked, crossing his arms as his brow dropped into a low frown. 
“我为什么要呢？”罗恩问道，交叉着双臂，眉头低垂。

“Because he’s your friend,” Hermione said. “And has been for a long time.”
“因为他是你的朋友，”赫敏说。“而且已经有很长一段时间了。”

Ron glanced at Harry who, to Hermione's surprise, nodded in agreement. “We’re too old for this, mate. He’s not really done anything wrong.”
罗恩看了哈利一眼，让赫敏惊讶的是，哈利点头表示同意。“我们太老了，伙计。他真的没有做错任何事情。

As Ron looked back and forth between Harry and Hermione, Hermione thought she saw something soften in his expression. Before she could say anything else, however, he grumbled something about finding more haggis bon bons and stalked off in the direction of the heavily-laden canapé trays. 
当罗恩在哈利和赫敏之间来回打量时，赫敏觉得她看到了他的表情中有些柔和的东西。然而，还没等她说什么，他就抱怨说要找到更多的羊糖果，然后大步朝着装满小菜的托盘的方向走去。

“I didn’t know you didn’t know about this,” Harry said quietly as they watched Ron go. “I just assumed –”
“我不知道你不知道这件事，”哈利看着罗恩离去，轻声说。“我只是假设——”

“Don’t worry,” Hermione said, shaking her head with a soft smile. “I get the impression your not knowing about the extent of my knowledge was a very deliberate move on the part of the Malfoys. We’re here now.”
“别担心，”赫敏说，摇了摇头，露出温柔的笑容。“我感觉你不知道我的知识范围是马尔福家族非常故意的举动。我们现在在这里。

“Pretty impressive, though,” Harry said, leaning back on his heels to look up at the cavernous ceiling of the ballroom. “And organised by none other than Lucius Malfoy?”
“不过，还是很令人印象深刻，”哈利说，向后靠在脚跟上，抬头看着宴会厅的洞穴状天花板。“而且不是别人，正是卢修斯·马尔福组织的？”

Hermione absentmindedly hummed her agreement, eyes darting around at the strangers in the room, some of whom had clearly spotted her and were now eyeing her with an interest that made her apprehensive.
赫敏心不在焉地哼着同意的小曲，眼睛四处扫视着房间里的陌生人，其中一些人显然已经发现了她，现在正以一种让她担心的兴趣看着她。

“Quite a gesture. Particularly from him.”
“真是个姿态。尤其是他。

Looking back at Harry, Hermione found his green gaze fixed on her with keen interest. “Well, I did tell you he has a heart,” she said, feeling suddenly very awkward and exposed. 
赫敏回头看向哈利，发现他绿色的目光饶有兴趣地盯着她。“嗯，我确实告诉你他有心，”她说，突然感到非常尴尬和暴露。

“You did.”
“你做到了。”

Hermione could only handle a beat of pregnant silence between them before she said, gesturing to the wider room, “I suppose I’d better –”
赫敏只能忍受他们之间孕育的沉默，然后她说，指着更宽阔的房间，“我想我最好——”

“Yeah, of course, go on,” Harry replied, shooing her away with his hands. “We’re here if you need us.”
“是的，当然，继续说，”哈利回答，用手把她赶走。“如果你需要我们，我们就在这里。”

With nothing but a strained smile to offer Harry, Hermione took a deep breath and prepared to throw herself into a series of conversations she wasn’t altogether prepared to have. In the end, however, they weren't quite as bad as she'd envisioned. 
赫敏对哈利露出一个紧张的笑容，她深吸了一口气，准备投入到一系列她还没有完全准备好的对话中。然而，最终，他们并没有她想象的那么糟糕。

The publishers didn't try to avoid her. They engaged with her. And Hermione did indeed find it much easier to talk her way around them when she could see their facial expressions and they couldn't simply pretend she wasn't speaking. They were, after all, at her event and they had to pay for their nosiness with politeness. After a while, she thought she might finally be getting through to some of them. Certainly, they weren’t edging away nearly as much.
出版商并没有试图避开她。他们与她进行了互动。赫敏确实发现，当她能看到他们的面部表情时，在他们身边交谈要容易得多，而且他们不能简单地假装她没有说话。毕竟，他们是在她的活动中，他们必须礼貌地为他们的爱管闲事付出代价。过了一会儿，她觉得自己可能终于能打通他们中的一些人了。当然，他们并没有那么多。

"Interesting that the Malfoys are so behind your venture, Miss Granger," said one witch.Sweeping the hand she was using to hold her champagne over the room she added, "This… is generous."
“有趣的是，马尔福家族竟然如此支持你的冒险，格兰杰小姐，”一个女巫说。她用那只手把香槟扫过房间，补充道，“这个......是慷慨的。

"Well, they’re involved as subjects," Hermione said, addressing the witch and the small group attached to their conversation. "Their support in this manner is appreciated but perhaps it’s less surprising if you view it in the context of their involvement before this."
“嗯，他们是作为对象参与进来的，”赫敏对女巫和他们谈话中的一小群人说。“他们以这种方式的支持是值得赞赏的，但如果你从他们在此之前的参与来看，也许就不那么令人惊讶了。”

"And I suppose this means they won’t seek any kind of…retribution, legal or otherwise for being published?" asked a weaselly, well-dressed wizard, his voice lowering and his eyes darting around nervously.
“我想这意味着他们不会寻求任何形式的......“一个衣着考究的黄鼠狼问道，他压低了声音，眼睛紧张地四处张望。

"I should think not," Hermione said with a small laugh. "I’m very clear with those I interview that I’m not seeking to damage their reputations –"
“我应该不这么认为，”赫敏小笑着说。“我对我采访的人非常清楚，我不是想损害他们的声誉——”

"No," the witch interrupted with a tinkling laugh, "the Malfoys have done quite enough of that on their own, haven't they?" 
“不，”女巫叮叮当当地笑着打断了他，“马尔福一家自己已经做得够多了，不是吗？

"Perhaps they have," Hermione said sharply over the tittering that had broken out. "Though I like to think my work explores that as something to take seriously rather than something to laugh at."
“也许他们有，”赫敏对爆发的嘲讽尖锐地说。“尽管我喜欢认为我的作品将其探索为值得认真对待的事情，而不是令人嘲笑的事情。”

Looking over the shoulder of the witch who was no longer laughing, Hermione’s attention was caught by the tall figure of Kingsley Shacklebolt. Standing alone by a plinth, he waved and met her eyes inclining his head towards the side of the room in an invitation to speak. 
越过不再笑的女巫的肩膀，赫敏的注意力被金斯莱·沙克尔博尔的高大身影吸引了。他独自站在基座旁，挥了挥手，与她的眼睛对上，他把头歪向房间的一侧，邀请他说话。

“Please excuse me,” Hermione said with an apologetic smile. “I’ll be happy to continue this discussion in a moment, I just have to –” She gestured to Kingsley and the witch, becoming wide-eyed as she glanced over her shoulder to see the Minister for Magic of all people, nodded. 
“请原谅我，”赫敏带着歉意的笑容说。“我很乐意一会儿继续这个讨论，我只需要——”她向金斯莱和女巫做了个手势，瞪大了眼睛，回头瞥了一眼所有人中的魔法部长，点了点头。

“Thank you, Minister,” Hermione said, sidling up to Kingsley with a smile, “for making me look quite important there.”
“谢谢你，部长，”赫敏说，微笑着走到金斯莱身边，“让我在那儿显得相当重要。

Kingsley’s eyebrows rose and he surveyed the grandeur of the room and all the people it contained. “More important than all of this does? Your flattery is out in force tonight, Hermione.”
金斯莱扬起眉毛，他打量着这个房间的宏伟和里面的所有人。“比这一切更重要？你的奉承今晚就要出场了，赫敏。

Brushing a curl from her face, Hermione felt heat rise in her cheeks. “Yes, well, I didn’t ask for this, Kingsley.”
拂去脸上的卷发，赫敏感到脸颊升起了热量。“是的，好吧，我不是要这个的，金斯利。”

“Lucius Malfoy had a reputation for generosity when he found a cause worth supporting back in the day.” Kingsley walked them slowly to the side of the room, away from the many curious eyes and ears surrounding them. “I’m sure it can be quite overwhelming.”
“卢修斯·马尔福（Lucius Malfoy）以慷慨著称，当年他找到了一项值得支持的事业时。”金斯莱慢慢地把他们带到房间的一侧，避开了他们周围许多好奇的眼睛和耳朵。“我敢肯定，这可能会让人不知所措。”

“I’ve been having some trouble persuading publishers to take up the book,” Hermione explained as she followed him. “He thought I might have more success in person than via owl.”
“我一直在努力说服出版商接手这本书，”赫敏一边跟着他解释道。“他认为我亲自去可能比通过猫头鹰更成功。”

Kingsley nodded, pushing his lower lip out in a considering manner. “He's learned your strengths, then,” he said. “Though I wonder that you are having any trouble, Hermione. You seemed certain of its value and you are not a poor communicator."
金斯莱点点头，若有所思地把下唇往外推。“那么，他已经了解了你的长处，”他说。“虽然我想知道你有什么麻烦吗，赫敏。你似乎很确定它的价值，而且你不是一个糟糕的沟通者。

They turned together so that their backs were to the wall and faced the room shoulder-to-shoulder while they continued to speak. By facing outward, they made it awkward for anyone to spend too long staring at them while they conversed. It was one of Kingsley’s favourite tricks – to gain a small amount of privacy by staring down those who might seek to take it. 
他们一起转过身来，背对着墙壁，肩并肩面对房间，继续说话。他们面朝外，让任何人在交谈时都无法长时间盯着他们看，这让别人感到很尴尬。这是金斯利最喜欢的伎俩之一——通过盯着那些可能试图夺取隐私的人来获得一点隐私。

Cringing, Hermione raised a shoulder. “Unfortunately, Lucius is sort of part of the problem there. “They haven’t been overwhelmingly eager to publish his contribution.”
赫敏畏缩着抬起了肩膀。“不幸的是，卢修斯是那里问题的一部分。”他们并没有压倒性地渴望发表他的贡献。

“I see.”
“我明白了。”

“But I think it should be read.” Hermione glanced up at Kingsley and found his expression unreadable. “Besides, as I told him, I really don’t think the Wizengamot will be amenable to my appeal for him if what he’s contributed never actually sees the light of day.”
“但我认为应该读一读。”赫敏抬头看了一眼金斯莱，发现他的表情难以捉摸。“此外，正如我告诉他的，如果他的贡献从未真正出现过，我真的不认为威森加摩会接受我为他的呼吁。”

“That is actually what I wanted to speak with you about, Hermione.”
“这其实就是我想和你谈的，赫敏。”

Catching her next words in her mouth, Hermione looked up at Kingsley’s serious expression and felt a tug of foreboding. “They’ve come to a decision?”
赫敏从嘴里听到接下来的话，抬头看着金斯莱严肃的表情，感到一阵不祥的预感。“他们已经决定了？”

“Yes.” He nodded, eyes flitting down to hers and then back up to the room. “And I’m afraid you’re not likely to like it.”
“是的。”他点点头，眼睛扫向她，然后又回到房间里。“而且我担心你不太可能喜欢它。”

Cold flooded Hermione’s veins. “They haven’t denied it?” she asked, her voice choked. Kingsley's silence spoke volumes. “Outright?”
寒冷淹没了赫敏的血管。“他们没有否认吗？” 她问道，声音哽咽。金斯利的沉默说明了一切。“直接？”

Kingsley nodded slowly, his lips pressed in a thin line. “No allowances.” 
金斯莱缓缓地点点头，他的嘴唇紧贴成一条细线。“没有津贴。”

“But Kingsley –”
“可是金斯利——”

“They acknowledged that it’s surprising that Lucius would be involved in helping you,” Kingsley said over Hermione’s attempt at protestation, “and that it might well be a sign of some kind of larger attitudinal shift. But it’s not enough for them, I'm afraid. It doesn’t, they say, help the wider wizarding community in any significant way.”
“他们承认卢修斯会参与帮助你，这很令人惊讶，”金斯莱对赫敏的抗议尝试说，“这很可能是某种更大态度转变的迹象。但恐怕这对他们来说还不够。他们说，这对更广泛的巫师社区没有任何重大帮助。

“It’s not financial contrition, they mean,” Hermione said with a dismissive scoff. "It doesn't pay for their next big statue."
“他们的意思是，这不是经济上的悔恨，”赫敏轻蔑地嘲笑着说。“这并不能为他们的下一个大雕像买单。”

“That’s not what they mean, Hermione.” Kingsley’s tone was stern, reproving. “You'll find he can’t pay his way out of this either. The Wizengamot thinks that Lucius helping you has a narrow field of beneficiaries. It’s even more narrow if you’re struggling to get published, though it isn’t aware of that yet.”
“他们不是这个意思，赫敏。”金斯莱的语气严厉，带着责备。“你会发现他也付不起这笔钱。威森加摩认为卢修斯帮助你的受益者范围很窄。如果你正在努力发表，那就更狭窄了，尽管它还没有意识到这一点。

“I will get published, Kingsley. This –”
“我会出版的，金斯利。这——”

“It won’t matter if you do, Hermione. They’ve made their decision.”
“你这样做也没关系，赫敏。他们已经做出了决定。

Swallowing, Hermione was mortified to feel the stinging in her nose that usually signalled angry tears were on the horizon. She clenched her jaw in an effort to hold them back. After she’d insisted that Lucius let her try. After telling him that it would give him a better chance. She felt like a naive little fool.
吞咽着，赫敏感到鼻子里的刺痛感感到羞愧，这通常预示着愤怒的眼泪即将出现。她咬紧下巴，试图阻止他们。在她坚持让卢修斯让她试试之后。在告诉他这会给他更好的机会之后。她觉得自己像个天真的小傻瓜。

“They didn’t say they don’t want to hear from him again,” Kingsley continued, a soothing quality to his voice. “They were interested by the change that seems to be taking place. Perhaps the next thing he does – whether for you or someone else – will better show his willingness to return to the wizarding world to make positive changes.”
“他们没有说不想再听到他的消息，”金斯利继续说道，他的声音里带着一种舒缓的品质。“他们对似乎正在发生的变化很感兴趣。也许他所做的下一件事——无论是为了你还是其他人——会更好地表明他愿意回到魔法世界做出积极的改变。

“What chance has he got to show that willingness if they won’t let him out of this manor?” Hermione asked angrily, her voice slightly thicker than usual.
“如果他们不让他离开这个庄园，他有什么机会表现出这种意愿呢？”赫敏生气地问道，她的声音比平时略显粗重。

“I’m afraid that’s something for him to figure out,” Kingsley said lightly. “Not us.”
“恐怕他要弄清楚，”金斯利淡淡地说。“不是我们。”

“But we –”
“可是——”

“Don’t owe him anything, Hermione.” There was a finality to Kingsley’s tone that made Hermione look up at him, blinking away a slight glaze that had formed over her eyes. She found Kingsley already looking back at her, his face firm. “Now, have you considered my offer any further?”
“别欠他什么，赫敏。”金斯莱的语气中带着一种终结，让赫敏抬头看着他，眨了眨眼，消除了她眼睛上形成的轻微呆滞。她发现金斯利已经回头看着她，脸色坚定。“现在，你有没有进一步考虑过我的提议？”

Hermione didn’t need to ask what the offer was. There was only one offer. Would she join his project to roll back the Pureblood laws? That was the question. One she hadn’t given nearly enough consideration.
赫敏不需要问这个提议是什么。只有一个报价。她会加入他的计划来推翻纯血法吗？这就是问题所在。她几乎没有考虑过。

“I have but I’ve just been a little –”
“我有，但我只是有点——”

“Distracted,” Kingsley finished for her, sounding disappointed of all things. She hated disappointment. 
“分心了，”金斯利替她说完，听起来对一切都很失望。她讨厌失望。

“Yes.”
“是的。”

There was a pause in which Kingsley swung his hands behind his back and nodded, his eyes drifting to the Wheezebox that was nearest him. There were two people beside it, listening intently. “I think I am a patient man, Hermione,” Kingsley said slowly. “Particularly given how busy I am.”
停顿了一下，Kingsley将双手在背后摆动，点了点头，他的眼睛飘向离他最近的Wheezebox。旁边有两个人，聚精会神地听着。“我觉得我是个有耐心的人，赫敏，”金斯莱缓缓地说。“特别是考虑到我有多忙。”

“Kingsley –”
“金斯利——”

“And while I can understand that this – your book – is important to you, I am afraid I am going to have to press you.” His eyes cut away from the wider room to hers. “The wizarding world – the real world that continues to move inexorably forward outside the walls of this manor – could use your help in tackling the outdated laws that do it a disservice. It cannot wait. If that’s really not something you wish to be a part of then I want to know now.”
“虽然我能理解这本书——你的书——对你很重要，但恐怕我得逼迫你。”他的目光从更宽阔的房间里移开，看向她。“魔法世界——在这个庄园的围墙外继续无情地向前发展的现实世界——可能需要你的帮助来解决对它有害的过时法律。它不能等待。如果那真的不是你希望参与的事情，那么我现在就想知道。

“It’s not that I don’t want to be a part of it, Kingsley,” Hermione assured him hurriedly. Because that wasn’t it. She’d wanted an opportunity like the one he was offering her for a long time but the timing was so inconvenient. “That’s not it.” 
“不是我不想成为其中的一部分，金斯莱，”赫敏急忙向他保证。因为那不是她一直想要一个像他长期以来给她的机会，但时机太不方便了。“不是这样。”

“Then am I to understand that you’re accepting my offer?”
“那么我能明白你是在接受我的提议吗？”

“That’s – I’m just –” Hermione huffed out a sigh, blowing her fringe out of her increasingly warm face. “Yes, I suppose I am accepting your offer in a sense, Kingsley, but –”
“那是——我只是——”赫敏叹了口气，吹掉了她越来越温暖的脸上的刘海。“是的，我想我在某种意义上接受了你的提议，金斯莱，但是——”

“Excellent,” Kingsley said, rolling momentarily onto his toes as a triumphant smile flitted over his face. “Then I will schedule a meeting for us to go over the final details of the arrangement next week. Expect my owl, Hermione.”
“太好了，”金斯利说，脚趾一会儿翻滚着，脸上闪过一丝胜利的笑容。“然后我会安排一次会议，让我们在下周讨论安排的最终细节。等着我的猫头鹰吧，赫敏。

Before Hermione could say anything else or do anything but gape, Kingsley purposefully pushed off on one foot and began a swift walk towards the exit of the ballroom, his magnificent scarlet robes sweeping behind him. 
赫敏还没来得及说什么，也没来得及做任何事情，金斯莱就故意单脚推开，开始快步走向舞厅的出口，他华丽的猩红色长袍在他身后扫过。

Bloody Kingsley. Shoulders slumping, Hermione ran an exasperated hand over her clammy forehead. Bloody Wizengamot . Turning on the spot, she looked at the sea of people around her and felt suddenly like she might drown. Too many of them were watching her, clearly keen to find out what she and the Minister for Magic had been discussing with such intensity.
血腥的金斯利。 赫敏耷拉着肩膀，恼怒地用一只手抚摸着她湿漉漉的额头。 血腥的威森加摩 .她原地转过身来，看着周围的人海，突然觉得自己快要淹死了。他们中有太多人在看着她，显然很想知道她和魔法部长一直在如此激烈地讨论什么。

She had to talk to Lucius. To tell him. About what Kingsley had said about the Wizengamot. About the laws she was going to be working on. They had to come up with a plan for his next steps because this couldn’t possibly be it . 
她得跟卢修斯谈谈。告诉他。关于金斯莱对威森加摩的评价。关于她将要制定的法律。他们必须为他的下一步制定一个计划，因为这不可能。

Taking a deep breath, Hermione searched the room for Draco’s white blonde hair like it was a lifeline. He’d be able to sneak her out just so that she could just speak to Lucius, just –
赫敏深吸一口气，在房间里寻找德拉科的白金发，就像它是一条救生索一样。他可以偷偷把她偷偷溜出去，这样她就可以和卢修斯说话了，只是——

There .
那里。

Sighing with relief, Hermione jolted forward when she saw the lithe figure of Draco across the ballroom. He was flanked by a content Luna, who was sipping a martini, and a very sour, resentful Pansy, while speaking with – Hermione stopped abruptly. Narcissa Malfoy. 
赫敏松了一口气，当她看到舞厅对面德拉科轻盈的身影时，她猛地向前冲去。他的两侧是心满意足的卢娜，她正在啜饮马提尼酒，还有一个非常酸涩、怨恨的三色堇，正在和他说话——赫敏突然停了下来。纳西莎·马尔福。

Tall, thin and strikingly beautiful in silvery-blue dress robes, Narcissa stood speaking to her son, seemingly without any awareness of the two girls standing beside him. Their conversation appeared to be tense, with Narcissa speaking more than her son in an almost interrogative fashion. Perhaps catching the stock-still figure of Hermione in the rippling crowd in his periphery, Draco fractionally turned his head and met her eye. 
身材高挑、瘦削、身穿银蓝色礼服长袍的纳西莎站在那里与她的儿子交谈，似乎完全没有注意到站在他身边的两个女孩。他们的谈话似乎很紧张，纳西莎以一种近乎质问的方式比她的儿子说得更多。也许是看到了赫敏在周围荡漾的人群中静止不动的身影，德拉科微微转过头来，与她的目光相遇。

There was a grim set to his jaw as he subtly shook his head in a way that told Hermione it would be best if she didn’t approach. Before she could turn away, however, Narcissa followed her son’s gaze and spotted Hermione for herself.
他的下巴变得严肃起来，他巧妙地摇了摇头，告诉赫敏最好不要靠近。然而，在她转身离开之前，纳西莎顺着儿子的目光，亲眼发现了赫敏。

“Ah, Hermione Granger.” Narcissa’s voice was cut glass in every sense of the word as it carried across the small space of the ballroom that separated them. “The guest of honour, I’m told.”
“啊，赫敏·格兰杰。”纳西莎的声音在任何意义上都是被切割的玻璃，因为它传遍了将他们分开的宴会厅的狭小空间。“我听说是主宾。”

Draco’s nostrils flared slightly as he sighed, casting an irritable look at some of the guests who had looked around with interest at Narcissa’s declaration. Swapping the shake of his head for an impatient, jerky nod, he invited Hermione to approach with an unspoken ‘and be quick about it’. Despite that, Hermione did so hesitantly, unwillingly, not entirely certain she was in the correct frame of mind to be encountering Narcissa Malfoy. 
德拉科叹了口气，鼻孔微微张开，恼怒地看了一眼那些饶有兴趣地四处张望着纳西莎宣言的客人。他把摇头换成了不耐烦、生涩的点头，他邀请赫敏走近，说了一句无声的“快点”。尽管如此，赫敏还是犹豫不决，不情愿地，不完全确定她是否处于正确的心态中遇到纳西莎·马尔福。

“Mrs – Narci –” Hermione swallowed each of her greetings and, with a panicked look at an eye-rolling Draco, finally settled on a quiet, “Hello.”
“太太——纳西——”赫敏吞下了她的每一个问候，惊慌地看了一眼翻白眼的德拉科，最后平静地说道，“你好。

Narcissa did not alleviate Hermione’s discomfort by offering her a preferred form of address. Instead, she increased it by giving her nothing more than a cold smile and a single, slow nod. 
纳西莎并没有通过给赫敏提供一种首选的称呼方式来减轻她的不适。相反，她只给了她一个冰冷的微笑和一个缓慢的点头，从而加剧了这种情绪。

“You’re supposed to be talking to publishers,” Draco said, his voice little more than a grumble. “Not floating about in the middle of the room like a piece of gillyweed that’s broken off its holdfast.”
“你应该和出版商谈谈，”德拉科说，他的声音只不过是抱怨。“而不是像一棵脱离了固定物的钼草一样漂浮在房间中央。”

“I was ,” Hermione insisted, trying to ignore the strange, piercing feeling that accompanied being inspected by Narcissa Malfoy. It was what she imagined lasers might feel like. “I was doing quite well, too, but I had to talk to Kingsley and –”
“我是，”赫敏坚持道，试图忽略伴随着纳西莎·马尔福检查而来的奇怪、刺痛的感觉。这就是她想象中的激光可能是什么感觉。“我也过得很好，但我得跟金斯利谈谈，然后——”

“It’s very nice of Mr Malfoy to do this for you, Hermione,” Luna piped up from Draco’s side, attracting the eyes of everyone in the small group. “You must have really won him over. But you’re much better at listening than you used to be; I’m sure that helped.”
“马尔福先生能为你做这件事真是太好了，赫敏，”卢娜从德拉科的身边站起来，吸引了小团体中每个人的目光。“你一定真的赢得了他的青睐。但你比以前更善于倾听;我确信这有帮助。

Not entirely sure how to respond to that, Hermione did nothing more than make a small, almost frightened wheezing sound that drew raised eyebrows from Pansy and a sharp look from Narcissa.
赫敏不完全确定该如何回应，只不过发出了一声小小的、几乎是惊恐的喘息声，这引起了潘西扬起的眉毛和纳西莎的尖锐目光。

“Is he home?” Luna continued before taking a sip of her martini and blinking owlishly at Draco over the rim of the glass.
“他在家吗？”卢娜继续说，然后喝了一口马提尼酒，隔着玻璃杯边缘对着德拉科眨了眨眼。

“My –” 
“我的——”

“Your father,” Luna confirmed with a nod when she had completely swallowed her sip.
“你的爸爸，”当 Luna 完全吞下她的啜饮时点头确认。

“Yes,” Draco said hesitantly, his eyes flitting briefly to his mother, “but he’s –”
“是的，”德拉科犹豫地说，他的眼睛短暂地扫向他的母亲，“但他是——”

“Not…able to attend,” Hermione finished for him and he nodded fervently.
“不......能够参加，“赫敏为他说完，他热切地点点头。

Luna made a small noise of disappointment, her lips pursing. “I know you don’t know about the Blibbering Humdingers, Draco, but I’m sure he will. I’d love him to talk to me like he talked with Hermione.”
Luna 发出一声失望的小声，她的嘴唇抿着。“我知道你不知道那些喋喋不休的Humdingers，Draco，但我相信他会的。我希望他能像和赫敏说话一样跟我说话。

Narcissa blinked rapidly at Luna, then at Hermione, then at her son, like she was struggling to process the conversation taking place around her. Taking a deep breath, Narcissa laid a hand on Draco’s arm. “Excuse me,” she said tightly and, though she was addressing Draco, her eyes were fixed on the exit across the room. 
纳西莎快速地对卢娜眨了眨眼，然后是赫敏，然后是她的儿子，就像她正在努力处理周围的对话一样。深吸一口气，纳西莎将一只手放在德拉科的手臂上。“对不起，”她紧紧地说，虽然她是在对德拉科说话，但她的眼睛还是盯着房间对面的出口。

“Mother,” he said, his voice low as his eyes followed the direction of hers, “the Aurors –”
“妈妈，”他说，他的声音很低，眼睛跟着她的方向，“傲罗们——”

“Won't say a thing,” Narcissa said, her chin raised and her voice confident. “Not to me. Not here .”
“什么都不说，”纳西莎说，她抬起下巴，声音自信。“对我来说不是。不在这里。

Swallowing, Hermione watched Narcissa click across the ballroom in her stilettos, moving through the crowd with sylph-like ease. After a moment, she slipped out of the door and, sure enough, she was not sent back. Blinking, Hermione’s attention came back to their small group and she found Draco frowning at her pinched expression. 
赫敏咽了口口水，看着纳西莎穿着细高跟鞋在舞厅里咔哒咔哒地走来走去，像仙女一样轻松地穿过人群。过了一会儿，她溜出了门，果然，她没有被送回去。眨了眨眼，赫敏的注意力又回到了他们那一小群人身上，她发现德拉科正皱着眉头看着她紧绷的表情。

“It’ll be fine, Granger,” he said stiffly, clearly unsure about how he was supposed to feel about what was happening. “They’ll just…” 
“会没事的，格兰杰，”他僵硬地说，显然不确定他对所发生的事情应该有什么感觉。“他们只会......”

Trailing off, Draco lifted his glass to his lips and, tipping his head back, drained it of champagne as effectively as he had just drained Hermione of confidence.
德拉科把酒杯举到嘴边，把头往后仰，像刚刚耗尽赫敏的信心一样有效地喝掉了香槟。

“I think we’re being dragged into some kind of psychodrama,” Pansy said, leaning around Draco to speak to Luna in an undertone. 
“我觉得我们被拖进了某种心理剧中，”潘西说，靠在德拉科身边，低声对卢娜说话。

“Oh, how exciting!” Luna exclaimed, clapping her hands in a way that made her radish earrings tremble with excitement.  
“哦，多么令人兴奋！”露娜惊呼道，拍手的方式让她的萝卜耳环兴奋地颤抖着。

更多注释见本章末尾Lucius was struggling to focus, despite being the very picture of ease. He was seated behind his desk, reclined with his legs crossed. He had a book lifted in front of his eyes as though blocking out the room might force him to actually read the words. Every time he tried, however, he found that his thoughts drifted to the event he knew was happening in the Manor’s ballroom. 
卢修斯正在努力集中注意力，尽管他看起来非常轻松。他坐在书桌后面，双腿交叉斜靠着。他把一本书举在眼前，仿佛挡住了房间可能会迫使他真正阅读这些文字。然而，每次他尝试时，他都会发现他的思绪飘向了他知道发生在庄园宴会厅的事件。

Had Draco managed to get Hermione there? Had he managed to get anyone there? Was she doing as he wanted? Or was she fighting tooth and nail at the threshold to the room, determined to rain hexes down on him?
德拉科设法把赫敏带到那里了吗？他设法把人弄到那里了吗？她是否按照他的意愿做了？还是她在房间的门槛上咬牙切齿地战斗，决心向他下雨？

Lucius’ rumination was interrupted by a sharp knock on the door and the rattle of the handle turning. Sighing, he squeezed his eyes closed and tried to channel some patience as he raised his voice into the pages of the book.
卢修斯的沉思被一阵尖锐的敲门声和门把手转动的嘎嘎声打断了。他叹了口气，闭上眼睛，试图在提高声音对着书页中传递一些耐心。

"I told Draco he was to keep you downstairs to speak to the publishers. You can't –”
“我告诉德拉科，他会让你留在楼下和出版商谈谈。你不能——”

“Don't fret, Lucius.” 
“别担心，卢修斯。”

Lucius stiffened at the sound of the familiar but entirely unexpected voice, his grip on his book tightening so that the tips of his fingers went white. 
卢修斯听到这个熟悉但完全出乎意料的声音，身体僵硬了起来，他抓着书的手越来越紧，以至于他的指尖都发白了。

“She's still downstairs. Staying . Doing as she's told. You always were an assiduous trainer.”
“她还在楼下。 住。按照她的指示去做。你一直都是个勤奋的教练。

Lowering the book from in front of his face, Lucius looked to the doorway where Narcissa was sliding into the room and closing the door behind her with a gentle click . 卢修斯把书从面前放下，看向门口，纳西莎正滑进房间，轻轻地咔嗒一声关上了她身后的门。他的眼睛转向坐在他手肘上的火威士忌，评估他喝了多少酒。不幸的是，这还不足以让幻觉如此令人信服。

卢修斯扬起眉毛，没有发表评论，想知道阿斯托利亚对这样的支持会有多欢迎或感激。纳西莎和她儿媳之间的关系从来没有像他那样温暖或特别深情。纳西莎不止一次明确表示她不赞成德拉科选择的妻子。当然，这在一定程度上是因为 Narcissa 是一位充满爱心的母亲，并且对她的孩子完全着迷。卢修斯有一种感觉，阿斯托利亚也会是一样的。他希望他们能在那里找到一些共同点，否则冲突将是不可避免的。

“好奇。”卢修斯在嘴里仔细斟酌着这个词，似乎不完全确定她会说什么。

“关于我今晚无意中听到的一些事情。你想知道它们是什么吗？

卢修斯把手臂放到桌子上，懒洋洋地挥手邀请她继续。他完全意识到停止或离开的要求不会得到重视，因此他不如表现得像一个自愿参与对话的人。这其中有力量，尽管它很小。

“我没有——”

“当然，我纠正了他们，”纳西莎继续平稳地试图说话。

他的下巴瞬间紧紧地合上了。他没有安排正式的宣布是有原因的——除了他们之外，没有人需要知道。当然，任何对这些信息感兴趣的人都不是他想要拥有的那种人。

“你没有权利那样做，纳西莎，”他说，声音冰冷。

“不是吗？”纳西莎轻轻地笑了起来，她苍白的眉毛略带怜悯地上扬，让他的衣领感觉太紧了。“我认为我完全有权利。这是——曾经是——我的婚姻，也是你的婚姻，卢修斯。即使你确实有忘记这一点的倾向。

Lucius shifted in his chair, like he was having to physically restrain himself from rising to Narcissa’s bait. For the most part, his own desires had not come into the conclusion of his marriage. What was best for everyone involved had. 
卢修斯在椅子上挪动了一下，就像他不得不用身体克制自己不敢上纳西莎的诱饵一样。在大多数情况下，他自己的欲望并没有成为他婚姻的结论。对每个参与者来说最好的东西都有。

Has Draco been slipping you babbling draughts?”
“我也对你最近决定表现得像个沉思者很感兴趣，这个决定已经被抛弃了......渗出。她说“渗”这个词，好像它是不体面的东西，公平地说，它确实是。“在我看来，你在过去六个月里说的话比你过去六年或更长时间说的都多。德拉科有没有给你溜走咿呀呀的草稿？

纳西莎伸出手，从桌子上拿出卢修斯的水晶杯，喝了一口里面的火威士忌。当她没有把杯子放回原处，而是松散地挂在手里时，卢修斯用鼻子叹了口气，然后站了起来。

他没有向纳西莎投去哪怕一丝怨恨的眼神，绕着桌子走了一圈，经过她，走到他的饮料车前，开始给自己倒一杯新鲜的酒。他有一种感觉，他会需要它。

“楼下发生了什么事，Lucius？”她天真地问了这个问题，但她的语气中有一些东西让卢修斯站直了身子，警惕起来。

“这是个事件，纳西莎，”他生硬地回答。“鸡尾酒会。我本以为你会认出其中的一个，因为你在那个房间里组织了多少人。

“德拉科告诉我这是给格兰杰女孩的。”纳西莎低头看了看她手里的玻璃杯，掀起了一些里面的火威士忌。“是吗？”

“是的。”

There was no point in denying it. Not if Draco had already told her the truth. He had always been terrible at hiding things from her. 否认它没有意义。如果德拉科已经告诉了她真相，就不会。他一直很不善于向她隐瞒事情。卢修斯仍然清楚地记得德拉科告诉她的那一天——在他明确警告他不要这样做之后——他已经带他去见了博金和伯克斯。“如果他碰到了什么怎么办”的呼喊声仍然在他耳边响起。

纳西莎对着她的饮料轻轻点了点头，他几乎能看到。

“这不是慈善行为。”

“No?”
“没有？”

“No.”
“不。”

“我的魔法。还有我的自由。

“我明白了。”

她安静下来，若有所思地打量着他。卢修斯已经很久没有受到纳西莎的审视了，他已经忘记了她的蓝眼睛有多么刺眼。

Had he said those things? Vaguely he could recall that he had, the memories like watching himself through a thick, distorted pane of glass. He had said them quite angrily, in fact.

When he’d been at his most bitter he had decided that he no longer wanted the magic that the rest of the Wizarding World had. He no longer wanted magic if it was considered equal to a Mudblood’s. 每次纳西莎建议他或许有办法让他恢复自己的生活时，他都告诉她他不想要。因为他知道这不会真的像他曾经的生活那样。这就是事实。马尔福庄园的围墙外没有任何东西让他感兴趣。

“我们有一个孙子在路上，纳西莎，正如你指出的，”他平静地说。“情况会发生变化。”

卢修斯以为他已经敞开心扉了。最终。当然，他是诚实的。“花了时间才明白，”他说。

“多少时间？”纳西莎问道，微微举起杯子，检查她是否还有足够的火威士忌。“比我们结婚这么多年还多？”

Lucius’ brow flattened into a perplexed frown. “Don’t be ridiculous –”
卢修斯的眉头皱成了困惑的眉头。“别荒谬——”

“是吗？”纳西莎问道，她的声音很轻，但不可否认地带着一种尖锐。“这很荒谬吗？原谅我，卢修斯，你很难想象为什么你会花几年时间把我推开，却在短短几个月内让一个陌生人进来。

Lucius swallowed. He hadn't just let Hermione in. She had forced her way in with anger and stubbornness. But then she had made it feel like she was always supposed to be there. "It’s complex, Narcissa."
卢修斯咽了口口水。他不只是让赫敏进来。她带着愤怒和固执强行闯了进来。但后来她让她觉得自己应该一直在那里。“这很复杂，纳西莎。”

She scoffed. "Oh, please, Lucius. Your feelings around consorting with Mudbloods have never been complex before. They were always one of the most straightforward things about you. 她嘲笑道。“哦，拜托了，卢修斯。你对与 Mudbloods 交往的感受从未如此复杂。他们一直是你最直接的事情之一。你为什么能发现自己和这个谈谈......这个女孩？你是什么时候决定，当你无法忍受我的公司时，你可以忍受一个泥巴种在你的公司里？我值得知道。

Lucius tightened his grip on his glass, his nostrils flaring at the distaste with which Narcissa said 'Mudblood'. Had he always looked as angry and disgusted when he had said the word? Had it contorted his upper lip in the same way? Made his voice come so close to a hiss? 
卢修斯紧紧握住了他的酒杯，他的鼻孔因纳西莎说“泥巴种”而感到厌恶。当他说出这个词时，他总是看起来生气和厌恶吗？它以同样的方式扭曲了他的上唇吗？他的声音变得如此接近嘶嘶声？

"Because she already hated me," he spat. There was truth in that. Once he'd known she wasn't planning to sell his every secret to the press, he'd found it surprisingly easy to tell Hermione things because she expected the worst from him. For a brief time, it had almost been enjoyable to confirm some of her worst thoughts. Her hatred had been such a comfort to him that he’d been alarmed when he’d lost it. “因为她已经恨我了，”他啐了一口。这是有道理的。一旦他知道她不打算把他的每一个秘密都卖给媒体，他就发现告诉赫敏事情出奇地容易，因为她对他有最坏的期望。有那么一小段时间，确认她最糟糕的想法几乎是一件令人愉快的事情。她的憎恨对他来说是一种安慰，以至于当他失去憎恨时，他感到震惊。“因为我不在乎在和她说话时看到她脸上的仇恨。”

There was a subtle jump in Narcissa's neck as she swallowed. "And you couldn’t stand the idea that I might hate you, is that what you’re saying?"
纳西莎的脖子在吞咽时微微跳动。“而且你受不了我会恨你的想法，你是这么说的吗？”

He didn't respond but Narcissa understood and her smile was bitter. 
他没有回答，但纳西莎明白了，她的笑容很苦涩。

"You couldn’t stand the idea that I might hate you," she said, standing up from her lean on the desk to her full height. "That I might resent you for everything we went through. So your response was to close me out? To refuse to meet my eyes? To leave rooms when I entered them? For years ?"
“你受不了我会恨你的想法，”她说，从靠在桌子上的身体站起来。“这样我就可以因为我们所经历的一切而怨恨你。所以你的反应是把我关起来？拒绝与我的眼睛对视？当我进入房间时离开房间？好几年了？

Lucius could only nod. She was speaking like it hadn't been for her. For Draco. Like he hadn't been trying to remove himself in the way one might obliviate a bad memory. Like he hadn't been trying to give them the chance to live a normal life. "I couldn't ruin your life more than I already had."
卢修斯只能点点头。她说话的样子，就像不是她一样。为了德拉科。就像他没有试图以一种可能会忘记糟糕记忆的方式离开自己一样。就像他没有试图给他们过正常生活的机会一样。“我不能比我现在更毁了你的生活。”

“你一直都是个愚蠢的人，卢修斯，”她说，她的声音有些颤抖。他从酒中抬起头来，感到被冒犯。“你是，”她坚持说。“你当然很聪明，但你总是能做愚蠢、短视、懦弱、自私的事情。”

Narcissa took a deep breath and then raised her glass to take a drink through pursed lips. 
纳西莎深吸了一口气，然后举起酒杯，通过噘起的嘴唇喝了一口。

所有的空气似乎都从卢修斯的肺里逸出。“我看到了你的痛苦，纳西莎，”他嘶哑地说。“还有你的恐惧。反复。我看到它很多年了，我明白我要为此负责。

"And you just decided you couldn’t bear feeling that responsibility any more, is that it? You decided it would be more convenient to drop it, like the heavy burden of a winter cloak in a hot room?" 
“而你只是决定你不能再忍受这种责任了，是吗？你觉得把它放下会更方便，就像在炎热的房间里披上一件沉重的冬天斗篷一样？

“别什么？”当她准备说出恶毒的话时，她上唇的那一翘起就在那里，就像一根高高举起的鞭子。他的每一块肌肉都绷紧了，准备承受这一击。

“因为你把我推开了！”

卢修斯无法从他的声音中抑制住这种指责。“你让我。”

纳西莎把空杯子砸在他的桌子上，然后抬起一只手，平放在胸前。

卢修斯盯着他，目光盯着纳西莎的肩膀，耳边传来奇怪的响声。她指责他残忍、自私，让她感到孤独。所有他一直试图避免的事情。但是如果他让她留下来，他无论如何都不会看她。他无情的懊悔感本可以确保这一点;它总是会以痛苦的方式结束。然而，他的遗憾又多了一层。

纳西莎的声音在她接下来说话时语气稳定多了。“不好的回忆来得这么快就超过了好回忆，这不是很有趣吗？”有几次我发现自己希望你去阿兹卡班。

他的退缩是本能的。不是因为她说的话特别残忍，而是因为这也是他长期以来的愿望，直到最近，他才开始觉得他可能有理由为他的愿望没有得到实现而感到高兴。

“至少那样我就可以假装我还有我的丈夫。相反，我留下的是一个我几乎不认识的外壳。

“意思是？”

“和泥巴种一起工作？”她问道，语气暗示她认为这应该是非常明显的。“帮她？”她转向他喝了一口，然后放下杯子，若有所思地歪着头。

卢修斯用一只手揉了揉他的下巴，他的心突然砰砰直跳，他的耐心也随之消磨。“别这么叫她了，纳西莎。”

“泥巴种。”

“她不是泥巴种。”

Eyes combing his defensive stance, Narcissa's smile faltered slightly, like a candle pushed into a cool breeze. "Has the definition of that word changed in my time in France?" she asked politely. “Perhaps I’ve been gone longer than I thought…”
纳西莎的眼睛梳理着他的防御姿态，他的笑容微微颤抖，就像一根被推入凉爽微风中的蜡烛。“我在法国的时候，这个词的定义有变化吗？”“也许我离开的时间比我想象的要长......”

“显然没有。”

"So, if it’s not the word that’s changed, Lucius, then what has?" 
“所以，如果不是这个词变了，Lucius，那是什么变了？”

他沉默不语，一动不动，纳西莎紧紧地看着他，就像她在等他犯错一样。卢修斯试图让他的脸变得高深莫测，避免直接的眼神接触，即使她发出了一声小小的喉咙呼气，其中夹杂着理解、厌恶和怜悯。

他无法给纳西莎一个直截了当的答案。他花了相当长的时间与他对赫敏的感情的羞耻作斗争，但这对她并不公平。他钦佩一个如此令人钦佩的人，他应该感到什么羞耻呢？他让儿子帮助一个他已经认为是朋友的人，他应该感到什么羞耻呢？

I can only assume she likes you without magic; perhaps you remind her of her father.”

卢修斯脸色发白，对她的暗示突然涌上一阵厌恶，使他回过神来。“别，纳西莎。”

卢修斯张开嘴想要争论，他犹豫了一下，额头上微微皱起了眉头。 睡裙？ 德拉科到底是怎么解释他的指示来让她变得好起来的？他没有进一步询问，而是冷冷地看了纳西莎一眼，这表明他不愿意再听到她对赫敏感兴趣的任何虚假理由。

“合同上的墨水还没干，”她厉声说。

Lucius watched her, his own drink dangling at his side between his fingertips. “是的，你很确定，”她冷笑着说，把酒杯举回嘴边，大口大口地喝了一口。卢修斯看着她，他自己的饮料在他的指尖之间晃来晃去。他以一种快速的脉动节奏挤压着自己的杯子边缘，他意识到这与他自己的心跳是及时的。

当纳西莎放下酒杯时，她低下头，从嘴唇两侧拂去火威士忌的湿漉漉的，然后闭上眼睛片刻，似乎在挣扎着看他。

“你真的这么想，不是吗？”

卢修斯紧紧咬紧下巴，没有回答，但他紧绷的表情对纳西莎来说已经足够了，纳西莎向他露出一个紧绷的笑容，但她的眼睛还没碰到。

In the silence, they stared at one another across the room. It stood to reason that the feeling of getting to know someone had a reverse but Lucius had never really experienced it. 
在寂静中，他们在房间的另一头凝视着彼此。按理说，了解某人的感觉是相反的，但卢修斯从未真正体验过。

“我记得有一次你担心德拉科对那个女孩太着迷了，”纳西莎轻声说。“我心想，他只是在做一个负责任的父亲——确保他的儿子明白对他的期望以及这些期望有什么限制。我错了吗？你只是担心他继承了你的......偏爱泥巴种？它一直在那里，我就是没看到吗？

“She is not a Mudblood, Narcissa. I told you.” 
“她不是泥巴种，纳西莎。我告诉过你了。

Narcissa cackled, her head falling back. “Oh, what is she then, Lucius? I can’t wait to hear it. And don’t say half your age because that much I am very clear on.” 
纳西莎咯咯地笑着，她的头向后仰。“哦，那么她是什么，卢修斯？我迫不及待地想听到它。不要说你的年龄只有一半，因为我很清楚这一点。

“She is…she is intelligent. And proud. And passionate. And…and hellishly stubborn and –” Lucius swallowed. “Good. She is good, Narcissa. To me. For me. If I’ve ever been a fool, it's been in believing that anyone, especially her, could be defined by one word.”
“她是......她很聪明。而且很自豪。而且充满激情。和。。。而且非常固执，而且——“卢修斯咽了口口水。“很好。她很好，纳西莎。对我来说。给我的。如果我曾经是个傻瓜，那就是相信任何人，尤其是她，都可以用一个词来定义。

Narcissa’s sarcastic smile had dimmed with every word Lucius spoke.
纳西莎讽刺的笑容随着卢修斯说的每一句话而变得黯淡。

“How long, Lucius, before you realise that you’re just going to ruin her life by association in the way that you apparently so feared you were ruining mine?” Her voice was soft, her gaze piercing. “Perhaps you feel like her kindness, her affection, is some kind of absolution? That the rest of our world will, one day, cease to see your darkness beside her golden glow? I doubt that will happen. I doubt there will be understanding. She will not restore you. You will most likely ruin her and you are deluded if you think she will be willing to languish in this Manor as I was.”
“多久，卢修斯，你才会意识到，你只会因为交往而毁掉她的生活，就像你显然如此担心你毁了我的生活一样？”她的声音很轻柔，目光锐利。“也许你觉得她的善良，她的爱，是某种赦免？我们世界的其他人总有一天会不再看到她金色光芒之外的黑暗？我怀疑这种情况会发生。我怀疑会有人理解。她不会让你恢复的。你很可能会毁了她，如果你认为她会愿意像我一样在这个庄园里受苦，那你就是被骗了。

Nausea rushed over Lucius, leaving him dizzy and reeling. Enough . Nothing about this was productive. Setting his nearly-full glass down on his drinks trolley with enough force to make the entire thing rattle threateningly, Lucius drew his shoulders back. 
恶心涌上了卢修斯的心头，让他头晕目眩，不知所措。 足够。这没有任何成效。卢修斯把几乎满了的杯子放在他的饮料手推车上，用力让整个东西发出威胁性的嘎嘎声，然后卢修斯把肩膀往后缩。

“I think it’s time you returned to the ballroom, Narcissa, before the Aurors come looking. Unless Letty has set up a room for you –”
“我想你该回舞厅去了，纳西莎，在傲罗们来找之前。除非莱蒂已经为你安排了房间——”

“Oh, I’m not staying here, Lucius.” Narcissa pushed herself up to her full height, her eyes flicking to his shoulders which had dropped fractionally under the weight of his relief. 
“哦，我不会留在这里的，卢修斯。”纳西莎把自己撑到最上面，她的眼睛瞥向他的肩膀，他的肩膀在他的解脱下微微下降了。

Turning to the dark window behind his desk, she assessed her reflection and brushed down her robes. “No,” she said, the word trailing out on a sigh. “Whatever it was in this Manor that ever made it feel like home –” she glanced over her shoulder at him, her eyes travelling the length of him “ – it’s long gone.”
她转向他书桌后面的黑暗窗户，评估了自己的倒影，拂去了她的长袍。“不，”她说，这个词在叹息中拖延。“不管这个庄园里有什么东西让它有家的感觉——”她回头瞥了他一眼，眼睛在他身上扫视着，“——它早就消失了。

“I shall tell Draco you –” Lucius began, speaking to her back as she walked towards the door. 
“我会告诉德拉科你——”卢修斯开始对她说，她一边走向门口。

“I’m meeting Draco and Astoria for breakfast at my hotel,” she responded sharply, her hand coming to rest on the door handle. “You need not say anything on my behalf.” 
“我要在我的酒店和Draco和Astoria一起吃早餐，”她尖锐地回答，她的手停在门把手上。“你不需要替我说什么。”

There was a pause, during which Narcissa seemed to deflate slightly, her gaze fixed on the door in front of her. “If Miss Granger does, by some miracle, manage to find a way to get you your freedom, Lucius, seize it. You might as well walk away from all this with something lasting.”
停顿了一会儿，纳西莎似乎稍微泄气了一下，她的目光盯着面前的门。“如果格兰杰小姐真的奇迹般地找到了让你自由的方法，卢修斯，抓住它。你还不如带着一些持久的东西离开这一切。

With that, Narcissa pulled open his study door and left as quietly and swiftly as she came in. The entire thing could have been a dream. Or a nightmare, based on the awful, dread-filled mood that had settled over Lucius.
说完，纳西莎拉开了他的书房门，和她进来一样安静而迅速地离开了。整件事可能是一个梦。或者是一场噩梦，基于笼罩着卢修斯的可怕、充满恐惧的情绪。

更多注释见本章末尾Hermione fidgeted with the small pile of business cards she had accumulated over the night, pressing the sharp, magically reinforced edges of them into the lines on her palms. 
赫敏坐立不安地摆弄着她一夜积累的一小摞名片，把它们锋利的、被魔法加固的边缘压在手掌上的线条上。

The hour was growing late and the event was petering out, drips and drops of people leaving the room at increasingly regular intervals. Weaving through the dissipating crowd, offering polite but distracted smiles to those around her, she spied the familiar gleam of Draco’s hair under the flickering candlelight and made towards him. 
时间越来越晚，活动逐渐消失，人们越来越有规律地离开房间。她穿行在散去的人群中，向周围的人提供礼貌但心不在焉的微笑，在摇曳的烛光下，她窥见了德拉科熟悉的头发，向他走来。

After Narcissa's departure, he had forced Hermione back into mingling. So she had. Somewhat unwillingly but still, she thought, quite successfully. She was bringing the business cards to him as trophies of sorts. Proof that she'd done as requested.
纳西莎离开后，他强迫赫敏重新交往。她确实做到了。有点不情愿，但她想，还是相当成功的。她把名片当作战利品拿给他。证明她已经按照要求做了。

Even if her mind had only been partially on the task. Her eyes had drifted regularly over the shoulders of her interlocutors towards the doors to the ballroom as she had contended with a nauseating mix of hope and fear that she would see Narcissa Malfoy – Black – whatever she wanted to be called – coming back through them. 
即使她的心思只是部分地放在了这项任务上。她的眼睛经常从对话者的肩膀上移向舞厅的门口，因为她一直在与一种令人作呕的希望和恐惧作斗争，她希望看到纳西莎·马尔福——布莱克——无论她想被叫什么——通过他们回来。

But she never did. 
但她从未这样做。

If there was one thing that was going to make Hermione more unsettled than Narcissa’s presence, it was her absence. Specifically where she was in said absence. Even more specifically, who she was with. It was hard for Hermione to imagine what any kind of meeting between Narcissa and Lucius might look like because, though she felt like she knew him increasingly well, she realised she didn’t really know him with Narcissa. She didn’t know them at all – their dynamic, their interactions, even the intricacies of their present feelings towards one another were all mysteries to her. 
如果说有一件事比纳西莎的存在更让赫敏感到不安，那就是她的缺席。具体来说，她在那个缺席的地方。更具体地说，她和谁在一起。赫敏很难想象纳西莎和卢修斯之间的任何一次会面会是什么样子，因为虽然她觉得自己越来越了解他，但她意识到她并没有真正了解他和纳西莎。她根本不了解他们——他们的动态、他们的互动，甚至他们现在对彼此的错综复杂的感情，对她来说都是个谜。

Hermione hated not knowing. Even more than that, she hated not having a means by which she could become knowing.
赫敏讨厌不知道。不仅如此，她更讨厌没有办法让她知道。

Reaching the edge of the room, Hermione found Draco leaning against the wall, his arms crossed and a glazed expression on his face as he gazed over the heads of the quietly conversing Pansy and Luna. He was, she realised, also watching the door. On first glance, he looked disinterested, but there was a pulsing in his jaw that indicated he was clenching and unclenching his teeth at a rapid pace. 
走到房间的边缘，赫敏发现德拉科靠在墙上，双臂交叉，脸上露出呆滞的表情，凝视着安静交谈的潘西和卢娜的头顶。她意识到，他也在看着门口。乍一看，他看起来不感兴趣，但他的下巴有一阵搏动，表明他正在快速咬紧和松开牙齿。

When he saw Hermione approaching, Draco pushed himself up off the wall, his action prompting Pansy and Luna to stop speaking and turn around to look at her too. 
当他看到赫敏走近时，德拉科把自己从墙上撑了起来，他的动作让潘西和卢娜停止说话，也转过身来看她。

“Well?” he asked. 
“嗯？”

Holding up the fistful of cards, Hermione gave him a weary smile. “A successful evening. I have a great many follow-up meetings to arrange, you’ll be pleased to know.”
赫敏举起那摞捏的纸牌，疲惫地向他露出一个微笑。“一个成功的夜晚。我有很多后续会议要安排，你会很高兴知道的。

Nodding, Draco brushed down the front of his robes briskly. “I’m pleased that this entire thing wasn’t an utterly pointless exercise in stress, certainly.”
点点头，德拉科轻快地拂过他的长袍前襟。“我很高兴这整件事当然不是完全毫无意义的压力练习。”

Bristling, Hermione wrinkled her nose at Draco. “I didn’t ask for this, you know. You could stop acting like I’ve been a great burden on you when you took it upon yourself to do –”
赫敏勃然大怒，对德拉科皱了皱鼻子。“我不是要这个的，你知道的。你可别再表现得像我自己承担了——”

“I think you’ll find my father   –”
“我想你会找到我爸爸——”

“You know what I mean,” Hermione snapped. “You were more in the know than me, Malfoy.”
“你明白我的意思，”赫敏厉声说。“你比我更了解情况，马尔福。”

In the unsettled silence that fell between them, Pansy raised her eyebrows, her gaze travelling between Hermione’s raised shoulders and Malfoy’s clenched fists. “There is an energy here,” she finally said, looking to Luna for confirmation of her body language reading. “Nargles?”
在他们之间不安的沉默中，潘西扬起眉毛，她的目光在赫敏抬起的肩膀和马尔福紧握的拳头之间来回扫视。“这里有一种能量，”她终于说，看向卢娜，以确认她的肢体语言阅读。“纳格尔斯？”

“No,” Luna replied blithely, gently shaking her head so that her long blonde hair fell across her shoulder and hid her shaking radish earrings. “The room’s quite clear. Someone’s been very thorough.”
“不，”卢娜轻快地回答，轻轻摇头，让她的金发长垂在肩膀上，藏住了她颤抖的萝卜耳环。“房间里很空。有人做得非常彻底。

“Just regular weirdness, then,” Pansy said, with an increased confidence that said that was her area of expertise. “Ignore him, Granger,” she continued, sparing Hermione a dismissive glance. “He’s been a right grump and done nothing but stare at that door since his mother left through it. Positively edible.”
“那么，就只是普通的怪异，”潘西说，信心增强，说那是她的专业领域。“别理他，格兰杰，”她继续说，不屑地瞥了赫敏一眼。“自从他妈妈离开那扇门后，他就一直脾气暴躁，除了盯着那扇门什么也没做。肯定可以食用。

“Head-a-ball,” Luna interjected softly, putting a hand on Pansy’s arm. 
“头球，”Luna轻声打断，将一只手放在Pansy的手臂上。

“ Oedipal ,” Hermione instinctively corrected them both, giving them a perturbed frown before turning back to Draco. “She hasn’t come back, then?” she asked quietly, not hiding her concern. His eyes cut down to hers and he shook his head, his face stony.
“俄狄浦斯，”赫敏本能地纠正了他们俩，让他们不安地皱了皱眉，然后转身看向德拉科。“那么，她还没回来吗？”她轻声问道，毫不掩饰她的担忧。他的眼睛盯着她，摇了摇头，脸色凝固。

“I’m sure it’ll be fine, Granger,” he eventually said on a sigh, running a hand through his hair despite the fact that it was sitting quite neatly. “They’ve not spoken in a long time but they’re grown-ups, y’know. I really don’t think there’s anything you – we – need to worry about.”
“我相信会没事的，格兰杰，”他最终叹了口气说，尽管他的头发已经相当整齐地坐着了。“他们已经很久没有说话了，但他们已经长大了，你知道的。我真的认为你——我们——不需要担心任何事情。

Frowning, Pansy placed a hand on her hip and tipped her head. “Wait a minute, why would Granger care if your mother and father are speaking –”
潘西皱着眉头，将一只手放在她的臀部上，歪着头。“等一下，格兰杰为什么在乎你爸爸妈妈在说话——”

“Absolutely nothing about this conversation is any of your business, Pansy,” Draco said shortly. “Keep quiet and don’t annoy me any more this evening; I’ve had quite enough of babysitting you.”
“这次谈话绝对不关你的事，潘西，”德拉科很快说。“别吵，今晚不要再惹我生气了;我已经受够了照顾你。

Drawing back, Pansy flattened an offended hand to her chest. “Well excuse me but I am in this conversation –”
潘西向后退，将一只被冒犯的手压在她的胸前。“嗯，对不起，我正在谈话——”

“Because you bloody inserted yourself into it. As you always have –”
“因为你把自己血腥地去了。就像你一直以来的——”

“Why does Granger care?” Pansy pressed, her petulant insistence making her nostrils flare.
“格兰杰为什么在乎？”潘西紧紧逼着，她任性的坚持让她的鼻孔张开。

“Pansy –”
“潘西——”

“What, is she shagging one of them now that they’re not together?” Pansy performatively gasped and then, voice lowered, she leaned in like they were sharing some great secret. “Is that why they’re not together?” 
“什么，既然他们不在一起了，她又要和他们中的一个上床吗？”潘西表演性地喘息着，然后，她压低了声音，俯身，就像他们在分享什么伟大的秘密一样。“这就是他们不在一起的原因吗？”

It struck Hermione that Pansy had been looking for perhaps the most shocking thing that she could think of in order to prompt Draco to tell her what she wanted to know via a horrified correction. In doing so, she had landed not particularly far from the truth. 
赫敏突然意识到，潘西一直在寻找也许是她能想到的最令人震惊的事情，以便促使德拉科通过一个可怕的纠正来告诉她她想知道的事情。在这样做的过程中，她离真相并不特别远。

“Pansy, please stop ,” Hermione finally said, spying the angry, telling pink that was rising in Draco’s cheeks. It was similar to what happened to his father and the last thing they needed was a scene on this particular subject matter when the room was beginning to clear out just enough that raised voices might echo. “It’s absolutely nothing to do with –”
“潘西，请停下来，”赫敏终于说了，窥探着德拉科脸颊上浮现的愤怒和告诉她的粉红色。这和他父亲的遭遇很相似，他们最不需要的就是这个特定主题的场景，当时房间里开始清理干净，刚好让高声的声音回荡。“这绝对和——”

“Mum or dad, Granger?” Pansy asked, a wicked, teasing grin on her face. It was clear she thought she was just annoying them, that she didn’t actually believe –
“妈妈还是爸爸，格兰杰？”潘西问道，脸上露出邪恶的、挑逗的笑容。很明显，她认为她只是在惹恼他们，她实际上并不相信——

“Dad,” Luna said with a factual simplicity that made everyone freeze and look at her. In response, Luna looked back into the room towards something that clearly interested her more than the conversation that was taking place between her girlfriend and friends. 
“爸爸，”Luna 以一种事实简单的方式说，让每个人都僵住了，看着她。作为回应，Luna 回头看向房间，显然比她的女朋友和朋友之间的对话更让她感兴趣。

In the still quiet, a frighteningly delighted smile slowly spread across Pansy’s narrow, pale face. Her teeth were dazzlingly white and, Hermione noticed, her incisors were appropriately sharp. “Granger, you dirty bitch . I’d never have thought you had it in you. Are you really?”
在一片寂静中，潘西狭窄而苍白的脸上缓缓地露出了可怕的喜悦笑容。她的牙齿洁白得令人眼花缭乱，赫敏注意到，她的门牙也相当锋利。“格兰杰，你这个肮脏的婊子......我从来没想过你有这种能力。你真的吗？

“No!” Hermione insisted, her voice high, just as Luna said “Yes” without looking around. 
“不！”赫敏坚持着，她的声音很高，就像卢娜没有环顾四周地说“是”。

“Luna!” Hermione yelped breathlessly. How did she know? How did Luna know bloody anything? To what other world was she connected and why did it sometimes make her say utterly bonkers nonsense and other times make her so insightful as to be practically oracular?
“露娜！”赫敏气喘吁吁地喊道。她是怎么知道的？露娜是怎么知道什么的？她与另一个世界相连，为什么有时让她说出完全疯狂的废话，有时又让她如此有洞察力，以至于几乎可以口齿伶俐？

“Oh.” Luna glanced around absently, blinking at Hermione like a confused owl. “I’m sorry, Hermione, are you not telling people yet? I thought it was obvious.”
“哦。”卢娜心不在焉地环顾四周，像一只困惑的猫头鹰一样向赫敏眨了眨眼。“对不起，赫敏，你还没告诉别人吗？我认为这是显而易见的。

Spluttering, Hermione looked imploringly at Draco only to find that he had utterly checked out of the conversation and dropped back against the wall, his eyes closed and his chin raised above the squabble taking place several inches below his eye line.
赫敏啪啪啪地恳求地看着德拉科，却发现他已经完全退出了谈话，向后靠在墙上，闭着眼睛，下巴抬高，高于发生在他视线以下几英寸处的争吵。

“I wouldn’t – we’re not telling – it’s not – nothing’s happening ,” Hermione finally managed to say. 
“我不会——我们不是说——不是——什么都没发生，”赫敏终于开口了。

“No, I can see it,” Pansy said, running a narrow-eyed, assessing glance up and down Hermione. “I can see why you’d get off on his whole hoity-toity, better-than-everyone attitude. That was your thing at school, after all, wasn’t –”
“不，我能看到，”潘西说，眯起眼睛，上下打量着赫敏。“我明白为什么你会对他整个圣洁、比每个人都好的态度感到厌烦。那是你在学校里的事，毕竟不是——”

“Pansy, that’s not very nice at all,” Luna said reprovingly, turning towards them to reveal that a frown was creasing her smooth forehead. Pansy shrunk somewhat, a guilty shade passing over her face.
“三色堇，那一点也不好，”露娜责备地说，转身看向他们，露出她光滑的额头上皱起了眉头。潘西稍微缩了缩，一丝愧疚的阴影掠过她的脸。

“Sorry, Granger,” Pansy mumbled to a wide-eyed Hermione – a Hermione who looked like she was quite close to fainting. There was a pause and then, with a surreptitious glance at Draco, Pansy asked quietly, “Is he good, though? A part of me always sort of wondered, y’know, if you got past the uptightness, with the really stern –”
“对不起，格兰杰，”潘西对睁大眼睛的赫敏喃喃自语——一个看起来快要晕倒的赫敏了。停顿了一下，然后，偷偷地瞥了一眼德拉科，潘西轻声问道，“不过，他好吗？我的一部分总是在想，你知道的，你是不是克服了紧张，真的严厉了——”

“ Enough ,” Draco snapped, finally rejoining the conversation with a fierce look that made Pansy press her lips together to suppress a laugh. “Pansy, stop this. There’s nothing –”
“够了，”德拉科厉声说，终于以一种凶狠的眼神重新加入了谈话，这让潘西紧紧地抿着嘴唇，压制住了笑声。“潘西，住手。什么都没有——”

“That anyone else needs to know,” Pansy finished for him, with a stage-wink in a very pink Hermione’s direction. “Got you.” Reaching for Luna’s hand, Pansy entwined their fingers and began dawdling away. 
“其他人都需要知道的，”潘西替他说完，朝粉红色的赫敏的方向眨了眨眼。“抓住你了。”潘西伸手抓住卢娜的手，缠住了他们的手指，开始蹒跚而行。

“Thanks for a lovely evening, Hermione and Draco,” Luna said pleasantly as she drifted away with Pansy, clearly oblivious to the fact that she had dropped a conversational bomb. “It’s always nice to be with friends.”
“谢谢你这个美好的夜晚，赫敏和德拉科，”卢娜和潘西一起渐行渐远时愉快地说，显然忘记了她已经投下了一枚谈话炸弹的事实。“和朋友在一起总是很高兴。”

“New respect, Granger,” Pansy said over her shoulder. “Shite night but thanks for the invite.”
“新的尊重，格兰杰，”潘西转过头说。“晚上真糟糕，但谢谢你的邀请。”

“She’s a right delight, isn’t she?” came Ginny’s dry voice to Hermione’s right, making her jump. “I still say Luna’s a million times too good for her.” 
“她真是个高兴的人，不是吗？”金妮干涩的声音传到赫敏的右边，让她跳了起来。“我仍然说 Luna 对她来说太好了一百万倍。”

Hermione turned to Ginny, still gaping at the interaction she had just had with Luna and Pansy. “Well, I’m not going to say that to Luna , obviously,” Ginny hurriedly assured her, misreading her expression. 
赫敏转向金妮，仍然对她刚刚与卢娜和潘西的互动目瞪口呆。“嗯，显然，我不会对卢娜说这些，”金妮急忙向她保证，误读了她的表情。

“Are you alright, Hermione?” asked Neville, who had joined Ginny and was squinting at Hermione’s pale face with concern. “You look like you’ve just had a round with a Boggart.”
“你还好吗，赫敏？”纳威问道，他已经加入了金妮的行列，关切地眯着眼睛看着赫敏苍白的脸。“你看起来就像刚刚和博格特打了一轮比赛。”

“She’s tired,” Draco grumbled. 
“她累了，”德拉科抱怨道。

“Not the only one apparently,” Ginny quipped, noting Malfoy’s brusque tone with a raised brow. 
“显然不是唯一一个，”金妮打趣道，注意到马尔福粗鲁的语气和扬起的眉毛。

“It’s been a long night,” he replied through gritted teeth. “With some surprises.”
“这是一个漫长的夜晚，”他咬牙切齿地回答。“有一些惊喜。”

“Yes,” Ginny said, her raised brow lowering into a thoughtful frown, “I thought I saw your –” 
“是的，”金妮说，她扬起的眉毛低垂成若有所思的眉头，“我以为我看到了你的——”

But whatever Ginny had seen, she didn’t say any more. Instead, her eyes drifted back to the shell-shocked Hermione and her frown deepened. 
但无论金妮看到了什么，她都没有再说什么。相反，她的目光又回到了震惊的赫敏身上，她的眉头皱得更深了。

“Maybe it’s time to go, Hermione. Harry and Ron are just getting our cloaks. We’re going to carry on at Godric’s Hollow if you want to join – Ron and Neville have a lot of catching up to do.” Seeing Hermione’s hesitation, Ginny gave her an encouraging smile and added, “It’s been a while since we had a catch-up, too. A real in-depth one, y’know?”
“也许是时候走了，赫敏。哈利和罗恩刚刚拿到我们的斗篷。如果你想加入，我们会继续在 Godric's Hollow 工作——Ron 和 Neville 还有很多事情要做。看到赫敏的犹豫，金妮给了她一个鼓励的微笑，并补充道：“我们也已经有一段时间没有见面了。一个真正深入的，你知道吗？

“I – I think I might just stay here a while longer, Gin,” Hermione said, glancing up at Draco who shot her a surprised look. “Help clean up, say thanks, that sort of thing.” Understanding flitted across Draco’s face and he nodded quietly, picking up on exactly why Hermione wanted to stay.
“我——我想我可能会在这里多呆一会儿，金，”赫敏说，抬头瞥了一眼德拉科，德拉科惊讶地看了她一眼。“帮忙打扫卫生，说声谢谢，诸如此类的事情。”德拉科的脸上闪过一丝理解，他悄悄地点了点头，明白了赫敏想要留下来的确切原因。

For a painful moment, Hermione thought Ginny was going to argue but, though her mouth opened and she drew in a preparatory breath, Ginny somehow found it in herself to close it and nod. Giving Hermione a look that made her feel like she was a valuable object being assessed for damage, Ginny said, “Alright. Well, come by later. Even if it’s late. Please.”
有那么一刻，赫敏以为金妮要争论了，但是，尽管她张开了嘴，准备吸一口气，但金妮不知怎么地发现自己想闭上嘴巴，点了点头。金妮看了赫敏一眼，让她觉得自己是一个正在接受损坏评估的贵重物品，她说，“好吧。好吧，稍后再来。即使已经很晚了。拜托了。

Nodding, Hermione gave Ginny and Neville a tight smile but made no promises; she couldn’t be sure how long she’d be with Lucius, if Narcissa wasn’t still with him. Aside from Narcissa, she and Lucius had to discuss Kingsley. And if Narcissa was still there, Hermione wasn’t entirely sure what her next move was.
赫敏点点头，对金妮和纳威露出一个紧绷的笑容，但没有做出任何承诺;她不确定如果纳西莎还不在他身边，她会和卢修斯在一起多久。除了纳西莎，她和卢修斯还得讨论金斯利。如果纳西莎还在，赫敏并不完全确定她的下一步行动是什么。

“Cheers for the night out, Malfoy,” Ginny said more loudly to Draco. But Draco wasn’t looking at her - he had turned to Neville and cleared his throat, his hands folded behind his back and Hermione could see him squeezing his own fingers. 
“为今晚的演出干杯，马尔福，”金妮对德拉科大声说。但德拉科没有看她——他转向纳威，清了清嗓子，双手交叉在背后，赫敏可以看到他正在挤压自己的手指。

“Thank you for the Dittany, by the way, Longbottom,” Draco said stiffly, looking everywhere but at Neville’s face until he absolutely couldn’t avoid it. “Very good of you.”
“顺便说一句，谢谢你，隆巴顿，”德拉科僵硬地说，四处张望，只看着纳威的脸，直到他完全无法避免。“你真好。”

Hermione watched Neville’s eyes widen as he looked into Malfoy’s face, his throat jumping as he swallowed. Neville studied Malfoy for a second but perhaps he saw sincerity where once there might have been mockery because he finally smiled softly and shrugged like it had been nothing. “Got loads at Hogwarts. Just take good care of it.”
赫敏看着纳威睁大了眼睛看着马尔福的脸，他的喉咙在吞咽时跳动。纳威端详了马尔福一会儿，但也许他看到了真诚，而曾经可能会有嘲笑的地方，因为他终于温柔地笑了笑，耸了耸肩，仿佛什么都没发生过。“在霍格沃茨吃了很多东西。好好照顾它就好了。

They said their goodbyes and Hermione waved from her place by Draco’s side, sending her love to Harry and Ron through Ginny and Neville. 
他们道别了，赫敏从德拉科身边的位置上挥手致意，通过金妮和纳威向哈利和罗恩表达了她的爱。

“Might have been better to go with them, you know,” Draco said under his breath to Hermione as he nodded his goodbyes to other guests. “Enjoy the rest of your night and come back tomorrow.”
“和他们一起去可能会更好，你知道的，”德拉科低声对赫敏说，同时向其他客人点头告别。“享受你剩下的夜晚，明天再来。”

Shaking her head, Hermione looked up at him. “This whole thing was for me,” she said. “I’ll see it out.” 
赫敏摇了摇头，抬头看着他。“这整件事都是为了我，”她说。“我去看看。”

Together, she and Draco stationed themselves by the door of the ballroom and said their thank yous and goodbyes to everyone as they passed.  When the last guests finally departed, leaning on one another for support after one too many glasses of champagne, a relieved exhale escaped Draco, his entire body seeming to deflate, as the door closed with a resounding clang behind them.
她和德拉科一起站在舞厅的门口，在他们经过时向每个人道谢和告别。当最后几位客人终于离开时，在喝了太多杯香槟后，他们互相依靠着彼此寻求支持，德拉科松了一口气，他的整个身体似乎都泄了气，门在他们身后发出响亮的叮当声关上了。

“Thank Merlin,” he said, rubbing a hand across his tired eyes. “Do you know, I think all the years I’ve spent in this manor have turned me into a bit of a recluse. Every single one of those people was somehow equal parts exhausting and uninteresting.”
“谢谢Merlin，”他说，用一只手揉了揉他疲惫的眼睛。“你知道吗，我觉得我在这座庄园里度过的这些年已经把我变成了一个有点隐居的人。那些人中的每一个人在某种程度上都同样令人筋疲力尽且无趣。

Not entirely listening, Hermione hummed noncommittally, prompting Draco to make an irritated scoffing sound in the back of his throat. “Just go, Granger,” he said, waving a hand in the direction of the door. “Your mind is already up there with him so your body might as well follow.”
赫敏没有完全听进去，漫不经心地哼了一声，这让德拉科的喉咙后部发出了恼怒的嘲讽声。“走吧，格兰杰，”他说，朝门的方向挥了挥手。“你的思想已经和他在一起了，所以你的身体也跟着走。”

“No,” Hermione insisted, shaking her head to bring herself back into the room. “I’m sorry, Malfoy, I want to help you sort this –” Hermione looked around the ballroom, seeing cocktail tables littered with canapés and empty glasses every few feet and waved a weak hand. “This.”
“不，”赫敏坚持说，摇了摇头，让自己回到房间里。“对不起，马尔福，我想帮你解决这个问题——”赫敏环顾宴会厅，看到每隔几英尺就堆满了小吃和空杯子的鸡尾酒桌，无力地挥了挥手。“这个。”

“Don’t be ridiculous, Letty will get this.” On seeing the frown developing on Hermione’s face, Draco raised a hand. “Don’t even start. I’m not going to make an arduous evening worse by insulting my elf because of your inability to just leave something. Go. I won’t be offended.”
“别荒谬，Letty会明白的。”看到赫敏脸上皱起的眉头，德拉科举起了一只手。“甚至不要开始。我不会因为你无法留下什么而侮辱我的精灵，从而让一个艰难的夜晚变得更糟。去。我不会生气的。

Hesitating on the spot, Hermione took in his uncompromising expression and finally relented with a nod. “Alright, fine. Thank you, Malfoy.” Hermione swept a hand out. “For this, obviously. But for…well, you know.”
赫敏当场犹豫了一下，接受了他毫不妥协的表情，最后点了点头。“好吧，好吧。谢谢你，马尔福。赫敏伸出一只手。“显然，为了这个。但是为了......嗯，你知道的。

Malfoy nodded to indicate that he did, indeed, know, and as Hermione turned to go, he cleared his throat. Pausing mid-step, Hermione half-turned back to him, the size of the ballroom making the distance between them feel larger than it actually was.
马尔福点点头表示他确实知道，当赫敏转身要走时，他清了清嗓子。赫敏在半步中停了下来，半转身回到他身边，舞厅的大小让他们之间的距离感觉比实际更大。

“Granger,” he said, cupping the back of his neck and looking away from her, a grimace on his face. “Look, if I’m being completely honest with you, I’d really rather they were still together. If it were up to me – not that anything ever seems to be – they would be.”
“格兰杰，”他说，搂着他的后颈，把目光从她身上移开，脸上露出愁苦的表情。“听着，如果我对你完全诚实，我真的宁愿他们还是在一起。如果由我决定——并不是说任何事情似乎都不是——他们会的。

Hermione swallowed hard, a sinking, guilty feeling descending into the pit of her stomach. 
赫敏用力咽了口口水，一股沉沦的、内疚的感觉涌入了她的胃深处。

“But…” Draco continued, glancing back at her with a puzzled sort of frown. “But they’re not. They haven’t been for a while. My mother seemed to be incapable of saying the right thing to him after the war –”
“但是......”德拉科继续说，回头瞥了她一眼，带着一种困惑的皱眉。“但他们不是。他们已经有一段时间没有了。战后我妈妈似乎没能力对他说正确的话——”

“Malfoy –”
“马尔福——”

Draco ignored her. “I don’t think that was her fault. I don’t even know if it was his. Maybe it doesn’t need to be anyone’s, I don’t know. Feels a bit pointless to assign blame now.” He sighed, tipping his head back and closing his eyes. “I don’t know the details and I really don’t want to – like, really – but you’ve done something right with him these past few months and I…I appreciate it.”
德拉科没有理会她。“我不认为那是她的错。我什至不知道是不是他的。也许它不需要是任何人的，我不知道。现在归咎于感觉有点没意义。他叹了口气，把头向后仰，闭上了眼睛。“我不知道细节，我真的不想——就像，真的——但你在过去几个月里对他做了一些正确的事情，我......我很感激。

“I…see,” Hermione said somewhat pathetically, not sure of what the right words were.
“我......看，“赫敏有点可怜地说，不确定该怎么说。

Malfoy’s responding smile was wry. “No, you don’t. Not really. That’s fine, though.”
马尔福的回应是苦笑。“不，你不需要。没有。不过，这没关系。

“What are you trying to say, Malfoy?” Hermione asked, wishing that just once a Malfoy could be straightforward.
“你想说什么，马尔福？”赫敏问道，希望马尔福能简单明了一次。

His shoulders jumped up in a chuckle and he shoved his hands into his pockets. “I’m saying , Granger, that…I suppose I’m saying that I don’t mind that you’re the one going up there.” Draco’s eyes swept the room, taking in the mess with a dispassionate air. “There’s only so much me, Astoria and a house elf can do, I guess.”
他的肩膀咯咯地笑着跳起来，双手口袋里。“我是说，格兰杰，那个......我想我是说，我不介意你是上去的人。德拉科的眼睛扫视着房间，以一种冷静的气氛观察着这片混乱。“我猜，我、阿斯托利亚和一个家养小精灵能做的就这么多了。”

Hermione wanted to assure Malfoy that she hadn’t done any more or any better than him; that the years he’d spent backing his father had been worth far more than the few months she’d spent with him; that Lucius would be just as happy, perhaps better off, having him at that moment instead of her; that she was sorry about his parents.
赫敏想向马尔福保证，她并没有比他做得更多或更好;他支持他父亲的岁月，远比她和他在一起的几个月更有价值;卢修斯也会同样高兴，也许会更好，因为那一刻有他而不是她;她对他的父母感到抱歉。

Before she could, however, he met her eyes. “I’m saying it’s good to have someone else that cares. Someone who doesn't ask why I'm still here.”
然而，在她来得及之前，他与她的眼睛相遇了。“我是说有其他人关心真是太好了。一个不问我为什么还在这里的人。

Swallowing down her words, Hermione offered him a smile, a warm feeling of acceptance tingling through her. He didn’t need reassurances; he was giving them.
赫敏吞下她的话，向他微笑，一种温暖的接纳感在她身上刺痛。他不需要安慰;他给了他们。

“Right,” Draco said gruffly, nodding his head at the door. “Go. You need to get out before I call Letty – she’ll have kittens if she knows you’ve seen the ballroom in such a state.”
“好吧，”德拉科粗鲁地说，对着门口点了点头。“走吧。在我打电话给莱蒂之前，你得出去——如果她知道你见过这种状态的舞厅，她就会养小猫的。

Hermione’s first knock on Lucius’ study door was soft to the point of being inaudible but the longer she waited for a response, the more firm she became until there was a stinging in her knuckles. She was just considering turning her hand on its side to beat the wood when a voice stopped her.
赫敏第一次敲响卢修斯书房的门，轻柔到听不见，但她等待回应的时间越长，她就越坚定，直到指关节发出刺痛。她正想把手转过来敲打木头，这时一个声音阻止了她。

“I wondered if you’d be by.”
“我想知道你是否会在身边。”

Hermione paused, her hand hanging in the air and looked around. “Sabine?” It took turning on the spot for Hermione to finally find Sabine in the painting on the wall directly across from Lucius’ closed door. She was leaning on a low, crumbling stone wall, seemingly unbothered by the lamb that was curiously nibbling at the bottom of her robes.
赫敏停顿了一下，她的手悬在空中，环顾四周。“萨宾？”赫敏原地转过身来，终于在卢修斯紧闭的门对面墙上的画中找到了萨宾。她靠在一堵低矮、摇摇欲坠的石墙上，似乎对那只好奇地啃咬她袍子底部的小羊毫不在意。

“He’s not in there,” Sabine said simply.
“他不在那儿，”Sabine 简单地说。

“Whe –”
“哎呀——”

“He left,” she said. “Not long after her.”
“他走了，”她说。“不久之后。”

There was a pause in which Sabine studied Hermione, perhaps to see if ‘her’ meant anything or was of any significance. Of course, it did and it was, so Hermione met Sabine’s eyes and nodded her understanding.
萨宾停顿了一下，打量着赫敏，也许是想看看“她”有什么意义或意义。当然，确实如此，而且确实如此，所以赫敏对上了萨宾的眼睛，点头表示理解。

“How…how was he?” she asked.
“怎么......他怎么样？

Sabine’s eyes drifted upwards towards the cloudless blue skies above her, her mouth opening as she considered her next words. “Distracted,” she finally said, dropping her gaze to Hermione again. 
Sabine 的眼睛向上飘向头顶万里无云的蓝天，她张大了嘴巴，考虑着接下来的话。“分心了，”她终于说了，再次把目光投向赫敏。

Hermione sighed. “When was that?”
赫敏叹了口气。“那是什么时候？”

“We don’t really do time, dear,” Sabine said, gesturing to the perpetually sunlit wide open field of her portrait before she stooped to shoo the lamb away from her robes.
“我们真的没有时间，亲爱的，”Sabine说，指着她画像上永远阳光明媚的开阔场地，然后弯腰把小羊从她的长袍上赶走。

“Well, if you had to guess ?”
“嗯，如果你必须猜的话？”

“An hour ago,” Sabine estimated, straightening up and placing her hands on her hips. “Maybe two.”
“一个小时前，”Sabine 估计着，直起身来，双手放在臀部上。“也许两个。”

“他去哪儿了？”对他来说，去温室或狗窝已经太晚了，赫敏确信他不会把自己藏在厨房里，因为庄园的那一边有客人和傲罗。

“Upstairs,” Sabine said. “To his room.” 
“在楼上，”Sabine 说。“到他的房间去。”

It was so odd to Hermione that the study was not Lucius’ room. It was so…him. Was there, in fact, a room that was more him? Apparently so. And apparently it was on a floor of the manor that she hadn’t even visited.
赫敏觉得太奇怪了，书房不是卢修斯的房间。太......他。事实上，有没有一个房间更像他？显然是这样。显然，那是在庄园的一层楼上，她甚至都没去过。

“Can you take me?” To Hermione’s surprise, Sabine looked almost hesitant and she wondered if it was for Lucius’ sake or her own. When no reply was forthcoming, Hermione added, “Please, Sabine”, her tone appealing.
“你能带我走吗？”令赫敏惊讶的是，萨宾看起来几乎犹豫不决，她想知道这是为了卢修斯还是为了她自己。当没有人回答时，赫敏又说了一句，“拜托了，萨宾”，她的语气很吸引人。

Absently rubbing her hand over the rough stone of the wall, Sabine assessed Hermione, her lips pursed. After a moment, she sighed. “Very well. You can hardly make things worse, can you?”
萨宾心不在焉地用手在粗糙的石头上摩擦，抿着嘴唇打量着赫敏。过了一会儿，她叹了口气。“很好。你几乎不会让事情变得更糟，对吧？

Dusting specks of dirt from her palm, Sabine lifted her robes slightly and turned, jerking her head to invite Hermione to follow. “Come on, then. It’s not far.”
萨宾掸去手掌上的泥土，微微掀起她的长袍，转过身来，猛地摇头让赫敏跟上。“那么，来吧。不远。

Lucius was so lost in his thoughts that he didn’t hear the first knocks on his bedroom door. Then, when he did hear them, he didn’t bother to acknowledge them. Until they became so insistent and irritating that he was forced to push himself up into a sitting position on his bed and glare across the room in their direction. 
卢修斯沉浸在自己的思绪中，以至于他没有听到卧室门的第一声敲门声。然后，当他真的听到他们时，他懒得承认他们。直到他们变得如此坚持和恼怒，以至于他被迫在床上坐起来，瞪着房间对面他们的方向。

When that didn’t stop the incessant pounding, Lucius growled and rose to his feet, crossing the room in a few strides to haul the door open. His angry words died in his throat when he found Hermione standing there in a long black gown. He squinted at her, like he wasn’t entirely sure whether he was really seeing her. 
当这还没能阻止不断的敲击声时，卢修斯咆哮着站了起来，大步穿过房间，把门拉开了。当他发现赫敏穿着一件黑色长袍站在那里时，他的愤怒话语在喉咙里消失了。他眯着眼睛看着她，好像他不完全确定自己是否真的看到了她。

Lucius wasn’t sure why he hadn’t expected it to be her. He wasn’t even really sure who he’d expected. A returning Narcissa, perhaps, ready to give him a further dressing down. Or Letty bearing a plate with enough food for three and bleating about his missed dinner. To his dismay, Lucius found that, with Narcissa's words echoing in his mind, he wasn’t overjoyed to see Hermione. 
卢修斯不知道为什么他没想到会是她。他甚至不确定自己期待的是谁。也许，一个回归的纳西莎，准备让他进一步穿衣服。或者 Letty 拿着一个盘子，里面装满了足够三个人吃的食物，咆哮着说他错过了晚餐。令他沮丧的是，卢修斯发现，纳西莎的话在他的脑海中回荡，他看到赫敏并没有高兴。

Did Hermione know that Narcissa had been in the manor? Had she seen her in the ballroom as Narcissa had certainly seen her ? He wasn’t sure he wanted to have that discussion without sufficient time to process and prepare.
赫敏知道纳西莎一直在庄园里吗？她在舞厅里见过她，就像纳西莎肯定见过她一样吗？他不确定自己是否想在没有足够的时间来处理和准备的情况下进行这种讨论。

他一只手扶着门，另一只手靠在门框上，挡住了房间的入口。“赫敏，”他说，他的声音低沉而沉默。

“Let her in, Lucius,” came a firm voice from over Hermione’s head.
“让她进来，卢修斯，”赫敏的头顶传来一个坚定的声音。

卢修斯的眼睛猛地抬起，他透过走廊的黑暗，窥视着萨宾熟悉的蓝色长袍，里面是华丽的青铜框架。她当然插手了。他们都是无休止的多管闲事的人;最麻烦的一对。

“Don’t be a fool,” Sabine added, her voice sharp. 
“别当傻瓜，”Sabine 补充道，她的声音尖锐。

Unwilling to embroil himself in what was sure to be a demeaning argument, Lucius swallowed a petulant retort, dropped his hand from the door frame and grunted. Turning back into the room, he left the door ajar for Hermione to follow him. The sound of quiet shuffling and the soft click of the door closing confirmed that she did.
卢修斯不愿卷入这场肯定会是贬低性的争论中，他吞下了一句娇气的反驳，把手从门框上放下来，咕哝了一声。他转身回到房间，把门半开着，让赫敏跟着他。安静的拖曳声和关门的轻柔咔嗒声证实了她确实如此。

他大步跨过房间苍白的石头地板，在最右边墙壁上的一个巨大的白色梳妆台前停了下来。他一直喝的那瓶火威士忌空空如也地躺在瓶子上，卢修斯毫无意义地戳了戳瓶子，然后对上了镜子里他自己那只略带血丝的眼睛。

He looked tired and drawn, his clothes crumpled and messy from his time spent lying down. One bloody encounter with Narcissa and he’d crumbled. He gave himself a disgusted look and attempted to straighten himself back up. As he did, he spied Hermione’s reflection facing him from the middle of the room. 
他看起来疲惫不堪，疲惫不堪，他的衣服因躺着的时间而皱巴巴的，凌乱不堪。与纳西莎的一次血腥相遇，他崩溃了。他厌恶地看了自己一眼，试图让自己站直。当他这样做的时候，他从房间中央看到了赫敏面对他的倒影。

清了清嗓子，他转向她，试图向她提供一个近乎微笑的东西，但没有与她的眼睛对上。这看起来不可能很真诚，因为她看起来完全不舒服，几乎是紧张的。他已经很久没有看到她在他面前如此不安了。

How long, Lucius, before you realise that you’re just going to ruin her life by association in the way that you apparently so feared you were ruining mine?
Lucius，你要多久才会意识到，你只会因为交往而毁掉她的生活，就像你显然如此担心你毁了我的生活一样？

“嗯，”他生硬地开始说，停下来清了清嗓子。“进展如何？”

Unable to meet her eyes, he allowed his gaze to settle on her fidgeting hands, which were pressed together in front of her at waist level. 
由于无法与她的眼睛对视，他的目光落在她坐立不安的手上，这双手在她的腰部齐平。

I got plenty of business cards and –” Hermione held out a hand and revealed to him that she’d been fidgeting with the cards. They'd left faint red marks on her palms where she'd been clutching them too tightly.
“事情进展得......好吧，“她犹豫地说，看着他紧张的姿势。然后，他更加自信地说，“进展顺利。我有很多名片，而且——“赫敏伸出一只手，向他透露她一直在摆弄这些名片。它们在她的手掌上留下了淡淡的红色痕迹，她把它们攥得太紧了。

赫敏似乎找到了更多的确定性，她穿过房间向他走来，伸出了手。卢修斯接过递来的名片，再次没有看她的脸，翻阅了一下，停顿在那些更熟悉的名字上。

“一些很好的人脉，”他喃喃自语。“至少，并非全是完全无用的。”卢修斯把卡片放在梳妆台上，半转身离开她，看着镜子。

“不，我不是，”赫敏皱着眉头说。“虽然我完全在我的权利范围内，你知道的。”

Lucius scoffed softly and shook his head. Of course he knew it. "Then why are you here?"
卢修斯轻声嘲笑，摇了摇头。他当然知道。“那你为什么在这里？”

"Why am I –" Hermione stopped herself and he thought he heard her attempt to swallow down some irritation. "Why are you being so bloody rude ?" Whatever irritation she had managed to swallow, she spat back up with that last word.
“我为什么——”赫敏停下了脚步，他觉得他听到了她试图压制住一些恼怒。“你怎么这么粗鲁？”无论她设法吞下了什么恼怒，她还是用最后一个字吐了出来。

“我只是我自己，如果你觉得这太难受了，那——”

"No, you're not," Hermione snapped. "If you were being yourself you'd look at me properly."
“不，你不是，”赫敏厉声说。“如果你做你自己，你会好好看着我。”

Perhaps you feel like her kindness, her affection, is some kind of absolution?
也许你觉得她的善良，她的爱，是某种赦免？

Lucius’ shoulders dropped and he tapped a finger on the surface of the vanity once, twice, before he finally looked up and met her eyes in the mirror. She stared back, unblinking, and he was reminded of just how much of an unyielding Gryffindor she was – she would sooner bite his head off than let him slither around or away from her.
卢修斯的肩膀垂下来，他用手指在梳妆台的表面敲了一下，两次，最后他抬起头来，与镜子里的她对上了眼睛。她回头凝视着，一眨不眨，这让他想起了她是多么不屈不挠的格兰芬多——她宁愿咬掉他的头，也不愿让他溜达或远离她。

She will not restore you. You will most likely ruin her and you are deluded if you think she will be willing to languish in this manor as I was.
她不会让你恢复的。你很可能会毁了她，如果你认为她会愿意像我一样在这个庄园里煎熬，那你就是被骗了。

“Properly, Lucius,” she said, her voice softer but still firm. 
“没错，卢修斯，”她说，她的声音更柔和但仍然坚定。

卢修斯用鼻子深吸一口气，转向赫敏。他慢慢地顺着她黑色礼服的丝绸向上看，在卧室昏暗的烛光下，这件礼服在她精致的锁骨上，看起来像湿漉漉的焦油，直到他遇到了她温暖的棕色眼睛。

他们和纳西莎的截然不同，以至于他停了一会儿。他看得越久，就越感到安慰。他感到足够安慰，从梳妆台上走到她身边，当她没有离开时，他松了一口气。一到她身边，他就用一只温柔的手顺着她的臀部曲线滑下。当他接触时，她的身体轻轻地颤抖了一下。

A man apparently so afraid that his wife might hate him that he couldn’t bear to give her the chance to love him.
这个男人显然非常害怕他的妻子会恨他，以至于他不忍心给她爱他的机会。

Lucius could admit that he wasn't especially good at seeing mistakes as he was making them but continuing to exhibit reticence towards a witch who did not deserve it felt like one. One he had made before. 
卢修斯可以承认，他并不是特别擅长看到他所犯的错误，但继续对一个不值得的女巫保持沉默感觉就像一个。他以前做过。

"How's this?" he asked, his eyes unwavering on hers. 
“怎么样？” 他问道，眼睛坚定不移地盯着她。

"Better," she said, her voice barely above a whisper. 
“好多了，”她说，她的声音勉强算是耳语。

“You look lovely,” he said, his volume lowering to matching hers. "Perhaps I should have started with that."
“你看起来很可爱，”他说，他的音量降低到与她的音量相匹配。“也许我应该从那个开始。”

“谢谢你，”赫敏说，听起来有些僵硬，就像她在克制住继续忍受他先前的粗鲁的冲动。“不过这主要归功于你的儿子。”

想起纳西莎的嘲讽，卢修斯微微皱起眉头，他用拇指滑过赫敏腰部垂下的裙子，指尖压在她的臀部。“这真的是睡裙吗？”

赫敏不舒服地动了动，耸了耸肩，但她并没有从他的触碰中抽身。“是的。就像我说的，功劳是你儿子的功劳。他在织物变形方面出奇的熟练。

“You really have no other formalwear?”
“你真的没有别的正装吗？”

“I don’t have a need for it.”
“我不需要它。”

Hermione’s lip curled in an almost comical fashion, like he’d just place something particularly foul-smelling in front of her. “I have no interest in you buying me things,” she said. “My clothes are fine.”
赫敏的嘴唇以一种近乎滑稽的方式卷曲，就像他只是在她面前放了什么特别难闻的东西。“我对你给我买东西没兴趣，”她说。“我的衣服很好。”

Lucius had never thought Hermione was interested in access to his vault but hearing her reject his offer with such clear disgust made a flash of relief pass through him, alongside some vindictive satisfaction that Narcissa was wrong. About that, at least. 
卢修斯从来没有想过赫敏对进入他的金库感兴趣，但听到她以如此明显的厌恶拒绝他的提议，他心中闪过一丝宽慰，同时对纳西莎错了感到报复性的满足。至少是这样。

“The offer is always there,” he said. 
“报价一直在那里，”他说。

“I didn’t come here to speak to you about my wardrobe, Lucius.”
“我来这里不是为了和你谈我的衣橱，卢修斯。”

“What else could we possibly have to talk about?” he asked, trying to sound flippant as he closed the small amount of space left between them and encircled her waist with his arms. 
“我们还能谈什么呢？”他问道，一边拉近他们之间剩下的一点空间，一边用手臂环住她的腰，尽量显得轻率。

Hermione’s eyes creased at the corners as she narrowed them and looked up at him. She could, he was sure, see right through the fact that he was attempting to avoid whatever she had in mind for him, whether it was conversation or confrontation. He’d had his fill of difficult discussions for one evening.
赫敏的眼睛在眼角上皱起，眯起眼睛，抬头看着他。他确信，她能看穿他试图避免她对他心中的一切，无论是对话还是对抗。他已经度过了一个晚上的艰难讨论。

“其实挺多的事——”她的声音沙哑停顿了一下，她低头看着他一只手顺着她手臂柔软的皮肤滑上去，用一根手指勾住了她裙子的带子下面。“他们很重要。”

“真的吗？”卢修斯扬起眉毛，假装感兴趣地伸出下嘴唇，轻轻拉扯她裙子的带子，让它从她的肩膀上掉下来。

“是吗？” 他问道，他的声音略微低沉地渗入了她的皮肤。

“I know what you’re doing.”
“我知道你在做什么。”

“You just did so terribly well this evening,’ he said. “I can’t help myself around such a clever, successful witch.”
“你今晚表现得太好了，”他说。我无法控制自己面对这样一个聪明、成功的女巫。

他把它涂得非常厚——到了不真诚的地步，他们都知道——但赫敏允许他继续，她的头微微低向一边，以便让他更好地接近她的脖子。

“我们为什么不在早上谈谈呢？”他大胆地提议道，抬起头低头看着她。

“我现在是来说话的，”她说，她的声音略显沙哑，因为她的眼睛颤抖着睁开，用一种毫不妥协的眼神注视着他。“我不会走的。”

“I didn’t suggest that you leave.”
“我没建议你走。”

‘You mean –”
“你是说——”

“Stay.”
“留下来。”

Pressing her lips together, Hermione glanced over to his large four poster bed that sat against the centre of the back wall of the room. He spotted a jump in her throat as she swallowed and turned back to him but she didn’t give him a response. Lucius raised a brow, tilting his head as he trailed his eyes down her. “You’re already in a nightdress…”
赫敏紧抿着嘴唇，瞥了一眼靠在房间后墙中央的那张四柱大床。当她咽咽并转身看向他时，他发现她的喉咙一跳，但她没有回应他。卢修斯扬起眉毛，歪着头，目光顺着她往下看。“你已经穿上了睡裙......”

Hermione snorted with unwilling amusement but the slight tilt to her brow told him that she still wasn’t convinced. 
赫敏不情愿地哼了一声，但她微微的眉头歪着告诉他，她还是不相信。

“If you’d prefer not –”
“如果你不想——”

“不，”她迅速插嘴。“不，不是那个。它。。。人们可能会想知道我在哪里。她尴尬地低头看着他们脚下的一小块地板。“如果我不在家。如果他们来看，就说。

People . People were her friends, he could only assume. Those she cared about. Those who might see her in a negative light through her association with him. Even if he didn’t want to ruin her, he couldn’t control the reactions of other people. 
人。人们就是她的朋友，他只能假设。那些她关心的人。那些可能会通过她与他的交往对她产生负面影响的人。就算他不想毁了她，他也控制不住别人的反应。

A sinking in his chest, Lucius attempted to steel himself but only managed to drum up something that felt closer to a sort of squashed resignation. “We don't need to carry on,” he said with as much dignity as he could muster. “We could stop this.”
卢修斯的胸口一沉，他试图让自己变得坚强起来，但只能设法鼓起一些感觉更接近于某种被压扁的顺从的东西。“我们不需要继续下去，”他尽可能地带着尊严说。“我们可以阻止这种情况。”

It wasn’t what he wanted by any means but, after everything Narcissa had said, he felt he ought to offer it up as an option. Now that others knew about their relationship, he had a sense that they were quickly approaching a crossroads where the paths were 'end it' or 'reveal it'. Secrecy was no longer an option.
这绝不是他想要的，但是，在纳西莎说了这么多之后，他觉得他应该把它作为一个选项。现在其他人都知道了他们的关系，他有一种感觉，他们很快就接近了一个十字路口，在那里，道路是 “结束它 ”或 “揭示它”。保密不再是一种选择。

After all the pain he had caused Hermione in the past – directly and indirectly – Lucius reluctantly acknowledged that he owed it to her to ensure that he didn’t cause her any more. Even if it did strike him as unfair that he was not allowed to engage with the outside world, yet still had to mind it.
在他过去直接或间接地给赫敏带来了所有痛苦之后，卢修斯不情愿地承认他欠她，以确保他不会再给她带来痛苦。即使他不被允许与外界接触确实让他觉得不公平，但仍然不得不介意它。

Hermione’s head snapped up and she gave him an alarmed look. “That's not what I want.”
赫敏猛地抬起头，警惕地看了他一眼。“那不是我想要的。”

"I'm sure that it isn't, right now."
“我确定现在不是。”

"Right now –?"
