赫敏猛地抬起眼睛与他对视，发现眼睛盯着她，一眨不眨。“你怎么可能知道？”

“I do believe I once told you that you’re easier to read than a book,” he said, a slightly mocking drawl to his voice. “It was written all over your face.” 
“我确实相信我曾经告诉你，你比读书更容易读，”他说，声音里带着些许嘲讽。“你脸上写满了。”

He offered her a smile but it was half-hearted and tired. “Perhaps I can guess,” he continued. “The Wizengamot has declined your request. Either my freedom will not be coming as soon as we hoped or…” He eyed her more closely and then sighed softly through his nose as he gleaned the truth from her discomfited expression. “It’s not coming at all.”
他向她微笑，但那是半心半意和疲惫的。“也许我能猜到，”他继续说。“威森加摩拒绝了你的请求。要么我的自由不会如我们所愿地到来，要么......”他更仔细地看着她，然后通过鼻子轻轻叹了口气，从她不安的表情中搜寻到真相。“它根本不会来。”

Reaching out, Hermione placed a hand on his arm nearest her, squeezing him. “I’m sorry, Lucius,” she said quietly. “I really am.”
赫敏伸出手，将一只手放在离她最近的手臂上，挤压着他。“对不起，卢修斯，”她轻声说。“我真的是。”

Lucius shifted, sighing heavily, but he didn’t draw his arm away from her touch. “Should I have expected anything else, I wonder?” he asked, sounding resigned. “Your magnanimity is, I think, exceptional."
卢修斯动了动身子，重重地叹了口气，但他没有把手臂从她的触碰上移开。“我想知道，我还能期待什么吗？” 他问道，听起来很无奈。“我认为，你的宽宏大量是非凡的。”

“The Wizengamot haven’t…they just haven’t spent the time with you like I have.”
“威森加摩还没有......他们只是没有像我一样花时间陪你。

Lucius’ smile was grim. “They’ve spent as much time with me as I think they’d ever want to,” he said. On seeing Hermione’s expectant, raised eyebrows, he added, “I was the man who filled their pockets with coins or their ears with threats. I wouldn’t be surprised if more than a few of them are still afraid, either of what I might do to them or what I could reveal about them.”
卢修斯的笑容很严肃。“他们花了我认为他们想花多少时间就花多少时间，”他说。看到赫敏期待地扬起眉毛，他补充道，“我就是那个把他们的口袋装满硬币，或者用威胁塞进他们的耳朵的人。如果他们中的一些人仍然害怕，无论是我可能会对他们做什么，还是我能透露关于他们的什么，我都不会感到惊讶。

“You could have mentioned you felt like that,” Hermione said, unable to keep some resentment from her voice. “I might have addressed it a little more directly in my letter to them.”
“你本来可以说你有那种感觉的，”赫敏说，她的声音里忍不住有些怨恨。“我本可以在给他们的信中更直接地表达这个问题。”

“They have never seen an ounce of contrition or regret from me directly, Hermione,” he said, his lips pursing. “That, I think, could be the difference.” In an undertone, he added, “Not that some of them deserve it.”
“他们从来没有直接从我身上看到过一丝悔恨或遗憾，赫敏，”他说，嘴唇抿着。“我认为，这可能就是不同之处。”他低调地补充说，“并不是说他们中的一些人活该。

Sighing, Hermione allowed her hand to slide from his arm and land with a heavy thump on the bed. “You’ve kept to your word, though,” she said. “To me . I thought that might count for something. And I vouched for you.”
赫敏叹了口气，让她的手从他的手臂上滑落，重重地砰地一声落在床上。“不过，你信守诺言，”她说。“对我来说......我想这可能有意义。我为你担保了。

“Keeping one's word isn’t actually as important as you seem to think it is in the Ministry.” He raised an eyebrow and, taking in the sullen downturn of her lips, snorted softly. “Or are you more annoyed by the fact that they didn’t unquestioningly trust your judgement?”
“信守诺言实际上并不像你在魔法部里想象的那么重要。”他扬起眉毛，看着她闷闷不乐的嘴唇，轻轻地哼了一声。“还是说，他们不毫无疑问地相信你的判断，你更生气？”

“I mean, honestly,” Hermione said, ignoring him, her tone becoming more heated, “Kingsley was being – just – ugh – how many chances does anyone actually get to help the entire wizarding world in any kind of measurable way? They’d need to actually give you some opp –”
“我是说，老实说，”赫敏无视他，她的语气变得更加激烈，“金斯莱在——只是——呃——有多少机会真的能以任何一种可衡量的方式帮助整个魔法世界？他们得给你点机会——”

“– so conceited sometimes, really, I forget that –” Lucius stopped mumbling to himself and eyed Hermione who had suddenly stopped talking to stare at him, her mouth agape. “Are you alright?”
“——有时候太自负了，真的，我忘了——”卢修斯停止了喃喃自语，盯着突然停止说话的赫敏，盯着他，张大了嘴巴。“你还好吗？”

Hermione’s eyes were wide and bright as they met his. “I know how you can prove to the Wizengamot that you’re changing – how you can help more people.”
赫敏的眼睛睁得又大又亮。“我知道你怎么能向威森加摩证明你正在改变——你怎么能帮助更多的人。”

Lucius’ head dropped towards his shoulder, his brow crumpled with tiredness. “Hermione, I really would –”
卢修斯把头垂向他的肩膀，他的眉头因疲惫而皱起。“赫敏，我真的会——”

“No, Lucius. It’s brilliant, I promise, I –” Hermione grunted and scrambled up onto her knees beside him, barely noticing the cold as her movements pushed the duvet from her body. “Kingsley’s asked me to come back to the Ministry to unpick all the pro-Pure-blood laws that no one’s looked at in generations and you can help me do it. I don’t think the Wizengamot could ask for much more evidence than that; it’ll affect everyone!”
“不，卢修斯。这太棒了，我保证，我——“赫敏咕哝着，爬到他身边跪了下来，几乎没注意到她的动作把羽绒被从她身上推开时带来的寒冷。“金斯利让我回到魔法部，解开所有几代人都没有看过的纯血统法律，你可以帮我做。我认为威森加摩不能要求比这更多的证据;它会影响每个人！

Lucius seemed to freeze, his eyes sliding over to her beaming face. “The pro-Pure-blood laws,” he finally repeated flatly, slowly.
卢修斯似乎僵住了，他的眼睛滑向她喜气洋洋的脸庞。“支持纯血统的法律，”他终于平淡而缓慢地重复道。

It was only then that Hermione seemed to truly grasp the significance of what she was suggesting and to whom she was suggesting it. He had, for so long, been her primary example of what it meant to be an old-fashioned Pure-blood in the Wizarding World; he had been raised to believe that any and all advantages were his due. 
直到那时，赫敏似乎才真正领会到她所建议的意义，以及她向谁建议。长期以来，他一直是她在魔法世界中成为老式纯血统意味着什么的主要例子;他从小就相信，任何和所有的好处都是他应得的。

“Yes…” she said, shifting on her knees and arranging the sheets around her thighs, feeling suddenly exposed. “Of course, I’m sure you must know about them – a collection of… outdated legislation that makes it easier for Pure-blood witches and wizards to retain their hegemony.” 
“是的......”她说着，跪在地上，把床单整理在大腿上，感觉突然暴露了出来。“当然，我相信你一定知道他们——一系列......过时的立法让纯血统的女巫和巫师更容易保持他们的霸权。

Lucius raised his eyebrows but said nothing and so Hermione pushed on despite an increasing trepidation. “Kingsley wants things to be fairer going forward – more balanced – he thinks re-working these laws or even…even undoing some of them could help that.”
卢修斯扬起眉毛，但什么也没说，所以赫敏尽管越来越害怕，还是继续前进。“金斯利希望事情向前发展得更公平——更平衡——他认为重新制定这些法律，甚至......即使撤销其中一些也会有所帮助。

Lucius was quiet for a moment, his jaw sliding back and forth contemplatively. “And you’d like me to help you do that?” he finally asked, an undercurrent of incredulity to his voice. “Me?”
卢修斯沉默了一会儿，他的下巴沉思地来回滑动。“你希望我帮你做那件事吗？”他终于问道，他的声音里暗藏着一股难以置信。“我？”

In the face of Lucius’ lack of enthusiasm for her grand, albeit cobbled-together plan, Hermione found herself slipping towards defensiveness, her hands curling into fists on her thighs. 
面对卢修斯对她那宏伟的、尽管是拼凑起来的计划缺乏热情，赫敏发现自己正在走向防御，她的双手在大腿上蜷缩成拳头。

“Why not?” she demanded. “Why shouldn’t I ask you?”
“为什么不呢？”“我为什么不问你呢？”

“I am one of the terrible Pure-bloods who benefits from these laws.”
“我是那些从这些法律中受益的可怕的纯血统之一。”

Hermione stopped and contemplated his relaxed posture; she thought she spied a falseness in it, a tension. “Surely you can’t really think that you deserve all the advantages that come with these laws just because you’re a Pure-blood? After everything, Lucius, do you really think that?”
赫敏停下脚步，思考着他放松的姿势;她觉得她从中窥探到了一个虚假，一种紧张。“你肯定不能真的因为你是纯血统就认为你值得这些法律带来的所有好处吗？毕竟，卢修斯，你真的这么认为吗？

He was slow to respond, his words careful. “I don’t think it’s a matter of whether or not I deserve these advantages – I already have them. I think I’d be a fool to give them up. Anyone would be.”
他反应迟缓，说话小心翼翼。“我不认为这是我是否值得这些优势的问题——我已经拥有它们了。我想放弃他们就是个傻瓜。任何人都会。

Nostrils flaring, Hermione took a deep breath, her chest rising as she searched for calm. “Do you even know what they involve?”
赫敏张开了鼻孔，深吸了一口气，她的胸膛在寻找平静时起伏。“你知道他们涉及什么吗？”

There was a slightly knowing upturn to the corner of Lucius’ mouth as he took in her clenched fists and squared shoulders. “Do you?” 
卢修斯的嘴角微微上扬，他看着她紧握的拳头和方正的肩膀。“是吗？”

“That means no, then,” Hermione said, adopting a superior tilt to her head so that her nose and chin were pointing upwards.
“那意味着不，那么，”赫敏说，她把头歪得高一点，让鼻子和下巴都朝上。

“Oh, and you do?" he asked acidly, the knowing upturn of his lips curling, curdling, into something less pleasant. “Had the time to read up on them all already, have you?”
“哦，你愿意吗？”他酸溜溜地问道，他知道的嘴唇卷曲、凝结，变得不那么令人愉快。“你有时间把它们都读一遍了，对吧？”

Flustered, heat rising to her cheeks, Hermione pushed on. “If you don’t even know exactly how you’re benefiting, how can you be so sure you don’t want to help me?”
赫敏慌乱，热气升到她的脸颊上，继续前进。“如果你连好处都不知道自己到底是怎么受益的，你怎么能这么确定你不想帮助我呢？”

Sighing, Lucius crossed his arms over his chest, settling back into his pillow. “I just need to know that I am benefitting,” he said, with the tone of a man who was explaining a perfectly simple concept and didn’t understand why he had to.
卢修斯叹了口气，双臂交叉在胸前，坐回了枕头里。“我只需要知道我正在受益，”他说，语气就像一个正在解释一个非常简单的概念的人，他不明白为什么他必须这样做。

“At the likely disadvantage of others,” Hermione stressed, aghast.
“可能会对别人不利，”赫敏惊恐地强调。

“That tends to be how these things work,” he muttered, rolling his eyes. Looking back at her face, Lucius took in her wide gaze and the mildly disgusted scrunch in her nose. It’d been a while since he’d seen that. 
“这些事情往往就是这样运作的，”他咕哝着，翻了个白眼。卢修斯回头看着她的脸，看到了她睁大的目光和她鼻子里略带厌恶的皱褶。他已经有一段时间没有看到了。

“Hermione, dear,” he said, an almost sympathetic quality to his tone, “at what point in the last few months have I ever given you the impression that this is a heart that bleeds?”
“赫敏，亲爱的，”他说，语气中带着一种近乎同情的意味，“在过去的几个月里，我什么时候给你留下过这样的印象，那就是一颗流血的心？

“Well, it’s not like it's made of stone. It's not like you can’t care. You care about –”
“嗯，它不像是石头做的。这并不是说你不在乎。你在乎——”

“Those who matter to me,” he finished for her, making her close her mouth with a snap of her teeth. He loved and cared discriminately – she knew that. Perhaps she had forgotten it in becoming one of those people that mattered. 
“那些对我重要的人，”他替她说完，让她咬牙切齿地闭上嘴巴。他爱和关心——她知道这一点。也许她在成为那些重要的人之一时忘记了这一点。

“You could care about the rest of the Wizarding World just a little bit,” she said, lowering her voice to soften the reproachful tone. “It wouldn’t kill you.”
“你可以稍微关心一下魔法世界的其他地方，”她说，压低了声音以缓和责备的语气。“它不会杀了你。”

A short chuckle from Lucius drew her gaze up. “Why take the risk at my age?” he asked, raising his eyebrows. 
卢修斯短促的笑声吸引了她的目光。“为什么要在我这个年纪冒险呢？”

“You’re not that old.”
“你没那么老。”

“Old enough to know myself. Besides, I get the impression that you care about the rest of the Wizarding World quite enough for both of us.” Lucius allowed silence to fall between them and eyed her carefully. She could see a rueful smile playing about his lips that made her press her tongue to the roof of her mouth, frustrated. 
“年纪大到可以了解我自己。此外，我有一种感觉，你对魔法世界的其他部分的关心对我们俩来说都足够了。卢修斯让他们之间陷入沉默，小心翼翼地看着她。她可以看到他的嘴唇上浮现出一个悲哀的笑容，这让她沮丧地将舌头贴在嘴巴上颚。

“Rethinking your grand collaboration?” he finally asked.
“重新考虑你们的盛大合作？”

“No,” she said loftily. “I still think it’s a good idea.”
“不，”她高傲地说。“我仍然认为这是个好主意。”

Sighing, Lucius uncrossed his arms and dropped his head back against the pillow, his eyes closing. “Hermione,” he said to the ceiling, “I will not… steal the advantages of my peers – their birth rights. That’s not how being a Pure-blood – a Slytherin – works. We are loyal to our own.”
卢修斯叹了口气，解开了双臂，把头靠在枕头上，闭上了眼睛。“赫敏，”他对着天花板说，“我不会......窃取我的同龄人的优势——他们与生俱来的权利。这不是成为纯血统——斯莱特林——的运作方式。我们忠于我们自己的人。

“You didn’t consider their blood status quite so sacrosanct when you were handing over their names to the Ministry,” Hermione said, the words tumbling out in a rush. She pressed her lips together as soon as she’d finished speaking to stop anything else spilling out – there she went again, saying the ugly thing. 
“当你把他们的名字交给魔法部的时候，你没觉得他们的血统地位如此神圣不可侵犯，”赫敏说，这些话匆匆忙忙地翻滚而出。她一说完就紧抿着嘴唇，阻止任何其他东西溢出来——她又来了，说了那句难听的话。

Ever so slowly, Lucius raised his head from the pillow, his eyes opening and his brows arched. “Not all Pure-bloods served the Dark Lord,” he replied. Then, eyes narrowing, he added, “Might I remind you of your beloved Weasleys – you would take the few boons they have?”
Lucius慢慢地从枕头上抬起头，睁开了眼睛，眉头弯了起来。“不是所有的纯血统都为黑魔王服务，”他回答道。然后，他眯起眼睛，补充道，“我能让你想起你心爱的韦斯莱一家吗——你会接受他们仅有的几点恩惠吗？

“The Weasleys wouldn’t want them, even if they did know what they were.” Hermione was almost triumphant in pointing that out but it simply made Lucius bark out a short, cold laugh.
“韦斯莱一家不会想要他们，即使他们真的知道他们是什么。”赫敏几乎得意洋洋地指出了这一点，但这只是让卢修斯发出了一声短促而冰冷的笑声。

“Well, they’ve never known what’s good for them – just look at them.” 
“嗯，他们从来不知道什么对他们有好处——看看他们就知道了。”

At the sight of the flush rising up Hermione’s neck and the glint in her eyes, Lucius sat up straighter, his hand coming to lie flat on the duvet between them, fingers spread. “If I were to have involvement in this, I doubt I would ever be embraced in Pure-blood circles again. Even Draco would –”
看到赫敏的脖子上泛起的红晕和她眼中的光芒，卢修斯坐直了身子，他的手平躺在他们之间的羽绒被上，手指张开。“如果我参与其中，我怀疑我是否会再次被纯血圈所接受。就连德拉科也会——”

“You’re not welcome in them anymore anyway,” Hermione pointed out, shaking her head so that her shorter curls bounced against her pink cheeks. “You’re protecting them, safeguarding primacies they might not even know they have, and they don’t even know or care that you're doing it. They’re not trying to help you, Lucius, or get you free – they’re not interested. ”
“反正你现在已经不受欢迎了，”赫敏指出，摇了摇头，让她较短的卷发在她粉红色的脸颊上弹跳。“你在保护他们，保护他们甚至可能不知道自己拥有的首要地位，他们甚至不知道或不关心你在这样做。他们不是想帮助你，Lucius，也不是想让你自由——他们不感兴趣。”

“The freedom you’re talking about is freedom to live in ignominy,” he ground out, his patience wearing thin out of a combination of Hermione’s exhausting persistence and the threads of truth he could see in what she was saying. 
“你说的自由就是生活在耻辱中的自由，”他停下脚步，赫敏疲惫不堪的坚持和他从她所说的话中能看到的真理的结合，他的耐心逐渐消磨殆尽。

Half-turning, Lucius gripped the duvet and threw it back, intending to rise. Before he could, Hermione launched forward from her kneel and pulled him back. Scrambling onto him, she forced him back onto his pillow where he landed with an ‘ oomph’ .
卢修斯半转身，抓住羽绒被，把它扔回去，打算站起来。在他来得及之前，赫敏从她的跪下跳了起来，把他拉了回来。她爬到他身上，强迫他回到枕头上，在那里他以“哀嚎”的一声着陆。

The incredulity in Lucius’ expression as he looked up at her would have made Hermione laugh aloud in any other situation but she was far too agitated, too desperate to convince him, to see the humour. Sitting atop him in a heavy straddle, she pressed her hands into his chest and fixed him with a determined look.
卢修斯抬头看着她时，他那难以置信的表情在其他任何情况下都会让赫敏大笑起来，但她太激动了，太绝望了，无法说服他，看不到其中的幽默。她沉重地跨坐在他身上，双手按在他的胸前，用坚定的眼神注视着他。

 A part of her was aware that it was silly – practically a game – because, lean as Lucius was, feeling him beneath her, seeing her small hands planted on his chest, she was reminded that he was more than strong enough to simply throw her off. 
她的一部分意识到这很愚蠢——几乎是一场游戏——因为，像卢修斯一样瘦弱，感觉到他在她下面，看到她的小手放在他的胸前，她想起了他足够强大，可以简单地把她甩开。

But he didn’t. Surely she had to take some encouragement from that. 
但他没有。当然，她必须从中得到一些鼓励。

“Having you involved in this,” she said to him, pressing her palms into him for emphasis, “having you work with me, it just makes it all look so much better, don’t you see?” 
“让你参与这件事，”她对他说，用手掌压在他身上以示强调，“让你和我一起工作，只会让一切看起来好多了，你没看到吗？

“To who , exactly?” he asked, his eyes flicking down to her hands briefly, a disgruntled grimace marring his face.
“到底是对谁说的？”他问道，他的眼睛短暂地落在她的手上，脸上露出不满的表情。

“Everyone!” Hermione cried, leaning back and raising her arms wide. “A Pure-blood and a Muggleborn working on these things together, coming to an agreement, it’d be…wonderful! Don’t you think?”
“大家！”赫敏喊道，向后靠着，张开双臂。“一个纯血统和一个麻瓜出身的人一起做这些事情，达成协议，那就是......美妙！你不觉得吗？

One drawn-out, unamused blink was his response and Hermione sighed, dropping her arms. 
他的回答是拖延的、不高兴的眨眼，赫敏叹了口气，放下了手臂。

“Any one blood status could be accused of an inherent bias but with two of us there’s balance, Lucius. Half-bloods and Muggleborns can be certain that someone is working in their interests and Pure-bloods ought to be satisfied that they’re not simply being…brought to heel , I suppose.”
“任何一种血统都可能被指责为固有的偏见，但我们两个人就有平衡，卢修斯。混血儿和麻瓜出身的人可以确定有人在为他们的利益工作，而纯血统的人应该确信他们不仅仅是......我猜是被逼到脚下了。

With a quiet sigh through his nose, Evan set his quill down, clasped his hands and looked up at Hermione properly. His face was placid, pleasant, like he was entirely accustomed to being a brick wall for his Minister for Magic and had never once crumbled. 
Evan从鼻子里轻轻地叹了口气，放下了他的羽毛笔，紧握着双手，适当地抬头看着赫敏。他的脸色平静、和蔼可亲，就像他完全习惯了成为魔法部长的砖墙，而且从来没有倒塌过。

“Miss Granger, appointments are made for a reason; they don’t just move because it’s convenient to one party.”
“格兰杰小姐，预约是有原因的;他们搬家不仅仅是因为对一方方便。

“It’s not a matter of convenience,” Hermione said. “It’s a matter of urgency.”
“这不是一个方便的问题，”赫敏说。“这是一个紧急问题。”

“What is the urgent matter?”
“有什么紧急的事情？”

“It’s private.”
“这是私人的。”

“It’s private and urgent? Ah, well, that is convenient.”
“这是私人的和紧急的？啊，嗯，那很方便。

Hermione’s mouth fell open. She had never tried to get past Evan before, had never gotten on the wrong side of him, and now she was beginning to see why in some corners of the Ministry he was quietly referred to as ‘The Sphinx’. 
赫敏张大了嘴巴。她以前从未试图越过Evan，也从未站在他的一边，现在她开始明白为什么在魔法部的某些角落里，他被悄悄地称为“狮身人面像”。

“Well, fine,” Hermione said, trying her best to remain affable though she'd never done particularly well with that. “When does Kingsley have me booked in for an appointment?”
“嗯，好吧，”赫敏说，尽力保持和蔼可亲，尽管她从来没有在这方面做得特别好。“Kingsley 什么时候帮我预约？”

With a long, hard look at Hermione, Evan clucked his tongue and pulled a roll of parchment towards himself. Unfurling it, he disappeared from view. “Next Thursday,” he said from behind the parchment. Rolling it back up, he placed it carefully back on the desk and folded his hands over it protectively. “Ten in the morning.”
Evan狠狠地瞪了赫敏一眼，咯咯地吐了吐舌头，把一卷羊皮纸拉向自己。展开它，他就消失在了视线中。“下周四，”他从羊皮纸后面说。他把它卷起来，小心翼翼地把它放回桌子上，双手合十保护性地放在上面。“早上十点。”

“ Next Thursday? I was expecting –” Evan raised his eyebrows and tilted his head in a way that asked Hermione if she dared to have a problem with his meticulously organised calendar. “I just – isn’t there anything sooner?”
“下周四？我期待着——“Evan扬起眉毛，歪着头，问赫敏她是否敢对他精心安排的日历提出问题。“我只是——不是更早的时候吗？”

Evan nudged the roll of parchment away with the tips of his fingers. “He’s fully booked.”
Evan用指尖推开了羊皮纸卷。“他已经订满了。”

Glancing over Evan’s head, Hermione glared at the external wall of Kingsley’s office like she might be able to see through the panelled wood. “Is he in right now?”
赫敏瞥了一眼埃文的头，瞪着金斯莱办公室的外墙，仿佛她能看穿镶板木头。“他现在在吗？”

“I’m afraid I can’t say.”
“恐怕我说不上来。”

Crossing her arms, Hermione dropped her weight onto one hip and narrowed her eyes. “That means yes.” 
赫敏交叉双臂，将体重放在一侧臀部上，眯起眼睛。“那意味着是的。”

Even merely shrugged. “It means I can’t say.”
甚至只是耸了耸肩。“这意味着我不能说。”

“Evan, I’m barely going to take up any of his time, if you’d just let me –”
“Evan，我几乎不会占用他任何时间，如果你让我——”

“He doesn’t want to be disturbed, Miss Granger,” Evan insisted, a bite of frustration creeping into his tone. “This is one of the few times of day that he gets a moment to him –”
『他不想被打扰， Granger小姐， 』Evan坚持道， 他的语气中流露出一丝沮丧。“这是他一天中为数不多的能有时间陪伴他的时间之一——”

“Evan, is everything al – Hermione?”
“埃文，一切都是——赫敏吗？”

Both Hermione and Evan’s attention snapped to Kingsley’s office door, out of which the Minister for Magic had poked his head. When neither of them answered but simply gaped at him, Kingsley blinked once, twice and then tilted his head in expectation of a reply. 
赫敏和埃文的注意力都集中在金斯莱办公室的门上，魔法部长从门里探出头来。当他们都没有回答，只是目瞪口呆地看着他时，金斯利眨了眨眼，眨了一两次眼，然后歪着头期待得到回答。

“I was –”
“我是——”

“We were –”
“我们是——”

Hermione and Evan glanced at one another as they answered at the same time. Pressing her lips together, she allowed Evan to take the lead and address Kingsley. 
赫敏和埃文对视一眼，同时回答道。她紧抿着嘴唇，让Evan带头对Kingsley说话。

“I was just telling Miss Granger, Minister, that you are unavailable for an appointment and that she will have to wait –” Here, Evan spared Hermione a sidelong glare. “Until her appointment next week.”
“我刚才告诉格兰杰小姐，部长，你没时间赴约，她得等一等——”说到这里，埃文瞪了赫敏一眼。“直到她下周的预约。”

“I’d really rather speak now, Kingsley.”
“我现在真想说话，金斯利。”

“Miss Granger, this is the Minister’s administration hour and he –”
“格兰杰小姐，这是部长的行政时间，他——”

“Evan.” Kingsley’s voice was gentle but firm and Evan stopped speaking immediately. “I appreciate you safeguarding my time but if Hermione can promise that this won’t take too long?” Hermione nodded rapidly in response to Kingsley’s enquiring look. “Then I’ll see her briefly.”
“埃文。”金斯利的声音温柔而坚定，埃文立即停止了说话。“我很感激你保护我的时间，但赫敏能保证这不会花太长时间吗？”赫敏迅速点头回应金斯莱询问的眼神。“那我就短暂地见她。”

“Of course, Minister.”
“当然，部长。”

With a single nod, Kingsley stepped back into his office and threw open the door wide, beckoning for Hermione to follow. Directing a quiet “sorry” to Evan, who merely shrugged and waved a hand that said ‘it’s all part of the job’, she scurried after Kingsley.
金斯莱点了点头，走回他的办公室，把门大开，招手让赫敏跟上来。她轻声地对 Evan 说了声“对不起”，而 Evan 只是耸了耸肩，挥了挥手说“这都是工作的一部分”，然后她匆匆忙忙地跟在金斯利后面。

“Is everything alright, Hermione?” Kingsley asked over his shoulder as he swept towards his desk. “I booked you in for next Thursday. I thought, since we agreed that you were returning, there was no great hurry in sorting the finer details.”
“一切都还好吗，赫敏？”Kingsley回头问道，他扫向自己的办公桌。“我帮你预定了下周四。我想，既然我们同意你回来，就不用急着把更细的细节整理出来。

“Well…” Hermione closed the office door, lingering for a moment with her hand on the doorknob before she followed Kingsley to his desk. There was no going back. “I have something about my return and the project that I’d like to discuss with you. Um, sooner rather than later, hence my…” Hermione cringed. “Insistence with Evan.”
“嗯......”赫敏关上了办公室的门，手在门把手上逗留了一会儿，然后她跟着金斯莱走到了他的办公桌前。没有回头路了。“我有一些关于我的回归和项目的事情想和你讨论。嗯，宜早宜迟，因此我的......”赫敏畏缩了。“坚持与埃文。”

Kingsley stopped in the process of pulling out his chair and, as his eyes met hers, Hermione thought she could almost see his expression close over in preparation for a negotiation. “Go on,” he said slowly, resuming the process of taking a seat.
金斯莱在拉开椅子的过程中停了下来，当他的目光与她的眼睛相遇时，赫敏觉得她几乎能看到他准备谈判的表情。“继续，”他缓缓地说，继续坐下。

“So, these laws, Kingsley…” Hermione paused by her own seat and contemplated whether or not she wanted to sit in it. To stand above Kingsley or to bring herself down to his level. He would always leave it up to her. “This project…”
“所以，这些法律，金斯利......”赫敏在自己的座位旁停了下来，考虑着她是否想坐进去。站在金斯利之上，或者让自己降到他的水平。他总是把这事留给她。“这个项目......”

“Yes?” Kingsley prompted, leaning forward, elbows on his desk with his hands clasped. “What about it?”
“是吗？”金斯利提示道，身体前倾，双手紧握，手肘放在桌子上。“怎么样？”

Hermione met his eyes and, taking in a sharp breath, plunged into the seat across from him. “What if I didn’t work on them alone? What if I had a partner? More of a consultant, really, since they wouldn’t strictly be a part of the Ministry.”
赫敏与他对视，猛地吸了一口气，一头扎进了他对面的座位上。“如果我不单独处理它们呢？如果我有合作伙伴怎么办？真的，他们更像是一个顾问，因为他们不会严格地成为魔法部的一部分。

Kingsley drummed his fingers across his own knuckles and pursed his lips contemplatively. “I don’t think the idea of a partner or a consultant ever came up in our discussions, Hermione. Not once. Did you have anyone in particular in mind?”
金斯莱用手指敲打着自己的指关节，沉思地抿着嘴唇。“我认为我们的讨论中从未出现过合伙人或顾问的想法，赫敏。一次也没有。你有没有特别想过什么人？

Kingsley’s gaze was level, expectant. He knew. He knew she had someone in mind and that’s why she just let it tumble out. The sooner he knew, the sooner they could argue about it.
金斯莱的目光平缓而期待。他知道。他知道她心里有谁，所以她就这样让它流出来了。他越早知道，他们就能越早争论。

“Lucius Malfoy.”
“卢修斯·马尔福。”

The name hung in the air between them for a moment. Kingsley’s response was to smile and frown at the same time, like Hermione was making some kind of distasteful joke. 
这个名字在他们之间的空气中悬了一会儿。金斯莱的回应是微笑和皱眉，就像赫敏在开什么令人反感的玩笑一样。

“Hermione –”
“赫敏——”

“It’s a good idea, Kingsley, I promise.”
“这是个好主意，金斯利，我保证。”

Taking a deep breath, like he was preparing to argue, Kingsley settled for unclasping his hands, flattening them on his messy desk and sighing heavily. “Explain,” he said, eyes fixed on his hands. 
金斯利深吸一口气，就像他准备争论一样，他决定解开他的手，把它们压平在凌乱的桌子上，然后重重地叹了口气。“解释一下，”他说，眼睛盯着他的手。

And so Hermione told him as she had told Lucius – she explained the value of having a Pure-blood involved, another pair of eyes that saw the world differently and might, therefore, spy unfairnesses or even loopholes that she wouldn’t.
所以赫敏告诉他，就像她告诉卢修斯一样——她解释了让纯血统参与进来的价值，另一双以不同方式看待世界的眼睛，因此可能会窥探到她不会窥探的不公平甚至漏洞。

“I just think there’s no point in giving Pure-bloods additional grievances,” Hermione said. “In making them feel isolated or…disproportionately punished.”
“我只是觉得没有必要给纯血统的人额外的委屈，”赫敏说。“让他们感到孤立或......受到了不成比例的惩罚。

It took a moment for Kingsley to clear his throat and nod slowly. “I see your reasoning. I accept it. In fact, I heartily agree that your plan has many merits. A partner from the Pure-blood community could, indeed, add legitimacy to what we’re doing.” Hermione beamed at Kingsley as he finally looked up at her. “But what if I were to suggest that we selected someone who wasn’t Lucius Malfoy?”
金斯利过了一会儿才清了清嗓子，慢慢地点了点头。“我明白你的道理。我接受它。事实上，我由衷地同意您的计划有很多优点。来自纯血统社区的合作伙伴确实可以为我们正在做的事情增加合法性。赫敏对金斯莱笑了笑，他终于抬起头看向她。“但是，如果我建议我们选择一个不是卢修斯·马尔福的人呢？”

The smile that had burst onto Hermione’s face faltered, a candle threatened by a cool, uncaring breeze. “Who did you have in mind?”
赫敏脸上绽放的笑容变得摇摇欲坠，蜡烛被凉爽、冷漠的微风威胁着。“你心里想的是谁？”

“Well, no one in particular just yet but –”
“嗯，现在还没有特别的人，但是——”

Hermione’s smile steadied, though it was thinner than before, more polite than sincere. “That’s the thing, Kingsley, I do have someone in mind. And he’s agreed to do it. Why add additional hurdles that will make it even harder to get started?”
赫敏的笑容稳定了下来，尽管比以前更薄了，比起真诚，更多的是礼貌。“就是这样，金斯利，我心里确实有个人。他已经同意这样做了。为什么要增加额外的障碍，使开始变得更加困难？

Lips turned down, Kingsley slumped back in his chair, which creaked in protest. Raising a hand to his forehead, he leaned his temple on his thumb and rubbed at the deep set lines on his forehead with his fingers, like he was trying to massage them away. “You’ve already spoken to him about it?”
金斯利垂下嘴唇，瘫倒在椅子上，椅子吱吱作响以示抗议。他将一只手举到额头上，将太阳穴靠在拇指上，用手指揉搓着额头上深深的皱纹，就像他试图按摩它们一样。“你已经跟他谈过了？”

“I have.”
“我有。”

“And he agreed?”
“他同意了？”

“Yes.” 
“是的。”

Lowering his hand down to his face, Kingsley drew his cheeks between his fingers and thumb then pressed his knuckles over his lips, studying Hermione from under his brow. “Why?” 
金斯莱把手放到脸上，用手指和拇指抚摸着他的脸颊，然后用指关节捂住嘴唇，从赫敏的眉毛下打量着他。“为什么？”

“You assume there’s a reason, Kingsley. I mean, maybe he just –”
“你觉得这是有原因的，金斯利。我的意思是，也许他只是——”

“Hermione.” Kingsley’s voice, for all its deepness, was quiet but she noticed it lacked its usual patience. It was, Hermione had to admit to herself, a miracle that he hadn’t immediately told her she had no right going to Lucius before him about anything.  
“赫敏。”金斯莱的声音，尽管低沉，但很安静，但她注意到它缺乏平常的耐心。赫敏不得不承认，这是一个奇迹，他没有立即告诉她，她无权在他之前去找卢修斯任何事情。

Clearing her throat, Hermione pointlessly smoothed the crumpled cotton of the dress she was wearing. When she’d returned to her flat to fetch it, Lucius had suggested that she might leave some clothes with him. He had said it like it was nothing to him, simply a way to make her life more convenient. It had taken Hermione several minutes to reply that she would think about it. 
赫敏清了清嗓子，毫无意义地抚平了她所穿的裙子上皱巴巴的棉布。当她回到自己的公寓拿东西时，卢修斯建议她把一些衣服留给他。他说这话对他来说不算什么，只是为了让她的生活更方便。赫敏花了好几分钟才回答说她会考虑一下。

“Last night, you said that the Wizengamot felt that Lucius’ assistance in my book had a…what was it?”
“昨天晚上，你说威森加摩觉得卢修斯在我书中的帮助有......那是什么？

“A narrow field of beneficiaries.”
“受益者的范围很窄。”

“Yes. He wasn’t helping enough people with it. If he works with me on this, he'll certainly be helping a lot more people. Potentially, might I add, to his own disadvantage."
“是的。他没有帮助足够多的人。如果他和我一起做这件事，他肯定会帮助更多的人。我还可以补充一点，对他自己不利。

Kingsley tilted his head, acknowledging the truth of that and, encouraged, Hermione continued. "I don’t know how long all of this will take – I know it could be years – but at the end of it, I’d like him to have his freedom.”
金斯莱歪了歪头，承认了这件事的真实性，赫敏受到鼓励，继续说道。“我不知道这一切需要多长时间——我知道可能需要几年——但到最后，我希望他能获得自由。”

“And if I say no? Because I have every right to.”
“如果我说不呢？因为我完全有权利这样做。

Hermione steeled herself, swallowing. “Then I might do the same. Because I also have every right to.”
赫敏强起勇气，咽了咽口水。“那我也可以这样做。因为我也有完全的权利。

A smile, bitter and pained, flashed over Kingsley’s face. He looked more tired than Hermione had ever seen him and as she looked down at the mounds of parchment that littered his desk, the broken quills, a plate bearing a half-eaten sandwich, she wondered how much of a front he put on. 
金斯莱的脸上闪过一丝苦涩和痛苦的笑容。他看起来比赫敏见过的他更疲惫，当她低头看着散落在他桌子上的羊皮纸堆，破损的羽毛笔，一个装着吃了一半的三明治的盘子时，她想知道他装扮得有多大。

The last time she had been in his office, there had been nothing but tea on the desk. When she had worked at the Ministry and attended appointments with him, the parchment had always been neat and tidy, never encroaching on his space. She was catching him at short notice this time; he hadn’t had time to hide the true, ever-demanding nature of the job that no one could really, truly, simply take in their stride. 
她上次来他的办公室时，桌上除了茶什么都没有。当她在魔法部工作并与他一起参加约会时，羊皮纸一直都很整洁，从未侵占他的空间。这一次她是在短时间内抓住了他;他没有时间隐藏这份工作的真实、永远苛刻的本质，没有人能真正、真正、简单地从容不迫地接受。

“You understand that you’re putting me in a very difficult position here, Hermione,” he said, drawing her eyes up from a speech which had more sentences scored out with harsh black lines than not.
“你明白你把我放在了一个非常困难的境地上，赫敏，”他说，把她的眼睛从演讲中抬起来，这演讲中有很多句子被刺耳的黑线划掉了。

“I am offering you a willing candidate to work with me on this project,” Hermione said, pushing aside a squirming sense that she was making a friend’s stressful life even more stressful. “I’m offering you a way to make it an even stronger proposal. Nigh-on unassailable, actually.”
“我向你推荐一个愿意和我一起做这个项目的候选人，”赫敏说，把她让朋友的压力生活更加紧张的蠕动感抛在一边。“我为您提供一种方法，使它成为一个更强大的提案。实际上，几乎无懈可击。

“Hermione, I understand you’ve always liked to have a cause.” Hermione clenched her jaw, forcing her molars to take the weight of her irritation. ‘A cause’ – she was so tired of people saying that like it was a charming accessory; something frivolous she carried around as a talking point. 
“赫敏，我知道你一直都喜欢有自己的事业。”赫敏咬紧下巴，强迫她的臼齿承受她的刺激的重量。“一个原因”——她厌倦了人们说那好像它是一个迷人的配饰;她随身携带一些轻浮的东西作为话题。

“I admire that about you very much,” Kingsley continued, eyeing her tight expression wearily. “But Lucius Malfoy is, at best, an extremely unorthodox choice. Don’t you think it’s gone far enough?”
“我非常佩服你，”金斯莱继续说道，疲惫地看着她紧绷的表情。“但卢修斯·马尔福充其量只是一个极其非正统的选择。你不觉得它已经走得够远了吗？

“No.” 
“不。”

“This isn’t fair.” Only Kingsley, Hermione thought, could say something like that without it sounding whiny. 
“这不公平。”赫敏想，只有金斯莱能说出这样的话，而不会听起来像是抱怨。

“On who?”
“对谁？”

“On me ,” he said, exasperation creeping in. “You know I want you back here but there are so few people who want him given an inch and I…” Kingsley sighed, eyeing the uncompromising set of her jaw.
“对我而言，”他说，愤怒悄悄地蔓延开来。“你知道我想让你回到这里，但很少有人想让他一寸，而我......”金斯莱叹了口气，盯着她那毫不妥协的下巴。

“I am going to lay something out here, Hermione,” he said, planting a palm flat over three sheets of parchment that were filled from edge to edge with his neat script. “The Ministry is a challenging place for people that want to change the world, I know that. It’s old, it’s slow, it creaks. Merlin knows, I’ve seen enough people over the years who are only in it for the titles, money and personal influence. They stand for very little but themselves and, yes, they make change even harder either by being speed bumps or outright blockades.”
“我要在这里布置一些东西，赫敏，”他说，将一只手掌平放在三张羊皮纸上，羊皮纸上从头到尾都写满了他工整的字体。“我知道，对于想要改变世界的人来说，魔法部是一个充满挑战的地方。它很旧，很慢，吱吱作响。梅林知道，这些年来，我见过足够多的人，他们只是为了头衔、金钱和个人影响力而参与其中。他们只代表他们自己，是的，他们通过减速带或彻底的封锁，使变革变得更加困难。

Hermione sucked in a breath but Kingsley shook his head and held up a hand, halting her.
赫敏吸了一口气，但金斯莱摇了摇头，举起一只手，阻止了她。

“But we cannot be rid of them. They will always be here. What we can do is balance them out with good, selfless people. People with the bravery and intelligence necessary to envision a different and better future. That is why I am giving you this project – I know it’s the kind of thing you strive for and I want people like you working alongside me.” Kingsley paused for a moment, contemplating his words. “No, not want. Need. I need it.” 
“但我们不能摆脱他们。他们将永远在这里。我们能做的就是用善良、无私的人来平衡他们。具有必要的勇气和智慧，可以设想一个不同的、更美好的未来。这就是我给你这个项目的原因——我知道这是你为之奋斗的目标，我希望像你这样的人与我一起工作。金斯莱停顿了一会儿，沉思着他的话。“不，不想要。需要。我需要它。

“You still have good people, Kingsley,” Hermione said quietly. She’d never seen him so close to frayed and it gave her pause – she’d been so frustrated by the limited impact of her presence in the Ministry, she hadn’t ever contemplated what her absence would do. 
“你还有好人，金斯莱，”赫敏轻声说。她从未见过他如此接近磨损，这让她停顿了一下——她对自己在魔法部的存在所造成的有限影响感到非常沮丧，她从来没有想过她的缺席会带来什么。

Kingsley chuckled mirthlessly and glanced down at all the parchment beneath his hands. “I feel like I don’t have nearly enough of them and I am worried .” He met her eyes and Hermione saw it. “I won’t be here forever and I need to set up the pieces so that the right people move into the right positions when I’m gone. It might be years down the line but Merlin knows it’ll end up feeling like seconds.”
金斯利无情地笑了笑，低头看了一眼他手下的所有羊皮纸。“我觉得我几乎没有足够多的疫苗，我很担心。”他对上了她的眼睛，赫敏看到了。“我不会永远在这里，我需要做好准备，以便在我离开时，正确的人会进入正确的位置。可能需要几年时间，但 Merlin 知道这最终会感觉像几秒钟。

Kingsley pointed at Hermione, his eyes blazing. “You are one of those right people, Hermione. Not just because of what you want but because of who you are . Do you understand me?”
金斯莱指着赫敏，眼睛炯炯有神。“你就是那些合适的人之一，赫敏。不仅仅是因为你想要什么，还因为你是谁。你明白我的话吗？

“Kingsley…”
“金斯利......”

“When you left the Ministry, it didn’t reflect especially positively on me.”
“当你离开魔法部时，它并没有对我产生特别积极的影响。”

Hermione’s heart thumped loudly in her ears. “What do you –”
赫敏的心在耳边砰砰直跳。“你怎么——”

“When Ron departed to work with his brother, it was widely publicised and accepted as an act of familial solidarity – something for which the Weasleys are rather renowned. I could bear it given I still had you and Harry. But when you, Hermione, decided to depart so suddenly –”
“当罗恩离开去和他的兄弟一起工作时，这被广泛宣传并被接受为一种家庭团结的行为——韦斯莱一家因此而闻名。我能忍受，因为我还有你和哈利。但是，当你，赫敏，决定这么突然地离开时——”

Understanding landed on Hermione with a sickly splat. “Oh, I see,” she replied, trying not to sound overly scathing or hurt. “Didn’t like losing the whole set after the war, is that it? Ministry doesn’t shine quite as bright without the full Golden Trio?”
理解落在赫敏身上，病态地啪啪作响。“哦，我明白了，”她回答道，尽量不让自己听起来过于严厉或伤人。“我不喜欢战后失去整套，是吗？没有完整的黄金三重奏，事工就不会那么耀眼吗？

“Don’t make it sound so…” Kingsley winced and gave a concessionary wave of his hand. “ Yes , alright? Yes. But you cannot pretend you don’t mean something, Hermione. You three were – are – the heroes of our world! And when a hero simply leaves the institution that’s supposed to be guiding the world forward into a new era, what is everyone supposed to think?”
“别这么说......”金斯莱皱起眉头，让步地挥了挥手。“是的，好吗？是的。但你不能假装你没有意思，赫敏。你们三个曾经——现在是——我们世界的英雄！当一个英雄简单地离开了本应引导世界进入新时代的机构时，每个人都应该怎么想？

“Maybe they’re supposed to think that there’s a possibility the Ministry isn’t as efficient, all-knowing and united as it tries to make itself look.”
“也许他们应该认为，魔法部有可能并不像它试图让自己看起来那样高效、无所不知和团结。”

“They can’t think that, Hermione,” Kingsley snapped, leaning forward to jab a finger down on his desk. “Do you understand? We’re supposed to keep this world together, particularly in times of change and uncertainty. I told everyone you’d be back, of course, as you told me. But now the two years of your sabbatical have passed and they’ve started asking again. People are wondering why one of the great heroes of our age doesn’t want to be part of my Ministry and I’m running out of answers to give them.”
“他们不能这么想，赫敏，”金斯莱厉声说，身体前倾，用一根手指戳了戳他的桌子。“你明白吗？我们应该让这个世界团结在一起，尤其是在变化和不确定的时期。我告诉大家你会回来的，当然，就像你告诉我的那样。但是现在你的两年休假已经过去了，他们又开始要求了。人们想知道为什么我们这个时代的伟大英雄之一不想成为我事工的一部分，而我给他们的答案已经不多了。

“So, it’s all about the optics, is it?”
“所以，这一切都与光学有关，是吗？”

“Optics are important , Hermione!” Kingsley’s eyes were wide, his tone urgent. “Do you think I would have survived as a spy for the Order if I didn’t have some understanding of that? Not everything can be presented exactly as it is all the time . Right now, this Ministry needs to look strong and purposeful. It needs to look united. So I need you back and making positive changes. What I don’t need is Death Eaters.”
“光学很重要，赫敏！”金斯莱睁大了眼睛，语气急促。“你觉得如果我对此没有一些了解，我能作为组织的间谍活下来吗？并非一切都可以一直完全呈现。现在，这个事工需要看起来强大而有目的。它需要看起来团结一致。所以我需要你回来并做出积极的改变。我不需要的是食死徒。

Hermione’s breathing was fast through her nose, her heart hammering. “I’ve got good news for you, Kingsley: he’s not one of those anymore.”
赫敏的鼻子呼吸急促，她的心跳加速。“我有个好消息要告诉你，金斯利：他已经不是那种人了。”

“Hermione –”
“赫敏——”

“Don’t you see that you could be the Minister that was able to bring together a former Death Eater and a Muggleborn and have them work on something that’s to the benefit of the entire Wizarding World? I’d say that looks pretty good for you.”
“难道你没看到你能成为部长，把一个前食死徒和一个麻瓜出身的人聚集在一起，让他们做一些对整个魔法世界有利的事情吗？”我想说这对你来说还不错。

When Kingsley said nothing and instead dropped his head into his hands, drawing them down his face to peer at Hermione over his fingertips, she gave one final push.
当金斯莱什么也没说，反而把头埋进他的手里，把双手从他的脸上拉下来，从指尖盯着赫敏时，她给了他最后的推。

“You could be the Minister for whom one of Voldemort’s highest ranking Death Eaters was willing to turn against almost everything he once stood for.”
“你可以成为伏地魔中级别最高的食死徒之一，愿意反对他曾经代表的几乎所有事情的部长。”

Lifting his head fully, Kingsley scrutinised Hermione. She had a sense that he was finally allowing himself to look at something he had only dared to glance at before. “But he wouldn’t be doing it for me, would he, Hermione?”
金斯莱完全抬起头，仔细观察赫敏。她有一种感觉，他终于允许自己看着他以前只敢看一眼的东西。“但他不会为我做这件事的，对吧，赫敏？”

Beneath the desk, out of Kingsley’s eye line, Hermione twisted the fabric of her skirt in her fist. “Not everything can be presented exactly as it is all the time, Kingsley,” she said softly. “Isn’t that right?”
在桌子下面，在金斯莱的视线之外，赫敏用拳头扭动着裙子的布料。“不是所有的东西都能一直保持原样，金斯利，”她轻声说。“对吗？”

Something like true, wry amusement passed over Kingsley’s face then and, had they been in any kind of open combat, Hermione would have marked it as the moment that he would have lowered his wand. 
那时，金斯莱的脸上闪过了某种真实、讽刺的笑容，如果他们正在进行任何形式的公开战斗，赫敏会把它标记为他放下魔杖的那一刻。

“Oh, to have someone like you fighting in my corner all the time," Kingsley said, chuckling tiredly. Exhaling through his nose, he ran the edge of his forefinger along his lower lip for a moment before he said, "You actually think he’s right for the work? That he’ll be helpful?”
“哦，有你这样的人一直在我这边战斗，”金斯利说，疲惫地笑了起来。他从鼻子里呼出一口气，用食指的边缘在下唇上滑过了一会儿，然后说：“你真的觉得他适合这份工作吗？他会帮忙的吗？

“Aside from his blood status and the weight his family name still holds, I think his background in and around the Ministry more than qualifies him.” Hermione sucked in a breath. “And I trust him.” 
“除了他的血统地位和他的姓氏仍然具有分量之外，我认为他在事工内外的背景使他有资格。”赫敏吸了一口气。“我相信他。”

“I do not,” Kingsley said shortly. Then, his expression softening, he added, “But I do trust you.”
“我不知道，”金斯利很快说。然后，他的表情变得柔和，他补充道，“但我确实信任你。

“I don’t intend to give you reason to regret that, Kingsley.”
“我不打算让你有理由后悔，金斯莱。”

Kingsley nodded once slowly and, sinking down in his seat, he lowered his hand from his face so that it hung over the arm of his chair. Several long seconds passed, during which Kingsley simply inspected Hermione and she allowed him to, trying to hide her nerves.
金斯莱缓缓地点了点头，然后一头扎进座位上，把手从脸上放下来，悬在椅子的扶手上。漫长的几秒钟过去了，在此期间，金斯莱只是检查了赫敏，她允许他这样做，试图隐藏她的紧张。

“Very well, Hermione," he finally said. "I will approve your chosen consultant. Based on its previous demurrals, I can’t see the Wizengamot being able to deny your request and I will, of course, give my own recommendations that it be granted."
“很好，赫敏，”他终于说了。“我会批准你选择的顾问。根据之前的反对意见，我看不出威森加摩能够拒绝你的请求，当然，我会给出我自己的建议来批准它。

Hermione breathed an audible sigh of relief and Kingsley sat up straight, lifting a finger to ask for pause. "However, be assured that his freedom, in whatever form we eventually agree it will take, is not likely to come until after this project is complete, do you understand? He will get nothing unless he sees this through to the end.”
赫敏松了一口气，金斯莱坐直了身子，抬起一根手指要求暂停。“但是，请放心，他的自由，无论我们最终同意采取何种形式，都不太可能在这个项目完成之前到来，你明白吗？除非他把这件事坚持到底，否则他将一无所获。

“Understood. To be expected, actually, I think.”
“明白了。实际上，我认为这是意料之中的。

“Given Lucius’...” Kingsley sighed and hopelessly shuffled some fragments of parchment together. “ Singular circumstances, I will grant you permission to work with him outside the bounds of the Ministry. However –” Here he fixed Hermione with an unblinking stare over the parchment. “I expect weekly updates on your progress – a large degree of transparency will be necessary in this, particularly now that he’s involved. I wish you to be a more visible presence in the Ministry going forward, anyway.”
“鉴于卢修斯的......”金斯莱叹了口气，绝望地把一些羊皮纸碎片拼凑在一起。“特殊情况，我会允许你在魔法部的范围之外与他一起工作。然而——“说到这里，他盯着赫敏，一眨不眨地盯着羊皮纸。“我希望每周都能更新你的进度——这其中需要很大程度的透明度，尤其是现在他参与其中。无论如何，我希望你在未来的魔法部中能有更多可见的存在。

“Optics again?”
“又是光学？”

“Practicalities,” he said sternly. “Preparations. As I told you last night, there is a deputy head of department appointment due to come up in a couple of years and I would have you in an unimpeachable position to take it.”
“实用性，”他严肃地说。“准备工作。正如我昨晚告诉你的，几年后将任命一名副系主任，我希望你处于无可挑剔的位置来接受它。

“A couple of years is a long time.”
“几年是很长的时间。”

“Maybe to you,” Kingsley responded with a tired shrug as he tucked his papers into a folder. “To me, in this job, two years from now is as close and important as tomorrow.”
“也许对你来说，”金斯利疲惫地耸耸肩，把他的文件塞进了一个文件夹。“对我来说，在这份工作中，两年后和明天一样近在咫尺和重要。”

“The Wizarding World might not care so much about my reputation as a hero then,” Hermione said, trying to keep the bitter taste in her mouth out of her tone. “What if there’s some other bright young thing that will make the department look good?”
“那魔法世界可能就不那么在乎我作为英雄的名声了，”赫敏说，试图让嘴里的苦涩味道不出现在她的语气中。“如果还有其他一些聪明的年轻人会让这个部门看起来不错呢？”

“That will not make you any less suited to the job in my eyes,” he replied firmly, setting down the folder. “The optics are for everyone else. I see the reality – you are a strong and talented witch that the Ministry would be lucky to have, Hermione.”
“那不会让你不适合我眼中的这份工作，”他坚定地回答，放下了文件夹。“这些镜头是为其他人准备的。我看到了现实——你是一个强大而有才华的女巫，魔法部有幸拥有你就好了，赫敏。

When Hermione raised a doubtful brow, Kingsley said, “Please don’t take my pointing out the importance of your reputation from your role in the war as some kind of attempt to diminish your innate capabilities. It is not a case of one or the other. In fact, with intelligent utilisation of both, I see no reason why you could not be sitting in this very seat within the decade.”
当赫敏疑惑地扬起眉毛时，金斯莱说，“请不要把我从你在战争中的角色中指出你的声誉的重要性看作是某种削弱你与生俱来的能力的企图。这不是非此即彼的情况。事实上，通过巧妙地利用这两者，我认为你没有理由不能在十年内坐在这个位置上。

At that, Hermione stilled, her cheeks taking on a pink hue. “Kingsley, I’ve already said I’m coming back, you can tone down the flattery.”
听到这话，赫敏安静了下来，她的脸颊呈现出粉红色。“金斯利，我已经说过我要回来了，你可以把奉承调低一些。”

“It’s not flattery,” Kingsley said, turning his palms upwards, his fingers spread. “It is an invitation to think about your future. Something I think you have not done quite enough these past years." 
“这不是奉承，”金斯利说，手掌向上转动，手指张开。“这是一份考虑你未来的邀请。我认为你在过去几年里做得还不够。

Kingsley held her gaze for a moment longer before he cleared his throat and pulled a blank sheet of parchment towards himself. “Now, I don’t wish to be rude but our new agreement has given me some additional letters to write today and I really ought to get started.”
金斯利又凝视了她一会儿，然后清了清嗓子，把一张空白的羊皮纸拉向自己。“现在，我不想粗鲁，但我们的新协议给了我一些额外的信件今天要写，我真的应该开始了。”

“Of course! Of course,” Hermione hurriedly pushed herself to her feet and looked down at Kingsley’s head, bent over the parchment on which he was scratching a letter. “Kingsley…”
“当然！当然，“赫敏急忙站起来，低头看着金斯莱的头，弯下腰在羊皮纸上刮着一封信。“金斯利......”

He looked up and Hermione simply said, “Thank you", trying to inject as much feeling as possible into two words which felt wholly insufficient.
他抬起头，赫敏只是简单地说了一句“谢谢”，试图在两个感觉完全不够的词中注入尽可能多的感情。

Kingsley’s responding smile was warm but weary. “If you want to thank me, you can get started on this. I’ll have Evan owl you some guidance. Come and see me in a week or two with your progress and we can start thinking about an announcement.”
金斯莱回应的微笑是温暖的，但又是疲惫的。“如果你想感谢我，你可以开始做这个。我会让 Evan 猫头鹰给你一些指导。一两周后来找我，告诉你的进展情况，我们可以开始考虑发布公告。

Hermione was barely aware of the other Ministry employees in the lift as she ascended to the Atrium, her conversation with Kingsley chasing itself around her head in an anxious, excitable circle. 
赫敏在登上中庭时几乎没注意到电梯里的其他魔法部员工，她和金斯利的谈话在她脑海中以焦虑、兴奋的方式追逐着自己。

"Hermione?"
“赫敏？”

She’d gotten what she wanted. She was going to be working on something incredibly important to the future of the Wizarding World. She was going to be doing it with Lucius. Kingsley was handing her the power to make positive changes and he’d even gone so far as to suggest that she might, one day, actually be — no, she couldn’t think it. She didn’t even want it.
她得到了她想要的。她将要从事对魔法世界的未来非常重要的事情。她要和卢修斯一起做这件事。金斯利把做出积极改变的力量交给了她，他甚至暗示她有一天可能会真的成为——不，她无法思考。她甚至都不想要。

"Hermione."
“赫敏。”

But the idea that he thought it possible gave her such a surge of belief in herself that she felt she might actually be able to face whatever the Ministry tried to throw at her on her return. 
但是他认为这是可能的这个想法让她对自己有了如此大的信心，以至于她觉得她真的能够面对魔法部试图在她回来时向她扔出的任何东西。

“Hermione!”
“赫敏！”

Blinking as the sound of her own name being called broke through her reverie, Hermione realised she was already sweeping through the Atrium, the lifts far behind her. A hand on her arm made her turn and flinch before she realised that both it and the voice belonged to Harry. 
当她自己的名字被呼唤的声音打破她的遐想时，赫敏眨了眨眼，意识到她已经扫过了中庭，电梯远远地在她身后。一只手搭在她的手臂上，让她转过身来，畏缩了一下，然后她才意识到它和那个声音都属于哈利。

He was wide-eyed, his breathing slightly laboured like he’d been forced to chase her. A few Ministry employees had turned to look at them and, hand still on Hermione’s arm, he threw swift glares in every direction, wordlessly telling them all to mind their own business. Harry really had gotten incredibly good at that. 
他睁大了眼睛，呼吸略微费力，就像是被迫追赶她一样。几个魔法部的员工转过头来看他们，手仍然放在赫敏的手臂上，他迅速地向四面八方投来目光，无言地告诉他们都管好自己的事。哈利真的非常擅长这一点。

“Harry! God, I’m so sorry, I was completely in my own world,” Hermione said, turning fully towards him and removing his hand from her own to grasp his fingers between her warm, slightly clammy palms. 
“哈利！上帝啊，我很抱歉，我完全沉浸在自己的世界里，“赫敏说，完全转向他，把他的手从她自己的手上移开，用她温暖、略带湿漉漉的手掌抓住他的手指。

“I could see that,” Harry replied, looking somewhere between amused and relieved. “I didn’t expect to see you at the Ministry today. You were moving so quickly I wondered if I was hallucinating you.”
“我看得出来，”哈利回答，看起来介于好笑和松了一口气之间。“我没想到今天会在魔法部见到你。你移动得太快了，我怀疑我是不是让你产生了幻觉。

“Meeting with Kingsley,” Hermione explained. Then, seeing Harry’s raised eyebrows, she waved a hand. “You’ll hear all about it in great detail over the next few weeks but let’s just say you’ll be seeing a little more of me in the Atrium and elsewhere soon.”
“和金斯莱见面，”赫敏解释道。然后，看到哈利扬起的眉毛，她挥了挥手。“在接下来的几周里，你会听到所有关于它的信息，但你只能说，你很快就会在中庭和其他地方看到更多我。”

“Hermione, that’s fantastic!” Harry enthused, squeezing Hermione’s hand more tightly than she had held his. She felt her heart swell further. Coming back to the Ministry could be good. It could be. Especially if she and Harry were in the same department — they could face anything together.
“赫敏，那太棒了！”哈利兴奋地握住赫敏的手，比她握住他的手还紧。她感到自己的心跳得更厉害了。回到魔法部可能会很好。可能是。特别是如果她和哈利在同一个部门——他们可以一起面对任何事情。

“Hopefully it will be.” She lowered her voice, quickly looking around at the various witches and wizards streaming past them. “But keep it quiet for now. There are still some details that need to be worked out and I don’t know how Kingsley wants to play it.”
“希望会这样。”她压低了声音，迅速环顾四周，看着从他们身边流过的各种女巫和巫师。“但现在保持沉默。还有一些细节需要解决，我不知道金斯利想怎么演。

Harry winked at her, tapping a finger against the side of his nose, and Hermione beamed at him in response. 
哈利对她眨了眨眼，用一根手指敲了敲他的鼻子侧面，赫敏也对他露出了笑容作为回应。

"It’s nice seeing you look so happy," he said. "Especially here."
“看到你看起来这么开心，真是太好了，”他说。“尤其是这里。”

"You’re saying that like you have reason to believe I might not be." Hermione tried to say it jokingly but Harry read the wariness in her face easily.
“你是这么说的，就像你有理由相信我可能不是。”赫敏试图开玩笑地说出来，但哈利很容易就读出她脸上的警惕。

"Well, I just…" He sighed and shrugged. "Ginny said you looked a bit off at the end of last night so when I saw you practically running back there I did wonder."
“嗯，我只是......”他叹了口气，耸了耸肩。“金妮说你昨晚结束时看起来有点不对劲，所以当我看到你几乎跑回去时，我确实想知道。”

Hermione cast her mind back to the end of the night when she’d told Ginny and Neville that she’d hang around Malfoy Manor until the end of the event. Had it really only been the previous evening? She felt like so much had happened in the intervening hours. 
赫敏回想起那天晚上的结尾，她告诉金妮和纳威，她会在马尔福庄园闲逛，直到活动结束。真的只是前一天晚上吗？她觉得在这期间发生了很多事情。

“I was just tired. Really busy night, you know, and a pretty unexpected occasion so…”
“我只是累了。你知道的，晚上真的很忙，而且是一个非常出乎意料的场合，所以......”

Yeah.” Harry shot her a guilty grin and Hermione returned it with a smile of her own that told him she didn’t hold him responsible for any of it. 
是的。哈利向她露出一个内疚的笑容，赫敏也以她自己的微笑回应，告诉他她不让他为此负责。

"It’s just –" Harry grimaced. "I think Ginny was hoping you’d swing by after. Ron and Neville made things up. It was really something, actually – Ron held Neville’s hair back when a firewhiskey shot made him sick. Quite touching. They insisted on sharing the sofa even though we told them we have more than enough space."
“只是——”哈利做了个鬼脸。“我想金妮是希望你之后能过来。罗恩和内维尔编造了事情。实际上，这真的很了不起——当一瓶烈火威士忌让纳威感到恶心时，罗恩把他的头发往后拉。相当感人。他们坚持共用沙发，即使我们告诉他们我们有足够的空间。

Hermione snorted, her shoulders jumping. "I'm actually sorry I missed that." Though she certainly didn't regret how she'd ended up spending her night. "Like I said, though, it was a busy night and I just wanted to get to bed."
赫敏哼了一声，肩膀跳了起来。“我真的很抱歉我错过了那个。”尽管她当然不后悔她最终是如何度过这个夜晚的。“不过，就像我说的，那是一个忙碌的夜晚，我只想上床睡觉。”

Here Harry became awkward, like he wasn't sure how best to proceed. "So you did get home?" 
这时哈利变得尴尬起来，就像他不确定该如何最好地进行一样。“所以你真的回家了？”

When Hermione didn’t respond, instead pressing her lips in a thin line and dropping her eyes to the shining tiles of the Atrium, Harry gripped the back of his neck, his face contorting with an awkward cringe. 
赫敏没有回应，而是把嘴唇压成一条细线，把眼睛投向中庭闪闪发光的瓷砖，哈利抓住了他的后颈，他的脸因尴尬的畏缩而扭曲。

"It’s just…well, I stopped by your flat because Ginny was worried that you hadn’t shown up and you’d seemed so out of sorts and you sort of…weren’t…home."
“只是......嗯，我去了你的公寓，因为金妮担心你没有出现，而且你看起来那么不正常，你有点......不是。。。家。

"I stayed at Malfoy Manor."
“我住在马尔福庄园。”

She made the admission so baldly, so boldly, eyes rising to meet Harry’s, that she might have slapped him given the slack-jawed expression he wore in response. 
她如此赤裸裸地承认了这一点，如此大胆地抬起眼睛与哈利的眼睛对视，考虑到他作为回应时松弛的表情，她可能会扇他一巴掌。

"Oh." He blinked rapidly. "I see. Okay. Well, that’s good that you can…feel…” Harry waved a searching hand, still gripping the back of his neck with the other. “Y’know…that they have…that kind of…space."
“哦。”他迅速地眨了眨眼。“我明白了。好。嗯，这很好，你可以......感觉......”哈利挥了挥一只寻找的手，另一只手仍然紧紧抓住他的后颈。“你知道的......他们有......那种......空间。

"Yeah."
“是的。”

Silence fell between them, Harry visibly animated with a desire to ask more questions and Hermione tense and still with reticence to say anything more.
他们之间陷入了沉默，哈利显然很想问更多问题，而赫敏则紧张起来，仍然不敢再说什么。

"Do you want to come over tonight instead?" Harry finally asked. 
“你今晚想过来吗？”哈利终于问道。

When Hermione looked hesitant, Harry pressed. "It's been ages since we did one of our dinners and I think Ginny would really appreciate it. She was worried about you last night. When she didn’t hear from you and you weren’t home – you know how she gets."
当赫敏看起来犹豫不决时，哈利追问道。“我们已经很久没有吃过一次晚饭了，我想金妮会非常感激的。她昨晚很担心你。当她没有收到你的消息，你也不在家时——你知道她是怎么回事。

Hermione swallowed down the distasteful mix of guilt and the desire to snap at Harry that she was a grown woman with her own private affairs, opting to nod instead. An argument in the Ministry Atrium was not what she wanted. 
赫敏吞下了令人厌恶的内疚和想对哈利发火的渴望，说她是一个有自己私事的成年女人，而是选择了点头。魔法部中庭的争论不是她想要的。

"I won't cook," Harry offered and when Hermione shot him a puzzled look he explained, "Ginny thinks that'll make invitations to our home more appealing."
“我不会做饭，”哈利提议，当赫敏困惑地看了他一眼时，他解释说，“金妮觉得这会让我们家的邀请更有吸引力。

Hermione couldn't help but laugh. She hadn't seen enough of her friends in recent weeks. "Well, now that I have that assurance of course I'll come over. I'd love to."
赫敏忍不住笑了起来。最近几周，她没见过足够多的朋友。“嗯，既然我有这个保证，我当然会过来的。我很乐意。

"Great!" Harry beamed. "Great. I’ll let Ginny know – she’ll be so happy. Call it 7?"
“太好了！”哈利笑了。“太好了。我会让 Ginny 知道——她会很高兴的。叫 7 号？

"Sure," Hermione said, nodding. "I'll bring the wine."
“当然，”赫敏点点头说。“我来拿酒来。”

更多注释见本章末尾Lucius was already in the library when Hermione returned later that evening. He was just depositing a heavy pile of books on the desk that was, in his eyes, now purely hers when the fire blazed green and she appeared spinning like a top at its centre.
那天晚上赫敏回来时，卢修斯已经在图书馆里了。他只是把一堆沉重的书放在书桌上，在他眼里，这本来是她的，这时火堆闪耀着绿色的光芒，她像陀螺一样在中心旋转。

Stumbling out of the grate, distractedly brushing herself down, she looked up without really seeing him. It was, Lucius mused, going to take some time to get used to someone looking that happy to see him. He couldn't deny, however, that seeing her brought him an unexpectedly large amount of peace after what had ended up being a very unsettled afternoon.
她跌跌撞撞地从格栅里走出来，心不在焉地拂过自己，抬起头来，却没有真正看到他。然后，她停下来，正确地抬起头来，当她看到他看着她时，她的脸上露出了灿烂的笑容。卢修斯沉思着，要花一些时间来适应一个看起来那么高兴看到他的人。然而，他不能否认，在经历了一个非常不安的下午之后，见到她给他带来了意想不到的平静。

"Just who I was coming to see," she said, swiftly rounding the table to close the space between them. Wrapping her arms around him, she stood on her tiptoes to place a kiss on his lips and, when she drew her face away, he saw she was still grinning, her eyes creased at the corners.
“我就是来见谁的，”她说，迅速绕过桌子以拉近他们之间的距离。她搂着他，踮起脚尖在他的嘴唇上亲了一下，当她把脸移开时，他看到她仍然在咧嘴笑，眼角皱起。

“我是否可以假设，”卢修斯说，他的眉毛带着讽刺的笑容，“根据你现在普遍的喜悦，你和沙克尔博尔特的会面是积极的吗？

Practically hovering with excitement, Hermione nodded vigorously up at him. "My 'chaotic at best' negotiating style," she said, dropping her voice into a crude imitation of his drawl, "was a success."
赫敏几乎兴奋地盘旋着，用力地朝他点了点头。“我'充其量是混乱的'谈判风格，”她说，压低了声音，粗暴地模仿了他的拖沓，“很成功。

"Imagine my surprise," he said, the corner of his mouth quirking.

There was, of course, nothing surprising about it. Based on what she'd told him that very morning, he suspected that Shacklebolt had ambitions for Hermione in the Ministry. In his time, he had known Ministers to select favourites – with different Ministers seeking out vastly different qualities – and Hermione struck him as a good match for Shacklebolt’s particular brand of post-war idealism. Her righteousness and work ethic made her an indefatigable force in a time of general fatigue. Though he couldn't be entirely certain what Shacklebolt’s intentions were, a task of such magnitude and an invitation into the DMLE suggested they were not insignificant. Lucius was certainly keen to see them unfold.
当然，这并没有什么奇怪的。根据她那天早上告诉他的话，他怀疑沙克尔博尔特在魔法部对赫敏有野心。在他那个时代，他知道部长们会挑选最喜欢的人——不同的部长们会寻找截然不同的品质——赫敏觉得他很适合沙克尔博尔特特有的战后理想主义。她的正义和职业道德使她在普遍疲惫的时期成为一股不屈不挠的力量。虽然他不能完全确定沙克尔博尔特的意图是什么，但如此艰巨的任务和加入 DMLE 的邀请表明他们并非微不足道。卢修斯当然很想看到他们展开。

"You'll be working with me on the project as my consultant,” Hermione said. “For the whole thing. Kingsley quite agreed with the reasoning. We can do it from here, too, but I'll have to deliver weekly updates in the Ministry." When Lucius raised his eyebrows, she explained "transparency," with a dismissive shrug.
“你会作为我的顾问和我一起做这个项目，”赫敏说。“为了整件事。金斯利完全同意这个理由。我们也可以从这里开始，但我必须在魔法部每周提供更新。当卢修斯扬起眉毛时，她不屑一顾地耸了耸肩，解释了“透明度”。

“当它完成时，无论何时，无论你、金斯利和威森加摩之间最终达成什么和解协议，都会采取行动。”她停顿了一下，打量着他的脸。“以前没有。”

“A see it through or see nothing arrangement again, then,” Lucius replied, trying not to sound too disgruntled. Realistically, he'd have been more surprised if they'd made any kind of concession. There was, in fact, a good chance that Shacklebolt was hoping he wouldn’t see it through. The thought of proving him wrong and forcing his hand was more than enough to sustain Lucius.
“那么，要么看透，要么什么都没看到，”卢修斯回答道，尽量不让自己听起来太不满。实际上，如果他们做出任何让步，他会更感到惊讶。事实上，沙克尔博尔特很有可能希望他不会看穿这一切。证明他是错的，强迫他出手的想法就足以支撑卢修斯。

"You'll still do it?" she asked. "Even with that restriction? We don't know how long this will take, remember."
“你还会这样做吗？”“即使有那个限制？我们不知道这需要多长时间，记住。

Giving her an indulgent smile, Lucius slid a hand to the back of her neck and drew her in for a kiss. To his satisfaction, the frenetic, bouncing energy occasioned by her success with Shacklebolt and her worry about him lessened slightly and she melted into him. 
卢修斯对她露出一个纵容的微笑，将一只手滑到她的后颈上，将她拉进去亲吻。令他满意的是，她在 Shacklebolt 的成功和她对他的担忧所带来的狂热、弹跳的能量略微减轻，她融入了他。

"I have no intention of disappointing you," he said, his voice low as he kept his face close to hers. "Would I have bothered searching out these books if I did?"
“我不想让你失望，”他说，他的声音很低，把脸贴近了她的脸。“如果我这样做了，我会费心去找这些书吗？”

Arms still wrapped around him, she turned her head to look down at the books he'd piled up on the desk. 
她仍然搂着他，转过头来，低头看着他堆在书桌上的书。

They were all legal textbooks that he hoped would help them in their research of the pro-Pure-blood laws. There wasn’t, he had supposed, a better library to start with for that particular subject matter. 
“你很热，”她说，从他的怀抱中抽出来，拿起书，读起书名。他们都是法律教科书，他希望能帮助他们研究亲纯血统的法律。他认为，对于这个特定主题来说，没有更好的库可以作为起点。

“急于分散注意力，”卢修斯说，用一只手揉了揉他紧张的眼睛。书脊上褪色的文字和图书馆昏暗的灯光让他眯起眼睛。

“什么分散了你的注意力？”赫敏问道，从她随意打开的一堆书顶端的书中回头瞥了他一眼。

"That was a while ago," Hermione said, worrying her lower lip between her teeth .
“那是很久以前的事了，”赫敏说，她的下唇在牙齿之间担心。

卢修斯不满地哼了一声表示同意，促使她伸出手来握住了他的手。“德拉科会确保你一有消息就得到消息，”她温和地说。“你知道他会的。”

卢修斯的眼睛看着他们合在一起的手，歪着头表示认可。她肯定是对的。德拉科不会把他蒙在鼓里，当然纳西莎也不会恶毒到——

图书馆门口传来的声音让他们俩都僵住了。卢修斯抬头越过赫敏的头，看到门口的纳西莎，他的下巴紧紧了。

卢修斯如释重负，力量足以让他头晕目眩，他把赫敏捏得更紧了。它一定很顺利。一个孙子，大概很健康。不仅仅是一个孙子，一个继承马尔福名字的孙子。

那是一个沉闷阴沉的日子，纳西莎站在火堆的光圈外，但当他透过昏暗的灯光凝视着她时，卢修斯觉得她看起来异常苍白，在传达这个好消息时，她的语气出奇地平淡。

“布莱克女士，格兰杰小姐，”纳西莎简洁地说。“就说布莱克女士。”

“为什么......”赫敏的目光滑向哈利，哈利选择在那个时刻喝了一杯。“她为什么在那儿会打扰我？”

“I saw you talking to her and she had her usual… glacial aura,” Ginny said, pausing in her chopping to give Hermione a conspiratorial smile over her shoulder. “I was worried she might have said something to you to put a dampener on your night.”
“我看到你和她说话，她有她平常的......冰冷的光环，“金妮说，在她的劈砍中停顿了一下，在她的肩膀上给了赫敏一个阴谋般的微笑。“我担心她可能会对你说了什么，让你的夜晚变得闷闷不乐。”

“No, I – she didn’t bother me,” Hermione said, the pace of her heartbeat increasing from a trot to a gallop. “We barely spoke.”
“不，我——她没有打扰我，”赫敏说，她的心跳速度从小跑变成了疾驰。“我们几乎没有说话。”

“I get the impression she wouldn’t need many words to ruin a night,” Ginny muttered.
“我感觉她不需要很多话就能毁掉一个夜晚，”金妮咕哝道。

“Ginny,” Harry said, warning in his tone. “Don’t forget what she did –”
“金妮，”哈利说，语气中带着警告。“别忘了她做了什么——”

“I know, I know,” said Ginny and Hermione could practically hear the roll of her eyes. “She wasn’t very happy though, was she? Did you hear her talking about her divorce? Nearly bit that poor bloke’s head off.”
“我知道，我知道，”金妮说，赫敏几乎能听到她翻白眼的声音。“不过她不是很开心，对吧？你听过她谈论离婚吗？差点把那个可怜的家伙的头咬掉了。

“She was just telling people?” Hermione asked, aghast. After Lucius had been so keen to keep it quiet. Undoubtedly they had had words about it when Narcissa had gone to him. That went some way to explaining his mood when Hermione had gotten to him that night. Had it actually been a good idea to leave them in the Manor to come to the dinner?
“她只是在告诉人们？”赫敏惊恐地问。在卢修斯如此热衷于保持沉默之后。毫无疑问，当纳西莎去找他时，他们已经说过这件事了。这在某种程度上解释了他那天晚上赫敏来找他的心情。把他们留在庄园来参加晚宴真的是个好主意吗？

Ginny and Harry glanced at one another and Ginny, placing her knife down, turned to Hermione and crossed her arms. “You knew?” she asked. “No one else seemed to have heard a thing about it.”
金妮和哈利互相看了一眼，金妮放下刀，转向赫敏，交叉着双臂。“你知道吗？”“其他人似乎都没有听说过这件事。”

“I…” Hermione looked down into her wine. “Well, I found out sort of by accident ages ago.” She shook her head, remembering the unpleasantness of that day. “It was a whole thing and, honestly, I’d rather not go into it.”
“我......”赫敏低头看着她的酒。“嗯，我很久以前就知道了。”她摇摇头，想起那天的不愉快。“这是一整件事，老实说，我宁愿不去深入研究。”

“Ages ago?” Ginny asked, incredulous. ”And you didn’t tell us?”
“很久以前？”金妮难以置信地问道。“你没告诉我们吗？”

Frowning, Hermione looked up at her. “It wasn’t really any of my business in the first place.”
赫敏皱着眉头，抬头看着她。“这本来就不关我的事。”

Eyebrows raised, Ginny turned back to the counter and scooped a handful of chopped vegetables into a large bowl. “I don't know if I would keep secrets for Lucius Malfoy, Hermione.” She picked up the knife again and placed another tomato on the chopping board. “He might get the wrong idea.”
金妮扬起眉毛，转身回到柜台前，把一把切碎的蔬菜舀进一个大碗里。“我不知道我是否会为卢修斯·马尔福保守秘密，赫敏。”她再次拿起刀，在砧板上放了另一个西红柿。“他可能会想错主意。”

“The wrong idea about what?” Hermione asked, unable to keep a touch of sharpness out of her voice. “I wasn't keeping his secret, anyway; I was letting his private business be just that.”
“关于什么的错误想法？”赫敏问道，她的声音里忍不住有一丝尖锐。“反正我没有保守他的秘密;我让他的私人生意就这样。

“Yes, but he might see it as –”
“是的，但他可能会把它看作是——”

“No more talk of the Malfoys,” Harry interrupted loudly from his seat, his eyes darting between Hermione's deepening frown and Ginny’s rising shoulders. “Hermione, I told Ginny you’re coming back to the Ministry.”
“别再提马尔福家了，”哈利从座位上大声打断，他的眼睛在赫敏加深的眉头和金妮抬起的肩膀之间来回扫视。“赫敏，我告诉金妮你要回魔法部了。”

“Yes!” Ginny exclaimed, her voice sounding overly bright. “Tell us everything.”
“是的！”金妮惊呼道，她的声音听起来过于明亮。“告诉我们一切。”

Attempting to settle the roiling in her belly, Hermione took a moment to take another sip of her wine before answering. 
赫敏试图平息肚子里的翻腾，她花了一点时间又喝了一口酒，然后回答道。

“I am. Kingsley asked me to come back to take a look through a bunch of the old pro-Pure-blood laws to start making things fairer. I’ll be redrafting most, maybe overturning some; that kind of thing. I’ll be coming in as part of the Department of Magical Law Enforcement.”
“我是。金斯利让我回来看看一堆旧的亲纯血统法律，以开始让事情变得更公平。我会重新起草大部分，也许会推翻一些;诸如此类的事情。我将作为魔法执法部的一员进来。

“Bloody hell, Hermione,” Harry said, looking impressed. “That’s big.”
“的地狱，赫敏，”哈利说，看起来印象深刻。“好大。”

“It’s huge!” Ginny agreed enthusiastically. “But he couldn’t have picked anyone better – no one will be fairer than you. And you and Harry will get to work more closely together since you’ll be back in DMLE. It's perfect, you get him out of his habit of working through lunch.”
“好大啊！”金妮热情地同意了。“但他挑选的人再好不过了——没有人会比你更公平。 自从您将回到 DMLE 以来，您和 Harry 将可以更紧密地合作。这太完美了，你让他摆脱了吃午饭时工作的习惯。

“Well, I’ll definitely try to help with that,” Hermione said with a warm smile in Harry’s direction. “But I’ll be working directly with Lucius Malfoy on the project itself so I’ll only be in and out of the Ministry.”
“嗯，我肯定会试着帮忙的，”赫敏朝哈利的方向带着温暖的微笑说。“但我会直接与卢修斯·马尔福合作处理这个项目本身，所以我只会进出魔法部。”

Ginny’s knife skidded across the chopping board with a loud squeak just as the kitchen door swung open and a rosy-cheeked, red-eared Ron waltzed into the room wearing a wide grin.
金妮的刀在砧板上滑过，发出一声响亮的吱吱声，这时厨房的门打开了，脸颊红润、耳红的罗恩带着灿烂的笑容跳着华尔兹走进了房间。

“Sorry I’m late,” Ron said, oblivious to the tension into which he’d walked, shrugging off his jacket. “I was at the pub with Neville, Luna and Parkinson.” Ron grabbed a bread roll from the table and tore into it with his teeth. 
“对不起，我来晚了，”罗恩说，完全没有注意到他走过时的紧张情绪，耸了耸肩。“我和内维尔、卢娜和帕金森一起在酒吧。”罗恩从桌子上抓起一个面包卷，用牙齿撕了进去。

“Tell you what,” he continued through a mouthful of bread. “Parkinson is actually kind of funny. Totally different from the way Luna is funny, obviously – she was saying some mad stuff tonight, by the way – but definitely funny. I reckon Malfoy held her back at school."
“告诉你什么，”他继续吃了一口面包。“帕金森其实有点有趣。显然，这与 Luna 的搞笑方式完全不同——顺便说一句，她今晚说了一些疯狂的话——但绝对有趣。我估计马尔福在学校里拖了她的后腿。

Ron collapsed into a chair beside Harry at the dining table, clutching his bread roll. As he looked at them all in turn, his chewing slowed. “What? What’s happened?”
罗恩瘫倒在餐桌旁哈利旁边的椅子上，手里攥着他的面包卷。当他依次看着他们所有人时，他的咀嚼速度变慢了。“什么？发生了什么事？

“Hermione was just telling us she’s going back to the Ministry,” Harry said faintly, rubbing a tight circle on his temple with his fore and middle fingers.
“赫敏只是告诉我们她要回魔法部去了，”哈利淡淡地说，用食指和中指在他的太阳穴上划了一个紧紧的圆圈。

“Brilliant!” Ron cried, holding his bread aloft in celebration. “Can’t believe Kingsley finally managed to convince you. He’s been angling at that for ages, hasn’t he?” 
“太棒了！”罗恩喊道，高举着他的面包庆祝。“真不敢相信金斯利终于说服了你。他已经为此烦恼了很久了，不是吗？

“Mmm,” Ginny said, slowly turning to look at Hermione, leaning on the counter. “She’s going to be re-working a bunch of pro-Pure-blood laws for DMLE.”
“嗯，”金妮说，慢慢地转过身来看着靠在柜台上的赫敏。“她将为 DMLE 重新制定一堆支持纯血统的法律。”

Puffing out a gust of impressed air, Ron gave Hermione a proud look. “That’s one hell of a job for one person, Hermione,” he said. “But Kingsley always did think a lot –”
罗恩吐出一股印象深刻的空气，骄傲地看了赫敏一眼。“赫敏，对一个人来说，这真是一件地狱般的工作，”他说。“但金斯利总是想很多——”

“It’s not a job for one person,” Ginny said. “Apparently.”
“这不是一个人的工作，”金妮说。“显然。”

Ron’s face fell slightly. “Oh?”
罗恩的脸色微微一沉。“哦？”

All three turned to look expectantly at Hermione whose cheeks were almost painfully warm. “Kingsley and I agreed that I should work on the project with a Pure-blood,” she said, a hint of defensiveness creeping into her voice. “To avoid any accusations of bias.”
三个人都转过头来，期待地看着赫敏，她的脸颊几乎温暖得令人痛苦。“金斯利和我同意我应该和一个纯血统的人一起做这个项目，”她说，她的声音里带着一丝防御。“为了避免任何偏见的指责。”

“Who’zat then?” Ron asked, frowning as he took another bite of bread.
“那是谁？”罗恩问道，他皱着眉头又咬了一口面包。

“Lucius Malfoy.” 
“卢修斯·马尔福。”

Ron froze mid-chew. “Oh,” he said, muffled by the bread. He, Harry and Ginny all shared a meaningful look, then, swallowing his food, Ron cleared his throat and looked around the table. “Any wine?”
罗恩在咀嚼中愣住了。“哦，”他说，被面包压得闷闷不乐。他、哈利和金妮都意味深长地看了一眼，然后，罗恩吞下了他的食物，清了清嗓子，环顾了一下桌子。“有酒吗？”

Springing to life and seemingly glad of something to do, Harry lunged for the bottle and started pouring Ron a generous glass while Hermione looked between her three friends in turn, perplexed.
哈利活了过来，似乎很高兴能做点什么，他冲向瓶子，开始给罗恩倒一大杯，而赫敏则困惑地轮流看着她的三个朋友。

“What was that look?” she asked, waving a pointed finger at them.
“那是什么眼神？” 她问道，一边向他们挥舞着一根尖锐的手指。

“Nothing,” said Harry immediately. 
“没什么，”哈利立刻说。

“There was no look,” Ron said after taking a large swig from his glass.
“没看，”罗恩从杯子里喝了一大口后说。

“There bloody was,” Hermione insisted.
“那儿血腥，”赫敏坚持说。

Both Harry and Ron looked towards Ginny, who pursed her lips hesitantly. “That’s…don’t you think that’s a pretty surprising thing for Lucius Malfoy to want to do?”
哈利和罗恩都看向金妮，金妮犹豫地抿了抿嘴唇。“那是......你不觉得卢修斯·马尔福想这么做是一件相当令人惊讶的事情吗？

Shrugging, Hermione said, “I made him see the sense of it. Besides, he knows it’ll help his case with the Wizengamot if he’s seen to be doing things like this – things to show he’s making changes."
赫敏耸耸肩说，“我让他明白了。此外，他知道如果有人看到他正在做这样的事情——表明他正在做出改变，那会对他与威森加摩的案子有所帮助。

“Even so,” said Ginny.
“即便如此，”金妮说。

“Even so…what?”
“即便如此......什么？

“Well, he’s just…he’s not exactly likely to make it the easiest job in the world, is he?” Ginny asked. “If you needed Pure-bloods to help you with this, couldn’t you have asked me or Ron? We’d be happy to do it.”
“嗯，他只是......他不可能把这当作世界上最轻松的工作，对吧？金妮问道。“如果你需要纯血统来帮你，你就不能问我或罗恩吗？我们很乐意这样做。

Ron nodded enthusiastically to show his willingness to help. “No,” Hermione said, growing frustrated. “The whole point is that he won’t make it easy. We need the differing  perspectives.” 
罗恩热情地点头，表示他愿意提供帮助。“不，”赫敏说，越来越沮丧。“关键是他不会让事情变得容易。我们需要不同的观点。

“Hermione,” Harry said, his voice gentle like he was afraid of provoking her ire. “Have you stopped to think about other reasons Malfoy might have for doing this?”
“赫敏，”哈利说，他的声音很温柔，就像他害怕惹怒她一样。“你有没有停下来想一想马尔福做这件事的其他原因？”

Setting her wine glass on the kitchen counter with a loud clack , Hermione crossed her arms over her middle. “It certainly sounds like you have.”
赫敏把酒杯放在厨房的柜台上，咔嚓一声，双臂交叉在她的中间。“听起来你肯定有。”

Glancing anxiously at Ron and Ginny, Harry placed his own glass down carefully. “Okay, look,” he said, holding up his hands.  “We don’t want to freak you out or anything. It’s just, we’ve been talking, y’know – all of us, and Neville, and Luna –”
哈利焦急地瞥了一眼罗恩和金妮，小心翼翼地把自己的杯子放下。“好吧，你看，”他举起双手说。“我们不想吓到你或做任何事情。只是，我们一直在说话，你知道的——我们所有人，还有纳威，还有卢娜——”

“About?” Hermione asked, her voice measured while her heart cantered against her ribs.
“大约？”赫敏问道，她的声音很谨慎，她的心脏在她的肋骨上慢跑。

“About Malfoy and the time you’ve been spending with him.”
“关于马尔福和你和他在一起的时光。”

“I see.” Her heart had grown so loud, she was beginning to suspect it had journeyed up between her ears and replaced her brain.  
“我明白了。”她的心跳变得如此响亮，她开始怀疑它已经从她的耳朵之间爬上来，取代了她的大脑。

“It’s been a while now,” Harry continued. “Clearly he’s gotten over your whole…being a Muggleborn thing but you’ve been getting to know him in pretty unusual circumstances, haven’t you? He’s been locked up a long time – divorced, apparently. For months you’ve been his main company apart from his son –”
“已经有一段时间了，”哈利继续说。“显然，他已经控制了你的整个......你是个麻瓜出身的人，但你一直在非常不寻常的情况下了解他，不是吗？他被关了很久——显然是离婚了。几个月来，除了他的儿子之外，你一直是他的主要伙伴——”

“And you’ve being pretty fucking kind when he doesn’t deserve it,” Ginny piped up. “Neville told us about the plant you took him and you’re going to all this effort to help him get free –”
“而且你他妈的还挺善良的，当他不配的时候，”金妮哼哼哼唧。“纳威告诉我们你带走了他那棵植物的事，你要尽一切努力帮助他获得自由——”

“Plus, Ginny said you said he apologised to you –” added Ron, looking back at his sister who nodded vigorously.
“另外，金妮说你说他向你道歉了——”罗恩补充道，回头看向他的妹妹，她用力地点了点头。

“And he lets you use his library so you’re there even more –” Harry said.
“而且他让你使用他的图书馆，这样你就可以在那里呆得更久了——”哈利说。

“And that party last night!” Ron cried. “I mean, that was something else. It –"
“还有昨晚的那个派对！”罗恩喊道。“我的意思是，那是另一回事。它——”

“And you’ve got a great arse,” interjected Ginny, extending her hands to Hermione admiringly. “Fantastic, actually.”
“而且你的屁股真棒，”金妮插嘴说，钦佩地向赫敏伸出手。“实际上，太棒了。”

“And now this,” Harry finished, weakly. “Maybe when all this started he wanted his freedom but…well, do you think it could be something else now?”
“现在这个，”哈利虚弱地说完。“也许当这一切开始时，他想要他的自由，但是......嗯，你觉得现在可能是别的东西吗？

“Like?”
“比如？”

“Don’t you think he could be, y’know, into you?”
“你知道，你不觉得他会喜欢你吗？”

“Luna said love tonight, y’know,” Ron said in an undertone.
“露娜今晚说了爱，你知道的，”罗恩低声说。

“Don’t be ridiculous,” Ginny snapped at the top of her brother’s head. “We agreed he’s probably just trying to put his end away so it doesn’t fall off from lack of use. What the hell does Luna know?”
“别荒谬，”金妮对着她哥哥的头顶吼道。“我们一致认为他可能只是想把他的一端收起来，这样它就不会因为缺乏使用而脱落。露娜他妈知道什么？

“You know what she’s like, she has a real sense for stuff.”
“你知道她是什么样的人，她对事物有真正的感觉。”

Ginny scoffed and rolled her eyes. “We just want you to be on your guard, Hermione. Be more careful. We don’t want him to start thinking he’s, like, entitled to you or something, it’s –”
金妮嘲笑着翻了个白眼。“我们只是希望你保持警惕，赫敏。要多加小心。我们不希望他开始认为他有资格拥有你或其他什么，这是——”

As her friends had been speaking, cutting across one another, Hermione’s shoulders had started shaking until, finally, a loud burst of laughter escaped her, cutting Ginny off. Curling into herself, Hermione trembled and leaned back against the counter for support, seemingly unable to stop. The idea that they were arguing over whether or not Lucius might find her attractive – the suggestion that she should be wary of that – was just too much. 
当她的朋友们互相交谈时，赫敏的肩膀开始颤抖，直到最后，她发出一阵大笑，打断了金妮。赫敏蜷缩着身体，颤抖着向后靠在柜台上寻求支撑，似乎停不下来。他们争论 Lucius 是否会觉得她有吸引力——建议她应该警惕这一点——实在是太过分了。

She didn’t know how she and Lucius’ relationship would go but she knew she could be working with him for months, even years, on this project. Would her friends be watching her with furrowed brows and worried eyes for that entire period? Continuously talking to one another and her, convinced their covert observations somehow gave them true insight into what was happening? It would drive her mad.
她不知道她和 Lucius 的关系会如何发展，但她知道她可以在这个项目上与他合作数月，甚至数年。她的朋友们会不会在整个时期都皱着眉头和担忧的眼神看着她？不断地与彼此和她交谈，相信他们的秘密观察以某种方式让他们真正了解发生了什么？这会让她发疯。

What else could she expect, however, when she didn’t tell them the truth? What else could they do?
然而，当她不告诉他们真相时，她还能期待什么呢？他们还能做什么呢？

“Hermione, what –”
“赫敏，什么——”

“D’you know what?” Hermione said, wiping tears of mirth from the corners of her eyes as she straightened up to look at Ron, Ginny and Harry. “I hope he does.”
“你知道吗？”赫敏说，擦去眼角的泪水，直起身来看着罗恩、金妮和哈利。“我希望他能。”

“What?”
“什么？”

“I hope he does !” she said, laughing more faintly and shrugging helplessly. “I hope he does love me.”
“我希望他能！”她说，笑得更微弱了，无奈地耸了耸肩。“我希望他真的爱我。”

Several beats of stunned silence met her declaration and not a single, even faintly bemused smile. Then, a deep furrow forming in his brow, Ron said, “That’s a bit sadistic, Hermione. The bloke is absolutely the worst, no doubt about it, but to actually try to have him fall –”
她的宣言中响起了几声震惊的沉默，没有一个，甚至是微弱的困惑的微笑。然后，罗恩的眉头上皱起了眉头，他说，“这有点虐待狂，赫敏。毫无疑问，这个家伙绝对是最糟糕的，但居然要让他摔倒——”

Stepping forward, Ginny placed a hand on Ron’s shoulder to stop him mid-sentence. Her eyes were fixed on Hermione, piercing. “I don’t think that's not what she means, Ron.”
金妮向前走，将一只手放在罗恩的肩膀上，阻止了他的话。她的眼睛盯着赫敏，目不转睛。“我不认为她不是这个意思，罗恩。”

Looking up at Ginny and then at Hermione, Ron made a face like they had just asked him to recite the five exceptions to Gamp's Law of Elemental Transfiguration. “Well, what does she mean? What do you mean, Hermione?”
罗恩抬头看了看金妮，又看了看赫敏，做了个鬼脸，就像他们刚刚让他背诵甘普元素变形定律的五个例外一样。“嗯，她是什么意思？你什么意思，赫敏？

Ignoring Ron, Ginny addressed Hermione, “You don’t want Malfoy to love you because it’d be bad for him, do you?”
金妮无视罗恩，对赫敏说：“你不想让马尔福爱你，因为那对他不好，对吧？

“Hermione?” Ron asked.
“赫敏？”罗恩问道。

这是线路的尽头，真的，不是吗？它必须被公之于众，因为这种秘密不仅越来越站不住脚，而且令人难以忍受。这种认识并没有使告诉他们变得不那么可怕。

In the quiet that fell over them, Harry frowned and raised his nose into the air. “Can you smell burning?” he asked.
在笼罩他们的寂静中，哈利皱起眉头，把鼻子抬向空中。“你能闻到燃烧的味道吗？”

“The fucking chicken!” Ginny shrieked, snatching her wand out of her jeans pocket and pointing it at the oven. The door fell open with a clang and smoke billowed into the room, making them cover their mouths and squint their eyes as they coughed loudly. 
“那他妈的鸡！”金妮尖叫着，从牛仔裤口袋里掏出魔杖，指向烤箱。门哐当一声打开了，浓烟滚滚进入房间，让他们捂住嘴，眯起眼睛大声咳嗽。

The normality of the activities that followed felt almost like a dream to Hermione. Helping Ginny to salvage the chicken, grabbing cutlery, passing plates, serving the food – they were all things that would have happened if she hadn’t told them about Malfoy.
接下来的正常活动对赫敏来说几乎就像一场梦。帮助金妮抢救鸡，拿餐具，传递盘子，端上食物——如果她没有告诉他们关于马尔福的事情，这些事情都会发生。

But there was a friction underlying the friendly domesticity that made it hard for her to relax. Lucius was such an overhanging presence in the room, the empty chair at the table might as well have been filled by him. As they ate and talked, Hermione could feel Ron and Harry’s curious stares on her from across the table from time to time, while, beside her, Ginny barely looked at her at all. It was, Hermione reflected, Ginny’s feelings which concerned her most, particularly after their conversation with Draco.
但是，友好的家庭生活背后存在着摩擦，使她难以放松。卢修斯在房间里是一个悬而未决的存在，桌边的空椅子可能已经被他坐满了。他们吃饭聊天的时候，赫敏能感觉到罗恩和哈利不时从桌子对面好奇地注视着她，而在她旁边，金妮几乎什么也没看她。赫敏想，金妮的感受最让她担心，尤其是在他们和德拉科谈话之后。

When their plates were clear and it came time to open the second bottle of wine, Ginny said, “Hermione, I’m fine.” Finally, she turned to Hermione, looking both amused and exasperated. “I can feel you worrying in my direction.”
当他们的盘子收拾干净，该打开第二瓶酒时，金妮说：“赫敏，我没事。最后，她转向赫敏，看起来既好笑又生气。“我能感觉到你在为我的方向担心。”

“I feel like I need to explain more –”
“我觉得我需要解释更多——”

“Look, we weren’t there for everything,” Ginny said, shrugging as she picked up her newly-filled wine. “And it’s true, you haven’t exactly been telling us things, so it might take us a while to wrap our heads around this.”
“你看，我们不是为了所有事情都在那儿，”金妮说，她耸了耸肩，拿起了她新装满的酒。“这是真的，你还没有完全告诉我们事情，所以我们可能需要一段时间才能弄清楚这一点。”

“We will try though,” Harry said, meeting Hermione’s eyes as he leaned over the table to top up her glass.
“不过我们会试试，”哈利说，与赫敏的眼睛对上，赫敏俯身在桌子上为她的杯子加满水。

“You understand why we’re so surprised, surely,” Ginny said, leaning back in her seat.
“你肯定明白我们为什么这么惊讶，”金妮说，向后靠在座位上。

“He’s so old,” Ron groaned into his palm, prodding at a chicken bone on his plate.
“他这么老了，”罗恩对着他的手掌呻吟着，戳了戳他盘子里的一根鸡骨头。

“And everything else,” Ginny said with a sharp look at her brother. “You went from fighting tooth and nail with the man to get him to cooperate to telling us he’s turned a new leaf. It’s a lot to process from the outside.”
“还有别的，”金妮狠狠地瞪了她哥哥一眼。“你从与那个人咬牙切齿地争吵让他合作，到告诉我们他已经翻开了新的一页。从外部来看，需要处理很多事情。

“I know he hurt you,” Hermione said. “I don’t want you to think that I don’t care about that because –”
“我知道他伤害了你，”赫敏说。“我不想让你觉得我不在乎那个，因为——”

“That has to be the past,” Ginny said firmly, her eyes meeting Harry’s across the table. “It’s what he does going forward that’s our biggest concern now.”
“那一定是过去了，”金妮坚定地说，她的眼睛对上了桌子对面的哈利。“他未来的所作所为是我们现在最大的担忧。”

“If he is changing –” Harry began.
“如果他要改变——”哈利开始说。

“I really think he is –” Hermione cut in earnestly.
“我真的觉得他是——”赫敏认真地打断道。

“Then I’m sure we have nothing to worry about.”
“那么我确定我们没有什么可担心的。”

Reaching out, Ginny placed a warm hand over Hermione’s and squeezed, a fierceness on her face that spoke to how much she cared and how truly willing she was to try. To her mortification, Hermione felt tears gathering in her eyes again and, blinking rapidly, she sniffed loudly in an attempt to stave them off. Though she was sure the abundance of wine she’d consumed had something to do with her heightened emotions, it was all rather overwhelming. 
金妮伸出手，将一只温暖的手放在赫敏的手上，捏了捏，她脸上的凶狠说明了她是多么在乎，她是多么真诚地愿意尝试。令她感到羞愧的是，赫敏感到泪水再次在眼眶中聚集，她迅速眨了眨眼，大声嗅了嗅，试图阻止它们。虽然她确信自己喝的大量葡萄酒与她高涨的情绪有关，但这一切都相当令人不知所措。

“So,” Ginny said, pausing to take a drink, meeting Hermione’s eyes over the rim of her glass. When she lowered it, there was a mischievousness in her expression that made Hermione nervous. “I’m guessing it must be true what they say about Slytherins?”
“所以，”金妮说，停下来喝了一杯，隔着玻璃杯的边缘与赫敏的眼睛相遇。当她放下它时，她的表情中带着一种调皮的神情，让赫敏感到紧张。“我猜他们说的斯莱特林一定是真的吧？”

“I don’t…” Hermione glanced around at Ron and Harry who were looking curiously at Ginny. “What do they say?”
“我不......”赫敏环顾四周，看了一眼罗恩和哈利，他们正好奇地看着金妮。“他们怎么说？”

“Well,” Ginny began, her tone businesslike as she carefully set her glass down and lifted her hands to make an approximate measurement. “They say they have massive –”
“嗯，”金妮开始说，她的语气很公事公办，她小心翼翼地放下酒杯，抬起双手做了一个大概的测量。“他们说他们有大量的——”

A loud clatter signalled Ron’s wine glass toppling over, sending a stream of wine across the polished wooden table and their empty plates. Ginny and Hermione cried out, pushing themselves back from the table to avoid the red drips threatening to fall into their laps. 
一声响亮的咔嚓声表明罗恩的酒杯翻了个底朝天，一股酒流过了抛光的木桌和空盘子。金妮和赫敏大声喊道，把自己从桌子上往后推，以免红珠有可能掉进他们的腿上。

“Ron!” Ginny snapped, glaring at her brother who scowled straight back, his ears scarlet.  
“罗恩！”金妮厉声瞪着她的哥哥，他直接皱起眉头，耳朵绯红。

“If you dare to finish that sentence, Ginny, I swear I’ll do so much worse.”
“如果你敢把那句话说完，金妮，我发誓我会做得更糟。”
