Chapter 38
第三十八章Chapter Summary
本章小结

Hermione and Lucius begin working together in earnest and find it has its ups and downs.
赫敏和卢修斯开始认真合作，发现它有起有落。

Chapter Notes
章节注释

See the end of the chapter for notes
注释见本章末尾August 13th 
八月 13th

 

“Ugh.”
“呃。”

Lucius blinked down at the book in his lap, his concentration broken. Clearing his throat, he shifted in his seat and attempted to find his way back through the dense paragraph he’d been reading. The typescript was so tiny and smudged he rather felt like he was attempting to make sense of wet tar.
卢修斯对着他腿上的书眨了眨眼，他的注意力被打断了。清了清嗓子，他在座位上挪动了一下，试图在他一直在阅读的那段密集的段落中找到回去的路。打字稿又小又脏，他宁愿觉得自己在试图理解湿焦油。

A snort followed by another “ugh” prompted him to lift his head, a muscle in his jaw jumping in time with a pop in the roaring fire across from him. Placing a finger on the last word he’d managed to focus on, he turned to look at Hermione who was curled up on the other end of his study sofa, a heavy tome in her own lap. 
一声哼哼，紧接着又是一声“呃”，他抬起头，下巴上的一块肌肉及时跳动，在他对面咆哮的火焰中啪啪作响。他把手指放在他设法集中注意力的最后一个词上，转身看向蜷缩在书房沙发另一端的赫敏，她自己的腿上放着一本沉重的书。

It was clear from the way she was twirling a curl between her fingers and chewing at her lip that she was entirely lost in what she was reading. Another guttural noise of what sounded like disgust made him close his eyes momentarily. 
从她在手指之间旋转卷曲和咀嚼嘴唇的方式可以清楚地看出，她完全沉浸在她正在阅读的内容中。另一声听起来像是厌恶的喉音使他暂时闭上了眼睛。

“Hermione,” he began, even a soft spoken word making her jump as it disrupted her focus. “Permit me to suggest…putting words to your frustration?”
“赫敏，”他开始说，即使是一个轻声细语也让她跳了起来，因为它打乱了她的注意力。“请允许我建议......用语言来表达你的挫败感吗？

Using her hand as a bookmark, Hermione gave him a befuddled blink that distinctly asked him what had possessed him to interrupt her reading. “Am I making noise?”
赫敏用她的手当书签，困惑地眨了眨眼，显然是在问他是什么让他打断了她的阅读。“我在发出声音吗？”

“Often,” he said lightly. 
“经常，”他淡淡地说。

“Oh.” Her lips twisted with an apologetic grimace. “Sorry, that always drove Harry and Ron mad, too. It’s just –” She cast an offended eye down at the legal book in her lap. “Ugh, honestly, it’s just that some of these laws are utterly absurd . There are exemptions from taxes listed here that no one even pays anymore. Worse, there are exemptions from taxes that everyone should pay, regardless of their blood status. I don’t know how they’ve wrangled some of these.”
“哦。”她的嘴唇扭曲着，露出一个歉意的鬼脸。“对不起，这也总是让哈利和罗恩发疯。只是——“她低头看了一眼腿上的法律书。“呃，老实说，只是其中一些法律是完全荒谬的。这里列出了一些免税，甚至没有人再支付。更糟糕的是，每个人都应该缴纳免税，无论他们的血统如何。我不知道他们是怎么解决其中一些的。

Eyebrows raised, Lucius inclined his head to indicate that he was listening but kept his mouth firmly shut. He was, after all, actively using some of those exemptions as they sat there. But it wasn’t like he’d asked for them. 
卢修斯扬起眉毛，歪着头表示他在听，但还是牢牢地闭上了嘴。毕竟，当他们坐在那里时，他正在积极使用其中一些豁免。但这不像是他要求的。

He liked to think he had always been a notoriously generous donator instead. Truly, he found donating far more gratifying – generally it meant choosing exactly what his money was spent on and being able to demand that his name be engraved/carved/mounted on it. Unfortunately, he had a strong suspicion that vanity projects which were, deep down, for no one but himself weren't going to fly with Hermione. 
他喜欢认为自己一直是一个出了名的慷慨捐助者。确实，他发现捐赠要令人满意得多——通常这意味着准确地选择他的钱花在什么地方，并能够要求将他的名字刻在上面/雕刻/装裱在上面。不幸的是，他强烈怀疑，在内心深处，除了他自己之外，没有人会和赫敏一起飞翔的虚荣心。

“And I mean, look at this!” Swinging her legs down, Hermione shuffled over the sofa and curled up right beside him with the open book angled towards him in her lap. She jabbed her finger at the page and Lucius leaned over to her, squinting to read the text. “Pure-bloods can hunt Muggles and Muggle-borns as long as it’s on their private land according to this,” she explained, her lip curled with disgust. “Clearly some kind of intruder loophole and it’s never been overturned.”
“我的意思是，看看这个！”赫敏双腿往下摆动，在沙发上拖着脚步，蜷缩在他身边，打开的书在她的腿上斜对着他。她用手指戳了戳书页，卢修斯靠向她，眯着眼睛看课文。“根据这个规定，纯血统的人可以猎杀麻瓜和麻瓜出身的人，只要是在他们的私人土地上，”她解释道，她的嘴唇因厌恶而卷曲。“显然是某种入侵者的漏洞，而且从未被推翻。”

“That is rather…”
“那是......”

“Barbaric?” she spat, glaring down at the page of the book like it had personally attempted to hunt her. “Disgusting. Utterly Medieval ?”
“野蛮？”她啐了一口，低头瞪着书页，仿佛它亲自试图猎杀她。“恶心。完全是中世纪的吗？

Peering more closely at the page, Lucius said, “I think it may actually be Medieval in origin, Hermione.” 
卢修斯更仔细地盯着那页，说道，“我觉得它实际上可能起源于中世纪，赫敏。

Pausing, she looked up at him from the pages. “Did your family ever hunt Muggles?”
停顿了一下，她从书页上抬头看着他。“你家猎杀过麻瓜吗？”

Raising his eyebrows, Lucius tipped his head back against the sofa thoughtfully. “Certainly not in my lifetime. My great grandfather got rid of the stables and the horses with them and I would imagine it’d be rather laborious to –” He caught sight of Hermione’s mouth hanging open out of the corner of his eye and immediately retreated to the safety of monosyllables. “No.”
卢修斯扬起眉毛，若有所思地把头靠在沙发上。“当然不会在我的有生之年。我的曾祖父把马厩和马都带走了，我想这要是相当费力的——“他看到赫敏的嘴巴从眼角的余光中张开，立即退到单音节的安全处。“不。”

Eyeing him with disgust for a moment, she flicked the page over and directed his attention to a different paragraph. “Even worse, look at this,” she said. It was, Lucius surmised after a quick skim, an addendum that had been added thirty years after the initial law’s passing. “The right to claim the property of the hunted if they have no heirs,” she said, her voice rising with disbelief. “I mean, honestly!”
她厌恶地盯着他看了一会儿，然后翻了翻那页，把他的注意力引向了另一段。“更糟糕的是，看看这个，”她说。卢修斯快速浏览了一会儿后推测，这是在最初的法律通过三十年后添加的附录。“如果被猎杀的人没有继承人，他们有权要求他们的财产，”她说，她的声音因难以置信而提高。“我是说，老实说！”

“Mm…” Lucius agreed. Turning back to his own book, he flicked the page over with a flourish of his forefinger. “By the by,” he said, all affected nonchalance. “Do you own any property that is in any way valuable and, as a completely unrelated aside, are you a fast runner?”
“嗯......”卢修斯同意。他转回自己的书前，用食指轻弹着书页。“对了，”他说，所有人都表现出了冷漠。“你是否拥有任何有价值的财产，而且，完全无关，你是一个跑得快的人吗？”

“That’s not funny.”
“这可不好笑。”

“It is.”
“是的。”

“I hope all of the laws are so obviously disgusting,” Hermione said, dropping her shoulder and head against his arm as she scowled down at the book. “It’ll make our job much easier.”
“我希望所有的法律都这么明显地令人作呕，”赫敏说，一边把肩膀和头靠在他的手臂上，一边皱着眉头看着这本书。“这将使我们的工作轻松得多。”

“They won’t be,” he said. “Many of them will be more subtle.” 
“他们不会的，”他说。“他们中的许多人会更加微妙。”

Craning her neck, Hermione looked up at his profile, finding his expression troubled. “You seem very certain.”
赫敏伸长脖子，抬头看向他的侧影，发现他的表情很不安。“你看起来非常确定。”

“If you’re going to stamp on others, you had best make sure they either are or feel too powerless to stamp back,” he said before sighing softly through his nose and glancing down at her. "That requires at least a touch of sagacity.”
“如果你要踩踏别人，你最好确保他们要么是，要么是觉得无力回头，”他说，然后从鼻子里轻轻叹了口气，低头瞥了她一眼。“这至少需要一点智慧。”

“I suppose this is why it’s a good thing we’re working together,” she muttered, wiggling so that she could burrow further into him. Lifting an arm to let her, Lucius wrapped it around her shoulder and pulled her closer. “Rather have you with me than against me,” she added.
“我想这就是为什么我们一起工作是一件好事，”她咕哝着，扭动着身体以便能够更深入地钻入他。卢修斯抬起一只手臂让她走，把它搂在她的肩膀上，把她拉得更近了。“宁愿你和我在一起，也不愿反对我，”她又说。

A faint tapping, the sound of something sharp on glass, made them both still, ears straining for its source. While Hermione looked around them, Lucius looked directly over her head in the direction of the dark window behind his desk. Outside, an owl was attempting to get their attention, its large eyes bright in contrast with the night. 
一阵微弱的敲击声，什么尖锐的东西敲打玻璃的声音，使他们俩都静止了，耳朵紧紧地寻找它的来源。赫敏环顾四周，卢修斯直视着她的头顶，看向他桌子后面的黑暗窗户的方向。外面，一只猫头鹰正试图引起他们的注意，它的大眼睛与黑夜形成鲜明对比。

Following his gaze, Hermione yelped and, placing her book carefully to the side, leapt to her feet.
顺着他的目光，赫敏大叫了一声，小心翼翼地把书放在一边，跳了起来。

“Don’t tell me it’s the Weasley boy again ,” Lucius groaned, putting his own book aside to rise and follow her across the room.
“别再告诉我是那个韦斯莱男孩，”卢修斯呻吟着，把自己的书放在一边，站起来跟着她穿过房间。

Hermione grimaced as she closed the window behind the owl, which fluttered onto Lucius’ desk with a soft hoot. She rather hoped it wasn’t Ron for his own sake. 
赫敏愁眉苦脸地关上了猫头鹰身后的窗户，猫头鹰轻轻地吼了一声，飞到了卢修斯的桌子上。她宁愿这不是为了罗恩自己。

When she had told him as well as Ginny and Harry that she would be staying with Lucius for a few days while Draco remained with Astoria at the hospital, they had given her a politely supportive response. 
当她告诉他，还有金妮和哈利，她会和卢修斯住几天，而德拉科还在医院陪着阿斯托利亚时，他们礼貌地给了她一个支持性的回应。

In the days since, however, Ron – the friend who had once told her that letter writing ranked alongside feeding lettuce to flobberworms in a list of activities he enjoyed – had started what could only be described as a letter writing campaign. 
然而，在那之后的几天里，罗恩——那个曾经告诉她写信的朋友，在他喜欢的活动清单中，写信与喂生菜和蠕虫一样——开始了只能被描述为写信的活动。

Multiple owls a day had been bringing Hermione notes that were quite clearly attempts to check on her well being –  the last had come only an hour earlier and had simply been a scrap of parchment that read ‘alright?’. Hermione sensed Lucius had a growing desire to wring Ron’s neck. 
每天有好几只猫头鹰给赫敏带来笔记，这些笔记显然是想检查她的健康状况——最后一次只提前一个小时来了，只是一张写着“还好吗”的羊皮纸。赫敏感觉到卢修斯越来越想拧住罗恩的脖子。

“What exactly does he think is happening?” Lucius had snapped during breakfast when the first letter of that day had arrived. “Is he worried I’ve chained you to a wall and forced you to keep me company?”
“他到底觉得发生了什么？”卢修斯在吃早餐时，当那天的第一封信到来时，他吼了一声。“他担心我把你锁在墙上，强迫你陪着我吗？”

“I think his concern mostly stems from the fact that you haven’t done that, actually,” Hermione said lightly as she buttered her toast. “He’s just adjusting. They’ll stop.”  
“我觉得他的担心主要是因为你实际上没有那样做，”赫敏一边给吐司涂黄油，一边淡淡地说。“他只是在调整。他们会停下来的。

Though he had grumbled something about how the adjustment had better happen faster into his tea, Hermione knew that Lucius was pleased she had told her friends about them, even with Ron becoming a source of irritation.
虽然他抱怨说这种调整最好在他的茶里更快地发生，但赫敏知道卢修斯很高兴她把这些事情告诉了她的朋友们，即使罗恩成为了恼怒的来源。

It was possible the secrecy had been weighing on them more than she’d realised because in the aftermath of the revelation, a calmness and a sense of acceptance had developed between them that hadn't been there before. Being in one another’s company no longer required an excuse and it was freeing.
秘密对他们造成的压力可能比她意识到的要大，因为在事情被揭露之后，他们之间产生了一种前所未有的平静和接受感。在彼此的陪伴下不再需要借口，这是一种自由。

Bending to gently untie the letter from the owl’s leg, Hermione was relieved to see that it was addressed to Lucius and not her. Ron, for all his obstinacy, would surely not be foolish enough to write something to Lucius himself.
赫敏弯下腰轻轻地从猫头鹰的腿上解开那封信，看到这是写给卢修斯的，而不是她，她松了一口气。罗恩，尽管他很固执，但他肯定不会愚蠢到给卢修斯本人写点什么。

“It’s for you,” she said, holding the letter out to him. 
“这是给你的，”她说，把信递给他。

Wearing a puzzled frown, Lucius took the letter with a murmur of thanks and tore it open. Hermione watched on curiously as his eyes skimmed the paper. The more he read, the smoother his forehead got and the lower his shoulders sank. 
卢修斯皱着眉头，低声感谢地接过信，把它撕开了。赫敏好奇地看着他的眼睛扫过那张纸。他读得越多，他的额头就越光滑，肩膀就越低。

Lowering the parchment, he gave her a smile. "It's Draco. Astoria has improved enough to be discharged and they'll be returning to the Manor tomorrow with Scorpius."
他放下羊皮纸，向她微笑。“是德拉科。阿斯托利亚已经好到可以出院了，他们明天会和斯科皮一起回到庄园。

Delighted, Hermione threw her arms around him. He returned the embrace with his free hand, kissing the top of her head before holding the letter aloft to read it again.  
赫敏高兴地搂住了他。他用空出来的手回应这个拥抱，亲吻了她的头顶，然后高高举起信再读一遍。

"I'm so glad she's okay," Hermione said, looking up at him. "Does Draco seem well?"
“我很高兴她没事，”赫敏说，抬头看着他。“德拉科看起来还好吗？”

"His tone is brighter," Lucius said, setting the letter on his desk so that he could wrap both arms around her. "He said she's still weak but the healers can see no good reason why she should not enjoy the comforts of home."
“他的语气更开朗了，”卢修斯说，把信放在他的桌子上，这样他就可以用双臂搂住她。“他说她仍然很虚弱，但治疗师看不出她有什么好理由不应该享受家的舒适。”

"And Scorpius?"
“那么斯科皮呢？”

"Thriving," he said, chest swelling with pride. "They'll arrive around lunchtime. I should warn Letty to prepare their room and the nursery, not to mention the kitchen."
“欣喜若狂，”他说，胸口因自豪而膨胀。“他们会在午餐时间到达。我应该警告莱蒂准备他们的房间和托儿所，更不用说厨房了。

"I'll head back to the flat in the morning so that you can prepare. We've done so much work over the last few days, we can definitely afford to –"
“我早上回公寓，让你做好准备。我们在过去几天里做了这么多工作，我们绝对负担得起——”

"Hermione," he interrupted, frowning. "You've been staying here for days; there's more than enough room for all of us."
“赫敏，”他皱着眉头打断了他。“你已经在这里呆了好几天了;我们所有人的空间绰绰有余。

Shifting awkwardly, Hermione lifted a shoulder. "Well, yes, but I just thought you all might like to have some time together to –"
赫敏笨拙地挪了挪身子，抬起了肩膀。“嗯，是的，但我只是觉得你们都想一起——”

"Draco and Astoria will want you to meet their child," he said sternly. "And if you can't accept that then believe me when I say that I will be mortally offended if you do not wish to meet my grandson."
“德拉科和阿斯托利亚会希望你见见他们的孩子，”他严肃地说。“如果你不能接受这一点，那就相信我，当我说如果你不想见我的孙子，我会受到致命的冒犯。”

Suddenly shy, Hermione lowered her gaze to his chest. "You know I can't wait to meet him."
赫敏突然害羞了，低头看向他的胸口。“你知道我迫不及待地想见他。”

"Then take the opportunity when it presents itself," he said, bringing a hand around to place his finger under her chin and lift her gaze back up to his. 
“那就抓住机会，”他说，伸出一只手，将手指放在她的下巴下，然后将她的目光重新抬向他。

Curling her fingers into his shirt, Hermione pushed herself up onto her tiptoes and placed a soft, smiling kiss on his lips. He slid a hand into her hair to deepen it and Hermione got the impression he was channelling all of his relief and gratitude that his son and family were well into her.
赫敏把手指卷进他的衬衫里，踮起脚尖，在他的嘴唇上轻轻地、微笑地吻了一下。他把一只手伸进她的头发里，加深了头发，赫敏觉得他把所有的宽慰和感激都表达出来了，因为他的儿子和家人都对她很好。

Breaking away somewhat breathlessly, she lost several centimetres in height as she dropped back onto her heels.
她有些喘不过气来，当她重新落到脚跟上时，她的身高减轻了几厘米。

"Alright, you've convinced me," she said, not missing his smug expression. "But I might still run back for an hour first thing in the morning – I'd like to bake a lemon cake for Astoria to come home to and I desperately need some fresh underwear." 
“好吧，你说服了我，”她说，没有错过他得意的表情。“但我可能仍然会在早上第一件事就是跑回来一个小时——我想为 Astoria 烤一个柠檬蛋糕回家，我迫切需要一些新鲜的内衣。”

"I've already told you –"
“我已经跟你说过了——”

"Lucius," she said, pulling away from him to return to the sofa, "you can insist that I don't need to wear underwear around the Manor as much as you like, I've told you it's not happening."
“卢修斯，”她说，从他身边拉开，回到沙发上，“你可以坚持说，我不需要在庄园里穿多少内裤，你想怎么穿就怎么，我已经告诉你了，这不会发生的。

August 20th
8月20日

 

Kingsley's desk was, once again, perfectly neat. So much so that there was more than enough room for a pot of tea and a heaped plate of biscuits. Though now that she'd seen the desk's true messy nature, Hermione found her brain itching with curiosity over what Kingsley did with all his papers and folders when he had visitors.
金斯利的书桌又一次变得非常整洁。以至于有足够的空间容纳一壶茶和一盘饼干。虽然现在她已经看到了这张桌子真正凌乱的本质，但赫敏发现她的大脑好奇金斯莱在有访客时如何处理他的所有文件和文件夹。

She knew he'd never tell her. 
她知道他永远不会告诉她。

"So, here we are again," Kingsley said, wearing a genial smile as he slid a full cup of tea over to Hermione. "You're well?"
“所以，我们又来了，”金斯莱说，带着和蔼的笑容，把满满的一杯茶递给赫敏。“你还好吗？”

Picking up her cup, Hermione lifted a shoulder and nodded. "I am. Busy, of course but –" Unbidden, a smile rose to her face and she looked down into her tea like its steam had just communicated a particularly charming message. "Things are good."
赫敏拿起她的杯子，抬起肩膀，点了点头。“我是。当然很忙，但是——“她不由自主地露出了笑容，她低头看着她的茶，仿佛它的蒸汽刚刚传达了一个特别迷人的信息。“一切都很好。”

Kingsley eyed her over the rim of his own cup. "You certainly seem more… at ease than you did at our last meeting," he observed. "Does this mean you're making good progress on the project?"
金斯莱透过自己的杯子边缘盯着她。“你看起来肯定更......比你上次见面时还自在，“他说道。“这是否意味着你在项目上取得了良好的进展？”

"We are," Hermione said, leaning forward to pick up a digestive biscuit. "We're starting with the things that have the most obvious solutions. Getting them out of the way."
“我们是，”赫敏说，身体前倾，拿起一块消化饼干。“我们从具有最明显解决方案的事情开始。让他们离开。

"Such as?"
“比如？”

"Muggle hunting," she said, looking up at Kingsley from under her brows as she dunked the biscuit. "I think we can just get rid of permissions around that entirely, don't you?" Taking a bite of her biscuit, she fixed Kingsley with an expectant look as she chewed.
“麻瓜狩猎，”她说，一边从眉毛下抬头看着金斯莱，一边把饼干浸入水中。“我觉得我们可以完全摆脱这个权限，不是吗？”她咬了一口饼干，用期待的眼神看着金斯利，一边咀嚼着。

"But it was outlawed as a sport generations ago, Hermione, " Kingsley said, his brow lowering into a deep frown.
“但几代人以前，它就被当作一项运动来禁止了，赫敏，”金斯莱说，他的眉头低垂成深深的皱眉。

"Not on private wizarding land it wasn't," Hermione said darkly, returning her cup to the desk and touching the last bite of her biscuit to her lips. "I wonder how that little loophole was missed, hm?" 
“不是在私人巫师的土地上，”赫敏阴沉地说，把杯子放回桌子上，把最后一口饼干碰到嘴唇上。“我想知道那个小漏洞是怎么漏掉的，嗯？”

Rubbing his eyes tiredly, Kingsley shook his head. "If this isn't a perfect example of why these laws should have been looked into years ago, I don't know what is," he said. "Keep going."
金斯莱疲惫地揉了揉眼睛，摇了摇头。“如果这不是为什么几年前就应该研究这些法律的完美例子，我不知道什么才是，”他说。“继续。”

"We will.” She dusted crumbs from her hands onto her lap. “Lucius is drafting up our justifications for some of those today so I'll try to deliver them at our next meeting so we can get the ball rolling."
“我们会的。”她把手上的碎屑掸到膝盖上。“Lucius 今天正在为其中一些理由起草，所以我会尝试在下次会议上提供它们，这样我们就可以开始工作了。”

Kingsley inclined his head and tapped his finger against his cup. There was a faint ting as one of his gold rings connected with the porcelain.
金斯莱歪着头，用手指敲了敲他的杯子。当他的一枚金戒指与瓷器相连时，发出微弱的叮当声。

"You'll be glad to know," he said, after a moment, "that the Wizengamot has agreed that it certainly will have to reassess Lucius' sentence in the event that he sees this project through to completion."
“你会很高兴知道的，”他过了一会儿说，“威森加摩已经同意，如果卢修斯完成这个项目，它肯定必须重新评估卢修斯的判决。

Gulping her tea so quickly it scalded her throat, Hermione coughed and held a hand to her chest, her eyes watering. "That's fantastic," she rasped. "Thank you, Kingsley, I'll let him know."
赫敏大口大口地喝着茶，快到烫到她的喉咙，她咳嗽着，一只手捂着胸口，眼睛流泪。“那太棒了，”她嘶哑地说。“谢谢你，金斯利，我会让他知道的。”

He nodded, unsmiling. "And you think he will? See it through to completion?"
他点点头，不苟言笑。“你觉得他会吗？完成它？

"He's not given me any reason to think he won't," Hermione said, meeting Kingsley's contemplative gaze and holding it despite her still-watering eyes. "We're working well together."
“他没有给我任何理由认为他不会，”赫敏说，对上金斯莱沉思的目光，尽管她的眼睛仍然流泪，但她还是握住了它。“我们合作得很好。”

"Good," Kingsley said slowly, like he was struggling to figure out whether he actually meant what he was saying. "That's good.” He sounded more certain. “The members of the Wizenganot are extremely curious about this partnership and your persistence, you know. Not to mention Lucius' willingness."
“很好，”金斯莱缓缓地说，就像他在努力弄清楚自己是否真的在说什么。“那很好。”他听起来更确定。“你知道的，Wizenganot 的成员对这种伙伴关系和你的坚持非常好奇。更不用说卢修斯的意愿了。

"Oh, I'm sure they are," Hermione said with a bland smile that told Kingsley they could continue to be curious as far as she was concerned. 
“哦，我确定他们是，”赫敏带着淡淡的笑容说，告诉金斯莱，只要她关心，他们可以继续保持好奇。

"But they – we – are agreed it's very…well, it looks good for the Ministry. It's setting an encouraging example." He cleared his throat and set his tea down carefully. "We may put a small piece in the Prophet. No specifics, of course; I’d rather not shout about the exact nature of your project just yet but it might be good for people to know you’re working on something ."
“但他们——我们——都同意这非常......嗯，这对魔法部来说看起来不错。它树立了一个令人鼓舞的榜样。他清了清嗓子，小心翼翼地把茶放下。“我们可以在先知身上放一小块。当然，没有具体细节;我现在不想大声疾呼你的项目的确切性质，但让人们知道你正在做某事可能是件好事。

“The Prophet?” Hermione asked, her reluctance clear in her cringe.
“先知？”赫敏问道，她的不情愿在她的畏缩中显而易见。

“You don’t like that idea?”
“你不喜欢这个主意吗？”

“I mean…” She puffed out a sigh. “Well, I’ve avoided being in the Prophet for a few years now. I quite liked it that way.”
“我是说......”她叹了口气。“嗯，我已经避免成为先知已经有几年了。我非常喜欢这种方式。

Kingsley raised his eyebrows. “You’re working with Lucius Malfoy on a matter that will eventually be of public interest, Hermione. The question is not whether it’s reported in the Prophet at all but rather whether it happens now or later.”
金斯莱扬起眉毛。“你正在和卢修斯·马尔福一起处理一件最终会引起公众利益的事情，赫敏。问题不在于先知是否报道了它，而在于它是现在还是以后发生。

Barely holding back a groan, Hermione sank back in her seat. “Alright,” she said. “Something small, though, you said? Just a paragraph. No photos. Preferably sandwiched between two jaw-dropping exposés. Tiny font.” She held her thumb and forefinger barely a hair’s breadth apart to show Kingsley the kind of size that she had in mind. 
赫敏勉强忍住呻吟，瘫回了座位上。“好吧，”她说。“不过，你说的是小事吗？只是一个段落。没有照片。最好夹在两个令人瞠目结舌的揭露之间。小字体。她把拇指和食指分开，几乎分开一根头发丝宽，向金斯利展示她心目中的那种尺寸。

Kingsley offered her nothing but a cryptic smile. “I’ll let you know when it’s published.” There was no way he’d taken her font recommendation on board.
金斯利只给了她一个神秘的微笑。“我会在它发布时通知你。”他不可能接受她的字体推荐。

Picturing Lucius’ likely unamused expression on opening the Prophet one morning to find the 'small piece', Hermione rolled her eyes and dropped her hand into her lap, defeated. “I’m sure I’ll hear about it fairly quickly.”
赫敏想象着卢修斯在某天早上打开先知找到“小块”时可能不高兴的表情，她翻了个白眼，把手放在她的腿上，被打败了。“我敢肯定我很快就会听到这件事。”

“Anyway, I'm certainly glad everything is coming together,” Kingsley said, his tone shifting to one of Ministerial abruptness. “Because I've asked the DMLE to gather for an announcement in –" He checked his watch. "Ten minutes! We've nattered too long, Hermione, we'd best go." 
“不管怎样，我当然很高兴一切都走到了一起，”金斯利说，他的语气变成了部长级的突然。“因为我已经让 DMLE 聚在一起发布公告了——”他看了看手表。“十分钟！我们已经叽叽喳喳了太久了，赫敏，我们最好走了。

Throwing back the last of his tea in a gulp, Kingsley uttered a refreshed sigh and pushed himself to his feet with a burst of purposeful energy. 
金斯利一口喝完了最后一口茶，发出一声清爽的叹息，带着一股有目的的能量站了起来。

“Oh.” Hermione shook her head, her hands coming down to grip the sides of her chair like it had just attempted to buck her off. “Oh, no, Kingsley, I’m sure I don’t need to be there for that. You can just go right ahead without me. In fact –” Wrenching her hand off the chair, she pretended to check her own watch. “I have somewhere to be myself.”
“哦。”赫敏摇了摇头，她的手垂下来抓住椅子的两侧，就像它刚刚试图把她推开一样。“哦，不，金斯莱，我确定我不需要在那里。你就可以在没有我的情况下直接前进。事实上——“她把手从椅子上拽下来，假装看了看自己的手表。“我有地方可以做我自己。”

“Unless that ‘somewhere’ is the Department of Magical Law Enforcement, Hermione, I’m afraid it will have to wait.”
“除非那个'某个地方'是魔法执法部，赫敏，恐怕它得等一等。”

Quelling under his commanding stare, Hermione mumbled something about how whatever it was certainly could wait – of course, Minister – and unenthusiastically rose to her feet. 
赫敏在他威严的目光下喃喃自语着什么——当然，部长——然后不高兴地站了起来。

With a satisfied smile, Kingsley rounded his desk, passed her and beckoned over his shoulder for her to follow him. Sighing, Hermione snatched another digestive from the desk and took an oversized bite as she slunk after him. 
金斯利满意地笑了笑，绕过他的桌子，经过她，在他的肩膀上招手让她跟着他。赫敏叹了口气，从桌子上抓起另一本消化液，大口大口地咬了一口，慢慢地跟在他后面。

The meeting had a good turn out, as meetings called by the Minister for Magic himself tended to have. Employees from across the department had gathered in the central office space, some sitting behind their desks, others perched on the desks of friends, and more still gathered around the sides of the room. 
这次会议结果很好，因为魔法部长亲自召集的会议往往是这样。来自整个部门的员工都聚集在中央办公室，一些人坐在办公桌后面，另一些人坐在朋友的桌子上，还有更多人仍然聚集在房间的两侧。

When Kingsley swept into the room followed by Hermione, the buzz of many simultaneous conversations quickly died down. They took a central position at the front of the room and heat swiftly rose in Hermione’s cheeks under the weight of so many curious stares. As she scanned the crowd, she spotted the messy hair of Harry and gave him a weak smile when he waved madly.
当金斯莱跟在赫敏身后扫进房间时，许多同时进行的对话的嗡嗡声很快就平息了。他们在房间前面的中央位置，在这么多好奇的目光下，赫敏的脸颊上的热量迅速上升。当她扫视人群时，她发现了哈利凌乱的头发，当他疯狂地挥手时，她给了他一个虚弱的微笑。

“Good afternoon everyone,” Kingsley said, his deep voice easily carrying across the room and catching the attention of the one or two people who had been too busy chatting to notice his entrance. “Thank you for taking a few minutes out of your day to be here. Now, I’m sure you’re all curious –” Here, he cast a warm smile in Hermione’s direction and she prayed for the floor to open up. “So I’ll just get right into it.”
“大家下午好，”金斯利说，他低沉的声音轻松地传遍了整个房间，引起了一两个忙着聊天而没有注意到他进来的人的注意。“感谢您抽出几分钟时间来到这里。现在，我相信你们都很好奇——“说到这里，他朝赫敏的方向投来一个温暖的微笑，她祈祷地板能打开。“所以我就直接开始吧。”

As Kingsley announced Hermione’s return to the Ministry and her movement into the department, she had the torturous honour of standing beside him in silence, observing everyone's reactions with a faint ringing in her ears. 
当金斯莱宣布赫敏回到魔法部并进入魔法部时，她有幸默默地站在他身边，看着每个人的反应，耳边发出微弱的铃声。

To her relief, the general responses to the news ranged from the polite indifference of those who just wanted to get on with their own work, to genuine pleasure. Harry's face was, of course, a beaming beacon in the middle of the crowd but there were a number of warm smiles and friendly, even familiar, faces looking to catch her eye.  
令她松了一口气的是，人们对这个消息的普遍反应从那些只想继续自己工作的人的礼貌冷漠到真正的快乐。当然，哈利的脸是人群中一盏喜气洋洋的灯塔，但也有许多温暖的笑容和友好的、甚至是熟悉的面孔，希望吸引她的眼球。

Kingsley was light on the details of what she'd be working on, merely mentioning that she'd be looking into some of their older laws with an eye to improvement and fairness. This in itself raised some interested eyebrows and Hermione prepared herself to fend off some invasive questions in the near future.
金斯利对她将要从事的工作的细节并不感兴趣，只是提到她将研究他们的一些旧法律，着眼于改进和公平。这本身就引起了一些感兴趣的注意，赫敏准备好在不久的将来抵御一些侵入性的问题。

It was when Kingsley revealed that she was working with Lucius Malfoy that there was a palpable shift in the atmosphere. Smiles slipped, eyes bulged and the rustle and buzz of dozens of people turning to their neighbour to whisper forced Kingsley to raise his voice slightly.
当金斯利透露她正在与卢修斯·马尔福合作时，气氛发生了明显的变化。笑容溜走了，眼睛凸出，几十个人转向邻居窃窃私语的沙沙声和嗡嗡声迫使金斯利稍微提高了声音。

Some of her colleagues looked genuinely shocked, which was to be expected. Others appeared more intrigued, eyes fixed on her while they murmured excitedly to their colleagues behind their hands. Others still, however, looked annoyed and Hermione found her eyes lingering for longer on this frown or that tight jaw. It was hard not to notice that the majority of them were on the faces of Aurors.

Dropping her battered handbag on Harry’s cluttered desk, Hermione used both of her hands to support her as she leaned across it towards his face. 
赫敏把她破旧的手提包放在哈利杂乱的桌子上，用双手扶着她，把包靠在他的脸上。

“Right,” she said. “Quill down. I’m taking you for lunch.”
“是的，”她说。“羽毛笔下来。我带你吃午饭。

Gaping incredulously at the bag, Harry looked up at her from the report he had been engrossed in. “You nearly knocked over my ink.”
哈利难以置信地瞪着袋子，从他全神贯注的报告中抬起头看着她。“你差点打翻了我的墨水。”

“I’ll do worse than that if you don’t come to lunch with me.”
“如果你不来和我一起吃午饭，我会做得比这更糟糕。”

Alarmed, Harry surrounded his papers with a protective arm. “What’s gotten into you?” he asked. “You’re Hermione Granger – you never tell people to stop working.”
哈利惊慌失措，用一只保护手臂围住了他的文件。“你怎么了？”“你是赫敏·格兰杰——你从不告诉人们停止工作。”

“Your wife has gotten into me.” Hermione stopped and frowned. “Onto me? Anyway, it’s Ginny. This is Ginny’s fault.”
“你老婆搞定了我。”赫敏停了下来，皱起了眉头。“对我？总之，是金妮。这是金妮的错。

“I should have known,” Harry said, shaking his head. 
“我早该知道的，”哈利摇着头说。

“You married her,” Hermione pointed out. 
“你娶了她，”赫敏指出。

“Yeah, but I didn’t expect you to help her make me pay for it.”
“是啊，但我没想到你会帮她让我付钱。”

Pursing her lips, Hermione pushed herself up to stand straight and frowned down at Harry. “Should I be offended that you would class coming to lunch with me as ‘paying for it’?”
赫敏抿着嘴唇，挺起身子站直，皱着眉头看着哈利。“你把和我一起吃午饭当作'付钱'，我应该生气吗？”

“No,” Harry assured her quickly. “No, it’s just…” He glanced around at the sheafs of parchment scattered across his desk. “I’ve had a lot to do recently. Ginny thinks I’m pushing myself too hard.”
“不，”哈利很快向她保证。“不，只是......”他环顾四周，看了一眼散落在桌上的一捆捆羊皮纸。“我最近有很多事情要做。金妮觉得我把自己逼得太紧了。

“Well,” Hermione said, picking up a long inventory from a raid to peruse it. “When was the last time you took a lunch hour?”
“嗯，”赫敏说，从突袭中拿起一长串清单仔细阅读。“你上一次吃午饭是什么时候？”

Harry ran his hands through his hair, giving himself a particularly electrified look. “I honestly don’t know,” he said before sighing heavily. Taking a quick look around at the surrounding desks, he leaned towards her and jerked his head at her in an invitation to come closer. 
哈利用手抚摸着自己的头发，给自己一个特别兴奋的样子。“老实说，我不知道，”他说，然后重重地叹了口气。他快速环顾了一下周围的桌子，向她靠了靠，猛地向她转了摇头，邀请她靠近一点。

Curiosity piqued, Hermione set aside the inventory. Lowering herself onto her elbows, she brought their heads close together. “There’s an opening coming up for the head of the Auror department,” he whispered, “and I want to go for it.”
好奇心被激起，赫敏把库存放在一边。她低下身子，用手肘撑起，把他们的头靠得更近。“傲罗部门的负责人有一个空缺，”他低声说，“我想去争取。

Gasping quietly, a delighted smile spreading over her face, Hermione straightened up and clapped her hands together. “Harry, that’s so exciting!” He tried to hush her, holding up a hand. “You’re obviously going to get it.”
赫敏轻声喘息，脸上洋溢着欣喜的笑容，她直起身来，拍了拍手。“哈利，太令人兴奋了！”他举起一只手，试图让她安静下来。“你显然会得到它。”

Groaning doubtfully, Harry looked around at his various reports in search of something. “I’m trying to make sure of it.” He glanced up at her and Hermione spied dark smudges under his eyes behind his glasses. “I don’t want it to seem like I… expect it or something.” A shudder passed through him at the mere idea of anyone thinking that of him. 
哈利疑惑地呻吟着，环顾四周，翻阅着他的各种报告，寻找着什么。“我正在努力确保这一点。”他抬头看了她一眼，赫敏在眼镜后面发现了他眼睛下的黑色污迹。“我不想让它看起来像我...... 期待它什么的。他一想到有人会这样想他，就感到不寒而栗。

Hermione looked on sympathetically as Harry sifted through various stacks of parchment. She, more than anyone, recognised the signs of someone who needed to stop and take a breath. “Sometimes a break can be good,” she pressed hopefully. “An hour now to rest your brain could do you the world of good.”
赫敏同情地看着哈利筛选各种羊皮纸。她比任何人都更能识别出有人需要停下来喘口气的迹象。“有时候休息一下是好的，”她满怀希望地催促道。“现在休息一个小时，让你的大脑好好吃。”

“Honestly,” said Harry, aggressively lifting a pile of parchment and dropping it when it wasn’t hiding what he was looking for. “I think if I stop I might collapse.”
“老实说，”哈利说，咄咄逼人地拿起一堆羊皮纸，趁它没有藏住他要找的东西就扔了下来。“我想如果我停下来，我可能会崩溃。”

“All the more reason,” she insisted. When Harry merely reached for his quill again and hurriedly dipped it in ink, Hermione sighed. “That’s a shame.” Swallowing, she squeezed her toes down in her shoes before adding, “Because someone told me they love me recently and I’d like to talk to a friend about it.”
“更有理由，”她坚持说。当哈利再次伸手去拿他的羽毛笔，匆匆忙忙地蘸了墨水时，赫敏叹了口气。“真可惜。”她咽了口口水，用脚趾头挤进鞋子里，然后补充道，“因为有人告诉我他们最近很爱我，我想和朋友谈谈。

Harry froze, his quill halfway between his inkwell and his parchment. As his gaze slowly rose to Hermione’s, a single drop of ink that had been gathering on the point of his quill finally dropped onto his desk. “Right,” he said faintly. “Well, that’s news.”
哈利愣住了，他的羽毛笔夹在墨水瓶和羊皮纸之间。当他的目光慢慢地抬向赫敏时，一滴一直聚集在羽毛笔尖上的墨水终于落到了他的桌子上。“是的，”他淡淡地说。“嗯，这是新闻。”

Taking a deep breath, her shoulders rising, Hermione nodded, humming a sound of agreement.  
赫敏深吸一口气，扬起肩膀，点点头，哼唱着同意的声音。

“And what did you say?” He prompted impatiently, the shake of his hand making more ink droplets splatter. “What did you say back?”
“你说什么？”他不耐烦地催促道，握手让更多的墨滴飞溅。“你怎么回答？”

“That’s really a conversation I’d rather have over some lunch, Harry.”
“我真想在吃午饭的时候再聊，哈利。”

Glaring down at his report and then back up at Hermione, Harry let out an irritated scoff and dropped his quill. “Right,” he said, pointing at her. “Fine. You win.” He grabbed the inventory Hermione had been perusing and pushed himself to his feet, stepping away from his desk. “Wait here while I run this round to Napier then we can go.”
哈利低头瞪着他的报告，然后又抬头看向赫敏，恼怒地嘲笑了一声，扔下了他的羽毛笔。“对，”他指着她说。“好吧。你赢了。他抓起赫敏一直在翻阅的清单，站起身来，离开了办公桌。“在这里等我跑到内皮尔，然后我们就可以走了。”

Grinning triumphantly, Hermione stepped around him as he passed her, dropping into his seat to wait for him. “But I pick where we’re eating!” he called back to her. “Give me that, at least.”
赫敏得意地咧嘴一笑，当他从她身边经过时，他绕过了他，坐在座位上等他。“但我选我们吃饭的地方！”“至少，给我这个。”

Waving him off with a chuckle, Hermione set about placing his quill neatly away and stopping his ink so that it wouldn’t dry out. She hadn’t exactly intended to talk about the new development in her relationship with Lucius with anyone just yet but Ginny had seemed so worried about Harry that she was willing to do anything to drag him away from his desk. 
赫敏笑着挥手让他走，然后开始把他的羽毛笔整齐地收起来，停止他的墨水，以免它变干。她还不打算和任何人谈论她和卢修斯关系的新发展，但金妮似乎非常担心哈利，以至于她愿意做任何事情把他从他的办公桌上拖走。

Anyone else, she thought, would be satisfied that they’d proven themselves when they’d defeated the most evil wizard in a generation. Not Harry Potter, apparently. She supposed she could relate but he had to eat at least one lunch.
她想，其他人都会因为当他们击败了一代人中最邪恶的巫师时，就证明了自己而感到满意。显然不是哈利波特。她以为她能感同身受，但他至少得吃一顿午餐。

“Not working with your Death Eater pal today?”
“今天不和你的食死徒朋友一起工作吗？”

Jumping at the sound of the gruff voice, Hermione blinked and looked around. With a sinking in her stomach, she found herself facing the Auror who had sneered at her during Kingsley’s announcement. He had stopped beside Harry’s desk, his hands shoved in his pockets. The unpleasant sneer was still there. Was it possible it was just his face? Or was it just his face when he was looking at her?
听到这沙哑的声音，赫敏跳了起来，眨了眨眼，环顾四周。随着她的胃一沉，她发现自己面对的是那个在金斯莱宣布时对她嘲笑的傲罗。他停在哈利的桌子旁边，双手插在口袋里。那令人不快的冷笑还在。有没有可能只是他的脸？还是只是他看着她的脸？

“Excuse me?” Hermione asked, her tone polite but cold. “I don't think we've been introduced.”
“什么？”赫敏问道，她的语气礼貌但冰冷。“我不认为我们被介绍过。”

“We haven't,” the Auror said. “But you don't need an introduction, do you? Everyone knows you.” An unpleasant knot was forming in Hermione’s chest. This man did not like her. “Hermione Granger, the war heroine.” He paused for a moment, waiting to see what reply she might give to that. When she gave him none, he said, “How do you go from that to partnering up with Death Eaters, eh?”
“我们没有，”傲罗说。“但你不需要介绍，对吧？大家都认识你。赫敏的胸口正在形成一个令人不快的结。这个男人不喜欢她。“赫敏·格兰杰，战争女英雄。”他停顿了一会儿，等着看她会怎么回答。当她什么也没给他时，他说：“你是怎么从那个到和食死徒合作的，嗯？

Hermione noticed that some of those sitting at the desks nearest them had started to listen to the exchange, the sound of quills scratching and paper rustling only noticeable in its absence. 
赫敏注意到，坐在离他们最近的桌子上的一些人已经开始听他们的交流，羽毛笔刮擦的声音和纸张的沙沙声只有在没有的时候才会明显。

With growing irritation and embarrassment, she straightened in her seat. “You don't know what you're talking ab–”
随着越来越生气和尴尬，她在座位上直起身来。“你不知道你在说什么，ab——”

“Word on the grapevine ‘round here,” he said, not bothering to lower his voice, “is that whatever you’re working on with old Malfoy could get him out early.” The Auror’s sneer became more pronounced, his eyes narrowing. “Now why would you, a war heroine, want to help him out with something like that? All those years on half pay must have hit you hard.”
“小道消息说，”他懒得压低声音，“不管你和老马尔福做什么，都能让他早点出来。傲罗的冷笑变得更加明显，他的眼睛眯了起来。“那么，你，一个战争女英雄，为什么还要帮助他做这样的事情呢？那些年半薪的工资一定对你造成了沉重的打击。

Within the space of a thought, Hermione pushed herself to her feet, Harry’s chair sliding away with such force that it bumped the desk behind. “Now listen here –”
在一瞬间，赫敏用力站了起来，哈利的椅子滑开了，力道之大，撞到了后面的桌子。“现在听着——”

“Is there a problem here?” Harry had returned. His eyes flicked to Hermione, telling her to say nothing more, before moving to the Auror, at whom he raised his eyebrows expectantly. “Smythe?”
“这儿有问题吗？”哈利回来了。他的眼睛瞥向赫敏，告诉她不要再说什么了，然后转向傲罗，他期待地抬起了眉毛。“史密斯？”

“Potter,” Smythe greeted him neutrally. “I was just asking Granger what business she thinks she has working in a department that enforces the law. I suppose she’s trying to get an inside track to help her Death Eater buddies.” His eyes slid to Hermione. “Planned any more parties at the Manor that we’ll have to attend?”
“波特，”斯迈斯中立地向他打招呼。“我只是问格兰杰，她认为她在一个执法部门工作有什么业务。我想她是想找个内幕来帮助她的食死徒伙伴。他的眼睛滑向赫敏。“我们打算在庄园里再举办什么派对吗？”

If her jaw hadn’t been clamped shut, Hermione thought she might have been sick. At this point, most of the surrounding desks had stopped pretending to work and were looking at the three of them with unconcealed interest, bordering on hunger. 
如果她的下巴没有被夹住，赫敏觉得她可能生病了。此时，周围的大部分办公桌都停止了假装工作，都以毫不掩饰的兴趣看着他们三人，近乎饥饿。

By Harry’s side, his hand clenched into a tight fist but his voice was controlled and cold as he spoke. “You don’t know what you’re talking about, Smythe. Have you forgotten everything she did? For you? For the Wizarding World?”
在哈利身边，他的手紧紧握成拳头，但他说话时声音却很克制，很冷。“你不知道你在说什么，史密斯。你忘了她做过的一切吗？给你的？为了魔法世界？

Pink blotches developed on Smythe’s sallow cheeks. He was being told off by Harry Potter in front of everyone and the humiliating reality of that was clearly setting in. Unfortunately, his response was to double down because while no one else was agreeing with him, they hadn’t jumped in to stop him either.
Smythe 蜡黄的脸颊上出现了粉红色的斑点。他被哈利·波特当着所有人的面训斥了一顿，而这令人羞辱的现实显然正在显现。不幸的是，他的反应是加倍努力，因为虽然没有其他人同意他的观点，但他们也没有跳出来阻止他。

“Has she ?” he snapped, sparing Hermione a disgusted look. “Or maybe she’s realised that she can’t ride your cloak tails anymore and decided she’d better start finding ways to get galleons from the other side?”
“她吗？”他厉声说，不让赫敏厌恶地看一眼。“或者她已经意识到她不能再骑你的斗篷尾巴了，并决定她最好开始想办法从另一边弄来大帆船？”

Hermione was ready to jump on Smythe when Harry slammed a hand down on his desk, making her flinch. His green eyes, even more striking when his face was so pale with tiredness, blazed behind his glasses.
赫敏正准备跳到斯迈斯身上，这时哈利用一只手猛地砸在他的桌子上，让她畏缩了一下。他那双绿色的眼睛，当他的脸色因疲惫而苍白时，显得更加引人注目，在他的眼镜后面闪闪发光。

“I would be dead without her,” he barked into Smythe’s increasingly red face. “A hundred times over.” Noticing all of the eyes on them, Harry straightened his posture and, his voice dripping with disdain, said, “Don’t talk about things you don’t understand, Smythe. You’re making yourself look stupid.”
“没有她，我早就死了，”他对着Smythe越来越红的脸吼道。“超过一百倍。”注意到所有的目光都注视着他们，哈利挺直了姿势，他的声音里带着轻蔑，说道，“不要谈论你不明白的事情，史密斯。你让自己看起来很愚蠢。

Trying to keep her breathing even and calm, Hermione met Harry’s eyes as he turned to her. “Lunch?” he asked, acting like Smythe had disappeared or had never even been there in the first place. 
赫敏努力让她的呼吸保持平稳和平静，当哈利转向她时，她与哈利的眼睛对上了。“吃午饭吗？”他问道，表现得好像Smythe已经消失了，或者根本就没出现过一样。

Nodding, Hermione snatched her bag from the desk and, without another glance at Smythe, hurried out of the department with her head held high and Harry walking in her wake. 
赫敏点点头，从桌子上抓起她的包，没有多看斯迈斯一眼，昂首挺胸地匆匆离开了部门，哈利跟在她身后。

Lucius was writing when Hermione blew into his study. Glancing up, his greeting died on his lips when she made a beeline for his drinks table without even looking in his direction. Slowly setting his quill down, he watched her back with fascination as she grumbled and clinked , her movements hidden to him. When she turned, she had a bottle of good brandy in one hand and a crystal glass in the other. 
卢修斯正在写作，赫敏闯进了他的书房。抬头看了一眼，当她直奔他的酒桌时，他的问候在他的嘴唇上消失了。他慢慢地放下羽毛笔，着迷地看着她的背影，她咕哝着，叮叮当当，她的动作对他来说是隐藏的。当她转身时，她一只手拿着一瓶上好的白兰地，另一只手拿着一个水晶杯。

Marching towards his desk, she sat the glass down with a blink-inducing thud on the wood and poured herself a drink. Lucius’ eyebrows rose in line with the volume of liquid but she paid him no mind. Satisfied, she pushed the bottle aside and, glass in hand, dropped heavily into the seat across from him to take a long drink. 
她走向他的书桌，把杯子坐下来，眨眼间砰的一声敲打着木头，然后给自己倒了一杯饮料。卢修斯的眉毛随着液体的体积而上扬，但她并不在意他。她心满意足地把瓶子推到一边，手里拿着玻璃杯，沉重地坐在他对面的座位上，大口大口地喝了一口。

“Trying day?” he asked, his voice light as he observed her face contort in response to the strength of the brandy. 
“艰难的一天吗？”他问道，当他观察到她的脸因白兰地的强度而扭曲时，他的声音很轻。

Shooting him a sardonic look over the rim of her glass, she took a much smaller drink before setting it on the desk with far greater care than she had before. “I had an extremely irritating encounter with an Auror.”
她从杯沿讥讽地看了他一眼，喝了一小口，然后比以前小心翼翼地把它放在桌子上。“我和一位傲罗有过一次非常恼火的遭遇。”

“Oh, well, I can sympathise only too well with that ,” he said, earning himself a raised eyebrow from her. “Tell me.”
“哦，好吧，我对此非常同情，”他说，赢得了她扬起的眉毛。“告诉我。”

As Hermione recounted her brief but horrific interaction with Smythe, Lucius’ brow lowered with every word. Reaching across the desk, he lifted her glass of brandy and took a long drink for himself. 
当赫敏讲述她与史密斯短暂而可怕的互动时，卢修斯的每一个字都低下了眉头。他把手伸到桌子对面，举起她的白兰地杯，为自己喝了一大口。

“He had the audacity to imply that you might be bribing me,” she said, impatiently gesturing for him to pass the brandy back, which he did immediately. 
“他竟然大胆地暗示你可能在贿赂我，”她说，不耐烦地示意他把白兰地递回去，他立即照做了。

Lucius scoffed and leaned back in his seat, his elbows on its arms. “Well, I would do that but even before we were well acquainted I could tell that would never work on you,” he said with a dismissive wave of his hand. “He's clearly an idiot, Hermione.”
卢修斯嗤之以鼻，向后靠在座位上，手肘搭在座位的手臂上。“嗯，我会这样做的，但即使在我们很熟悉之前，我就知道这对你绝对不起作用，”他轻蔑地挥了挥手说。“他显然是个白痴，赫敏。”

“An idiot with a loud mouth,” she muttered into her glass, shuddering as she recalled all the curious eyes of the other DMLE employees. Closing her eyes she took another long drink, her nose wrinkling.
“一个大嘴巴的白痴，”她对着杯子咕哝着，回想起其他 DMLE 员工所有好奇的眼神，她不寒而栗。她闭上眼睛，又喝了一大口水，鼻子皱了起来。

“Yes, well, those two traits do have an unfortunate tendency to coincide,” Lucius replied, eyeing her worriedly. As soon as she deposited the glass back on the desk, he pulled it towards himself again, just out of her reach. 
“是的，嗯，这两个特征确实有一种不幸的重合倾向，”卢修斯回答道，担忧地看着她。她一把杯子放回桌子上，他就又把它拉向自己，刚好够不到。

“Harry defended me,” she said, leaning her elbow on the arm of her chair and dropping her face into her hand. “But I’m worried it made him look bad –” She peered up at him, her right eye half-concealed by her fingers. “He’s going for head of department and I just…” Burying her head again, she groaned.
“哈利保护了我，”她说，用手肘靠在椅子的扶手上，把脸埋在手里。“但我担心这会让他看起来很糟糕——”她抬头凝视着他，右眼被手指半遮住。“他要竞选系主任，而我只是......”她再次埋下头，呻吟着。

“If he wants to be head of the Auror department, telling jumped-up imbeciles they’ve come to the wrong conclusion will be half the job,” Lucius said. “If anything, he just proved why he should get it.”
“如果他想成为傲罗部门的负责人，告诉那些跳起来的低能儿他们得出了错误的结论就成功了，”卢修斯说。“如果有的话，他只是证明了为什么他应该得到它。”

When Hermione didn’t do anything but moan and continue to hide her face, Lucius looked down into the brandy glass, his heart sinking. Lifting the glass to his lips, he threw the last of the brandy back. “Look, if this is going to be a problem, Hermione, then I am going to step back and –”
当赫敏除了呻吟并继续掩面时，卢修斯低头看着白兰地玻璃杯，他的心沉了下去。他把杯子举到嘴边，把最后一瓶白兰地扔回去。“听着，如果这会是个问题，赫敏，那我就退后一步，然后——”

“Shut up, please, Lucius,” she said, finally lifting her head to fix him with a steely look.
“闭嘴，拜托了，卢修斯，”她说，终于抬起头，用坚毅的眼神盯着他。

“Excuse me, I –”
“对不起，我——”

“I’m upset,” she said. “It was upsetting. But I won’t let you try to do that manipulative thing where you wrangle with the unfamiliarity of guilt by pushing me away, claiming it’s for me when it’s actually just a way to punish yourself. I’m tired and I can’t be arsed with it.”
“我很沮丧，”她说。“这很令人沮丧。但我不会让你尝试做那种操纵性的事情，你通过推开我来与陌生的内疚感发生争执，声称这是为了我，而实际上这只是惩罚自己的一种方式。我累了，我不能为此感到愤怒。

Opening his mouth, Lucius gave up on the words he was trying to find and huffed out an offended sigh. Crooking two fingers, he gestured to the brandy bottle and Hermione pushed it over the desk towards him. 
卢修斯张开嘴，放弃了他试图找到的词语，并冒犯地叹了口气。他用两根手指指着白兰地瓶子，赫敏把它从桌子上推向他。

“We’re working together,” she said, watching him pour a much smaller measure than she had. “And the result of that work will be a reduction in your sentence. People will get used to the idea that you’re going to be free. They’ll get used to the idea that I helped make it happen.” She paused, pursing her lips. “They’ll have to.”
“我们正在一起工作，”她说，看着他倒出的量比她小得多。“这项工作的结果将是减刑。人们会习惯你自由的想法。他们会习惯我帮助实现它的想法。她停顿了一下，抿起了嘴唇。“他们必须这样做。”

Lowering the glass from his lips, Lucius held up a finger and began searching his desk. “You’ve reminded me,” he said grimly. “I saw something this morning that might help with that.” He extracted a copy of the Prophet from beneath a heavy legal book and slid it over to Hermione. “Page five,” he explained, with a ‘go on’ gesture before he sat back in his chair and took another drink. 
Lucius放下嘴里的酒杯，举起一根手指，开始搜索他的桌子。“你提醒过我了，”他严肃地说。“我今天早上看到了一些可能有助于解决这个问题的东西。”他从一本沉重的法律书下面抽出一本先知，把它滑给赫敏。“第五页，”他解释道，做了个“继续”的手势，然后坐回椅子上，又喝了一杯。

With a curious look up at him, Hermione opened the paper and flicked through it. On reaching page five she had no further questions. Sandwiched between a handful of other articles in the middle of the page was the headline “An Unlikely Alliance” in thick, black print. Beneath it, were two pictures: one of Hermione and one of Lucius. 
赫敏好奇地抬头看了他一眼，打开了那张纸，翻了翻。读到第五页时，她没有再问什么了。夹在页面中间的几篇其他文章之间的是粗黑字的标题“一个不太可能的联盟”。在它下面，有两张照片：一张是赫敏的，一张是卢修斯的。

Pulling the paper closer, Hermione leaned forward. “ Today, the Ministry of Magic announced that it has brought together two highly unlikely figures to work on an as-yet undetailed project as part of Minister for Magic, Kingsley Shacklebolt’s, efforts to —” 
赫敏把纸拉得更近，身体前倾。“今天，魔法部宣布，它已经召集了两个极不可能的人物，作为魔法部长金斯利·沙克尔博尔特努力的一部分，从事一个尚未详细项目的工作——”

“Oh,” she said, glancing up at Lucius from beneath her brow to find his eyebrows raised in anticipation of her reaction. 
“哦，”她说，从眉毛下抬头瞥了一眼卢修斯，发现他扬起了眉毛，期待着她的反应。

“Imagine my surprise,” he said dryly, “when I found out that it was the Ministry that brought us together. Is there nothing it can’t do?”
“想象一下，”他干巴巴地说，“当我发现是魔法部把我们聚集在一起时，我感到多么惊讶。它没有做不到的事情吗？

Hermione snorted. “Yes, Kingsley said he might do this. Apparently, us working together could be a good look for the Ministry. Makes it look like a uniting force.”
赫敏哼了一声。“是的，金斯利说他可能会这样做。显然，我们一起工作可能会给教育部带来好处。让它看起来像一股团结的力量。

“Speaking of good looks,” Lucius added, setting his brandy down and leaning forward. “Is there any reason they used my Azkaban mugshot?” 
“说到好看，”卢修斯补充道，放下他的白兰地，身体前倾。“他们有什么理由用我的阿兹卡班大头照吗？”

Clamping her hand over her mouth, Hermione attempted to muffle an incredulous laugh when she noticed that was indeed the case. Beside a very pretty photo of her laughing and waving out of the page was a very unkempt and angry Lucius dressed in black and white. 
赫敏用手捂住嘴巴，试图压制住难以置信的笑声，但她注意到情况确实如此。在一张她大笑和挥手的照片旁边，是一个非常蓬头垢面、生气的卢修斯，穿着黑白衣服。

“Hardly my best look,” he said, sharply pulling the paper back over the desk and closing it so that he didn’t have to look at the article or his own face anymore. 
“可不是我最好看的样子，”他说，猛地把报纸拉回桌子上，然后合上它，这样他就不必再看那篇文章或自己的脸了。

“I’m sure they had their reasons.”
“我敢肯定他们有他们的理由。”

“Yes, and as soon as I’m free I’ll be stopping by the offices of the Prophet to hear them,” he said darkly. “Perhaps I’ll pay Auror Smythe a visit, too.”
“是的，一旦我有空，我就会去先知的办公室听他们说话，”他阴沉地说。“也许我也要去拜访傲罗斯迈斯。”

Hermione’s smile slipped. “Lucius.”
赫敏的笑容滑落了。“卢修斯。”

“I love you,” he reminded her, like it was some kind of explanation or justification. 
“我爱你，”他提醒她，就像是某种解释或辩解。

“So, you’ll try not to end up with another Azkaban mugshot, yes?”
“所以，你尽量不要再拍一张阿兹卡班的头像，对吧？”

Rolling his tongue in his mouth, he considered her for a moment then nodded. “Being an Auror is a very dangerous job.” Lifting his glass between his forefinger and thumb, he gave her a sarcastic smile. “I’m sure someone will get there before me.”
他在嘴里滚动着舌头，考虑了她一会儿，然后点了点头。“当傲罗是一份非常危险的工作。”他用食指和拇指举起酒杯，对她露出一个讽刺的微笑。“我相信有人会比我先到达那里。”

It's Christmas!
今天是圣诞节！

Chapter Notes

December 25th 
12 月 25 日

 

“Are you sure we can’t keep you?”
“你确定我们留不住你吗？”

The Weasleys were all gathered around the fireplace in Harry and Ginny’s sitting room, preparing to see Hermione off. All with the exception of Molly, who had declared that there were simply too many enchanted utensils to be supervised in the kitchen for her to take a moment away. 
韦斯莱一家都聚集在哈利和金妮客厅的壁炉旁，准备为赫敏送行。除了莫莉，她宣称厨房里有太多的魔法用具需要看管，她不能抽出片刻时间。

Hermione wasn't entirely surprised – she was leaving after the Weasley Christmas dinner to spend the night with the Malfoys at their manor and Molly wasn't entirely on board.
赫敏并不完全惊讶——她要在韦斯莱圣诞大餐后离开，去和马尔福一家在他们的庄园过夜，而莫丽并不完全同意。

It was only in anticipation of her Christmas arrangements that Hermione had finally decided to announce her relationship with Lucius to the wider Weasley family. While the revelation had not, as Ron and Ginny had gloomily predicted, resulted in the untimely deaths of Molly and Arthur, reactions had been mixed. 
只是在期待她的圣诞节安排时，赫敏才终于决定向更广泛的韦斯莱家族宣布她与卢修斯的关系。虽然这一发现并没有像罗恩和金妮悲观地预测的那样导致莫莉和亚瑟的英年早逝，但人们的反应却喜忧参半。

Molly had, of course, looked to Ron with a frankly alarming aggressiveness and asked him what he thought about it. When he'd shrugged, she'd asked him what he was going to do about it. And when he'd said "Nothing, mum!", she'd stormed out of the room. Ever since, she'd just pretended it wasn't happening and, actually, Hermione found she could deal with that because Molly wasn't accompanying it with her usual spate of passive aggressive slights. Well, with the exception of not saying farewell.
当然，莫莉以一种坦率地说令人担忧的咄咄逼人地看着罗恩，问他对此有何看法。当他耸耸肩时，她问他打算怎么做。当他说“没什么，妈妈！”时，她已经冲出了房间。从那以后，她就假装这件事没有发生，实际上，赫敏发现她可以处理这个问题，因为莫莉并没有伴随着她一贯的被动攻击性轻视。嗯，除了不说再见。

Percy had been the least incredulous. Having rubbed shoulders with Malfoy at the Ministry, he had readily pointed out that "the man can be charming when he wants", giving Hermione an understanding if irritatingly pitying look before he raised his book back in front of his face.
珀西是最不怀疑的。在魔法部与马尔福擦肩而过后，他欣然指出“这个男人可以随心所欲地迷人”，给了赫敏一个理解的眼神，虽然令人恼火地怜悯，然后他把书举回了他的面前。

George had transitioned from genuinely outraged disgust to jokes and not-so-tongue-in-cheek enquiries about Malfoy's potential as a Weasley’s Wizard Wheezes investor remarkably quickly. 
乔治已经从真正愤怒的厌恶转变为关于马尔福作为韦斯莱巫师喘息投资者的潜力的笑话和不那么半开玩笑的询问，速度非常快。

“How much of the wealth is actually gold , though, Hermione?” he’d asked, hands clasped as he’d leaned across the Burrow’s kitchen table towards her. “Are we talking a vault packed with galleons or has he just got assets coming out of his –” Only a sharp thwack with a tea towel on the back of his head from Ginny had stopped him.
“不过，赫敏，这些财富到底有多少是黄金呢？”他问道，双手紧握，隔着陋居的厨房桌子向她靠去。“我们说的是一个装满大帆船的金库，还是他刚刚从他的——”只有金妮用茶巾在他的后脑勺上猛烈地敲打阻止了他。

Arthur and Charlie, meanwhile, had given her very little reaction, which she interpreted as quiet if unenthusiastic support. When George had reminded his father that he had once knocked Lucius around the head in Flourish and Blotts, his tone suggesting that Arthur might want to do that again, Arthur had simply gone ruddy and said, “that was a long time ago, George.”  
与此同时，亚瑟和查理对她的反应很少，她将其解释为安静但并不热情的支持。当乔治提醒他的父亲，他曾经在Flourish and Blotts中敲过卢修斯的头时，他的语气暗示亚瑟可能想再做一次，亚瑟只是红润地说，“那是很久以前的事了，乔治。

Bill and Fleur were still coming around. It was, perhaps, because it had been them who had cared for her in the immediate aftermath of her ordeal at Malfoy Manor. They had seen her injuries, her tears, her haunted expression. They had fed her Dreamless Sleep. And they had not forgotten it. 
比尔和芙蓉仍然在身边。也许，是因为在她在马尔福庄园遭受磨难后，他们立即照顾了她。他们看到了她的伤势，她的眼泪，她萦绕不去的表情。他们喂饱了她的无梦睡眠。他们并没有忘记。

They, therefore, could not be convinced with words alone. Instead, each passing week which brought evidence of Hermione staying healthy and happy whilst being in a relationship with Lucius helped them slowly defrost.
因此，他们不能只用言语来说服他们。相反，赫敏在与卢修斯的关系中保持健康和快乐的证据每过一周都帮助他们慢慢解冻。

“I appreciate that, Harry,” Hermione said with a cheery smile as she reached for the bag of Floo Powder on their mantle. “But ‘tis the season for sharing and giving.” 
“我很感激，哈利，”赫敏一边开心地笑着说，一边伸手去拿他们斗篷上的飞路粉袋。“可是，现在是分享和给予的季节。”

“Feels a bit wrong to be giving the Malfoys a Muggleborn, though, doesn’t it?” asked George, looking around at his family uneasily. “Got a touch of the sacrificial offerings about it.”
“不过，给马尔福一家一个麻瓜出身的感觉有点不对劲，不是吗？”乔治问道，不安地环顾着他的家人。“稍微了解一下关于它的祭品。”

There was a dark murmur of agreement from Ron, Bill and Charlie, while Percy and Arthur appeared to be trying their hardest not to react at all. 
罗恩、比尔和查理发出了一阵同意的低语，而珀西和亚瑟似乎在尽最大努力不做出反应。

“Don’t let him unwrap you straight away,” Ginny said, drawing closer to fix Hermione’s dress at the waist. “Make him work for it.”
“别让他马上解开你的包裹，”金妮说，一边凑近去把赫敏的裙子固定在腰间。“让他为此努力。”

“Ginny!” came the collective groan of the Weasley boys and Harry.
“金妮！” 韦斯莱男孩和哈利集体呻吟起来。

Ignoring them, Ginny fixed her with a smile that was barely pained. She had, Hermione thought, been magnificent in her support and Hermione wasn’t sure she’d ever be able to truly express how grateful she was.
金妮无视他们，用一个几乎没有痛苦的微笑注视着她。赫敏想，她对她的支持非常出色，赫敏不确定她是否能够真正表达她有多么感激。

Swallowing a lump in her throat, Hermione lifted her eyes from Ginny to scan the gathered Weasleys and gave them a wave. 
赫敏咽下喉咙里的一团东西，把目光从金妮身上抬起，扫视着聚集在一起的韦斯莱一家，然后向他们挥了挥手。

“Don’t forget the New Year’s walk!” Ron reminded her as the fire lit his face with a green glow. “You’re on tea duty.”
“别忘了新年散步！”罗恩提醒她，火光照亮了他的脸。“你在值茶。”

“I won’t!” And with that, she stepped neatly into the fireplace and vanished in a burst of flame.
“我不会的！”“说完，她利落地走进壁炉，消失在一阵火焰中。

When Hermione arrived in the Malfoy Manor library, it was empty and the dim, lingering green glow of the fire was the only light source. Squinting at her watch, she realised she was around half an hour earlier than she’d told Lucius to expect her – she’d built in some buffer time in case the Weasleys were a little more insistent that she stayed. 
当赫敏到达马尔福庄园图书馆时，图书馆里空无一人，昏暗的、挥之不去的绿色火光是唯一的光源。她眯着眼睛看了看手表，意识到自己比她告诉卢修斯的等待时间早了大约半小时——她已经安排了一些缓冲时间，以防韦斯莱一家更坚持要她留下来。

Biting her lip, Hermione contemplated the unappealing prospect of sitting in the freezing library for half an hour to wait for Lucius to come looking for her. Adjusting her handbag on her shoulder, she whispered “Letty?” into the room. 
赫敏咬着嘴唇，想着在冰冷的图书馆里坐上半个小时，等卢修斯来找她，这是多么不吸引人的前景。她调整了一下肩上的手提包，对着房间低声说：“莱蒂？

Barely a second later, a loud crack signalled Letty’s arrival. “Hermione Granger is early!” was her shrill greeting, her high voice echoing in the library. “Master will be most surprised." Her eyes widened. "But pleased! Pleased, of course, for he was just telling the young master that Miss would not be long and now that Miss is here Letty can –”
仅仅过了一秒钟，一声响亮的噼啪声标志着莱蒂的到来。“赫敏·格兰杰来得早了！”她尖锐的问候，她高亢的声音在图书馆里回荡。“师父会非常惊讶。”她睁大了眼睛。“但很高兴！当然，他很高兴，因为他只是告诉少爷，小姐不会太久了，现在小姐来了，莱蒂可以——”

“Merry Christmas, Letty,” Hermione cut in, keen to bring Letty’s explanatory ramble to a neat conclusion.
“圣诞快乐，莱蒂，”赫敏打断了她，急切地想把莱蒂的解释性漫谈画上一个简洁的句号。

With a soft gasp, Letty bowed so low her nose almost touched the ground, fortunately missing Hermione’s instinctive cringe as she did so. It was always going to be a hard thing to accept. “Merry Christmas to Hermione Granger.” 
莱蒂轻轻地喘息着，低低地低下了头，她的鼻子几乎碰到了地面，幸运的是，她这样做时错过了赫敏本能的畏缩。这总是一件很难接受的事情。“祝赫敏·格兰杰圣诞快乐。”

“Would you mind taking me to the master?” she asked. “I’m not sure where they spend their Christmasses and Lucius didn’t exactly say…” 
“你介意带我去见主人吗？”“我不确定他们在哪里度过圣诞节，卢修斯也没有确切地说......”

“Yes, yes.” Letty nodded enthusiastically, her ears waggling. “Of course. Hermione Granger must follow Letty.” 
“是的，是的。”莱蒂热情地点点头，她的耳朵晃动着。“当然。赫敏·格兰杰必须跟着莱蒂。

Letty snapped her legs together and straightened her back in a way that reminded Hermione of a nutcracker, before walking at an impressively fast pace towards the door. Hermione hurried after her, her low heels clicking loudly against the floor. 
莱蒂把双腿并拢，挺直了背，让赫敏想起了胡桃夹子，然后以惊人的速度向门口走去。赫敏急忙跟在她后面，她的低跟鞋在地板上发出响亮的咔哒声。

“So, where are they, Letty?” Hermione asked conversationally as they wound their way through the far more brightly lit corridors of the manor. “The dining room?”
“那么，他们在哪里，莱蒂？”赫敏在他们蜿蜒穿过庄园灯火通明得多的走廊时，交谈着问道。“餐厅？”

“No, Miss. The family is in the drawing room now,” squeaked Letty, not noticing that Hermione’s pace immediately slowed. “Although Miss is right; the Master said that they is to move into the dining room before Hermione Granger arrives but now that Miss is here he might – Miss?”
“不，小姐。一家人现在都在客厅里，“莱蒂吱吱作响，没有注意到赫敏的步伐立刻放慢了。“虽然小姐是对的;主人说他们要在赫敏·格兰杰到来之前搬进餐厅，但现在小姐在这里，他可能会——小姐？

Hermione had slowed to a stop in the middle of the corridor, an uneasy roiling in her stomach that made her worry she would shortly get another look at that third yorkshire pudding Molly had forced onto her plate. “The drawing room?” 
赫敏放慢了脚步，停在了走廊中间，一阵不安在她的胃里翻腾着，让她担心自己很快就会再看一眼莫莉强行放在她盘子里的第三个约克郡布丁。“客厅？”

“Yes,” said Letty, her wrinkles deepening as she frowned. “If Miss would like to come, Letty is taking Miss.”
“是的，”莱蒂说，她的皱纹随着她的皱眉而加深。“如果小姐想来，莱蒂就带小姐去。”

Swallowing, Hermione hesitated. The drawing room. In the many months since it had last been brought up to her, she still hadn’t revisited it and Lucius hadn’t once pressed it. The fact that Letty had said that he was planning to move their evening into the dining room before Hermione’s arrival suggested that he hadn’t planned to press it tonight either. 
吞咽着，赫敏犹豫了。客厅。自从上次向她提起这件事以来的好几个月里，她仍然没有重新审视它，卢修斯也从未催促过它。莱蒂说他打算在赫敏到来之前把他们的晚上搬到餐厅，这一事实表明他也不打算今晚再坚持下去。

That they were going to move from their usual room for her and just pretend that it was normal didn’t sit all that well with Hermione. She was appreciative, of course, but it made it feel like they were…tiptoeing around her and that she did not like. Not only that, Hermione hated the idea that she would be forcing Astoria to move – she had rallied admirably after giving birth but she still weakened easily and Hermione didn’t relish the idea of effectively forcing her from a comfortable position.
他们要从她平常的房间里搬走，只是假装这很正常，这让赫敏不太舒服。她当然很感激，但这让感觉他们很感激......蹑手蹑脚地绕着她走，她不喜欢。不仅如此，赫敏还讨厌她会强迫阿斯托利亚移动的想法——她在生完孩子后恢复得令人钦佩，但她仍然很容易虚弱，赫敏不喜欢有效地将她从舒适的位置逼走的想法。

“Yes,” Hermione finally said, forcing her legs back into action with the sense that she was unsticking her soles from the thick carpet. “Sorry, Letty, carry on.”

Hitting the floor with a soft thump , it emitted a grumbling roar, drawing a scowl from Draco. A snuffling, tearful noise from Scorpius, however, prompted Draco to hurriedly set his glass down and lunge out of his seat to pick the lion up.
就在那一刻，斯科皮用力、兴奋地摇晃了他的狮子，狮子从他的手中飞了出去。轻轻的砰的一声撞在地板上，它发出了咕哝的咆哮，引来了德拉科的皱眉。然而，斯科皮发出的鼻息声、泪流满面的声音促使德拉科匆忙忙放下酒杯，从座位上冲出来把狮子抱起来。

德拉科跪在妻子面前，轻轻地将狮子压回斯科皮疯狂挥舞的手中。“如果这让他成为格兰芬多，”德拉科对赫敏说，“我怪你。

“你敢吗，”德拉科厉声说，用一只保护性的手臂搂住了斯科皮和阿斯托利亚，让他的儿子大笑起来。

赫敏翻了个白眼，发现卢修斯在玻璃杯边缘给了她一个微妙的微笑。她也回以微笑，她的脸颊温暖起来，这与她离火堆的距离无关。

赫敏对卢修斯的所有喜爱都从她的表情中消失了，她瞪了他一眼，但他只是抿了抿嘴唇，把目光转向火堆，以一种可笑的天真。

“你来了，马尔福，”她说，比赛的前景消除了她最后的不适。

赫敏走进客厅时，客厅里空无一人，除了圣诞树还亮着，几乎完全是黑暗的。但她觉得这并不对劲。它看起来不像她整晚围着的那棵树。它更像是她父母每年都竖起来的那棵树——它有同样凌乱的灯光，对于大空间来说太小了。

“卢修斯？”她在黑暗中喊道，她的声音回荡着。她不记得自己为什么在客厅里找他。他去哪儿了？他请她在那里见他吗？

她还是不喜欢这个房间，尤其是没有他。当他不在时，没有什么可以抵消她的不适。没有温暖。

有什么东西在她脚下嘎吱作响，她低头看去。玻璃。不。晶体？很多。顺着它的踪迹，赫敏环顾四周，发现吊灯已经掉了下来，砸在了地板上。它很大，比它高高悬挂在她头顶时看起来要大得多。它反射着树上的圣诞灯饰，呈现出一种几乎不真实的微光。她来的时候，它没有被砸成那样，对吧？不，房间里空无一人。不是吗？

“Mudblood.”
“泥巴种。”

Bellatrix. Her singsong voice crept up Hermione's back like a spider.
贝拉特里克斯。她的歌声像蜘蛛一样爬上赫敏的背。

"Mudblood."
“泥巴种。”

就像黑暗本身把她吐了出来一样，贝拉特里克斯出现在她面前。时间并没有改变她。她还穿着她死时穿的衣服。拿着赫敏的魔杖......她不是偷了吗？还有那把刀。刀。

赫敏僵在原地，试图叫卢修斯来。试。她试图大喊大叫，但她的声音传不来，所以她所能做的就是逃跑。她原地转身寻找门，但没有门。惊慌失措的她跑向她认为应该在的地方，但她还没走两步就被自己的脚绊倒了。

然后贝拉特里克斯就扑在她身上，跨坐在她身上，把她固定在地板上。她是个狂野的东西，全是疯狂的笑声和黑色的卷发。纯粹的恶意的模糊。侮辱、威胁和拳头如雨点般落在赫敏身上。每一次击打，她都以为会感觉到刀子的冰冷刺痛。

Bellatrix grabbed Hermione’s hair and pushed her face into the floor. Through her tear-filled eyes she could see Lucius standing by the…the door. It had reappeared. He could get her out if he was by the door. But he was ghost-like, just staring. 
“卢修斯！”赫敏终于尖叫起来，他的名字从她身上被撕了下来。她一遍又一遍地喊着他的名字，哭泣着，试图抬起手臂以保护自己免受 Bellatrix 的耳光和拳打脚踢。贝拉特里克斯抓住赫敏的头发，把她的脸推到地板上。透过她充满泪水的眼睛，她可以看到卢修斯站在......门。它又出现了。如果他在门口，他可以把她救出来。但他就像鬼一样，只是盯着看。

叫他的名字也没用。他什么也没做。他为什么什么都没做？

“泥巴种，”贝拉特里克斯一遍又一遍地唱着，把赫敏浓密的头发从头上扯下来。赫敏挣扎着，但没用——她的身体不知何故太重了，她无法移动，但又如此轻盈，以至于贝拉特里克斯很容易，如此容易地将她压住。为了伤害她。

“卢修斯，”赫敏上气不接下气地啜泣着，贝拉特里克斯把刀举过头顶。“拜托。请帮帮我。

圣诞灯饰让刀刃在空中划出弧线，闪闪发光，赫敏发出了一声令人毛骨悚然的尖叫。然后地板掉下来了，她也开始跌倒。独自。从空中坠落。没有贝拉特里克斯——她和刀一起消失了。

地板又回来了。冷。不同的楼层。石头。苍白。熟悉。赫敏喘着粗气，就像她刚刚从水下深处出来一样，但还没来得及缓解，就变成了一声痛苦的啜泣。

“赫敏。”

卢修斯的声音急促而关切，他跪在她身边。他不知何故和刚刚看到贝拉特里克斯攻击她的卢修斯是一样的，而不是一样的。当他伸出一只手时，赫敏把它拍开，试图爬开，却发现自己被困住了，她的背压在床架上。他的床。他们的床。他们已经分享了几个月的那个。又一声喘息的抽泣使她的身体颤抖。

“赫敏。”他更温柔地说着她的名字，但他没有试图再次触碰她。“这是一场噩梦。那不是真的。

“贝拉特里克斯，”她解释道。光是名字就足以让他理解。

当他紧紧抓住法兰绒时，他的指关节处闪过一丝白骨。“你在喊我的名字，”他说。

她并不是要说什么有什么指责，但她怀疑卢修斯听到了，因为他的眼睛抽搐了一下，这表明他几乎设法压制住了一丝畏缩。

贝拉特里克斯已经很久没有造访过她的梦了。赫敏的大脑把她逼回那个客厅已经很久了。月复一月。

这很奇怪，但她开始怀疑，她在庄园里度过的所有时间，以及她与卢修斯的和平，是否随着时间的推移，帮助他们缓解了平静。客厅几乎变成了一个虚幻的地方，与她喜欢的马尔福庄园完全脱节，因此，更容易忘记。

那天晚上早些时候进入客厅肯定很不和谐，但她认为随着夜晚的进行，她已经应付得很好。也许只是被迫再次将其视为一个真实的地方，对她的潜意识来说就足够了。

“但我本来可以阻止你，”他说，他的声音严厉而充满自责。

因为他没有接受无梦睡眠，赫敏也无意强迫他，他通常只是等到疲惫赶上他。

“I don’t want to go back to bed,” Hermione said, her voice small. Nothing about going back and lying in the dark appealed to her in that moment, even if it would be in Lucius’ arms. 
“我不想回去睡觉，”赫敏说，她的声音很小。在那一刻，她对回去躺在黑暗中没有任何吸引力，即使它会在卢修斯的怀里。

“No,” Lucius agreed, rising to his feet. “No. Let’s…would you be able to get dressed?”
“不，”卢修斯同意道，站了起来。“不。让我们...你能穿衣服吗？

Curiosity tingling at the edges of her numbness, Hermione looked up at him questioningly. “I think…yes. Why?”
好奇心在她麻木的边缘刺痛，赫敏疑惑地抬头看着他。“我认为......是的。为什么？

He shook his head and held his hands out to her to help her out of the bath. “Dress warm.”
他摇摇头，向她伸出双手，帮助她从浴缸里出来。“穿得暖和。”

Still sniffling, Hermione rummaged through the kitchen cupboards of Malfoy Manor, looking for some kind of jar. One of Lucius’ woollen outer cloaks was making the job more difficult than it had to be thanks to its weight but he’d insisted that her jeans and jumper would not be warm enough and had wrapped it around her shoulders. 
赫敏仍然抽着鼻子，在马尔福庄园的厨房橱柜里翻找，寻找某种罐子。由于它的重量，卢修斯的一件羊毛外衣使这项工作变得比它必须的要困难，但他坚持认为她的牛仔裤和套头衫不够暖和，并把它缠在她的肩膀上。

They were, he’d revealed once he’d led her into the kitchen, going into the grounds. When Hermione had disbelievingly pointed out that it was around four in the morning and still dark, he had simply said “yes”, instructing her to wait before disappearing outside. 
他们是，他在带她进厨房，走进院子后透露。当赫敏难以置信地指出现在是凌晨四点左右，天还很黑时，他只是简单地说了一句“好”，指示她等一等，然后消失在外面。

Dreading facing the freezing winter morning, Hermione had decided that some bluebell flames were in order. 
面对寒冷的冬日早晨，赫敏感到恐惧，她决定来点风信子的火焰。

Hauling two jars that she suspected were supposed to hold homemade jams out of the back of a cupboard with a victorious grunt, she withdrew her wand from her jeans and deposited some of the flames inside. She was just screwing the lids onto the jars when Lucius leaned into the kitchen and gestured for her to join him outside with a jerk of his head. 
她从橱柜后面拖出两个罐子，怀疑这些罐子应该是用来装自制果酱的，她咕哝了一声，从牛仔裤里抽出魔杖，把一些火焰放进去。她刚把盖子拧到罐子上，卢修斯就靠进厨房，猛地摇了摇头，示意她和他一起出去。

It was a mercifully dry, clear morning but the cold December air made Hermione inhale sharply through clenched teeth as she slipped out into the darkness. When the door creaked closed behind her, the comforting glow of the kitchen disappeared and they were left with only the eerie blue light of her jarred flames.
这是一个干燥、晴朗的早晨，但十二月的寒冷空气让赫敏在滑入黑暗时，咬紧牙关猛地吸了一口气。当门在她身后吱吱作响地关上时，厨房里令人欣慰的光芒消失了，只剩下她被激怒的火焰发出的诡异的蓝光。

“Oh!” Hermione yelped, flinching as something began snuffling around her at hip height. Holding a jar aloft, she was relieved when it illuminated Cato. He was so much larger than that first afternoon she’d seen him, closer to a full-grown dog than the excitable puppy he’d been. He barked once, seemingly in greeting, before a hush from Lucius stopped any more.  With the exception of the sound of Cato’s panting breath and the rustle of the wind in the trees, they were left in silence. 
“哦！”赫敏大喊着，当有什么东西开始在她的臀部高度嗖嗖作响时，她畏缩了一下。她高举着一个罐子，当罐子照亮卡托时，她松了一口气。他比她看到的第一个下午大得多，比起他以前那只兴奋的小狗，他更像一只成年狗。他吠叫了一声，似乎是在打招呼，然后卢修斯的安静又停止了。除了卡托喘息的声音和风吹在树上的沙沙声，他们一片寂静。

Hermione handed Lucius a jar and he took it with a murmur of thanks, a shiver passing through him as the hot glass made contact with his cold hands. Without a word, they walked side-by-side away from the manor and into the grounds, Cato plodding alongside them.
赫敏递给卢修斯一个罐子，他接过来，低声感谢，当热玻璃碰到他冰冷的手时，他全身发抖。他们一言不发地并肩走出庄园，走进了院子里，卡托在他们身边蹒跚而行。

Lifting the jar up to his face, Lucius inspected the writhing blue flames with interest, the vapour of his breath cast into relief by their glow. He gave the jar a firm shake, raising his eyebrows when the flames didn’t even flicker. “This is a good charm.”
卢修斯将罐子举到脸上，饶有兴致地检查着扭动的蓝色火焰，他的呼吸蒸汽被它们的光芒所笼罩。他用力摇晃罐子，在火焰甚至没有闪烁时扬起眉毛。“这真是个好护身符。”

“I know,” Hermione said smugly, bringing her free hand down to absently pet Cato’s head as he brushed by her. “I like to think it’s my speciality.”
“我知道，”赫敏得意地说，在卡托擦过她时，她空出来的手伸到心不在焉地抚摸着她的头。“我喜欢认为这是我的专长。”

The morning frost crunched beneath their feet as they crossed the grass and Hermione closed her eyes briefly, raising her chin to inhale deeply. The cold, clear air was almost enough to clear her stuffy nose and it cooled her cheeks more effectively than the damp flannel had. 
当他们穿过草地时，清晨的霜冻在他们脚下嘎吱作响，赫敏短暂地闭上了眼睛，抬起下巴深吸一口气。冰冷、清澈的空气几乎足以清除她闷热的鼻子，而且比潮湿的法兰绒更有效地冷却了她的脸颊。

Turning her head to Lucius, she found he was already looking at her. A gust of wind swept over them, blowing her hair off her shoulders and making her teeth chatter. “Why are we out here?” she asked, hugging her jar protectively to her middle.
她转头看向卢修斯，发现他已经在看着她了。一阵风吹过他们，吹走了她肩膀上的头发，让她的牙齿打颤。“我们为什么在这里？” 她问道，一边保护性地将她的罐子抱在中间。

“I thought it might be better than remaining in the manor,” Lucius said, lifting his shoulders. “In the first year of my house arrest, I must have spent every night walking out here. The open space is good for the mind, I think.”
“我想这可能比留在庄园里要好，”卢修斯说，抬起了他的肩膀。“在我被软禁的第一年，我肯定每天晚上都在这里散步。我认为，开放空间对心灵有好处。

“It is nice,” Hermione admitted, nodding. Drawing in a deep breath, she watched it billow out in front of her as she released it. “Freezing but nice.”
“很好，”赫敏承认道，点点头。她深吸一口气，看着它在她面前翻滚而出，同时她松开了它。“很冷，但很好。”

Cato slipped between them, sylph-like until his wagging tail beat their legs. Hermione laughed and stroked his back as he passed, drawing a faint smile from Lucius. “And Cato is an excellent distraction,” he added.
卡托滑到他们之间，像仙女一样滑行，直到他摇晃的尾巴敲打着他们的腿。赫敏笑着走过时抚摸着他的背，引来了卢修斯淡淡的微笑。“而 Cato 是一个很好的分散注意力的人，”他补充道。

They walked in silence for a time, seemingly aimlessly, with the bluebell flames proving to be just enough to light a path. Hermione found herself wondering what they must look like from the manor – two wills-o'-the-wisp in search of travellers, perhaps. 
他们沉默地走了一会儿，似乎漫无目的地，事实证明，风信子的火焰刚好足以照亮一条路。赫敏发现自己在想，他们从庄园里看出去一定是什么样子——也许是两个寻找旅行者的精灵。

Slowing, she turned to look at the manor over her shoulder. It loomed up in the darkness, a couple of its illuminated windows the only indication that there was life within. Stopping entirely, Hermione turned and simply stared at the building, catching her lower lip between her teeth. A moment later, she felt Lucius at her shoulder, gazing with her.
她放慢了脚步，转身看向肩膀上的庄园。它在黑暗中若隐若现，几扇灯火通明的窗户是唯一表明里面有生命的迹象。赫敏完全停了下来，转过身来，只是盯着那栋建筑，用牙齿夹住了她的下唇。过了一会儿，她感觉到卢修斯在她的肩膀上，与她一起凝视着。

“We could block off the drawing room, you know. It’d be easy to do. You’d never have to look at it again.”
“我们可以把客厅堵住，你知道的。这很容易做到。你再也不用看它了。

Sighing, Hermione shook her head. “I really wouldn’t want you to do that,” she said. “It’s –”
赫敏叹了口气，摇了摇头。“我真的不希望你那样做，”她说。“这是——”

“It’s a single room in a very large house,” he cut in, glancing down at the top of her head with a frown. “I can live without it. I should have done it already.”
“这是一座非常大的房子里的一个单人间，”他打断道，皱着眉头低头瞥了一眼她的头顶。“没有它我也能活下去。我应该早就这么做了。

Looking up over her shoulder, Hermione smiled softly at him. “No. No, I think I was doing well when the room was in my periphery. I sort of…got used to it. And the rest of the manor is so familiar to me now, maybe I can start looking at it directly.” 
赫敏抬起头来，对他温柔地笑了笑。“不。不，我认为当房间在我周围时，我做得很好。我有点......已经习惯了。而且庄园的其余部分现在对我来说太熟悉了，也许我可以开始直接看看它。

She turned back, her eyes trailing to the centre of the lower floor where she knew the drawing room was located. “Slowly, of course, but…I think I can do it.”
她转过身来，目光落在下层的中央，她知道那里是客厅。“当然，慢慢来，但是......我想我能做到。

“You’re not at fault if you can’t,” he said, his voice low. “Protecting yourself wouldn’t make you any less of a Gryffindor.”
“如果你不能，那你也没有错，”他低声说。“保护自己不会让你变得不那么像个格兰芬多。”

Tucking the jar into the crook of her arm, Hermione tore her gaze away from Malfoy Manor and reached out to take Lucius’ hand. “Let’s keep going,” she said, tugging him gently. 
赫敏把罐子塞进她的臂弯里，把目光从马尔福庄园上移开，伸手握住卢修斯的手。“我们继续吧，”她说，轻轻地拉着他。

They were rounding a tall clump of hedges when Hermione gasped. Ahead of them, a large spindly tree glowed all the colours of the rainbow. All its leaves had fallen, gathering in damp piles around the base of its trunk, but various bulbs of light flit between its thick, dark branches, lending it an ethereal beauty. The lights twittered as they moved, like they were conversing with one another.
他们正在绕过一丛高高的树篱，这时赫敏倒抽了一口气。在他们面前，一棵细长的大树闪耀着彩虹的所有颜色。它所有的叶子都落下了，在树干的根部聚集成一个个潮湿的堆积，但各种光亮的灯泡在它又粗又黑的树枝之间飞舞，赋予它一种空灵的美感。灯光随着他们的移动而叽叽喳喳地响着，就像他们在互相交谈一样。

"Oh," Hermione breathed, her eyes alight as she broke away from Lucius to approach the tree with slow steps. "It's fairies." 
“哦，”赫敏喘着气，眼睛闪闪发光，她挣脱了卢修斯，迈着缓慢的步伐接近那棵树。“是仙女。”

She wrapped her arms around her jar of flames, allowing her cloak to cover their light so that she could create a perfect darkness in which to appreciate the tree. When Lucius didn't stop at her side as he had before, she glanced back and saw his attention was primarily on Cato, ensuring that the excitable dog wouldn't alarm the fairies.
她用双臂搂住她的火焰罐，让她的斗篷遮住它们的光芒，这样她就可以创造一个完美的黑暗，在其中欣赏这棵树。当卢修斯没有像以前那样停在她身边时，她回头看了一眼，发现他的注意力主要集中在卡托身上，确保这只兴奋的狗不会惊动仙女。

"This might be the safest distance," Lucius said, a calming hand on Cato's head. 
“这可能是最安全的距离，”卢修斯说，一只手放在卡托的头上。

Nodding, Hermione dropped back to stand with him and Cato, taking in the spectacle of the tree with wide eyes. She'd only seen a tree so populated with faeries once before. In these very grounds, in fact.
赫敏点点头，退后一步，与他和卡托站在一起，睁大眼睛欣赏着树的奇观。她以前只见过一棵树上长满了仙灵。事实上，正是在这些理由中。

"Wait." Hermione leaned around Lucius to count along the windows of the manor. "Is this the tree from the summer?" she asked, her voice rising with surprise."I thought Care and Control were going to come and sort it? I sent a letter to Graves."
“等等。”赫敏靠在卢修斯身边，沿着庄园的窗户数着。“这是夏天的树吗？” 她问道，她的声音因惊讶而提高。我以为 Care and Control 会来解决这个问题？我给格雷夫斯写了一封信。

A small hum from Lucius was the only response she received. 
Lucius 轻轻地哼了一声，这是她收到的唯一回应。

"They didn't come?" she asked, her brow lowering and her eyes narrowing.
“他们没来吗？” 她问道，眉头低垂，眼睛眯起。

"No, they didn’t."
“不，他们没有。”

"That's unaccountable of them," Hermione said, outraged. "They have a responsibility to these creatures! Did they at least say why ?"
“那是对他们的不负责任，”赫敏愤怒地说。“他们对这些生物负有责任！他们至少说了为什么吗？

"No," Lucius said lightly. "But I think we can both make an educated guess, hm?"
“不，”卢修斯淡淡地说。“但我想我们俩都可以做出有根据的猜测，嗯？”

Huffing out a frustrated sigh, Hermione looked back to the tree, her lips pursing. "Why didn’t you tell me?" she eventually asked, the words practically bursting out of her. "I'd have chased them up."
赫敏沮丧地叹了口气，回头看向树，抿着嘴唇。“你为什么不告诉我？” 她最终问道，这些话几乎是从她身上迸发出来的。“我会追上去的。”

"I truly can't imagine anything worse than having you make appeals for me to that department," he said dryly. "No offence."
“我真的想不出还有什么比让你替我向那个部门上诉更糟糕的了，”他干巴巴地说。“没有冒犯。”

Tutting, Hermione gave him a sidelong look. "You seem…" She lifted a shoulder, the right side of her face scrunching in a cringe. " Alright about it, to be fair."
啧啧，赫敏侧头看了他一眼。“你看起来......”她抬起一个肩膀，右脸皱成一团。“好吧，公平地说。”

Lucius tipped his head left then right consideringly. "Well, I broke one of the good crystal glasses and cracked another. But then I decided…I quite like them."
卢修斯若有所思地向左倾斜，然后向右倾斜。“嗯，我打碎了一只上好的水晶眼镜，又打碎了另一只。但后来我决定......我很喜欢他们。

"They’re festive," Hermione offered.
“他们很喜庆，”赫敏提议。

"I thought so, too."
“我也是这么认为的。”

"What about the Bowtruckles? What will you do about them?"
“那 Bowtruckles 呢？你会怎么处理他们？

"I don’t have to worry about them until spring." Lucius adjusted his jar in his arm so that he could lean down to properly scratch Cato behind his ears. "I rather thought: why not enjoy the fae for what they are while I can, rather than fret about the problem they'll become."
“在春天之前，我不必担心他们。”卢修斯调整了一下他手臂上的罐子，这样他就可以俯下身来适当地抓挠卡托的耳后。“我宁愿想：为什么不在我能的时候享受一下精灵的本来面目，而不是担心它们会变成什么问题。”

When he received no response but silence, Lucius peered at Hermione and found her expression warm. Or at least, as warm as it could appear in the cool blue glow of the flames.
当他没有得到回应，只有沉默时，卢修斯凝视着赫敏，发现她的表情很温暖。或者至少，在火焰的凉爽蓝色光芒中显得尽可能温暖。

"That's quite measured," she said, a smile playing around her lips. "I think I'm impressed."
“这很有分寸，”她说，嘴角露出笑容。“我觉得我印象深刻。”

"After nearly a decade under house arrest, I was due a breakthrough," was his tired reply.
“在被软禁了近十年之后，我应该取得突破，”他疲惫地回答。

Laughing through her nose, Hermione reached out and slid her hand into his. Interlinking their fingers, she sighed and turned her gaze to the tree. The multi-coloured glow of the faeries created a kaleidoscopic effect on her face.
赫敏从鼻子里笑了起来，伸出手把她的手滑进了他的手里。他们十指相接，她叹了口气，将目光转向那棵树。仙灵的五彩光芒在她的脸上营造出万花筒般的效果。

"Thank you," she said after a few minutes. "For this. It’s helping, I think."
“谢谢你，”几分钟后她说。“为了这个。我认为这很有帮助。

"None of it would be necessary if not for me," he replied quietly. "In part, anyway."
“如果不是我，这一切都没有必要，”他平静地回答。“至少在一定程度上。”

"Mmm." Hermione nibbled her lip, nodding slowly. "Still." She squeezed his hand tightly. "Thank you. For this moment, at least."
“嗯。”赫敏咬了咬嘴唇，缓缓地点了点头。“还是。”她紧紧地捏住他的手。“谢谢你。至少在这一刻。

January 12th 2007
一月 12th 2007

 

Hermione crossed a thick line through her most recent sentence and huffed a sigh through her nose. Re-reading her work as a whole, her eyes darting to-and-fro across the page, she absent-mindedly ran the feather of her quill between her lips. A natural continuation finally occurring to her, she hurriedly re-inked her quill and began scribbling again.
赫敏在她最近的一句话中越过了一条粗线，从鼻子里叹了口气。她把自己的作品作为一个整体重新阅读，她的眼睛在书页上来回扫视，她心不在焉地把羽毛笔的羽毛滑过嘴唇。她终于自然而然地想到了，她匆忙地重新给羽毛笔上墨，又开始涂鸦。

“I do believe that’s my desk.”
“我确实相信那是我的桌子。”

Stiffening, Hermione glanced up from her parchment to see Lucius standing in the door to his study, his hand resting on the door handle. Catching her eye, he raised his eyebrows to indicate his expectation of an explanation.
赫敏僵硬地从羊皮纸上抬起头来，看到卢修斯站在书房的门口，他的手放在门把手上。吸引她的目光，他扬起眉毛，表示他期待得到解释。

“You weren’t using it,” Hermione replied, bowing her head to continue writing. It wasn’t only that; his study was much more pleasant to work in than the library early in the morning, especially in winter. When she had walked in to see the faintly pink fingertips of dawn on the horizon through the windows, it had been an easy decision to settle in and enjoy the sunrise.
“你没用它，”赫敏回答，低头继续写作。不仅如此;他的书房比清晨在图书馆工作要愉快得多，尤其是在冬天。当她走进去，透过窗户看到地平线上淡淡的粉红色黎明指尖时，安顿下来欣赏日出是一个很容易的决定。

“I hardly had a chance – you didn’t wake me up.” Lucius stepped into the room and closed the study door with a click . “Aren’t we supposed to be working on this together?” he asked as he strolled towards her, slipping his hands into his pockets.
“我几乎没有机会——你没叫醒我。”卢修斯走进房间，咔嚓一声关上了书房的门。“我们不是应该一起做这件事吗？”他一边问道，一边向她走来，双手口袋里。

“I didn’t dare wake you – it was before ten.” Hermione briefly glanced up at him from beneath her brow as she re-inked her quill. “Besides, are you forgetting that you barely slept the past two nights? I couldn’t have woken you even if I’d wanted to, Lucius, you were dead to the world.”
“我不敢叫醒你——已经不到十点了。”赫敏从眉毛下短暂地抬头看了他一眼，重新给她的羽毛笔上墨。“再说了，你忘了这两天晚上你几乎没睡吗？就算我想叫醒你，卢修斯，你对这个世界已经死了。

Lucius came around to her side of the desk and half sat on its edge, crossing one ankle over the other as he looked down at her. With a sidelong glare at his hips, Hermione paused in her writing to shift a sheet of parchment away from where he had almost sat on it. “How long have you been here?” he asked.
卢修斯走到她这边，半坐在桌沿上，低头看着她，一只脚踝交叉在另一只脚踝上。赫敏侧头瞪了一眼他的臀部，停下了她的写作，将一张羊皮纸从他几乎坐在上面的地方移开。“你在这里多久了？”

“A few hours.”
“几个小时。”

He nodded slowly, crossing his arms and glancing up to look out of the window at the clear winter morning. “And it wasn’t because of any –?”
他缓缓地点点头，交叉双臂，抬头瞥了一眼窗外晴朗的冬日清晨。“那不是因为什么——？”

“不，”赫敏说，以华丽和淡淡的叹息结束了一句话。“我睡得很好。只。。。要做的事情。

He made a satisfied noise and Hermione set down her quill, picking up her parchment to hold it out to him. “Can you read this?” she asked, scratching her forehead and sending her fringe askew. “It's only a subsection but I want to make sure it’s absolutely clear; nothing up for interpretation.”
他满意地发出声音，赫敏放下她的羽毛笔，拿起她的羊皮纸递给他。“你能读懂这个吗？”她问道，挠了挠额头，歪歪扭扭地歪歪扭扭的刘海。“这只是一个小节，但我想确保它绝对清晰;没有什么可以解释的。

Plucking the parchment from her hand, Lucius rested his elbow on the forearm he still had crossed across his middle and scanned over the paragraphs she’d spent the last hour and a half carefully constructing. Hermione kept her eyes fixed on his face, searching for any shift in expression so that she could preemptively explain any issues he might think about raising. It was her continual instinct to do this, she was sure, which ensured he kept his face utterly unreadable. 
卢修斯从她手里掏出羊皮纸，将手肘放在他仍然交叉在他中间的前臂上，扫视着她花了最后一个半小时精心构建的段落。赫敏的眼睛一直盯着他的脸，寻找任何表情的变化，这样她就可以先发制人地解释他可能想提出的任何问题。她确信，这是她持续的本能，这确保了他的脸完全看不懂。

卢修斯悄悄地清了清嗓子，从桌子上站起来，转过身来面对它。他把羊皮纸放在表面，弯下腰，伸手去拿她一直在用的羽毛笔。当他举起它时，他发现末端的羽毛聚集在一起，他的脸上闪过厌恶。

“我说过我不嚼它们，”赫敏气愤地说。“我只是有点......当我集中注意力时，把它们放在我的嘴唇附近。

Lucius did nothing but hum critically as he reached up to ink the quill. Hesitating, he added another couple of words and set the quill down before sliding the parchment back to her.
卢修斯什么也没做，只是挑剔地哼了一声，伸手给羽毛笔上墨。他花了一点时间重新阅读了羊皮纸，然后在第五段中划掉了几个字，无视了赫敏搂着他的手臂，带着想要抗议的神情。犹豫了一下，他又说了几个字，放下羽毛笔，然后把羊皮纸滑回给她。

赫敏指着他划掉并替换的单词问道，“这有什么问题？

卢修斯歪着头，嘴巴若有所思地扭动着。“啊......太具体了。他直起身来，低头看着她淡淡的皱眉。“我知道你没说什么可以解释的，但一点点含糊会让它更容易接受。此外，它不一定对你不利。

当赫敏带着他所说的内容重新阅读草稿时，卢修斯扫视了桌子的其余部分，看到角落里又有四个卷轴。“天哪，我的人一直很忙。”

“很好。”卢修斯一言不发，转身走到桌子的另一边，把自己放到她平时坐的椅子上，伸手去拿最近的卷轴。

当他拿着它坐回椅子上并交叉双腿时，他停了下来。放下卷轴，他在座位上挪动了一下，从桌子对面皱起眉头看着她。“我忘了我把它短了一两英寸，”他抱怨道，一边拉着椅子的扶手。

“也许我们应该交换一下，”卢修斯说，继续变换。

卢修斯对这个陌生的麻瓜短语眨了眨眼。“它几乎没有药用感。”

“Well, it is for me.”
“嗯，这是给我的。”

卢修斯抱怨着，坐回座位上，展开羊皮纸，用羊皮纸挡住了赫敏的视线，这样他就可以忘记自己离地面有多近了。他们沉默地工作了一会儿，赫敏刮掉草稿，卢修斯一遍又一遍地读着，然后修改，把它们单独堆起来，让她再读一遍。

卢修斯快到需要喝茶的地步了，他放下了他最新的羊皮纸卷轴，告诉赫敏，当他发现她双手抱着头盯着一张空白的羊皮纸时。他低头看了一眼他一直在阅读的相对简短的草稿，想知道距离他上次看她已经有多久了，以及她是如何如此迅速地螺旋式上升的。

赫敏张开了嘴，愤怒地张开了嘴，然后明显地控制住了自己。“我对我们正在做的事情并不感到厌烦，”她强行平静地说。

“你知道沙克尔博尔特在为你做准备，”卢修斯平淡地说。

“为了什么？”

赫敏垂下目光，勉强地耸了耸肩。“我只知道他想让我成为魔法执法的副局长。我应该明年去做这份工作。

“一个很好的角色，可以发起魔法部长的竞选，”卢修斯指出。“DMLE 是这个角色的经典跳板部门，你知道的。”

赫敏低头看着卢修斯的礼物，嘴角浮现出一丝亲切的微笑，她的手指好奇地抚摸着闪亮的绿色包装纸和黑色天鹅绒丝带。在一片寂静中，德拉科短暂地滚到他的脚掌上，深吸一口气，看着哈利。

哈利似乎犹豫了一下，然后从他的一品脱啤酒中抽出一只手，果断地把它了他们之间的空隙。“马尔福。”

His grey eyes darted briefly to Hermione, who gave him an encouraging smile over her gifts. Quietly clearing his throat, Malfoy unclenched his fist and finally shook Harry’s hand firmly. 
德拉科眉毛扬起，低头看着哈利的手，就像它刚刚开始了一段特别跑调的生日快乐。他灰色的眼睛短暂地瞥向赫敏，赫敏对她的礼物给了他一个鼓励的微笑。马尔福悄悄地清了清嗓子，松开了握紧的拳头，终于用力握住了哈利的手。

“很高兴见到你。”

“哦，那真是个美妙的时代，”金妮兴奋地说，双手把饮料攥在胸前。“他们变得如此可爱。”

“哦，对了，他喜欢拥抱，”德拉科嘲笑道。“从他的母亲那里。他变得特别喜欢打我了。

“是啊，詹姆斯去年对他太依恋了，”金妮说，恼怒地瞪了哈利一眼。“我没能进去看。”

“实际上，金妮告诉我詹姆斯是你的忠实粉丝，”哈利说，慢慢地躲开了金妮。

当德拉科本能地近乎紧张地环顾四周时，哈利咯咯地笑了起来。“他不在这里，别担心;Molly 和 Arthur 今天有了孩子。但他不会那么快就接受所有人。他朝赫敏的方向狡猾地笑了笑，补充道，“问问赫敏就知道。

“真的花了一段时间，”金妮疑惑地说，她的眼睛没有焦点，因为她回想起儿子红着脸避免被赫敏抱着的决心。

“是她想把他招募到SPEW来吗？”德拉科干巴巴地问。

“我只是送礼物，我真的不打算——”德拉科试图说，然后金妮的手被饮料占据，开始用她的整个身体把他引向吧台。

“我给你加杯，赫敏，”她转过头说。“然后我们就可以开始了。”

By the time Hermione had gotten halfway through opening her gifts, she'd managed to draw an audience, her friends gathering around with their drinks in hand to observe and, in some cases, offer commentary on, what she'd received.
当赫敏打开礼物的一半时，她已经成功地吸引了一群观众，她的朋友们手里拿着饮料围在一起观察，在某些情况下，对她收到的东西发表评论。

It’s just what I needed,” Hermione said, unfolding it to drape it around her neck and rub her cheek against it. “I’ll need to stop in and see them tomorrow.”
赫敏咧嘴一笑，撕开纸，发现一条漂亮柔软的猩红色围巾，显然是莫丽·韦斯莱自己编织的。“哦，我喜欢它！这正是我需要的，“赫敏说，展开它，把它挂在她的脖子上，用脸颊摩擦它。“我明天得停下来看看他们。”

赫敏把那张纸放到她身边那堆破烂不堪的纸上，给金妮腾出了一些空间，金妮已经把德拉科带来的那个大黑匣子推进去了。“对，马尔福，”她气喘吁吁地说。“你赢得了最大的盒子奖。”

Hermione smiled at him, pleased that Ginny had persuaded him to stay for a while, even if it had been with some aggression. It was nice to see him outside of the manor – sometimes she forgot that he wasn't under house arrest.
“谢谢，韦斯莱，这就是我的目标，”德拉科在人群边缘说，举起酒杯发出嘲讽的欢呼。赫敏对他微笑，很高兴金妮说服他留下来一段时间，即使有些咄咄逼人。在庄园外面见到他真是太好了——有时她忘记了他没有被软禁。

赫敏解开盒子上的银色丝带，在她缓开盖子时，从她的额头下好奇地看了德拉科一眼。她向里面望去，轻轻地喘息了一声。“哦，马尔福。”

“让我们看看这是什么，格兰杰，”潘西厉声说，吸引了珀西睁大眼睛的目光。“我想看看礼物，而不是猜它们是什么。”

“Yes, Hermione,” Luna said, a good deal more gently and enthusiastically. “Show us.”
“是的，赫敏，”卢娜说，语气更加温和和热情。“让我们看看。”

Dipping her hands into the box, Hermione lifted out a set of dress robes, prompting an envious gasp from Fleur. 
赫敏把手伸进盒子里，拿出一套礼服长袍，惹得芙蓉羡慕地倒抽了一口气。

As she turned the robes to hold them against herself, Hermione noticed faint silvery swirls in the material when they caught the light
长袍是午夜蓝色的，由如此优质的丝绸制成，当赫敏将它们高高举起时，它的行为更像是液体，将自己倒出，直到它刷到地板上。当她转动长袍以将它们贴在自己身上时，赫敏注意到当它们受到光线的影响时，材料中出现了微弱的银色漩涡

“他们很漂亮，德拉科，”赫敏说，从长袍上抬起头来，在她的腿上晃动着它们。“我真的不知道该说什么。非常感谢。

赫敏笑了起来，她的脸颊在大家好奇的注视下变得粉红色，赫敏点了点头。

“他什么时候来找你的睡裙的？”罗恩反问道，但赫敏假装没听见他的话，巧妙地把长袍叠回盒子里，把盖子盖回去。

虽然没有人说什么，但赫敏感觉到气氛发生了明显的变化，就像她周围的每个人都刚刚饶有兴趣地直起身来。

They all knew about her and Lucius but Hermione was well aware that she was still relatively secretive about their relationship. None of them, with the exception of Draco, had actually witnessed it. This was, she supposed as she weighed the gift in her hands, their first real insight.
他们都知道她和卢修斯的事情，但赫敏很清楚她对他们的关系仍然相对保密。除了德拉科之外，他们都没有真正目睹过这一切。当她权衡手中的礼物时，她想，这是他们第一次真正的洞察力。
